articles.title: Health insurance coverage and quality of care for reproductive and maternal health in LMICs: a multicountry propensity score matching study.
articles.authors: Marthias T, Anindya K, McPake B et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Poor maternal and child health remains a major challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study assessed differences in the reproductive, maternal and child health (RMCH) continuum of care between insured and uninsured populations across nine LMICs.
METHODS: We analysed the latest two Demographic and Health Survey waves collected in Cambodia, Dominican Republic, Ghana, Guatemala, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Kyrgyz Republic and Peru, constituting around 23% of the global population. Propensity score matching assessed associations between health insurance and effective coverage across the care cascade for family planning, antenatal care (ANC), maternal delivery and postnatal care (PNC). Average treatment effect on the treated with 95% CIs was reported.
RESULTS: Insurance effects varied substantially across countries. Family planning service contact was significantly higher among insured population in five of seven countries with available data, with the largest effect in Ghana (16.9 percentage points (pp), 95% CI 11.2 to 22.5). ANC quality-adjusted coverage was significantly higher among insured women in six countries, with the largest effect in India (17.2 pp, 95% CI 15.8 to 18.6). Maternal delivery service contact was significantly associated with insurance coverage in five countries, with the largest effect in Ghana (10.5 pp, 95% CI 6.1 to 14.9). PNC service contact showed significant associations in four countries, with the largest effect in Cambodia (10.3 pp, 95% CI 4.3 to 16.4). Pooled analyses showed positive associations across all outcomes, largest for ANC quality-adjusted coverage (9.9 pp, 95% CI 8.6 to 11.2) and family planning service contact (7.7 pp, 95% CI 6.0 to 9.4). Importantly, insurance coverage was concentrated among more educated women in seven countries and wealthier populations in five, highlighting persistent equity concerns.
CONCLUSIONS: Health insurance coverage was associated with higher RMCH coverage and quality, but persistent socioeconomic inequalities raise equity concerns. Expanding insurance coverage without ensuring inclusivity risks exacerbating disparities and undermining progress towards universal health coverage.

articles.title: Leuprorelin Suppresses Angiogenesis and Malignant Progression in Endometrial Cancer via Downregulation of the ELAVL1/VEGFA Axis.
articles.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
articles.authors: Zhang N, Zhao F, Tan L
articles.abstract: Leuprorelin, a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist, is currently used clinically to suppress estrogen-dependent endometrial cancer (EC) through pituitary desensitization. However, whether this agent exerts direct anti-neoplastic effects via post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms remains unclear. The phenotypic effects of leuprorelin were evaluated in EC cell lines using colony formation, 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation, Transwell migration, wound healing, flow cytometry, and HUVEC tube formation assays. Mechanistic exploration employed RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), mRNA decay kinetics analysis, and RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization combined with immunofluorescence microscopy. A murine xenograft model system was implemented for in vivo validation studies. Leuprorelin treatment significantly reduced proliferation and migration of EC cells, induced apoptosis, and suppressed HUVEC tube formation. At the molecular level, leuprorelin administration reduced cytoplasmic accumulation of ELAVL1, an RNA-binding protein that physiologically associates with VEGFA transcripts and enhances their stability. This reduction resulted in accelerated decay of VEGFA mRNA and subsequent downregulation of VEGFA protein expression. Forced overexpression of VEGFA substantially abrogated the anti-tumor effects mediated by leuprorelin. In nude mouse xenograft models, leuprorelin administration suppressed tumor growth and tumor-associated neovascularization, effects that were reversed upon VEGFA overexpression. Leuprorelin impedes EC progression by disrupting ELAVL1-mediated stabilization of VEGFA mRNA, highlighting the ELAVL1/VEGFA axis as a potential therapeutic target for anti-angiogenic therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: ZC3H13 promotes cervical cancer cell proliferation and stemness and reduces cisplatin sensitivity and apoptosis by stabilizing CTHRC1 mRNA in an m6A-Dependent manner.
articles.authors: Aihemaitijiang F, Meng X, Yumai A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer (CC) remains a global health burden. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification regulated by ZC3H13 is critical in carcinogenesis. Collagen triple helix repeat containing 1 (CTHRC1) is dysregulated in multiple malignancies, but the role of the ZC3H13/CTHRC1 axis in the malignant progression of CC stemness and cisplatin sensitivity remains unclear.
METHODS: Bioinformatic analyses, including differential gene screening, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, random forest, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and support vector machine recursive feature elimination, were performed on the GSE63514 dataset to identify core genes. SRAMP was used to predict m6A sites on CTHRC1 mRNA. Gene expression was detected by quantitative real-time PCR and western blot. Cell proliferation, stemness, apoptosis, and cisplatin sensitivity were assessed by EdU, tumorsphere formation, CD44 flow cytometry, Annexin V-PI staining, and CCK-8 assay, respectively. Regulatory mechanisms were explored by RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), methylated RIP, and mRNA stability assays, and verified by rescue experiments.
RESULTS: Bioinformatic analysis identified CTHRC1 as a core upregulated gene in CC (P = 8.4e-10). CTHRC1 depletion inhibited proliferation and stemness, and promoted cisplatin sensitivity and apoptosis. ZC3H13 was overexpressed in CC (P < 0.001) and positively correlated with CTHRC1 (r = 0.578, P < 0.001). ZC3H13 knockdown decreased CTHRC1 expression and m6A enrichment on CTHRC1 mRNA, accompanied by reduced mRNA stability. CTHRC1 overexpression rescued the phenotypes induced by ZC3H13 knockdown.
CONCLUSION: The ZC3H13/CTHRC1 axis modulates CC stemness and cisplatin sensitivity through an m6A-dependent mRNA stabilization mechanism, laying a solid molecular foundation for developing novel anti-cervical cancer strategies.

articles.title: Interleukin-37 in cancer: Context-dependent roles in tumor immunity, prognosis, and therapeutic targeting.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Wang X, Xu M et al.
articles.abstract: Interleukin-37, a member of the interleukin-1 family, is increasingly recognized as a regulator of cancer biology and tumor immunity. Across cancer types, interleukin-37 expression exhibits divergent patterns and clinical associations. In non-small cell lung cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and acute myeloid leukemia, decreased interleukin-37 expression is more often associated with aggressive clinicopathologic features and poor outcomes. By contrast, in gastric cancer, epithelial ovarian cancer, melanoma, and several other malignancies, increased interleukin-37 expression has been linked to tumor progression and adverse prognosis. Mechanistically, interleukin-37 acts through intracellular and extracellular pathways, including Smad3-dependent nuclear translocation and signaling through the interleukin-18 receptor alpha/interleukin-1 receptor 8 complex, with downstream effects on signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, nuclear factor kappa B, transforming growth factor beta/Smad, and related networks. Depending on cancer type, immune context, isoform usage, and disease stage, interleukin-37 may inhibit proliferation, metabolic reprogramming, angiogenesis, invasion, and metastatic dissemination or promote immune suppression and premetastatic niche formation. Beyond its tumor-intrinsic effects, interleukin-37 reshapes the tumor microenvironment by modulating macrophages, dendritic cells, natural killer cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and T-cell subsets. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the dual roles of interleukin-37 in cancer, discusses major sources of inconsistency across studies, and highlights its potential relevance to prognostic stratification, biomarker development, and therapeutic targeting.

articles.title: "I always thought I was fertile": Reproductive uncertainty, bodily doubt and andarooni kami in North India.
articles.authors: Patel R
articles.abstract: This paper examines how infertility reshapes experiences of body, self, and uncertainty among married couples seeking assisted conception at a private infertility clinic in Uttar Pradesh. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork conducted across three phases between 2020 and 2023, it traces how participants moved from unquestioned assumptions about their reproductive capacity toward growing bodily doubt as repeated attempts at conception failed. The paper argues that prior to infertility, most participants carried what it terms a "fertile self": an assumed confidence in reproductive capacity so embedded in social expectations of marriage and adulthood that it rarely surfaced as conscious thought until disrupted. When conception repeatedly failed despite apparently normal bodily functioning, this confidence gave way to uncertainty and bodily doubt. Central to the analysis is the explanatory idiom andarooni kami (internal deficiency), invoked by participants and their families to account for reproductive failure in bodies that appeared outwardly healthy. The paper demonstrates that this idiom functioned as a culturally intelligible explanation for an epistemological crisis that biomedicine itself could not always resolve. It further shows that reproductive blame was distributed along gendered lines, with women's bodies subjected to suspicion on the basis of failed conception alone while doubt toward men required visible dysfunction or medical confirmation. By attending to how women interpret their own bodies before and beyond medical diagnosis, this paper contributes to anthropological understandings of infertility, embodiment, and gendered reproductive experience in North India. It argues that infertility does not necessarily begin with a diagnosis, it begins with the first unanswered question about a body that appears normal yet will not conceive.

articles.title: CT-based adaptation of the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in advanced ovarian cancer: Agreement and inter-reader reproducibility.
articles.authors: Versienti E, Arcieri M, De Martino M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate agreement of proposed CT-based variants with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in suspected advanced ovarian cancer and assess inter-reader agreement of CT-derived components.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included consecutive adults evaluated between January 2021 and November 2025 for suspected advanced ovarian cancer who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT and staging laparoscopy. Proposed CT-based modifications were operationalized as six score variants combining CT-derived peritoneal tumor burden, CT-estimated ascites, cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), and either Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG-PS) or CT-derived body composition parameters. Agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation coefficient, and weighted Cohen's kappa.
RESULTS: The final cohort included 80 patients. All CT-based variants showed agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. For the variant combining CT-derived PCI, CT-estimated ascites, ECOG-PS, and CA-125, the consistency ICC was 0.76, Spearman's ρ was 0.806, and weighted Cohen's kappa was 0.76. This variant showed 70.0% agreement across the three risk categories and 83.8% agreement for high-risk versus non-high-risk classification, classifying 20 of 22 laparoscopic high-risk patients as high risk. The PCI-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) variant maintained substantial agreement: ICC, 0.73; Spearman correlation coefficient, 0.742; weighted Cohen's kappa, 0.74. Inter-reader agreement was high for CT-derived PCI, with an ICC of 0.91.
CONCLUSION: Proposed CT-based variants showed agreement with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. The PCI-based ECOG-PS variant showed the highest agreement metrics, suggesting that structured CT assessment may help approximate laparoscopic risk categories before invasive evaluation.

articles.title: Leukocyte mtDNA methylation mediates the association between prenatal ozone exposure and gestational diabetes mellitus: Modification by residential greenness.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Liu F, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Prenatal ozone (O3) exposure has been associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), but the role of mitochondrial epigenetic alterations remains unclear. This nested case-control study investigated the association between prenatal O3 exposure and GDM, and evaluated the mediating role of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) methylation and the modifying effect of residential greenness. A total of 500 pregnant women in Tianjin were included, comprising 250 GDM cases and 250 age-matched controls. Prenatal O₃ exposure was estimated using a spatiotemporal model, and residential greenness levels were characterized by the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Leukocyte mtDNA methylation was quantified using bisulfite pyrosequencing. Conditional logistic regression was used to assess the associations. Joint effects of O3 exposure and NDVI were evaluated by dichotomizing both variables at the median. Mediation and effect modification analyses were also conducted. Each 10 μg/m³ increase in O₃ exposure during the 1st and 2nd trimesters was associated with 34% (OR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.17-1.55) and 34% (OR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.17-1.53) higher odds of GDM, respectively, whereas higher NDVI was associated with reduced risk. Women exposed to high O3 and low NDVI had a higher risk of GDM. Mediation analyses suggested that MT-COX1-Pos.1 and MT-COX3-Pos.1 methylation accounted for 7.93% and 5.87%, respectively, of the association between 2nd trimester O3 exposure and GDM. NDVI modified the association between MT-COX1-Pos.1 methylation and GDM. Leukocyte mtDNA methylation may be a potential mediator of the association between prenatal O3 exposure and GDM, while greenness may attenuate this association.

articles.title: Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of Group B Streptococcus isolates recovered from pregnant individuals in Greece.
articles.authors: Akinosoglou K, Gavatha M, Ziakas PD et al.
articles.abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) remains an important pathogen in pregnancy and a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to investigate the antimicrobial susceptibility profile of GBS isolates recovered from pregnant individuals in Greece. A retrospective observational study was conducted, including 89 non-duplicate GBS isolates recovered from vaginal and rectal swab specimens during routine antenatal screening at a maternity clinic in Athens, Greece, between 2021 and 2025. Bacterial identification was performed using the VITEK 2 automated system, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) according to the European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (EUCAST) criteria. High resistance rates were observed for erythromycin and clindamycin, with 58.62% and 54.55% of tested isolates classified as resistant, respectively. Tetracycline showed the highest resistance rate (89.77%), while most isolates remained susceptible to benzylpenicillin (97.75%) and vancomycin (98.86%). Multidrug resistance was detected in 50% of isolates. These findings underscore the need for susceptibility-guided prophylaxis and ongoing surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in Greece.

articles.title: Chinese Herbal Medicine for the Treatment of Abnormal Uterine Bleeding: A Comprehensive Review of Molecular Mechanisms.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Zhang D, Shen W et al.
articles.abstract: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is a highly prevalent clinical condition affecting women of reproductive age. Beyond causing severe secondary complications such as iron-deficiency anemia and infertility, AUB profoundly impairs women's emotional well-being, social functioning, and overall quality of life. Current mainstream guidelines typically recommend conventional treatments as first-line strategies; however, these approaches face significant challenges regarding long-term efficacy and patient tolerability. This unmet need has prompted both patients and clinicians to seek safer and more effective alternative therapies. Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) is widely utilized in the management of gynecological disorders, demonstrating remarkable clinical advantages in alleviating AUB symptoms, reducing recurrence rates, and improving patient tolerability. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the molecular mechanisms underlying CHM formulas and plant-derived bioactive monomers for the treatment of AUB, based on a three-tiered body of evidence encompassing clinical studies, animal models, and in vitro experiments. Current evidence indicates that classical CHM prescriptions and Chinese patent medicines primarily exert their therapeutic effects by rectifying endocrine imbalances, promoting structural repair of the endometrium, regulating systemic metabolism, and restoring coagulation homeostasis. Regarding CHM-derived bioactive monomers (eg alkaloids and flavonoids), their principal mechanisms are characterized by the inhibition of inflammatory cell infiltration, attenuation of oxidative stress, and suppression of pathological angiogenesis. Furthermore, they contribute to endometrial tissue remodeling through the regulation of abnormal cellular proliferation and the induction of apoptosis. It should be emphasized, however, that the mechanistic evidence summarized herein originates primarily from preclinical investigations. Robust clinical evidence targeting specific PALM-COEIN subtypes is still lacking and does not yet permit firm subtype-specific therapeutic recommendations. Moreover, available clinical evidence is unevenly distributed across AUB etiologies, and safety reporting remains inconsistent; these limitations should be considered when interpreting the clinical relevance of findings derived from animal, cellular, omics, or computational studies. Notwithstanding these limitations, the present review offers a coherent scientific framework for…

articles.title: Circulating Biomarkers with Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Risk Assessment and Therapeutic Monitoring: Evidence, Limitations, and Translation.
articles.authors: Wei W, Zhang R, Zhang Z
articles.abstract: Circulating biomarkers, particularly cell-free DNA (cfDNA), are transforming contemporary medicine through their capacity to provide dynamic, minimally invasive assessments of disease dynamics. Their clinical utility has broadened substantially to include oncology, cardiovascular conditions, transplant monitoring, infectious diseases, and persistent inflammatory disorders. Nevertheless, the increasing complexity and volume of biomarker-related data pose substantial challenges, necessitating the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning methodologies for improved data interpretation, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. This review presents a thorough examination of recent progress in the integration of circulating biomarkers with AI within therapeutic contexts and clinical risk management. It outlines the translational trajectory from molecular signatures to precision medicine, addresses present constraints, and explores prospective developments. The objective of this review is to serve as a systematic resource for both clinical practice and research, thereby promoting the evolution of personalized medicine through innovative, biomarker-driven strategies supported by AI.

articles.title: Effect of a Comprehensive Perinatal Education Program on Maternal Outcomes in Primigravida Mothers.
articles.authors: Karale RB, Salunkhe J
articles.abstract: Antenatal care is essential for ensuring a healthy pregnancy, especially in first-time mothers (primigravida) who may experience greater uncertainty and risks. The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of a perinatal education program on maternal outcomes among primigravida mothers. A total of 144 primigravida mothers attending the antenatal outpatient department at a tertiary care hospital were enrolled. The intervention group (n = 72) received perinatal education covering antenatal care (diet, hygiene, exercise, and relaxation), intranatal guidance (back massage, breathing techniques, and labor expectations), and postnatal education (breastfeeding, newborn care, maternal health, and family planning) in seven sessions. The control group (n = 72) received routine care. Maternal outcomes were assessed throughout pregnancy, during labor, and postpartum, and data were analyzed using appropriate parametric and nonparametric statistical tests. The posttest knowledge scores were significantly higher (t = 20.59, p < .001) in the intervention group (33.9 ± 2.5) than the control group (21.2 ± 4.6). The intervention group had lower stress scores and a higher rate of normal vaginal births compared with the control group. The intervention group showed a significantly shorter duration of labor in the second and third stages, increased placental weights, and lower blood loss during birth (p < .001 for all). The perinatal education program significantly improved maternal knowledge and outcomes in primigravida mothers, including higher rates of normal vaginal birth, shorter labor duration, reduced blood loss, and fewer complications. These findings support integrating structured perinatal education into routine antenatal care to enhance maternal knowledge and clinical parameters and improve overall pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: The intergenerational and transgenerational effects of miRNAs in fertility, obesity and stress responses.
articles.authors: Tang YC, Lei KH, Wong ESW et al.
articles.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators that play pivotal roles in diverse physiological and pathological processes. They primarily act by inhibiting protein translation and promoting degradation of messenger RNA (mRNA), thereby inducing post-transcriptional regulatory effects. Most miRNAs can travel through blood, in extracellular vesicles, and between maternal and fetal tissues. When altered miRNAs were present in germ cells, this induces epigenetic inheritance, which influences embryonic development after fertilization. Aberrant miRNA expression is associated with a wide range of human diseases. This review article will summarize current evidence on how miRNA dysregulation contributes to transgenerational effects on reproduction, metabolism, and stress-related phenotypes. This research focuses on the impacts of miRNAs on reproductive impairment, obesity, and stress-related phenotypes, and highlights evidence that these epigenetic changes can persist across multiple generations. Relevant studies were identified mainly through PubMed database using "miRNA" and "transgenerational effect", with a third keyword according to the topic of interest, including "reproduction", "hormones", "spermatogenesis", "obesity", "high-fat diet", "diabetes", "stress", and "therapy". In reproduction, environmental pollutants (including endocrine disruptors) can alter miRNA expression, impairing gonadal development, reducing primordial germ cells, inducing granulosa cell apoptosis, and disrupting sex hormone synthesis. miRNA-dependent pathways also affect spermatogenesis, sperm function, and oocyte development. In obesity, miRNAs regulate adipogenesis by modulating signaling pathways and transcription programs that control fat-cell formation. Paternal high-fat diet and gestational diabetes can shift miRNA profiles, raising offspring risk for obesity and metabolic disease. Chronic stress changes miRNA expression in germ cells and embryos, shaping stress reactivity and social behavior in later generations. Prenatal maternal stress is linked to lasting psychiatric vulnerability in offspring, with effects potentially persisting across multiple generations without continued stress. Overall, miRNA dysregulation can impair reproduction, metabolism, and stress responses, and these effects may be transmitted transgenerationally via epigenetic mechanisms.

articles.title: Effects of Follicular versus Luteal Phase on Postoperative Mechanical Hyperalgesia Following Laparoscopic Myomectomy: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Long B, Yang H, Yan Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have suggested that pain sensitivity may be lower during the follicular phase than during the luteal phase, and similar findings have been observed following gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. However, the effect of the menstrual cycle phase on postoperative mechanical hyperalgesia following laparoscopic myomectomy and its potential value for guiding the timing of surgery remain unclear.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare postoperative mechanical hyperalgesia in women undergoing laparoscopic myomectomy during the follicular versus the luteal phase.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eighty patients scheduled for elective laparoscopic myomectomy were enrolled. Forearm pressure pain thresholds (FPPT) and incisional pressure pain thresholds (IPPT) were measured preoperatively and at 1 h, 24 h, and 48 h postoperatively. Postoperative pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) within 48 h after surgery. Total sufentanil consumption and the number of patients requiring rescue analgesia were also recorded.
RESULTS: FPPT showed a significant group main effect (P = 0.04), with higher FPPT in the follicular group than in the luteal group (mean difference 0.18, 95% CI 0.03-0.73). The group × time interaction and IPPT comparison were not significant (P > 0.05). For NRS, the group × time interaction was significant (P = 0.046). After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, NRS at 24 h was higher in the luteal group (mean difference 0.43, 95% CI 0.13-0.72, P = 0.03), with no differences at other time points. More luteal-phase patients required rescue analgesia within 24 h, although total sufentanil consumption did not differ.
CONCLUSION: The luteal phase was associated with a lower overall forearm pressure pain threshold and a higher rescue analgesia rate after laparoscopic myomectomy, suggesting that the phase of the menstrual cycle may be associated with postoperative pain sensitivity and analgesic requirements.

articles.title: Association of Placental Morphological Abnormalities with Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Tao H, Sun L, Ma R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between placental morphological abnormalities and adverse pregnancy outcomes in patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with HDP who delivered at Wuhan Union Hospital, Wuhan, China, between May 2020 and June 2025. Based on prenatal ultrasound, patients were classified as having abnormal placental morphology (thickened or small placenta) or normal morphology. A two-stage propensity score matching procedure was used to balance baseline characteristics at a 1:2 ratio. Conditional logistic regression stratified by matched pairs evaluated maternal and neonatal outcomes. Model 1 included placental morphology alone, whereas Model 2 additionally adjusted for abnormal umbilical artery or middle cerebral artery Doppler findings and ultrasound-estimated fetal growth lag.
RESULTS: Among 1928 patients, 111 (5.8%) had abnormal placental morphology. After matching, abnormal morphology was associated with higher odds of preterm birth, early preterm birth, low birth weight, very low birth weight, 1-minute Apgar score <7, and NICU admission in Model 1. After additional adjustment in Model 2, these associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant. In subtype analyses, small-placenta subgroups showed more frequent abnormal Doppler findings and suspected fetal growth restriction and generally less favorable neonatal outcomes than the isolated thickening group. Landmark analyses showed that associations detected at 28 weeks included early preterm birth and very low birth weight, with the latter remaining significant after additional adjustment, whereas associations observed at 34 weeks were attenuated after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Placental morphological abnormalities were associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes in HDP, but these associations were attenuated after accounting for concurrent Doppler and fetal growth abnormalities. Placental morphology may provide complementary structural information as part of integrated assessment of placental and perinatal risk in HDP.

articles.title: The Role of NK‑Cell Dysregulation in Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Rheumatic Immune Diseases: Mechanisms and Translational Advances.
articles.authors: Zhu L, Hua L, Du H
articles.abstract: Rheumatic autoimmune diseases induce sustained systemic inflammatory imbalance and substantially elevate the incidence of adverse pregnancy complications, such as recurrent spontaneous abortion, preeclampsia, preterm delivery, and fetal growth restriction. Decidual natural killer (dNK) cells constitute the major lymphocyte subset at the maternal-fetal interface and maintain the homeostasis of immune tolerance, trophoblast invasion and spiral artery remodeling; peripheral NK (pNK) cells differ greatly from dNK cells in phenotype, cytotoxicity and secretory function under the regulation of local uterine microenvironment. Emerging evidence indicates that dysregulated NK‑cell number, subset distribution, receptor signalling and cytokine release may perturb the decidual immune‑vascular microenvironment and contribute to inflammatory placental‑associated pathology, with considerably more robust mechanistic support in antiphospholipid syndrome than in systemic lupus erythematosus, primary Sjögren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic sclerosis. Solid preclinical and clinical evidence confirms that excessive NK cell activation participates in placental injury in antiphospholipid syndrome, whereas the direct inflammatory pathogenic cascades underlying gestational complications remain insufficiently clarified for other rheumatic disorders. This work elucidates the physiological heterogeneity of pNK and dNK cells, delineates six core inflammatory axes driving NK-mediated placental injury, characterizes disease-specific aberrant inflammatory phenotypes of NK cells, summarizes translational advances in NK-targeted anti-inflammatory strategies, and identifies existing research bottlenecks. We also put forward prospective research schemes based on single-cell multi-omics and large-scale clinical cohorts to reveal NK-centered inflammatory pathology, which offers theoretical support for immune inflammation regulation in childbearing-age women with rheumatic autoimmune diseases.

articles.title: Bridging the gap in maternal care: the role of community-based workers in preventing maternal mortality.
articles.authors: Kruzan M
articles.abstract: The United States continues to face a persistent maternal mortality crisis, underscoring the need to explore innovative approaches to prevention that extend beyond traditional clinical care. Mental health and substance use disorders are among the leading causes of preventable maternal deaths, particularly during the postpartum period when clinical perinatal care ends. Community-based workers-including community health workers, doulas, peer support specialists, and patient navigators-may address gaps in maternal healthcare by responding to social determinants of health, connecting patients with community resources, and supporting engagement with healthcare and behavioral health services. This commentary explores opportunities to integrate community-based workers into perinatal care and highlights their potential roles in addressing mental health and substance use, navigating social and structural barriers, and strengthening continuity of support throughout pregnancy and the postpartum period. The commentary also highlights the importance of investing in the community-based workforce and developing partnerships between community-based workers and perinatal providers. Rather than replacing physicians, community-based workers may complement clinical care by addressing needs that extend beyond the traditional scope of medical practice and expanding the reach of maternal healthcare.

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Symptoms in Performing Artists and Artistic Athletes: Prevalence and Impact.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.abstract: This infographic summarises the key messages of Frydenberg's et al. (2026) article on the prevalence and impact of pelvic floor symptoms in performing artists and artistic athletes. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(11):750. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.9004.

articles.title: Single-Cell Insights Into Pathogenic Profile of Orchitis and SREBP2-Associated Cholesterol Dysregulation in Spermatogenic Failure.
articles.authors: Tang Y, Jiang Q, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Orchitis, a testicular inflammation often triggered by infection, is a major cause of male infertility due to disruption of the testicular immune microenvironment and progressive loss of germ cells. Currently, no effective or targeted therapies are available. Here, we profile 66,147 single-cell transcriptomes from testes of orchitis patients and healthy controls, complemented by histological validation. We observe profound remodeling of testicular cell composition, with marked infiltration of CD8+ effector T cells and inflammatory macrophages, accompanied by germ cell loss. Undifferentiated spermatogonia exhibit cell-cycle arrest, while somatic cell populations display fibrosis, apoptosis, and loss of homeostatic functions. Notably, interstitial cells show SREBP2- associated reprogramming of cholesterol metabolism, characterized by increased synthesis. Inhibition of SREBP2 in a mouse orchitis model improves spermatogenesis, reduces lipid accumulation, and alleviates fibrosis. These findings demonstrate that immune activation-induced SREBP2 upregulation drives cholesterol metabolic imbalance and spermatogenic failure in orchitis, offering potential therapeutic options for inflammation-associated male infertility.

articles.title: Associations Between Self-Reported Experiences of Racial Discrimination and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy among Black and White Women in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.authors: Dodds LV, Feaster DJ, Kiefe CI et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are major contributors to maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Perceived experiences of racial discrimination (EORD) have been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study investigates the association between EORD and incident HDP among Black and White women.
METHODS: The Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study is a prospective cohort of 5,115 Black and White adults aged 18 to 30 years at baseline (1985-1986), followed for over 30 years. EORD was analyzed as a continuous proportion, a three-category variable (no discrimination, overall proportion < 33%, and 33% or greater), and dichotomously (none vs. ever). HDP was self-reported in pregnancies lasting at least 23 weeks. Logistic regression assessed the association between EORD and HDP among 1,184 parous women, adjusting for age, race, education, income, cardiovascular risk factors, and parity.
RESULTS: At baseline, the mean age was 24.1 years; 48.1% were Black, 72.3% were nulliparous, and 19.7% had an income less than $16,000. Overall, 60.6% reported EORD (86.0% of Black and 37.1% of White women). Those reporting EORD were more likely to be Black, unmarried, have higher BMI, and have had one birth at baseline (p < 0.001). EORD was associated with increased odds of HDP (OR: 1.73 [1.20-2.48]) among both Black and White women. EORD < 33% (OR: 1.75 [1.20-2.55]) and 33% or greater (OR: 1.65 [1.04-2.64]) were significantly associated with HDP.
CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS: EORD, regardless of race, is significantly associated with increased odds of HDP. The disproportionate burden among Black women highlights the need for targeted interventions.

articles.title: Association between hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and neurocognitive development in children aged 36 months: a cohort study in Matlab, Bangladesh.
articles.authors: Rahman M, Aktar S, Yesmin N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and neurodevelopmental outcomes among children aged approximately 36 months in a rural area of Bangladesh.
METHODS: The study was based on HDP cases identified within a pregnancy cohort conducted between April 2015 and March 2018. Children born to HDP-exposed mothers (n=173) and a randomly selected group of HDP-unexposed mothers (n=350) were assessed for cognitive, language and motor development using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Third Edition (Bayley-III), between November 2019 and July 2021. Multiple linear regression analysis was used to examine the associations and results were reported as adjusted mean differences in composite scores (β coefficients) with 95% CIs.
RESULTS: Overall, children born to mothers with HDP had lower mean composite scores for cognitive (β=−1.14, 95% CI −2.06 to −0.22), language (β=−1.54, 95% CI −2.56 to −0.52) and motor (β=−2.52, 95% CI −3.95 to −1.08) development compared with children of HDP-unexposed mothers. Significant associations were also observed across several developmental subdomains. When analyses were stratified by specific HDP types, the effects were more pronounced among children exposed to chronic hypertension, whereas no significant association was detected for exposure to pre-eclampsia.
CONCLUSION: HDP were associated with impaired neurocognitive development among children in a rural area of Bangladesh. The strength of these associations varied across developmental domains and by specific HDP types.

articles.title: Knowledge and Perceptions of Female Pelvic Floor Disorders Among Partnered Males.
articles.authors: Xu H, Dreyfuss LD, Hu S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the knowledge and perceptions of female pelvic floor disorders (PFDs) among men in active or former long-term relationships.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Men 45 years and older previously or currently in a long-term (≥3 years) intimate relationship with a woman were recruited from a urology clinic. Respondents completed the validated Prolapse and Incontinence Knowledge Questionnaire, with supplemental questions assessing attitudes on PFDs. The primary outcome was knowledge proficiency in the pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and urinary incontinence (UI) domains, defined as ≥50% and >75% correct, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analysis assessed factors associated with proficiency in both domains. Secondary outcomes included rates of high response confidence, defined as responding with "don't know" less than 50% of the time.
RESULTS: Of the 134 respondents, 22% demonstrated proficiency in the POP and 13% in the UI domain, with median scores of 1/12 and 3.5/12, respectively. Employed men were more likely to demonstrate knowledge proficiency (POP: aOR 6.24, P <.01; UI: aOR 6.94, P = .024) and exhibit higher rates of response confidence (POP: aOR 5.39, P = .01; UI: aOR 5.54, P <.01), relative to retired men. Higher education, older age, and having a partner with POP were associated with proficiency in the POP domain only. Fewer than 25% of men felt they should be involved in treatment decisions related to PFD.
CONCLUSION: Men in long-term relationships exhibited low PFD knowledge. Future research is needed to determine if a relationship exists between improved knowledge among male partners and care-seeking behavior among women with PFDs.

articles.title: Is blastocyst culture failure during first IVF cycle a sign of poor prognosis in subsequent cycles? A matched case-control study.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Boughzala I, Lammers J, Chaillot M et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Embryonic development arrest in extended culture during in vitro fertilization (IVF) presents a major challenge to achieving successful pregnancy outcomes. While blastocyst transfer has become the preferred method due to improved implantation rates, a significant proportion of embryos fail to develop to the blastocyst stage, resulting in cycle cancellations and reduced chances of pregnancy. Does failure to reach the blastocyst stage in a first IVF cycle signal an inherently poor prognosis for future attempts?
DESIGN: In this monocentric retrospective matched case-control study (2020-2023) analyzing 1126 IVF/ICSI cycles, we compared outcomes of patients with total blastocyst culture failure (T1 Failure, n = 113) against a propensity-score-matched control group (T1 Control, n = 113).
RESULTS: T1 Failure cycles were characterized by significantly fewer mature oocytes (6.54±4.78 vs. 8.29±4.5, p < 0.001) and Day 3 embryos (3.36±3.11 vs. 5.31±3.53, p < 0.001). Notably, 72.6% of patients with initial culture failure achieved transferable blastocysts in their second cycle (T2). In T2, repeat failure was specifically associated with higher basal FSH (8.01±2.85 vs. 6.73±1.87, p = 0.008) and lower AMH levels (2.02±1.48 vs. 3.79±5.43, p = 0.036).
CONCLUSION: While initial failure is linked to lower oocyte yield and early embryo competence, it is not an absolute barrier to success. Most patients recover in subsequent cycles through protocol optimization, though diminished ovarian reserve remains the primary risk factor for recurrent failure. Our findings underscore the multifactorial nature of embryonic arrest and highlight potential clinical indicators for predicting and managing blastocyst development failure to optimize IVF success rates.

articles.title: Metamizole (dipyrone) versus ibuprofen for post-cesarean analgesia in women with preeclampsia with severe features: a quadruple-blind, randomized, active-comparator trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Pordeus ACB, Katz L, Maia MT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adequate analgesia after cesarean delivery is a priority in women with preeclampsia, in whom opioid-sparing strategies are desirable. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) were historically avoided in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy because of a presumed effect on blood pressure, but randomized trials and meta-analyses have since shown no clinically meaningful blood-pressure effect, and current guidance supports their postpartum use when otherwise appropriate. Metamizole (dipyrone) is a non-opioid analgesic widely used in Brazil, Latin America, and parts of Europe, but its regulatory status varies internationally. It is not approved in the United States, and agranulocytosis is a recognized rare but potentially serious adverse reaction. European regulatory guidance also advises against its use during breastfeeding. No randomized trial has directly compared metamizole with an NSAID after cesarean delivery in women with preeclampsia.
OBJECTIVE: To compare metamizole and ibuprofen for analgesic effectiveness and short-term safety, with particular attention to blood pressure trajectory and renal function, after cesarean delivery in women with preeclampsia with severe features.
STUDY DESIGN: Quadruple-blind (participant, care provider, investigator, outcome assessor), randomized, active-comparator, phase 4 trial at a tertiary maternity hospital in northeastern Brazil. Seventy-four women received oral metamizole 1 g or ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours for up to 5 days, with intravenous tramadol available as rescue analgesia. Co-primary outcomes, as prospectively registered, were postoperative pain-categorized as mild, moderate, or severe by visual analogue scale (VAS)-and acute kidney injury (AKI). Continuous VAS, the D1-to-D2 mean reduction in VAS, the clinically interpretable threshold VAS ≥4, the Faces Pain Scale-Revised, peri-incisional pressure pain thresholds by algometry, rescue analgesia, serial blood pressure, hypertensive episodes, laboratory values, satisfaction, and length of stay were secondary or supportive outcomes. Effects were estimated with risk differences, risk ratios, exact tests, Hodges-Lehmann differences, standardized effect sizes with Holm correction, and linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight women were allocated to metamizole and 36 to ibuprofen. The registered three-category pain distribution did not differ between groups on day 1 (exact P=.45) or day 2 (exact P=.55). Median VAS was 4 (IQR 2-5) in…

articles.title: Gaps in Reproductive Health Counseling Among Adolescents with Chronic Medical Conditions.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Campwala Z, Sheeder J, Richards MJ
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Adolescents and young adults (AYAs) with chronic medical conditions (CMCs) face increased risks with unintended pregnancy, yet may receive limited reproductive health counseling. This study describes these AYAs' experiences with contraceptive counseling and perceived barriers to contraceptive access and use.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of pregnancy-capable AYAs aged 12-24 years receiving care in pediatric subspecialty clinics. Eligible participants had a CMC associated with pregnancy-related health risks or were prescribed potentially teratogenic medications, informed by U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria guidance.1 The survey assessed counseling experiences, preferences, and perceived barriers. Analyses were descriptive with subgroup exploration by age.
RESULTS: Among 322 participants (median age 16), most reported comfort discussing birth control (76.3%) and valued subspecialty provider input (88.2%). However, only 16.1% reported discussing pregnancy-related risks with a subspecialist, and 6.8% reported being advised about pregnancy prevention in the context of their condition. While 78.9% endorsed the importance of private time with providers, only 48.9% reported confidential discussions. Participants also reported informational and access barriers, including uncertainty about where to obtain contraception.
CONCLUSIONS: AYAs with CMCs report low rates of reproductive health counseling despite valuing subspecialty input and reporting comfort with these discussions. Missed opportunities for counseling and confidential communication in subspecialty care may contribute to persistent reproductive health inequities for adolescents with chronic medical conditions.

articles.title: Metabolite profiling and antiproliferative activity of endophytic fungus Alternaria alternata Y-13 isolated from Ageratina adenophora against cervical cancer cells.
articles.authors: Yang F, Yousif M, Okyere SK et al.
articles.abstract: Ageratina adenophora is an invasive plant known for its toxicity to livestock. Many advantageous endophytes, extracts, and metabolites with antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory properties have been identified from A. adenophora in recent years. However, there is little information about the antiproliferative activity of these plant resources. Therefore, this study aims to screen and identify endophytic fungi from Ageratina adenophora that show favourable antiproliferative properties in vitro. Firstly, putative strains antiproliferative activity were screened and identified using the Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) method, and the chemical constituents of the extract were characterized by LC-MS/MS analysis, then potential targets and pathways were predicted through network pharmacologyand further explored through molecular docking and in vitro experiments. Our results showed that, Alternaria alternata Y-13 endophyte exhibited potent antiproliferative activity at IC₅₀ value of (15.90 ± 2.54) μg/mL against HeLa S3 cells. The network pharmacology identified 157 potential targets, and 10 core genes including AKT1 and CASP3; KEGG enrichment revealed pathways such as cancer, PI3K-Akt, and apoptosis; the molecular docking suggested that theputatively annotated metabolites could bound to AKT1 and EGFR. In vitro experiments showed that Y-13 ethyl acetate extracts (EAE) regulated the expression of apoptosis-related genes and proteins. This is the first study to show that extracts from endophytic fungus, Alternaria alternata Y-13 isolated from A. adenophora exerts prominent antiproliferative effects against cervical cancer cells, providing preliminary insights into its potential molecular mechanisms and a basis for further investigation of its bioactive constituents.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Treatments and Embolic Agents for Symptomatic Uterine Fibroids: A Bayesian Network Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.authors: Coutinho ML, Bregalda Neves CR, Torres IO et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare, using Bayesian network meta-analysis, the effectiveness and safety of treatments and embolic agents for symptomatic uterine fibroids.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of randomized controlled trials (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library; inception through July 2026) compared, via two prespecified Bayesian network meta-analyses, (1) uterine artery embolization (UAE) with hysterectomy, myomectomy, magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound, microwave ablation, and laparoscopic uterine artery occlusion, and (2) embolic agents used during UAE. Primary outcomes were technical success and major complications for treatment strategies, and complete/near-complete fibroid infarction for embolic agents; reintervention was secondary in both networks.
RESULTS: Twenty-three RCTs (N=2,055 women) were included. Technical success and major complication rates did not differ significantly across treatment strategies or embolic agents in the Bayesian analysis, though frequentist analysis showed slightly higher technical success with hysterectomy than UAE (RR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.17). Myomectomy had significantly lower reintervention than UAE (OR, 0.21; 95% CrI, 0.10-0.40). Several Bayesian associations emerged for polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) particles versus tris-acryl gelatin microspheres (TAGM), including higher complete infarction (OR, 4.8; 95% CrI, 1.0-40), higher reintervention (OR, 5.3; 95% CrI, 1.4-28), and divergent findings with PVA700-900; none was reproduced in the frequentist analysis.
CONCLUSION: UAE did not differ significantly from alternative strategies in procedural success or safety, but myomectomy showed greater durability. Evidence is insufficient to establish definitive embolic-agent differences. Treatment strategy appears to influence outcomes more than embolic material, supporting individualized selection and larger trials.

articles.title: Patient-held tools supporting gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) care across the perinatal continuum: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Zehra A, Sushko K, Sherifali D et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) requires continuous care across the perinatal period, yet fragmented systems create gaps in follow-up and coordination. Patient-held tools support self-management and continuity, but their scope across the perinatal continuum has not been synthesized. We conducted a scoping review following Arksey and O'Malley guidelines, searching five databases (MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Web of Science) from January 2000 to November 2025. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data on patient-held GDM tools in pregnancy, postpartum, or both. 62 studies from 24 countries were included. Most tools were mobile applications (n = 48, 77%), predominantly targeting the prenatal period (n = 44, 71%). Common features included glucose monitoring, education, and provider communication. Some studies reported improvements in glycemic control, engagement, and satisfaction, though implementation outcomes (n = 48, 77%) were more commonly reported than clinical outcomes (n = 28, 45%). Only 12 unique tools supported prenatal-to-postpartum continuity. Key barriers included health literacy, technological limitations, and health system challenges; facilitators included personalized content, ease of use, and real-time visual feedback. Patient-held tools show promise for short-term outcomes; however, continuity of care remains infrequently reported, possibly reflecting gaps in tool design, reporting, or both. Future tools should address equity barriers and incorporate continuity mechanisms to reduce long-term cardiometabolic risk.

articles.title: Persistent Fetal Neck Hyperextension in Early Gestation.
articles.authors: Mangla M, Motwani R, Palo S et al.
articles.abstract: Hyperextension of the fetal neck is an uncommon but clinically significant finding with diverse etiologies ranging from isolated postural variations to lethal congenital anomalies. Potential associated conditions include anencephaly, iniencephaly, cervical spine malformations, and syndromic musculoskeletal disorders. Advances in prenatal imaging have improved recognition, yet diagnostic challenges and management dilemmas persist. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on the embryology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, differential diagnosis, clinical implications, and management strategies of fetal hyperextended neck. Further studies are needed to refine diagnostic cut-offs, explore the natural course of the condition over time, and establish consensus protocols for clinical practice.

articles.title: Integrating Music Therapy Into Antepartum Care: A Humanistic Approach to the Perinatal Continuum.
articles.authors: Vernisie SN, Schwartz KE, Janssen O
articles.abstract: Inpatient antepartum hospitalization may be warranted for a variety of reasons during pregnancy and can be associated with distinct psychological stressors, anxiety, and increased vulnerability to mental health challenges. Prolonged hospitalization during pregnancy can create an emotional burden that is not always addressed by medical care alone. Music therapy may serve as a valuable adjunct to care for patients in the hospital who are pregnant, offering trauma-informed psychosocial support through a musical, relational lens. In this manuscript, we explore how music therapy may address emotional containment and expression, offer nonpharmacological pain management, foster parental-fetal attunement, and provide continuity across the perinatal continuum. As awareness of perinatal mood and anxiety disorders continues to expand, integrating music therapy into inpatient perinatal care models may enhance patient-centered care, improve patient experience, and increase engagement with supportive services. We also discuss future implications for interdisciplinary collaboration, research, and program development within hospital systems.

articles.title: Effect of toll-like receptors 7/8 agonist R848 on X-bearing sperm enrichment in dairy goat semen.
articles.authors: Zhangtao H, Zhiwen B, Xiaoxu C et al.
articles.abstract: Sperm separation through protein activation or inhibition, based on proteins differentially expressed in X- and Y-chromosome-bearing sperm, represents a novel approach to controlling offspring sex. This method separates X- and Y-bearing sperm by directly activating these differentially expressed proteins. However, technical limitations and inconsistent sperm concentrations remain. This study established a Toll-like receptors 7 and 8 (TLR7/8) activation-based sorting system for goat sperm and developed a corresponding technical protocol. Building on our laboratory's previous technique for sorting X- and Y-chromosome-bearing sperm by targeting specific proteins, we investigated interactions among sperm concentration, agonist R848 concentration, and incubation time. R848 (resiquimod) is a synthetic imidazoquinoline compound that acts as an agonist of Toll-like receptors 7 and 8 (TLR7/8). The results indicated that R848 binding to TLR7/8 on the tails of X-bearing sperm inhibited their motility, causing them to accumulate in the lower fraction of the sorting system. In contrast, Y-bearing sperm motility was unaffected, allowing these sperm to migrate to the upper fraction. Acrosome integrity did not differ significantly between the selected experimental groups and the control group, with values exceeding 50%. Plasma membrane integrity in the selected experimental groups was either significantly higher than or not significantly different from that in the control group. SRY immunofluorescence staining revealed X-bearing sperm proportions of 88.29% ± 1.68%, 84.50% ± 0.18%, and 80.32% ± 1.94% in one set of selected experimental groups, and Y-bearing sperm proportions of 80.95% ± 0.00%, 88.89% ± 0.00%, and 84.03% ± 2.38%. We subsequently investigated the effect of centrifugal force on R848 removal. The results demonstrated that centrifugation effectively removed R848. Only in this study, the optimal centrifugal force was 800 × g for sorted X-bearing sperm and 700 × g for sorted Y-bearing sperm from dairy goats. Finally, the optimized sorting system was used for sperm separation. In a single independent exploratory IVF batch, 21 of 25 sexed embryos in the upper-fraction B7 group were classified as male (84.0%), whereas 16 of 20 sexed embryos in the lower-fraction E8 group were classified as female (80.0%). B7 and E8 were intended for Y- and X-bearing sperm enrichment, respectively. These observations were limited to the embryos analyzed in this batch and do not…

articles.title: Trends in use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in obese patients with endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Chang HH, Hsieh TYJ, Esselen KM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most endometrial cancers (EC) are obesity-related; yet, there is little known about utilization of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RAs), which are effective weight loss medications, in EC.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study using TriNetX US Collaborative Network, a de-identified, longitudinal electronic health record dataset. Female patients were identified from 1/1/2018-4/15/2024 with BMI ≥30 and grouped by presence or absence of EC diagnosis. Patients were followed for two years or up to 4/15/26, whichever came first. These two groups were 1:1 propensity score matched for demographics, BMI, and comorbidities. Patients with prior bariatric surgery or GLP-1RA use were excluded. The primary outcome was GLP-1RA use. Subgroup analysis was conducted among patients with BMI ≥40.
RESULT: From 2018 to 2024, GLP-1RAs use in both cohorts increased. However, utilization was consistently lower among patients with EC. In 2018, GLP-1RA use was 1.0% among patients with EC vs. 1.2% among those without EC (RR 0.82, CI 0.60-1.13). By 2024, use increased to 7.8% and 10.6%, respectively (RR 0.73, CI 0.61-0.87). Similar findings were observed among patients with a BMI ≥40, with significantly faster uptake of GLP-1RAs among women without EC.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with EC were less likely to receive GLP-1RAs than matched patients without EC despite obesity being a major risk factor for EC. These findings highlight a potential gap in obesity management among EC survivors and support further investigation of the safety and efficacy of GLP-1RAs in this population.

articles.title: Human papillomavirus vaccination following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and subsequent cervical cancer: A retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Farolfi A, Casadei C, Strada I et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination following cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and subsequent invasive cervical cancer (CC) diagnoses.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with CIN (ICD-10-CM: N87, N87.0, N87.1, D06) during 2020-2022 who underwent regular cervical screening (Z12.4) were compared according to subsequent HPV vaccination records. Propensity score matching (PSM) incorporated demographic characteristics, selected diagnosis, and cervical procedures. Outcomes were assessed for day 1 through year 3 after the CIN diagnosis. Patients with CC recorded before diagnosis were excluded. Exploratory analyses evaluated code-defined CIN1-2 and CIN3 subgroups.
RESULTS: Matching yielded 7397 patients per cohort. After outcome-specific exclusions, 7194 vaccinated patients and 7233 comparators remained, with 47 and 92 CC diagnoses, respectively (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.39-0.79; p=0.001). By CIN grade, a significant association was observed in CIN3 patients (HR 0.32; 95% CI 0.20-0.53; p < 0.001), but not CIN1-2 patients (HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.51-1.92; p=0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Recorded HPV vaccination was associated with fewer CC diagnosis overall and in CIN3 patients. Exposure misclassification, residual confounding, differential observation, and non-proportional hazards limit casual interpretation.

articles.title: Thoracic recurrence after complete gross resection in advanced ovarian cancer: The clinical impact of occult subdiaphragmatic lymphatic invasion.
articles.authors: Onishi J, Nagamine M, Wakabayashi M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Complete gross tumor resection is an important prognostic factor in advanced ovarian cancer (AOC), and total parietal peritonectomy (TPP) is a key method to achieve it. Despite undergoing complete gross resection, some patients experience thoracic recurrence, which is associated with a poor prognosis. Clinicopathological factors associated with such recurrence remain unclear. We hypothesized that occult lymphovascular invasion within the subdiaphragmatic peritoneum, the lymphatic interface between the peritoneal and thoracic cavities, may be associated with thoracic recurrence.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage IIIB-IVB ovarian cancer who underwent complete resection using TPP. Clinicopathological factors evaluated were stage, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, homologous recombination deficiency status, and intraoperative macroscopic findings. The subdiaphragmatic regions were microscopically assessed for lymphovascular invasion using D2-40 and CD31 immunohistochemistry. Thoracic recurrence was analyzed using Fine-Gray model.
RESULTS: Seventy-four patients were included: 47 (63.5%) and 27 (36.5%) had stage III and IV disease, respectively. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy was administered to 38 (51.4%) patients. Subdiaphragmatic lymphatic invasion (SLI) was detected in 37 patients (50.0%), including seven without macroscopic lesions; venous invasion was rare (n = 1). During a median follow-up of 30.9 months, 20 (27.0%) and 18 (24.3%) patients developed thoracic and abdominal recurrence, respectively. Thoracic recurrence was significantly higher with SLI (43.2% vs. 10.8%); SLI independently predicted thoracic recurrence (subdistribution hazard ratios, 16.5, 95% confidence interval, 5.1-53.9; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: SLI was independently associated with thoracic recurrence after complete gross resection in AOC, supporting a potential transdiaphragmatic pathway of tumor dissemination.

articles.title: Defining quality care in gynecologic cancers: A Society of Gynecologic Oncology review.
articles.authors: Barber EL, Paraghamian S, Taylor J et al.
articles.abstract: Quality metrics are quantifiable measures that are used to assess healthcare processes and outcomes. Gynecologic oncologists encounter quality measures in their daily practice. These include measures associated with different phases or episodes of care including inpatient care, surgical care and cancer care. Common examples include surgical complication rates, rates of chemotherapy-related adverse events and broader institutional metrics such as length of stay, readmissions and mortality. Measures can be used for different purposes including direct quality improvement, payment reform, accreditation, public reporting and external rankings. While quality metrics can drive standardization and improve performance, they can increase administrative burden and cause unintended consequences. In this review, we discuss commonly encountered metrics in gynecologic oncology, first by general metrics and then by specific disease sites. In cases where specific disease site metrics do not exist, the best available evidence for high value care in gynecologic oncology is summarized. CATEGORY: 270: Health Services Research, 0.30 Outcomes research.

articles.title: Timing matters: Maternal stress and mental health symptoms from pregnancy to postpartum in shaping infant development.
articles.authors: Jarkas DA, Lalani S, Nausheen S et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal perceived stress, mental health, and physiological dysregulation during pregnancy can alter the intrauterine environment, shaping infant development through fetal programming processes. Nonetheless, few longitudinal studies in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) have jointly examined psychological and biological factors in relation to infant outcomes. This longitudinal study followed 146 Pakistani mother-infant dyads at early to mid-gestation (T1), mid- to late gestation (T2), and postpartum (T3). Maternal perceived stress, depressive symptoms, and social support were measured across all timepoints, whereas pregnancy-related anxiety and an allostatic load index of physiological dysregulation were measured during pregnancy. Infant developmental outcomes across five domains were assessed using the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ-3). Perceived stress at each timepoint, depressive symptoms at T1 and T3, and allostatic load at T1 were associated with poorer infant fine motor skills. Perceived stress at T3 was linked to poorer infant problem solving. Communication, gross motor, and personal-social skills in infants showed no associations. Higher T3 social support attenuated the relationship between prenatal perceived stress and fine motor skills. Moreover, an exploratory interaction showed that T1 allostatic load related to lower fine motor skills when T3 stress is high. Psychological and biological pathways may link maternal prenatal risk to infant fine motor development, with the postpartum environment possibly influencing whether prenatal vulnerabilities translate into delays. Interventions strengthening social resources and reducing postpartum stress may help disrupt intergenerational stress transmission in LMICs.

articles.title: ART utilization outcomes and trends for single and coupled male intended parents at a large fertility centre.
articles.authors: Patel K, Morse B, Sakkas D et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the updated outcomes and trends regarding assisted reproductive technology (ART) for single and coupled male intended parents (SCMIP) undergoing family building?
DESIGN: A retrospective analysis was performed at a single, academically affiliated infertility centre in the USA from 2014 to 2023. SCMIP that underwent an initial consultation, or initiated treatment with oocyte donation and/or embryo transfer via a gestational carrier were included. Demographic data, oocyte donation cycle outcomes, embryo transfer data, and pregnancy outcomes were obtained from the cohort of SCMIP.
RESULTS: In total, 395 SCMIP had an initial consultation during the study period and 149 (37.7%) (23 single males, 126 male couples) underwent treatment. The mean age at initial consultation was 38.1 years; data over time show a trend towards initiating care at a younger age. One hundred and thirty-three fresh oocyte retrieval cycles, 51 frozen oocyte warming cycles, and 222 embryo transfers were performed. The mean number of embryos obtained per cycle was 8.0 (SD 5.7) in fresh oocyte donation cycles versus 3.3 (SD 2.5) in frozen oocyte donation cycles. The live birth rate per embryo transfer was similar when comparing fresh oocyte donation with frozen oocyte donation (55.4% versus 52.8%, respectively; P = 0.86). The use of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy did not impact treatment success. Overall, after all cumulative embryo transfers via a gestational carrier in the study period, 87% of SCMIP achieved a live birth, with an average latency of 1.6 years between initial consultation and embryo transfer.
CONCLUSION: This large data set of male patients illustrates that, despite the significant time and costs associated with the process, SCMIP are increasingly accessing ART to achieve fatherhood with good success.

articles.title: Good embryos left behind: morphokinetic prioritization may penalize chromosomally competent embryos.
articles.authors: De Martin H, Sá EG, Lima AM et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Do morula compaction patterns and morphokinetic scoring systems accurately reflect chromosomal competence, or do they introduce bias that deprioritizes viable embryos?
DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included 1711 blastocysts derived from 611 intracytoplasmic sperm injection cycles cultured in a time-lapse system. Embryos were classified according to KIDScore, morula compaction pattern [fully compacted morulae (FCM) versus partially compacted morulae with cells excluded from compaction from the outset (Exc-PCM)], and the Blastocyst Fragmentation Indicator (BFI). Chromosomal status was assessed using next-generation sequencing.
RESULTS: Embryos derived from Exc-PCM exhibited significantly slower developmental kinetics (standardized developmental interval between the 5-cell and blastocyst stages: 0.780 versus -0.216 for FCM; P < 0.001), and were disproportionately classified into the lowest morphokinetic category, namely KIDScore C (73.9% versus 25.5% for FCM). Despite this, euploidy rates were similar between Exc-PCM and FCM embryos (43.7% versus 43.4%, respectively). In multivariable models, blastocyst fragmentation was most strongly associated with euploidy [adjusted OR (aOR) 0.04 for combined inner cell mass and trophectoderm fragmentation versus no fragmentation; P < 0.001]. After adjustment, Exc-PCM embryos showed higher odds of euploidy than FCM embryos (aOR 1.56; P = 0.008). Within KIDScore C embryos, those without fragmentation (rated as 'no fragmentation' on the BFI) retained relatively high euploidy rates (50.0-66.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: Morphokinetic scoring systems based on developmental speed may introduce bias in embryo prioritization, particularly affecting embryos derived from PCM. Structural integrity, rather than developmental timing, may better reflect chromosomal competence. Integrating structural assessment may improve embryo prioritization strategies.

articles.title: Exploring associations between testosterone and cardiovascular disease in females: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Alexander SE, Thompson EJ, Levelt E et al.
articles.abstract: There are increasingly recognised yet modestly understood sex-based differences in cardiovascular physiology, implicating endogenous sex hormones in cardiovascular disease aetiology. However, the role of androgens in female cardiovascular disease risk remains unclear. Therefore, this systematic review examined associations between endogenous testosterone concentrations and cardiovascular disease in females. MEDLINE complete, Embase and CINAHL complete were searched from 2000 to September 2025. Articles that investigated the association between endogenous plasma testosterone and cardiovascular disease in female adults were included. Quality assessment was performed using the QUALSYST tool. Of the 445 articles that underwent full-text screening, 28 met the inclusion criteria (n = 598,440), most (75%) of which had a low risk of bias. Findings for incident cardiovascular disease outcomes were inconsistent or absent. Substantial and systematic methodological heterogeneity across the evidence base precluded meta-analyses; only 10 of the 28 studies (35.7%) quantified testosterone using gold-standard liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, only seven (25%) excluded exogenous hormone (menopause hormone therapy or oral contraceptive) users, and disease definitions, exposure metrics (total, free, bioavailable, free androgen index) and statistical models varied widely. This review highlights substantial methodological heterogeneity throughout the evidence base. We provide four addressable areas which require resolution before definitive conclusions regarding the association between testosterone and cardiovascular disease in females can be made.

articles.title: How patients with advanced gynecological cancer perceive clinicians' attention to their values, wishes, and needs: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: de Vries S, Eilander R, Vervoort S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Understanding patients' values, wishes, and needs (VWN) is essential to guiding appropriate palliative care in home and hospital settings, thereby optimizing quality of life. This study aims to gain insight into the expectations and experiences of patients with advanced gynecological cancer in the palliative phase regarding clinicians' attention to their VWN throughout the illness trajectory.
METHODS: A qualitative study grounded in an interpretivist-constructivist approach was conducted from March 2024 to October 2024. Patients with advanced gynecological cancer were recruited from outpatient clinics at two hospitals in the Netherlands, using purposive sampling to achieve variation in age, diagnosis, and time since diagnosis. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Twenty-one patients (aged 39-86) participated; most were diagnosed with ovarian cancer (N = 17). Three key needs shaped patients' ability to express and discuss their VWN: 1) feeling recognized as a person, 2) being involved in the decision-making process in accordance with their preferences, and 3) receiving help and guidance in navigating the complex healthcare system. Participants hesitated to share non-physical issues, perceiving communication as primarily focused on the illness and medical treatment.
CONCLUSION: The findings highlight the importance of dialogues that create space for patients to express and discuss their VWN related to both the illness and broader aspects of living with advanced cancer, tailored to their individual preferences and need for support in navigating care. The way clinicians time and structure conversations is among the important factors shaping these opportunities.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: A systematic approach can support continuous attention to VWN throughout the illness trajectory, thereby guiding appropriate palliative care and optimizing quality of life. This approach requires explicit agreements on which clinician explores and monitors VWN, when this should occur, and how this is documented and transferred between settings.

articles.title: Association between menstrual-related health problems and mental disorders in male partners: A nested case-control study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Ishida R, Sasabuchi Y, Michihata N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, and premenstrual syndrome/premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMS/PMDD) are associated with psychological distress in affected women. However, evidence of their potential effects on the mental health of male partners is limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between menstrual-related health problems (MRHPs) and male partners' mental health.
METHODS: This nested case-control study was conducted using a large Japanese claims database from January 2005 to July 2024. Cases were men who were newly diagnosed with mental disorders and had female spouses. For each case, up to four controls without mental disorders were selected using risk-set sampling and matched for age, insurance status, calendar year, and registration month. Exposure was defined as the diagnosis of at least one MRHP (dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, or PMS/PMDD) in the female spouse within 1 year before the index date. Conditional logistic regression analysis and sensitivity and disease-specific analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: In total, 85,478 cases and 306,512 controls were identified. The presence of a spouse with an MRHP was associated with increased odds of a mental disorder in the male partner (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.09). These findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Disease-specific analyses revealed similar associations for endometriosis (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.11) and dysmenorrhea (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00-1.09). No significant association was observed for PMS/PMDD (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.96-1.25).
CONCLUSION: MRHPs in women, particularly endometriosis and dysmenorrhea, were modestly associated with newly diagnosed mental disorders in male partners.

articles.title: Era-specific interrupted and continuous barbed-suture myometrial closure for laparoscopic cesarean scar defect repair: A historical cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Nobuta Y, Tanaka Y, Kasei R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare 3-month postoperative residual myometrial thickness (RMT) and symptoms between two era-specific closure strategies for laparoscopic cesarean scar defect (CSD) repair, and to describe subsequent pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective historical cohort included 63 patients undergoing laparoscopic CSD repair from March 2021 to August 2025. Two-layer closure was performed in both the earlier-period interrupted closure group (EP group; n = 27) and the later-period continuous barbed-suture closure group (LP group; n = 36). The principal analysis compared 3-month postoperative RMT after adjustment for preoperative RMT. Changes in dysmenorrhea NRS and bleeding duration were secondary outcomes. Pregnancy within 18 months was exploratory among patients desiring pregnancy with at least 18 months of follow-up.
RESULTS: In the principal baseline-adjusted analysis, 3-month postoperative RMT was 2.48 mm greater in the EP group than in the LP group (95 % CI, 1.26-3.69; P < 0.001).
