Sensitivity analyses yielded smaller point estimates in the same direction. The reduction in dysmenorrhea NRS was greater in the EP group [median change, -3 (IQR, -6 to - 2) vs - 2 (-4 to 0); P = 0.017], whereas the change in bleeding duration did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.141). Pregnancy within 18 months occurred in 13/20 (65.0 %) and 10/15 (66.7 %) eligible patients, respectively; the small sample precluded meaningful between-group comparison.
CONCLUSION: Although residual confounding and concurrent changes in closure configuration, suture material/product, and treatment era preclude attribution to a specific component, the greater adjusted 3-month RMT observed in the EP group provides a hypothesis-generating anatomical signal that warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Predicting adverse maternal outcomes using antenatal and peripartum predictors: A multicenter machine learning study in low- and middle-income countries.
articles.authors: Soares MQ, de Camargo V, Silva IVD et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate machine learning models for composite maternal outcomes using antenatal care and peripartum predictors across eight low- and middle-income countries (LMIC) sites.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective longitudinal predictive modeling study using prospectively collected registry data.
METHODS: We analyzed 2014-2019 data from the Maternal and Newborn Health Registry (MNHR). Two models were developed: one using antenatal predictors and another adding peripartum predictors. Three tree-based ensemble algorithms were evaluated. Models were recalibrated by isotonic regression and assessed using calibration curves and decision curve analysis. Sensitivity analyses examined the contribution of intrapartum management variables and the exclusion of hospitalization from the composite outcome; leave-one-site-out (LOSO) validation assessed cross-site transportability.
RESULTS: The dataset included 334,553 women, and the composite adverse maternal outcome occurred in 12.8% of the temporal test set. XGBoost was selected for subsequent analyses. The antenatal model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.691 (95% CI 0.673-0.707) and the model with peripartum predictors 0.817 (95% CI 0.799-0.832), a difference of 0.126 (95% CI 0.123-0.130), of which 82% persisted after removing mode of delivery. After isotonic recalibration, both models were well calibrated (integrated calibration index ≤ 0.006), with unchanged discrimination, and both yielded greater net benefit than treat-all and treat-none strategies. Performance was heterogeneous across sites, with peripartum predictors improving discrimination in every site under LOSO.
CONCLUSIONS: The peripartum model may support peripartum surveillance and postpartum maternal risk stratification, but both models should undergo local evaluation and calibration before implementation.

articles.title: Optimization and application of a sensitive UPLC-MS/MS method for the quantitative determination of antibiotics in PM2.5.
articles.authors: Bei X, Liu J, Yao Q et al.
articles.abstract: The increasing occurrence of antibiotics in the environment has raised concerns about their atmospheric transport, human exposure, and potential contribution to antibiotic resistance dissemination. In this study, a sensitive ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed and validated for the simultaneous determination of 74 antibiotics from multiple classes in fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Key chromatographic and sample-preparation parameters were systematically optimized. Optimal performance was achieved using a T3 chromatographic column, mobile phases containing 0.1% (v/v) formic acid, Oasis HLB cartridges for solid-phase extraction, 0.1 mol/L disodium ethylenediaminetetraacetate, and methanol containing 1% (v/v) formic acid as the elution solvent. These conditions improved extraction efficiency, chromatographic performance, and quantitative sensitivity while reducing matrix-related interference. The validated method yielded accuracy values of 69.7%-131.7% and relative standard deviations of 1.0%-18.1% at three fortification levels, with estimated method quantification limits as low as 0.37 pg/m3. The method was applied to 29 ambient PM2.5 samples collected over 24-h periods in Beijing. Twenty-two antibiotics were detected above their respective method detection limits, with concentrations reaching 121.38 pg/m3. Seven compounds exhibited detection frequencies above 50%, and roxithromycin was detected in all samples. Oxytetracycline showed the highest mean concentration among the quantifiable results, at 14.48 pg/m3. Compared with previously reported methods that generally cover fewer antibiotic classes or focus on conventional environmental matrices, the proposed method enables sensitive and simultaneous determination of a broad range of antibiotics in the analytically challenging PM2.5 matrix. It therefore provides a comprehensive workflow for monitoring airborne antibiotics and supporting subsequent exposure and environmental-occurrence studies.

articles.title: Agricultural Waste-derived bio-sorbents used for the analysis of UV filters in sea water samples: An in-depth comparison with commercial sorbents.
articles.authors: Voutsas P, Perrucci M, Locatelli M et al.
articles.abstract: The development of sustainable sample preparation strategies is increasingly important for reducing the environmental footprint of analytical methods. In this study, waste-derived biosorbents were investigated as low-cost and green alternatives to commercial materials for the extraction of organic UV filters from sea water samples. Banana (BAN), lime, orange, and pomegranate peels, alongside with activated carbon derived from waste chestnut shells (ACCHE), were evaluated for the extraction efficiency of oxybenzone, enzacamene, avobenzone, octocrylene, and ethylhexyl salicylate. BAN and ACCHE exhibited the highest adsorption performance, with BAN selected for further optimization. A dispersive solid-phase extraction (d-SPE) procedure using BAN as sorbent, coupled with HPLC- DAD was developed and validated. The method demonstrated good linearity (R² > 0.99), relative recoveries of 84.4-106.8% in intra-day study and 88.8-103.6% in inter-day study, and satisfactory precision (RSD: 0.7-12.6%). Natural sorbents BAN and ACCHE were also compared with commercial SPE sorbents, Oasis HLB, LiChrolut RP-18, and Discovery C18 and showed comparable extraction performance. The optimised method was applied to seawater samples to confirm its suitability, with avobenzone and octocrylene detected at sub-ng/mL concentrations in samples collected during the summer season. Green analytical metrics (RAPI, ComplexMoGAPI, BAGI and VIGI) were utilised to further support the sustainability, practicality, robustness and innovation of the proposed method. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential use of banana peels as an effective waste-derived sorbent for the extraction and preconcentration of UV filters, offering an efficient alternative to conventional sorbents, while valorising biomass waste.

articles.title: Survivorship in gynecological cancers: addressing psychosocial and physical challenges.
articles.authors: Reid HW, Davidson BA
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gynecologic cancers represent 16% of cancers in women worldwide. With the advent of novel therapeutics, gynecologic cancer patients are increasingly experiencing longer disease-free intervals or cure. Optimizing survivorship care for patients can improve post-cancer quality of life.
AREAS COVERED: We searched PubMed and utilized OpenEvidence to identify citations relevant to gynecologic cancer survivorship. Gynecologic cancer has a distinct impact on sexual health and fertility. We characterize and explore interventions for fertility management, sexual dysfunction, and premature menopause. Physical concerns following systemic therapy, radiation, and surgery can have lasting effects into survivorship. We emphasize the most common post-operative chronic morbidities including ostomies and lymphedema, sequalae of pelvic radiation, and chronic health conditions due to immunotherapy and targeted therapy. Emotional and psychosocial aspects of survivorship both impact and are impacted by the physical and sexual domains of survivorship. We discuss mental health, financial, and interpersonal implications of survivorship and avenues to improve psychosocial outcomes after gynecologic cancer.
EXPERT OPINION: Survivorship in gynecologic cancer will continue to gain importance as the field makes gains in therapeutic treatments and early diagnosis and treatment. Subsequent research will need to focus on models of care implementation including virtual components and coordination across health systems.

articles.title: Uncovering Inequities: The Role of Social Determinants of Health in Hospitalized Adolescents and Young Adults With Heavy Menstrual Bleeding.
articles.authors: Carter-Febres M, Tarango C, Childress A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) is a common condition among adolescents and young adults (AYAs) and is the leading cause of iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in this population. Growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH) influence menstrual bleeding patterns, access to care, and treatment. However, no studies have comprehensively evaluated how SDOH impacts the full clinical course of AYAs hospitalized for HMB.
OBJECTIVES/HYPOTHESIS: This study aims to evaluate how factors such as race, ethnicity, geographic location, and socioeconomic status (SES) impact the severity of anemia at presentation, inpatient evaluation and management, and post-discharge subspecialty follow-up for AYAs hospitalized for HMB.
METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed for AYAs admitted to our medical center for anemia secondary to HMB from January 2008 to January 2026. SES was characterized using the Community Deprivation Index (CDI) and Child Opportunity Index (COI). Patients were categorized into three SDOH groups: Black non-Hispanic English-speaking (BNHES), White non-Hispanic English-speaking (WNHES), and other race, ethnicity, and/or language (OREL).
RESULTS: A total of 271 admissions were included. BNHES individuals had lower Hgb and MCV than WNHES individuals (6.6 vs. 7.8 g/dL and 74.3 vs. 82.2 fL; p < 0.05 and <0.005, respectively); however, they did not have a higher transfusion burden, iron administration rate, or longer hospitalizations. BNHES individuals resided in neighborhoods with greater socioeconomic disadvantage and lived significantly closer to the hospital yet presented at an older age and further from menarche. CDI and COI scores did not independently correlate with admission Hgb or MCV.
CONCLUSIONS: BNHES AYA females hospitalized for HMB presented with more severe IDA and at a greater interval from menarche despite proximity to the hospital, suggesting that complex SDOH factors, including SES, led to progressive anemia at presentation. Standardizing laboratory testing, bleeding disorder (BDO) screening, and the use of hormonal and iron therapies in the outpatient setting could potentially reduce disparities in care among these populations.

articles.title: Impact of gestational diabetes mellitus and assisted reproductive technology on maternal and neonatal outcomes in twin pregnancies: A multicentre retrospective study in China.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.authors: Zhou LY, Wu XB, Wang YQ et al.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Twin pregnancies are inherently at high risk of maternal and neonatal complications. Assisted reproductive technology (ART) and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are both common in this population, but it remains unclear whether their coexistence is associated with excess risk beyond their individual associations.
METHODS: In this multicentre retrospective cohort of 4522 liveborn twin pregnancies across three hospitals in China, pregnancies were categorized according to mode of conception and GDM status. Generalized linear mixed models were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with hospital included as a random effect. Multiplicative and additive interaction analyses were performed to assess whether the joint associations of ART and GDM with maternal and neonatal outcomes exceeded their individual associations.
RESULTS: The overall prevalence of GDM was 22.2%, with 30.0% in ART-conceived women and 14.0% in spontaneously conceived (SC) women. Compared to SC twin pregnancies without GDM, ART-conceived twin pregnancies with GDM showed significantly increased risks of placental adhesion (aOR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.03-2.33), caesarean section (aOR: 2.72; 95% CI: 1.21-6.15), preterm birth <37 weeks (aOR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.15-1.78) and low birth weight (aOR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.01-1.60). Notably, statistically significant multiplicative (aOR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.11-2.80) and additive (relative excess risk due to interaction: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.14-0.96) interactions between GDM and ART were observed for preterm birth <34 weeks, whereas no statistically significant interactions were detected for the other examined outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Twin pregnancies with both ART conception and GDM had higher risks of several adverse outcomes than spontaneously conceived pregnancies without GDM. However, evidence of statistical interaction between ART and GDM was limited to preterm birth <34 weeks, suggesting that the excess risk associated with their coexistence may be outcome-specific. These findings may help refine risk stratification and prenatal surveillance in twin pregnancies.

articles.title: A Structured Approach to Teaching Volumetric Fetal Echocardiography Using Fetal Intelligent Navigation Echocardiography (FINE).
articles.authors: Giubilato AF, Bravo-Valenzuela NJ, Albrecht MEM et al.
articles.abstract: Fetal volumetric echocardiography using Fetal Intelligent Navigation Echocardiography (FINE) enables automated reconstruction of standardized echocardiographic views from a cardiac volume dataset. However, automation of navigation does not eliminate dependence on technically adequate acquisition or the need for operator quality control. We describe the PROBE Educational Workflow, a structured educational approach comprising five sequential steps-Position, Refine, Obtain, Build and Evaluate-designed to organize the teaching of the process from preparation of the two-dimensional image and acquisition of the Spatio-Temporal Image Correlation (STIC) volume to construction of the navigation and systematic assessment of the reconstructed views. PROBE was conceived as an iterative workflow: when the quality of a step is considered insufficient, the operator should identify the probable origin of the problem and return to the corresponding step before proceeding. The workflow does not modify the FINE algorithm and does not constitute a diagnostic protocol; its purpose is to provide a simple and reproducible cognitive framework for technical training in volumetric fetal echocardiography. Future studies should assess its impact on competency acquisition, volume quality, reproducibility and training efficiency.

articles.title: A competitive PDLIM1-USP14 axis destabilizes ACTN4 to disturb the invasive homeostasis of trophoblast in preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Zhang C, Zhang X, Chen R et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by insufficient extravillous trophoblast (EVT) invasion, but the cytoskeletal mechanisms restraining EVT motility remain unclear. TMT-based placental proteomics identified the cytoskeletal adaptor PDLIM1 as markedly upregulated in PE. In primary trophoblasts and cell lines, PDLIM1 depletion remodeled the actin cytoskeleton and enhanced migration and invasion, whereas trophoblast-restricted Pdlim1 overexpression impaired trophoblast invasion and placental development in mice. Mechanistically, PDLIM1 bounds the rod domain of α-actinin-4 (ACTN4) and competitively displaced USP14, limiting ACTN4 deubiquitination and shifting ACTN4 toward RNF38-associated K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover. Importantly, placenta-targeted chondroitin sulfate A-binding nanoparticles delivering Pdlim1 short hairpin RNA (shRNA) alleviated PE-like maternal and fetal phenotypes in mice. Collectively, these findings define a PDLIM1-USP14-ACTN4 proteostatic axis controlling trophoblast invasive homeostasis and identify PDLIM1 as a potential therapeutic target in PE.

articles.title: Study design of the phase III ADELA trial of elacestrant with or without everolimus in ESR1-mutated ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after progression on endocrine therapy plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor.
articles.authors: Pérez-García JM, Llombart-Cussac A, López-Miranda E et al.
articles.abstract: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT06382948; EU Clinical Trials identifier is EUCT 2024-512926-27-00.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of 5-day administration of topotecan combined with bevacizumab for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer: a multicenter retrospective analysis.
articles.authors: Takatori E, Shoji T, Jo A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of topotecan and bevacizumab is a treatment option for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. However, the efficacy and safety of the standard 5-day topotecan regimen in real-world practice remain unclear. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes of 5-day topotecan plus bevacizumab in a heavily pretreated population.
METHODS: This two-institution retrospective analysis included patients with platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancers treated with a 5-day topotecan plus bevacizumab regimen. Progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), antitumor efficacy, and treatment-related toxicities were assessed. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify the prognostic factors.
RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were included. The median number of prior chemotherapy regimens was 3, and 85% had previously received bevacizumab. The median PFS and OS were 4.0 and 11.0 months, respectively. No clinical variables were significantly associated with PFS in univariate analysis; however, histological subtype was associated with PFS in the multivariable model. The objective response rate was 18.5%, and the disease control rate was 57.4%. Hematologic toxicities were frequent and severe: grade ≥ 3 neutropenia occurred in 81.5% of patients, and grade ≥ 3 thrombocytopenia occurred in 37.0%. Gastrointestinal perforation occurred in two patients.
CONCLUSIONS: The combination of 5-day topotecan and bevacizumab showed limited clinical benefits and substantial hematologic toxicity in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. This regimen may not provide an optimal balance between efficacy and tolerability, underscoring the need for prospective studies to identify patients who may benefit from and optimize treatment sequencing in this era of prior bevacizumab and PARP inhibitor exposure.

articles.title: Brain-bladder network disruption in urinary incontinence: subtype-specific patterns and targeted neuromodulation.
articles.authors: Dong Y, Zou Z, Cao L
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Urinary incontinence (UI) is a highly prevalent condition, affecting more than 400 million adults worldwide. The three main subtypes-stress, urgency, and mixed-exhibit markedly different clinical features and treatment responses that cannot be fully explained by peripheral mechanisms alone.
METHODS: In this narrative review, we summarise evidence suggesting that UI subtypes are associated with distinct patterns of disruption to brain networks.
RESULTS: We propose that the prefrontal cortex-anterior cingulate cortex-insula-periaqueductal grey circuit constitutes a core brain-bladder network and that different UI subtypes may reflect disruption to different nodes within this network. Urgency UI has been associated with reduced prefrontal-cingulate connectivity, which may impair top-down inhibition. Stress UI has been associated with reduced insular and emotion-regulation activation during bladder filling. Post-stroke UI appears to involve failure to recruit the salience network. Mixed UI is hypothesised to show combined deficits. Neuroimaging evidence from functional MRI, PET and SPECT scans is consistent with this network-based subtyping. These distinct patterns suggest differentiated candidate intervention strategies: prefrontal-targeted neuromodulation for urgency UI, insula-focused approaches for stress UI and salience network restoration for post-stroke UI, all of which remain investigational at present.
CONCLUSION: This framework conceptualises UI as a family of brain-bladder communication disorders and generates testable hypotheses for subtype-specific neuromodulation; its clinical utility requires prospective, longitudinal and interventional validation. It also identifies future research priorities for network-based diagnostics and personalised intervention.

articles.title: miR-493-3p mediates sex-specific cardiac hypertrophy induced by maternal high-fat diet in offspring via PI3K/AKT pathway.
articles.authors: Zhang H, Cheng P, Guo L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Maternal high-fat diet (HFD) exposure induces sex-dependent cardiac hypertrophy in adult offspring, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role of miR-493-3p in maternal HFD-induced cardiac hypertrophy and its potential association with estrogen regulation and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling.
METHODS: Pregnant rats were fed either a standard chow diet or HFD (60% kcal fat). Hearts from adult offspring were analyzed by miRNA sequencing, real-time RT-PCR, and western blotting. Ovariectomy (OVX) and sham operations were performed in adult female offspring. Neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (NRCMs) were treated with estrogen or transfected with miR-493-3p mimic or inhibitor, with or without angiotensin II (Ang II) stimulation.
RESULTS: miR-493-3p was the most markedly upregulated miRNA in the hearts of HFD-exposed male offspring. Maternal HFD increased cardiac miR-493-3p expression in adult males but decreased it in females. OVX increased cardiac miR-493-3p expression in female offspring, and HFD combined with OVX further enhanced this increase. Consistently, estrogen suppressed miR-493-3p expression in NRCMs. miR-493-3p overexpression increased cardiomyocyte surface area, upregulated Nppa and Myh7, and reduced Myh6, whereas miR-493-3p inhibition attenuated Ang II-induced hypertrophic responses. KEGG analysis indicated enrichment of predicted miR-493-3p targets in the PI3K/AKT pathway. Maternal HFD also increased PI3K p85, PI3K p110, p-AKT, and p-mTOR protein expression in adult male offspring, but decreased p-AKT/AKT and p-mTOR/mTOR in adult female offspring.
CONCLUSION: Maternal HFD-induced miR-493-3p upregulation may promote cardiac hypertrophy through PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation, whereas estrogen-mediated suppression of miR-493-3p may contribute to protection in female offspring.

articles.title: Evaluation of surgical outcomes and costs during the learning curve in robotic gynecologic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Sen S, Sen FG
articles.abstract: To quantify the potential surgical and financial benefits associated with progression along the learning curve in robotic gynecologic surgery. Observational studies comparing earlier and later cases of the same robotic gynecologic procedure were identified from nine bibliographic sources. Single-reviewer preselection preceded two-reviewer assessment. Continuous outcomes from chronological or experience-period comparisons were pooled using REML random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp intervals; outcome-derived comparisons were analyzed separately. Complications and reported hospital costs were summarized descriptively, while resource use was valued in separate exploratory models. Appraisal used the JBI cohort checklist and adapted GRADE. Registration followed searching (INPLASY2026100011). Twenty-one reports contributed: 19 provided 25 time comparisons (1,305 phase observations); two were economic-only. Across 13 primary reports (923 observations), later procedures were 31 min shorter (95% CI 16-46; I²=65.3%; very low certainty), a 19.6% reduction. Four of these yielded - 10.4 min per 10 cases (95% CI -25.0 to 4.2). Blood-loss (-6.3 mL) and hospital-stay (-0.08 days) differences remained uncertain (very low certainty); complication findings varied. Three programs reported lower hospital costs: mean reductions of $2,222 and $4,457 and a median difference of $83 (2025 USD). Exploratory resource valuation estimated -$1,068 per case (95% CI -$3,747 to $1,610). Later phases were associated with approximately 31 minutes shorter operative time, withoperative minutes valued using an external reference input of $28.43 per minute. Available evidence didnot establish clear reductions in blood loss or hospital stay, while heterogeneous definitions precluded apooled complication estimate. The time and personal financial investment required for surgeons to reachthis stage remains an important separate cost requiring prospective evaluation.

articles.title: The association between labor complications and posttraumatic stress symptoms among women with low social support.
articles.authors: Bowers K, Ammerman RT, Ding L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trauma during childbirth can lead to childbirth-related posttraumatic stress disorder (CB-PTSD), affecting maternal attachment and infant behavioral health. This study examined the association between birth complications and posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) at one month postpartum in a cohort of low-income women enrolled in a home visiting program.
METHODS: Pregnancy conditions (e.g., preeclampsia, gestational diabetes) and labor complications (e.g., prolonged labor, fetal distress) were self-reported at the 1-month postnatal visit. Sociodemographic and psychosocial risk factors were assessed prenatally and postnatally. PTSS was measured using the Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Checklist-Civilian (PCL-C) at baseline and one month postpartum. PTSS was analyzed continuously and using a cutoff score of ≥14, indicating risk for clinically elevated symptoms and possible PTSD. Linear regression assessed associations between complications and PTSS, adjusting for covariates.
RESULTS: Of 212 participants, 22.6% scored ≥14 on the PCL-C at one month. Labor complications were associated with higher PTSS risk (33.3% vs. 19% without complications). A significant interaction was found between labor complications and maternal social support (p=0.03); the association was significant only among mothers with low social support (β=4.32, 95% CI: 1.93, 6.71).
INTERPRETATION: Labor complications, but not pregnancy conditions, were linked to increased PTSS, particularly among mothers with limited social support. Social support and potentially traumatic events emerged as factors that may be important for future intervention research seeking to prevent or reduce PTSS in the postpartum period.

articles.title: A homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the C-terminal of Tdrd5 causing early spermiogenesis arrest and azoospermia in mice.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Xie M, Zhang Y, Zu C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: TDRD5 is a germ cell-specific RNA granule component that plays a crucial role in chromatoid body organization, piRNA biogenesis, and spermiogenesis. We previously identified a homozygous C-terminal nonsense mutation in TDRD5 in an infertile patient. While in vitro studies suggested the production of a stable truncated protein, the physiological consequences of this specific C-terminal truncation in vivo remain unknown.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to elucidate the in vivo pathogenicity of the TDRD5 C-terminal nonsense mutation and its underlying mechanism using a mouse model.
METHODS: We generated a Tdrd5 knock-in mouse carrying a premature termination mutation (Q764X) at the corresponding C-terminal region of murine TDRD5 using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. The reproductive phenotype was assessed through fertility testing, histological analysis (H&E, PAS), and evaluation of apoptosis (TUNEL). The expression of TDRD5 protein was assessed by immunoblot analysis, and retrotransposon activity was examined by co-staining for LINE1 and the DNA damage marker γH2AX.
RESULTS: Homozygous Tdrd5Q764X/Q764X male mice exhibited infertility, reduced testis size, and azoospermia. Histological examination revealed spermiogenic arrest at the round spermatid stage with defective acrosome biogenesis. Contrary to in vitro findings, immunoblot analysis demonstrated the complete absence of both full-length and truncated TDRD5 proteins in Tdrd5Q764X/Q764X testes. In addition, the mutant testes exhibited aberrant LINE1 upregulation, increased γH2AX signals in spermatocytes, and elevated germ cell apoptosis, thereby phenocopying the defects observed in Tdrd5-/- mice.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that the C-terminal nonsense mutation causes a loss-of-function phenotype in vivo. This study highlighted the indispensable role of the TDRD5 C-terminus in maintaining protein stability and ensuring successful spermiogenesis in mice.

articles.title: Step-specific temporal patterns in robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy: an exploratory CUSUM analysis.
articles.authors: Takahashi A, Tanaka Y, Yoneoka Y et al.
articles.abstract: Learning curves for robot-assisted sacrocolpopexy (RSC) are commonly evaluated using total operative or console time, although RSC consists of multiple technically distinct steps. We explored step-specific temporal efficiency patterns using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. We retrospectively analyzed the first 29 consecutive RSC procedures performed by a single surgeon with approximately 100 prior robotic procedures and experience in robotic surgical instruction. Seven procedural steps were timed using prespecified video landmarks. CUSUM curves and Spearman correlations with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were used to describe temporal efficiency patterns. The console-time CUSUM peak was used only for a descriptive post hoc early-versus-late illustration and was not treated as an independently validated learning transition. Median operative and console times were 183 and 139 min, respectively. Neither total operative time nor total console time showed a significant monotonic relationship with case sequence, although both mean-centered CUSUM curves reached their maximum positive deviation at case 14. Step-specific temporal patterns varied substantially. Hysterectomy, anterior and posterior mesh suturing, and peritoneal closure showed negative correlations with case sequence, whereas bladder dissection showed the opposite trend and a later CUSUM peak. Early-versus-late comparisons were descriptive and did not independently validate a transition point. RSC demonstrated heterogeneous step-specific temporal efficiency patterns that were not captured by total console time alone. Because the global time trends were flat, the phase cutpoint was data-derived, and technical quality and safety were not assessed, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of proficiency or training effectiveness.

articles.title: Recalled Childhood and Familial Urinary Incontinence History as Correlates of Urinary Incontinence Occurrence, Severity, and Phenotype in Women: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Saylam Dönmez K, Derim Yeğen B, Yılmaz Altay A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: To determine the prevalence, severity, and phenotypes of urinary incontinence (UI) among adult women and to identify factors associated with UI occurrence, severity, and phenotype, with particular emphasis on recalled childhood UI and family history of UI.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 849 women. We assessed UI using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form. Multivariable Poisson regression identified factors associated with UI prevalence; multinomial logistic regression evaluated factors associated with UI severity and phenotype.
RESULTS: Overall UI prevalence was 42.6%. Increasing age (aPR 1.018, 95% CI 1.007-1.030), body mass index (BMI) (aPR 1.026, 95% CI 1.014-1.039), recalled childhood UI (aPR 1.57, 95% CI 1.34-1.84), family history of UI (aPR 1.64, 95% CI 1.43-1.88), vaginal delivery (aPR 1.79, 95% CI 1.22-2.63), and both vaginal and cesarean delivery (aPR 1.64, 95% CI 1.09-2.47) were independently associated with UI prevalence. Older age, higher BMI, parity, childhood and family UI history were also associated with greater UI severity. Recalled childhood UI and family UI history were strong predictors across all severity categories. In phenotype analyses, childhood and family UI history were independently associated with urge, stress, and mixed UI. Vaginal delivery was associated specifically with stress UI, whereas cesarean delivery was not associated with UI phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: Recalled childhood UI was consistently associated with adult UI occurrence, severity, and phenotype. Age, obesity, family history, and vaginal delivery further contribute to UI risk, with vaginal birth predominantly influencing stress UI.

articles.title: Exploratory Evaluation of Mirabegron-Associated Changes in Bladder Remodeling and Cell-Death-Related Markers in a Rat Model of Bladder Outlet Obstruction.
articles.authors: Chen L, Yang J, Yang J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Mirabegron, a selective β3-adrenoceptor agonist, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in regulating bladder function. This study investigated representative markers related to ferroptosis, apoptosis, pyroptosis-related inflammatory signaling, and autophagy-related responses in bladder outlet obstruction (BOO)-induced bladder dysfunction, and evaluated the protective effects of mirabegron.
METHODS: This study was conducted in two phases. In the first phase, 24 rats were randomized into control, sham-operated, and BOO groups to assess representative cell-death-related markers in bladder smooth muscle. In the second phase, 32 rats were assigned to four groups: sham-operated, BOO, BOO + vehicle (BOO+M(-)), and BOO + mirabegron treatment (BOO+M(+)). Subcutaneous osmotic pumps were implanted to deliver mirabegron (0.3 mg/kg/h) or vehicle.
RESULTS: Bladder outlet obstruction was associated with significant alterations in representative cell-death-related markers in bladder smooth muscle, including ferroptosis- and apoptosis-related markers, as well as exploratory pyroptosis- and autophagy-related markers. In the treatment phase, mirabegron treatment was associated with partial restoration of GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, reduced expression of cleaved PARP and cleaved caspase-3, decreased collagen deposition in bladder tissue, and lower serum creatinine levels from 94.37 ± 29.95 μmol/l to 58.78 ± 19.49 μmol/l (p < 0.01). These findings indicate improvements in ferroptosis-related antioxidant defense markers, apoptosis-related markers, bladder remodeling, and downstream renal outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that mirabegron treatment was associated with partial normalization of ferroptosis-related antioxidant defense markers and attenuation of apoptosis-related changes, together with reduced bladder remodeling and improved downstream renal histological and biochemical outcomes in rats with BOO.

articles.title: Appalachian residents' perceptions of abortion issues in their communities prior to the repeal of Roe v Wade.
articles.authors: Ely GE, Auerbach S, Amen Z et al.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate Appalachian residents' perceptions about abortion access in their communities and to examine the relationship between these perceptions and state-level abortion restrictions, prior to the Dobbs v Jackson court case that repealed Roe v Wade. Residents of the Appalachian region of the United States, between 18 and 49 years of age, were recruited using targeted Facebook advertisements (N = 608). Participants completed an anonymous electronic survey inquiring about perceptions of abortion and accessibility in their communities. Relationships between abortion perceptions, sample characteristics, and state-level abortion restrictions were analyzed. Participants reported that abortion was perceived as unaffordable, geographically inaccessible, of unknown legality, and as occurring uncommonly in their communities. Findings suggest perceptions were informed by religious engagement, shame, and fear of judgment from others. Income, rurality, religious engagement, and hostility of state-level abortion policies were each associated with select abortion perceptions. Results point to opportunities for social workers to engage in abortion policy advocacy and community education in the Appalachian region that would help improve abortion accessibility in regional communities, including those that are rural.

articles.title: Variability in Postoperative Voiding Practices Across Gynecologic Services: Opportunities for Standardized Protocols in Outpatient Care.
articles.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
articles.authors: Galang C, Chang E, Dumlao M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Delayed trial of void (TOV) after outpatient gynecologic surgery can prolong recovery and delay discharge. Despite its importance, no standardized voiding protocol exists, leading to inconsistent practices across general gynecology (GYNE), urogynecology (UROGYNE), and gynecologic oncology (GYNEONC) services. This project characterized variation in postoperative TOV management and identified factors associated with time to first void to inform future standardized, risk-stratified protocol development.
DESIGN: A single-center retrospective review of outpatient gynecologic surgery was conducted using quality improvement methodology.
METHODS: Patients undergoing outpatient gynecologic procedures at a tertiary hospital between August 2023 and August 2024 were included (n = 185). Descriptive statistics compared patient characteristics, operative factors, and postoperative bladder management practices. Multivariable linear regression evaluated time to first void, adjusting for age and body mass index (BMI). Secondary outcomes included post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay, retrofill practices, and physician-directed voiding criteria. Exploratory sensitivity analyses using nested linear models evaluated the influence of operative duration, intraoperative narcotic administration, and retrofill volumes.
FINDINGS: Postoperative bladder management varied across services, including retrofill practices, voiding criteria, post-void residual thresholds, and the number of permitted voiding attempts. After adjustment for age and BMI, time to first void attempt was 44.7 minutes longer in GYNE patients and 57.8 minutes longer in GYNEONC patients than in UROGYNE patients. Further adjustment for operative duration and intraoperative narcotic administration attenuated between-service differences, suggesting that operative complexity accounted for part, but not all, of the observed variation; most variance in time to first void remained unexplained. PACU length of stay was similarly prolonged across all services (GYNE 306.7 ± 140.6 minutes, GYNEONC 314.8 ± 136.1 minutes, UROGYNE 303.9 ± 109.5 minutes) despite differences in TOV timing.
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation in postoperative TOV management existed across outpatient gynecologic surgical services. Although differences in time to first void were partially explained by operative duration and intraoperative narcotic administration, meaningful variability persisted in retrofill practices, void timing,…

articles.title: Dietary Pattern Modeling Reveals Gaps in Meal Kits in Meeting Nutritional Goals of Gestational Diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of nutrition education and behavior
articles.authors: Dickman A, Taylor CA, Ilic S
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test whether a selection of commercial meal kits meets pregnancy and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) nutrient goals using a dietary pattern modeling approach.
METHODS: Cross-sectional modeling of 64 theoretical daily patterns was performed using 12 randomly selected recipes (4 breakfasts, 4 lunches, and 4 dinners) drawn from a database of 1,220 recipes across 10 US commercial meal kit providers. Nutritional adequacy for pregnancy and GDM was assessed via Dietary Reference Intakes, and overall diet quality was assessed via the Healthy Eating Index 2020.
RESULTS: Modeled intakes produced an average Healthy Eating Index score of 55.4 out of 100, indicating suboptimal diet quality. Fiber, vitamin D, iron, and calcium were consistently below the recommended levels. Carbohydrate content often exceeded GDM targets, and no recipes included whole grains.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Commercial meal kits did not meet pregnancy or GDM-specific nutrient goals. Dietary pattern modeling can identify gaps and guide the optimization of meal kits for future interventions.

articles.title: Lessons learned from pregnant women's experiences with COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil: A qualitative study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Maudonnet B, Fesshaye B, Schue JL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore pregnant women's perceptions of COVID-19 vaccination and factors influencing their decision making.
METHODS: This qualitative study, part of a multinational project led by WHO and Johns Hopkins University, was conducted in Brazil between August and December 2023. In-depth interviews were conducted with 25 pregnant women across all three trimesters of pregnancy and 25 postpartum women, exploring their knowledge, attitudes, and decision making regarding COVID-19. Data were analyzed thematically through an iterative process until saturation, examining confidence levels, vaccination history, risk perceptions, fears of adverse events, and the influence of healthcare professionals. Based on these dimensions, distinct profiles of vaccine hesitancy were developed.
RESULTS: Five profiles of COVID-19 vaccine attitudes during pregnancy were identified among 50 pregnant and postpartum women: trust in vaccination during pregnancy (n = 23), characterized by confidence in vaccine safety, science, and protection; need for external encouragement to vaccinate (n = 6), mainly influenced by healthcare professionals or family; waning interest in additional doses (n = 6), associated with low perceived risk, prior infection, or pandemic fatigue; concerns about vaccine safety or side effects (n = 7), often linked to previous adverse reactions and insufficient information; and concerns about vaccine effects on pregnancy or the fetus (n = 8), contributing to delayed or refused vaccination during pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: Despite overall high vaccine acceptance in Brazil, pregnancy introduced hesitations related to fetal safety, communication gaps, and trust in health information. The identification of five distinct profiles highlights lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic and reinforces the need for targeted communication strategies and consistent healthcare guidance to support maternal immunization in future public health scenarios.

articles.title: Advancing Evidence Generation in Small, Diverse, Understudied Population.
articles.authors: Mitra A, Dosne AG, Steinbach D et al.
articles.abstract: Many clinically important patient groups remain systematically underrepresented in drug development. Among these are patients with severe or time-varying organ dysfunction, pregnant and lactating women, children with ultrarare diseases, and people from socioeconomically or geographically underserved communities. Traditional clinical trials frequently exclude such groups. Little direct evidence is generated as a result, leaving benefit-risk and dosing decisions uncertain and trial findings poorly generalizable to the patients who will ultimately receive the drug. No single method closes this gap. This review argues that progress instead comes from integration, combining model-informed drug development, registries and real-world data, external and virtual controls, Bayesian borrowing, and patient-centric trial designs into a coherent totality-of-evidence package. These tools are maturing from a role that supplements clinical data toward one that can, in defined settings, partially replace it. The appropriate approach may differ by population. For example, (1) mechanistic modeling and exposure prediction for organ replacement therapy/changing organ function or from the altered maternal-fetal-infant physiology that makes prospective studies impractical; (2) registry-based external controls and natural history data where patients are too few to randomize; and (3) decentralized, partnership-driven designs to reach populations that structural barriers would otherwise exclude. Three case studies (dose justification across hepatic and renal impairment, evidence generation in women of childbearing potential with chronic autoimmune disease, and a registry-anchored ultrarare pediatric program) illustrated these approaches. Mapped to evolving regulatory frameworks, these strategies can deliver population-appropriate dosing at approval rather than through postmarketing commitments, accelerating equitable access to safe and effective therapies.

articles.title: Prognostic Analysis of Combined Laparoscopic-Hysteroscopic Surgery for Tubal Factor Infertility: A Retrospective Study in Chinese Women.
articles.authors: Zhong L
articles.abstract: To examine the clinical outcomes of tubal factor infertility (TFI) following combined laparoscopic-hysteroscopic surgery and evaluate the time to natural pregnancy, this retrospective study analyzed clinical data from TFI patients with isolated tubal obstruction treated at a Women and Children's Health facility in China. Tubal condition was evaluated using the Gerard Mage scoring system based on the extent of obstruction, integrity of the fimbrial mucosa, and tubal wall quality, with damage classified into four stages (I-IV). Among 174 patients with bilateral fallopian tube obstruction, the overall tubal recanalization rate was 89.7%. Recanalization rates were highest in stages I and II (95.8% and 94.1%, respectively) and lowest in stage IV (80%). Intrauterine pregnancy rates decreased with increasing tubal damage severity, and no pregnancies occurred in stage IV patients (P < 0.05). Preoperative hysterosalpingography showed a tubal obstruction rate of 59.2%, with 95% agreement between diagnostic and surgical findings. The sensitivity and specificity were 94.4% and 86%, respectively. Factors affecting tubal recanalization included early age at first sexual intercourse, pelvic inflammatory disease, history of uterine procedures, tubal ectopic pregnancy treatment, pelvic or abdominal surgeries, and multiple sexual partners (P < 0.05). These findings demonstrate that increasing tubal damage severity is associated with reduced recanalization and pregnancy rates, along with higher infertility and ectopic pregnancy risk.

articles.title: Germ traCre and Germbow: Cre-Based Transgenic Lineage Tracing Systems to Examine Early Gametogenesis and PGC Germline Contributions in Zebrafish.
articles.authors: Pahima M, Marlow FL
articles.abstract: Studies to date on reproductive development and gametogenesis in zebrafish have been limited by the availability of methods to visualize the developing germline. These include transient labeling approaches, such as injection of DNA or RNA encoding germline-localizing markers, or transgenic approaches that leverage germline promoters that are activated only after gonad formation. Degradation of injected elements before germline-specific zygotic promoter activation leaves a period when the early germ cells cannot be reliably labeled and tracked. To bridge this gap, Germ traCre and Germbow were developed: two Cre-based transgenic lineage tracing systems which provide the earliest inducible and targeted long-term labeling of germ cell precursors -primordial germ cells (PGCs) - and their progeny. It was recently demonstrated that the Germ traCre and Germbow systems are effective for investigating PGC differentiation and the establishment of the pre-gametic germline. This cell fate transition is critical for the formation of a functional vertebrate gonad but has largely been inaccessible. Using these systems, we lineage-traced early PGC contributions to the gonad and found that PGCs give rise to a more diverse repertoire of germ cell progeny than anticipated. It was further demonstrated that individual PGC contributions affect ovarian reserve composition and lifelong reproductive potential. Together, these systems permit access to gametogenesis from the earliest germ cell differentiation events to gamete maturation, making them useful systems for germline lineage tracing that can be applied to any stage of reproductive life. This article presents comprehensive protocols for clonal lineage tracing of zebrafish PGCs and their progeny in the developmental day 16 (d16) juvenile zebrafish gonad, as well as multispectral labeling and analysis of ovarian reserve composition in adult females. This study demonstrates how to use the systems and provide methods for staining, dissection, and imaging of the juvenile zebrafish germline.

articles.title: Causal effects of physical activity and sedentary behaviors on hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.authors: Zhang C, Song W, Luo C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) are major causes of maternal and perinatal morbidity. While observational studies suggest physical activity may reduce HDP risk, confounding and reverse causality limit causal inference.
METHODS: We conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization study using genetic instruments for 11 activity traits from UK Biobank and outcome data for gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia from FinnGen.
RESULTS: Light do-it-yourself (DIY) activities were associated with lower risks of gestational hypertension (β[Formula: see text]  = -3.56, P = 0.002) and pre-eclampsia (β = -3.54, P = 0.029). Aerobic exercise was associated with lower pre-eclampsia risk (β = -3.56, P = 0.017). No significant associations were found for vigorous activity, moderate-to-vigorous activity, or the three specific sedentary behaviors examined (time spent using a computer, time spent watching television, and time spent driving).
CONCLUSION: This study provides causal evidence that specific physical activities confer protection against HDPs. Genetically predicted light DIY activities were associated with lower risks of both gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia, while aerobic exercise was associated with lower pre-eclampsia risk. The three sedentary behaviors examined showed no causal associations. These findings highlight light-intensity domestic activities and aerobic exercise as accessible strategies for HDP prevention in prenatal care.

articles.title: Quality of Life, Immune Function, and Treatment Outcomes with Astragalus Injection in Endometrial Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Ye X, Zhang Y, Feng X et al.
articles.abstract: Adjuvant chemotherapy with paclitaxel and carboplatin is commonly used for high-risk postoperative endometrial cancer but is associated with significant toxicity. Astragalus Injection has immunomodulatory properties, yet clinical evidence regarding its adjunctive role remains limited. This retrospective cohort study compared quality of life, immune parameters, exploratory serum biomarkers, performance status, and adverse events between patients receiving paclitaxel-carboplatin with or without adjunctive Astragalus Injection. A total of 136 patients treated between January 2022 and March 2023 were included in an observation group (chemotherapy plus Astragalus Injection, n = 68) or control group (chemotherapy alone, n = 68). Treatment consisted of six 21-day cycles. Outcomes included European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) scores, CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T-cell counts, CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio, squamous cell carcinoma antigen (SCC-Ag), cytokeratin 19 fragment (CYFRA21-1), adverse events, and Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) scores. Changes in all five EORTC QLQ-C30 functional domain scores were significantly greater in the observation group than in the control group (P < 0.001). The increase in CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio was also significantly greater in the observation group (P < 0.001). SCC-Ag and CYFRA21-1 decreased more substantially in the observation group (P = 0.003 and P < 0.001, respectively). The incidences of grade ≥ 2 gastrointestinal toxicity (14.71% vs. 32.35%, P = 0.015) and bone marrow suppression (11.76% vs. 27.94%, P = 0.019) were lower in the observation group. KPS improvement was greater in the observation group (P < 0.001). Adjunctive Astragalus Injection was associated with improvements in quality of life, immune parameters, performance status, selected chemotherapy-related adverse events, and exploratory serum biomarkers. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: The Interleukin-33/Growth Stimulation Expressed Gene 2 Signaling Axis in Transplantation: Context-Dependent Roles and Clinical Implications.
articles.authors: Ying H, Feng S, Jiang H
articles.abstract: This article comprehensively summarizes the expression, mechanisms of action, and clinical significance of the IL-33/ST2 axis in solid organ transplantation and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Rather than being uniformly protective or pathogenic, the IL-33/ST2 axis exerts context-dependent effects: ST2L, expressed on regulatory T cells, group 2 innate lymphoid cells, and Th2 cells, promotes immune tolerance, whereas sST2 acts as a decoy receptor that blocks this pathway and promotes inflammation and fibrosis. The net effect depends on tissue-specific innate immune cell composition, differential ST2 isoform expression, donor versus recipient compartment, intervention timing and dosage, and the degree of ischemia-reperfusion injury. Clinically, elevated sST2 is associated with antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplantation, graft dysfunction in heart transplantation, and treatment-refractory graft-versus-host disease in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, these are primarily observational associations; direct causal evidence from genetic or pharmacological intervention studies remains limited and is often derived from animal models. Comparative analysis across transplant types reveals that sST2 may complement established biomarkers such as donor-derived cell-free DNA and donor-specific antibodies, particularly for chronic graft fibrosis and DSA-negative rejection. Future research should use single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize the dynamic expression of ST2 isoforms across immune cells and transplant stages, and explore strategies to induce immune tolerance targeting the IL-33/ST2 axis to improve long-term outcomes for transplant patients.

articles.title: Treatment outcomes and safety of metformin versus insulin in gestational diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
articles.authors: Al-Nemer K, Alruwaili H, Alnashwan A et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy complication associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. While insulin remains the traditional treatment, metformin has emerged as a potential alternative due to its ease of use and favorable metabolic effects. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of metformin versus insulin in the management of GDM. This review was registered with International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (CRD42025644196) and conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed using PubMed and Google Scholar for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing metformin and insulin in pregnant women diagnosed with GDM and reporting relevant maternal or neonatal outcomes. Data screening and extraction were performed using Rayyan software. Statistical analysis was conducted using Stata version 17. Pooled effect sizes were calculated using a random-effects model. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to assess continuous and dichotomous outcomes, respectively. Heterogeneity was evaluated using the I² statistic and Cochran's Q test. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger's test. Twenty-two RCTs met the inclusion criteria. Metformin achieved glycemic control comparable to insulin, with a pooled SMD for fasting blood glucose (FBG) of -0.29 (95% CI: -0.55 to -0.03; P = 0.03). No significant difference was observed in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels (SMD = -0.26; 95% CI: -0.75 to 0.23; P = 0.30). Metformin was associated with significantly less maternal weight gain and a reduced risk of neonatal hypoglycemia (OR = 2.72; 95% CI: 1.02-7.26; P = 0.05). The incidence of pre-eclampsia and hypertensive disorders was similar between groups. Patient satisfaction was consistently higher in the metformin group, with most participants preferring it over insulin. Funnel plots and Egger's test indicated no significant publication bias. Metformin is a safe and effective alternative to insulin for the management of GDM in most pregnant women, offering comparable glycemic control, reduced maternal weight gain, lower risk of neonatal hypoglycemia, and higher patient acceptability. While some patients may still…

articles.title: Hemophilia: Carrier testing and therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
articles.authors: Hemaliya C, Singh AK, Meena LP et al.
articles.abstract: Hemophilia is an X-linked to recessive bleeding disorder and occurs due to a deficiency of the factor level. Leading disease models for human molecular genetics include hemophilia. For family counseling, it is critical to identify the genetic abnormalities that cause the affected people's Propensity to bleed and the danger of inhibitors. The percentage of families with a recognized issue has increased along with improvements in carrier screening, and prenatal diagnosis brought about by genetic testing. The field of hemophilia treatment is changing quickly due to the availability of long-acting drug pharmacokinetics, physiotherapy, and the quick progress being made in gene therapy. In this age of advancement, it is essential to comprehend the variables affecting hemostatic, and clinical outcomes as well as therapeutic responses. Advancements: Gene therapy, NGS, and personalized medicine; Challenges: Cost, and accessibility. This review will look at how molecular genetic analysis fits into the hemophilia diagnostic algorithm, and highlight its benefits for clinical practice, especially as Techniques for Measuring FVIII's [Hemophilia A (HA)] Functional Activity, FVIII's Chromogenic Method (Ccro), The process entails utilizing the FVIII gene (F8) using the polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and then identify any mutations using various screening methods or DNA sequencing, Linkage Analysis for Factor VIII gene, genetics testing approaches for at high-risk male and female. All ethnic groups in the globe are equally affected by hemophilia. Around 400,000 persons worldwide are thought to have hemophilia, which impacts roughly 1 in 10,000 live births. Between 80% and 85% of people with HA are the majority in the general population. Hemophilia B (HB) affects one in five live male neonates, and HA affects one in 30,000 live male infants. As early diagnosis techniques have improved, affected persons should anticipate a typical life expectancy after treatment regimens.

articles.title: Discriminatory power of organ-specific Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores: Predictors of maternal mortality in obstetric intensive care units (ICU).
articles.journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
articles.authors: Agrawal M, Nelia K, Ahmed A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critically ill obstetric patients in intensive care units (ICUs) present unique challenges, and maternal mortality remains a major concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, though widely used in general ICUs, has not been adequately studied for its organ-specific discriminatory power in predicting maternal mortality. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic accuracy of individual organ SOFA sub-scores to improve risk stratification in obstetric critical care.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted over one year in the obstetric ICU of a tertiary center in Northern India. A total of 125 obstetric patients (pregnant or within 42 days postpartum) were enrolled. SOFA sub-scores for respiratory, cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, coagulation, and neurological systems were calculated on admission and throughout ICU stay. Patients were classified into survivors and non-survivors. Associations between individual organ dysfunction and maternal mortality were assessed. Discriminatory accuracy of organ-specific SOFA scores was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
RESULTS: Mortality increased proportionally with the number of dysfunctional organs (χ² =39.693; P < 0.001). Escalating organ-specific SOFA scores were significantly associated with maternal mortality. ROC analysis revealed that cardiovascular dysfunction had the highest predictive accuracy (area under the curve [AUC] =0.875), followed by hepatic (AUC = 0.808), respiratory (AUC = 0.804), hematological (AUC = 0.763), and renal (AUC = 0.757) dysfunction.
CONCLUSION: Cardiovascular, hepatic, and respiratory SOFA sub-scores provide strong discriminatory power for predicting maternal mortality in Obstetric ICU patients. Incorporating organ-specific SOFA assessments may enhance early risk stratification and guide life-saving interventions in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Postpartum risk and prognosis of pregnancy-associated intracerebral haemorrhage: a nationwide cohort-crossover study.
articles.journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
articles.authors: Chen YN, Hsu HH, Chun-Yuan Cheng M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The temporal pattern and maternal-offspring burden of pregnancy-associated intracerebral haemorrhage (P-ICH), an uncommon but devastating pregnancy-postpartum complication, have not been comprehensively elucidated.
METHODS: This cohort-crossover study linked four nationwide databases to include pregnancies from 2012 to 2020 in Taiwan. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for P-ICH were estimated across six intervals from pregnancy through the full 1-year postpartum, with the corresponding period 730 days prior serving as the control. Cohort-time-control and cohort-cohort-time-control sensitivity analyses were performed to adjust for the 730-day age gap. Maternal-offspring outcomes were compared between pregnancies with and without P-ICH.
FINDINGS: 406 P-ICH events were identified (crude incidence 19·22 per 100,000 pregnancies). The overall IRR was 1·79 (95% CI 1·52-2·10). The P-ICH risk showed no meaningful difference across pregnancy but peaked during 0-42 days postpartum (IRR 7·44; 95% CI 4·55-12·18), remaining elevated through 43-180 days (IRR 1·58; 95% CI 1·13-2·20) and 181-365 days (IRR 1·38; 95% CI 1·04-1·83) postpartum. Postpartum elevations were sustained meaningfully in sensitivity analyses, except the 181-365-day cohort-time-control estimate. Women with HDP other than chronic hypertension showed a greater P-ICH risk than those without (pinteraction = 0·0024). Two-year maternal (12·1% vs 0·1%) and offspring (2·2% vs 0·4%) mortality were substantially higher following P-ICH, with 38·8% of maternal deaths in women developing P-ICH 43-365 days postpartum.
INTERPRETATION: P-ICH imposes a substantial and extended postpartum burden, supporting at least 6-month postpartum surveillance and prevention.
FUNDING: National Cheng Kung University Hospital.

articles.title: Near-Infrared Light-Responsive Liposomes for Modulating Switchable CAR-T Cell Therapy.
articles.authors: Lu G, Zhang H, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy has great potential but is limited by off-target effects and cytokine release syndrome. To address these challenges, we developed a mesothelin-targeted switchable CAR-T cell system whose activity can be externally controlled by near-infrared (NIR) light-responsive liposomes.
METHODS: We constructed mesothelin-targeted switchable CAR-T cells via lentiviral transduction. A NIR-responsive liposomal formulation was prepared to encapsulate a small-molecule switch agent (rapamycin or AP21967) for controlled release upon NIR irradiation. By encapsulating a NIR-triggerable photosensitizer, the liposomes became photo-labile, and exposure to 730 nm light induced lipid peroxidation, consequently allowing drug release. The switchable CAR-T cells were co-cultured with mesothelin-expressing ovarian cancer cells (OVCAR-3) under various conditions, with or without NIR irradiation. Cytotoxicity was assessed by LDH release assay, and cytokine secretion (TNF-α and IL-2) was measured by ELISA.
RESULTS: The switchable CAR-T cells exhibited minimal baseline cytotoxicity in the absence of the inducing agent. Upon NIR irradiation, the liposomes released the encapsulated switch agent, which activated the CAR-T cells in a concentration-dependent manner. NIR-triggered activation significantly enhanced the secretion of TNF-α and IL-2 and potentiated the killing effect against mesothelin-positive ovarian cancer cells in vitro.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that the combination of switchable CAR-T technology with NIR-responsive liposomes enables spatiotemporally controlled CAR-T activation, offering a potential strategy to mitigate off-target toxicity and facilitating the clinical application of CAR-T therapy in solid tumors.

articles.title: Signal of venous thromboembolism with ethinyl estradiol vs natural estrogens in oral contraceptives: analysis of the EudraVigilance and Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System databases.
articles.journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
articles.authors: Raskin L, Didembourg M, Locquet M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disproportionality analyses in the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System (FAERS) and EudraVigilance reported lower reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) with natural estrogen-based combined oral contraceptives (COCs) than with ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel. However, using ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel as the reference showed reduced reporting only for natural estrogen-based products. We therefore reanalyzed both databases separately, using natural estrogen-based COCs as the reference.
METHODS: Previously extracted individual case safety report datasets and published disproportionality analyses were re-examined, using natural estrogen-based contraceptives as the comparator. Proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) were recalculated separately for each database. COCs were categorized as ethinylestradiol-based or natural estrogen-based formulations. Drospirenone-only pills were included for comparison. Analyses used pooled natural estrogen contraceptives, estetrol/drospirenone, or estradiol/dienogest as reference groups. Disproportionality was defined as PRR >2, at least 3 cases, and χ2 ≥ 4.
DISCUSSION: Consistent patterns were observed in EudraVigilance and FAERS. Compared with natural estrogen-based COCs, ethinylestradiol-based COCs showed a disproportionate reporting of VTE (EudraVigilance: PRR, 5.10 [95% CI, 4.68-5.56]; FAERS: PRR, 4.21 [95% CI, 3.49-5.08]). In EudraVigilance, when using estetrol/drospirenone as the reference, all ethinylestradiol-based formulations showed disproportionality according to the conventional PRR threshold. A similar trend was noted in FAERS, though not statistically significant, with the drospirenone-only formulation comparable to estetrol/drospirenone.
CONCLUSION: This analysis revealed a consistent and disproportionate reporting of VTE associated with ethinylestradiol-based COCs compared with natural estrogen-based alternatives across 2 pharmacovigilance databases. These results, together with prior biological and observational research, support further reevaluation of COC options given the estrogenic component's potential influence on VTE risk.

articles.title: Pregnancy after transcatheter closure of atrial septal defects: safety and clinical outcomes.
articles.journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
articles.authors: Trojanowicz K, Prochownik P, Tworek M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In recent years, there has been rapid development of minimally invasive cardiovascular procedures, such as atrial septal defect (ASD) transcatheter closure. Many female patients of reproductive age have undergone this procedure, but evidence regarding pregnancy outcomes after transcatheter closure of ASD remains limited.
AIM: Our aim was to assess maternal and fetal outcomes and investigate the magnitude and determinants of obstetric complications in patients after transcatheter closure of an ASD.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We analyzed 130 women with an average age of 28.6 ±9.1 years (19-44) who underwent ASD transcatheter closure using the Amplatzer Septal Occluder. Detailed records of each pregnancy (n = 130), occurring an average of 18.2 ±4.1 months (11-35) after transcatheter closure, were analyzed. Cardiac events were defined as heart failure exacerbation, stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), arrhythmias, or endocarditis; obstetric events as pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH), preeclampsia, HELLP syndrome, premature labor, or postpartum hemorrhage; neonatal events as premature delivery, small-for-gestational age, or fetal or neonatal morbidity or mortality.
RESULTS: Cardiac events were observed during 20.8% (n = 27) of pregnancies and included supraventricular arrhythmias (n = 24, 18.5%) and severe peripheral edema (n = 3, 2.3%). Obstetric events occurred in 22 (16.9%) patients. Neonatal events complicated only 2 (1.5%) pregnancies.
CONCLUSIONS: Most pregnancies after transcatheter ASD closure with the Amplatzer Septal Occluder were completed successfully, with favorable obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Maternal complications were more common among women aged over 30 years.

articles.title: From Gaps in Maternity Care to Maternal Rescue: An Interprofessional Implementation Agenda for Anesthesia and Maternal Critical Care in Somalia.
articles.authors: Ali HA, Mudei NM
articles.abstract: Somalia's maternal health system faces a dual challenge: limited access to skilled maternity care and insufficient capacity to rescue women who deteriorate during or after obstetric emergencies. Hemorrhage, hypertensive emergencies including eclampsia, sepsis, obstructed labor, and urgent cesarean delivery require coordinated maternity, anesthesia, nursing, resuscitation, postoperative surveillance, and critical-care functions. This evidence-informed commentary shifts the discussion from documenting gaps to an interprofessional implementation agenda. We propose five linked priorities: a regulated and supported maternity and obstetric-anesthesia workforce; an evidence-based cesarean safety bundle; step-up maternal high-care capacity; early-warning, crisis resource management, escalation, and referral pathways; and routine measurement through maternal and perioperative quality systems. The approach emphasizes actions that referral maternity hospitals can introduce progressively, with named local accountability, team training, minimum resource requirements, and measurable indicators, while avoiding unsupported assumptions about national critical-care capacity. Somalia does not need to wait for a fully developed intensive-care system before improving maternal rescue. The immediate opportunity is to connect five functions that are too often fragmented: competent anesthesia provision, reliable cesarean safety processes, early recognition of deterioration, monitored maternal high care, and accountable review of outcomes. Strengthening these functions as one interprofessional maternal-rescue pathway offers a practical route to reducing preventable severe maternal morbidity and mortality in Somalia.

articles.title: Efficacy of prophylactic tranexamic acid in preventing postpartum hemorrhage following repeat cesarean sections: a retrospective matched-cohort study.
articles.journal: Frontiers in drug safety and regulation
articles.authors: Di X, Li X, Zheng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is a leading cause of maternal mortality, and women with repeat cesarean sections are at high risk. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of prophylactic tranexamic acid (TXA) in preventing PPH among women undergoing repeat cesarean sections.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted including women with repeated cesarean sections at a tertiary obstetrical center in South China between July 2016 and December 2023. Patients were divided into the TXA group and the control group according to intraoperative prophylactic TXA administration. Given the imbalance in baseline characteristics, 1:2 propensity score matching (PSM) with a caliper of 0.01 was performed to balance confounding variables. The primary outcome was PPH incidence. Secondary outcomes included estimated blood loss, hemoglobin decline, additional uterotonic use, and blood transfusion rate.
RESULTS: After 1:2 PSM, 2,777 women in the TXA group were matched with 5,554 women in the control group, with baseline characteristics well balanced. The incidence of PPH was significantly lower in the TXA group than in the control group (11.09% vs. 17.03%, P < 0.001). The TXA group also demonstrated less calculated estimated blood loss, smaller hemoglobin reduction (12.06% vs. 18.44%, P < 0.001), and lower requirements for additional uterotonic agents (26.90% vs. 29.80%, P = 0.006). Multivariate logistic regression confirmed that prophylactic TXA was an independent protective factor against PPH (OR 0.620, 95% CI 0.540-0.712, P < 0.001). No significant difference was observed in blood transfusion rates (1.55% vs. 2.09%, P = 0.089).
CONCLUSION: Prophylactic TXA use was associated with a lower incidence of PPH and the need for additional uterotonics in women undergoing repeat cesarean sections. Randomized trials in this specific population are needed.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Preventive Practices Regarding Thyroid Disorders During Pregnancy: A Nationwide Online Cross-Sectional Study : Short title: Thyroid Knowledge and Practices in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Alomair BM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid dysfunction during pregnancy is an important endocrine concern because untreated disease may adversely affect maternal health, pregnancy outcomes, and fetal neurodevelopment. Public awareness is particularly relevant in Saudi Arabia, where historical iodine deficiency, regional variation in dietary iodine intake, and differences in health literacy may influence preventive behaviors. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and preventive practices regarding thyroid disorders during pregnancy among Saudi adults of reproductive age.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A nationwide online cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,053 Saudi adults aged 18-45 years from the five major geographical regions of Saudi Arabia. Participants completed a structured self-administered questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of thyroid disorders in pregnancy, attitudes toward screening and treatment, preventive practices, and sources of health information. Knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were summarized using descriptive statistics. Group differences were examined using independent-samples t-tests or one-way analysis of variance, as appropriate.
RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was moderate at 5.9 ± 2.4 out of 10. Although most participants recognized that thyroid disorders can be diagnosed using blood tests (84.2%) and may affect fetal brain development (76.1%), only 52.1% knew that thyroid disorders during pregnancy may be asymptomatic. Attitudes were generally favorable, with a mean score of 26.9 ± 4.5 out of 35; 82.9% agreed or strongly agreed that thyroid screening is important in prenatal care, and 96.0% recognized the importance of management for fetal health. Preventive practices were less optimal, with a mean score of 5.4 ± 2.3 out of 10. Only 44.1% had previously undergone thyroid function testing, and 30.1% regularly consumed iodine-rich foods.
CONCLUSION: Saudi adults of reproductive age demonstrated favorable attitudes but only moderate knowledge and suboptimal preventive practices regarding thyroid disorders during pregnancy. These findings support targeted public health education, improved preconception counseling, and clearer clinical communication regarding thyroid screening and treatment safety during pregnancy.

articles.title: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery versus laparoscopy for salpingo-oophorectomy and adnexectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
articles.authors: Khayat S, Khojah M
articles.abstract: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) and laparoscopic surgeries have widely been utilized in gynecologic surgeries including adnexectomy and hysterectomy. The aim of conducting this comprehensive meta-analysis is to evaluate the peri- and post-operative safety and clinical efficacy of vNOTES versus laparoscopic surgeries for the indications of unilateral or bilateral salpingectomy, unilateral or bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, oophorectomy, and adnexectomy with or without hysterectomies for gynecological pathologies. Five electronic databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, ERIC, and Cochrane CENTRAL) were searched for studies published from their inception till 28th March 2024, following the PRISMA guidelines. Mendeley Desktop 1.19.8 was used to evaluate and remove the duplicates.
