Inclusion criteria comprised of: (a) female patients; (b) vNOTES for salpingectomy/salpingo-oophorectomy/adnexectomy; (c) control group of laparoscopy; (d) outcomes like mean operation time, post-operative 24-h visual analogue scale (VAS) score, intra- and post-operative complications, estimated blood loss, length of stay (LOS) in hospital, hemoglobin level changes, conversion, and total post-operative analgesic usage; (d) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Cochrane risk of bias tool 2.0 (ROB 2.0) were used to assess the quality of cohorts and RCTs respectively. Review Manager (Version 5.3) was utilized to perform statistical analysis. Mantel-Haenszel statistical tests were applied for dichotomous data keeping risk ratio (RR) as effect measure while inverse variance statistical method was selected and weighted mean difference (WMD) was used as the effect measure for continuous data. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Forest plots were constructed to evaluate the pooled results. Confidence interval (CI) value was chosen at 95%. Higgins I 2 statistics were applied to assess the heterogeneity among the studies. The included eight studies comprised of a total of 1203 patients (vNOTES: 542 patients; laparoscopy: 630 patients. Mean change in hemoglobin before and after the procedure was slightly higher in vNOTES (WMD: 0.10; 95% CI = 0.02, 0.17; P = 0.01). LOS was relatively shorter in vNOTES patients (WMD: -0.75; 95% CI = -1.09, -0.41; P < 0.0001). Mean operation time was 22 min shorter in vNOTES (WMD: -22.08; 95% CI = -33.64, -10.52; P = 0.0002). articles.title: Access to maternal health services and perinatal outcomes among pregnant migrant and displaced women in Colombia: A mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: Bello-Álvarez LM, Mejía-Pérez DL, Rubio-Romero JA et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Migration and forced displacement pose major challenges for sexual and reproductive health (SRH) systems in Latin America. Colombia hosts more than 2.8 million Venezuelan migrants and a large population of internally displaced persons, offering a unique context to examine inequities in maternal health service access and perinatal outcomes. We aim to assess differences in maternal and perinatal outcomes among migrant, forcibly displaced, and non-migrant women in Colombia; explore barriers and facilitators to SRH access from the perspectives of women, healthcare providers, and stakeholders; and analyze how the Colombian healthcare system has adapted to meet the SRH needs of mobile and vulnerable populations.
METHODS: A mixed-methods study with a parallel convergent design was conducted between November 2023 and May 2024 in Bogotá and Cali. Quantitative data from 929 women (250 migrants (26.9%), 134 forcibly displaced women (14.4%), and 545 non-migrants (58.7%) hospitalized for obstetric events were analyzed to compare SRH access and outcomes across migrant, forcibly displaced, and non-migrant groups. Multivariate logistic regressions adjusted for sociodemographic confounders. Qualitative data from 44 semi-structured interviews with women, healthcare providers, and policy stakeholders were analyzed using a multi-framework approach integrating the Tanahashi Coverage Model, Social Determinants of Health, and Complex Systems Theory.
RESULTS: Antenatal care utilization and testing rates were similar across groups (mean 5.8 visits, p=0.15). However, maternal mortality occurred exclusively among migrants (400 per 100,000 live births), and perinatal mortality was highest among migrants (37.3/1,000 vs. 18.7/1,000 in non-migrants). Qualitative findings revealed barriers including legal precarity, fragmented insurance, stigma, and limited cultural competence, reducing effective coverage despite nominal access.
CONCLUSIONS: Although formal service availability appears equitable, structural and sociocultural barriers produce inequitable outcomes for mobile populations. Strengthening SRH equity in Colombia requires adaptive, culturally responsive health policies that integrate social protection, insurance reform, and intercultural training.

articles.title: Family and neurosurgery - a balancing act between vocation and responsibility.
articles.authors: Hautmann X, Neufeld E, Lilla N et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reconciling a career in neurosurgery with caregiving responsibilities can present major challenges. While recent scientific work has increasingly focused on the disadvantages faced by women, less attention has been paid to the experiences of men who engage in caregiving in an increasing proportion. The potential tension between the role of a man taking over with caring and that of a neurosurgeon remains largely unexplored.
RESEARCH QUESTION: The aim of our survey is to shed more light on the perceived disadvantages faced by neurosurgeons of both genders in balancing childcare with career advancement.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a Germany-wide, 33-question online survey focusing on discrimination and burden due to "caring" in a neurosurgical career.
RESULTS: In total, 272 individuals responded to the survey. The male to female ratio was 173/98 (p < 0.001). Inappropriate comments on caring were perceived by 49.78% of respondents, with women being significantly more frequently affected (67.0% vs 39.4%, p < 0.001). During job interviews, 28.63% were asked about family planning with women being affected more often (40.9% vs. 21.4%, p < 0.001). On a satisfaction scale of 0-100 (0 = negative, 100 = positive), experienced disadvantages due to caring were rated at 48.1, management flexibility at 52.4, team flexibility at 61.2, and actual working conditions at 31.4.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: According to our data, a significant proportion of men are also affected by discrimination due to "caring," even though women still appear to be affected to a greater extent. Working conditions are perceived as the worst factor for balancing caregiving and work.

articles.title: Bleeding-Related Perinatal Outcomes Following Hormone Replacement Cycle Frozen Embryo Transfer Compared With Non-ART, Fresh Embryo Transfer, and Ovulatory-Cycle Frozen Embryo Transfer: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Yoshihara T, Ono Y, Miyashita D et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Frozen embryo transfer (FET) is associated with increased maternal complications, but whether these risks are specific to the hormone replacement cycle (HRC-FET) protocol or shared broadly across FET pregnancies remains unclear. This study compared perinatal outcomes among non-ART, fresh embryo transfer, ovulatory-cycle FET (OC-FET), and HRC-FET pregnancies.
METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of 5417 singleton deliveries (2017-2025), comprising 4427 non-ART, 158 fresh embryo transfer, 208 OC-FET, and 624 HRC-FET pregnancies. Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for maternal age, BMI, and parity, was used to calculate adjusted odds ratios (aORs), with non-ART as the reference group.
RESULTS: Compared with non-ART, HRC-FET was associated with significantly increased risks of manual removal of the placenta (aOR 14.54), postpartum hemorrhage (aOR 2.33), and uterine atony (aOR 3.23). These risks remained significant after stratifying by mode of delivery. In contrast, fresh embryo transfer and OC-FET showed risk profiles resembling non-ART for most outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Increased perinatal risk associated with ART is not uniform but concentrated primarily in HRC-FET. Perinatal management after HRC-FET should account for bleeding-related complications.

articles.title: Association between infertility prevalence and exposure to heat stress: an ecological study based on the Universal Thermal Climate Index.
articles.authors: Wang D, Qian J, Zhang X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Repeated exposure to heat stress may adversely affect reproductive health, yet the population-level relationship between heat stress and infertility has not been well characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a global ecological analysis across 174 countries and regions from 1990 to 2021. Heat exposure was quantified as the annual number of days falling into four Universal Thermal Climate Index categories: moderate, strong, very strong, and extreme heat stress. We additionally constructed a weighted score combining very strong and extreme heat stress. Associations with male and female infertility prevalence were estimated using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Each additional day of very strong and extreme heat stress was associated with increases in male infertility ASPR of 1.292 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.675-1.908) and 1.654 (95% CI: 0.214-3.096) per 100,000 population, respectively. The corresponding increases in female infertility ASPR were 2.126 (95% CI: 0.785-3.467) and 7.133 (95% CI: 3.940-10.323) per 100,000 population, respectively. Higher weighted heat-stress scores were also consistently associated with greater infertility prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that recurrent heat-stress exposure may be associated with a higher population burden of infertility and support consideration of reproductive health in climate-change adaptation and heat-protection strategies.

articles.title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism.
articles.authors: Leite WF, Ribeiro WN, Povoa RMDS et al.
articles.abstract: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal-fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

articles.title: Calycosin synergistically promotes ferroptosis in cervical cancer cells by inducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Shen Q, Zhu J et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer treatment faces challenges from chemotherapy resistance. Inducing ferroptosis is a promising strategy. Calycosin (Cal), an active component of Astragalus membranaceus, exhibits antitumor activity, but its role in cervical cancer, particularly regarding epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and ferroptosis, remains unclear. Cell Counting Kit-8, colony formation and Transwell assays assessed Cal's effects on cell viability, migration and invasion. Ferroptosis was evaluated by detecting reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde, glutathione and ferrous iron (Fe2+) levels, mitochondrial morphology and expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. EMT markers and signaling pathways (TGF-β/Smad and Hippo/YAP) were analyzed using western blot. TGF-β1 knockdown was used to investigate the functional link between EMT and ferroptosis in vitro and in vivo. Cal inhibited proliferation and induced ferroptosis in cervical cancer cells, evidenced by mitochondrial shrinkage, lipid peroxidation and altered glutathione peroxidase 4/solute carrier family 7 member 11/acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 expression. However, Cal also promoted migration and invasion, upregulated mesenchymal markers, and activated TGF-β/Smad while inhibiting Hippo/YAP signaling. Importantly, TGF-β1 knockdown suppressed both Cal-induced EMT and ferroptosis, indicating a synergistic relationship. In vivo studies confirmed these findings, showing Cal inhibited primary tumor growth but promoted metastasis, effects attenuated by TGF-β1 knockdown. Cal exerts dual effects in cervical cancer: Inducing ferroptosis to inhibit growth while promoting EMT-associated metastasis via TGF-β/Smad and Hippo/YAP pathways. Crucially, Cal-induced EMT synergistically enhances ferroptosis sensitivity. These findings highlight the complex pharmacology of Cal and suggest that combining with EMT inhibitors may optimize its therapeutic potential while mitigating pro-metastatic risks.

articles.title: Venlafaxine in oncology: supportive-care evidence and emerging preclinical anticancer signals: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Harahsheh AJ, Myrzabay Z, Askambayeva N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venlafaxine, a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, has been investigated in oncology for several supportive care indications and, more recently, for potential anticancer activity. However, the available evidence remains fragmented across clinical and preclinical studies.
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence regarding the role of venlafaxine in oncology, including established supportive care applications and emerging anticancer potential.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to 22 August 2026. Original clinical and preclinical studies evaluating venlafaxine in cancer populations or experimental cancer models were eligible. Clinical and preclinical evidence was synthesized separately using a narrative approach. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools for clinical studies and the SYRCLE Risk of Bias tool for animal studies.
RESULTS: 25 studies were included, comprising 23 clinical studies and 2 preclinical studies. The strongest clinical evidence supported venlafaxine for treatment-related hot flashes, particularly among breast cancer survivors receiving endocrine therapy, with the strongest randomized, placebo-controlled trial evidence showing significantly greater reductions with venlafaxine than placebo (P < 0.0001 for higher doses); within-group percentage reductions are also reported but should not be interpreted as treatment effects. Evidence for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy was inconsistent, with potential benefit for acute oxaliplatin-related neurotoxicity but insufficient support for prevention or routine treatment of chronic CIPN. Evidence for other supportive care outcomes, including oral mucositis-associated pain, fatigue, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and quality of life, was limited. Venlafaxine was generally well tolerated, although adverse effects varied by dose and comparator. Preclinical studies investigated anticancer activity, but not equivalently: one in melanoma models showed direct antiproliferative/pro-apoptotic effects of venlafaxine via JNK1/2-Nur77 signaling, whereas a colorectal cancer study showed only context-dependent antagonism of norepinephrine-driven tumor progression, with no significant effect of venlafaxine alone. No clinical evidence currently supports venlafaxine as a direct anticancer treatment.
CONCLUSION: Venlafaxine has an…

articles.title: PCOS discussions on a Turkish online forum: a qualitative netnographic study of concerns, peer advice, and information gaps.
articles.authors: Aksoy Ö
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a multidimensional endocrine, metabolic, and reproductive condition, yet little is known about how related concerns and peer advice unfold within Turkish online forums. This study examined initial concerns and associated peer-response patterns in a publicly accessible Turkish forum.
METHODS: A qualitative netnographic study was conducted using 120 initial posts and 708 peer responses published between August 2025 and May 2026. Initial posts were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and assigned one dominant theme for descriptive frequency analysis. Peer responses were categorized by their dominant communicative function using qualitative content analysis.
RESULTS: Fertility, pregnancy, and motherhood anxiety was the most frequent initial concern (n = 24, 20.0%), followed by treatment and medication-related uncertainty (n = 22, 18.3%). Among peer responses, incomplete or uncertain advice predominated (n = 398, 56.2%), followed by biomedical guidance or normalization (n = 137, 19.4%), practical navigation (n = 50, 7.1%), and experiential advice (n = 47, 6.6%). Cross-tabulation demonstrated that incomplete or uncertain advice predominated across most initial concern categories.
DISCUSSION: Turkish PCOS forum discussions represent a mixed peer-information environment in which reassurance, experiential knowledge, practical guidance, incomplete advice, non-evidence-based recommendations, and stigmatizing interactions coexist. Healthcare professionals should address patients' online information-seeking and provide clear, person-centered guidance on diagnosis, treatment, fertility, visible symptoms, and healthcare pathways.

articles.title: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes following exposure to GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists: a time-window-stratified systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Mavigök E, Mavigök AN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes after preconception or gestational exposure to glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual glucagon-like peptide-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists, and to assess the reproducibility of reported safety signals.
METHODS: Six databases plus a drug-level safety search were searched through 16 July 2026. Exposure was classified into four clinically defined time windows. Independent studies or data sources were the analytic unit; one primary comparator was selected per study, and odds ratios and risk ratios were synthesized separately. Random-effects meta-analysis, timing-stratified and dominant-study sensitivity analyses, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment, and GRADE certainty assessment were used.
RESULTS: Fourteen comparative data sources were included; 13 were quantitatively eligible and eight contributed to at least one pooled estimate. In the timing-specific analysis of major congenital malformations, four studies with verified periconceptional/first-trimester exposure yielded an odds ratio of 0.99 (95% confidence interval 0.77-1.27). A secondary pregnancy-period analysis that added one unadjusted, trimester-unspecified cohort yielded 1.00 (0.94-1.06); that cohort contributed 93.5% of the weight. Pooled preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, and stillbirth analyses showed no statistically significant differences. Preeclampsia and other sparse outcomes were not pooled. Certainty was very low for all key outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear or consistent increase in major congenital malformation risk, but very low certainty, imprecision, residual confounding, heterogeneous comparators, sparse agent-specific data, and uncertain exposure timing preclude conclusions of safety. Reported preeclampsia and renal or urinary signals have not been independently replicated.

articles.title: Changing predictive asymmetry: network agenda correspondence between state media and the user on China's fertility policy (2013-2025).
articles.authors: Deng W, Mao Z, Yang Y
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over the past decade, China's fertility policy has shifted from restrictive population control toward pronatalist support, creating an important case for examining the adaptation of government communication in a platformized media environment.
METHODS: We analyzed 126 fertility-policy posts published by People's Daily and 196,218 associated user comments on Weibo between 2013 and 2025. The LDA model was used to identify four topic-derived policy attributes. Event-based cross-lagged correlations evaluated directional associations against the Rozelle-Campbell baseline, while topic joint-intensity networks and event-level QAP correlations assessed aggregate structural correspondence. Analyses were conducted across three periods: the selective two-child reform period, the universal two-child policy period, and the three-child and pronatalist-support period.
RESULTS: Four topic-derived attributes emerged: Policy Change and Childrearing Burdens, Women's Employment and Work-Family Responsibilities, Gender Preference and Family Norms, and Maternity Care and Childbirth Support. In the first two periods, media-preceding-only patterns were descriptively more frequent than user-preceding-only patterns. In the third period, user-preceding-only patterns became more frequent. Gender analysis revealed gender- and period-specific differences in users' relative attention to the four policy attributes.
DISCUSSION: The relationship between the state-media and user agendas was heterogeneous rather than consistently media-led or user-led. Aggregate thematic similarity could coexist with weaker event-level structural correspondence. The findings are consistent with a potentially more reciprocal communication environment in the later policy period. It also indicates that fertility-policy communication should recognize gender-differentiated issue attention within the user agenda.

articles.title: From menarche to menopause: a lifespan perspective on women's health in sickle cell disease.
articles.authors: Farooqui M, Christmas M, Goba G et al.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) has long been associated with high childhood mortality and reduced life expectancy; however, advances in newborn screening, disease-modifying therapies, and comprehensive care have substantially improved survival. As increasing numbers of women with SCD reach midlife, new challenges are emerging that extend beyond the traditional focus on fertility and pregnancy. Despite growing recognition of reproductive health issues in SCD, menopause remains an underexplored and underrecognized phase of the disease trajectory. In this Perspective, we propose a lifespan framework for women's health in SCD that extends from menarche through menopause and healthy aging. We discuss how the underlying pathophysiology of SCD-including chronic hemolysis, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive organ injury-intersects with reproductive transitions across the female life course. We highlight emerging evidence suggesting earlier menopause in women with SCD and examine the potential implications for pain burden, cognitive health, bone health, cardiovascular risk, iron overload, and quality of life. We further explore how symptom overlap between menopause and SCD may contribute to underdiagnosis and undertreatment during midlife. At the same time, we highlight the role of protective factors-including comprehensive multidisciplinary care, the development and evaluation of menopause-specific interventions through dedicated clinical trials in individuals with SCD, reproductive health services, and coordinated lifespan care models-in supporting healthy aging and improving long-term outcomes. Finally, we argue that menopause should be recognized as a critical component of comprehensive SCD care and research. Integrating reproductive aging into clinical practice, research agendas, and health policy represents an important opportunity to improve lifelong health outcomes, strengthen women-centered care, and advance health equity for women living with SCD worldwide.

articles.title: Maternal thyroid function and subsequent markers of insulin resistance in pregnant women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.authors: Trouva A, Vanky E, Alvarsson M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Low maternal free thyroxine (fT4) levels have been associated with markers of insulin resistance and gestational diabetes. Our primary aim was to investigate whether maternal thyroid function was associated with subsequent insulin resistance in pregnant women with polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS, previously known as PCOS).
METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of two randomized controlled trials, we used linear regression analyses to examine associations of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) and fT4 with parameters of metabolic profile (pre- and post-load glucose, fasting insulin and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) in 284 pregnant women with PMOS who were randomized to metformin or placebo in early pregnancy. Blood samples were drawn at gestational weeks (gw) 5 to12, 19, 32 and 36. An oral glucose tolerance test was performed at inclusion, gw19 and 32.
RESULTS: At baseline, the women had a mean body mass index (BMI) of 28.9 and HOMA-IR 3.2, and none had overt hypothyroidism. We found significant inverse associations between the change in TSH during pregnancy and post-load glucose at gw19, as well as fasting glucose at gw36, i.e. the smaller increase in maternal TSH, the higher subsequent maternal glucose levels. Furthermore, lower maternal fT4 levels were significantly associated with higher subsequent insulin/HOMA-IR levels, and the change in TSH was also inversely associated with HOMA-IR at gw32. All associations were independent of treatment with metformin or placebo.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, a smaller maternal TSH increase and lower fT4 levels during pregnancy in overweight women with PMOS are associated with higher subsequent glucose and insulin/HOMA-IR levels later in pregnancy.

articles.title: Testosterone treatment prevents most gonadectomy-induced metabolic and skeletal deficiencies in female mice.
articles.authors: Kruger RE, Yohannes H, Cho E et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian hormone depletion, whether due to ovariectomy, primary ovarian insufficiency, menopause, or gonadotoxic therapies, is associated with metabolic and skeletal dysfunction, while hyperandrogenic states such as polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome are also linked to increased cardiometabolic risk. However, whether testosterone exacerbates, mitigates, or modifies the consequences of ovarian hormone loss remains poorly understood. This study examined whether testosterone treatment ameliorates ovariectomy-induced metabolic and skeletal impairments using an adult female mouse model. Eight-week-old CD-1 mice underwent sham surgery or ovariectomy and were implanted subcutaneously with capsules containing 10 mg testosterone or empty control capsules, yielding four experimental groups: Blank+Intact (n=7), Blank+OVX (n=7), Testosterone+Intact (n=7), and Testosterone+OVX (n=8). Each treatment combination resulted in hormonal milieus distinct to each group. After six weeks of treatment, testosterone mitigated ovariectomy-induced hyperglycemia and impaired glucose tolerance but did not prevent dyslipidemia or adipocyte hypertrophy (two-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test, p<0.05). Testosterone treatment also increased circulating triglycerides, heart weight, femoral trabecular bone density, and radial strength independent of ovarian status. These findings indicate that testosterone compensates for some, but not all, metabolic and skeletal consequences of ovarian hormone loss, revealing distinct roles for androgens and estrogens in metabolic homeostasis. This may inform clinical management of ovarian insufficiency, menopause, hyperandrogenic disorders, and testosterone-based therapies.

articles.title: Urethroplasty for bulbomembranous strictures after benign prostatic hyperplasia surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Scilipoti P, Zorzi F, Folcia A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate surgical outcomes of urethroplasty for bulbomembranous urethral strictures developing after endoscopic surgery for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), focusing on patency, urinary continence, and erectile function.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A pre-registered systematic review (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews [PROSPERO] identifier: CRD420261374244) was performed following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. PubMed and the Excerpta Medica database (EMBASE) were searched for observational studies reporting urethroplasty outcomes in ≥10 patients with post-BPH bulbomembranous, membranous, or proximal bulbar strictures. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analysis with logit back-transformation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction pooled proportions of patency and urinary incontinence (UI), stratified by technique.
RESULTS: A total of 11 studies comprising 669 patients were identified, of which nine (417 patients) were included in the primary quantitative analysis. All studies were retrospective or prospective observational cohorts with moderate-to-serious risk of bias. Definitions of patency and continence were heterogeneous across studies. The overall pooled patency rate, predominantly defined as freedom from re-intervention rather than objectively confirmed anatomical patency, was 90% (95% confidence interval [CI] 85-93%), with moderate heterogeneity (Q = 11.22). Subgroup analysis by technique yielded patency rates of 87% (95% CI 76-93%) for ventral onlay buccal mucosal graft (BMG) (four studies), 94% (95% CI: 87-97%) for anastomotic urethroplasty (three studies), and 91% (95% CI 83-95%) for dorsal onlay BMG (one study). The pooled UI rate was 5% (95% CI 3-10%), with moderate heterogeneity (Q = 11.38). Sensitivity analysis excluding studies incorporating simple prostatectomy cases (two studies) yielded consistent results. Erectile function data were insufficient for pooled analysis; the two studies reporting Sexual Health Inventory for Men scores documented no significant deterioration.
CONCLUSIONS: Urethroplasty for bulbomembranous strictures following BPH surgery achieves high, heterogeneously defined patency-predominantly freedom from re-intervention-with low de novo UI in experienced centres. The heterogeneous, non-comparative evidence precludes…

articles.title: USP22 Facilitates Cervical Cancer Progression via Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing IRAK1 to Activate NF-κB Signaling.
articles.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.authors: Chen W, Li S, Wang X et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies among women worldwide. Although USP22 is known to be involved in tumor progression, its specific function in cervical cancer remains unclear. This study explored the biological significance of USP22 and the mechanism by which it regulates cervical cancer progression. Through bioinformatic analysis, we identified that USP22 expression was significantly upregulated in cervical cancer tissues and was associated with proliferative potential. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis revealed high USP22 expression in malignant epithelial cells, and USP22 expression was associated with the differentiation potential of cervical cancer cells. Moreover, USP22 deficiency suppressed cervical cancer cell proliferation, triggered cell cycle arrest in G0/G1, accelerated apoptosis, and inhibited migration and invasion. Mechanistically, USP22 bound to and deubiquitinated IRAK1, thereby preventing its proteasomal degradation and maintaining NF-κB pathway activation. USP22 deficiency significantly suppressed xenograft tumor growth and inhibited expression of the proliferation marker Ki67. Furthermore, IRAK1 overexpression abolished the suppressive effects of USP22 deficiency on cervical cancer cell growth and stemness. Collectively, this study provides evidence that USP22 regulates NF-κB signaling pathway by deubiquitinating and stabilizing IRAK1, suggesting that the USP22/IRAK1/NF-κB axis is a promising target for developing novel therapeutic strategies in cervical cancer.

articles.title: Peripheral and Placental KLRG1+ Senescence-Associated T Cells in Placenta Accreta Spectrum: Diagnostic and Clinical Correlations.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Abdelhakeem AG, Elsherbiny NM, Bakr MH et al.
articles.abstract:
PROBLEM: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) disorders are considered to be iatrogenic conditions. There is growing evidence for the role of T cell senescence in the pathophysiology of pregnancy complications. This study aimed to investigate peripheral and placental CD4/CD8 T cell subsets and senescence-associated/highly differentiated T cell frequencies in PAS and to explore their diagnostic performance and correlations with clinical, inflammatory, and proliferative (Ki-67) parameters.
METHOD OF STUDY: Placental tissue and maternal peripheral blood were obtained from PAS pregnancies and controls in their third trimester. Flow cytometric immunophenotyping was conducted for peripheral blood and placental CD4/CD8 T cell subsets, senescence-associated subsets, and their KLRG1 expression intensity. Immunohistochemical analysis of Ki-67 expression in placental tissue of subjects and controls was performed.
RESULTS: PAS placental tissue showed an increase in CD28-CD57+ senescence-associated, KLRG1+ senescence-associated T cells, and KLRG1 MFI within all T-cell compartments. KLRG1 MFI increased progressively toward senescence-associated (CD28-CD57+) T cell phenotypes across all T-cell lineages in PAS placental tissue. In contrast, analysis of KLRG1+ percentages in PAS PB revealed limited, largely non-significant dysregulation of T cells. Ki-67 expression correlated positively with senescence-associated DP T cells and KLRG1+ senescence-associated CD4+ Th cells cells, linking the possible association of trophoblastic proliferation with T-cell senescence.
CONCLUSION: This is the first study analyzing senescence-associated T cell subsets in PAS patients as well as the previously unexplored double-positive and double-negative lineages. Localized immunosenescence at the implantation site may contribute to the pathogenesis of PAS. Senescence-associated T-cell signatures show promise as exploratory tissue-based indicators of the immune dysregulation in PAS.

articles.title: Body Mass Index-Specific Central Adiposity and Risk of Incident Type 2 Diabetes Among Aging Women.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Beydoun MA, Beydoun HA, Manson JE et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Body mass index (BMI) does not capture central adiposity, which may provide additional information for type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk stratification.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate BMI-specific waist circumference (WC) categories in relation to incident T2D and assess their performance across independent cohorts.
METHODS: Prospective analyses included 133,620 Women's Health Initiative (WHI) participants free of T2D at baseline, randomly assigned to training (70%; n=93,463) and test (30%; n=40,157) samples. External validation included the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n=2,885) and Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS; n=1,037). Cox models estimated T2D risk across BMI and BMI-specific WC categories. Discrimination was assessed using Harrell's C-statistic.
RESULTS: In WHI, T2D risk increased progressively across BMI categories (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.51-3.30) and joint BMI-WC categories (HRs, 1.40-4.43). Within BMI strata, higher WC generally identified greater T2D risk. Associations were directionally consistent in HRS and HANDLS. Age modified associations, with stronger gradients at younger ages, whereas race and ethnicity interactions were not statistically significant. Model discrimination was modest (C-statistics approximately 0.60-0.75).
CONCLUSIONS: BMI-specific WC categories refine adiposity-related T2D risk stratification beyond BMI alone but provide modest individual-level discrimination. WC may complement BMI in identifying women warranting more comprehensive metabolic risk assessment rather than serving as a stand-alone T2D prediction tool.

articles.title: Do Adverse Intrauterine Environments Affect Body Mass Index in Infants and Preschool Children?
articles.journal: American journal of human biology : the official journal of the Human Biology Council
articles.authors: Koglin G, da Silva CH, Bandeira DR et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Exposure to adverse intrauterine environments resulting from different maternal clinical conditions may alter childhood growth patterns. This study investigated the influence of such environments on body mass index-for-age (BMI-for-age) trajectories from birth to preschool age.
METHODS: A total of 342 mother-child dyads recruited from three hospitals in southern Brazil were allocated into five groups: diabetes mellitus (DM), systemic arterial hypertension (SAH), maternal smoking, small for gestational age (SGA, used here as a proxy for impaired fetal growth), and a control group. Children were assessed at seven time points from birth to preschool age using anthropometric measurements to calculate BMI-for-age z-scores.
RESULTS: Generalized estimating equations (GEE) identified a significant interaction between group and time (p < 0.001). Among girls, at birth, the DM group presented higher BMI-for-age z-scores than the smoking group and reached elevated BMI-for-age z-scores at preschool age, differing from the control group. At 6 months of age, girls in the SGA group showed a marked increase in BMI-for-age. Among boys, the SGA group reached higher BMI-for-age values at preschool age than the DM and control groups. Differences were observed across time, group, and sex in the SGA and control groups (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that adverse intrauterine environments may influence BMI-for-age trajectories during early life, with greater variability and evidence of catch-up growth among children exposed to maternal DM and SGA. Results should be interpreted cautiously due to unequal subgroup sizes and substantial loss to follow-up at preschool age.

articles.title: Maternal Intensive Care Admission, Unplanned Peripartum Hysterectomy, and Breast Milk Feeding by Hospital Discharge: A Population Based Repeated Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Sarker MR, Wiley R, Harvey S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Characterize trends and factors associated with breast milk feeding among patients undergoing maternal ICU admission or peripartum unplanned hysterectomy.
DESIGN: Population-level repeated cross-sectional study.
SETTING: United States National Vital Statistics System data between 2016 and 2023.
POPULATION: Liveborn singleton, non-anomalous deliveries from 34 + 0 to 42 + 6 weeks.
METHODS: Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression reported as annual average percentage change (AAPC). Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to assess the association between morbidity and breast milk feeding by hospital discharge.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Temporal trends in severe morbidity defined as maternal ICU admission and/or unplanned hysterectomy and associated breast milk feeding by hospital discharge.
RESULTS: Of the 23 589 073 births included, 33 121 (0.14%) were complicated by severe morbidity. Any severe morbidity increased from 102 to 157 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.1%, 95% CI: 1.3% to 7.2%) with increased hysterectomy only from 15 to 24 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.2%, 95% CI: 0.7% to 8.2%), ICU admission only from 75 to 117 per 100 000 (AAPC 4.5%, 95% CI: 1.5% to 7.8%), and no change in concurrent hysterectomy and ICU admission. Patients with any severe morbidity had lower breast milk feeding by hospital discharge (65.2% vs. 84.1%, adjusted OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.45-0.47). Despite temporal increases in breast milk feeding by hospital discharge for patients without severe morbidity, the same was not seen for those with severe morbidity.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify a population in whom additional support and services would help individuals who wish to breastfeed or provide expressed breast milk, when clinically appropriate.

articles.title: Self-Sampling for CDO1/CELF4 Methylation Accurately Identifies Endometrial Cancer in a Resource-Limited Region: A Prospective Study From Gansu.
articles.authors: Xu F, Yin S, Wei M et al.
articles.abstract: Timely diagnosis and risk stratification of endometrial cancer (EC) remain difficult in resource-limited regions. This prospective diagnostic accuracy and feasibility study evaluated whether self-collected cervical specimens combined with CDO1/CELF4 methylation testing, defined as the CISENDO assay, could identify histologically confirmed EC in symptomatic women from Gansu, northwest China. Of 302 screened women, 154 participants with self-collected specimens and histopathological diagnoses formed the primary analytic cohort; 35 had EC and 119 had non-EC diagnoses. An exploratory paired subset included 35 participants with both self- and physician-collected specimens. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and logistic regression, while paired sampling was evaluated using correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, and classification concordance. In self-collected specimens, CISENDO showed strong discrimination for EC at manufacturer-defined cutoffs (AUC 0.834). Bland-Altman mean differences were -1.05 ΔCt for CDO1 and -1.73 ΔCt for CELF4. CISENDO classifications were concordant in 31/35 paired specimens (88.6%), with positive agreement of 84.6%, negative agreement of 90.9%, and Cohen's κ of 0.76. CISENDO positivity remained the strongest independent predictor of EC after adjustment (adjusted OR 85.08; 95% CI 12.21-592.71; p < 0.001). Endometrial thickness showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.646) and did not improve performance when combined with CISENDO. Self-collected CISENDO testing showed strong discrimination for histologically confirmed EC and may provide a feasible molecular triage and risk-stratification approach for symptomatic women in underserved settings. This approach could support decentralized sample collection and reduce dependence on immediate specialist-based evaluation, particularly in geographically dispersed, resource-constrained populations.

articles.title: Is SARS-CoV-2 Infection (COVID-19) Associated With Congenital Anomalies? A Population Study of Congenital Anomaly Surveillance Data and Maternal SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Wales.
articles.authors: Fisher SR, Maddison-Jarvis R, Cresswell-Jones P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Explore the relationship between maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection and congenital anomalies in Wales.
STUDY DESIGN: Mixed observational epidemiological cross-sectional and cohort.
METHODS: Congenital anomaly prevalence data were provided by the Congenital Anomaly Register and Information Service. Two comparisons were made using these data: firstly, congenital anomaly subgroup prevalence prior to and during the pandemic at population level, and in a cohort of women with laboratory-confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with the population trend.
RESULTS: Prevalence of congenital anomalies in Wales was lower during the pandemic (mean 365 per 10,000 in 2020-22 vs. 454 per 10,000 in 2009-19) showing stable trends. However, the mean for abdominal wall defects increased from 9.8 per 10,000 births between 2009 and 2019 to 13.9 per 10,000 births in 2020-2022, largely attributed to an increase in omphalocele. A cohort of 486 confirmed maternal SARS-CoV-2 infections led to 181 births affected by congenital anomalies, and the trimester of infection did not impact the adjusted odds of this occurring. Circulatory anomalies were most frequently reported, consistent with pre-pandemic population-level data. Urinary and cardiac anomalies were more prevalent in this cohort group than at population level.
CONCLUSIONS: There was no clear evidence at population-level of an association between congenital anomalies and maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wales. However, a potential association with specific congenital anomalies cannot be excluded. Increased omphalocele is consistent with a Europe-wide trend that pre-dated COVID-19. National surveillance registries should remain vigilant.

articles.title: Long-Term Relugolix Monotherapy for Uterine Fibroids: Surgery Avoidance in a Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Horibe Y, Kumakiri J, Tabata T
articles.abstract:
AIM: Relugolix monotherapy for uterine fibroids is approved in Japan for only 180 days, and almost all long-term evidence concerns relugolix combination therapy with estradiol and norethisterone acetate. We evaluated surgery avoidance, transition to menopause, symptom control, and bone mineral density (BMD) beyond 180 days.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 83 women with uterine fibroids given relugolix 40 mg monotherapy for at least 180 days at a single center between January 2015 and December 2024. Continuous variables are presented as median [interquartile range]; paired comparisons used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and group comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test and Fisher's exact test (two-sided α = 0.05).
RESULTS: Median treatment duration was 327 days [239.5-420.0] (maximum 1030) and median age was 43 years [37-47]. Overall, 55.4% (46/83) avoided fibroid surgery and 8.4% (7/83) reached menopause without surgery; symptoms resolved or improved in 60.2% (50/83). Among women not wishing surgery, 90.0% (27/30) avoided it, whereas 77.3% (34/44) of those wishing surgery underwent it (Fisher's exact test, p < 0.001). Uterine volume fell from 658 to 502 cm3 (median within-patient reduction 19.0%, p < 0.001) and maximum fibroid diameter by 7.8% (p = 0.001). BMD trended downward at every site without reaching significance (lumbar spine -3.0%, p = 0.11). In addition, the median duration of the drug-free period for patients who measured bone mineral density was evaluated was 726 days (range: 7-2359 days).
CONCLUSION: Long-term relugolix monotherapy frequently enabled surgery avoidance and transition to menopause in women who declined surgery and controlled symptoms in most. Because estrogen add-back is absent, BMD monitoring and a prespecified exit strategy are essential.

articles.title: The gut microbiota-derived butyrate improves gestational glucose homeostasis through HDAC3 inhibition and epigenetic activation of the SCGN/GLP-1 axis.
articles.authors: Han W, Zhang Y, Huang J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A deficiency in the gut microbiota-derived metabolite butyrate is associated with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the causative molecular pathways remain undefined. Given its established role as a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, we hypothesised that butyrate exerts its beneficial effects on gestational glucose homeostasis through epigenetic reprogramming of intestinal hormone secretion.
METHODS: We integrated clinical observation with causal experimentation. First, a nested case-control study measured serum butyrate and active GLP-1 in pregnant women. Second, a GDM mouse model induced by high-fat diet and antibiotics was treated with the butyrate-producing probiotic Clostridium butyricum for metabolic and microbial profiling. Colon tissues were analysed for HDAC expression and histone acetylation. Third, the mechanism was dissected in enteroendocrine cells using sodium butyrate, HDAC3 modulation, and integrated RNA-sequencing/H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing. Finally, HDAC3 heterozygous knockout mice were used for genetic validation.
RESULTS: In the clinical cohort, serum butyrate and GLP-1 levels were consistently lower in women who developed GDM, evident both in early and mid-pregnancy (both p < 0.05). In mice, C. butyricum supplementation alleviated hyperglycaemia, insulin resistance, and circadian glucose rhythm disruption. This was paralleled by elevated systemic butyrate, enrichment of butyrate-producing gut bacteria, decreased colonic HDAC3 protein, and increased global histone H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac). Multi-omics analysis in enteroendocrine cells identified secretagogin (SCGN) as a direct target gene, with butyrate enhancing both its transcription and promoter-associated H3K27ac. Consequently, butyrate and HDAC3 knockdown increased SCGN expression and GLP-1 secretion, whereas HDAC3 overexpression suppressed this axis-an effect reversible by co-treatment with butyrate. The metabolic improvements and SCGN upregulation driven by C. butyricum were abolished in HDAC3-haploinsufficient mice.
CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrate that butyrate ameliorates GDM by specifically inhibiting intestinal HDAC3. This inhibition epigenetically activates the transcription of SCGN via enhanced H3K27ac, leading to potentiated GLP-1 secretion. Our work delineates a novel gut microbiota-epigenetic-hormonal axis, identifying HDAC3 and the downstream SCGN/GLP-1 pathway as potential targets for the prevention or treatment of GDM.

articles.title: Long-acting reversible contraceptive use in postpartum and postabortion adolescents: initiation, predictors, and continuation outcomes.
articles.authors: Sangvornrungsie P, Panichyawat N, Wongwananuruk T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant global public health issue. Thailand enacted the Act on Prevention and Solution to the Adolescent Pregnancy Problem and implemented a public health policy that provides free long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) access to adolescents. At our institution, a structured, adolescent-focused protocol was developed to improve contraceptive counselling and access for postpartum and postabortion adolescents. This study aimed to determine the LARC initiation rate following implementation of this practice. Continuation rates and factors associated with LARC initiation and early discontinuation were also analyzed.
METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary referral university hospital. Thai adolescents aged under 20 years at the time of delivery or abortion at our hospital were included. Demographic and clinical data were collected, including selected contraceptive method, LARC insertion and removal dates, and follow-up data for up to 36 months. Independent sample t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests and chi-square tests were used as appropriated. The primary outcome was reported as frequency and percentages. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis assessed continuation rates, while logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models identified factors associated with initiation and early discontinuation (defined as LARC removal before 3 years), respectively.
RESULTS: Of 1,081 postpartum and post-abortion adolescents, 839 (77.6%) participants initiated LARC. Of these, 91.7% initiated LARC before hospital discharge. The most commonly chosen methods were the 2-rod levonorgestrel implant (44.2%) and the 1-rod etonogestrel implant (32.9%), while 0.6% chose the copper intrauterine device. Significant factors of LARC initiation included younger maternal age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.598; 95% CI: 0.518-0.691; p < 0.001), being employed (aOR 2.233; 95% CI: 1.050-4.751; p = 0.037), and younger partner age (aOR 0.966; 95% CI: 0.935-0.998; p = 0.035). The cumulative LARC continuation rates were 98.1% at 1 year, 93.0% at 2 years, and 79.7% at 3 years. The most commonly reasons for early removal were bleeding disturbances (40.7%), weight changes (18.5%) and desire for pregnancy (13.0%).
CONCLUSION: Thailand's health policy of free LARC access, combined with a tailored structured adolescent protocol, resulted in high LARC initiation and continuation rates, demonstrating the effectiveness of integrated…

articles.title: Development of a risk identification model for sPTB in patients with GDM based on ensemble learning algorithms.
articles.authors: Hao J, Rong Y, Xue J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global prevalence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) continues to rise, and GDM significantly increases the risk of spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB), posing serious threats to maternal and neonatal health. Existing models for assessing sPTB risk in patients with GDM remain limited in accuracy, nonlinear relationship capture, and the handling of complex feature interactions. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the performance differences between eight individual machine learning algorithms and a Stacking ensemble learning architecture, and to achieve risk identification and stratification through optimized model-building strategies.
METHODS: Clinical data were collected from 661 patients with GDM who were hospitalized for delivery at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University from March 2021 to March 2025. The patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 463) and a testing set (n = 198) at a 7:3 ratio. Clinical characteristics were initially screened using univariate analysis. LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm were then jointly used to determine the full-set feature indicators, and Wald tests were further applied to identify independent risk factors and construct the reduced-set feature space. Based on the two feature sets, eight individual machine learning models were developed, including logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), naïve bayes (NB), artificial neural network (ANN), and gradient boosting machine (GBM). To address the limitations of individual models in calibration and generalization performance, a Stacking ensemble learning framework was introduced for model fusion optimization, and a visual online risk calculator was developed.
RESULTS: LASSO regression and the Boruta algorithm selected nine variables for the full-set feature group: fasting plasma glucose on OGTT, 1-hour post-load glucose, white blood cell count (WBC), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), hemoglobin (Hb), fibrinogen (FIB), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and uric acid-to-creatinine ratio (UA/Cr). Wald tests confirmed that ALP, ALT, fasting plasma glucose (FPG), UA/Cr, and Hb were independent influencing factors and constituted the reduced-set core indicators. Comparison of individual models showed that the full-set GBM model performed well in risk recognition, whereas the LR model had advantages in calibration…

articles.title: The relationship between hemoglobin concentration in the third-trimester and gestational age, birth weight of newborns: stratified analysis based on maternal age.
articles.authors: Ge J, Wang W, Zhang H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study retrospectively analyzed the association between hemoglobin concentration in the third trimester of pregnancy and neonatal gestational age and birth weight, and further explored whether there were differential effects between advanced maternal age and women of reproductive age.
METHODS: Based on the Electronic Medical Record database of Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child-care Hospital, the clinical data of all singleton pregnant women who were registered and underwent prenatal check-ups at the hospital from January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2024 were collected. After screening according to the inclusion and exclusion criteria, a total of 31,690 pregnant women were ultimately enrolled in this study. Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze the effect of third-trimester hemoglobin concentration on neonatal gestational age and birth weight. A restricted cubic spline (RCS) function with five knots was applied to analyze the association between changes in third-trimester hemoglobin concentration and neonatal birth weight outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 31,690 pregnant women were included, among whom 4,664 (14.7%) were of advanced age and 27,026 (85.3%) were of childbearing. Third-trimester hemoglobin concentration exhibited an inverted U-shaped relationship with neonatal birth weight. In the advanced-age pregnant women, multivariable analysis revealed that, compared with a hemoglobin level of 110-119 g/L, a level ≤109 g/L significantly increased the risk of low birth weight and preterm birth, with the highest risk observed at <100 g/L. Meanwhile, the risk of preterm birth significantly increased at hemoglobin levels ≥140 g/L. In the women of reproductive age, compared with a hemoglobin concentration of 110-119 g/L, concentrations≥ 120 g/L were risk factors for low birth weight and preterm birth.
CONCLUSION: Third-trimester hemoglobin level is closely associated with adverse birth outcomes. Management strategies should consider maternal age stratification, with emphasis on early screening, dynamic monitoring, and rational iron supplementation to reduce the risk of adverse birth outcomes.

articles.title: Association of Maternal Immune Activation With Pruritic Urticarial Papules and Plaques of Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Patel NB, Baer RJ, Chambers C
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP) is a common dermatosis of pregnancy, but its etiology remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify whether maternal immune activation (MIA) is associated with PUPPP.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of pregnant patients using a population-based administrative cohort of all live births in California from 2016 to 2021. Patients with PUPPP were identified using ICD-10 code O26.86. MIA was defined by ICD-10 diagnoses of infection, autoimmune disease, or atopic disease during pregnancy. Poisson log-linear regression was used to estimate crude and adjusted risk ratios (RR, aRR) for associations between PUPPP and MIA.
RESULTS: Among 2,275,929 pregnancies, there were 3286 (0.14%) patients with PUPPP. Compared with patients without PUPPP, patients with PUPPP had higher rates of gestational hypertension (6.2% vs. 4.0%, p < 0.0001) and preeclampsia (10.9% vs. 5.2%, p < 0.0001). Atopy was associated with increased risk of PUPPP (aRR 1.7, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.6-1.9), as was autoimmunity (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.1) and maternal infection (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.4-1.7). Patients with PUPPP were less likely to have a pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2 (21.2% vs. 25.4%, p < 0.0001) but more likely to exceed recommended gestational weight gain (64.3% vs. 52.4%, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: MIA during pregnancy, including atopy, autoimmunity, and infection, was independently associated with increased risk of PUPPP. These findings suggest immune dysregulation may contribute to PUPPP pathogenesis. The association with excessive gestational weight gain further supports a potential role for inflammation secondary to connective tissue injury from abdominal distension.

articles.title: Platelet-containing systemic inflammatory indices show reduced prognostic discrimination in critically ill cirrhosis: a MIMIC-IV cohort study with external validation in eICU-CRD.
articles.authors: Ding T, Yin Y, Ying Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices are increasingly used as prognostic markers in critical illness. Three of the commonest, the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), contain the platelet count, which in cirrhosis is determined largely by processes other than inflammation. They have not been compared head-to-head in critically ill cirrhosis.
METHODS: In a retrospective MIMIC-IV cohort of adults with cirrhosis in intensive care, six indices were derived from the first white cell differential within 24 h, and discrimination for in-hospital mortality was measured by the area under the ROC curve (AUC), with external validation in eICU. Because each platelet-containing index equals a platelet-free counterpart multiplied by the platelet count (e.g. SII = platelet × neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR]), testing that multiplication was the primary analysis, with the neutrophil count as a positive control.
RESULTS: Of 2,227 patients, 627 (28.2%) died in hospital. NLR discriminated best (AUC 0.651) and the platelet-containing indices lowest (PLR 0.546). Multiplying by the platelet count degraded discrimination (NLR to SII, ΔAUC - 0.048; SIRI to PIV, - 0.038; both p < 0.001), whereas multiplying by the neutrophil count improved it (+ 0.093, p < 0.001), the change depending on which cell count was introduced. The platelet count alone discriminated no better than chance (AUC 0.522), added nothing to a model containing MELD-Na, OASIS, age, and sex (ΔAUC + 0.0003), and showed no independent association with mortality when entered separately. The ranking was reproduced externally (eICU, n = 800).
CONCLUSIONS: The conventional platelet-containing indices did not outperform their platelet-free counterparts. Thrombocytopenia in critically ill cirrhosis is multifactorial and no direct measure of portal hypertension was available, so the reason cannot be established here. Incremental value over established severity scores was marginal for every index, and indices from other diseases require re-evaluation in cirrhosis before use.

articles.title: Effect of a free sugar-restricted diet on anthropometric parameters, lipid profile, and glycemic control in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Gholamshahi H, Tehrani AH, Fotros D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sugar diets rich in fructose and other simple sugars are associated with increased lipogenesis and insulin resistance, potentially increasing the risk of metabolic syndrome, a condition closely linked with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a free sugar-restricted diet on anthropometric parameters, lipid profile, and glycemic control in women with PCOS.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled clinical trial, 74 women aged 18-45 years with diagnosed PCOS were randomly assigned to either a free sugar-restricted diet group (n = 37) or a standard diet group (n = 37) for 12 weeks. Anthropometric indices, fasting blood glucose (FBG), serum insulin, insulin (HOMA-IR), insulin sensitivity (QUICKI), and lipid profile parameters including triglycerides (TG), total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol were measured at baseline and at the end of the study.
RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in body weight and body mass index (BMI) (P = 0.017 and P = 0.026, respectively). There was a significant reduction in FBG (P < 0.001) and an increase in QUICKI (P = 0.022) in the intervention group in comparison with control, though QUICKI lost significance after adjusting for confounders. Both groups experienced significant reductions in TC and LDL during 12 weeks, while TG levels decreased significantly only in the intervention group (P = 0.001). Between-group comparisons revealed a significant difference in TG (P = 0.037), and a near-significant difference in LDL (P = 0.054). After adjusting for confounders, lipid profile components, except for LDL, improved in the intervention group.
CONCLUSIONS: This study showed that a 12-week free sugar-restricted diet can lead to weight reduction and improvements in blood glucose and lipid profile parameters in women with PCOS.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: IRCT20230615058489N1; Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials ( https://www.irct.ir ); Date of registration: June 25, 2023.

articles.title: Factors associated with cannabis use among infertile patients and their partner.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Steckler A, Kruzan M, Angeles I et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize cannabis use and factors associated with use among couples presenting for infertility evaluation.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, retrospective chart review of female patients with infertility and their male partners presenting to an academic fertility center from 2016 to 2021. Demographic and clinical factors associated with self-reported cannabis use were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Semen parameters were compared by cannabis use in an exploratory analysis.
RESULTS: Among 1531 female patients, 4.4% reported cannabis use. Users were younger, had higher BMI, were less often married and more frequently nulliparous, and had higher rates of tobacco and alcohol use and anxiety/depression (all p < 0.05). In adjusted analyses, cannabis use was associated with younger age (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.97), lower odds of being married (OR = 0.33, 95% CI 0.19-0.60), and higher odds of tobacco use (OR = 3.93, 95% CI 2.08-7.18), alcohol use (OR = 2.62, 95% CI 1.35-5.61), and psychiatric diagnosis (OR = 2.67, 95% CI 1.59-4.52), as well as more recent year of presentation (OR = 1.34, 95% CI 1.16-1.55). Among 1472 male partners, 8.6% reported cannabis use. After adjustment, cannabis use was associated with lower odds of being married (OR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.29-0.78), and higher odds of tobacco use (OR = 3.05, 95% CI 1.95-4.72), psychiatric diagnosis (OR = 3.23, 1.75-5.72), and more recent year of presentation (OR = 1.30, 95% CI 1.16-1.46). Semen parameters did not differ significantly by cannabis use.
CONCLUSIONS: Cannabis use increased over the study period and clustered with other behavioral and psychosocial factors. Younger, non-married individuals and those reporting tobacco use or anxiety/depression may benefit from targeted cannabis screening and preconception counseling.

articles.title: Regional Anesthesia in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Current Landscape and Future Directions.
articles.authors: Sargent T, Mua FH, Dobrowski A et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Regional anesthesia (RA) is increasingly promoted as a strategy for expanding safe surgical and obstetric anesthesia access in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where general anesthesia (GA) carries disproportionate risk. This review examines current RA utilization patterns, recent advances in training and implementation, persistent barriers, and the evidence linking RA to clinical outcomes in LMICs, in order to identify what is needed for durable, system-wide scale-up.
RECENT FINDINGS: Large observational analyses show lower perioperative and maternal mortality with regional or neuraxial anesthesia compared with GA. Hybrid training models combining online instruction, simulation, and mentored clinical practice have improved provider knowledge and peripheral nerve block competence, and portable ultrasound has expanded point-of-care applications. However, workforce shortages, inconsistent equipment and medication supply, limited capacity to manage local anesthetic systemic toxicity, and fragmented, single-center safety data continue to constrain reliable implementation. RA offers a safe, lower-resource alternative to GA in LMICs, but sustainable expansion depends on addressing underlying workforce, supply, and monitoring deficits rather than isolated procedural training. Embedding RA within National Surgical, Obstetric, and Anesthesia Plans, supported by multicenter outcome registries and economic evaluation, should guide future research and implementation efforts.

articles.title: Single-Cell Omics Profiling Reveals Enhanced Heterogeneity of Cord Blood Basophils at Birth.
articles.authors: Low JH, Man X, Ong J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Basophils are important mediators in the pathobiology of atopic diseases, yet the heterogeneity of basophils within the perinatal environment remains incompletely understood. In our study, we aimed to perform comprehensive profiling of paired maternal and cord blood basophils using a single-cell omics approach to look into their distinct transcriptional signatures.
METHODS: Basophils were isolated from four paired maternal-cord blood samples at the time of delivery, including one mother who delivered monozygotic twins. Basophil characterization of maternal blood (MB) and cord blood (CB) was analyzed in flow cytometry. Single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to further examine the basophils composition and heterogeneity in MB and CB.
RESULTS: We observed that CB basophils have lower expression of FCER1A, and no cell-bound or circulating IgE levels as compared to MB. Our scRNA-seq data show that MB and CB basophils are different in both transcriptomic and functional profiles. CB basophils exhibit greater heterogeneity than MB. Low interindividual variability between twin CB basophil samples confirmed that the transcriptomic difference between MB and CB basophils is biologically meaningful. Trajectory pseudotime analysis revealed that CB basophils have an earlier pseudotime, potentially indicating a more naïve state. In addition, we demonstrated that CB basophils exhibit distinct functional capacities.
CONCLUSION: Our data identified protein and gene signatures in MB and CB basophils. We demonstrated that CB has greater heterogeneity than MB basophils, thereby highlighting the relevance of single cell profiling of basophils in the context of the maternal-fetal interface.

articles.title: Impact of family planning messages on modern contraceptive use: an observational study of women of reproductive age in Zambia 2007-2018.
articles.authors: Kazibwe J, Sundewall J, Masiye F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reducing unintended pregnancies in low-income and middle-income countries requires enhancing the use of modern contraceptives. Country level evidence on the role of the media and counselling in this process is scanty. The aim of the study is to estimate the impact of family planning messages received through mass media and counselling by health workers on modern contraceptive use among women of reproductive age in Zambia over the study period of 2007 to 2018.
METHODS: We analysed three rounds of Zambia Demographic and Health Survey data (2007, 2013/14, 2018). We used different modelling approaches, including logistic regressions, probability weighting and propensity score matching to determine the average treatment effects (ATE) of media messages and counselling by health workers. ATE were also estimated by year. Post-estimation and robustness checks were conducted using overlap plots and bootstrapping.
FINDINGS: Across all surveys, a total of 19 958 women of reproductive age (15–49 years) were identified for inclusion in the study. The magnitude of impact of family planning messages varied by mode of delivery of the messages. Receiving family planning messages through a combination of health worker counselling and mass media had the most significant positive impact on contraceptive use (ATE 17.06%) followed by counselling (ATE 14.55%) and mass media messages only (ATE 3.37%). The impact of the different modes of delivery of family planning varied by year, showing a decreasing trend.
CONCLUSION: The mode of delivery influences the impact of family planning messages on modern contraceptive use among women. Family planning counselling and combined approaches outperform mass media messages only. A declining impact over time raises concerns and highlights the need for further investigation into delivery effectiveness.

articles.title: Postoperative recovery following pelvic organ prolapse surgery: Preliminary data from a French prospective cohort.
articles.authors: Vassal M, Pierson A, Six JC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelvic organ prolapse surgery is common, but postoperative recovery is rarely assessed from the patient's perspective.
OBJECTIVE: To describe early patient-reported recovery using the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score.
METHODS: Preliminary single-center prospective observational study nested in an ongoing cohort. Patients completed the QoR-15 on postoperative days 1 to 3. Procedures were grouped as vaginal repair without sacrospinous fixation (n=3), vaginal repair with sacrospinous fixation (n=16) and laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy (n=12).
RESULTS: Of 34 patients, 31 were analyzed; 85 of 93 questionnaires (91%) were completed. In the 25 patients assessed on days 1 and 3, the mean score increased from 109.4 to 116.7 (+7.3), exceeding the 6-point minimal clinically important difference, with wide individual variability. Psychological support scored highest from day 1, whereas physical independence and pain scored lowest.
CONCLUSION: The QoR-15 is feasible after prolapse surgery and captures clinically meaningful, multidimensional early recovery from the patient's perspective.

articles.title: Gestational weight gain and health-related quality of life during pregnancy and the early postpartum period in women with cystic fibrosis receiving elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor.
articles.authors: Vagt-Detering NK, Picker M, Thoms C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Highly effective CFTR modulator therapy, such as elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI), has significantly increased pregnancy rates in women with cystic fibrosis (wwCF). Data on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) during pregnancy and the early postpartum period under ETI remain limited.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study evaluated 18 wwCF receiving ETI during pregnancy. Maternal outcomes (lung function, BMI, gestational weight gain, pulmonary exacerbations) and HRQoL using the Cystic Fibrosis Questionnaire-Revised (CFQ-R) were assessed at baseline, during pregnancy, and postpartum.
RESULTS: Maternal lung function remained stable across pregnancy and the postpartum period, while pulmonary exacerbations occurred in 50% of pregnancies. Gestational weight gain (GWG) deviated in 16 of 17 women (94%) from Institute of Medicine (IOM) recommendations: 8/17 (47%) had insufficient and 8/17 (47%) excessive GWG, while only 1/17 (6%) achieved adequate GWG. All women with insufficient GWG had a baseline BMI of 18.5-24.9 kg/m2, whereas excessive GWG occurred across all baseline body mass index (BMI) categories. In exploratory CFQ-R analyses, the largest changes were observed in the physical, respiratory, and social domains, with lower physical and social scores observed postpartum compared with baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy in wwCF receiving ETI was associated with preserved maternal pulmonary stability. The high rate of GWG outside recommended ranges and exploratory changes in selected HRQoL identify nutritional and patient-reported outcomes that warrant further prospective investigation.

articles.title: Implementing Image-Guided Brachytherapy (IGBT) For Cervical Cancer in Resource-Limited Settings: An International Multicentric Cross-Sectional Study of Resource and Workflow Impact.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.ta: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
articles.authors: Hande V, Ndarukwa S, Rubio AP et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of image-guided brachytherapy (IGBT) in cervical cancer improves patient outcomes. However, implementation in resource-limited settings is challenging due to limited capacity upscale, absence of workflow enhancement strategies, and financial barriers. Optimizing workflows is essential, yet the relationship between workflow efficiency and IGBT uptake remains unclear.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study examined brachytherapy (BT) workflows across 14 nationally representative centers. Standardized forms collected data on infrastructure, treatment workflows ((A): Conventional two-dimensional (2D) X-Ray-Guided BT, with point-A-based fractions planned using 2D X-ray imaging, (B): Standard intracavitary (IC) three-dimensional (3D) IGBT, with fractions planned using computed tomography (CT)- or magnetic resonance (MR)-based imaging with volume-based prescriptions, (C): Advanced 3D IGBT, with fractions delivered using advanced IC or intracavitary-interstitial (IC-IS) techniques and planned using CT- or MR-based imaging with volume-based prescriptions.)), procedural times, anesthesia, imaging, and treatment planning. National BT resource data was also collected. Recommendations were developed to optimize workflows and facilitate IGBT transition.
FINDINGS: A total of 365 workflows were analyzed, wherein workflow B was most common (51%). Median procedure times were 2 hours 08 minutes (Interquartile range (IQR) 1 hour and 7 minutes), 2 hours 35 minutes (IQR 1 hour and 51 minutes), and 4 hours 16 minutes (IQR 2 hours and 33 minutes) for workflows A, B, and C, respectively. Using sedation instead of full anesthesia shortened workflows by a median of 35 minutes. BT machine demand, based on national cervical cancer incidence, ranged from 0.2 to 9.5; four countries had low (< 0.5), two moderate (0.5 - 1.0), and eight high demand (>1.0). Resource- and context-specific recommendations for IGBT transition were provided.
INTERPRETATION: BT workflows varied widely. Substantially increased procedure times and resource use were observed with advanced workflows. Findings highlight opportunities to improve efficiency through anesthesia choice, imaging strategy, and planning workflow optimization. Implementing context-specific strategies will be crucial for IGBT transition.
FUNDING: Funding from the XXXX, in collaboration with XXXX and participating sites.

articles.title: Exploring the therapeutic role of Chinses herbal medicine in the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after conservative surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Liu Z, Liu Y, Li S et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Since surgery can only remove lesions of a larger size visible to the naked eye, the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery is high. In recent years, numerous scholars have found that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment is effective in reducing the recurrence rate of postoperative fibroids, as well as improving the clinical treatment rate, regulating serum hormone levels, reducing plasma viscosity, and promoting the restoration of uterine volume following surgery.
