Several randomized controlled trials have been undertaken on the prevention and treatment of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids using patented Chinese medicines and self-proposed formulations, such as Guizhi Fuling Pill, Xiaozheng decoction, Xiangleng pill, Zhengjia decoction, Xiaoliu decoction, Guizhi Jiliu pill, Huoxue Huayu formula, Huoxue Xiaozheng decoction, Shugan Sanjie decoction, Gongliuxiao capsule, Hongjin Xiaojie concentrated pill, and Jiawei Guizhi Fuling decoction. However, no study has systematically evaluated Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) in reducing the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of CHM for the prevention of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids, evaluating its efficacy and safety.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted on PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Information Database (VIP), WanFang Database, and China Biomedical Database (CBM) to identify randomized controlled clinical studies conducted up to March 2025 that examined the efficacy of CHM in treating patients with postoperative uterine fibroids. Two institutes were independently under-selected, and data were extracted and quality assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager software 5.4, and forest plots were generated. The quality of evidence was assessed using GRADEpro 3.2.2. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000288).
RESULTS: 16 trials were included in this study, and the postoperative recurrence rate after treatment was mainly analyzed. CHM treatment reduces postoperative recurrence rates in patients with uterine fibroids compared to the blank (6 trials, n = 588; OR (odds ratio) = 0.22; 95 % CI (95 % confidence intervals) = 0.14-0.34; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001), conventional western…

articles.title: Perspectives of Older Adults on Digital Health Interventions for Overactive Bladder: A Pre-Implementation Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Gunamany S, Dzinoreva M, Sinclair S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine patient perspectives on the acceptability, perceived usefulness, and implementation expectations of digital health interventions (DHIs) for overactive bladder (OAB) management among older adults.
METHODS: We conducted a pre-implementation qualitative study using 16 in-depth, semi-structured interviews with adults aged 60 and older. The pilot-tested interview guide was informed by an integrated conceptual framework combining the eHealth Literacy Model and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis with independent dual coding.
RESULTS: Three main themes were identified. First, perceived usefulness was the primary driver of willingness to adopt DHIs. Their capacity to support symptom and trigger monitoring, provide actionable personalized feedback, and facilitate clinician communication was particularly valuable. Second, willingness to engage depended on low-burden features such as voice input, intuitive interfaces, and flexible monitoring, while cognitively demanding features were identified as barriers to sustained use. Third, trust and acceptance were closely linked to clinician endorsement, trusted institutional affiliation, human connection, confidence in data privacy, with stigma reinforcing the need for discreet design.
CONCLUSION: Acceptance of DHIs for OAB is shaped by the interplay between perceived usefulness, usability, and trust within the context of unpredictability, embarrassment, and stigma unique to OAB. Successful implementation requires attention to both functional design and contextual factors, including clinician endorsement and data governance. Future research should prospectively evaluate whether interventions designed around these patient-defined priorities improve adherence to behavioral therapy and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Disparities and Temporal Trends in Syphilis Testing Among Pregnancies Ending in Stillbirth and Miscarriage, U.S., 2016-2023.
articles.authors: Azqul M, Chinchilli VM, Risher K et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Syphilis during pregnancy represents a significant public health issue in the U.S., leading to rising rates of congenital syphilis and preventable adverse outcomes such as stillbirth and miscarriage. However, the understanding of syphilis screening/testing among pregnancies ending in stillbirth and miscarriage is limited. The purpose of this study was to analyze the monthly trends of syphilis screening/tetsing among pregnancies ending in stillbirth and miscarriage.
METHODS: A retrospective longitudinal study was conducted using the Marketscan® Commercial Claims and Encounters Database from 2015 to 2024. To identify pregnancies ending in stillbirth and miscarriage, validated ICD-10, CPT-4, and HCPCS codes were used. Monthly syphilis screening/testing rates were identified and summarized at any point during the prenatal care and at delivery, stratified by age, region, and urban/rural residence. Temporal trends were assessed using generalized linear mixed models with a Poisson distribution.
RESULTS: Syphilis screening/testing among pregnancies ending in stillbirth remained stable, with no notable changes. Prenatal syphilis screening ranged from 72% to 90%, while at-delivery testing ranged from 5% to 15%. Testing during the at-delivery window was higher in the South and lower in rural areas. Syphilis screening/tetsing among pregnancies ending in miscarriage was consistently low.
CONCLUSION: Syphilis screening/testing among pregnancies ending in stillbirth and miscarriage remains insufficient, with no improvement over time. Ongoing gaps and disparities in screening/testing may contribute to preventable adverse outcomes. A deeper understanding of the ongoing low screening/testing rates and disparities is needed to support the development of more focused and effective strategies to improve syphilis screening coverage.

articles.title: Implementation and Impacts of Maternal and Perinatal Quality Collaboratives across U.S. States: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Alvarado G, Howell K, James KF et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal and Perinatal Quality Care Collaboratives (M/PQCs) are voluntary state-based initiatives that leverage shared data systems, evidence-based toolkits, and quality improvement science to reduce preventable maternal and infant harm.
METHODS: A scoping review of academic and grey literature was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and registered in Open Science Framework. Seven databases were searched for U.S.-based M/PQC studies published between January 2000 - November 2024, analyzed in 2025. Two independent reviewers screened 456 deduplicated records; 31 met eligibility criteria. Quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by implementation theme and intervention topic.
RESULTS: Thirty-one studies spanning 16 states and one national analysis were included. Five themes were identified across two domains. Implementation approaches included: (A) building statewide governance infrastructure; (B) translating evidence into practice through standardized toolkits; and (C) strengthening communication, teamwork, and process outcomes. Impacts included: (D) demonstrated reductions in maternal and birth morbidity, including 45-95% reductions in early elective deliveries, 76-87% improvements in timely hypertension treatment, and national-level reductions in eclampsia and intensive care unit admissions; and (E) expansion of the collaborative mission toward contraceptive access, opioid use disorder care, and racial health equity.
DISCUSSION: M/PQCs function as a form of primary and secondary prevention, institutionalizing evidence-based protocols before obstetric emergencies occur. M/PQCs' evolution from clinical safety bundles toward equity, access, and social determinants signals an expanding mandate. Future initiatives should prioritize disaggregated outcome reporting, health equity frameworks, and inclusion of community birth and outpatient settings to ensure M/PQC gains are equitably distributed.

articles.title: ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT PERSPECTIVES ON HOME-BASED TESTING FOR SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS: A QUALITATIVE STUDY.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Johnson RM, Abacan AA, Raphael M
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Home-based sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing has emerged as a promising strategy to expand access to sexual and reproductive healthcare (SRH) services. However, perceptions of home-based STI testing among underserved adolescents and young adults (AYA) remain poorly understood. This qualitative study explores AYA attitudes toward home-based STI testing and telehealth, as well as factors influencing acceptability.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with AYA (n=21, 18-24 years old) receiving care at nine urban publicly funded family planning and school-based clinics in Houston, Texas. Interviews explored attitudes, intentions, and perceived barriers and facilitators related to home-based STI testing and telehealth. Deidentified transcripts were qualitatively analyzed using descriptive content analysis. Participants were categorized as expressing acceptance ('Yes'), rejection ('No'), or conditional acceptance ('Maybe') of home-based STI testing.
RESULTS: Nine participants (42.9%) expressed comfort with home-based STI testing, citing convenience, privacy, and confidence in their ability to self-collect specimens. Many in this group viewed telehealth and in-person care as equally acceptable. Six participants (28.6%) rejected home-based testing, primarily because of low self-efficacy and concerns regarding specimen collection, mailing logistics, and delayed results. This group uniformly preferred clinic-based care. Six participants (28.6%) expressed conditional acceptance, with hesitations centered on logistics and self-efficacy regarding self-collection.
CONCLUSIONS: Most participants demonstrated at least conditional acceptance of home-based STI testing. Successful implementation among underserved AYA may require strategies that enhance self-efficacy, address logistical barriers, and support patient choice through flexible screening pathways. These findings provide actionable guidance for expanding access to STI screening among underserved youth.

articles.title: A Prospective Study of Life Impact in Five Domains During Menses in a Cohort of Early Adolescents.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Jz AW, O'Brien SH, Kistler I et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To prospectively characterize life impacts in five domains (health, school, activities, family, friends) during menses in early adolescents and examine the association of a modified WaLIDD (location, intensity, days of pain) dysmenorrhea score with life impacts.
METHODS: Prospective, observational study utilizing a multiplatform mobile application for menstrual tracking. English speaking, post-menarcheal biologic females, aged 10-14, with smart device access were recruited via electronic platforms and in person between March 2021-January 2023. Participants documented menstrual pattern and flow, presence and severity of dysmenorrhea, and life impact in five domains over 6-months. General linear mixed models with a binomial link were used to estimate the association of a modified WaLIDD score with any life impact.
RESULTS: 126 participants from 17 states with 506 documented menstrual cycles were included. Median age was 13.0 years (IQR 12,0, 14.0), and 112 (89%) had a gynecological age <3 years. Dysmenorrhea was reported with at least one cycle in 113 (90%) participants and affected 375 (74%) cycles. Life impacts in health, extracurricular activities, and school affected approximately one in five cycles and included symptoms such as fatigue, headaches, and anxiety. Median modified WaLIDD score per cycle was 5.0 (IQR 0.0 - 6.0). Higher modified WaLIDD scores were associated with greater odds of reporting a life impact (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.43-1.88).
CONCLUSION: Dysmenorrhea was highly prevalent in early post-menarcheal adolescents and symptoms beyond pain, such as anxiety and headaches, were frequently reported. The modified WaLIDD score was associated with life impact during menses in this population.

articles.title: The psychosocial impact of living with cloacal malformations in young people: A qualitative study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Samuels E, Turgoose D, Latchford G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cloacal malformations are rare congenital condition affecting females, characterised by the convergence of the urinary tract, reproductive tract, and rectum into a single channel. Complex medical interventions are often required from the neonatal period onwards, with potential lifelong implications for bowel, urinary, and gynaecological health. Few centres have substantial experience in treatment and long-term support. Research on the lived experience and psychosocial impact of cloacal malformations is limited, particularly during the transition from adolescence to adulthood. This qualitative study explored how young people born with cloacal malformations live with the condition and what their experiences are of past and ongoing treatment.
DESIGN: One-to-one interviews were conducted and analysed using grounded theory and major themes identified.
PARTICIPANTS: Eight participants (aged 16-38) from the UK, Central Europe, North America and Australia were interviewed.
RESULTS: Three themes were developed. Sense of the bodily self highlights the impact of treatment and symptom management on body perception and the development of sexual identity. Medical complexity reflects awareness of the complexity of the condition and treatment, interactions with medical professionals, self-management and vulnerability to medical anxiety and trauma. Growing up with the impact of cloaca explores how cloacal malformations are integrated into identity, including decisions around disclosure, and how connecting with others with cloaca offers sense-making opportunities.
CONCLUSION: Growing up with a cloacal malformation and the necessary treatments can significantly impact long term psychological wellbeing and identity formation. It is recommended that psychological aspects are considered as part of routine surgical and clinical care from first contact across the lifespan.

articles.title: Incidence and Management of Pelvic Pain in Patients with Obstructive and Non-Obstructive Müllerian Anomalies.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.authors: Rush MA, Foster H, Babu V et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: The incidence, presentation, and management of pelvic pain in patients with Müllerian anomalies has not been well characterized. This study aimed to determine the incidence of pelvic pain at presentation in patients with obstructive versus non-obstructive Müllerian anomalies and to describe management of pelvic pain in these populations.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with Müllerian anomalies identified at a single academic center from 2008 to 2024. Anomalies were classified as obstructive or non-obstructive using imaging and operative reports in accordance with the 2021 American Society of Reproductive Medicine guidelines. Data collected included demographics, symptoms, hormone use, surgical interventions, and post-treatment pelvic pain. Logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between anomaly type and pelvic pain, adjusting for relevant covariates.
RESULTS: Among 148 patients, 76 had obstructive and 72 had non-obstructive anomalies. Patients with obstructive anomalies presented younger (14.5 ± 5.0 vs. 21.1 ± 8.3 years). Pelvic pain was reported by nearly all post-pubertal patients with obstructive anomalies, and was less common among those with non-obstructive anomalies (100.0% vs. 38.9%, p<0.001). Most patients with obstructive anomalies (86.8%) were treated with surgery. Persistent chronic pelvic pain was common in this cohort after surgery, affecting 50% of patients and requiring postoperative hormonal therapy. Among patients with non-obstructive anomalies, 44.4% underwent surgery, and 19.4% reported chronic pelvic pain.
CONCLUSIONS: Obstructive Müllerian anomalies are strongly associated with earlier age of onset and presentation with pelvic pain. Persistent pain after surgery underscores the need for long-term, multidisciplinary management and further investigation into underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor-23 as a biomarker to refine cardiovascular risk identification: A cross-sectional study in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.authors: Pickering ME, Oris C, Morel V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Postmenopausal osteoporosis presents with heterogeneous comorbidities including cardiovascular disease. Objectives of this study were the identification of clusters of osteoporotic patients in relation to the cardiovascular risk, comorbidities, and levels of intact Fibroblast Growth Factor (iFGF23), a key player of the bone-cardiovascular axis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis took place in the Rheumatology Department, University Hospital Clermont-Ferrand, France. Twelve variables representative of comorbidities were selected according to their associations and clinical relevance: age, bone mineral density, flow-mediated dilation, cardiovascular risk (SCORE2/2OP), muscle mass, handgrip, sleep, quality of life, pain and plasma iFGF23. Multiple correspondence analysis followed by hierarchical clustering was used to propose profiles of patients and associations related to iFGF23 and cardiovascular risk.
RESULTS: Three comorbidity clusters were identified in 102 women (69.1 ± 7.7 years old): clusters of older age with worse outcomes, of younger age with better results and an intermediate cluster. iFGF23 is unveiled as a marker of the cardiovascular risk even in patients with normal renal function, with a threshold of 94.14 ng/L, and is significantly associated with age, fat mass, poor handgrip, poor quality of life, pain and impaired sleep.
CONCLUSIONS: Comorbidity clusters of post-menopausal osteoporosis based on the severity of health impairment highlight in this exploratory study iFGF23 as a possible biomarker of the cardiovascular risk. We suggest that iFGF23 measurement may complement SCORE2/2OP calculation to better predict the cardiovascular risk of osteoporosis patients. A suggested hypothesis-generating algorithm is proposed and future validation in a larger prospective study is warranted.

articles.title: Injectable and bio-responsive hydrogels for on-demand intraperitoneal delivery of anti-cancer therapeutics in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Fan F, Liu Y, Petrosini G et al.
articles.abstract: The standard treatment of ovarian cancer involves surgical resection followed by chemotherapy to target residual microscopic tumors. Current chemotherapy is most commonly delivered intravenously (i.v.) because of the toxicity and difficulty in administering intraperitoneal (i.p.) chemotherapy. However, clinical trials have demonstrated that i.p. chemotherapy is superior to i.v. chemotherapy because it can achieve a higher therapeutic concentration and prolonged retention in the peritoneal cavity. To improve the efficacy and safety of i.p. chemotherapy, we developed an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA)-based hydrogel platform for combinatorial and localized delivery of bevacizumab (BVZ), albumin-bound paclitaxel (nab-paclitaxel, nab-PTX) and carboplatin (CPT) in a manner that responds to the high level of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in the i.p. space. HA and dextran sulfate (DS) are chemically modified to allow hydrogels to form with MMP-degradable crosslinkers in <1 min upon injection. The in vitro release of BVZ, nab-PTX and CPT is sensitive to MMP concentration and is sustained for up to 28 days. The combined release of BVZ, nab-PTX and CPT from the hydrogels effectively inhibits angiogenesis and tumor cell proliferation in vitro. Moreover, the i.p. administration of the hydrogel system results in tumor burden reduction comparable to the multiple injections of the free drug combination, with reduced systemic side effects. Our work suggests that the injectable MMP responsive hydrogel is a promising i.p. delivery system of BVZ, nab-PTX and CPT to improve i.p. retention and clinical therapeutic effects for ovarian cancer treatment with minimum side effects. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This study presents the first use of hydrogels for intraperitoneal delivery of bevacizumab (BVZ), carboplatin (CPT), and albumin-bound paclitaxel (nab-PTX) to locally treat ovarian cancer. An injectable hyaluronic acid (HA)-based hydrogel platform can be engineered for combinatorial and localized delivery of BVZ, nab-PTX, and CPT in a manner that responds to the high level of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in the intraperitoneal (i.p.) space. HA and dextran sulfate (DS) are chemically modified to allow hydrogels to form with MMP-degradable crosslinkers in <1 min upon injection. The combined release of BVZ, nab-PTX and CPT from the hydrogels results in tumor burden reduction comparable to the multiple injections of the free drug combination, with reduced systemic side…

articles.title: Mixture effects of organophosphate flame retardants on human semen quality and sex hormone levels: A weighted quantile sum regression analysis.
articles.authors: Pan HY, Wu WT, Lin YJ et al.
articles.abstract: We evaluated levels of urinary five organophosphorus flame retardant (OPFR) diesters and their primary metabolites, serum sex hormones, and semen quality among men in southern Taiwan. Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear regression and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression models to examine both individual and mixture effects on male reproduction. Each level of bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (BDCPP), tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCPP), and sum of OPFRs (ΣOPFRs) were significantly associated with a reduced percentage of morphologically normal sperm. Di-n-butyl phosphate (DnBP) and TDCPP were positively associated with the proportion of sperm with abnormal mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), BDCPP, tris(n-butyl) phosphate (TnBP), tris(2-butyloxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), triphenyl phosphate (TPHP), and ΣOPFR were positively associated with the estradiol/testosterone ratio. WQS regression demonstrated positively associations between OPFR mixtures, sperm abnormal morphology and MMP. Mixture-based analyses identify TDCPP, TCEP, and DnBP as key contributors to the observed associations with reproductive outcomes in environmental risk assessment.

articles.title: Referral Pattern of Breast Cancer Patients Treated with Tamoxifen or Aromatase Inhibitors to Gynaecology.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Lemay JA, Suarthana E, Côté L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Tamoxifen and Aromatase Inhibitors are commonly used as adjuvant treatment for estrogen receptor positive (ER+) breast cancer. Our objective was to evaluate the gynecological referral of breast cancer patients treated with tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 153 breast cancer patients treated at the McGill University Health Centre (MUHC) between 2015 and 2025. Variables assessed included age, body mass index (BMI), parity, menopausal status, symptoms at presentation (particularly abnormal uterine bleeding [AUB]), type of adjuvant therapy (tamoxifen and/or Aromatase Inhibitor), and findings from pelvic ultrasound, hysteroscopy, endometrial biopsy, and histopathology.
RESULTS: Most patients (n = 143, 93.5%) were premenopausal. Tamoxifen alone was used in 50 patients (34.5%), Aromatase Inhibitors in 34 (24%), and sequential tamoxifen and Aromatase Inhibitors were used in 15 (10.5%). Among the 99 patients treated with tamoxifen and/or Aromatase Inhibitors, 7 (7.1%) experienced AUB, compared to none in the untreated group. Endometrial thickness during treatment was greater in those with AUB (median 11.0 mm, IQR 7.2-16.8) than in those without AUB (median 3.9 mm, IQR 1.5-6.8). Of 153 patients, 19 (12.4%) were referred to gynaecology for AUB and/or thickened endometrium.
CONCLUSION: Only a small proportion of patients with breast cancer treated with tamoxifen or Aromatase Inhibitors are referred for gynaecological evaluation with AUB and/or a thickened endometrium as the main referral indications. Gynaecologic referrals at our institution align with current guidelines, with specialized assessment reserved primarily for symptomatic patients rather than for routine surveillance of asymptomatic patients receiving endocrine therapy.Résumé OBJECTIFS: Le tamoxifène et les inhibiteurs de l'aromatase sont couramment utilisés comme traitement adjuvant dans le cancer du sein à récepteurs d'œstrogènes positifs (ER+). Notre objectif était d'évaluer l'orientation en gynécologie de patientes atteintes d'un cancer du sein et traitées par le tamoxifène ou un inhibiteur de l'aromatase. MéTHODOLOGIE: Nous avons mené une étude de cohorte rétrospective auprès de 153 patientes atteintes d'un cancer du sein et traitées au Centre universitaire de santé McGill (CUSM) entre 2015 et 2025. Les variables évaluées comprenaient l'âge, l'indice de masse corporelle (IMC), la parité, l'état ménopausique, les symptômes initiaux…

articles.title: Reduction in unnecessary oxytocin administration for elective first trimester suction dilation and curettage.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Danesh G, Dephoure S, Elangainesan P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To reduce the rate of unnecessary oxytocin administration during scheduled first trimester uterine aspiration procedures by 50% over an eight-week intervention period.
METHODS: A quality improvement study was implemented at an urban academic ambulatory hospital. Baseline oxytocin use for first trimester uterine aspiration procedures, along with patient and provider characteristics, was recorded during an eight-week retrospective period. Iterative Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles informed the design. The first intervention removed oxytocin from a pre-populated electronic anesthesia standard care pathway, while the second was an educational presentation to anaesthesia and obstetrics providers.
RESULTS: Baseline oxytocin administration was 20% (26/130). The first and second interventions reduced oxytocin use to 10.2% (9/88) and 9.2% (6/65), respectively. Over all time periods combined, advancing gestational age was associated with oxytocin use (OR = 1.364, 95% CI 1.196, 1.556; P = 0.000), while early-career surgeons were less likely to use oxytocin (OR = 0.313, 95% CI 0.150, 0.653; P = 0.002). Adjusted odds ratios for oxytocin administration were 0.360 (95% CI 0.142, 0.838; P = 0.023) and 0.433 (95% CI 0.147, 1.118; P = 0.101), during the first and second interventions, respectively. There was no difference in the administration of antihemorrhagic agents (OR = 2.035, 95% CI 0.527, 7.857; P = 0.303) or surgical bleeding (OR = 6.486, 95% CI 0.397, 105.960; P = 0.190) between the pre and post intervention periods.
CONCLUSION: Simple interventions resulted in a 50% reduction of oxytocin administration for uterine aspiration procedures without increasing the use of antihemorrhagic agents or procedural bleeding.Résumé OBJECTIF: Réduire de 50 % le taux d'administration inutile d'ocytocine lors des aspirations utérines programmées au premier trimestre sur une période d'intervention de huit semaines. MéTHODOLOGIE: Une étude sur l'amélioration de la qualité a été menée dans un hôpital universitaire offrant des soins ambulatoires, en région urbaine. Les données de référence sur l'utilisation de l'ocytocine lors des aspirations utérines au premier trimestre et les caractéristiques des patientes et des prestataires ont été recueillies sur une période rétrospective de huit semaines. La conception de l'étude s'est appuyée sur des cycles PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) itératifs. La première intervention consistait à retirer l'ocytocine d'un parcours de soins anesthésiques…

articles.title: Continuation or Termination? Maternal Outcomes in Severe Fetal Anomalies.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Meir O, Wolf MF, Odeh M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare maternal and obstetric outcomes in pregnancies complicated by severe structural fetal anomalies according to management: continuation versus termination after the threshold of viability.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women with singleton pregnancies complicated by prenatally diagnosed severe structural fetal anomalies managed at a tertiary center from 2010-2025. The primary outcome was a composite of adverse maternal events: cesarean delivery (CD), PPH, placental abruption, blood transfusion, uterine rupture or scar dehiscence, and prolonged maternal hospitalization.
RESULTS: A total of 186 women were included:139 continued the pregnancy and 47 underwent termination. Continuation was associated with higher composite adverse maternal outcomes than termination (55.4% vs 19.1%, P < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, continuation remained independently associated with adverse maternal outcome (aOR = 4.81, 95% CI 1.83-12.65). Polyhydramnios and prior CD were also independent risk factors. In the continuation group, intrauterine fetal demise occurred in 23.1% and neonatal death in 16.3%. In subsequent pregnancies, CD was more common after continuation than termination (40.5% vs 15.0%,P = 0.034).
CONCLUSION: In pregnancies complicated by severe structural fetal anomalies, continuation was associated with greater maternal morbidity, and these risks should be incorporated into counseling alongside fetal prognosis and shared decision-making.

articles.title: Hormone replacement after radiotherapy for premenopausal patients with cervical cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Gray K, McRae K, Kong I et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Radiotherapy is integral to cervical cancer management, but can cause iatrogenic premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) or early menopause, leading to vasomotor symptoms, sexual dysfunction, mood changes, and long-term health risks. Systemic menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is recommended to mitigate these effects in women with POI. Its role is physiologic hormone replacement, termed menopausal replacement therapy (MRT). This study assessed systemic MHT use and prescribing patterns in premenopausal patients treated with radiotherapy for cervical cancer in British Columbia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women aged 18-45 years, diagnosed with cervical cancer, and treated with curative intent primary or adjuvant radiotherapy between January 1 and December 31, 2022. Data was obtained from the BC Cancer Registry and extracted through chart review. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used for analysis.
RESULTS: Fifty-one patients met inclusion criteria (median age 38 years). Most received primary chemoradiotherapy (86.3%), while 13.7% received adjuvant radiotherapy. Overall, 74.5% (n = 38/51) were prescribed MHT after treatment. The proportion of patients receiving MHT was higher among those treated with adjuvant radiotherapy compared to those who received primary chemoradiotherapy (85.7% vs. 72.7%, P = 0.66). Median time to first MHT prescription was 3.47 months after completing radiotherapy (range 2 weeks-2 years). All MHT prescriptions were provided following completion of radiotherapy. Among those prescribed MHT, 63.2% required dose escalation, 78.9% had formulation changes, 18.4% had dose reductions, and 18.4% discontinued therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Three quarters of patients were prescribed MHT. Initiation was delayed until after radiotherapy completion. Frequent dose and formulation adjustments highlight the complexity of survivorship care and the need for standardized counseling and management pathways to improve quality of life.

articles.title: Superparamagnetic iron oxide tracer for sentinel lymph node detection in vulvar cancer: a single-center experience.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Ferreira BS, Brás I, Marques P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility of sentinel lymph node detection using a combined technique with superparamagnetic iron oxide tracer and patent blue dye in patients with vulvar cancer.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included patients with vulvar cancer who underwent sentinel lymph node biopsy at a Portuguese oncological center between 2021 and 2025. Sentinel lymph node mapping was performed in patients with clinically negative groins. The procedure was also performed in selected cases of carcinoma in situ in which stromal invasion could not be preoperatively excluded.
RESULTS: Five patients were included. The median age was 68 years (range 56-86), and all tumors were located in the midline. Final histopathology confirmed squamous cell carcinoma in all cases, including two in situ lesions and three invasive tumors. Sentinel lymph node detection was achieved in all patients (100%), with bilateral detection in four patients (80%) and a detection rate per groin of 90% (9/10). The mean number of sentinel lymph nodes retrieved per patient was 3.4 (range 1-5). In two groins, sentinel lymph nodes were identified exclusively by the magnetic tracer, with no progression of patent blue dye. No metastatic involvement was identified. The median follow-up was 20 months (range 8-51), and no inguinal recurrences were observed.
CONCLUSION: Sentinel lymph node biopsy using a combined magnetic and dye technique was feasible in this series of patients with vulvar cancer and may represent a useful approach in selected patients, although further studies are needed. Résumé.
OBJECTIF: Évaluer la faisabilité du repérage du ganglion sentinelle à l'aide d'un traceur à base d'oxyde de fer superparamagnétique combiné à un colorant bleu breveté chez les patientes atteintes d'un cancer de la vulve. MéTHODOLOGIE: La présente étude observationnelle rétrospective a été menée auprès de patientes atteintes d'un cancer de la vulve qui ont subi une biopsie du ganglion sentinelle dans un centre oncologique portugais entre 2021 et 2025. Une cartographie du ganglion sentinelle a été réalisée pour les patientes dont l'examen clinique des aines s'est avéré négatif. Une cartographie a également été réalisée pour certains cas de carcinome in situ, dans lesquels l'invasion stromale ne pouvait être exclue avant l'intervention chirurgicale. articles.title: Reoperation Rates and Pain-Related Outcomes Following Hysterectomy in Pathologically Confirmed Endometriosis: Impact of Oophorectomy Status.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Salmanpour A, Kaur P, Long AJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate how oophorectomy during a hysterectomy for endometriosis impacts reoperation rates and pain-related healthcare services in a cohort of histopathologically confirmed endometriosis cases.
METHODS: In this population-based retrospective cohort study, we included 990 cases of pathologically confirmed endometriosis in people aged 19-50 years who underwent hysterectomy between 2001 and 2016. The primary outcome was reoperation, and secondary outcomes included physician visits as well as filling prescriptions for opioids, oral contraceptive pills (OCP), and endometriosis medications within the 3-12 months after surgery. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards were used.
RESULTS: Compared to hysterectomy with ovarian conservation, hysterectomy with oophorectomy was associated with lower rates of reoperations (19.2% for hysterectomy with ovarian conservation vs 13.2% for hysterectomy with unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and 4.9% for hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; aHR= 0.56, 95%CI= (0.36-0.88) and aHR= 0.20, 95%CI= (0.12-0.35), respectively). Pelvic peritoneal adhesions, recurrence of endometriosis, and endometrioma were the most common reasons for reoperations. No differences were observed between ovarian conservation versus bilateral oophorectomy in terms of physician visits, as well as opioid, OCP, and endometriosis medication dispensations within three to 12 months after surgery. HRT was filled in only 67.2% of those who entered premature surgical menopause CONCLUSION: Undergoing hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy resulted in a lower rate of reoperation in this cohort of pathologically confirmed endometriosis patients. However, the number of physician visits for endometriosis or pelvic pain, or the rate of pain medication prescriptions, did not suggest an improvement for those who underwent hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy.

articles.title: Physical activity and pregnancy outcomes: an observational study of Greek pregnant women.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Mitrogiannis I, Makrydimas S, Zagoriannakou N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical Activity during pregnancy has been a controversial field for years, despite its widely proven benefits in general population. The benefits of PA in both mother and the fetus should be highlighted to provide new insights.
OBJECTIVE: Examine the association of PA in Greek pregnant women with pregnancy outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: This is a multicenter, prospective, observational study. The participants completed the Greek PPAQ and pregnancy outcomes were collected after birth. The level of PA and consistency with the international PA recommendations was evaluated with the use of METs. All pregnant women speaking greek fluently were eligible. The study was approved by the Ethical Committee of the University Hospital of Ioannina. Statistical analysis was conducted with the R program version 4.3.1. A regression analysis was also conducted for all pregnancy outcomes adjusted to potential cofounders.
RESULTS: A total of 915 pregnant women filled the PPAQ Greek version and were contacted postnatally for the outcomes. Neonates of active pregnant women had a lower median birthweight (3100 g vs 3170g, OR: 1.12, 95% CI:0.54- 2.11), lower incidence of admission to NICU (6.2% vs. 8.2%, OR: 0.76, 95% CI:0.33- 1.54) or neonatal complications (4.7% vs. 7.1%, OR: 0.64, 95% CI:0.24- 1.40). Moreover, pregnancy related hypertensive disorders and gestational diabetes mellitus were lower in the active group (0.01% vs. 3.8% OR: 0.20, 95% CI:0- 1.21 and 11.6% vs. 13.5%, OR: 0.85, 95% CI:0.46- 1.47 respectively). Vaginal delivery was more common in the active group (43% vs. 37.5% OR: 0.81, 95% CI:0.56- 1.19), as well as the incidence of PTB< 37 weeks (6.2% vs. 7.4%, OR: 0.84, 95% CI:0.36- 1.72). After adjusting for confounders, only birthweight differences were statistically significant (p = 0.036; 95% CI: -153, -5.5).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that PA during pregnancy is safe and beneficial for maternal-fetal health in several aspects of pregnancy outcomes. Clinicians should encourage incorporating PA in prenatal care in the absence of complications, while further studies using objective measures are needed to strengthen these findings.

articles.title: Assessment of treatment response response and the role of completion surgery after concurrent CRTand brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer - a review from the French cervical cancer guidelines group.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Mimoun C, Carcopino X, members from the FRENCH CERVICAL CANCER GUIDELINES GROUP et al.
articles.abstract: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by brachytherapy is the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer. However, post-treatment management remains challenging. Accurate response assessment is essential because it informs subsequent management, particularly the indication for completion surgery. Radiation-induced tissue changes may impair the reliability of clinical examination and conventional imaging, while the respective roles of advanced imaging modalities and completion surgery remain debated. Functional lumbopelvic MRI incorporating diffusion-weighted and perfusion sequences is the reference imaging modality for response assessment and provides greater diagnostic performance than clinical examination alone. FDG PET-CT offers complementary information, particularly regarding nodal disease and early metabolic response, but the routine combination of FDG PET-CT with MRI has not been shown to improve diagnostic accuracy. MRI performed early during CRT may help differentiate responders from nonresponders based on changes in the apparent diffusion coefficient. However, the optimal timing of MRI after treatment completion remains uncertain. Available evidence does not support the routine use of conization for response assessment. Completion surgery provides no prognostic benefit and increases morbidity in patients with squamous cell carcinoma who achieve a complete response after CRT and brachytherapy. Evidence remains insufficient to establish its role in adenocarcinoma. When completion surgery is indicated, delaying the procedure until at least 6-8 weeks after CRT may reduce postoperative morbidity. Simple hysterectomy should be favored over radical hysterectomy, which increases morbidity without improving survival. Current evidence demonstrates no superiority of minimally invasive surgery or laparotomy in terms of oncologic outcomes or overall morbidity.

articles.title: The neurobiology of menopause: Implications for brain aging and Alzheimer's risk.
articles.authors: Mosconi L
articles.abstract: A growing body of evidence implicates the menopausal transition as a neurobiological inflection point in women's brain aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) vulnerability. Menopause is a midlife neuroendocrine transition characterized by a decline in sex steroid hormones and widespread systemic effects. The brain is not a passive recipient of ovarian hormones but an active endocrine-sensing organ. Menopause, however, does not act in isolation: the ovarian-brain axis is established embryonically, activated at puberty, remodeled during pregnancy and postpartum, and reconfigured during the menopausal transition, with implications for later-life brain aging. This review places menopause within a lifespan neuroendocrine framework, examining mechanisms by which the transition may influence the brain, including altered hormone signaling, bioenergetics, synaptic plasticity, neurovascular function, inflammation, and AD-related pathology. It then reviews evidence linking menopausal timing to neurobiological and AD vulnerability, discusses estrogen therapy, and considers menopause as a biologically plausible window for risk stratification and prevention.

articles.title: Prospective associations between childhood stress characteristics and prenatal cortisol response to stress.
articles.authors: Laifer LM, Keenan K, Hipwell AE
articles.abstract: Maternal hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis functioning has important implications for maternal and offspring health, yet findings on cortisol responsivity to acute stress during pregnancy are mixed. Further, little is known about how childhood stress exposure relates to physiological stress regulation during this period, particularly among Black and White women. The present study leveraged multiple waves of prospectively gathered data from a large population-based sample to examine associations between degree of exposure to subsistence-, safety- and caregiving-related stress across childhood and cortisol responsivity during a later pregnancy. Participants (N = 338, 69.7% Black, 26.7% White) were enrolled in the longitudinal Pittsburgh Girls Study in middle childhood. Caregivers reported annually on exposure to a range of stressors when participants were 7-17 years of age. During a prenatal laboratory visit in which participants were between 22 and 31 years of age, participants completed the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST) and provided saliva samples for cortisol assay. Adjusting for covariates, the TSST did not produce a significant increase in cortisol levels over time, though 28.3% of participants were classified as responders. Greater exposure to subsistence-related stress (e.g., resource strain, housing instability) across childhood was associated with blunted cortisol levels during pregnancy. Findings suggest that childhood exposure to subsistence-related stress may have enduring effects on physiological stress regulation and underscore the potential value of targeted preventive interventions to promote intergenerational health. Results also highlight the relevance of public health initiatives aimed at reducing population-level differences in subsistence-related stress exposure.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of luteal phase support strategies in natural cycle frozen-thawed embryo transfer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Zeng M, Zhu B, Duan J
articles.abstract:
AIM: Luteal phase support (LPS) may improve pregnancy outcomes in natural cycle frozen-thawed embryo transfer (NC-FET), though the comparative effectiveness of different regimens remains uncertain. This network meta-analysis (NMA) was conducted as an exploratory synthesis.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library was conducted through March 2026. We performed pairwise meta-analyses using Review Manager 5.3 and exploratory network meta-analyses with Stata 14.0. We assessed certainty of evidence using the CINeMA framework.
RESULTS: Twenty studies (8 RCTs, 12 retrospective studies) were included. Pairwise meta-analyses suggested LPS was associated with improved clinical pregnancy rate (CPR) and live birth rate (LBR) compared with no LPS, with no apparent increase in miscarriage rate (MR). The RCT-only NMA could not be performed because the network was disconnected, with no closed loops among the 8 RCTs, reflecting the current lack of head-to-head randomized evidence for LPS regimen selection in NC-FET. In the exploratory full-network analysis, VP + triptorelin + hCG showed a relatively high surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) for CPR, and VP + triptorelin for LBR.
CONCLUSION: LPS was associated with improved pregnancy outcomes in NC-FET. The RCT-only network was too sparse to support valid rankings. While VP + triptorelin ( ± hCG) showed relatively high SUCRA values for CPR and LBR, the very low certainty of evidence precludes definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Comparative prognostic performance of the FIGO 2023 and FIGO 2009 staging systems integrated with molecular classification in endometrial cancer: a retrospective single-centre cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Xia W, Liu B, Kong R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 revision of the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) staging system incorporates molecular classification, aggressive histology, and substantial lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) as key determinants. Its prognostic performance compared with FIGO 2009 requires validation in real-world cohorts.
METHODS: A retrospective review was undertaken of 712 consecutive patients with endometrial carcinoma treated between January 2019 and April 2025. Cases were restaged according to FIGO 2009 and FIGO 2023 integrated with molecular classification (FIGO 2023 m). Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Prognostic discrimination was assessed using Harrell's concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the curve, information criteria, and continuous net reclassification index (NRI).
RESULTS: Stage migration occurred in 26.4% of patients, predominantly due to upstaging driven by p53 abnormality, aggressive histology, and substantial LVSI. Molecular subtypes included. POLE-ultramutated (7.2%), microsatellite instability hypermutated (25.8%), no specific molecular profile (copy-number low) (51.3%), and p53 abnormal (copy-number high) (15.7%). Five-year PFS varied substantially across molecular groups. The C-index improved from 0.712 to 0.785 for PFS, and from 0.725 to 0.811 for OS. The continuous NRI for PFS was 0.241.
CONCLUSIONS: FIGO 2023 m demonstrated superior prognostic discrimination compared with FIGO 2009, supporting incorporation of molecular subtypes into routine endometrial cancer staging and risk assessment. Clinically, this integrated framework may help identify patients at risk of under- or over-treatment, particularly in those with disease previously considered as early stage, although prospective studies are needed before treatment algorithms can be changed definitively.

articles.title: Intrathecal morphine versus fascial plane blocks after caesarean delivery: An updated meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Dost B, Turunc E, Karapinar YE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrathecal morphine (ITM) provides prolonged analgesia after caesarean delivery but causes opioid-related adverse effects. Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) may be an alternative, although their comparative efficacy remains uncertain.
METHODS: We systematically searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus (from inception to 24 July 2026) for randomised controlled trials comparing ITM with FPBs. The primary outcome was 24-h opioid consumption in intravenous morphine milligram equivalents (IV-MME).
RESULTS: Twenty-six trials were included. Fifteen trials involving 1250 participants reported 24-h opioid consumption. ITM produced a small reduction compared with FPBs (mean difference - 3.16 mg IV-MME, 95% confidence interval - 6.30 to - 0.02; p = 0.049; I2 = 96.1%). The prediction interval crossed the null, Egger's test indicated funnel plot asymmetry, and the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis produced a non-significant estimate in the opposite direction. These findings are difficult to interpret in the presence of substantial heterogeneity. TSA showed that the accrued information size was sufficient. Pain scores were similar, with small differences favouring ITM at isolated time points. ITM increased postoperative nausea and vomiting (risk ratio 1.87), pruritus (1.65), urinary retention (3.89), and respiratory depression (2.60). The trim-and-fill estimate for pruritus was not statistically significant, although this finding should also be interpreted cautiously. Effects differed by FPB technique but not by ITM dose. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.
CONCLUSION: The comparative effects of ITM and FPBs varied by block technique, and the findings do not support routine replacement of ITM with FPBs. Selected FPBs may be considered when ITM is not administered, with the choice guided by technique-specific evidence, patient preferences, and the additional procedural time, expertise, and resources required.

articles.title: Sleep deprivation compromises sperm quality and early embryo development by disrupting folate metabolism and DNA repair.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Zhong Y, Zhou Q et al.
articles.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD), a prevalent modern lifestyle issue, has been associated with impaired male reproductive function, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In a mouse model, sustained SD triggered germ cell apoptosis, reduced sperm motility, and increased morphological abnormalities. Furthermore, SD compromised sperm fertilization capacity and impaired preimplantation embryo development. Proteomic analysis identified SLC46A1, a proton-coupled folate transporter, as the only consistently downregulated protein in both testicular tissue and sperm. Furthermore, the expression of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR), a key enzyme in folate metabolism, was also markedly decreased, accompanied by reduced levels of core DNA repair proteins (RAD51 and TOPBP1). Notably, folate supplementation prior to and during SD partially restored the expression of MTHFR, RAD51, and TOPBP1, suggesting that enhanced folate availability can counteract some of the molecular alterations induced by SD. Collectively, our findings suggest a mechanistic link whereby SD disrupts folate transport and metabolism, potentially compromising DNA repair in sperm and thereby impairing sperm quality and embryonic development. This suggests that targeting folate metabolism may offer a therapeutic strategy to mitigate SD-associated male infertility.

articles.title: Platinum-based Nanozyme screening coupled with ISAR-generated pyrophosphate for dual-mode detection of cardiovascular disease-associated miRNA-21.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.ta: Spectrochim Acta A Mol Biomol Spectrosc
articles.authors: Chen M, Zhu J, Xu L et al.
articles.abstract: Early assessment of cardiovascular disease (CVD)-associated molecular alterations may provide valuable information for disease monitoring and clinical evaluation. MicroRNA-21 (miRNA-21) is involved in multiple cardiovascular pathological processes and has been widely investigated as a CVD-associated circulating biomarker. Rationally modulating the activity of platinum-based nanozymes can expand sensing strategies and improve the performance of miRNA-21 detection. Herein, four platinum-based nanozymes are synthesized via a one-step reduction method and systematically evaluate their peroxidase (POD)-like catalytic activities. Among them, the NiPt nanozyme exhibits a favorable apparent peroxidase-like activity under an equal mass concentration, with the lowest Michaelis-Menten constant of 0.462 mM. Then, a colorimetric and fluorescent dual-mode biosensor is developed for the rapid and sensitive detection of miRNA-21 via NiPt nanozyme couple with the target-triggered invading stacking primer-based amplification reaction (ISAR). Sequence-specific hybridization between miRNA-21 and the designed hairpin DNA probe initiates ISAR and generates pyrophosphate (PPi), which suppresses the peroxidase-like activity of NiPt NPs and enables fast, instrument-free, and colorimetric qualitative detection of miRNA-21 at 5 × 10-11 M. Simultaneously, the Cy5 fluorescence signal exhibits sensitive quantitative detection of miRNA-21 with a limit of detection (LOD) of 2.27 × 10-13 M over a linear range of 10-12-10-9 M (R2 = 0.971). The biosensor demonstrated high selectivity toward miRNA-21 against representative interfering miRNA sequences and showed consistency with qRT-PCR in clinical serum samples from heart failure patients and healthy individuals. This dual-mode platform provides a rapid, sensitive, and reliable approach for miRNA-21 detection, demonstrating potential utility for CVD-associated biomarker analysis and further clinical investigation.

articles.title: Longitudinal trajectories of menopausal symptoms in women receiving endocrine therapy for breast cancer compared with natural menopause.
articles.authors: Lee SK, Choi HR, Kang D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endocrine therapy (ETx) for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer frequently induces menopausal symptoms that may compromise treatment adherence. However, longitudinal symptom trajectories compared with natural menopause remain unclear.
METHODS: This longitudinal study included 5734 women from two prospective cohorts: 2583 women with breast cancer from the Breast Cancer Information Grand Round for Survivorship cohort and 3151 women without breast cancer from the Kangbuk Samsung Health Study. Menopausal symptoms were assessed using the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS). Linear mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal changes by breast cancer status, menopausal status, and ETx use. Difference-in-differences (DiD) analyses designated premenopausal women without breast cancer as the reference group.
RESULTS: Among premenopausal women, ETx was associated with greater increases in total MRS scores than in women without breast cancer (DiD, 3.30; 95% CI, 2.04-4.58 at 1 year). Within the breast cancer cohort, premenopausal women receiving ETx experienced sustained increases in menopausal symptoms over 3 years, with the largest increases observed among those receiving regimens including gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists. Among postmenopausal women, ETx was associated with modest changes in total MRS scores but a significant increase in urogenital symptoms (DiD 0.71; 95% CI, 0.26-1.16).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with women without breast cancer, women receiving ETx experienced greater increases in menopausal symptoms during the first year of follow-up. Within the breast cancer cohort, elevated symptom burden persisted over 3 years, particularly among premenopausal women receiving ovarian function suppression. These findings highlight the importance of proactive symptom monitoring and supportive care during long-term endocrine therapy.

articles.title: The mitochondria-immune axis: A self-amplifying vicious cycle driving the pathogenesis of preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Zhu Q, Chen X, Chen Z et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a severe pregnancy-specific disorder and a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. Although the traditional two-stage model links abnormal placentation to maternal endothelial dysfunction, it does not fully explain how placental stress is converted into persistent systemic inflammation. This review reframes the mitochondria-immune axis as a hierarchical and self-amplifying network in PE. In this model, placental hypoxia-reoxygenation, endoplasmic reticulum stress and anti-angiogenic stress act as initiating events that destabilize mitochondrial homeostasis in trophoblasts, endothelial cells and immune cells. Damaged mitochondria then release reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and other danger signals, which activate innate immune sensors, including the NLRP3 inflammasome, cGAS-STING, TLR9 and NF-kB pathways. These pathways induce IL-1β, TNF-α, type I interferon signaling, complement activation, neutrophil extracellular traps and macrophage/T-cell imbalance, which in turn aggravate mitochondrial injury and sustain a pathogenic feedback loop. We further distinguish the likely contribution of this axis across PE subtypes, including early-onset, late-onset, maternal, canonical and immunological PE. The review critically evaluates circulating mtDNA and mitochondria-related genes as biomarkers, emphasizing the effects of sample processing, vesicle-bound mtDNA, cellular contamination, gestational timing and assay choice. Therapeutic opportunities are discussed according to translational maturity, from clinically relevant supportive approaches and PE-tested preclinical interventions to extrapolated mitochondrial and immunopharmacological strategies. Overall, the mitochondria-immune axis provides a structured framework for subtype-aware biomarker development and mechanism-guided intervention in PE, while highlighting the need for standardized longitudinal cohorts and pregnancy-specific safety validation.

articles.title: Intrauterine exposures to legacy and emerging PFAS in the first trimester and their associations with early pregnancy loss.
articles.authors: Liu A, Ran M, Tian Y et al.
articles.abstract: Exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including emerging substitutes, is associated with several adverse pregnancy outcomes. However, the evidence on intrauterine exposure to PFAS during human early pregnancy was limited. This study measured the concentrations of 31 (18 legacy and 13 emerging) PFAS chemicals in 402 maternal serum and 221 placental villi tissues collected during the first trimester. The associations of individual and combined PFAS exposures with early pregnancy loss (EPL) were estimated using multivariable generalized additive models, logistic regression models, quantile g-computation, subgroup stratified, and interaction analyses. Six PFAS chemicals detected simultaneously in the serum and villi with detection rates exceeding 80% showed strong correlations between the two matrices, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.78 to 0.93, and with 9-chlorohexadecafluoro-3-oxanonane-1-sulfonate (9Cl-PF3ONS) exhibiting the highest correlation. Odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) of EPL were 1.72 (1.04, 2.83), 2.18 (1.02, 4.69), 1.99 (1.04, 3.79), 2.66 (1.35, 5.22), and 5.17 (2.30, 11.63) associated with per ten-fold increase in the concentrations of serum 9Cl-PF3ONS, serum perfluorohexane sulfonate (PFHxS), serum perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), villi 9Cl-PF3ONS, and villi perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), respectively. However, the associations of serum 9Cl-PF3ONS, PFHxS, and PFOS with EPL were no longer statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. The joint association between PFAS mixture in villi and EPL was positive, with 9Cl-PF3ONS having the largest positive weights. Subgroups with age ≤ 30 years, body mass index ≥ 24 kg/m2, or tobacco exposure showed higher odds ratios of EPL associated with specific PFAS chemicals. In conclusion, emerging substitute 9Cl-PF3ONS could arrive at early placenta. Maternal and placental exposure to PFAS including 9Cl-PF3ONS showed positive associations with EPL; however, the findings in serum should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Effect of empowering mothers of children with nocturnal enuresis on knowledge, practices and quality of life.
articles.authors: Elsawy MM, Shokr EA, Atress MS et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturnal enuresis adversely affects school-aged children and family quality of life.
AIM: To evaluate the effect of the empowerment program on mothers' knowledge, self-reported practices, and quality of life.
DESIGN: Two-arm randomized controlled trial with assessments at baseline, four weeks, and three months post-intervention.
METHODS: At the outpatient urinary incontinence clinic of the Center for Social and Preventive Medicine, Cairo University, Egypt, 200 purposively recruited mothers were randomly assigned 1:1 using a computer-generated sequence with allocation concealed in numbered, sealed envelopes. Outcomes were assessed using two researcher-developed, content-validated instruments and a modified Arabic Pediatric Enuresis Module on Quality of Life, Short Form. Linear mixed models compared groups over time.
RESULTS: Groups were comparable at baseline. Group × time interactions favored the intervention for knowledge (F(2, 396) = 124.5), practices (F(2, 396) = 68.9), and quality of life (F(2, 396) = 92.3); all p < 0.001. At three months, improvements in intervention versus control groups were 8.23 versus 1.30 points for knowledge, 3.84 versus 0.72 for practices, and 19.9 versus 3.5 for quality of life. Between-group effect sizes were large (Cohen's d = 2.12, 1.17, and 1.78, respectively).
CONCLUSION: The program improved mothers' knowledge, self-reported practices, and quality of life, with effects maintained at three months. These mother-reported outcomes do not demonstrate improvement in children's enuresis.
RECOMMENDATIONS: The program may be considered an adjunct to standard care in outpatient settings. Multicenter trials with longer follow-up and objective child outcomes are needed before routine implementation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.govNCT07753304 (retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
articles.authors: Payne T, Liu D, Frawley T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.
METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination.
RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%).
DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

articles.title: Paroxetine-induced transient apoptosis with delayed neurogenesis triggers brain-preferential regeneration in developing zebrafish.
articles.authors: Sato T, Saito K, Oyu T et al.
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition caused by a combination of genetic and environmental factors. Its cardinal symptoms include impaired social behavior involving the amygdala. Maternal use of antidepressants such as paroxetine during early pregnancy increases the risk of ASD in offspring. However, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that early exposure of zebrafish embryos to paroxetine delays neurogenesis in the optic tectum and telencephalon, including a region corresponding to the mammalian amygdala. Paroxetine-treated embryos exhibit growth restriction characterized by small heads and short-body lengths resulting from transient apoptosis. This phenotype resembles the early-onset fetal growth restriction (FGR) associated with ASD. Interestingly, we observed regeneration of delayed neurogenesis in the reduced brain following paroxetine withdrawal. This regenerative process was accompanied by extended retinotectal projections, suggesting brain-preferential regeneration. Finally, we examined the social behavior of paroxetine-treated fish. Taken together, our findings suggest a biological mechanism linking early paroxetine exposure, a risk factor for ASD, to its pathogenesis.

articles.title: Short and long-term outcomes after gestational diabetes diagnosis using different glycemic criteria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Liu Q, Mayer DFR, Harding JE et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Lower gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic criteria on an oral glucose tolerance test are widely recommended, but their impacts on maternal, neonatal, long-term and economic outcomes remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare outcomes after GDM diagnosis using lower versus higher diagnostic strategies.
METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing outcomes following assessment for GDM and treatment if indicated, using lower versus higher glycemic diagnostic criteria or thresholds in four databases and four trial registries (PROSPERO registration CRD420251183179) to 27th July 2026. Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias, conducted random-effects meta-analyses and evaluated GRADE certainty.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included, with nine RCTs and one cohort study contributing to the meta-analysis (81,528 women). Lower diagnostic criteria or thresholds, compared with higher diagnostic criteria or thresholds, doubled GDM diagnosis and pharmacotherapy use, increased neonatal hypoglycemia (RCTs: 18 more per 1,000; 95% CI 11 to 25 more) and maternal-neonatal separation (RCTs: 6 more per 1,000; 95% CI 1 to 12 more), but had little to no effect on other short-term outcomes. Longer-term evidence was limited to follow-up of one RCT reporting reduced maternal hypertension and child neurodevelopmental impairment but increased subsequent GDM at five-year follow-up with use of lower criteria or thresholds. Findings on GDM-related healthcare costs were inconsistent, with no long-term economic data.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower diagnostic criteria increased the diagnosis of GDM and some aspects of healthcare utilization, without improving short-term outcomes. Limited evidence suggested possible longer-term benefits, warranting further long-term follow-up from high-quality RCTs.

articles.title: Sex-specific mechanisms and therapeutics in heart failure: translating biology into personalized care.
articles.authors: Papp Z, von Haehling S, Biegus J et al.
articles.abstract: Sex is one of the most consistent, yet clinically underexploited, determinants of heart failure (HF) phenotype, mechanism, and outcome. Building on landmark reviews and the 2024 scientific statement of the Heart Failure Association, which documented well-recognized phenotypic differences but noted that their mechanisms remain only partially defined, this review examines how sex differences in HF arise and how firmly they should guide practice. Epidemiologically, female predominance in HF with preserved ejection fraction (EF) is age- and menopause-dependent rather than lifelong. Mechanistically, sex-divergent hormonal signalling, autonomic tone, coronary microvascular dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis often produce similar phenotypes through different mechanisms: microvascular dysfunction is similarly prevalent in both sexes but linked to fibrosis in women and atherosclerotic risk factors in men, and oestradiol regulates collagen synthesis in opposite directions in female and male cardiac fibroblasts. Clinically, comorbidities carry divergent prognostic weight by sex. Graded against the strength of evidence, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors show established sex-neutral efficacy, whereas the greater benefit of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism in women rests on subgroup signals that await confirmation. Natriuretic peptide concentrations are substantially sex-dependent, yet diagnostic thresholds remain sex-neutral, although sex-specific calibration is methodologically achievable. Women remain underrepresented in HF trials and less often referred to specialized care. HF is therefore best understood as a sex-differentiated syndrome whose frameworks were built largely around male-pattern disease. Sex-calibrated trial enrolment, sex-specific biomarker and EF thresholds, and stratification by menopausal stage are concrete next steps towards personalized care.

articles.title: Pregnancy in patients with type 1 diabetes and diabetic nephropathy: sailing between Scylla and Charybdis.
articles.authors: Chiara M, Lida T, Federica E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy in women with type 1 diabetes (T1D) complicated by overt diabetic nephropathy (DN) remains a major clinical challenge, with limited data on maternal-foetal outcomes. This study describes the clinical course and outcomes of pregnancies in women with overt DN followed in a dedicated nephrology-obstetric care setting.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis including 15 pregnancies, 13 of which had complete baseline and delivery data, in women with T1D and overt DN followed at Policlinico Umberto I (Rome-Italy), between 2010 and 2022. Maternal characteristics, renal and obstetric complications, and perinatal outcomes were analysed from baseline to six months postpartum.
RESULTS: Thirteen pregnancies were analysed. Median baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 67.6 (42.9-95.8) ml/min/1.73m2, median proteinuria 0.8 (0.5-1.6) g/day; 69% had chronic hypertension and 84% diabetic retinopathy. Proteinuria increased during pregnancy in 9/13 cases. Two patients developed acute kidney injury, one of whom required haemodialysis during pregnancy and remained dialysis-dependent thereafter. Superimposed preeclampsia occurred in five cases and was associated with lower baseline eGFR. Preterm delivery was common; all the patients delivered by caesarean section. A decline ≥10 mL/min/1.73 m2 in eGFR or dialysis initiation was observed in 4 patients at 6-month follow-up; in the remaining patients, no significant changes were observed, although the follow-up was limited to 6 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy in women with overt DN continues to entail substantial maternal and foetal risk. Early nephrology referral, strict metabolic and blood pressure control, and systematic preconception counselling are crucial to optimising outcomes and preventing irreversible renal decline.

articles.title: Cultural and structural barriers to HPV vaccine acceptance among young women in the United Arab Emirates.
articles.authors: Langhe R, AlKhatib A, Saber A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus, and oncogenic genotypes are linked to cervical cancer. Vaccination reduces cervical cancer burden, yet uptake remains suboptimal in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) despite national immunisation initiatives. This exploratory study aimed to identify and characterize potential cultural and structural barriers that may impede vaccine uptake among educated, digitally connected women in the UAE to inform future, more representative research.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, descriptive study surveyed 1455 women aged 18-30 years across all emirates regarding vaccination status, cultural beliefs, and institutional factors influencing vaccine acceptance and uptake.
RESULTS: The participants were predominantly educated, non-Emirati, digitally connected young women (mean age 22.4 years, 77.7% non-Emirati, 44.8% healthcare-affiliated). While 58.8% respondents viewed vaccination as culturally acceptable, only 26.2% admitted to being vaccinated. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination included concerns about side effects, feeling too young for vaccination, and fear of family judgment (47.5%, 28.4%, 27.8%, respectively). The most reported reason for receiving the vaccine was its inclusion in the immunisation schedule (37.9%), followed by parental consent and encouragement (36.6%), and for self-protection purposes (25.6%). Furthermore, acceptance increased when the vaccine was presented as a cancer prevention strategy (64.6%), offered at more convenient location (63.8%) or made more affordable (61.5%).
CONCLUSION: Overall, the primary barriers to vaccination included concerns regarding the fear of public judgment, reflecting a combination of informational gaps, timing-related considerations, and sociocultural influences affecting HPV vaccine uptake. Future research employing representative sampling is needed to determine whether these barriers generalize to broader UAE populations including non-digitally connected, non-healthcare workers, and Emirati women. Once population level barriers are identified through representative research, public health strategies can be designed to address context-appropriate concerns through targeted education on vaccine safety and culturally sensitive engagement with families and young women to improve uptake.

articles.title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore.
articles.authors: Blythe R, Graves N, Iyer NG et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers.
METHODS: We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type. We applied sex- and cancer-specific Cox regressions to the Singapore Cancer Registry for annual predicted survival from 1992 to 2022. These were combined with census and employment data to estimate HPV-associated income losses in Singapore. Attributable fractions and vaccine effectiveness data for HPV 16/18 from the literature were used to estimate the effectiveness of bivalent HPV vaccination. Structural sensitivity analysis examined the role of 80% population coverage conferring herd immunity.
RESULTS: The registry contained 17,294 individuals with an HPV-associated cancer diagnosis. Lost income was greatest for cervical cancer due to its high prevalence, however the losses per diagnosis were highest for oropharyngeal cancer.
