Bivalent HPV vaccination led to income benefits of $SGD1,397 [$895 to $1,838] in girls and -$62 [-$76 to -$48] in boys. A gender-neutral HPV vaccination of 80% of 15-year-old Singaporeans, conferring herd immunity, would have lifetime income protective benefits of $24.4m [$14.2m, $33.7m] per cohort, a five-fold return on investment.
CONCLUSIONS: In addition to avoiding healthcare costs and lost quality of life, parents should consider vaccination as a means of avoiding potential income losses. A national policy of gender-neutral HPV vaccination could deliver substantial income protection due to both individual vaccine protection and herd immunity.

articles.title: Pregnant women's health beliefs about pre-eclampsia in a resource-limited setting: A qualitative study.
articles.authors: Garti I, Menlah A, Fuafugo E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pre-eclampsia, a high-risk pregnancy complication, poses significant threats to maternal and fetal health. Globally, little is known about how women navigate a pre-eclampsia diagnosis or their perceptions of the pathology, unpredictable course, and treatment. Guided by the Health Belief model, this study explores pregnant women's beliefs about pre-eclampsia in Ghana's most populous region.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted at a district hospital in the Ashanti Region of Ghana to explore pregnant women's narratives of their health beliefs and perceptions regarding pre-eclampsia. Sixteen participants were purposively selected, and one-on-one semi-structured interviews were conducted in October 2021. Data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Categories were developed inductively from participants' accounts and subsequently interpreted in relation to the constructs of the Health Belief Model.
RESULTS: Pregnant women's risk perceptions of pre-eclampsia varied, with some not perceiving personal risk, while a few felt vulnerable based on community experiences and observations of other women. Pre-eclampsia was widely regarded as a serious condition, with many expressing fears of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Participants recognized the benefits of antenatal care and lifestyle modifications in reducing risk and empowering care-seeking, while previous experiences with pre-eclampsia and guidance from health providers served as key cues to action. However, several barriers to care were identified, including financial constraints, mistrust of the health system, and inadequate communication from health providers.
CONCLUSION: This study highlights the need for context-specific approaches to address health beliefs related to pre-eclampsia. Strengthening maternal health literacy, effective risk communication, and respectful care can improve early recognition, care-seeking, and outcomes for pre-eclampsia.

articles.title: Rising contraceptive use, falling couple concordance: A mixed-methods analysis of the concordance paradox in Nigeria.
articles.authors: Sanni OF, Sanni AE, Onyeagwaibe CI
articles.abstract: Couple agreement on contraception is widely treated as a marker of programme success, yet whether such agreement has kept pace with rising contraceptive use in sub-Saharan Africa is largely unknown. We analysed three rounds of the Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey Couples' Recode (2013, 2018, 2024; 23,547 couples) using design-weighted descriptive, trend, and multivariable logistic analyses. We defined practice concordance from partners' independently reported current method status and decomposed it into five mutually exclusive categories. A qualitative study of 42 Ogun State couples illustrated the mechanism behind the pattern. National practice concordance fell from 81.6% to 73.5% (and from 70.0% to 46.4% in Ogun State) even as women's modern use (9.7% to 16.1%), spousal communication (33.0% to 42.1%), and Unmet need (16.1% to 21.3%) rose. Concordance was overwhelmingly shared non-use (69.5% in 2024); genuine mutual active use remained near 4%; and wife-only discordance nearly doubled (7.5% to 14.0%), which supplied most of the offsetting rise in discordance as shared non-use contracted. An inverse socioeconomic gradient and a north-south gradient persisted after adjustment, and spousal communication was negatively associated with concordance (odds ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.76-0.91). Rising, increasingly female-led contraceptive practice is associated at the population level with falling couple concordance, a pattern consistent with an incomplete gender transition rather than programme failure.

articles.title: HPV-associated extracellular vesicles and the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms of immune modulation and translational implications.
articles.authors: Goodarzi M, Aghbash PS, Baghi HB
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus infections are a major cause of cervical cancer and are also associated with several anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies. Persistent infection with high-risk HPV types and sustained expression of viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 contribute to malignant transformation. Extracellular vesicles are increasingly recognized as important mediators of intercellular communication and can transfer proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and other regulatory molecules between cells. HPV-associated changes in EV cargo, such as viral transcripts, may influence immune and stromal cells within the tumor microenvironment. Experimental studies have implicated HPV-associated EVs in the regulation of dendritic cell function, macrophage polarization, T-cell responses, immune checkpoint signaling, chronic inflammation, and mechanisms related to viral persistence and immune evasion. Cell-based and preclinical studies also suggest that EVs released by HPV-positive tumor cells may contribute to related disorders including angiogenesis and metastatic progression. On the other hand, human studies have primarily provided observational evidence linking EV-associated molecular profiles with HPV status or disease characteristics. Beyond these mechanistic insights, a growing body of work explores the translational potential of EVs, including their use as liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as engineered delivery platforms such as Nefmut-based vesicles carrying HPV16 E7 that elicit protective CD8 + T-cell responses in preclinical models. This narrative review, with emphasis on tumor-immune interactions, and also discusses emerging diagnostic and therapeutic applications together with the methodological and clinical barriers that must be addressed before EV-based strategies can be translated into routine practice.

articles.title: Multifaceted HPV16 E2 as a potential therapeutic target for cervical cancer and beyond.
articles.authors: Mo X, Wang H, Wang Z et al.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) can cause a variety of epithelial lesions, including the malignant proliferation of host cells and even cervical cancer. HPV E2 can play an important role in regulating viral gene expression, viral replication and transcription, and also can participate in the isolation of viral genome during cell division. HPV16 E2 protein is highly expressed in low-differentiated cervical lesion cells, but decreased or disappeared with the increase of cervical lesion grade. As both the initiation protein for DNA replication and the major transcriptional regulator for HPV16 gene expression, E2 protein may play a key role in the viral life cycle. HPV16 E2 protein as a sequence specific DNA binding protein, can bind with the specific DNA recognition sequence on the promoters of E6 and E7 oncogenes, and then inhibit the transcription and expression of E6 and E7 oncogenes, thus inducing cell apoptosis and suppressing tumor formation. Therefore, therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing HPV16 E2 function may hold promise for the prevention and treatment of HPV-related cancers, including (i) gene-therapy-mediated E2 restoration; (ii) direct delivery of E2 protein; (iii) E2 stabilization through modulation of interacting pathways (e.g., TopBP1, Brd4); and (iv) E2-based therapeutic vaccines. These approaches may exert antitumor effects by repressing E6/E7 oncogenes, regulating the cell cycle, inhibiting cell proliferation, and inducing apoptosis.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound in the combined diagnosis of endometrial polyps: a retrospective observational study.
articles.authors: Huang L, Zhang P
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial polyps (EP) are common benign lesions that require early and accurate diagnosis. Hysteroscopy, considered the gold standard, is invasive; although transvaginal ultrasonography (TVUS) is the preferred initial imaging modality, its diagnostic performance warrants systematic evaluation. This study aimed to compare different application modalities of TVUS in the diagnosis of EP.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 109 patients with suspected EP (January 2022-July 2024). All underwent preoperative transabdominal sonography (TAS) and two-dimensional TVUS (2D-TVUS). Using hysteroscopy plus histopathology as reference, we compared TAS, 2D-TVUS, and their combination for sensitivity (Sen), specificity (Spe), positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), accuracy (Acc), and Kappa.
RESULTS: The confirmed diagnosis rate of EP was 84.4% (92/109). 2D-TVUS demonstrated superior accuracy and consistency (88.07%, Kappa = 0.612) compared with TAS (84.4%, Kappa = 0.493). The combined modality achieved the best performance across all metrics (Sen 93.48%, Spe 88.24%, Acc 92.66%), which was significantly better than either modality alone.
CONCLUSIONS: The combined use of 2D-TVUS and TAS can enhance the diagnostic efficacy for EP and may offer complementary diagnostic value in specific clinical settings. However, its routine application requires validation through prospective multicenter studies.

articles.title: Long-term MRI surveillance of hepatocellular adenomas selected for conservative management: time to regression after oral contraceptive cessation.
articles.authors: Jain N, Kim TK, Khalili K et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the long-term MRI evolution of hepatocellular adenomas (HCAs) selected for conservative management and to quantify the time to predefined degrees of lesion size reduction after oral contraceptive pill (OCP) cessation.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, adults with pathologically proven or imaging-typical HCA who underwent serial liver MRI between January 2010 and December 2024 were reviewed. Up to three indexed lesions per patient were tracked, and lesion evolution was categorized using predefined lesion-level size-change thresholds derived from RECIST 1.1 conventions. In lesions from patients with documented post-diagnosis OCP cessation, time to ≥ 10%, ≥ 20%, and ≥ 30% diameter reduction was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Primary outcomes were repeated in one-lesion-per-patient sensitivity analyses (largest lesion per patient).
RESULTS: 116 patients (110 women; mean age 38 ± 10 years) with 269 HCAs; median follow-up 6.5 years. Among 174 lesions selected for continued conservative management, 166 (95.4%) were stable or regressed. In an exploratory subgroup of 17 lesions with baseline diameter ≥ 5 cm, all were stable or regressive and 11 (64.7%) measured below 5 cm at last imaging. Among 81 lesions after OCP cessation, median times to ≥ 10%, ≥ 20%, and ≥ 30% diameter reduction were 8.6, 24.3, and 49.9 months (95% CI for ≥ 30%, 36.2-75.1). Findings were similar in sensitivity analyses. Both observed malignant transformations occurred in β-catenin-activated HCA, with no surveillance hemorrhage.
CONCLUSION: In this selected surveillance cohort, most HCAs managed without intervention remained stable or decreased in size during long-term MRI follow-up. After OCP cessation, regression was gradual, with modest reduction often apparent within the first year but larger reductions frequently requiring several years; findings in the small ≥ 5 cm subgroup were exploratory. Limited early size reduction should therefore not, in isolation, be interpreted as failure of conservative management.

articles.title: Syncytiotrophoblast differentiation defects drive ER stress and reprogram placental PSG1 glycosylation in preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Harms C, Wang Y, Warren J et al.
articles.abstract: During pregnancy, placenta-derived proteins such as pregnancy-specific glycoprotein 1 (PSG1) enter the maternal circulation, providing a window into placental health and enabling liquid biopsy strategies for monitoring pregnancy disorders. PSG1, a highly glycosylated protein secreted by syncytiotrophoblast (STB) cells, reflects trophoblast differentiation status. Circulating PSG1 levels are reduced in early-onset preeclampsia (PE), but how PSG1 glycosylation is altered in this condition remains unclear. Here, we show by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry that native PSG1 purified from healthy and early-onset PE pregnancies carries an O-linked glycan in its N domain in addition to diverse N-linked glycans. In PE, PSG1 N-glycans displayed a shift toward increased oligomannose structures and reduced sialylation. Induction of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in primary STBs altered the glycosylation enzyme machinery, and single-nucleus transcriptomic data indicated a reduced contribution of mature STB populations in PE, consistent with an immature STB-like glycoprotein signature. Altered N-glycosylation increased binding to mannose and asialoglycoprotein receptors and cellular uptake, suggesting enhanced hepatic clearance as a possible explanation for reduced circulating PSG1 levels in PE. Our data link ER stress during STB differentiation to altered glycoprotein maturation and identify PSG1 glycosylation as a readout of a stress-impaired STB in PE. Glycan features of circulating placental proteins could therefore provide information beyond protein levels alone and complement liquid biopsy approaches.

articles.title: Phospholipase C Zeta 1 Supports Post-Fertilization Embryo Development beyond Oocyte Activation: Evidence from Sperm mRNA Analysis and Functional Studies.
articles.authors: Park MS, Kim JW, Kim JH et al.
articles.abstract: Phospholipase C zeta 1 (PLCZ1), the principal sperm-derived factor, initiates intracellular calcium (Ca²⁺) oscillations at fertilization; however, its contribution to post-fertilization embryonic development remains unclear. This study investigated whether PLCZ1 protein and PLCZ1 mRNA levels influence embryo quality beyond their canonical role in oocyte activation (OA) in human assisted reproductive technology (ART) cycles and functionally examined this hypothesis using a mouse embryo model. Sperm PLCZ1 protein expression assessed in 48 infertile couples undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection significantly correlated with clinical fertilization rates. Sperm PLCZ1 mRNA levels were significantly higher in samples from patients producing good quality embryos (Grade A or B) than in those from patients yielding poor quality embryos (Grade C and D, p < 0.001), independent of paternal age. Functionally, microinjection of human PLCZ1 (hPLCZ1) cRNA into mouse metaphase II oocytes induced repetitive Ca²⁺ oscillations, thus confirming biological activity. Injecting hPLCZ1 cRNA into mouse pronuclear-stage embryos following parthenogenetic activation significantly enhanced blastocyst development compared with that in diethyl pyrocarbonate-treated water-injected controls (p = 0.0101), achieving rates comparable to those of diploid embryos generated using cytochalasin B treatment. These findings are consistent with a dual-component model in which sperm-derived PLCZ1 protein initiates OA at fertilization, while sperm-derived PLCZ1 mRNA is translationally competent within the oocyte and may contribute to sustained post-fertilization PLCZ1 activity and preimplantation developmental competence. Because the functional data were generated with exogenous cRNA rather than by manipulating the endogenous sperm transcript, this model remains a hypothesis that will require loss-of-function validation in future work. Despite limitations such as the moderate clinical sample size and use of mRNA as a surrogate for PLCZ1 protein in clinical samples, sperm PLCZ1 mRNA quantification represents a candidate, hypothesis-generating biomarker for embryo quality that warrants prospective validation.

articles.title: The role of microbial enzymes in intervention strategies for metabolic diseases targeting the gut microbiota.
articles.authors: Gao Y, Gao X, Wang K et al.
articles.abstract: Metabolic diseases-including obesity, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), atherosclerosis (AS), and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)-pose a significant global health crisis due to their rapidly increasing prevalence. The therapeutic potential of the gut microbiota and its metabolites is gaining recognition, with microbial enzymes playing a pivotal role. These enzymes catabolize dietary fibers into mono- and oligo-saccharides, ultimately yielding beneficial short-chain fatty acids, while concurrently converting phytochemicals into absorbable, bioactive small molecules. An increasing array of small-molecule agonists and inhibitors has been developed to target microbial pathways, such as bile acid metabolism and trimethylamine formation. Furthermore, engineered bacteria and fecal microbiota transplantation are gaining traction as promising therapeutic strategies. This review synthesizes evidence on how microbial enzymes underpin these diverse interventions, aiming to advance the development of microbial enzyme-based management strategies for metabolic diseases.

articles.title: Research hotspots and dynamic trends in sacral neuromodulation for pelvic floor dysfunction: a comprehensive bibliometric analysis.
articles.authors: Ma T, Song Y, Ma F et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) includes urinary and bowel dysfunction, chronic pelvic pain, and sexual dysfunction and can substantially impair quality of life. Sacral neuromodulation (SNM) is uesd for selected refractory urinary and bowel disorders, while evidence for other PFD domains continues to develop. We aimed to characterize publication patterns, contributors, collaboration networks, co-citation structures, and keyword trends in the literature on SNM for PFD. Publications on SNM for PFD from January 2000 to November 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Bibliometric and visual analyses were conducted using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R software to evaluate temporal trends, geographic and institutional distributions, journal and author productivity, reference co-citation networks, and keyword dynamics. A total of 1986 publications (1520 original articles and 466 reviews) were included. Annual publication output increased overall during the study period, with year-to-year fluctuations. The United States (n = 681), the United Kingdom (n = 276), the Netherlands (n = 135), and China (n = 125) contributed the largest numbers of publications. Neurourology and Urodynamics, Colorectal Disease, and Diseases of the Colon & Rectum were the most productive journals. The strongest reference bursts were observed for Wexner SD (2010; strength 32.91), Matzel KE (2017; strength 30.40), and Lightner DJ (2019; strength 30.19). Keyword analyses were dominated by sacral neuromodulation, sacral nerve stimulation, fecal incontinence, efficacy, and quality of life; keywords with bursts continuing through 2025 included percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, overactive bladder, and urgency urinary incontinence. This bibliometric analysis maps publication growth, major contributors, collaboration patterns, co-citation structures, and keyword themes in the literature on SNM for PFD. Urinary and bowel dysfunction were the most prominent research themes, whereas chronic pelvic pain and sexual dysfunction were less represented in the keyword analyses. By identifying major thematic concentrations, patterns of scientific collaboration, and comparatively underrepresented topics, these findings may support hypothesis generation, prioritization of future studies on SNM across different PFD domains, and stronger international and interdisciplinary collaboration.

articles.title: Cigarette smoking and circulating androgens in women from the Epic Florence cohort.
articles.authors: Doccioli C, Bendinelli B, Assedi M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The harmful effects of smoking on health include respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, adverse reproductive outcomes, and an increased risk of several cancers, including breast cancer. While the effect of circulating estrogens on breast cancer development is well established, recent studies suggest androgen involvement, but little is known about lifestyle factors influencing their levels. We investigated the relationship between smoking habits and circulating androgen levels in pre- and postmenopausal women.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study on 867 women randomly selected from participants enrolled in the EPIC Florence study between 1993 and 1998. At enrollment, participants provided data on diet, lifestyle, reproductive history, and anthropometry. Blood samples were collected, aliquoted, and stored in liquid nitrogen. To assess the association between active smoking and circulating androgens, we used linear regression models adjusted for age, body mass index, waist circumference, education level, physical activity level, alcohol consumption, caloric intake, and reproductive history, separately for pre- and postmenopausal women.
RESULTS: In pre- and postmenopausal women, current smokers had higher testosterone (premenopause: exp(β) 1.13; 95% CI 1.01-1.26 and postmenopause: exp(β) 1.13; 95% CI 1.00-0.26) and androstenedione levels (premenopause: exp(β) 1.14; 95% CI 1.04-1.26 and postmenopause: exp(β) 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.28) compared to never smokers. A significant trend toward increasing androstenedione with increasing pack-years of smoking was observed in postmenopausal women.
CONCLUSIONS: Our analysis revealed a direct association between circulating levels of testosterone and androstenedione and smoking habit, and a dose-response effect for androstenedione in postmenopausal women. This association could provide insights into the mechanisms linking smoking to breast cancer risk.

articles.title: Virulence and genetic determinants of Staphylococcus spp. in human mastitis: a prevalence study.
articles.authors: Patel M, Gondkar P, Patel K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lactational mastitis is a common inflammatory breast disease affecting breastfeeding women and is associated with Staphylococcus spp. Increasing antimicrobial resistance and virulence among these pathogens complicate treatment and emphasize the need for accurate laboratory diagnostic methods. This study investigated the microbiological profile, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence characteristics of Staphylococcus spp. isolated from lactational mastitis and evaluated the correlation between phenotypic and molecular detection of major virulence and methicillin-resistance determinants.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in central Gujarat, India, using 180 human milk samples collected from 150 women with lactational mastitis and 30 healthy lactating controls. Somatic cell count, bacterial isolation, biochemical identification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, haemolysis, slime production, biofilm assays, polymerase chain reaction detection of the hla, icaA, and mecA genes, and phylogenetic analysis were performed. All mastitis samples exhibited somatic cell counts exceeding 1,000 cells/µL, whereas healthy controls remained below this threshold (p < 0.001). Staphylococcus spp. accounted for 89.4% of isolates. The icaA, hla, and mecA genes were detected in 76.39%, 54.65%, and 46.58% of isolates, respectively. Phenotypically, biofilm formation, alpha-haemolysis, and cefoxitin resistance were observed in 72.67%, 52.79%, and 37.88% of isolates, respectively. Excellent agreement was observed between the corresponding phenotypic and molecular findings, with κ values of 0.89 for icaA/biofilm formation, 0.97 for hla/alpha-haemolysis, and 0.89 for mecA/cefoxitin resistance.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated somatic cell count effectively distinguished mastitis from healthy controls. The high prevalence of virulent and antimicrobial-resistant Staphylococcus spp., particularly mecA-positive isolates, underscores the need for continuous surveillance, targeted antimicrobial therapy, and cost-effective phenotypic screening to support routine clinical diagnosis and epidemiological monitoring.

articles.title: Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India.
articles.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
articles.authors: Mummadi MK, Koshy R, Rajitha ET et al.
articles.abstract: Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency, once considered controlled in India, has re-emerged in parts of Northeast India, raising concern for maternal and infant health. We conducted a community-based cross-sectional study during 2023-2024 to estimate its prevalence and dietary determinants among pregnant and lactating women in the Barak Valley of Assam and adjoining districts of Tripura. Using multistage cluster sampling, women were recruited from 120 villages with documented beriberi clusters. Thiamine status was assessed by determining the erythrocyte transketolase activation coefficient (ETKAC), a functional marker, and whole-blood thiamine diphosphate (ThDP), a biochemical marker measured by high-performance liquid chromatography. Of 1329 women, 1083 were analyzed. Both markers gave similar estimates of suboptimal status: 20.1% by ThDP (95% CI: 17.8-22.6; deficient: 4.9%, marginal: 15.2%) and 20.6% by ETKAC (95% CI: 18.3-23.1; severe: 8.5%, marginal: 12.1%), higher among pregnant than lactating women. Diets were rice-based with low diversity. As the functional marker ETKAC was more sensitive to dietary context, we focused on its determinants: stored rice, washing rice repeatedly before cooking, and drinking salted tea were each associated with higher odds of ETKAC-defined suboptimal status. Socioeconomic disadvantage further increased risk. This substantial, subclinical, preventable burden driven by dietary monotony and thiamine-depleting rice practices underscores the need for targeted maternal nutrition strategies.

articles.title: Medicaid Work Requirements and Maternal Health-Exempt but Unprotected.
articles.authors: Daw JR, Gordon SH

articles.title: REALITY OF INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE IN BRAZILIAN PREGNANT WOMEN (2007/2024).
articles.authors: Cury DB, Cury LCB, Micheletti AC
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel diseases (Crohn's and Ulcerative colitis) have been increasing alarmingly in Brazil. They affect mainly young people at reproductive age, which is extremely worrying in such a young country. To date, there´s no study that demonstrates how these diseases can affect pregnant women, like drug side effects and how off-springs of Brazilian patients evolve over time.
OBJECTIVES: The study aimed to analyze the side effects of medications used by patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) during pregnancy; to assess the impact of disease activity on the course of pregnancy and fetal development and to monitor the development of these children.
METHODS: This was a longitudinal retrospective analysis of patients registered over time (2007/2024), regarding the medications used during the conception, side effects, complications during pregnancy and post-delivery. All patients were recruited at the Inflammatory Bowel Disease service at Scope Clinic, located in the Midwest region of Brazil.
RESULTS: Out of the 329 patients, 25 got pregnant (mean age 30.38 years), 48% were in endoscopic activity and 52% were in remission at conception time, and all patients maintained prescribed medication (chimeric and fully human anti-TNF agents, as well as immunosuppressive medications). Disease activity had direct influence on the babies' weight and on the Apgar score when compared to women in remission, but despite this fact, prematurity was not observed. No undesirable drug effects were observed in both groups (mother and fetus), endorsing their safety over this population. In the postpartum follow-up over a period of two years, no abnormalities were observed.
CONCLUSION: This study shows the importance of continuously monitoring patients with inflammatory disease and guiding them on drug maintenance and the most appropriate time for conception.

articles.title: Partner hygiene-related behaviors and vaginitis subtypes: an exploratory observational study.
articles.authors: Kartal DU, Peker ME, Atlihan U et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate the association between partner hygiene behaviors, quantified using an exploratory partner hygiene score, and vaginitis subtypes, and to evaluate the relationship between baseline partner hygiene and short-term recurrence.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included women aged 18-45 years presenting with vaginitis symptoms to a gynecology outpatient clinic. Vaginitis subtypes were diagnosed using standardized clinical and laboratory criteria. Partner hygiene behaviors were assessed using a seven-item partner hygiene score (range: 0-14). Participants were followed for 3 months to assess clinically confirmed symptomatic recurrence. Associations between partner hygiene score and vaginitis subtypes were analyzed cross-sectionally, while recurrence analyses were performed prospectively.
RESULTS: A total of 108 women were included. Diagnoses included bacterial vaginosis (45.4%), vulvovaginal candidiasis (29.6%), Trichomonas vaginalis infection (10.2%), mixed vaginitis (11.1%), and non-specific vaginitis (3.7%). Median partner hygiene score scores were significantly lower in women with bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis compared with vulvovaginal candidiasis (p<0.001). Each one-point decrease in partner hygiene score was associated with higher odds of bacterial vaginosis. During follow-up, recurrence occurred in 33% of cases, but baseline partner hygiene score was not associated with recurrence.
CONCLUSION: Lower partner hygiene scores were associated with dysbiosis-predominant vaginitis phenotypes, particularly bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis. Although no association was observed with short-term recurrence, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Associations of Adaptive Coping, Self-Efficacy, and Hope With Psychological Resilience in Women Receiving Chemotherapy for Gynecological Cancer: A Descriptive Correlational Study.
articles.authors: Purtul S, Uslu-Sahan F
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological resilience is important for women coping with the physical and emotional challenges of chemotherapy for gynecological cancer. However, the associations of psychological resources with resilience during treatment remain insufficiently understood.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the associations of hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies with psychological resilience among women receiving chemotherapy for gynecological cancer.
METHODS: A descriptive correlational design was used. The study sample consisted of 144 women receiving outpatient chemotherapy in Turkey. Data were collected using standardized self-report measures assessing psychological resilience, hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies. Descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, and hierarchical linear regression analyses were conducted to examine the associations between psychological resilience and hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies.
RESULTS: The mean psychological resilience score indicated a moderate level of resilience. Psychological resilience was positively associated with hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping strategies. In the final regression model, self-efficacy showed the strongest independent association with psychological resilience (β = 0.524, P = .001), followed by hope (β = 0.257, P = .001) and adaptive coping (β = 0.146, P = .015). Together, these variables explained 56.2% of the variance in psychological resilience.
CONCLUSIONS: Hope, self-efficacy, and adaptive coping were positively associated with psychological resilience among women undergoing chemotherapy for gynecological cancer. These findings may inform nurse-led psychosocial support approaches that address self-efficacy, hope, and adaptive coping strategies as part of resilience-related care. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to examine whether changes in these psychological resources are followed by changes in resilience and other psychosocial outcomes during cancer treatment.

articles.title: Bazi Bushen Attenuates Skeletal Muscle Decline Associated With Oestrogen Deficiency and Modulates FGFR1/ERK Signalling.
articles.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
articles.authors: Huang D, Xu N, Chu Q et al.
articles.abstract: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

articles.title: Effects of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) on the Endometrium.
articles.authors: Chafitz O, Niderberg T, Yang S et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is the most common reproductive, endocrine, and metabolic disorder affecting 11-13% of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age. Although anovulation has traditionally been considered the primary cause of PMOS-associated infertility, accumulating evidence demonstrates that impaired endometrial receptivity and decidualization also contribute substantially to embryo implantation failure, recurrent pregnancy loss, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes, including miscarriage, gestational diabetes, pregnancy-induced hypertension, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. In addition to reproductive disorders, women with PMOS also commonly present with obesity, insulin resistance, and other long-term health conditions. This review summarizes current knowledge of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which PMOS disrupts endometrial function. We discuss how hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, obesity, and chronic inflammation, both independently and collectively, impair endometrial receptivity by altering androgen receptor (AR) signaling, glucose metabolism, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, immune homeostasis, cell-cell junctions, adhesion molecules, and key regulators of decidualization. We also highlight recent advances in transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing studies that have revealed cell type-specific alterations and molecular heterogeneity within the PMOS endometrium. Despite substantial progress, the mechanisms linking endocrine and metabolic abnormalities to impaired endometrial function remain incompletely understood. A better understanding of PMOS-associated endometrial dysfunction will facilitate the identification of novel therapeutic targets and improve embryo implantation success, pregnancy outcomes, and reproductive health in women with PMOS.

articles.title: Epigenetic Regulation in Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome: Mechanisms, Environmental Interactions, and Therapeutic Perspectives.
articles.authors: Wang L, Liao Y, Zhang G et al.
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), which has recently been proposed to be renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), is a reproductive endocrine-metabolic disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It is clinically characterized by hyperandrogenemia, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology, and is frequently accompanied by metabolic abnormalities, including insulin resistance and obesity. Despite extensive investigation, the pathogenesis of PCOS remains complex and incompletely understood. Increasing evidence indicates that epigenetic modifications play a critical role in the initiation and progression of PCOS. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and the regulation of non-coding RNAs, modulate gene expression without altering the underlying DNA sequence and thereby contribute to pathological processes such as ovarian dysfunction, hormonal imbalance, and metabolic dysregulation. This review summarizes current research on the association between epigenetic modifications and PCOS. It focuses on aberrant DNA methylation of genes involved in steroid hormone synthesis and metabolic regulation that contribute to hyperandrogenemia and insulin resistance; histone modifications, such as acetylation and methylation, which alter chromatin structure and regulate the transcription of genes essential for follicular development, leading to ovulatory disorders; and non-coding RNAs, including microRNAs and long non-coding RNAs, which further exacerbate the PCOS phenotype by targeting key genes involved in hormone biosynthesis and insulin signaling pathways. In addition, environmental factors, such as the intrauterine environment and exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals, can induce abnormal epigenetic modifications and interact with genetic susceptibility, thereby increasing the risk of PCOS. A comprehensive understanding of epigenetic mechanisms in PCOS not only provides new insights into its etiology but also lays a theoretical foundation for the development of diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies based on epigenetic regulation.

articles.title: One-Sided and unbalanced? An automated descriptive large-scale analysis of contraceptive information on German Instagram posts.
articles.journal: The European journal of contraception & reproductive health care : the official journal of the European Society of Contraception
articles.ta: Eur J Contracept Reprod Health Care
articles.authors: Wielga J, Schüz B
articles.abstract:
METHODS: Automated data collection via the Meta Content Library API was used to retrieve publicly available German Instagram posts about contraceptive methods (N = 33,596). The two most frequently mentioned contraceptive methods were identified. The barriers and benefits were identified through a literature review and a keyword-in-context analysis. Afterward, a co-occurrence analysis was conducted to examine how often the identified barriers and benefits are mentioned together in a post with the two contraceptive methods.
RESULTS: Hormonal contraceptive methods, particularly the pill, were mentioned most frequently, followed by natural contraception, particularly the abbreviation of natural family planning 'NFP'. The analyses revealed a striking polarisation: the pill was predominantly framed in terms of barriers, while NFP was predominantly framed in terms of benefits.
CONCLUSION: Contraceptive information on German Instagram is characterised by a one-sided and unbalanced presentation of contraceptive methods. These findings carry significant public health implications, highlighting the need for balanced, evidence-based health communication on social media.

articles.title: Epididymis-derived RNAs in sperm affect the next generation: potential clinical implications.
articles.authors: Chen AJ, Meyers AJ, Rainsford S et al.
articles.abstract: Until recently, the sole function of sperm was thought to be as delivery agents for the paternal contribution of zygote genes encoded in the DNA they carry. However, recent research has shown that sperm contribute substantially more information to oocytes upon fertilization through a select population of non-coding (nc)RNAs obtained while traversing the epididymis. Strikingly, their content can be altered by the environment in which males have lived, such as their exposure to various types of pollutants, traumas, addictive drugs, diet, and other factors. These changes in sperm ncRNA content can be responsible for transmitting the negative consequences of these environments to their offspring, via 'epigenetic inheritance', which is reminiscent of Lamarckian inheritance. This mini-review aims to provide an overview of the role of environment-regulated sperm ncRNAs in this process. We include studies on the relationship between specific paternal environments and the associated changes in sperm ncRNA content. These studies have been performed largely in rodent models, but we also describe evidence supporting the same processes occurring in humans. As an example, we focus on the epigenetic inheritance of stress phenotypes through changes in sperm miRNA profiles. We propose that identifying these specific ncRNAs carried by human sperm could lead to future diagnostic and treatment paradigms positively impacting ART. Screening out these potentially harmful sperm, or further research that provides approaches to reverse these changes before conception, may therefore prevent negative consequences related to epigenetic inheritance.

articles.title: Adapted Screening Methods for Gestational Diabetes in Low-Resource Settings-A Narrative Review of Observational Studies.
articles.authors: Kittelmann M, Monod C, Mosimann B
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) affects approximately 14%-17% of pregnancies worldwide, with the vast majority of cases occurring in low-resource settings. There is an ongoing debate concerning the optimal screening and diagnosis of GDM, as the current diagnostic recommendation of performing a universal oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) for every pregnant woman (WHO, 2013) is resource-intensive and can potentially lead to overdiagnosis. This narrative literature reviews aimed to evaluate the diagnostic sensitivity of alternative, less resource-demanding screening methods that could be appropriately used for low-resource settings.
METHODS: For this narrative review, observational studies were identified via PubMed. The PRISMA guidelines were used to guide this process. As the studies investigated very diverse screening methods, no statistical meta-analysis was performed due to methodological heterogeneity; instead, the results were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included, examining various alternatives such as fasting plasma glucose thresholds (sensitivity 95.6%), selective screening strategies (sensitivity 73.6%), capillary blood glucose testing (sensitivity 67.9%, 79.3%, and 92.5% for different fasting cut points), and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) measurements (sensitivity approximately 84%, depending on the cut-offs).
DISCUSSION: All alternatives showed inferior sensitivity compared to the standard OGTT; therefore, none can currently substitute the OGTT. However, basically all approaches have the potential to either reduce the number of OGTTs or improve access to GDM screening for more patients. Further research and validation are necessary for all approaches to safely reduce the number of OGTTs without compromising diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Disease, Functional Disability, and QoL as Associated Factors With Urinary Incontinence in Older Individuals-Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Tamanini JTN, Diehl LG, Santos JLF et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urinary incontinence (UI) is highly prevalent among older adults and is associated with functional decline and reduced quality of life (QoL). This study estimated the prevalence of UI and investigated factors independently associated with UI among community-dwelling older adults in São Paulo, Brazil.
METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2015 wave of the Health, Well-being, and Aging (SABE) Study. Of 1224 participants aged ≥ 60 years, 1213 (789 women; 424 men) were included after excluding missing outcome data. UI was defined as an International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF) score ≥ 3. Covariates included sociodemographic factors, chronic conditions, cognitive status, functional disability (basic activities of daily living [BADL]), and QoL (SF-12). Sex-stratified survey-weighted logistic regression models were performed.
RESULTS: UI prevalence was 18.33% in men and 30.04% in women (p < 0.001). Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and BADL impairment (functional disability) were independently associated with UI in both sexes (men: OR 1.84 and 1.72; women: OR 1.63 and 1.46, respectively). Among women, cognitive decline was also associated with UI (OR 1.81). Higher SF-12 physical and mental component scores were associated with lower odds of UI in women. Osteoarticular disease was independently associated with UI in women (OR 0.54), with a direction differing from most prior reports.
CONCLUSIONS: UI is common among older adults and is independently associated with CVD and functional disability in both sexes. In women, cognitive status and QoL were additionally associated with UI. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture for Mild-to-Moderate Stress Urinary Incontinence in Women: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Shi J, Wu Y, Zhang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is a prevalent condition in women, characterized by involuntary urine leakage during physical exertion. Electroacupuncture (EA) is an effective therapy for SUI, offering minimal side effects, a low economic burden, and good patient compliance. To our knowledge, no systematic review or meta-analysis has specifically evaluated EA for mild-to-moderate SUI in women.
METHODS: We systematically searched eight Chinese and English databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2002 and 2025. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (ROB-2), RevMan 5.3, and GRADEpro GDT (version 3.6). Meta-analysis was conducted where feasible, while a qualitative systematic review approach was adopted for outcomes with limited data.
RESULTS: A total of 652 studies were retrieved, of which 10 met the inclusion criteria. The results indicate that EA may be effective in treating mild-to-moderate SUI in women, but the overall quality of evidence is limited and only two studies were categorized as having a low risk of bias, while the remaining eight were appraised as presenting "some concerns". Key limitations include small sample sizes, regional restriction to China, simplistic statistical methods in some studies, limited accuracy, and insufficient trial protocols.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on small-scale Chinese trials, EA appears more effective than sham EA, medication, or pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) in reducing urine leakage and improving ICIQ-SF scores, with superior long-term effects. However, due to limited, low-quality evidence restricted to Chinese populations, we cannot conclusively demonstrate EA's superiority over PFMT or pharmacotherapy for mild-to-moderate SUI in women.

articles.title: Metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive effects of GLP-1 receptor agonizts in hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant women: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Sherif Mohamed M, Farrag A, Bachkangi P
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states, most commonly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and severe phenotypes such as HAIR-AN syndrome, are characterized by metabolic dysfunction, androgen excess, and reproductive disturbance. Insulin resistance is a central pathogenic driver and therapeutic target.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonizts on metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive outcomes in adult women with hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states. Data Sources and Study Selection: A systematic search identified randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and case series evaluating GLP-1 receptor agonizts in PCOS and HAIR-AN syndrome, reflecting the heterogeneity of the current evidence base.Data extraction and synthesis Outcomes were synthesized across metabolic (anthropometric and glycaemic), hormonal, reproductive, dermatologic, and safety domains, accounting for heterogeneity in interventions and study designs.
RESULTS: Metabolic responses appeared more consistent and robust than endocrine outcomes. Reproductive outcomes such as menstrual regularity were variably reported and showed inconsistent improvement across studies, limiting firm conclusions regarding fertility-related benefit. Evidence in severe phenotypes remains limited but suggestive of clinical benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 receptor agonizts are a promising adjunctive therapy in hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states, with the strongest evidence for metabolic improvement. Reproductive and endocrine outcomes remain less consistent, likely reflecting heterogeneity in study design, populations, and outcome reporting. Further high-quality, phenotype-specific trials are required.

articles.title: Cell-free DNA methylation profiling for lung cancer risk stratification in an LDCT-based clinical cohort.
articles.authors: Senkyrova T, Sauer Mikyskova P, Kramarova A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening enables earlier lung cancer detection but identifies indeterminate pulmonary findings in approximately 10-20 % of screened individuals. This study aimed to identify circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation markers associated with lung cancer in an LDCT-based clinical cohort.
METHODS: The study included 72 patients with histologically confirmed lung cancer, initially indeterminate LDCT findings, or negative LDCT findings. Exploratory reduced representation bisulfite sequencing of pooled cfDNA identified candidate regions for targeted analysis. Individual samples were analysed using a custom xGen methylation panel. CpG sites were preselected using q<0.05 and an absolute methylation difference >5 %. Marker panels were selected by Elastic Net and entered into multivariable logistic regression models. Discriminatory performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and optimism by bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Twenty-two CpG sites within the RASSF1A and SLC26A4 regions met the predefined selection criteria. Elastic Net yielded a seven-CpG panel for lung cancer vs. initially indeterminate findings, with apparent and optimism-corrected areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.855 and 0.773. For lung cancer vs. negative findings, the six-CpG panel yielded AUCs of 0.858 and 0.769, while the seven-CpG panel for lung cancer vs. the combined non-carcinoma group yielded AUCs of 0.787 and 0.688.
CONCLUSIONS: The seven-CpG panel distinguishing lung cancer from initially indeterminate findings yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.773. CpG sites within the RASSF1A and SLC26A4 regions warrant external validation to determine whether they can provide complementary information to imaging-based malignancy risk assessment in patients with indeterminate LDCT findings.

articles.title: Hormonal remodeling and molecular mechanisms in postmenopausal osteoporosis: Pathogenesis and therapeutic implications (Review).
articles.authors: Liu W, Li Z, Wang P et al.
articles.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO) is a prevalent metabolic bone disorder characterized by accelerated bone loss, reduced bone mineral density, and increased fragility fracture risk. Although estrogen deficiency is considered a central driver of PMO, increasing evidence indicates that bone loss after menopause results from broader endocrine remodeling involving multiple hormones. Estrogen decline and the accompanying rise in follicle‑stimulating hormone (FSH) are characteristic of the menopausal transition. Alterations in the parathyroid hormone (PTH)‑vitamin D axis, oxytocin (OT) and calcitonin (CT) may also influence skeletal homeostasis, although their patterns and causal contributions are less consistently established in postmenopausal women. These pathways are discussed as interacting components of an endocrine framework with differing levels of supporting evidence. These coordinated hormonal alterations disrupt bone remodeling through several mechanisms, including impaired bone mechanical homeostasis, dysregulated osteoimmune interactions, altered calcium metabolism, and gut microbiota‑bone axis imbalance. Collectively, these changes promote osteoclast activation, suppress osteoblast function, and accelerate skeletal deterioration. Current therapeutic approaches, such as hormone replacement therapy, bisphosphonates, selective estrogen receptor modulators, and PTH analogs, have improved the management of PMO but remain limited by safety concerns or restricted long‑term efficacy. Emerging approaches, including FSH blockade, selected phytoestrogen‑related interventions, modified CT delivery, and OT‑related pathways have different levels of supporting evidence; most specific experimental strategies require human efficacy and safety validation before clinical application. An improved understanding of hormonal interactions and endocrine network remodeling may facilitate the development of more precise and individualized strategies for the prevention and treatment of PMO.

articles.title: Urological manifestations in obesity.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.authors: Jayapal B, Kapoor N
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The global prevalence of obesity continues to rise, with effects ranging across urology. This review summarizes recent evidence on obesity and its impact on various urological conditions, including malignancy, infections, stone disease, functional urology and male reproductive health, chronic kidney disease, and pediatric urology, to guide comprehensive management in this population.
RECENT FINDINGS: Obesity has a paradoxical survival benefit in patients with renal cell carcinoma, while its impact drives aggressive prostate cancer. Obesity increases kidney stone risk, with sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists showing divergent effects on lithogenesis and urinary tract infections. It is a modifiable risk factor for overactive bladder and stress urinary incontinence, both of which improve with weight loss/ bariatric surgery. Robotic surgery mitigates obesity-related perioperative risk. Hypogonadism secondary to obesity is a major reversible cause of male infertility. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) reverse metabolic hypogonadism and helps in slowing chronic kidney progression. Maternal and childhood obesity may impair testicular descent and can also increase the risk of nocturnal enuresis.
SUMMARY: Obesity's urological effects are heterogeneous, paradoxical from pediatric to adults, mediated by insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and hormonal dysregulation. Weight loss and the use of GLP-1 RA may offer a unique strategy for optimizing and treating urological conditions.

articles.title: Recent advances in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome and obesity: a comprehensive review.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.authors: Rajan R, Nandakumar D, Kapoor N
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review evaluates recent advances in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), emphasizing its complex association with obesity and the ongoing transition toward precision medicine. The synthesis of current evidence addresses pathophysiology, emerging biomarkers, and multiomics approaches, highlighting their potential to enhance diagnosis, risk stratification, and individualized management.
RECENT FINDINGS: PMOS is a multifactorial disorder involving insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, genetic predisposition, gut dysbiosis, and environmental factors. Obesity intensifies metabolic and reproductive dysfunction through mechanisms including chronic inflammation, adipose tissue dysfunction, and altered gut-ovary signalling. Traditional phenotype-based classifications do not adequately capture this biological heterogeneity. Multiomics approaches that integrate genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome data have identified distinct molecular subtypes, including insulin-resistant, steroidogenic, inflammatory, and neuroendocrine clusters. Novel biomarkers, including anti-Müllerian hormone, free androgen index, and specific metabolomic and lipidomic signatures, have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and phenotyping.
SUMMARY: The integration of multiomics represents a pivotal advancement toward patient-centred care in PMOS by enabling early risk prediction and mechanism-based therapies. While current evidence remains largely exploratory, these developments support a shift from uniform treatment strategies to precision endocrinology, with the potential to substantially improve long-term metabolic and reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Learning Curve, Training, and Operator Experience in Vaginoscopic Hysteroscopy: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Monzango Sibo GLM, Phoba P
articles.abstract: Vaginoscopic hysteroscopy, also known as the no-touch technique, is widely used in outpatient gynecologic practice, but the experience required to achieve reproducible competence remains uncertain. This systematic review synthesized clinical and simulation-based evidence on learning curves, training, operator experience, technical performance, and competency assessment in vaginoscopic hysteroscopy. Eligible reports explicitly described vaginoscopic or no-touch access and evaluated at least one learning-related outcome. The included studies differed substantially in design, operator experience, training context, and definitions of technical performance. Clinical reports suggested improvement in procedural efficiency and success with experience, while simulation-based studies identified differences in technical performance between operators of varying experience. However, procedural speed, overall outpatient hysteroscopy proficiency, and vaginoscopy-specific competence were not assessed consistently, and the available evidence did not establish a validated, universal case-number threshold for independent vaginoscopic cervical access. No included clinical study established an individualized competency threshold for vaginoscopic access using sequential learning-curve methodology. These findings favor multidimensional, performance-based assessment rather than reliance on procedure counts alone and support prospective studies with standardized success criteria and individualized monitoring.

articles.title: Comparative study between dexmedetomidine, magnesium sulfate, and lidocaine on the pressor response to laryngoscopic intubation and optic nerve sheath diameter measurement in laparoscopic gynecological surgery.
articles.authors: Mansour SM, Abd El Sabour AI, Abbas H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of laryngoscope and intubation in general anesthesia can cause stress response like hypertension and tachycardia. Intravenous (IV) dexmedetomidine, magnesium sulfate (MgSO4), and lidocaine have been used to compare their effect on pressor response, hemodynamics, and optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD).
METHODS: One hundred and two female patients slated for elective gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia were involved in this randomized, double-blinded study. They were randomized to receive IV dexmedetomidine (Group D, n = 34), IV magnesium SO4 (Group M, n = 34), or IV lidocaine (Group L, n = 34). Heart rate (HR) and mean arterial pressure were assessed prior to and following medication usage, prior to and following the induction of anesthesia, following intubation (cuff inflation (1 minute), and 5 and 10 minutes following intubation. At the same timeframe, the ONSD measurement was conducted.
RESULTS: After intubation for 1 min (cuff inflation), Group D had the lowest HR compared to groups M and L and also Mean blood pressure (MBP) was lower in group D and group M than group L. At 5 min and 10 min after intubation, HR was lower in group D than group M and group L and MBP was lowest in group D than group M and group L. ONSD was lower in group D than group M and group L at 1, 5, and 10 min after intubation.
CONCLUSIONS: IV dexmedetomidine offers the best control on hemodynamics and ONSD responses during laryngoscopic intubation than IV MgSO4 and lidocaine.

articles.title: An ultrasound model for stress urinary incontinence at six weeks postpartum.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Long Y, Liu S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) after childbirth has both clinical risk factors and measurable changes in urethral support. Whether integrating these complementary features can identify affected women at six weeks postpartum remains uncertain.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-centre study included 454 women, divided chronologically into development (n=351) and temporal internal-validation (n=103) cohorts. LASSO selected ultrasound predictors. Ultrasound-only and combined clinical-ultrasound models were evaluated for discrimination, calibration and clinical utility.
RESULTS: SUI prevalence was 17.7 % and 26.2 % in the development and validation cohorts, respectively. LASSO retained bladder-neck mobility (BNM) and urethral funneling; the combined model additionally included age, vaginal delivery and overweight. The combined model outperformed the ultrasound-only model in development (C-statistic, 0.780 [95 % CI, 0.717-0.843] vs. 0.703 [0.634-0.771]; p=0.002). In validation, the corresponding C-statistics were 0.805 (0.716-0.894) and 0.737 (0.633-0.841), but the difference was not significant (p=0.141). The validation calibration intercept, slope and Brier score were 0.704, 1.054 and 0.161, respectively. Decision-curve analysis indicated potential net benefit at selected thresholds; continuous-predictor analysis yielded similar discrimination.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining clinical and transperineal ultrasound features improved concurrent SUI identification over ultrasound features alone. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Multi-modal AI: Integrating electrocardiography with molecular biomarkers for noninvasive detection of cardiac allograft rejection.
articles.authors: Chen K, Koesmahargyo V, Ronan R et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Noninvasive rejection biomarkers (AlloMap, AlloSure) demonstrate high negative predictive value but positive predictive values of only 10-30%, driving avoidable endomyocardial biopsies. We developed a multi-modal AI model integrating electrocardiography with molecular biomarkers in 389 heart transplant recipients (5338 ECG-biopsy pairs), performing the first head-to-head comparison of AI-ECG, AlloMap, AlloSure, and their integration against biopsy-proven rejection. Individual modalities showed modest discrimination (AI-ECG AUC 0.65; AlloSure 0.67; AlloMap 0.56), while combining biomarkers alone did not improve performance (AUC 0.65). In the multi-modal test subset of ECGs (n=38, 2 rejection events), the integrated model achieved AUC 0.81 with 100% specificity (0/36 false positives) and 97% negative predictive value, eliminating all 19 false-positive combined-biomarker referrals. These hypothesis-generating results support prospective multi-center validation to determine whether requiring concordance across electrical and biomarker signals reduces unnecessary biopsies while preserving high negative predictive value.
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive rejection biomarkers (AlloMap gene-expression profiling (GEP); AlloSure donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA)) deliver high negative predictive value but positive predictive values of only 10-30%, driving avoidable endomyocardial biopsies. Each biomarker interrogates a single biological compartment. Whether integrating AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) with these molecular assays improves specificity has not been tested.
METHODS: We retrospectively assembled 5338 unique ECG-endomyocardial-biopsy pairs from 389 adult heart transplant recipients at a single center (2018-2024). A ResNet-18 convolutional neural network was trained on 8-lead ECG waveforms with clinical covariates. In the 340-patient subset with same encounter AlloMap and AlloSure testing (405 ECG-biomarker-biopsy triplets), an integrated model fused the ECG embedding with biomarker values via late concatenation. We performed the first head-to-head, same-cohort comparison of AI-ECG, AlloMap, AlloSure, and their integration against biopsy-proven rejection (ISHLT ≥2R ACR or pAMR ≥2). Discrimination was evaluated with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Individual modalities showed modest discrimination (AI-ECG AUC 0.65, 95% CI 0.58-0.72; AlloSure 0.67, 0.56-0.78; AlloMap 0.56, 0.46-0.67); combining biomarkers alone did not improve…

articles.title: Multi-Niche Microbiome Alterations in Endometrial Cancer: Drivers, Biomarkers and Translational Targets.
articles.authors: Li Y, Zhang H, Hu L et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is the commonest gynecological malignancy in high-income countries and one of the few solid tumors whose incidence and mortality are rising despite advances in oncological care. Conventional hormonal, metabolic and genetic risk factors fail to fully explain EC tumorigenesis, and the multi-niche human microbiome has emerged as a novel, modifiable regulatory axis governing EC onset, progression and immunotherapy responsiveness. However, existing reviews have largely examined individual anatomical sites in isolation, and a cross-compartment synthesis that integrates the gut, cervicovaginal, uterine cavity, and intratumoral niches-together with their mechanistic and therapeutic implications-remains lacking. This narrative review screened English articles from PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar using keywords covering EC, microbiome, reproductive tract microbiome alterations, the estrobolome and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), prioritizing prospective cohorts, clinical trials and multi-omics mechanistic studies. We synthesize evidence across four interconnected niches and integrate them into a unified mechanistic framework. Reproducible compartmental signatures characterize EC: cervicovaginal samples show severe Lactobacillus depletion and enrichment of pathogenic anaerobes including Porphyromonas, Prevotella and Atopobium; malignant endometrial tissues display elevated α-diversity dominated by Anaerococcus, Peptoniphilus and Gardnerella, together with poorly explored fungal community shifts; the intratumoral niche harbors distinct taxa that directly modulate tumor proliferation, immune evasion and therapeutic responsiveness; and gut microbiome alterations deplete short-chain fatty acid-producing Firmicutes while expanding β-glucuronidase-rich Enterobacteriaceae, driving estrogen reactivation via the estrobolome and systemic pro-tumor inflammation. The PRIMMO trial further validates gut microbial clusters as predictive biomarkers of pembrolizumab efficacy in recurrent EC. By positioning the intratumoral microbiome as a distinct niche and linking multi-niche alterations to hormonal, inflammatory, immunological and genotoxic pathways, this review provides a new cross-compartment perspective that reframes the microbiome as both a mechanistic contributor and a translational target in EC. Standardized analytical workflows and large-scale prospective cohorts are urgently needed to translate these discoveries into routine…

articles.title: Biofunctional Molecular Large Surfaces Enabling Ultrasensitive Detection for Early Diagnosis of Cervical Cancer.
articles.journal: Chemistry of materials : a publication of the American Chemical Society
articles.authors: Castrignanò E, Sarcina L, Mongelli V et al.
articles.abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infections are among the leading causes of cervical cancers globally. The World Health Organization has established global targets aimed at reducing the spread of HPV and its associated disease burden. To date, the detection of HPV infections relies primarily on genomic assays targeting viral DNA or mRNA, which, although highly sensitive, require time-consuming PCR protocols performed by trained personnel. In addition, these approaches may be challenged in biological matrices, such as saliva, where viral concentrations are low (e.g., head-neck HPV cancer) or early stage infections. Therefore, alternative strategies enabling rapid, sensitive, and direct detection of viral biomarkers are highly desirable. In this study, we present the Single-Molecule-with-a-Large-Surface (SiMoLS) technology for the detection of the HPV-16 L1 capsid protein in both model and clinically relevant samples added with HPV-16 L1. The SiMoLS platform exploits a biofunctionalized gate electrode integrated within an electrolyte-gated organic field effect transistor, enabling label-free detection at the single- or few-molecules level. By targeting HPV-16 L1, a structural protein abundantly expressed during productive infection, the platform provides direct evidence of viral presence without the need for nucleic acid amplification. The device demonstrates high sensitivity and selectivity across a broad concentration range, extending down to 10-20 M with a confidence level of 99%, while PCA shows a well-defined clustering pattern that separates positive from negative swab real samples in an unsupervised manner. The SiMoLS platform (i) offers rapid analysis with ultrahigh sensitivity, (ii) it is compatible with low sample volumes, supporting its application in point-of-care (POC) settings due to its scalability and ease of use, and (iii) represents a promising tool for the early and decentralized HPV highly sensitive yet reliable screening, particularly in scenarios where conventional methods face limitations.

articles.title: Valuing Insurance Coverage for Infertility Treatment: A Double-Bounded Contingent Valuation Study in Kermanshah, Iran.
articles.authors: Soofi M, Karamimatin B, Mahaki B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility imposes substantial medical, psychological, and financial burdens. Despite recent expansion of insurance coverage for infertility services in Iran, evidence on public willingness to contribute to pooled insurance arrangements remains limited. This study estimated willingness to pay (WTP) for infertility insurance among adults in Kermanshah, western Iran, and identified associated determinants.
METHODS: A cross-sectional contingent valuation study was conducted among 630 adults recruited via convenience sampling in Kermanshah. WTP for a hypothetical package covering 70% of infertility treatment costs (up to two cycles/year) was elicited using a double-bounded dichotomous choice (DBDC) format (bids: 4,000-16,000 thousand IRR). Mean WTP was estimated via maximum-likelihood interval-data regression. Sensitivity analyses evaluated gender composition and response certainty.
RESULTS: Of 626 valid respondents, 85.5% expressed positive WTP. Acceptance declined monotonically with increasing bids, supporting construct validity. Mean monthly WTP was 11,107 thousand IRR (95% CI: 10,212-12,003; base) and 11,266 thousand IRR (95% CI: 10,317-12,216; n=451, adjusted). Higher education (β=3,145.56, P=0.011) and socioeconomic status (β=5,254.04, P<0.001) predicted greater WTP; government-funding expectations (β=-5,046.92, P=0.004) and basic insurance (β=-3,697.27, P=0.050) predicted lower WTP. Certainty-calibrated and gender-balanced analyses confirmed robustness.
CONCLUSION: Adults in Kermanshah expressed substantial support for infertility insurance. Given the single-city convenience sample, generalization requires caution. Findings suggest that affordability, socioeconomic gradients, and public expectations regarding government responsibility should be considered in benefit-package and financing design.

articles.title: Dysregulated T helper cytokines in serum and peritoneal fluid of women with endometriosis-related infertility.
articles.journal: Asian biomedicine : research, reviews and news
articles.authors: Ahsan F, Rahmawati NY, Ardianta Widyanugraha MY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory condition and is one of the leading causes of infertility. The role of T helper (Th) cytokines in infertility remains largely unexamined, despite their recognized importance in endometriosis.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the serum and peritoneal fluid levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-10, IL-17A, IL-17F, and IFN-γ in women with endometriosis and to explore their correlations with disease severity.
METHODS: Eighty-seven infertile women undergoing diagnostic laparoscopy were included, comprising 44 endometriosis patients and 43 controls with benign gynecologic disorders. Serum and peritoneal cytokines were measured using Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Statistical analyses assessed differences and correlations with clinical parameters.
RESULTS: Both serum and peritoneal fluid levels of IL-4 and IL-5 were markedly higher in endometriosis patients compared to controls (P < 0.001). Although serum IL-10 levels did not show significant differences, there was an increase in peritoneal fluid (P < 0.001). Among those with endometriosis, serum levels of IL-4, IL-10, IL-17A, and IL-17F exhibited a positive correlation with the revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine score, while IL-17F indicated an inverse correlation with the Endometriosis Fertility Index (EFI) scores (r = -0.422, P = 0.004). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated that IL-4 and IL-5 effectively distinguished endometriosis cases from controls, with IL-17F also providing significant predictive value for EFI scores (P = 0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated IL-4 and IL-5 levels in endometriosis suggest a Th2-skewed immune response. Meanwhile, the correlation of IL-17A with disease severity and the inverse relationship of IL-17F with fertility scores highlight the complex role of the Th17 response. These findings enhance understanding of cytokine dysregulation in endometriosis and may guide future therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Advanced Age and Low Parity as Predictors of Non-Endometrioid Histopathological Subtypes in Endometrial Carcinoma: A Cross-Sectional Study in Indonesia.
articles.authors: Mustaqim RF, Aditiyono A, Winarno GNA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is the most common gynecological malignancy in developed countries and is increasing in incidence in low- and middle-income settings, including Indonesia. Age and parity are well-recognized epidemiological risk factors; however, their differential impact on histopathological tumor subtypes-particularly in older women-remains insufficiently characterized in Southeast Asian populations.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the associations between patient age and parity with the histopathological subtype of endometrial carcinoma in women treated at a tertiary referral hospital in Indonesia.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional analytic study was conducted using retrospectively collected medical records from 207 patients aged ≥50 years with histopathologically confirmed endometrial carcinoma at Prof. Dr. Margono Soekarjo Regional Public Hospital, Purwokerto, between January and December 2024. Patients with incomplete clinicopathological data were excluded. Age was categorized into 50-60 years and >60 years; parity into nulliparous/primiparous and multiparous (≥2 deliveries). Histopathological subtypes were classified as endometrioid vs non-endometrioid carcinoma. Associations were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression; statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05, with 95% confidence intervals (CI) reported.
RESULTS: Of 207 eligible patients, the majority (92.5%) were aged 50-60 years. Non-endometrioid carcinoma predominated in women aged >60 years (p < 0.001; relative risk [RR] = 19.2; 95% CI: 8.7-42.0). Multiparous patients exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of endometrioid histology (93.8%) compared with nulliparous/primiparous patients (90.6%; p = 0.02; RR = 20.7). On multivariate analysis, both age and parity were predictors of histopathological subtype, with age demonstrating a stronger effect size.
CONCLUSION: Advanced age (>60 years) and low parity are independently associated with non-endometrioid histopathological subtypes of endometrial carcinoma in an Indonesian tertiary center. These findings underscore the clinical importance of incorporating patient age and reproductive history into risk stratification and surveillance strategies for endometrial cancer.

articles.title: Enhanced detection of polymicrobial bloodstream infections with 16S rDNA PCR library amplicons and clinical relevance.
articles.authors: Li G, Wu G, Yin H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polymicrobial bloodstream infections (BSIs) are clinically challenging because conventional blood culture may fail to recover all causative microorganisms, particularly in patients with low microbial burden, prior antimicrobial exposure, or infections caused by fastidious organisms. This study evaluated a 16S rDNA PCR library construction strategy based on cloning and Sanger sequencing as a complementary approach to conventional blood culture and compared its microbial detection profile with that of direct 16S rDNA amplicon high-throughput sequencing.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 16,970 blood culture specimens collected at a hospital in northwestern China to characterize the clinical distribution and epidemiological features of BSIs.
