In a retrospective cohort of 295 patients with culture-confirmed BSI, clinical predictors associated with blood culture-defined polymicrobial BSI were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses, with particular emphasis on white blood cell (WBC) count and procalcitonin (PCT) levels. In a separate molecular comparison cohort of 20 patients, cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was analyzed using two 16S rDNA-based workflows: a clone-based approach involving PCR amplification, gel purification, cloning, amplified ribosomal DNA restriction analysis (ARDRA), and Sanger sequencing, and a direct 16S rDNA amplicon high-throughput sequencing approach.
RESULTS: Among the 16,970 blood culture specimens, 1,321 were positive, including 45 polymicrobial BSI cases. Escherichia coli was the most frequently identified pathogen, followed by coagulase-negative staphylococci and Brucella spp. Compared with monomicrobial BSI, polymicrobial BSI was associated with higher WBC counts and PCT levels. In multivariable analysis, both WBC count and PCT were independently associated with polymicrobial BSI, and their combination showed good discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.927). In the separate molecular comparison cohort of 20 patients, the three methods showed distinct detection ranges. Blood culture detected 0-1 microbial taxon per patient, with one pathogen identified in 17 patients and negative results in 3 patients. The clone-based method detected a broader microbial spectrum, identifying 0-5 taxa per patient, whereas direct 16S rDNA amplicon sequencing showed the broadest detection range, with more than five taxa detected in 9 patients. In contrast, 16S rDNA…

articles.title: Research Progress of Stem Cell Therapy for Premature Ovarian Insufficiency.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Wang F, Wang R et al.
articles.abstract: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a heterogeneous reproductive and endocrine disorder characterized by impaired ovarian function before the age of 40 years. Conventional management, particularly hormone therapy, addresses hypoestrogenic symptoms and long-term health risks but does not reliably restore endogenous ovarian activity or fertility. Stem cell-based strategies have therefore attracted considerable interest because of their potential paracrine, immunomodulatory, anti-apoptotic, angiogenic, and microenvironment-remodeling effects. This review summarizes current evidence on stem cell sources, therapeutic mechanisms, preclinical models, clinical studies, extracellular vesicle-based approaches, biomaterials, gene-editing strategies, and translational challenges in POI. Particular emphasis is placed on the distinction between mechanistic and animal evidence, uncontrolled or pilot human studies, and controlled clinical evidence. Across preclinical models, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) frequently improve ovarian histology, hormone profiles, follicular parameters, and reproductive performance; however, these findings cannot be assumed to represent restoration of ovarian reserve or fertility in humans. Clinical evidence remains limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly derived from small non-randomized studies, with outcomes ranging from menstrual recovery and changes in AMH, FSH, estradiol, or antral follicle count to a small number of reported pregnancies. These surrogate changes should be distinguished from clinically meaningful endpoints such as ovulation, ongoing pregnancy, and live birth. Emerging approaches involving extracellular vesicles, biomaterials, and gene editing may improve cell retention or therapeutic potency, but most remain preclinical or early translational strategies. Overall, stem cell therapy should currently be regarded as an investigational approach for POI. Progress toward clinical translation will require standardized cell products, clearly defined dosing and administration routes, appropriate comparator groups, clinically meaningful reproductive endpoints, rigorous long-term safety surveillance, and adequately powered controlled trials.

articles.title: Synthesis, molecular structure, supramolecular and biological evaluation of benzimidazole-based Schiff bases.
articles.authors: Enamullah M, Haque I, Akter T et al.
articles.abstract: Benzimidazole-based Schiff bases, (Z)-2-(((1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)imino)methyl)phenol monohydrate (HL1·H2O) and (Z)-1-(((1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)imino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol monohydrate (HL2·H2O) were synthesized and characterized by IR, UV-vis, EI-mass, 1H NMR spectroscopy, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies. Molecular structure determination suggested the presence of crystal water in the unit cell of each compound. The structure adopted a usual enol-imine form, with an intramolecular hydrogen bond between the phenolate-oxygen and the imine-nitrogen atoms. Supramolecular packing indicated that the structure was assembled and stabilized by several significant intermolecular non-covalent interactions between symmetrically related lattice water and the molecules, as supported by quantitative Hirshfeld surface analyses. DSC analyses revealed an irreversible phase transition from solid-crystal to isotropic liquid. Computational modeling by DFT/TD-DFT supported the experimental results of the molecular and electronic structures of the compounds. Molecular orbital (MO) calculations revealed a relatively lower HOMO-LUMO energy gap for HL2 (ΔE g = 2.41 eV) compared with HL1 (2.65 eV), suggesting the former had enhanced charge delocalization due to the extended π-electrons conjugation system, in parallel with molecular electrostatic potential (MEP) surface maps. Biological activities were assessed using cytotoxicity, antioxidant, α-amylase, and antibacterial tests. HL1 possessed more pronounced cytotoxic effects on cervical cancer (HeLa) cells (IC50 = 75.53 ± 3.10 µM) than HL2 (IC50 = 462.61 ± 5.24 µM). DPPH radical-scavenging studies revealed moderate antioxidant activity for HL2 (IC50 = 168 ± 4 µM) and weaker activity for HL1 (IC50 = 233 ± 5 µM) compared with the standard ascorbic acid (IC50 = 106 ± 1 µM). HL1 showed moderately the inhibit α-amylase enzyme (IC50 = 399 ± 2.7 µM), while no inhibitory activity for HL2 was noted. Both compounds were moderately active against selected bacterial strains in a concentration-dependent manner. Computational analyses on Escherichia coli BepA metalloprotease (6SAR) and human DNA topoisomerase IIα (5GWK) using molecular docking exhibited favorable predicted protein-ligand interactions, involving hydrogen-bonding, hydrophobic and π-stacking interactions. HL1 had a more favorable predicted binding affinity towards BepA metalloprotease, whereas HL2 had a more favorable predicted binding affinity towards human DNA…

articles.title: Synthesis and In Silico and In Vitro Antitumor Potential of Novel Organochalcogens Derived from Azidothymidine and 2,4,6-Trichloro-1,3,5-triazine.
articles.authors: Rocha NS, da Silva SR, Carvalho BB et al.
articles.abstract: The preparation of a new class of organochalcogen compounds derived from arylchalcogeno aminothymidine (ACAT) and 2,4,6-trichloro-1,3,5-triazine is described. The compounds were obtained in good yields via aromatic nucleophilic substitution reactions between ACAT derivatives and the triazine ring. The developed protocol selectively afforded monosubstituted derivatives, avoiding the formation of di- and trisubstituted isomers. Antitumor activity was evaluated against HT-29 (human colorectal adenocarcinoma) and NCI/ADR-RES (multidrug-resistant human ovarian carcinoma) cell lines using the MTT assay. Sulfur- and selenium-containing derivatives showed only moderate cytotoxic effects, reducing cell viability mainly at the highest tested concentration (100 μM). In contrast, tellurium-containing derivatives exhibited pronounced cytotoxic activity, with minimum IC50 values of 9.90 μM in HT-29 cells and 12.18 μM in NCI/ADR-RES cells, demonstrating notable efficacy against multidrug-resistant tumor cells. In addition, the antioxidant properties of the compounds were investigated in vitro. Tellurium derivatives displayed significant antioxidant activity, as demonstrated by inhibition of lipid peroxidation in the TBARS assay and by thiol-peroxidase (GPx-like) activity. A possible mechanism of action based on tubulin polymerization inhibition was investigated by means of a molecular docking study. The results demonstrate the potential of these novel organochalcogen compounds as antitumor agents, highlighting tellurium incorporation as a promising strategy to overcome multiple drug resistance (MDR) in cancer.

articles.title: VAMP5 Mediates Sevoflurane-Induced Immune Modulation in Cervical Cancer: A Clinical Translational Study.
articles.authors: Zhang Z, Dong X, Yu T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sevoflurane, a commonly used inhaled anesthetic, has been implicated in modulating tumor biology and perioperative immune responses, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate whether sevoflurane regulates key immune-related genes in cervical cancer patients undergoing laparoscopic radical hysterectomy (LRH) and to explore the clinical relevance of such regulation.
METHODS: Based on prior RNA-seq screening, we established a two-step validation framework to identify sevoflurane-regulated genes in a clinical cohort. A total of 116 cervical cancer patients undergoing LRH were enrolled, including 70 who received sevoflurane anesthesia and 46 who received propofol anesthesia. Peripheral blood samples were collected at five perioperative time points. mRNA expression levels of candidate genes were measured by qRT-PCR, lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry, and VAMP5 protein expression was assessed by intracellular staining. Bioinformatics analyses were performed using TCGA data to evaluate associations between candidate genes and tumor immune infiltration.
RESULTS: MAP3K7 and VAMP5 were validated as sevoflurane-downregulated targets, showing sustained suppression postoperatively compared to the propofol group. VAMP5 expression correlated significantly with tumor progression and immune cell infiltration in cervical cancer, particularly CD8+ T-cells, B-cells, and macrophages. Among sevoflurane-treated patients, those with lower VAMP5 expression exhibited delayed postoperative recovery of CD8+ T-cell counts at 48 and 72 h after surgery, whereas no such difference was observed for other lymphocyte subsets.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identify VAMP5 as a novel molecular link between anesthetic choice and immune modulation, suggesting that sevoflurane may influence perioperative immune recovery through vesicle-associated mechanisms, with potential implications for optimizing anesthesia strategies to improve oncologic outcomes.

articles.title: Periodontal inflammation may amplify genitourinary vulnerability in perimenopause and postmenopause.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Hua J, Li W et al.
articles.abstract: During perimenopause and postmenopause, changes in estrogen exposure may alter mucosal barriers, microbial ecosystems, and inflammatory responsiveness across the oral and genitourinary tracts. These stages differ in their hormonal patterns, and much of the available evidence comes from postmenopausal women or experimental models of estrogen deficiency. In the oral cavity, altered salivary function, gingival immunity, epithelial integrity, and alveolar bone metabolism may increase the inflammatory potential of established biofilms without generating a uniform menopause-associated microbial signature. When periodontitis develops, disruption of the gingival barrier can promote repeated exposure to microbial products, cytokine spillover, hepatic acute-phase responses, endothelial activation, and myeloid activation, thereby adding to systemic inflammatory burden. In parallel, hypoestrogenism can weaken vaginal, urethral, and bladder epithelial resilience, reduce Lactobacillus-associated colonization resistance, and impair tissue repair. The association between hypoestrogenism and recurrent urinary tract infection is better supported than corresponding associations with bacterial vaginosis or vulvovaginal candidiasis. Genitourinary syndrome of menopause may cause overlapping symptoms and coexist with infection. In this narrative review, we propose an estrogen-sensitive oral-systemic-genitourinary axis in which periodontal inflammation may amplify genitourinary susceptibility through systemic inflammatory signals and possibly through changes in intestinal and vaginal ecosystems. Hypoestrogenism may provide a permissive background, while local microbial or inflammatory challenges contribute to clinical disease. This proposed interaction does not require direct bacterial dissemination to the genitourinary tract. Evidence supporting the individual components is stronger than direct human evidence for the complete pathway, and a contribution from persistent myeloid reprogramming remains unproven. Longitudinal multisite studies integrating hormonal trajectories, periodontal status, systemic immune markers, and microbiologically confirmed genitourinary outcomes, together with combined periodontal and local estrogen interventions, are required to test this hypothesis in perimenopausal and postmenopausal women.

articles.title: Recombinant humanized type III collagen freeze-dried fibers for vaginal laxity: a narrative review of mechanisms, clinical evidence, and potential relevance to pelvic floor dysfunction.
articles.authors: Shi R, Wang L
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal laxity (VL) is a prevalent condition affecting women's quality of life, characterized by reduced vaginal tightness, sexual function impairment, and psychological distress. While surgical vaginoplasty and energy-based devices (radiofrequency and laser) are commonly used, these approaches have important limitations, including surgical risks, variable durability, and limited evidence quality. Collagen dysregulation is increasingly recognized as a key pathophysiological feature of VL, and collagen-based biomaterials have emerged as potential regenerative interventions. However, the evidence specifically linking collagen fiber biology to VL remains scattered, and a systematic synthesis of recombinant humanized type III collagen (rhCol III) for this indication is lacking.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review systematically summarizes current evidence on the pathophysiological role of collagen in VL, the material properties and mechanisms of action of rhCol III freeze-dried fibers, and the available preclinical and clinical data for this intervention, with consideration of its potential relevance to the broader spectrum of pelvic floor dysfunction.
FINDINGS: Recombinant humanized type III collagen freeze-dried fibers exhibit good biocompatibility and biodegradability due to their structural homology with native human collagen. Their proposed mechanism of action involves three complementary pathways-physical support and structural filling, biochemical regeneration via upregulation of endogenous collagen synthesis, and microenvironment modulation including angiogenesis and anti-inflammatory effects-although several specific molecular pathways have been characterized primarily in non-vaginal tissue models and require direct validation in vaginal tissue. Available clinical evidence from a single small two-center randomized controlled trial (n = 84) demonstrates significant short-term improvements in VL symptoms and sexual function at 4 weeks, with a favorable short-term safety profile. However, the evidence base remains early-stage, with no large-scale multicenter trials, no long-term follow-up data, and no head-to-head comparisons with established treatments.
CONCLUSION: rhCol III freeze-dried fibers represent an emerging, biologically plausible intervention for VL that warrants further investigation. Key knowledge gaps include the need for large-scale randomized trials with long-term efficacy and safety data, standardized treatment protocols,…

articles.title: Predicting concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia without preoperative suspicion of malignancy.
articles.authors: Zeevi G, Yeoshoua E, Dahan C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (EIN) is a premalignant lesion with variable risk of concurrent endometrial carcinoma. Identifying predictors of endometrial carcinoma in women with EIN without pathological suspicion of carcinoma may improve surgical planning.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of patients with EIN who underwent hysterectomy between 2014 and 2024. Preoperative clinical and diagnostic variables were evaluated as predictors of concurrent endometrial carcinoma and incorporated into a multivariable logistic regression model to construct a nomogram. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Ridge and Firth penalized regression were performed as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The final cohort included 124 women, of whom 18 (14.5%) had concurrent endometrial carcinoma. Type 2 diabetes mellitus was associated with increased odds of concurrent carcinoma (adjusted OR 4.18, 95% CI 1.11-15.69). Hysteroscopy-guided sampling or dilation and curettage was associated with lower odds compared with pipelle biopsy (adjusted OR 0.11, 95% CI 0.02-0.50). A nomogram incorporating age, body mass index, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and diagnostic modality demonstrated an AUC of 0.828 (95% CI 0.725-0.931) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.784. Penalized sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSION: A simple preoperative nomogram based on routinely available clinical variables showed promising discrimination for concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with EIN. Prospective and external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Prevalence of qualitative platelet disorders in adolescents and young adults with heavy menstrual bleeding: a single center experience.
articles.journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
articles.authors: Carter-Febres M, Tarango C, Childress A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) is a chronic condition that impacts an estimated 34% to 37% of the adolescent and young adult (AYA) population. Two of the most common causes of HMB in the AYA population are anovulatory cycles and inherited bleeding disorders (BDOs). Qualitative platelet disorders (QPDs) comprise a substantial portion of these BDOs, though the reported prevalence among AYAs with HMB is variable, with rates ranging from 28% to 49%.
OBJECTIVES/HYPOTHESIS: Our primary aim was to assess the prevalence of QPDs among AYA individuals with unexplained HMB who were referred to our BDO clinic. In addition, we sought to understand how social determinants of health impacted time to testing for a QPD.
METHODS: This is a single-site, retrospective chart review of AYAs with unexplained HMB who underwent platelet function testing (PFT), composed of lumiaggregometry, quinacrine uptake/release, CD63 expression, and glycoprotein expression, at our institution. Data points collected included demographics, menstrual history (menarche and menstrual bleeding), which was determined by chart review, laboratory testing (PFT results), and timing from menarche to the first BDO visit, from menarche to PFT, and from first BDO visit to PFT to evaluate the impacts of social determinants of health.
RESULTS: A total of 411 individuals were included, and 44 individuals (10%) were ultimately diagnosed with a QPD. Of the 411 individuals, 103 (25%) had abnormal findings on initial PFT, many of which were nonspecific, prompting repeat testing. Repeat testing was performed in 63 of the 411 individuals (15%), and of those, 40 (10%) had normalization of PFT. Although there were no differences in time from menarche to first BDO visit or PFT, Black individuals had a longer median time from first BDO visit to first PFT than White individuals.
CONCLUSION: QPD is less prevalent in individuals with unexplained HMB than previously described. This study highlights the importance of repeating PFT to confirm abnormal results before diagnosing a QPD.

articles.title: Thrombophilia-Related Gene Polymorphisms and Recurrent Miscarriages in Lebanese Population: A Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Sharif-Askari E, Atoui K, Srour O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genes associated with cardiovascular diseases are strongly linked to idiopathic recurrent pregnancy loss. Because these genetic mutations often involve coagulation factors, anticoagulant therapy, particularly low-molecular-weight heparin, is increasingly encountered in obstetric practice in Lebanon for selected maternal and pregnancy-related indications. However, data describing the prevalence and prescribing patterns of anticoagulant use among Lebanese obstetricians remain limited. In this multicenter retrospective case-control study, 12 mutations within 10 CVD-related genes in Lebanese women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss were assessed to uncover further potential genetic links between these two conditions.
METHODS: Data were collected from a total of 117 women with recurrent pregnancy loss (≥ 2 pregnancy losses with the same partner before the 22nd week of gestation) and 38 women with a history of at least one successful pregnancy. Data were collected from two independent medical centers in Lebanon, Abou Jaoude Hospital and the Lebanese Diagnostic Medical Center, through medical-record review and participant interviews. Twelve mutations were covered employing polymerase chain reaction and reverse-hybridization techniques. Because of the variation in genotyping completeness across assays, the effective sample size for individual polymorphisms ranged from 27 to 38 controls and 78 to 117 cases.
RESULTS: Genetic analysis revealed a significant association between Factor V Leiden (OR = 0.31; p = 0.017), Factor XIII: V34L (OR = 0.3; p = 0.009), plasminogen activator inhibitor-1: 4G/5G (OR = 0.3; p = 0.034), and lower odds of recurrent pregnancy loss. However, these associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing and should therefore be considered exploratory. No significant associations were observed for other evaluated polymorphisms, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase C677T and A1298C.
CONCLUSION: Repeated pregnancy loss is multifaceted and not necessarily linked to coagulopathy-related mutations; in the Lebanese population, certain polymorphisms showed nominal associations with lower odds of recurrent pregnancy loss that require confirmation in larger, independent studies, and no statistically significant association was observed between methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase mutations and recurrent pregnancy loss in the present study. These findings suggest that the routine presumption of a…

articles.title: Cellular Phenotypic Changes in Endometriosis: Pathogenetic Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.authors: Zhang J, Bai Y, Luo S et al.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a common gynecological disorder characterized by extra-uterine growth of endometrial-like tissues, which causes chronic inflammation, pelvic pain and infertility and greatly impairs patients' quality of life. Despite its high prevalence, the exact pathogenesis of endometriosis remains incompletely understood and clinical therapeutic options are still limited. This paper is a combined narrative-bibliometric review. It systematically summarizes the roles and molecular mechanisms of multiple cellular phenotypic alterations including hypoxic microenvironment, aberrant cell proliferation, dysregulated autophagy, pyroptosis, ferroptosis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in the pathogenesis of endometriosis. Bibliometric analyses were performed based on the Web of Science Core Collection for each sub-theme, with dozens to hundreds of English-language publications included to assist in identifying research hotspots. By integrating evidence from in-vitro cellular experiments, animal models and human tissue studies, this review illustrates the interconnections among these cellular phenotypes, provides theoretical references for understanding the pathophysiology of endometriosis, and discusses corresponding translational and therapeutic implications.

articles.title: Plasma microbial cell-free DNA metagenomic sequencing for early detection of infection after liver transplantation: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.authors: Lee Y, Min EK, Park YJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) is a promising technique for diagnosing infectious diseases. However, research on mcfDNA-based mNGS for diagnosing infections in liver transplantation (LT) recipients remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of plasma mcfDNA mNGS during the early post-LT period.
METHODS: In this prospective diagnostic cohort study, adult LT recipients underwent plasma mcfDNA mNGS on postoperative days 7 and 14. The findings were compared with results of the blood cultures and other conventional microbiological tests at the species level.
RESULTS: Among 193 LT recipients, mNGS positivity was observed in 14.5% on day 7 and 21.8% on day 14. The concordance between mNGS and blood culture for bacterial pathogens was modest on days 7 (35.0%) and 14 (14.3%) but increased substantially when other clinically relevant specimens were included (80.0% and 71.4%, respectively). mNGS identified additional pathogens not detected using blood culture in 59.3% and 74.2% of cases on days 7 and 14, respectively. Viral pathogens, including cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and roseolovirus, were also detected. Among the 13 discordant cases (blood culture-positive and mNGS-negative), two (15.4%) were classified as contamination/colonization, five (38.5%) as weak positives, and six (46.2%) as not detected by mNGS.
CONCLUSION: Plasma mcfDNA mNGS demonstrated substantial concordance with conventional microbiological testing when clinically relevant specimens were considered. mNGS may serve as a useful adjunct tool for early pathogen detection and clinical assessment of LT recipients.

articles.title: Cardiovascular complications as a consequence of coronavirus infection in pregnant women managed in ambulatory settings.
articles.authors: Davarashvili I, Israel A, Vinker S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 has been linked to cardiovascular complications in the general population. However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. In this retrospective population-based matched cohort study, we evaluated whether COVID-19 infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular complications among pregnant women managed predominantly in outpatient settings.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based matched cohort study using electronic health record data from pregnant women between 2020 and 2025. Women with COVID-19 during pregnancy were matched 1:1 to women without documented COVID-19 during pregnancy according to demographic, obstetric, and clinical characteristics. The final analytical cohort included 4,068 women in each group. Cardiovascular outcomes during pregnancy and within a year since last menstrual period were assessed. Baseline demographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the COVID-19 and control groups. No significant differences were observed between the groups in the incidence of major cardiovascular complications, either when analyzed individually or as a composite endpoint (0.15% vs. 0.15%; OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.27-3.74). Specifically, there were no significant differences in the occurrence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, or deep venous thrombosis. In contrast, cough and backache were significantly more frequent among women with COVID-19 than among matched controls (6.88% vs. 4.87%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.19-1.75; 13.8% vs. 11.8%; OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05-1.37; p = 0.007 respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that among pregnant women in ambulatory community settings, COVID-19 infection is not associated with an increased risk of major cardiovascular complications.

articles.title: Assessing an educational strategy to improve community health provider-led provision of cervical cancer screening services in western Kenya: A secondary analysis of the Elimisha-HPV cluster-randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Chepkoech P, Jordan SB, Makhulo B et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer disproportionately impacts women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where over 90% of global cervical cancer deaths occur. Lay health workers, such as community health promoters (CHPs), with appropriate training and support, can play a pivotal role in cervical cancer prevention. Our team developed a multi-level intervention, Elimisha-HPV, to support CHP-delivered human papillomavirus (HPV) testing in Kenya. The present analysis evaluates impact of Elimisha-HPV on the following CHP outcomes: i) knowledge of screening delivery and privacy, confidentiality, and professionalism; ii) stigma associated with cervical cancer, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and HPV; and iii) confidence to counsel in screening delivery. We used descriptive statistics and linear mixed effects regression models to evaluate intervention effects (intervention group, n = 64; control group, n = 60). For knowledge and privacy, no statistically significant effects were observed (knowledge: β= -0.08 [95% CI, -0.22 to 0.07]; privacy: β= 0.04 [95% CI, -0.05 to 0.13]). No statistically significant intervention effects were observed for stigma associated with cervical cancer, HIV, or HPV (cervical cancer: β= 0.02 [95% CI, -0.13 to 0.16]; HIV: β= 0.01 [95% CI, -0.11 to 0.13]; HPV: β= 0.02 [95% CI, -0.11 to 0.14]). For the confidence to counsel Likert scale-style questions, evaluated using descriptive and regression approaches, proportional increases were observed across both arms, but the main effect was not statistically significant ( β= 0.01 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.11]). Our findings align with previous work demonstrating that stigma surrounding cervical cancer in LMICs is difficult to effectively influence, and provide a foundation for shaping future stigma-reduction campaigns. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05736588.

articles.title: Association between maternal dysglycaemia and adverse perinatal outcomes: A retrospective cohort study using a Japanese mother-infant-linked claims database.
articles.authors: Yamamoto K, Ihana-Sugiyama N, Sugiyama T et al.
articles.abstract: Claims-based perinatal studies in Japan are limited because normal pregnancies are not covered by health insurance. This study aimed to examine the association between maternal dysglycaemia and perinatal outcomes using a mother-infant-linked claims database. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the JMDC Claims Database from April 2012 to March 2023. Singleton mother-infant pairs were presumed by family ID and categorised into six mutually exclusive claims-based categories: anti-diabetic prescriptions both before and during pregnancy with (Category 1) or without (Category 2) a pre-pregnancy type 1 diabetes code, prescriptions in prenatal period only (Category 3), prescriptions before pregnancy only (Category 4), a gestational diabetes (GDM) management-fee claim without anti-diabetic prescriptions (Category 5) and no identified claims-based indicator of dysglycaemia (Category 6). Outcomes included caesarean section, macrosomia, preterm birth, neonatal asphyxia, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission and congenital malformations of the circulatory system. Among 115,113 presumed mother-infant pairs, 21.5% of mothers underwent caesarean section, with higher proportions in Categories 1 and 2 (40.6% and 48.3%). Highest point estimates were observed in Category 1 for most outcomes. Category 2 was associated with increased risks of caesarean section (adjusted risk ratio 2.04, 95% confidence interval 1.77-2.35), preterm birth (3.69, 2.57-5.28) and NICU admission (3.88, 3.02-4.99). Category 5 was positively associated with macrosomia (2.43, 1.64-3.62). Claims-based indicators of maternal dysglycaemia were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. These findings suggest potential utility of mother-infant-linked claims data for Japanese perinatal monitoring, subject to further validation.

articles.title: Real-world experience with INTERLACE-style induction chemotherapy: Tumor regression and MRI-guided brachytherapy in locally advanced cervical cancer.
articles.authors: Chavana A, Flanagan M, Owrangi A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Achieving optimal brachytherapy coverage for bulky cervical tumors (>30 cc) remains challenging, and the ideal treatment approach is unclear. This study describes real-world tumor volume response, brachytherapy dose delivery, and toxicity in patients treated with an INTERLACE-style induction chemotherapy regimen followed by chemoradiation and MRI-guided adaptive brachytherapy.
METHODS: This retrospective, two-institution cohort included eight patients with locally advanced cervical cancer treated with weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel induction chemotherapy followed by cisplatin-based chemoradiation and MRI-guided brachytherapy. All three serial tumor measurements (at diagnosis, after induction chemotherapy, and after chemoradiation/before brachytherapy) were obtained by pelvic MRI. Gross tumor volumes (GTV) were contoured by the treating radiation oncologist; organ-at-risk volumes were delineated by treating physicians.
RESULTS: FIGO stage was IIIC1 in 6 patients, IIA in 1, and IB3 in 1. Five patients (62.5%) were PD-L1 positive. Seven patients received tandem-and-ovoid brachytherapy and one received a Syed-Neblett interstitial implant. Median GTV was 88.3 cc (range 18-370) at diagnosis, 15.3 cc (range 0-187.1) after induction chemotherapy, and 2.2 cc (range 0-11.5) after chemoradiation. Median per-patient GTV reduction was 70% (range, 45-100%) after induction chemotherapy alone and 97% (range 74-100%) by completion of chemoradiation. Seven patients presented with bulky disease (>30 cc); three remained bulky after induction chemotherapy and none after chemoradiation. Median high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) D90 cumulative dose in 2-Gy fraction equivalents (EQ.D2) was 90.5 Gy (range 87-93.7) and median HR-CTV D98 was 79.8 Gy EQ.D2 (range 77.2-84.8; n = 7). Grade ≥ 3 hematologic toxicity was more common during chemoradiation than during induction chemotherapy (neutropenia in 3/8 [37.5%] vs 1/8 [12.5%]; leukopenia in 2/8 [25%] vs 0/8 [0%]). Thrombocytopenia (1/8,12.5%) and one case of anemia were observed exclusively during induction chemotherapy. Two patients discontinued cisplatin early because of hematologic toxicity. Seven of eight patients achieved a complete metabolic response on PET at 3 months post-treatment and remained disease-free at last follow-up (median 62.4 months; range 23.0-72.9).
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, INTERLACE-style induction chemotherapy produced substantial tumor regression that facilitated…

articles.title: Long-term endocrine and reproductive outcomes in female adolescent and young adult survivors after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence.
articles.authors: Zajączkowska W, Derwich K, Miedziarek C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer treatment during childhood and adolescence, particularly hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), may adversely affect long-term reproductive and endocrine health in female adolescent and young adult (AYA) survivors, leading to premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), which may be associated with impaired pubertal development, low bone mass, and reproductive complications.
METHODS: This study included 34 female survivors treated with HSCT for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence (median age 10.8 years). The median follow-up from HSCT to the last gynecological assessment was 8.5 years. Hormonal assessment, pelvic ultrasound, and bone mineral density (BMD) evaluation were performed. Patients were classified as having normal ovarian function, transient ovarian insufficiency (TOI), or persistent POI.
RESULTS: At the last follow-up, normal ovarian function was observed in 15 patients (44.1%), TOI in 7 (20.6%), and persistent POI in 12 (35.3%). Patients with normal ovarian function were significantly older at HSCT (p = 0.0432), whereas premenarchal status was associated with impaired ovarian outcome (p = 0.0066). In multivariable analysis including cyclophosphamide equivalent dose (CED), radiotherapy, and menarchal status at HSCT, postmenarchal status was associated with markedly lower odds of ovarian insufficiency (adjusted OR 0.056, 95% CI 0.005-0.566; p = 0.0147). All postmenarchal patients received GnRHa, precluding separation of the effects of menarchal status and GnRHa exposure; GnRHa-treated survivors had higher AMH concentrations (p =0.0032). AMH and FSH concentrations differed significantly between groups (both p < 0.01). Uterine and mean ovarian volumes, antral follicle count (AFC), and BMD were significantly lower in patients with TOI and POI (all p < 0.05). Radiotherapy exposure was associated with both lower uterine and ovarian volumes, while puberty induction was also associated with lower uterine volume (all p <0.05). Two patients diagnosed with POI achieved spontaneous pregnancies during follow-up, one resulting in a live birth.
CONCLUSIONS: Ovarian dysfunction is highly prevalent after childhood HSCT, although partial recovery of ovarian function may occur even in patients with a diagnosis of POI. Persistent POI is associated with impaired uterine development and lower BMD despite ongoing hormone replacement therapy, underscoring the need for timely and long-lasting individualized endocrine and…

articles.title: Yijing Decoction improves oocyte quality and inhibits lactate accumulation in mice with diminished ovarian reserve.
articles.authors: Yang J, Chu M, Zhang H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diminished ovarian reserve (DOR) is characterized by a decline in both oocyte quantity and quality, leading to compromised fertility. Yijing Decoction (YJD) has demonstrated promising therapeutic potential in DOR management. Nevertheless, the mechanisms driving this phenomenon are still largely unclear. This study is designed to comprehensively assess the effects of YJD on ovarian reserve function and oocyte quality in DOR mice, while investigating its potential underlying mechanisms of action.
METHODS: A DOR mouse model was established by administering cyclophosphamide via a single intraperitoneal injection. The therapeutic efficacy of YJD was systematically assessed through multiple functional and histological parameters, including ovarian index, estrous cycle regularity, serum sex hormone levels (FSH, LH, E2, AMH, and INH-B), and follicle counts, as well as the number, quality, and spindle morphology of metaphase I (MI) oocytes. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, ATP levels, pyruvate uptake, and lactate production were further quantified using commercially available ATP, pyruvate, and lactate assay kits. Additionally, immunofluorescence microscopy was employed to assess the protein expression levels of glycolysis-related proteins, including GLUT1, GLUT4, and LDHA, as well as components of the SIRT3/HIF-1α/PDK1 signaling axis in MI oocytes.
RESULTS: YJD treatment improved ovarian reserve function and oocyte quality in DOR mice, as evidenced by increased ovulated oocyte numbers, improved spindle integrity, and restored ATP levels. In addition, YJD treatment was associated with reduced expression of glycolysis-related proteins, including GLUT1, GLUT4, and LDHA, as well as decreased pyruvate uptake and lactate production in MI oocytes. YJD treatment also partially restored the expression pattern of the SIRT3/HIF-1α/PDK1 signaling pathway in DOR oocytes.
CONCLUSION: YJD improves oocyte quality in DOR mice, and its protective effects may be associated with the regulation of lactate metabolism and the SIRT3/HIF-1α/PDK1 signaling pathway.

articles.title: First-trimester trace-element profiles in pregnant women with epilepsy: An exploratory prospective association between selenium and subsequent seizure recurrence.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Altınsoy H, Reyhan Toptaş G, Altındiş Bal A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compares first-trimester serum zinc, copper, selenium and zinc-to-copper ratios between pregnant women with pre-existing epilepsy and healthy controls and assesses associations with subsequent seizure recurrence.
METHODS: This prospective controlled study included 48 pregnant women with pre-existing epilepsy and 59 controls. All women with epilepsy had been seizure free for at least 2 years before conception. Trace elements were measured at 6-12 gestational weeks, before recurrence. Between-group differences were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for maternal age, body mass index, smoking, and gestational week at sampling. Seizure recurrence was evaluated using logistic regression adjusted for epilepsy duration and type.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, women with epilepsy had 9.1% higher zinc, 56.3% higher copper, 16.8% lower selenium, and a 30.2% lower zinc-to-copper ratio after adjustment; all remained significant after false discovery rate correction. During follow-up, 20/48 women (41.7%) experienced recurrence. Selenium was lower in women with recurrence than in those who remained seizure free (36.53 [34.70-41.41] vs 46.36 [42.77-47.83] μg/L; P < 0.001), and each one-standard deviation increase in selenium was associated with lower odds of subsequent seizure recurrence after adjustment for epilepsy duration and type (adjusted OR 0.11, 95% CI 0.03-0.37). Zinc, copper, and the zinc-to-copper ratio were not associated with recurrence.
CONCLUSION: Pregnant women with epilepsy showed a distinct first-trimester trace-element profile. Lower first-trimester selenium was prospectively associated with subsequent seizure recurrence; however, this exploratory finding requires external validation before any predictive or clinical interpretation.

articles.title: Relationship between pre-micro-TESE serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels and sperm retrieval success in patients diagnosed with non-obstructive azoospermia: A retrospective study.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Yücetürk A, Peker N, Karaosmanoğlu Ö et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the relationship between serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels measured before microdissection testicular sperm extraction (mTESE) and sperm retrieval (SR) success in men diagnosed with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present study was based on retrospective evaluation of 58 patients who presented to our clinic between January 2025 and April 2026, were diagnosed with NOA, and underwent mTESE. Patient age, duration of infertility, serum AMH, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH) testosterone levels, and the AMH/testosterone ratio were recorded. Demographic and hormonal parameters were compared between the successful SR (+SR) and unsuccessful SR (-SR) groups after mTESE.
RESULTS: The mean age of the study population (n=58) was 35.53±6.10 years, and the mean infertility duration was 8.25±4.53 years. The mean serum AMH level was 2.42±2.35 ng/mL (median: 2.14 ng/mL; range: 0.01-9.87 ng/mL). +SR was achieved in 29 patients (50%), whereas no sperm could be retrieved in the remaining 29 patients (50%). Comparison of two groups revealed no statistically significant difference between the sperm-positive and sperm-negative groups with respect to age, duration of infertility, AMH, FSH, LH, testosterone, or the AMH/testosterone ratio. Receiver operating characteristic analysis revealed an area under the curve value of 0.531 for AMH (95% confidence interval: 0.379-0.683, p=0.690), indicating no significant predictive value. Binomial logistic regression analysis also found no variable to be a significant predictor of +SR.
CONCLUSION: Serum AMH level, either alone or in combination with other hormonal parameters, was not found to be a reliable clinical biomarker for predicting SR outcomes in men with NOA undergoing mTESE. Larger, prospective, etiologically stratified studies are required to determine the definitive role of AMH in preoperative evaluation.

articles.title: Self-reported genitopelvic pain disorders and symptoms among individuals with confirmed or suspected slipping rib syndrome: An exploratory cross-sectional survey.
articles.journal: The Journal of international medical research
articles.authors: Niedenfuehr J, Stevens D
articles.abstract: ObjectiveSlipping rib syndrome is an underrecognized condition characterized by hypermobility of the false ribs (ribs 8-10), resulting in pain throughout the abdominal and pelvic regions. This study aimed to describe genitopelvic pain disorders and related experiences among individuals with slipping rib syndrome.MethodsAn exploratory, descriptive, cross-sectional survey was distributed using convenience sampling from July 2024 to November 2024. Sociodemographic characteristics, diagnostic timelines, and the Patient Global Impression of Change were used to assess the self-reported efficacy of pelvic floor physical therapy for genitopelvic pain disorders among individuals with slipping rib syndrome.ResultsSeventy-nine individuals with slipping rib syndrome participated; most were women (92.2%) and White (96.9%), and the mean age was 33.4 years. The average diagnostic delay was 5.4 years, and frequent misdiagnoses included costochondritis, anxiety, and gastrointestinal conditions. More than half (54.4%) had Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, predominantly the hypermobile subtype (81.1%). More than 50% reported moderate to severe impacts of slipping rib syndrome on sexual activity, and 26.9% attributed their vulvar or pelvic pain directly to the condition. Common comorbidities included hypertonic pelvic floor, chronic pelvic pain syndrome, endometriosis, vaginismus, interstitial cystitis, and pudendal neuralgia. Among participants who received pelvic floor physical therapy for genitopelvic pain disorders and symptoms, the mean Patient Global Impression of Change score was 4.5, indicating no change to minimal improvement, and 18.2% reported worsening symptoms. Diaphragmatic breathing similarly resulted in no improvement or worsening of symptoms in many participants.ConclusionsThis study is the first to explore the potential impact of slipping rib syndrome on sexual activity and its possible contribution to genitopelvic pain disorders. Symptom overlap with gynecologic conditions complicates diagnosis and management. These findings underscore the importance of evaluating for slipping rib syndrome during pelvic health assessments, particularly in patients with persistent or unexplained pelvic and abdominal pain. Further research is needed to clarify the musculoskeletal mechanisms underlying pelvic pain and to guide interdisciplinary care for individuals with slipping rib syndrome.

articles.title: Comparison of embryological and clinical outcomes of ICSI cycles using ejaculated versus testicular sperm (TESA/mTESE) in men with cryptozoospermia: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Yücetürk A, Peker N, Karaosmanoğlu Ö et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the embryological and clinical outcomes of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycles using ejaculated versus testicular sperm (TESA/mTESE) in men with cryptozoospermia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 127 ICSI cycles performed in couples with male cryptozoospermia at the Acıbadem Maslak Hospital Assisted Reproductive Technology Center between 2017 and 2026. Cycles were grouped according to sperm source as ejaculated (n=58) or testicular (n=69; mTESE, n=51; TESA, n=18). The primary outcome was the pregnancy rate per embryo transfer. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for confounders.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar, except for a higher number of previous IVF attempts in the testicular sperm group (p=0.032) and a more frequent history of miscarriage in the ejaculated sperm group (15.5% vs. 4.5%, p=0.037). The testicular sperm group had more day 5 blastocysts (median 5 vs. 3, p=0.004) and a higher blastocyst formation rate (57.2% vs. 34.3%, p<0.001), but also more grade 3 blastocysts (p<0.001). Per embryo transfer, pregnancy (80.0% vs. 54.5%, p=0.006) and clinical pregnancy rates (78.0% vs. 47.3%, p=0.001) were higher in the ejaculated sperm group, whereas live birth rates were similar (48.0% vs. 45.5%, p=0.794). After adjustment for female age, previous IVF attempts, embryo stage at transfer and embryo quality, sperm source was not independently associated with pregnancy (adjusted odds ratio: 1.94, 95% confidence interval: 0.71-5.26, p=0.195); blastocyst-stage transfer and grade 1 embryo quality were the independent predictors.
CONCLUSION: In men with cryptozoospermia, testicular sperm increased blastocyst yield but did not improve pregnancy or live birth rates compared with ejaculated sperm. When ejaculated spermatozoa are available, routine surgical sperm retrieval does not appear to provide a clinical advantage.

articles.title: Apigenin and Placental β-Endorphin Signaling: A Hypothesis-Generating Mechanistic Review.
articles.journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.authors: Goswami B, Adhikari T, Das S
articles.abstract: The placenta functions as a dynamic endocrine hub that translates maternal exposures into offspring developmental programming, consistent with the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) framework. Beta-endorphin (β-EP), a placental POMC-derived opioid peptide, signals through MOR/DOR/KOR receptors to regulate angiogenesis, immune tolerance, oxidative stress, inflammation, and nutrient transport. Apigenin, a dietary flavone found in parsley, chamomile, and celery, modulates several pathways that overlap with this axis, including CREB/PKA signaling, DNA methyltransferase activity, Nrf2, NF-κB/NLRP3, and Foxp3+ Treg differentiation, although most supporting evidence derives from non-placental systems such as cancer lines, keratinocytes, and macrophages. This review proposes that apigenin may amplify placental β-EP signaling across three conceptual tiers: a biosynthetic tier involving CREB/PKA-mediated POMC activation and 11β-HSD1 inhibition; a receptor-level tier involving DNMT1/3a inhibition and OPRM1 demethylation; and an effector-level tier involving Nrf2 activation, NF-κB/NLRP3 suppression, and Treg expansion, the last representing the strongest trophoblast-level evidence. Given reported β-EP dysregulation in preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and intrauterine growth restriction, apigenin's relevance to these disorders remains an untested hypothesis rather than a validated therapeutic strategy, informed by a structured, non-systematic literature search (1986-2026).

articles.title: The role of artificial intelligence in predicting late-onset intrauterine growth restriction in singleton pregnancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Miranda MT, Atienza AE, Santos JNM et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Late-onset intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is difficult to detect and is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning, for predicting late-onset IUGR in singleton pregnancies.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies published during the past decade that used AI to predict IUGR. Nineteen studies including 13,379 pregnancies were analyzed. Sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratios were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; the area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was estimated in STATA.
RESULTS: In the primary analysis (one model per study, k=17), pooled sensitivity was 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89), specificity was 0.89 (95% CI, 0.85 to 0.91), the positive and negative likelihood ratios were 6.6 (95% CI, 5.3 to 8.1) and 0.22 (95% CI, 0.16 to 0.30), and the AUC was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.91 to 0.95). Estimates were unchanged when all model entries were included (k=51). No threshold effect or funnel-plot asymmetry was detected. Subgroup estimates for support vector machines, random forests, and logistic regression were similar but reflected indirect comparisons.
CONCLUSION: AI/ML models showed high pooled discriminative accuracy for late-onset IUGR. However, the evidence derives mainly from retrospective, single-center case-control studies without external validation; calibration was reported in six of 19 studies and decision-curve analysis in none. These estimates are an optimistic upper bound, not evidence of superiority over current ultrasound practice.

articles.title: Elevated Level of Fannyhessea vaginae Correlated with Implantation Outcomes in Women undergoing in vitro fertilization Treatment.
articles.authors: Paramita L, Teng CH, Ma MC et al.
articles.abstract: The vaginal microbiome plays a significant role in reproductive health. While maintaining a balanced vaginal microbiome is crucial for successful in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, the specific bacteria associated with adverse outcomes may vary by region and are largely unknown. This study aims to investigate the bacterial profiles and their influence on embryo implantation, thereby supporting the development of microbiome-based therapies. One hundred women undergoing IVF provided vaginal swabs at three stages: oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and hCG pregnancy testing. An in-house 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and bioinformatics pipeline was used to profile the vaginal microbiota. Bacterial communities were constructed, and the transitions across IVF stages were analyzed. We also used custom quantitative PCR assays to validate NGS results and provide species-level resolution for selected bacterial species. Unlike other regions where Lactobacillus crispatus predominates, we found that Lactobacillus iners is the main vaginal microbiota across all IVF stages in Taiwan. Nevertheless, significant shifts in bacterial community types were correlated with hormonal changes during IVF treatment. Importantly, while Lactobacillus levels didn't predict pregnancy success, higher levels of bacteria associated with bacterial vaginosis, particularly Fannyhessea vaginae, significantly correlated with implantation failure and early embryonic loss. The strong association between elevated F. vaginae levels and adverse implantation rate in Taiwanese women highlights the potential benefit of incorporating routine screening for this pathogen. Personalized microbiome interventions targeting F. vaginae may improve embryo implantation for women undergoing assisted reproductive technologies.

articles.title: Curcumin extract addition to bull semen does not adversely affect in vitro fertilization.
articles.authors: Cojkic A, Sajecka O, Sjunnesson Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Curcumin extract has demonstrated antioxidant and antibacterial properties in bull semen samples at a concentration of 5%. Nevertheless, its impact on fertilization outcomes remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate if curcumin extract added to bull semen had an effect on in vitro fertilization (IVF) results. Bovine ovaries were collected from an abattoir, cumulus-oocyte complexes (COCs) were aspirated, graded, and randomly assigned to treatment groups before maturation. The COCs were matured for 22 hours and fertilized using semen from one bull with verified fertility. Semen samples were thawed and treated with 5% curcumin extract for 30 minutes at room temperature, and IVF was conducted at a reduced sperm concentration (0.5 × 106/mL) to better assess treatment effects. Cleavage was evaluated, 44 hours post-fertilization, and embryo development was assessed on day 8. Sperm quality parameters were evaluated using Computer-Assisted Sperm Analysis for motility and kinematics, and Flow Cytometry for viability markers, including membrane integrity, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), and chromatin integrity.
RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed between groups for any IVF outcomes. A trend toward significance was observed for total motility and immotile spermatozoa, with higher motility and lower immotility in the curcumin-treated group compared to controls.
CONCLUSION: The results demonstrated that curcumin treatment does not seem to have an effect on in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes since no statistically significant differences were observed between the curcumin-treated and control groups in cleavage rate, the proportion of oocytes reaching more than two cells, or blastocyst formation on day 8. These findings indicate that, under the experimental conditions of this study, curcumin does not impair the fertilization capacity of bull sperm.

articles.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
articles.authors: Al-Amili WA, Ayyed Najm M, Jumaah SS et al.
articles.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in-silico functional annotations against this experimental ground truth revealed poor predictive performance (cross-validated ROC-AUC = 0.55-0.59), demonstrating that computational predictions cannot reliably substitute for measured allelic activity. We therefore treated the ovarian analysis as hypothesis-generating. Convergent annotation evidence prioritised 44 of 176 ovarian cancer GWAS leads (31 independent loci); a core of 21 SNPs (17 loci) was stable under alternative weights, leave-one-feature-out scoring and threshold changes, and candidates were enriched in ovarian and fallopian-tube regulatory chromatin (OR = 7.9, FDR = 5 × 10⁻5). Copy-number recurrence at candidate genes agreed between two tumour cohorts (Spearman ρ = 0.75, 95% CI 0.46-0.88) but no more than for chromosome-arm-matched control genes, so this observation is exploratory. Formal colocalisation with full summary statistics supported a shared causal variant for prostate cancer risk and TLCD3A expression at 17p13.3 (PP.H4 = 0.92), whereas the ovarian 17q21.31 signal could not be resolved to a single gene. Transcription-factor motifs disrupted in both cancers were over-represented for the interferon-regulatory factor (IRF) and STAT families (FDR = 3 × 10⁻6), a motif-level hypothesis. In an independent MPRA in primary ovarian epithelial cells, variants disrupting interferon-stimulated response elements (ISREs) were depleted, not enriched, for allele-specific activity (4.6% vs 9.2%; OR = 0.47, nominal p = 0.06, FDR = 0.10), so the IRF/STAT hypothesis was not supported; the same assay confirmed allele-specific activity at one prioritised ovarian candidate, rs2976384 (skew = - 0.67, FDR = 3 × 10⁻5). These results provide an audited prostate regulatory-SNP catalogue, quantify the limits of annotation-based fine-mapping, and offer testable cross-cancer hypotheses.

articles.title: "I am the expert of my own self, and this is what I choose": a qualitative investigation of diverse cultural experiences with birth control.
articles.authors: Eligado GM, Cleveland A, Ramirez EG et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite medical advances and widespread use, approximately 1 in 4 current and prospective female contraceptive users in the United States do not access their preferred method of contraception. Understanding how to address cultural barriers to contraceptives is critical to improving access. This study investigated how different aspects of cultural background influence contraceptive perceptions and experiences. We explored this question with an intersectional lens, recruiting participants with a range of multicultural identities.
METHODS: Between 2023 and 2024, we conducted 32 in-depth interviews with a diverse sample of pregnancy-capable people around the puget sound in Washington, asking how culture influences attitudes and decisions regarding birth control. Codes were created inductively from interview transcripts and were grouped by definitional similarities and co-occurrences with each other. The research team identified themes that represented the overarching influences of cultural norms and experiences on birth control perceptions and use.
RESULTS: From analysis of 32 in-depth interviews, our analysis revealed four main themes: (1) Cultural Birth Control Stigma Spread Through Gossip, Misinformation, and Silence; (2) Expectations from Family and Gendered Norms Hinder Preferred Birth Control Use; (3) Autonomy, Access to Culturally Competent Providers, and Access to Comprehensive Information Facilitate Positive Perceptions of Birth Control; (4) Desire for Birth Control Accessibility, Comprehensive Education, Decreased Stigma, and Shared Contraceptive Responsibility.
CONCLUSION: A diverse group of participants reported nuanced themes of cultural birth control stigma and familial and gendered expectations as barriers to positive birth control perceptions and use, while values of autonomy, culturally understanding healthcare providers, and comprehensive education facilitated positive birth control perceptions. To address unique patient needs, providers should acknowledge perceptions of stigma, address patient and familial knowledge gaps through tailored contraceptive counseling, and prioritize full transparency on benefits and side effects. Providers must recognize patients' individual experiences and consider culture as a nuanced and complex influence.

articles.title: "One counselling strategy does not fit all": Midwives' experiences of providing contraceptive counselling to girls and young women with ADHD - a Swedish qualitative interview study.
articles.authors: Johansson M, Haglund A, Asplin N
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite accessible services, unmet contraceptive needs persist among young women in Sweden. Young women with ADHD may have diverse sexual and reproductive health needs, and previous research has identified challenges related to healthcare access, communication, and contraceptive use. However, less is known about how midwives experience providing contraceptive counselling to girls and young women with ADHD. This study aimed to describe midwives' experiences of providing contraceptive counselling to girls and young women with ADHD in Swedish youth clinics.
METHODS: A qualitative exploratory study design using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis of interviews, including ten midwives providing contraceptive counselling to young women with ADHD. The average interview time was 34 min.
RESULTS: The participating midwives were aged 31 to 62 years and had between six months and 24 years of experience working in youth clinics across four of Sweden's six healthcare regions. Their experiences were captured by the overarching theme, Adapting contraceptive counselling to individual needs despite limited ADHD-specific support, which encompassed three themes: Striving to provide person-centered counselling, Navigating counselling in response to increased support needs, and Recognizing the importance of ADHD-specific knowledge and resources to support counselling.
CONCLUSIONS: Midwives described adapting contraceptive counselling to perceived individual needs through changes in communication, consultation structures, access to care, and interprofessional collaboration. They also described a need for stronger ADHD-specific education and evidence-informed professional guidance. Support for counselling should provide a structured professional foundation while allowing flexibility to respond to individual circumstances and preferences.

articles.title: Effectiveness of health mediation to promote organised cancer screening among underserved and under-screened populations in Marseille, France: findings from a repeated cross-sectional survey.
articles.authors: Legendre E, Dutrey-Kaiser A, Attalah Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since 2022, the "13 en Santé" health mediation program has been implemented in Marseille, France, to reduce social health inequalities, in socioeconomically disadvantage neighbourhoods, with a particular emphasis on promoting participation in population-based organised cancer screening programs. Led by multidisciplinary teams including health mediators, nurses, coordinators, and volunteers, the intervention is structured around three core components: (i) territory exploration to develop knowledge of local communities and resources; (ii) culturally appropriate health education delivered through outreach activities to reach underserved populations; and (iii) individualised navigation support tailored to needs and level of autonomy. This study evaluates the effectiveness of this program in promoting breast, colorectal, and cervical cancer screening.
METHODS: A controlled before-after design based on two cross-sectional knowledge-attitude-practice surveys was conducted in 2022 and 2024 in intervention or control neighbourhoods. Individuals aged 18-74 were randomly selected and interviewed via door-to-door questionnaires. Weighting was applied to account for stratified sampling and to align age and sex distributions with census data. For each cancer, weighted logistic regression models assessed associations between health mediation exposure and screening uptake and awareness at both individual and population levels.
RESULTS: Overall, 4,523 individuals were included across the two cross-sectional surveys. The program successfully reached individuals facing cumulative socioeconomic barriers to healthcare access. No significant population-level association was observed between health mediation and cancer screening uptake or awareness. At the individual level, declared exposure to health mediation was associated with significantly higher uptakes of breast and colorectal cancer screenings (breast: 74% vs. 54%, OR = 2.3 [1.1-4.5]; colorectal: 50% vs. 30%, OR = 2.8 [1.3-5.8]). In addition, colorectal cancer screening awareness was significantly higher among exposed participants (93% vs. 83%, OR = 8.1 [2.1-31]).
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first evidence that reported individual exposure to a multicomponent health mediation intervention was significantly associated with an important increase in breast and colorectal cancer screening uptake in disadvantaged European neighbourhoods. Although the limitations of this observational study preclude…

articles.title: Clinical utility of chromosomal microarray analysis for genetic diagnosis in 708 cases of spontaneous abortion tissues.
articles.authors: Huang Y, An Q, Tao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic yield, abnormality spectrum, and clinical interpretation value of chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) in products of conception from pregnancy loss, and to explore the associations of maternal age and gestational age with different categories of chromosomal abnormalities.
METHODS: This study involved a retrospective cohort analysis of chorionic villus or fetal tissue samples obtained from patients with spontaneous abortion who visited our center between 2017 and 2025. Genomic DNA was extracted from all samples and subjected to genome-wide screening using CMA to detect chromosomal aneuploidies and copy number variations (CNVs). The pathogenicity of detected CNVs was evaluated according to the guidelines established by the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG). Furthermore, clinical characteristics such as maternal age were used as stratification variables to compare the chromosomal abnormality rates across different subgroups.
RESULTS: Of the 708 samples analyzed, 348 cases (49.15%) were found to have clinically significant chromosomal abnormalities, comprising 347 pathogenic and one likely pathogenic variants. In the 705 samples with successful testing results, there were 365 detected chromosomal abnormalities, yielding a detection rate of 51.77%. This finding highlights that chromosomal abnormalities constitute a major genetic etiology of spontaneous abortion. Furthermore, within the successfully tested cohort, numerical chromosomal abnormalities were the most prevalent type, identified in 287 cases (40.71%). This was followed by microdeletions in 37 cases (5.25%) and microduplications in 27 cases (3.83%). However, mosaicism, whole-genome uniparental disomy (UPD), and long contiguous stretches of homozygosity (LCSH) were rare, being detected in only four cases in total. Among the numerical anomalies, autosomal trisomy was the primary subtype, with trisomy 16 being the most frequently observed autosomal trisomy.
CONCLUSION: Chromosomal microarray analysis plays a pivotal role in the etiological diagnosis of spontaneous abortion. As a high-resolution, high-throughput detection method, it enables genome-wide identification of CNVs, particularly submicroscopic deletions and duplications that are difficult to detect with conventional karyotyping. CMA showed a high testing success rate and provided clinically useful information for the genetic evaluation of products of conception. Its advantages…

articles.title: Determinants of institutional delivery in Afghanistan: evidence from the 2022/2023 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS).
articles.authors: Gardiwal H, Saeedzai SA, Feroz F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Afghanistan has one of the highest maternal mortality ratios in the world, and the place where a woman gives birth is a critical determinant of maternal and newborn survival. Although the determinants of institutional delivery have been widely studied, nationally representative evidence from the most recent post-2021 data covering both urban and rural women remains scarce. This study examined the determinants of institutional delivery in Afghanistan.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Afghanistan Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) 2022/2023. The descriptive analysis included 12,578 women aged 15-49 years who had a live birth in the two years preceding the survey. The outcome was institutional (health-facility) versus home delivery. Descriptive and bivariate analyses used survey-weighted methods accounting for the multistage cluster design, stratification, and sampling weights. Multivariable associations were estimated using three-level mixed-effects logistic regression, with women nested within households, which were nested within primary sampling units (PSUs). A common complete-case sample of 12,462 women was used for four models: Model 0 (null), Model I (individual-level factors), Model II (household- and community-level factors), and Model III (full model). PSU-level contextual measures of community educational attainment and community socioeconomic status were derived from within-PSU aggregates and modeled alongside urban/rural residence. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), random-effects variances, intraclass correlations (ICCs), median odds ratios (MORs), proportional change in PSU variance (PCV), and model-fit statistics were reported. A two-level PSU-only model was fitted as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Overall, 66.3% of women delivered in a health facility (95% CI 64.5-68.1). In the fully adjusted three-level model, higher education was associated with higher odds of institutional delivery compared with pre-primary/ECE or no education (AOR 7.92; 95% CI 2.40-26.11), while women with five or more children had lower odds than those with 0-1 child (AOR 0.19; 95% CI 0.12-0.31). Antenatal care was strongly associated with institutional delivery (AOR 7.12; 95% CI 5.32-9.53), as were urban residence (AOR 2.46; 95% CI 1.61-3.78) and residence in communities with high socioeconomic status (AOR 6.90; 95% CI 4.23-11.24 versus low socioeconomic status). The PSU-level variance declined from 7.44 in…

articles.title: Genetic diagnostic yield of prenatal testing for fetal central nervous system abnormalities: a phenotype-driven study in a large single-center cohort.
articles.authors: Fu X, Zhong W, Yao Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic yield and clinical value of a phenotype-driven genomic testing strategy in fetuses with central nervous system (CNS) abnormalities.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 966 fetuses with CNS abnormalities detected by prenatal ultrasound and/or fetal magnetic resonance imaging were included. All cases underwent copy number variation sequencing (CNV-seq), while karyotyping and trio exome sequencing (trio-ES) were performed based on clinical indications and parental preference. Fetuses were stratified into isolated-single, isolated-complex, and non-isolated subgroups according to CNS involvement and extracranial abnormalities. Diagnostic yields were compared across phenotypic subgroups and common CNS phenotypes.
RESULTS: Among 966 fetuses with prenatal CNS abnormalities, pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants were identified in 12.63% of cases. CNV-seq had a diagnostic yield of 8.07% (78/966), while trio-ES had a diagnostic yield of 16.32% (70/429) and provided an additional 10.92% yield (44/403) following negative CNV-seq results. Diagnostic yield varied significantly across phenotypic subgroups, with a higher CNV-seq yield in non-isolated cases than in isolated cases (15.41% vs. 4.25%, P < 0.001), and a higher ES yield in isolated-complex cases than in isolated-single cases (32.56% vs. 9.20%, P < 0.001). After excluding mild isolated CNS anomalies, diagnostic yields increased to 15.60% for CNV-seq and 26.67% for ES. In the adjusted cohort, differences among the three subgroups remained significant for CNV-seq (P < 0.001) but not for ES (P = 0.156). Across phenotypes, major structural abnormalities demonstrated substantially higher diagnostic yields than mild or soft markers, with a clear severity-dependent increase observed in ventriculomegaly and head circumference reduction.
CONCLUSION: Fetal CNS abnormalities show substantial genetic heterogeneity, and diagnostic yield is closely associated with prenatal imaging phenotypes. A phenotype-driven testing strategy may help prioritize genetic evaluation and improve prenatal counseling for fetuses with CNS abnormalities.

articles.title: Novel Mobile and Facility Reproductive Health Kits: enhancing safe abortion and post-abortion care during disasters and humanitarian crises.
articles.authors: Ray-Bennett NS, Mustary E, Klangboonkrong T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal deaths from unsafe abortion and post-abortion complications are entirely preventable. Yet, women and adolescent girls in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) continue to die due to a lack of timely, quality care, especially during disasters. Access to safe abortion and post-abortion care (PAC) is promoted through several strategies, including the Inter-Agency Reproductive Health (IARH) Kit 8. This study introduces the findings of two novel RH Kits prototypes, Facility and Mobile for disasters and crises, exploring: (i) the estimated number of affected persons a combined Kit can serve; (ii) the total and itemised cost of producing these Kits; and (iii) how the prototype Facility Kit aligns with national safe abortion aka menstrual regulation (MR) and PAC guidelines in Bangladesh compared to Kit 8.
METHODS: A mixed-methods explanatory sequential design was used to prototype the Kits, combining document reviews, survey findings, key informant consultations, a focus group discussion, and expert input (Jan 2024-July 2025). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, side-by-side analysis and triangulation.
RESULTS: Findings indicate the Kits can serve 5-30 affected persons, depending on facility capacity. Estimated costs range from USD 535 (small Facility Kit) to USD 1,178 (large Facility Kit) and USD 82 (Mobile Kit). The Facility Kit offers a comprehensive, locally adapted package, including sterilisation equipment and context-specific design.
CONCLUSIONS: These Kits have the potential to strengthen health system resilience to disasters. The Mobile Kit has the potential to address last-mile delivery, enabling trained providers to reach women in hard-to-reach areas affected by disasters. This innovation can improve access to safe abortion and PAC during disasters and can offer a scalable model for Bangladesh and other LMICs facing recurrent climate-related hazards.

articles.title: "…our goal is to avoid abortions whenever possible.": A qualitative study on clinical and structural barriers to abortion in Mongolia in 2025.
articles.authors: Schwandt HM, Tegshee B, Dugarsuren O et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are a number of structural barriers to abortion in Mongolia including limitations on who can provide abortions and where, exaggerated fears of abortion infertility, particularly for minors, cost of the procedure, and required pre procedure clinical tests.
METHODS: This 2025 qualitative study utilized 24 in depth interviews with abortion clients, male partners of abortion clients, and abortion providers to better understand clinical and structural barriers to abortion in Mongolia.
RESULTS: Abortion providers are barriers to abortion through their desire to dissuade potential clients from abortion through persuasive language and emphasizing exaggerated risks of abortion. Mandated clinical procedures prior to the abortion are also barriers to abortion in this setting - in terms of increased wait time, expenses, and pre procedure tasks. The tasks include an ultrasound, vaginal swab, and blood tests for STIs.
