CONCLUSIONS: Abortion clients have many systemic hurdles to obtain an abortion in Mongolia out of their control - from providers openly sharing unabashedly their negative attitudes and beliefs about abortion to the government mandated policies regarding abortion.

articles.title: Post-abortion contraceptive uptake of clients and its related factors in Northwest Ethiopia, 2020.
articles.journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
articles.authors: Gashaye KT, Kassie BA, Taddese AA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The post-abortion period is the right time to introduce contraceptive services as women's fertility returns early. A majority of women in Ethiopia had an abortion for unwanted pregnancies and this cycle could continue unless contraceptive counseling and services are available and provided for women after an abortion. Thus, our study aimed to fill this gap and prepare strategies to improve uptake.
METHODS: Institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted to collect data in private and public health facilities in northwest Ethiopia. Data were entered with Epi-info and transported to Stata 14 for cleaning (using frequencies, sorting, and listing to identify missed values and outliers) and analysis. Bivariate analysis was carried out first to observe the crude association between independent and outcome variables. The variables with p-value < 0.2 in bivariate analysis, not collinear (checked with Variance Inflation Factor -VIF-Value 0.86), were entered into multiple logistic regressions to assess net effect by controlling confounders. Finally, statistically significant variables were reported with the odds ratio, a 95% confidence interval, and p-value < 0.05.
RESULT: About, about three-fifth (61.5%) utilized Post Abortion Contraception (PAC) immediately after the procedure. Five hundred thirty-one (86%) reported that they had counseling sessions. Having post-abortion contraceptive counseling [AOR = 4.83, 95% CI: (2.77-8.40)]; ever use of contraceptives [AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: (1.04-2.96)]; history of abortion [AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: (0.15-0.68)]; being aged 24 to 28 years [AOR = 0.28, 95% CI: (0.09-0.81)], Primigravida [AOR = 0.48, 95% CI: (0.24-0.96)], wanted pregnancy status [AOR = 0.36, 95% CI: (0.21-0.62)]; being single [AOR = 2.42, 95% CI: (1.25-4.71)], never married [AOR = 0.55, 95% CI: (0.31-0.97)], and separated from partner [AOR = 0.37, 95% CI: (0.2-0.68)] were found to have significant association with postabortion contraception use.
CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS: The study found that PAC uptake was low compared with the recommendations. Strengthening contraceptive counseling (regardless of women's status) by giving priorities for who had unstable relationships (single and separated), have first pregnancy, and encountering repeated abortion care services. Moreover, provision of value clarification training for providers could also improve service use. We recommended that researchers to explore deep feelings and reasons that women had for…

articles.title: "She cannot use these methods before she has at least one child": a qualitative study on family planning attitudes, knowledge, and experiences among adolescent girls and young women living with HIV in Moshi, Tanzania.
articles.authors: Salm MF, Ngowi H, Rugalabamu L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Each year, about half of pregnancies in adolescents (15-19 years of age) are unintended, and the rate of adolescent pregnancy in sub-Saharan Africa is twice the global rate. Adolescent pregnancies have similar social determinants as those of HIV acquisition, resulting in adverse health outcomes for adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) and exacerbating adverse HIV-related health outcomes. To better understand reproductive choice for AGYW living with HIV (AGYWLWH), this study examined family planning attitudes, knowledge, and experiences among young women living with HIV in Moshi, Tanzania.
METHODS: Young female participants previously enrolled in the SYV pilot trial were purposively sampled to understand their attitudes, knowledge, and experiences with family planning services through in-depth interviews and a focus group discussion. Participants with a pregnancy experience (PE) and those without (NPE) were recruited to explore contextually relevant factors shaping these constructs. Thematic analysis included inductive and deductive coding, a data reduction matrix, and memo writing to identify and synthesize themes.
RESULTS: Of 16 enrolled participants, 13 had a pregnancy experience. The average age at first pregnancy was 20 years old, and almost two-thirds of participants experienced an unintended pregnancy (9/13). Participants shared that family planning services and hormonal contraception felt inaccessible until they had a pregnancy, often due to perceived social norms around sexual promiscuity or due to a fear of contraception-induced infertility. As a result, participants shared they did not feel well-informed about contraceptive options prior to their first pregnancy, while mentioning that contraceptive information pre-pregnancy often did not feel relevant. Therefore, no participants used hormonal contraception prior to their first pregnancy, and the most common method ever used was the male condom (8/16). After a first pregnancy, hormonal method use was more prevalent (9/13), and the most common hormonal method used was the implant (5/13). Almost all participants felt contraception was useful and promoted reproductive choice, citing the importance of birth spacing, particularly related to the successful prevention of maternal to child transmission. Despite perceived social norms related to family planning use pre-pregnancy, participants recommended AGYWLWH use family planning to achieve their personal and family composition goals, and…

articles.title: Exploring male involvement and support in long-acting reversible contraceptive decision-making: a mixed-methods cross-sectional study in Kampala, Uganda.
articles.authors: Nyasulu B, Ngomi N, Kibonire RA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male involvement in family planning is a critical yet underexplored factor influencing contraceptive uptake and decision-making, particularly for long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs). In Kampala, Uganda, socio-cultural norms and misconceptions may limit men's participation in reproductive health services. This study assessed the extent, determinants, and barriers to male involvement in LARC decision-making among couples.
METHODS: A mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted between March and September 2025 in Makindye Division and Kisugu Health Centre III. Quantitative data were collected from 362 women using structured questionnaires, while qualitative data were obtained from six focus group discussions (FGDs) with men and women, and five key informant interviews (KIIs) with healthcare providers. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS, and qualitative data were thematically analyzed in NVivo. Instruments were pre-tested and assessed for reliability.
RESULTS: While 96% of women reported that their partners discussed contraception with healthcare providers, only 10% accompanied their partners to clinics. Male support for family planning was mainly financial (60%), and joint decision-making on LARCs occurred in 39% of couples. Key determinants of male involvement included marital status, education level, and number of children. Cultural norms and religious beliefs emerged as significant barriers. Qualitative findings highlighted entrenched gender norms, misconceptions about contraceptives, and the perception that reproductive health services are primarily for women. Participants reported limited couple-focused counseling, with only 44% indicating men's concerns were adequately addressed during consultations.
CONCLUSIONS: Male involvement in LARC decision-making in Kampala remains low due to socio-cultural barriers and limited male-friendly services. Strengthening male engagement requires inclusive counseling by trained health workers, community and religious leader involvement, and promotion of male-friendly and couple-centered reproductive health services.

articles.title: Prevalence of Factor V Leiden mutation in yemeni women with gestational diabetes mellitus and recurrent pregnancy loss: a case-control study.
articles.authors: Al Matari NA, Al-Obeidi AM, Al-Zabedi E
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most common metabolic disorders during pregnancy and has been associated with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and other obstetric complications. The Factor V Leiden (FVL) is a common inherited thrombophilic mutation. However, data on the prevalence of the FVL mutation among Yemeni women with GDM and a history of RPL remain scarce. Therefore, this case-control study aimed to determine the prevalence of the FVL mutation and examine its association among Yemeni women with GDM and recurrent pregnancy loss compared with healthy pregnant controls.
METHODS: This case-control study included 200 Yemeni women with GDM and 200 healthy pregnant controls without a previous history of GDM. Ethical approval was obtained from the Research Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, Sana'a University. The GDM group consisted of women with a history of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including spontaneous abortion and/or stillbirth. The FVL (G1691A) mutation was detected by real-time PCR using genomic DNA extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes (white blood cells). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 22.
RESULTS: Allelic frequencies for FVL were 0.93 (G) and 0.07 (A) in the GDM group, compared to 0.98 (G) and 0.02 (A) in controls. The FVL mutation was more common among women with GDM and recurrent pregnancy loss. Clinical findings in the GDM group showed significantly higher PT, APTT, fasting blood glucose, blood pressure, HbA1c, and lipid profile values than healthy controls. Differences in FVL mutation incidence and clinical measures between the GDM and control groups were statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Our study found a higher prevalence of the Factor V Leiden (FVL) mutation among Yemeni women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and a history of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) than among healthy pregnant controls. The observed association suggests that the FVL mutation may contribute to the clinical profile of this group. However, further large-scale prospective studies with appropriate comparison groups are needed to validate these findings and to clarify whether FVL screening could have a meaningful role in the clinical management of pregnancies.

articles.title: Effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices and oxidative-stress biomarkers in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and dose-response analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Yang XY, Xu P, Tan X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes and metabolic syndrome are major public health challenges closely linked to oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired insulin signaling. Selenium, an essential trace element with antioxidant and immunomodulatory roles, has been proposed as an adjunctive strategy for metabolic regulation; however, evidence from randomized trials remains inconsistent. We evaluated the effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices, oxidative-stress-related biomarkers, lipid metabolism, and related metabolic indicators in adults, and explored potential effect modifiers.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CINAHL, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed through 12 August 2025 for randomized controlled trials of oral selenium supplementation in adults, including pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Outcomes included fasting plasma glucose, glycated hemoglobin, fasting insulin, indices of insulin resistance and β-cell function, oxidative-stress-related and inflammatory biomarkers, lipid parameters, and anthropometric and hemodynamic indicators. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated weighted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Subgroup, dose-response, and sensitivity analyses were performed, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Fifty-two treatment arms involving 10,916 participants were included. Selenium supplementation reduced fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and HOMA-β values and increased QUICKI, but showed no clear overall effect on fasting plasma glucose or glycated hemoglobin. Favorable changes were observed in selected antioxidant and inflammatory biomarkers, including increases in glutathione, total antioxidant capacity, superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, and serum selenium, and reductions in malondialdehyde and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, with no clear effect on nitric oxide. Modest changes in lipid parameters were also observed, including higher high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. Among anthropometric and hemodynamic outcomes, only diastolic blood pressure was reduced. Effects varied by dose, duration, participant characteristics, and geographical selenium exposure context.
CONCLUSIONS: Selenium supplementation was associated with modest improvements in insulin-sensitivity markers, selected antioxidantand inflammatory biomarkers, and lipid parameters,…

articles.title: Placental malaria and preeclampsia: shared pathways and translational perspectives in endemic regions.
articles.authors: Quaye D, Konadu EA, Letsa TE et al.
articles.abstract: Placental malaria (PM), driven by sequestration of Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes within the placental intervillous space, remains a major contributor to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes in endemic regions. Increasing evidence suggests that PM may also contribute to the development of preeclampsia (PE), a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide. Although PM and PE arise from distinct initiating events, Plasmodium falciparum sequestration in PM and defective spiral artery remodeling in PE, both conditions converge on shared placental and systemic biological pathways. In PM, P. falciparum-infected red blood cells (iRBCs) sequester within the placental intervillous space through binding of parasite-expressed variant surface antigen 2-chondroitin sulfate A (VAR2CSA) adhesion to chondroitin sulfate A (CSA) on the syncytiotrophoblast. This sequestration, together with the accumulation of parasite derived products such as hemozoin, promotes local inflammation, syncytiotrophoblast stress, and disruption of placental vascular homeostasis. In PE, placental hypoperfusion and ischemia-reperfusion injury induce oxidative stress and abnormal trophoblast turnover. Despite these different origins, both conditions produce some overlapping patterns of placental injury including angiogenic dysregulation, characterized by elevated anti-angiogenic factors and reduced pro-angiogenic mediators. This convergence is further marked by activation of inflammatory signalling through NF-κB and inflammasome pathways, oxidative injury, complement activation, and systemic endothelial dysfunction. This review synthesizes current evidence on the shared biological pathways linking PM and PE and explores how malaria-induced placental injury may increase susceptibility to PE. We also examine the implications of overlapping biomarker signatures for diagnosis and risk stratification in malaria-endemic settings. Key knowledge gaps are highlighted, and priorities for future research are proposed to inform integrated strategies for malaria control and improved clinical management of PE in malaria-endemic settings.

articles.title: Microbial cell-free DNA sequencing for diagnosing lung infections in immunocompromised patients.
articles.authors: Brick K, Jarman KH, Nolte F et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Rapid and comprehensive detection of respiratory pathogens is essential for immunocompromised patients with suspected pneumonia. Conventional diagnostic methods are limited in scope, often slow, and lack sensitivity, leading to reduced diagnostic yield.
OBJECTIVES: To analytically and clinically validate a microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing assay for bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) that enables broad and sensitive detection of pathogens causing pneumonia in immunocompromised patients.
METHODS: The BALF-mcfDNA assay detects more than 500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites. Analytical validation used 324 contrived samples containing DNA from 11 representative organisms and 1,294 in-silico samples. Clinical validation compared BALF-mcfDNA sequencing with usual care (UC) testing in 118 immunocompromised adults with suspected pneumonia. An independent expert panel adjudicated the etiologic diagnoses.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: BALF-mcfDNA testing demonstrated high inclusivity (97%), exclusivity (96%), and precision (coefficient of variation < 15%), with linear quantification across four orders of magnitude. Limits of detection were consistent across taxa, GC content, and genome size. In clinical evaluation, BALF-mcfDNA sequencing identified probable pneumonia pathogens in 34% of participants versus 24% for UC testing, increasing diagnostic yield by 43% (57% when combined with UC). In 24% of concordant cases, mcfDNA sequencing provided additional clinically relevant information by identifying new or species-level pathogens.
CONCLUSIONS: BALF-mcfDNA sequencing enables sensitive, comprehensive, and rapid pathogen detection from BALF specimens, outperforming conventional methods and improving etiologic diagnosis of pneumonia in immunocompromised hosts.

articles.title: Physical activity and health-related quality of life in women with polycystic ovary syndrome attending fertility clinics in Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Lakshan GAR, Rishard M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent endocrine disorder that substantially impairs health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Regular physical activity is a recommended first-line intervention, but the relationship between activity and HRQoL is understudied in South Asian women, particularly in those attending fertility clinics who carry the additional psychological burden of infertility. This study aimed to examine the association between physical activity levels and PCOS-specific HRQoL in women with PCOS attending fertility clinics in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted at the fertility clinics of two tertiary care hospitals in Colombo, Sri Lanka: De Soysa Hospital for Women and Children and Castle Street Hospital for Women between 13 October and 7 November 2025. Eighty-five women aged 18-45 years with a clinician-confirmed diagnosis of PCOS were recruited by convenience sampling. Physical activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire - Short Form (IPAQ-SF), validated to the Sri Lankan setting, and expressed as MET-minutes per week. HRQoL was measured using the Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Questionnaire (PCOSQ), validated in the Sri Lankan setting, which yields a total score and five domain scores (emotions, body hair, weight, infertility, menstrual problems) on a 1-7 scale, with higher scores indicating better HRQoL. PCOS phenotype was classified according to the Rotterdam criteria. Continuous variables were summarized using medians and interquartile ranges, and Spearman's rank correlation (rs) was used to examine the association between physical activity and HRQoL.
RESULTS: The mean (SD) age was 28.0 (4.9) years, and the median (IQR) age was 28 (24-30) years; the median body mass index was 30.2 (28.0-32.4) kg/m². The majority of participants (60.0%, n = 51) were classified as having low physical activity, with a median total activity score of 1017.0 (569.5-2459.3) MET-minutes/week. The median overall PCOSQ score was 3.07 (2.37-3.64), indicating moderate HRQoL impairment; the lowest-scoring domain was body hair and appearance (median 2.20), and the highest was infertility-related worries (median 3.50). Physical activity showed a statistically significant moderate positive correlation with overall HRQoL (rs = 0.465, p < 0.001). Domain-specific analyses revealed significant moderate positive correlations with emotional well-being (rs = 0.493, p < 0.001), weight…

articles.title: The impact of menstruation-related symptoms on women's quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden: a structured narrative review.
articles.authors: Enomoto Y, Wada-Hiraike O, Nariai M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menstruation-related disorders, including dysmenorrhoea, premenstrual syndrome (PMS)/ premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), and heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB)/ abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), are common among women of reproductive age and associated with impairments in quality of life (QOL), mental health, and daily functioning. Increasing evidence indicates that these conditions adversely affect academic and work productivity, with presenteeism constituting a major component of the economic burden. However, the existing evidence remains fragmented.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review supported by a targeted literature search of PubMed and Scopus. Studies published in English between January 2014 and December 2025 were considered if they included female individuals aged 14-59 years and examined menstruation-related symptoms in relation to QOL, work productivity, academic or occupational functioning, or economic outcomes. Because of heterogeneity in study designs, populations, and outcome measures, findings were synthesised thematically rather than quantitatively pooled.
RESULTS: A total of 86 studies were used to inform the thematic synthesis. Across conditions, menstruation-related disorders were consistently associated with reduced health-related QOL, psychological distress, and impaired academic and occupational functioning. Productivity loss was observed across disorders and predominantly driven by presenteeism rather than by absenteeism. Dysmenorrhoea and PMS/PMDD were associated with both absenteeism and presenteeism, whereas HMB/AUB was strongly associated with work impairment, which is frequently mediated by anaemia-related symptoms. Psychological distress, including anxiety, depressive symptoms, emotional dysregulation, and sleep disturbance, has emerged as a key contributor to QOL impairment across age groups and regions. Lifestyle factors appeared to modify symptom severity and functional impact. Although treatment and medical consultations often improved symptoms, productivity gains were inconsistent.
CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the multidimensional burden of menstruation-related disorders extending from physical symptoms to mental health and functional outcomes. The predominance of presenteeism suggested that conventional metrics based on absenteeism underestimate the true societal impact. The observed gap between symptom improvement and functional recovery underscored the need for…

articles.title: Hysteroscopic vs. laparoscopic management of cesarian scar defect: a meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Aldiab R, Alswian M, Halawani A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of cesarian scar defects (CSD) is increasing worldwide mainly due to the increasing rates of cesarian deliveries (CD). While hysteroscopic (H) and laparoscopic (L) are both popular approaches in the management of CSD, the superiority of one over the other remains debated. Therefore, this meta-analysis will compare H and L approaches for CSD treatment.
METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane, and Google Scholar were queried through May 2026. Inclusion criteria consisted of studies comparing the outcomes of CSD management between H and L approaches. Extracted data included adverse events (overall complications, chronic pelvic pain, abnormal bleeding, dyspareunia, dysmenorrhea), CSD parameters (change in isthmocele depth, change in residual myometrial thickness (RMT)), surgical parameters (operative time, estimated blood loss (EBL), length of stay (LOS), and cost), and pregnancy outcomes among patients desiring pregnancy (subsequent pregnancies, abortions, premature deliveries, and term deliveries).
RESULTS: Ten studies met the inclusion criteria including 798 patients, with 361 being in the H group and 437 in the L group. Patients in the H group had a lower rate of overall complications (Odds-Ratio = 0.24, p = 0.02), shorter operative time (Mean difference= -55.94 min, p<0.001), less EBL (Mean difference= -37.73 ml; p<0.001), shorter LOS (Mean difference= -2.84 days; p<0.001), and less costs (Mean difference= $-1310; p<0.001). However, the H group also had less change in RMT compared to the L group (Mean difference= -2.60 mm; p = 0.0007). There were no differences in the remaining outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Patients undergoing hysteroscopic management of CSD had shorter operative time, shorter length of stay, less blood loss, less costs, and less complications. However, they also had less improvement in RMT. Nevertheless, both techniques did not differ in post-operative symptoms, adverse events, or pregnancy-related outcomes, making them both a viable option for the management of CSD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Algorithm for classifying the underlying pathologies in postpartum hemorrhage using bleeding rate, fibrinogen, and fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products: a case series study.
articles.authors: Tada K, Miyagi Y, Yasuhi I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding patients' underlying pathologies is essential for appropriate treatment during postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) management. The objective of this study is to develop an algorithm that quantitatively classifies the underlying pathologies in PPH using clinical parameters.
METHODS: A multicenter case series study involving nine perinatal centers in Japan was conducted on patients with severe PPH (blood loss > 2000 mL) excluding placental abruption, and placental abruption irrespective of blood loss spanning August 2020 to June 2024. The primary outcome was the development of an algorithm for classifying the underlying pathologies in PPH, based on bleeding rate, fibrinogen, and fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products (FDP). We used collected data to develop an algorithm by which cases with abnormally high bleeding rate (≥ 61 mL/min) were classified as whole blood loss with high bleeding rate (WBLH). Of cases with bleeding rate < 61 mL/min, those with fibrinogen ≥ 237 mg/dL were classified as non-coagulopathy (NCP). Of cases with fibrinogen < 237 mg/dL, those with FDP < 2 mg/dL and FDP ≥ 2 mg/dL were classified as whole blood loss with low bleeding rate (WBLL) and coagulation factor consumption (CFC), respectively. In CFC cases, a predictive formula distinguished between disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) from locally initiated and progressive consumptive coagulopathy for hemostasis (LIPC). We used the Mann-Whitney test and Fisher's exact test for the statistical analysis.
RESULTS: Among 171 participants, comprising 131 severe PPH cases and 40 placental abruption cases, the algorithm classified cases into WBLH (n = 9), NCP (n = 88), WBLL (n = 12), and CFC (n = 62). Of the CFC cases, 3 had DIC and 59 had LIPC. FDP levels did not differ between WBLH (median, 1.19 mg/dL) and WBLL (median, 0.91 mg/dL). Hemoglobin (median, 6.3 g/dL) in WBLL and fibrinogen (median, 168.5 mg/dL) in CFC were significantly lower than for the other three categories (P < 0.05). Coagulation-fibrinolytic activation in DIC was significantly increased compared with LIPC cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Our algorithm, using bleeding rate, fibrinogen, and FDP as clinical parameters, classified PPH cases into four underlying pathologies. This pilot study provides a foundation for pathophysiology-based clinical management of PPH.

articles.title: Cerebral venous thrombosis during pregnancy and the puerperium in the setting of hyperhomocysteinemia and methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase c.677 C > T polymorphism.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Fang K, Zhou C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is an uncommon but serious complication of pregnancy and the puerperium that arises in a physiologically hypercoagulable milieu. Hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) is a recognized metabolic risk factor for venous thrombosis, and common variants in the methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) gene may influence homocysteine metabolism. However, the specific interplay between MTHFR variation, HHcy, and pregnancy-associated CVT remains insufficiently defined. This case series explored the clinical relevance of HHcy in obstetric CVT in the presence of the common MTHFR c.677 C > T polymorphism.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center case series of four pregnant or postpartum patients with imaging-confirmed CVT, elevated plasma homocysteine, and documented MTHFR c.677 C > T genotypes. Clinical, radiological, laboratory, treatment, and short-term follow-up data were reviewed.
RESULTS: Two patients were homozygous (TT) and two heterozygous (CT) for MTHFR c.677 C > T. All four patients had dural venous sinus thrombosis and elevated homocysteine at presentation. TT carriers showed higher homocysteine levels and appeared to have more severe neurological manifestations, including hemorrhagic venous infarction and generalized tonic-clonic seizures. CT carriers also had substantial thrombotic burden but showed comparatively less severe neurological involvement overall, although one experienced a prolonged seizure. All patients received therapeutic anticoagulation, with endovascular intervention in selected severe cases, together with folate, vitamin B₆ and B₁₂ supplementation. Homocysteine normalized in all patients by one month, accompanied by early clinical improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, HHcy was observed in all four patients with pregnancy- or puerperium-associated CVT and the MTHFR c.677 C > T polymorphism, while higher homocysteine levels and more severe neurological manifestations were observed in the two TT carriers. These observations are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and do not support changes in routine homocysteine screening, MTHFR genotyping, or standard CVT management. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required to clarify the relationships among genotype, metabolic phenotype, and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Expanded Carrier Screening in gamete donation identifies clinically relevant donor-recipient genetic incompatibilities.
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Fucci R, Iserani A, Oliva I et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Most individuals carry pathogenic variants associated with autosomal recessive disorders. In donor-assisted Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART), broader carrier screening may identify additional donor-recipient genetic risks beyond standard donor screening. This study evaluated the frequency of donor-recipient shared carrier findings identified through Expanded Carrier Screening (ECS) and explored their potential clinical relevance.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 250 couples undergoing donor-assisted ART between January 2022 and September 2025 were analyzed. The cohort included 220 oocyte donation cycles (88%), 20 sperm donation cycles (8%), and 10 double-donation cycles (4%). 1 ECS was used to assess carrier status and donor-recipient genetic compatibility according to the study's recorded matching criteria. All participants received pre-test genetic counseling.
RESULTS: The use of ECS increased markedly over the study period. A donor-recipient shared carrier status was identified in 26-44% of couples undergoing ECS-based donor-recipient matching. Shared carrier status was observed in 35% of sperm-donation, 24% of oocyte donation, and 20% of double-donation cycles (p > 0.05). The probability of incompatibility increased with increasing individual pathogenic variant burden (p < 0.05), reaching 40-50% in individuals carrying two to four pathogenic variants before ECS-based donor matching.
CONCLUSION: ECS identified a substantial proportion of donor-recipient shared carrier findings. However, the clinical relevance and incremental contribution of ECS beyond standard donor screening depend on the specific condition and the genes and variants already assessed in the donor. These findings support the use of ECS as a broader approach to reproductive risk assessment, while highlighting the need for gene-level matching data to quantify its incremental clinical utility.

articles.title: Evaluation of Umbilical Cord Blood Culture for Detection of Early Onset Sepsis in Neonates with Spontaneous Preterm Birth: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Kapoor A, Kainth D, Prakash S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) is associated with early-onset sepsis (EOS) in neonates. The authors aimed to compare the umbilical cord blood culture (UCBC) positivity (as a marker of intra-amniotic infection) in neonates with sPTB to those born at term, and evaluate its ability to detect EOS.
METHODS: In a prospective cohort study design, the authors included neonates (<35 wk) born via sPTB and term neonates (37-41 wk) born between June 2021 to May 2022 at a level III neonatal intensive care unit in north India. The primary outcome was to evaluate the proportion of neonates with positive UCBC in preterm and term groups. The authors also evaluated the role of UCBC positivity in those neonates who developed EOS.
RESULTS: The authors enrolled 47 neonates born via sPTB and 40 term neonates. In the preterm group, 10 neonates (21%) developed EOS (two culture-positive and eight culture-negative). UCBC positivity was 19% (9/47) in preterm vs. 2% (1/40) in the term group (RR 7.6; 95% CI 1.0%, 57.9%; p = 0.015). Escherichia coli was the predominant organism (n = 4). Of nine UCBC positive cases in the preterm group, six developed EOS (2 culture-positive and 4 culture-negative). Both the preterm neonates with culture-proven sepsis had concordant growth of the same organism in umbilical and peripheral blood culture. UCBC demonstrated a sensitivity of 100% (95% CI 15.8%-100%) and specificity of 94.8% (95% CI 87.2%-98.6%) to detect culture-proven sepsis.
CONCLUSIONS: Preterm neonates with sPTB exhibit a higher rate of UCBC positivity, compared to term neonates with low risk of EOS. Preliminary findings suggest the potential utility of UCBC to detect EOS. However, further research is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Surgical quality and long-term outcomes in advanced ovarian cancer: a population based registry study from Hamburg, Germany 2014-2024.
articles.authors: Annemarie S, Frederik P, Anna J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association of surgical quality and survival in patients with advanced ovarian cancer in a real-world setting.
METHODS: This population-based registry study analysed FIGO stage III/IV ovarian cancer patients in Hamburg, Germany (2014-2024). Patients were categorized by surgical outcome (no macroscopic residuals vs. macroscopic residuals). Kaplan-Meier functions and Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations with survival outcomes.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 576 patients (median age 65 years, median follow-up 57 months). No macroscopic residuals were achieved in 370 patients (64.2%). In multivariable analysis, no macroscopic residuals were associated with reduced mortality risk (HR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.42-0.90) and reduced progression risk (HR 0.68, 95% CI: 0.49-0.94). Advanced FIGO stage, poor performance status, and increasing age were independent predictors of worse outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Achieving no macroscopic residuals remains a critical prognostic factor in advanced ovarian cancer. The rate of 64.2% demonstrates that optimal surgical outcomes are achievable in routine practice, though opportunities for improvement remain compared to specialized centres.

articles.title: Towards a sequential microbiome therapy for HPV-associated cervicovaginal dysbiosis.
articles.authors: Molina MA, Zhang Y, Steenbergen RDM et al.
articles.abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are the principal cause of cervical cancer, and are increasingly associated with ecological instability of the cervicovaginal microbiome. Multiomics studies indicate that hrHPV persistence is linked to reduced Lactobacillus dominance, increased anaerobic taxa, and metabolic alterations that may compromise epithelial integrity and antiviral immunity. In this Perspective article, we introduce a sequential microbiome therapy (SMT) framework designed to restore cervicovaginal ecological balance and support viral clearance. SMT is a two-phase, strain-resolved strategy. The first phase targets dysbiotic communities using antimicrobials, biofilm-disrupting or microbiota-modulating approaches to create a window for ecological reset. The second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species selected for their acidification capacity, competitive fitness, and ability to stabilize the mucosal environment. We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

articles.title: Persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction among infants with Fetal growth restriction at one year of age.
articles.authors: Nayak V, Samanth J, Nayak K et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with altered cardiac development and subclinical myocardial dysfunction; however, longitudinal data during infancy are limited. This study evaluated serial changes in cardiac structure and function in infants with FGR during the first year of life.
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included 128 FGR neonates and 64 appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) neonates, of whom 39 early-onset FGR (EOFGR), 47 late-onset FGR (LOFGR), and 64 AGA neonates completed the 1-year follow-up. FGR was diagnosed antenatally using estimated fetal weight <10th percentile with abnormal Doppler findings and confirmed postnatally using Intergrowth-21 standards. Cardiac evaluation included conventional echocardiography, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography.
RESULTS: At birth, FGR infants showed significantly lower anthropometric parameters and smaller cardiac dimensions compared with AGA controls. By 12 months, both FGR groups demonstrated catch-up growth with normalization of left ventricular dimensions and wall thickness. However, speckle-tracking analysis revealed persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Global longitudinal strain and strain rate indices remained significantly impaired across follow-up. Right ventricular dysfunction was evident at 12 months, particularly in the EOFGR group.
CONCLUSION: Despite structural normalization and catch-up growth, infants with FGR exhibit persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction during the first year of life.
IMPACT: Infants with fetal growth restriction exhibit reduced cardiac size and altered myocardial function at birth compared to AGA neonates. Both early- and late-onset FGR infants demonstrate significant catch-up growth and cardiac structural normalization by 12 months. Despite normalization of cardiac dimensions, speckle-tracking parameters (GLS and strain rates) remain impaired throughout infancy. Right ventricular dysfunction becomes evident by 12 months, particularly in early-onset FGR infants. Early myocardial impairment in FGR infants may represent a precursor to future cardiovascular risk, highlighting the need for longitudinal cardiac surveillance.

articles.title: Oocyte-specific OMC1 is required for maintaining chromosome cohesion through reproductive life.
articles.authors: Iisaka S, Yoshida S, Shimada R et al.
articles.abstract: In mammals, oocytes initiate meiosis during fetal development and then enter a prolonged meiotic arrest. During this female-specific long-term arrest, chromosome cohesion mediated by nonrenewable REC8 cohesin gradually deteriorates, predisposing oocytes to age-associated chromosome segregation errors when meiosis resumes for maturation in adulthood. Female-specific factors that counteract this deterioration remain unknown. Here we identify OMC1 as an oocyte-specific chromosomal protein required for the maintenance of chromosome cohesion through reproductive life. OMC1 associates with REC8-cohesin-containing chromosome axes from fetal stages through adult meiotic maturation. Using Omc1 knockout mice, we show that OMC1 is required for cohesin maintenance until completion of meiotic maturation, thereby suppressing age-associated chromosome segregation errors. These findings provide insight into the female germ-cell-intrinsic molecular basis that supports reproductive longevity by suppressing age-associated chromosome cohesion loss, which leads to egg aneuploidy, a major cause of infertility and congenital disorders.

articles.title: Enhanced cfDNA methylation profiling by detection and correction of jagged ends.
articles.authors: Wang R, Hamilton EG, Almanza D et al.
articles.abstract: Analysis of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation can enable noninvasive disease detection by leveraging tissue-specific epigenetic differences between malignant and nonmalignant cells. However, such analyses can be confounded by the repair of jagged DNA fragment ends during double-stranded sequencing library preparation, which introduces spurious methylation signals into cfDNA molecules. Here we present JEEPERS, a framework to detect and correct jagged-end-induced methylation errors while preserving duplex integrity and native methylation patterns. We showed high fidelity for measuring tumor burden and demonstrated allele-specific methylation differences at recurrent somatic mutations, revealing a link between adjacent CpG methylation and EGFR/TP53 driver and resistance mutations. We further demonstrated enhanced diagnostic performance across liquid biopsy applications, including tumor-type-specific methylation profiles, hemimethylation profiling, epigenetic-clock-based age estimation and cell type deconvolution. By faithfully correcting end-repair errors, JEEPERS provides a versatile framework for integrating mutations and methylation features in cfDNA at high resolution, enabling more precise molecular profiling and disease monitoring.

articles.title: Ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors are part of the BAP1-tumor predisposition syndrome: evidence from human carriers and mouse models.
articles.authors: Elsayed AM, Kadariya Y, Byrne L et al.
articles.abstract: Germline heterozygous BAP1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants are associated with the BAP1-tumor predisposition syndrome (BAP1-TPDS). This study evaluated evidence for an association between ovarian cancers and BAP1-TPDS. We evaluated ovarian cancer incidence in two independent cohorts of female subjects with germline BAP1 P/LP variants. Additionally, we investigated whether the high incidence of spontaneous ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors (OSCSTs) in heterozygous Bap1-mutant FVB/N mice was strain-specific by examining their occurrence in several other Bap1-mutant mouse models with different genetic backgrounds. In the combined human cohort of 176 females with BAP1 P/LP variants, 7 (4%) had ovarian cancer, including 3 with OSCST. Another OSCST occurred in a patient with a germline BAP1 variant with conflicting pathogenesis, for which functional studies supported pathogenicity. OSCSTs were observed in all mouse strains with germline heterozygous Bap1 mutations (incidence: 32%-73%). Biallelic inactivation of BAP1 was observed in 3/3 human and 10/10 murine OSCSTs. OSCSTs from Bap1-mutant mice showed marked decreases in Bmpr1b, Erb, and Foxl2 expression, suggesting disruption of pathways involved in ovarian differentiation and homeostasis. In conclusion, ovarian cancers, particularly OSCSTs, represent a rarer phenotype of the BAP1-TPDS. Downregulation of Bmpr1b, Erb, and Foxl2 may reflect alterations in pathways amenable to therapeutic targeting in OSCSTs.

articles.title: Twin pregnancy.
articles.authors: Khalil A, Craig JM, Ernst S et al.
articles.abstract: Twin pregnancies occur in ~12 per 1,000 pregnancies worldwide and are associated with substantially increased maternal, fetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality compared with singleton pregnancies. Although zygosity describes whether twins arise from one fertilized egg (monozygotic) or two fertilized ova (dizygotic), clinical risk is primarily determined by chorionicity (whether twins share a placenta) and amnionicity (whether twins share an amniotic sac). Accurate early determination of chorionicity and amnionicity is therefore fundamental to counselling, risk stratification, surveillance and management, and should be established and documented consistently throughout pregnancy. Monochorionic twins are uniquely susceptible to complications arising from shared placental vascular anastomoses, including twin-twin transfusion syndrome and twin anaemia-polycythaemia sequence or unequal placental sharing in the form of selective fetal growth restriction. Preterm birth remains the leading cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality in twin pregnancies, with the risk of extreme preterm birth markedly higher than in singleton gestations. Contemporary surveillance strategies aim to identify evolving complications sufficiently early to enable timely intervention and optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Strategies and tools for enhancing early detection of pancreatic cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.authors: Liao WC
articles.abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAC) remains the most lethal malignancies, with a 5-year survival rate of only around 12%. The dismal prognosis is largely attributable to late diagnosis, as early PAC is frequently asymptomatic and radiologically inconspicuous. Contemporary international guidelines recommend surveillance for well-defined high-risk groups, particularly carriers of pathogenic germline mutations such as BRCA2, STK11, and CDKN2A, as well as familial pancreatic cancer kindreds. In these settings, endoscopic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging are the recommended surveillance modalities. Recent advances in biomarker discovery, including circulating tumor DNA, methylation signatures of cell-free DNA, and extracellular vesicles, have demonstrated encouraging results, particularly when combined with CA19-9. Paraneoplastic phenomena such as pancreatic cancer-associated diabetes and cancer-induced cachexia provide additional opportunities for earlier clinical recognition. Parallel progress has been achieved in artificial intelligence-driven radiomics analysis and deep learning algorithms, which can increase the sensitivity of cross-sectional imaging for small or otherwise occult lesions. The integration of clinical risk stratification, molecular biomarkers, and AI-enhanced imaging represents a promising framework to shift diagnosis toward surgically resectable stages. This review synthesizes the current evidence, highlights recent advances, and discusses practical considerations for physicians to facilitate earlier detection of PAC.

articles.title: Securing Maternal Identity: Halachic Concerns in the Age of Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy.
articles.authors: Loike JD, Flaum RT, Kadish A
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT) encompasses assisted reproductive technologies designed to prevent the transmission of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations by combining the DNA in the nucleus (nuclear genome) of the intending parents with another woman's enucleated egg that provides healthy donor-derived mtDNA. The use of advanced genomic engineering in MRT raises distinct ethical and halachic considerations regarding the ontological status of embryos containing genetic material from more than two individuals. This paper advances an original theoretical protocol, termed biparental mitochondrial replacement therapy (Bi-MRT), that mitigates the central halachic concerns associated with multi-parent embryos. In this protocol, future advances in stem cell technology could be employed to generate an enucleated gamete-like cell containing healthy mitochondria from the husband. The meiotic spindle-chromosome complex from the wife's oocyte could then be transplanted into this reconstituted gamete, which could be subsequently fertilized with the husband's sperm for IVF. If technically feasible and developmentally competent, the resulting embryo could potentially be transferred to the wife for gestation. By combining the wife's nuclear genetic contribution, gestation, and parturition with the husband's paternal DNA, this framework isolates the third-party mitochondrial contribution as a non-maternal factor, thereby reinforcing the wife's singular claim to halachic maternity. Biparental MRT therefore represents a theoretical framework that could potentially reduce some halachic concerns associated with conventional MRT, but substantial scientific and safety barriers remain before any clinical application could be contemplated.

articles.title: Six Decades of Pelvic Exenterative Surgery for Gynaecological Malignancies: A Meta-analysis of Indications and Surgical Outcomes in 13,434 Cases Across 29 Countries.
articles.authors: Sideris M, Caricato C, Dibden A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Robust international data on pelvic exenteration (PE) are limited. This study aimed to summarise indications, intent, surgical outcomes, morbidity, and mortality of PE for gynaecological malignancies.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed was searched from inception to November 2024 (PROSPERO CRD42024615187) following PRISMA guidelines. Data on histology, demographics, body mass index, PE type and intent, prior radiotherapy, resection margins, operative time, hospital stay, and Clavien-Dindo (CD) morbidity/mortality were extracted. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). Exploratory subgroup analyses compared pre- versus post-2005 studies and regions. Study quality was assessed using MINORS.
RESULTS: We included 132 studies comprising 13,434 women. Pooled proportions of anterior, posterior, and total PE were 33%, 19%, and 49%, respectively. Indications were cervical (61%), uterine (13%), vulval (13%), and vaginal/other malignancies (17%). PE was performed for recurrent disease in 68%, and negative margins were achieved in 76%. Pooled CD grade I-IV complication rates were 21%, 38%, 28%, and 10%, respectively; 30-day mortality was 5%. From pre- to post-2005 studies, cervical indications declined from 76.1% to 61.0% (p=0.008), uterine indications increased from 3.0% to 12.4% (p<0.001), and mortality decreased from 8.1% to 3.7% (p<0.001). Mortality was 4.5% in Europe, 5.9% in the US, and 11.4% in Latin America (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: PE carries substantial morbidity, while perioperative mortality was approximately 5% overall and 3.7% in post-2005 studies. Given substantial heterogeneity, pooled estimates should be interpreted as broad descriptive summaries rather than universal benchmarks.

articles.title: Incidence of Nausea and Vomiting in Patients With Cervical Cancer Undergoing Chemoradiotherapy With Steroid-Sparing.
articles.authors: Matsumoto T, Yoshida K, Nakai M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Although dexamethasone (DEX) is essential for preventing chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for cervical cancer, prolonged administration carries risks of adverse events. Therefore, we evaluated the effect of a shortened DEX duration (steroid-sparing therapy) on the total control (TC) of nausea and vomiting in patients with cervical cancer undergoing CCRT comprising cisplatin 40 mg/m2 to avoid the risk of adverse effects associated with DEX administration.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study included 579 patients with cervical cancer who underwent CCRT between January 2016 and March 2024. Patients were classified into the steroid- sparing (DEX day 1; N=80) and non-steroid-sparing (DEX days 1-3; N=499) groups. TC was defined as the absence of vomiting and nausea without rescue medication during the entire CCRT period. A multivariate logistic regression analysis was used for between-group comparisons to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: The baseline rate of olanzapine use was significantly higher in the steroid-sparing group [28.8% vs. 10.6% (non-steroid-sparing group); p<0.001]. TC rates during the entire CCRT period were 30.0% and 36.5% in the steroid and non-steroid-sparing groups, respectively. No statistically significant difference in the overall TC period [odds ratio (OR)=0.826; 95% confidence interval (CI)=0.480-1.420; p=0.490] was observed. Furthermore, propensity score matching analysis adjusted for olanzapine use, radiation dose, and other covariates confirmed these findings (OR=0.736; 95% CI=0.370-1.460; p=0.381). However, the TC rate during the delayed phase in the non-steroid-sparing group (71.7%) was higher than that in the steroid-sparing group (60.0%), indicating an increased risk of treatment failure (OR=0.591; p=0.035). This difference was not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (significance threshold: p<0.0125). Furthermore, propensity score-matched univariate analysis confirmed no significant difference in the delayed phase between the two groups (p=0.243).
CONCLUSION: Steroid-sparing therapy did not compromise TC rates, suggesting that it may be a clinically acceptable option for patients undergoing CCRT. However, individualized risk assessment and appropriate antiemetic use remain essential.

articles.title: Differential Modulation of Galectin-3 by Tamoxifen and Progesterone Receptor Modulators: An In Vitro and In Silico Study.
articles.authors: Kontogeorgi A, Boutas I, Agrogiannis G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Tamoxifen remains one of the most widely used endocrine treatments for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer. However, its partial estrogen-agonist activity in the endometrium is associated with endometrial proliferation, hyperplasia, polyps, and, rarely, carcinoma. Antiprogestins and selective progesterone receptor modulators, including mifepristone and ulipristal acetate, have been proposed as alternative or adjunctive endocrine strategies, but their effects on endometrial molecular remodeling remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigates whether Galectin-3, a multifunctional lectin that is involved in epithelial integrity, angiogenesis, receptor signaling, and tumor-associated remodeling, could serve as a candidate marker of the endometrial epithelial response to endocrine modulation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ishikawa endometrial adenocarcinoma cells were exposed to different concentrations of tamoxifen, mifepristone, and ulipristal acetate. Galectin-3 protein expression was evaluated using Western blot analysis, and densitometric measurements were normalized to β-actin. Complementary STRING and STITCH bioinformatics analyses were performed to examine the molecular interactions linking Galectin-3 with steroid receptor and growth-factor-associated signaling pathways.
RESULTS: Tamoxifen produced a biphasic response, characterized by modest induction of Galectin-3 expression at low concentration and marked suppression at intermediate and high concentrations. Mifepristone preserved Galectin-3 expression at low and intermediate concentrations but reduced its expression at the highest concentration. Ulipristal acetate increased Galectin-3 expression at low-to-intermediate concentrations, followed by a return toward baseline at high concentration. STRING and STITCH analyses indicated that Galectin-3 is indirectly linked to steroid receptor signaling through growth-factor-associated pathways, particularly EGFR/ERBB- and VEGF-related networks.
CONCLUSION: Galectin-3 expression differs according to the type and concentration of endocrine modulator used, suggesting that it may reflect distinct endometrial epithelial responses to hormonal treatment. Galectin-3 therefore warrants further investigation as a potential biomarker for assessing endometrial safety during endocrine therapy.

articles.title: Histopathological and Clinical Perspectives on Prognostic Markers in Endometrial Cancer.
articles.journal: International journal of gynecological pathology : official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Pathologists
articles.authors: Aslan F, Kurtuluş G, Açıkalın D et al.
articles.abstract: The microcystic, elongated, and fragmented (MELF) invasion pattern, tumor budding (TB), and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) may have prognostic value in endometrial carcinoma; however, their relationships are not fully defined. This retrospective study included 216 endometrioid endometrial carcinomas. MELF pattern, TB (BD1-3), and TIL levels were evaluated on hematoxylin-eosin sections. Clinicopathologic variables and immunohistochemical markers (HER2, p53, mismatch repair proteins) were analyzed statistically, including survival analysis.MELF pattern of invasion (present in 32.4%) was significantly associated with larger tumor size, low-to-intermediate grade, deep myometrial invasion, lymphovascular invasion (LVI), and nodal metastasis; on multivariate analysis, it remained independently associated with LVI (odds ratio=38.15) and nodal metastasis (odds ratio=12.82). TB was significantly associated with high-grade, deep invasion, cervical involvement, advanced FIGO stage, and mortality after Bonferroni correction; associations with tumor size, LVI, and nodal metastasis were significant only at the conventional threshold and considered trends. TB did not retain independent prognostic significance in the Cox regression model. TIL showed no significant association with any parameter, survival, or the other 2 patterns. MELF pattern of invasion is a clinically important marker independently associated with LVI and nodal metastasis. Notably, MELF was more common in low-to-intermediate grade tumors, suggesting that it may identify aggressive invasive behavior in tumors otherwise considered lower risk by grade alone. TB reflects aggressive tumor behavior without independent survival significance. TIL had limited prognostic value by routine assessment. Combined evaluation of MELF and TB may improve risk stratification in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, particularly where molecular profiling is unavailable.

articles.title: Hormone hesitancy: Young adults' experiences with long-acting reversible contraceptives.
articles.authors: Zia Y, Wong I, Hecht H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate young adults' values and preferences regarding hormones throughout their decision-making process in using long-acting reversible contraception (LARC).
STUDY DESIGN: From January to June 2025, we conducted 40 semi-structured in-depth interviews with young adults currently or previously using hormonal or non-hormonal LARC. The interview topics included decisions and experiences starting, using, and discontinuing their LARC method. We utilized both deductive and inductive coding and conducted thematic analysis around hormonal hesitancy and how it impacts LARC use.
RESULTS: Most participants expressed hesitancy around hormones in contraception. Their apprehension centered on four main themes. Participants expressed how contraception can be a divergence from "natural" lifestyles and noted anti-hormonal social media messaging they had encountered. They attributed undesired changes in their menstruation or libido to hormones. Lastly, participants described how non-hormonal methods (including copper IUD, fertility awareness methods, and condoms) were better aligned with their desired contraceptive features.
CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate current contraceptive decision-making among young LARC users and reflect broader trends toward non-hormonal methods and "holistic" lifestyles. This work highlights the importance of engaging young adults with medically-accurate information about hormones so they can consider evidence in aligning their preferences with decisions about contraception.
IMPLICATIONS: Hormone hesitancy was a prominent theme in contraceptive decision-making and reflected broader trends toward non-hormonal methods and "natural" lifestyles. There is a crucial need for healthcare providers to engage with clients in a way that enhances trust while minimizing the effect of misinformation.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and maternal whole-exome sequencing findings in patients with recurrent oocyte, zygote, and early embryo maturation arrest: a single-center experience.
articles.authors: Kahraman S, Cetinkaya M, Cetinkaya CP et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical phenotype, cumulative assisted reproductive technology (ART) experience, and maternal whole-exome sequencing (WES) findings in patients with recurrent Oocyte, Zygote, and Early Embryo Maturation Arrest (OZEMA), and to assess the contribution of phenotype-guided genomic evaluation in this clinically challenging population.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study conducted in a fertility clinic within a general private hospital equipped with an in‑house genetic laboratory.
SUBJECTS: A total of 115 females with a history of OZEMA were included, all of whom presented to the ART clinic.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The distribution of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in established OZEMA-associated genes, variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in established genes, monoallelic variants in established autosomal recessive genes, and exploratory candidate-gene findings. ART outcomes were described according to whether a prioritized WES finding was reported.
RESULTS: The mean female age was 33.47 +/- 4.37 years, with a median infertility duration of 6.0 years (range, 1.0-21.0). Patients had experienced recurrent OZEMA across multiple ART cycles (median, 4; range, 1-16). Parental consanguinity was observed in 37 of 115 cases (32.2 %). Prioritized maternal WES findings were identified in 64 of 115 patients (55.7 %): 12 patients (10.4 %) had P/LP variants in established genes with genotypes consistent with the reported inheritance pattern, 17 (14.8 %) had VUS in established genes, 15 (13.0 %) had monoallelic variants in established autosomal recessive genes without a second relevant allele, and 20 (17.4 %) had exploratory candidate-gene findings. No prioritized WES finding was identified in 51 patients (44.3 %).
CONCLUSIONS: Phenotype-guided maternal WES identified established P/LP findings with inheritance-consistent support in a clinically meaningful subset of patients with recurrent OZEMA and revealed a broader spectrum of additional genomic findings. These results support genomic evaluation, while the clinical interpretation of VUS, monoallelic findings in recessive genes, and exploratory candidate-gene findings should remain evidence-based.

articles.title: Metabolite changes in equine amniotic fluid associated with experimentally induced ascending placentitis.
articles.authors: Marchio SP, El-Sheikh Ali H, Klemashevich C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Equine ascending placentitis is a major cause of late-term pregnancy loss and stillbirth. However, early diagnosis remains limited, and its effect on amniotic fluid metabolite composition is poorly understood.
AIMS/OBJECTIVES: Characterize alterations in the amniotic fluid metabolome of mares with experimentally induced ascending placentitis.
METHODS: This was a controlled experimental study. At 280 days of gestation, six pony mares received an intracervical inoculation of Streptococcus equi subspecies zooepidemicus (placentitis group), and five mares were left untreated (control group). Placentitis mares developed signs of placental inflammation and were euthanized 8 days post-inoculation. Control mares were euthanized at corresponding gestational ages. Amniotic fluid was collected immediately after euthanasia and analyzed by untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Metabolites were annotated against a spectral library, with a match score above 60% considered a confident identification.
RESULTS: Eighteen metabolites differed between groups (P ≤ 0.05). Two were confidently identified. L-threonine was lower in placentitis mares than in control mares. L-isoleucine was higher in placentitis mares than in control mares.
CONCLUSION: In mares with ascending placentitis induced at 280 days of gestation, the amniotic fluid metabolome was altered, including decreased L-threonine and increased L-isoleucine.

articles.title: Current status and prospects of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) in drug delivery for women's health.
articles.authors: Rizg WY
articles.abstract: Women's health includes many biological and social challenges, such as reproductive disorders, maternal complications, osteoporosis, and gynecological cancers. Many current treatments have limitations like poor drug solubility, side effects, and lack of targeted delivery for female physiology. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), crystalline porous materials made of metal nodes and organic linkers, are being studied as advanced drug delivery systems to solve these problems. This review explains how MOF-based systems can be used in women's healthcare. MOFs like UiO-66 and ZIF-8 are used in targeted chemotherapy for breast and ovarian cancers. These systems are pH-responsive and ligand-functionalized, which improves treatment efficiency and reduces side effects. MOFs are also useful in bone health, where they deliver calcium, vitamin D3, and other osteogenic ions for treating postmenopausal osteoporosis. MOFs are being explored for hormonal regulation, non-hormonal contraception, and treatment of gynecological infections. However, there are still challenges such as long-term safety, metal ion leakage, and the need for proper testing in maternal-fetal conditions. With further research on safe synthesis methods and toxicity evaluation, MOFs can become an important platform for personalized and effective treatments in women's health.

articles.title: Developmental exposure to PBDE-47 induces sex- and organ-specific glucose uptake alterations linked to thyroid hormone disruption in rats: phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.
articles.authors: Wei H, Wen S, Tan B et al.
articles.abstract: 2, 2', 4, 4'-Tetrabromodiphenyl ether (PBDE-47) is a ubiquitous persistent organic pollutant with developmental toxicity and thyroid-disrupting activity. Increasing evidence links PBDE-47 exposure to metabolic disorders, yet it remains unclear whether developmental PBDE-47 exposure disturbs glucose metabolism in multiple organs of offspring and how thyroid hormone (TH) changes relate to such effects. Using a rat model of perinatal PBDE-47 exposure, organ-specific glucose metabolism were assessed via positron emission tomography with the 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) tracer. Adult male offspring exhibited increased FDG uptake in the heart but decreased uptake in the brain and kidneys, whereas female offspring showed elevated uptake in the brain and kidneys and reduced cardiac FDG uptake. These changes were accompanied by sex-specific TH alterations, with increased T3 in males and decreased T3 and T4 in females. Correlation analyses revealed significant associations between TH levels and organ-specific FDG uptake. Intriguingly, these coordinated metabolic and endocrine disruptions exhibited early phenotypic parallels to features of the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Network toxicology identified 89 core targets, with PIK3CB, PIK3R1, PIK3R2, PLCG1, and PLCG2 as hub molecules enriched in apoptosis, endocrine signaling, insulin resistance, and central carbon metabolism pathways. Molecular docking suggested high-affinity binding of PBDE-47 to these targets, and gene set analysis further implicated PI3K/AKT, insulin receptor signaling, and the AGE-RAGE pathway. Collectively, this study suggests that perinatal PBDE-47 exposure elicits sex-specific multi-organ alterations in FDG uptake that correlate with TH disruption, providing a hypothesis-generating basis for developmental metabolic toxicity and highlighting phenotypic parallels to early cardiorenal-metabolic crosstalk.

articles.title: Effects of perfluorohexane sulfonic acid on female reproductive function and oocyte quality.
articles.authors: Xu M, Ma Q, Jin S et al.
articles.abstract: An emerging persistent organic pollutant, perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS), has drawn considerable attention owing to its female reproductive toxicity. PFHxS penetrates the blood-follicle barrier and accumulates in follicular fluid, with a prolonged elimination half-life in humans. Mechanistically, PFHxS impairs oocyte quality through oxidative stress, mitochondrial damage, disruption of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis signaling, meiotic spindle abnormalities, and epigenetic modifications. Animal models demonstrate that PFHxS exposure leads to follicular arrest, reduced ovulation, and intrauterine growth restriction in offspring. Human studies have associated exposure with diminished ovarian reserve, prolonged amenorrhea, and reduced high-quality embryos. Current research highlights a shift from single-compound to mixture effects and transgenerational epigenetic inheritance, yet significant gaps remain regarding chronic low-dose exposure and causal evidence in clinical populations. Future research should focus on realistic exposure models and large-scale prospective cohorts, and the existing evidence should be integrated into regulatory frameworks to safeguard reproductive health.

articles.title: Cervical cancer in older women - A narrative review of age-specific management issues from the French cervical cancer guidelines group.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Dugast M, Moureau A, Tromelin E et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To summarize the available evidence on the management of cervical cancer in older women across early and advanced disease stages, with particular attention to treatment selection, feasibility, tolerance, and specific clinical situations, including cervical cancer associated with pelvic organ prolapse.
METHODS: A narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. Studies addressing surgery, radiotherapy, concurrent chemoradiotherapy, brachytherapy, para-aortic lymphadenectomy, cervical cancer associated with pelvic organ prolapse, and pre-treatment geriatric assessment were considered. The evidence was synthesized qualitatively according to six predefined clinical questions.
RESULTS: In early-stage disease, radical hysterectomy is feasible in selected fit elderly patients but is associated with increased perioperative morbidity, with advancing age. The available evidence does not establish whether surgery or definitive radiotherapy provides superior oncological outcomes in this population. In locally advanced cervical cancer, concurrent chemoradiotherapy appears to improve survival compared with radiotherapy alone in selected older patients, but with increased toxicity. Brachytherapy is associated with improved local control and survival, yet its use decreased with advancing age. No age-specific evidence demonstrated a survival benefit form pretreatment para-aortic lymphadenectomy. Data on cervical cancer associated with pelvic organ prolapse are limited to heterogeneous case reports and small retrospective studies. Pretreatment geriatric assessment influences treatment decisions in mixed cancer populations, but cervical cancer-specific outcome data are lacking.
CONCLUSION: Age-specific evidence remains limited and largely retrospective, and chronological age alone should not determine access to standard treatment. Treatment selection requires integration of tumor characteristics, frailty, comorbidities, functional status, expected treatment tolerance, quality of life, and patient preferences.

articles.title: Transvaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) for adnexal torsion (detorsion followed by ovarian cystectomy) in 10 steps.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Chene G, Cerruto E, Nohuz E
articles.abstract: Adnexal torsion is a surgical emergency usually treated by laparoscopy. The transvaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) may be a relevant minimally invasive alternative to laparoscopy. We propose a step-by-step video of the adnexal detorsion followed by ovarian cystectomy by the vNOTES approach.

articles.title: Post-treatment surveillance and management of recurrent cervical cancer - A review from the french cervical cancer guidelines group.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Buffeteau A, Chauvet P, Cordoba A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the available evidence on post-treatment follow-up and recurrence management after cervical cancer.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of the literature on surveillance modalities, and the management of pelvic and nodal recurrences.
RESULTS: Most recurrences occur within three years of treatment, but the survival benefit of detection before symptom onset remains unproven. After fertility-sparing surgery, HPV testing is sensitive for detecting asymptomatic pelvic recurrence. After hysterectomy, most recurrences are symptomatic, and clinical examination has a higher diagnostic yield than HPV testing or vaginal vault cytology. After concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT), persistent HPV infection is associated with an increased recurrence risk, but its limited specificity and the absence of a validated HPV-based surveillance strategy restrict its clinical utility. MRI and FDG PET/CT are useful for response assessment and investigation of suspected recurrence, but evidence supporting routine imaging of asymptomatic patients is lacking. Intensive follow-up schedules have not improved recurrence detection or survival. Evidence on recurrence management is predominantly retrospective. Pelvic recurrences after primary surgery have been treated with CRT, supplemented by brachytherapy for vaginal involvement. In selected patients with central pelvic recurrence after CRT, complete surgical resection may provide prolonged survival, but carries substantial morbidity. Nodal recurrences outside previously irradiated fields have been treated with CRT.
CONCLUSION: Available evidence supports a predominantly clinical, treatment-adapted follow-up. The survival benefit of intensive surveillance, routine imaging, or detecting asymptomatic recurrence remains uncertain. Recurrence management requires individualized multidisciplinary assessment based on disease extent, disease-free interval, and previous treatments.

articles.title: Safety of Multiple Sclerosis Treatments During Pregnancy: An Overview of the EU Regulatory Approach to Risk Management Planning.
articles.authors: Strassmann V, Gault N, Stark AK et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) may affect women of childbearing age. Information on safety of disease modifying treatment (DMT) in pregnancy is often limited at time of marketing authorisation. We summarised the EU regulatory experience with the implementation and performance of additional pharmacovigilance activities concerning safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding for medicines to treat MS.
METHODS: We reviewed EU risk management plans (RMPs) for centrally authorised MS DMTs to identify additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding. Information was analysed descriptively for type of measure, data collection method and data source. For non-interventional cohort studies and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases, information on current status, planned and actual size and duration was retrieved.
RESULTS: We identified 17 DMTs that included 21 additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding across 15 RMPs. These comprised nine non-interventional cohort studies and four structured follow-up activities of pregnancy cases that had been started. Of those, three were terminated due to low recruitment with an inclusion rate slower than planned, while inclusion was faster than planned in three finalised activities. Inclusion rate was slowest in primary data collection and faster in secondary analyses and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases.
CONCLUSION: Despite efforts to evaluate safety of MS medicines during pregnancy, recruitment and data collection remain challenging. Planning for use of multiple real-world data sources-including primary data collection, secondary use of electronic health records, and analyses of case reports-may help overcome these challenges and strengthen MS drug safety evaluations in pregnancy.

articles.title: Identification and prognostic value of non-hotspot POLE exonuclease domain mutations in endometrial cancer.
articles.authors: Kawai T, Yoshida H, Kobayashi Kato M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer with somatic POLE exonuclease domain mutations (EDMs) has a highly favorable prognosis; however, the clinical implications of non-hotspot EDMs in POLE remain unclear.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In 793 patients with endometrial cancer enrolled at the National Cancer Center and Juntendo University Hospitals, 25 prespecified variants were screened using the Luminex assay. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was carried out to evaluate 54 patients with hotspot and non-hotspot EDMs. In patients with endometrial cancer (n = 4864) registered in Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange (GENIE), those harboring hotspot EDMs were matched with randomly sampled patients without EDMs, and a polymerase epsilon (POLE) score for gene panel testing was developed.
RESULTS: In our cohort, POLE-EDMs, including hotspot (n = 91) and non-hotspot (n = 12) EDMs, were identified in 103 (12.9%) of 793 patients. The prevalence of grade 3 and advanced-stage endometrial cancer was higher in patients with non-hotspot EDMs than in those with hotspot EDMs. WES analysis of 54 patients revealed no significant differences in genomic mutations between the groups, and four non-hotspot EDMs were identified. A POLE-specific mutational signature was observed in tumors with EDM. In addition, the POLE score criteria were developed based on hotspot EDMs using the GENIE cohort, achieving a detection sensitivity of 0.94. Using the established POLE score, we identified nine non-hotspot EDMs.
CONCLUSIONS: We identified 13 novel candidate non-hotspot EDMs using a newly established POLE score for gene panels and demonstrated an association between non-hotspot EDMs and favorable prognosis. The identification of additional non-hotspot EDMs will facilitate precise molecular classification of endometrial cancer.

articles.title: An interpretive perspective on the childhood experiences of individuals born preterm: A meta-ethnographic synthesis.
