articles.authors: Çay ME, Çelik OT, Sağlam M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to understand the childhood experiences of individuals born preterm by examining qualitative studies within an interpretive and comparative framework.
METHOD: To develop a synthesis that interpretively integrates the subjective experiences of individuals born prematurely, search were conducted in the MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, PsychINFO, and EMBASE databases, yielding 2433 studies. Following screening based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, six studies were included in the meta-ethnography.
RESULTS: The analyses identified six themes reflecting the experiences of individuals born preterm from childhood through adulthood. These themes were: (1) family dynamics and interactions, (2) growing up with a fragile body, (3) falling behind in school and academic burden, (4) social exclusion, bullying, and the experience of being different, (5) a crisis of self-esteem and emotional burden, and (6) resilience and protective experiences.
DISCUSSION: These themes demonstrate that prematurity is experienced not merely as a medical event or an overcome challange, but as a multifaceted experience involving difficulties, identity formation, and resilience processes that become visible in specific domains and across different stages of life. Our findings indicate that individuals born preterm may experience academic, social, psychological, and health-related challenges, and that prematurity may shape their development. In this context, comprehensive and lifelong supportive approaches beginning at birth are recommended.

articles.title: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA and inflammation in Charcot-Marie-Tooth 1A and Charcot-Marie-Tooth 2A.
articles.authors: Li Z, Li Y, Li P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) is released from cells during such processes as mitophagy and apoptosis and can act as an endogenous damage-associated molecular pattern that activates innate immune responses. We investigated levels of circulating cell-free DNA (ccf-DNA), including ccf-mtDNA and circulating cell-free nuclear DNA (ccf-nDNA), and serum interleukin-1β (IL-1β) in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease, specifically with CMT1A and CMT2A.
METHODS: This study enrolled 51 patients with CMT disease (42 with CMT1A and 9 with CMT2A, 31 males and 20 females) and 13 healthy controls (6 males and 7 females). The numbers of copies of serum ccf-mtDNA and ccf-nDNA, were quantified using ND1 and ACTB, respectively, before being measured via quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Serum IL-1β levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The number of ccf-DNA copies, ND1/ACTB ratio, and IL-1β levels were compared between the three groups. And the correlation analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Serum ND1 levels were higher in patients with CMT1A (p < 0.01) and CMT2A (p < 0.001) than in healthy controls, so was the ND1/ACTB ratio in the CMT1A (p < 0.001) and CMT2A (p < 0.05) groups. Serum IL-1β levels were higher in patients with CMT1A (p < 0.01) and CMT2A (p < 0.001) than in healthy controls. The ND1/ACTB ratio was positively related to the number of onion bulbs in CMT2A. No significant differences in serum ACTB, ND1, ND1/ACTB, or IL-1β levels were observed between the CMT1A and CMT2A groups.
CONCLUSION: Patients with CMT1A and CMT2A had higher levels of serum ccf-mtDNA and IL-1β than in healthy controls. These findings suggest association between increased circulating mitochondrial DNA and inflammation in CMT disease. However, no subtype-specific differences were identified between CMT1A and CMT2A.

articles.title: Chlorogenic acid attenuates ovarian inflammation and oxidative stress and is associated with NF-κB/NLRP3-related molecular changes in PCOS rats: An integrated in vivo and in silico study.
articles.authors: Talebi SF, Shoorei H, Bhandari RK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and hyperandrogenism. This study investigated the effects of chlorogenic acid (CGA) on ovarian alterations in an estradiol valerate (EV)-induced rat model of PCOS, with particular attention to NLRP3-related inflammatory changes.
METHODS: Female rats (n = 36) were assigned to control, PCOS, and PCOS+CGA groups. PCOS was induced by a single intramuscular injection of EV (4 mg/kg). After confirmation of PCOS at 8 weeks, CGA (100 mg/kg/day, i.p.) was administered for 8 weeks. Hormonal profiles, ovarian histomorphology and fibrosis, oxidative stress markers, inflammatory mediators, miR-93-5p, TLR4, NF-κB, and NLRP3 expression, and NLRP3 immunoreactivity were evaluated. ADMET prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were also performed.
RESULTS: PCOS rats showed increased T, LH, LH/FSH ratio, ROS, MDA, pro-inflammatory mediators, NF-κB, miR-93-5p, TLR4, and NLRP3 expression, NLRP3 immunoreactivity, cystic follicles, and ovarian fibrosis, together with reduced FSH, CAT, IL-10, developing follicles, and corpora lutea. CGA significantly attenuated these alterations, although several parameters remained different from controls. Docking supported the structural plausibility of CGA interactions with the investigated targets. Ligand-centered MD analyses showed relatively persistent CGA association with NLRP3, more variable association with IKKβ, and substantial displacement in the TLR4/MD-2 system.
CONCLUSIONS: CGA ameliorated endocrine, oxidative, inflammatory, and histopathological abnormalities in experimental PCOS. These effects were accompanied by coordinated changes in ovarian miR-93-5p expression and TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3-associated inflammatory markers. Further studies are required to determine the functional relationships among these molecular changes.

articles.title: Comparing contraceptive requests and initiation following in-person versus telehealth medication abortion.
articles.authors: Ichikawa M, Yang E, Tschann M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compare post-abortion contraception (PAC) requests at initial consultation and PAC method initiation at follow-up between people seeking telehealth and in-person medication abortion.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study of all medication abortions performed by the University of Hawai'i Options Center between 2019 and 2021. Using electronic health records, we collected data on patient demographics, clinical characteristics, receipt of contraceptive counseling, PAC method requested at initial consultation, and PAC method initiated at follow-up.
RESULTS: Of 681 medication abortion patients, 341 received initial consultation in-person and 340 via telehealth. At initial consultation, contraceptive preferences differed significantly (p < 0.01), with a greater proportion of telehealth patients undecided or without a stated preference (36.5% telehealth vs. 27.3% in-person). Of patients who followed up, those who had their initial consultation in-person were significantly more likely to have initiated a form of contraception at the time of follow-up (30.0% telehealth vs. 52.0% in-person, p < 0.001). Of the patients who initiated contraception, those who had their initial consultation in-person more frequently initiated provider-dependent methods such as long-acting reversible contraceptive methods (19.1% telehealth vs. 39.3% in-person) and injectable contraception (4.5% telehealth vs. 12.1% in-person).
CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving medication abortion care via telehealth were less likely to have a contraceptive preference at initial consultation and less likely to have initiated a contraceptive method at follow-up. Telehealth patients also initiated provider-dependent methods less frequently than in-person patients. PAC initiation may be subject to the same barriers that impact access to abortion, and attention is needed to ensure equitable contraceptive access in communities.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: These findings indicate a difference between PAC preferences based on mode of medication abortion delivery, highlighting a need to address contraceptive service availability, particularly for provider-dependent methods, in areas with limited access to in-person reproductive health care.

articles.title: Mode of birth and maternal health up to three years postpartum: A dutch retrospective population-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Berends-Hoekstra WE, Homburg TM, Danoe G et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal postpartum health problems can persist well beyond the conventional six-week postpartum care period. No nationwide studies have combined large-scale electronic health records (EHRs) from perinatal and general practice (GP) care linking long-term health problems to birth mode. We aimed to examine how birth mode (spontaneous vaginal, instrumental vaginal, and caesarean section) influences the frequency and hazard of maternal physical and psychological health problems in GP care from six weeks to three years postpartum. In this observational population-based cohort study we linked Dutch perinatal EHRs (2014-2020) to GP EHRs (2015-2023), including women who gave birth to a term singleton. Health problems were retrieved from GP EHR's using International Classification of Primary Care codes and GP notes, the latter analysed with natural language processing. Women were stratified by parity. Cox proportional hazard models estimated crude and adjusted associations between birth mode and postpartum health problems, using spontaneous vaginal birth as the reference. In total, 10 628 primiparous and 11 719 multiparous women were included. Adjusted for confounders, caesarean section and instrumental vaginal birth were linked to significantly increased hazards of dyspareunia. Caesarean section was additionally associated with an elevated anaemia hazard but reduced hazards of urinary incontinence and ureterovaginal prolapse compared to spontaneous vaginal birth. We showed that maternal health problems may persist up to three years postpartum and vary by birth mode. These findings may raise awareness among mothers and care providers of key long-term maternal health problems, underscoring the need for a new paradigm of prolonged postpartum care.

articles.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea is associated with reduced semen quality and compartmentalized seminal inflammation: A prospective cohort with non-randomized CPAP follow-up.
articles.authors: Ji Y, Wang H, Lv M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is associated with systemic inflammation and male reproductive dysfunction, but its relationship with semen quality and local seminal inflammation remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations of OSA with semen parameters, erectile function, and inflammatory profiles, and to assess longitudinal changes in these markers following continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy.
METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 72 reproductive-aged men with OSA and 22 non-OSA controls. Polysomnography was performed at baseline only. During CPAP follow-up, treatment efficacy was ascertained from device-recorded hours of use and residual apnoea-hypopnoea index. Erectile function (IIEF-5), semen quality, and serum/seminal cytokines were assessed.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, OSA patients showed significantly lower total and progressive sperm motility and semen volume, along with elevated seminal IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, and IL-17A, without corresponding changes in serum cytokines or erectile function. During CPAP follow-up, adherent patients demonstrated early improvements in progressive sperm motility as early as 1 month post-treatment. Sleep architecture disruption and local seminal inflammation were independently associated with reduced semen quality.
CONCLUSION: OSA is associated with reduced semen quality and localized seminal inflammation, without corresponding systemic or erectile changes. CPAP therapy is accompanied by longitudinal improvements in sperm motility, suggesting that evaluation for sleep-disordered breathing may be considered an exploratory assessment in men presenting with unexplained semen abnormalities.

articles.title: The associations of triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index and relative handgrip strength with new-onset frailty: evidence from two prospective cohort studies.
articles.authors: Long M, Han L, Zhao X
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index and relative handgrip strength are emerging indicators of nutritional-metabolic status and muscle function, respectively. Their associations with new-onset frailty remain unclear. This study examined their separate and joint associations with new-onset frailty.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (participants aged 45 years or older) and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (participants aged 50 years or older). Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate associations with incident frailty. Joint analyses assessed cumulative incidence using Kaplan-Meier curves, and predictive performance using the Harrell C-index, time-dependent area under the curve, and calibration plots. Exploratory mediation and subgroup analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 1774 participants in the Chinese cohort and 1013 in the English cohort developed frailty. In Model 2, the triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index was positively associated with frailty (Chinese cohort, hazard ratio = 1.15; English cohort, hazard ratio = 1.32), whereas relative handgrip strength was inversely associated with frailty (Chinese cohort, hazard ratio = 0.57; English cohort, hazard ratio = 0.36). Participants with a high triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index and low relative handgrip strength had the highest frailty risk. Exploratory attenuation proportions were 27.10% and 29.32% for the triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index-frailty association, and 6.99% and 9.95% for the relative handgrip strength-frailty association.
CONCLUSION: Higher triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index and lower relative handgrip strength were separately associated with increased frailty risk, and their combination conferred the highest risk. Exploratory analyses suggested that each association was partially attenuated after mutual adjustment.

articles.title: Optimizing care for children with ovarian masses: development and evaluation of a multidisciplinary management algorithm.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: van Leeuwen J, Hulsker CCC, Kooij CD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Ovarian masses in children between 0 and 18 years old are usually benign, although 10% are malignant. To avoid unnecessary oophorectomies and ensure the best possible outcome, we aimed to develop and validate a management algorithm for accurate diagnosis, referral and management of children with ovarian masses.
METHODS: A management algorithm was developed based on a systematic review of studies that provided recommendations for the diagnostic approach and management of pediatric ovarian masses. Subsequently, this management algorithm was validated in a retrospective cohort of patients, aged 6 months to 18 years, with an ovarian mass who were treated between 2019 and 2022 with a sufficient follow-up at the Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology and/or the Wilhelmina Children's Hospital, The Netherlands. Medical records were searched for clinical characteristics, diagnostic findings, treatment and outcome.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies were included in the design of our management algorithm. The validation cohort included fifty-five patients with an ovarian mass, of which 8 were suspected of ovarian torsion. All malignant tumors were complex/solid on ultrasound and, after a multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting, had been referred to the pediatric oncology center for individualized treatment. Of the ovarian masses that were suspected benign based on our algorithm, benign histology was confirmed and an ovarian sparing surgery was performed when feasible.
CONCLUSION: The proposed algorithm appears clinically applicable for the accurate management of pediatric ovarian masses. This standardized approach seems helpful to accurately stratify benign and malignant ovarian masses and will prevent over- or undertreatment.

articles.title: Baseline HPV16 status and genotype multiplicity independently predict subsequent high-grade cervical lesions in HR-HPV-positive women referred for colposcopy with negative or low-grade cytology: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Gardella B, Dominoni M, Pano MR et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prospective risk of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (HSIL+) in high-risk HPV (HR-HPV)positive women, assessing the independent and interactive effects of baseline HPV16-status, genotype multiplicity, and follow-up HPV persistence.
METHODS: A prospective cohort of 2562 HR-HPV-positive women referred for colposcopy were categorized into four groups: single non-HPV16, single HPV16, HPV16 plus other HR types, or multiple non-HPV16. HSIL+ risk was analysed using Cox-proportional-hazards-regression, restricted mean survival time (RMST) at 36months, and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated concurrent HSIL+ risk associated with follow-up HPV persistence.
RESULTS: Overall, 691 women (27.0%) developed HSIL+. Infection with HPV16 plus other HR types carried the highest risk (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]2.10, 95%CI: 1.69-2.62) and shorter median HSIL+-free survival than single non-HPV16 infection (24 vs. 54months), corresponding to 5.1 fewer HSIL+-free-months at 36months (p<0.001). Baseline HPV16 positivity and genotype multiplicity exerted independent, additive effects without multiplicative interaction (adjusted p=0.600). Incorporating multiplicity improved model discrimination beyond entry cytology and HPV16 status (concordance index 0.612 vs. 0.587, p<0.001). Results remained robust in competing-risk analyses (subdistribution HR2.03, 95%CI: 1.64-2.52) and after excluding early-treated women (aHR2.00, 95%CI: 1.52-2.62). Follow-up viral persistence strongly correlated with concurrent HSIL+ (aHR5.71-8.59, p<0.001), reflecting a cross-sectional risk correlation complementary to baseline prognostication.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline HPV16 positivity and genotype multiplicity are independent, additive risk factors for HSIL+, with HPV16 plus other HR types marking the highest-risk subgroup. Genotype multiplicity provides distinct clinical predictive value alongside HPV16 status, while follow-up HPV persistence offers complementary, non-redundant information for concurrent risk evaluation in risk-based management strategies.

articles.title: Role of Liver Parameters in Preterm Birth: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Li Q, Yang J, Chen J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between liver dysfunction during pregnancy and the risk of preterm birth (PTB).
METHODS: We conducted a prospective birth cohort study in China that included 23,194 women with singleton pregnancies. Several biomarkers, including total bile acids (TBA), gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), the AST-to-ALT ratio, and total bilirubin (TBiL), were measured in the first and third trimesters. The primary outcome was PTB (delivery before 37 weeks of gestation).
RESULTS: The incidence of PTB among our participants was 5.7%. After multivariable adjustment, increased levels of TBA, GGT, ALT, and AST, as well as abnormal liver function tests (LFTs) in early pregnancy, were associated with a higher risk of PTB. An increased AST-to-ALT ratio was associated with a lower risk of PTB. Furthermore, a nonlinear test revealed a linear association between PTB and TBiL, TBA, GGT, ALT, AST, and the AST-to-ALT ratio in the first trimester. The association between liver enzyme levels and PTB in late pregnancy was similar to that observed in early gestation. In addition, TBiL in late pregnancy was negatively correlated with PTB. Interestingly, a consistent association was observed between GGT and PTB, whether iatrogenic or spontaneous, in both the first and third trimesters (p <0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Associations have been observed between liver enzyme levels in both early and late gestation and the risk of PTB. Consequently, future mechanistic and interventional studies are warranted to further investigate these links.

articles.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
articles.authors: Sanidas G, Simonti G, Ghaemmaghami J et al.
articles.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

articles.title: Attitudes toward using non-medical eligibility criteria for publicly funded IVF: a population survey in Belgium.
articles.authors: Van Muylder A, Kessels R, D Hooghe T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) such as in-vitro fertilization (IVF) are often reimbursed based on non-medical eligibility criteria, such as patients' age, marital status, relationship type or reproductive history. These criteria reflect normative assumptions about parenthood and remain ethically contested.
OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the Belgian public's awareness of and attitudes toward the use of such non-medical criteria in reimbursing IVF and identifies socio-demographic patterns underlying these views.
METHODS: A sample of 3,000 adults (18-70y) completed an online survey that elicited attitudes towards public funding of IVF and using funding restrictions based on patients' age, partner age and gender, relationship type, number of prior children, and different infertility etiologies. Latent class cluster analysis (LCCA) was used to detect opinion subgroups, and logistic regression to assess socio-demographic predictors of subgroup membership.
RESULTS: Although there was strong overall support for public reimbursement of IVF, respondents showed limited knowledge about eligibility criteria within the Belgian system. Majorities endorsed several eligibility restrictions, including those based on maternal age (74%), partner age (57%), number of prior biological children (60%), and consciously delayed childbearing (70%). Two thirds opposed prioritizing heterosexual couples. LCCA revealed three distinct opinion profiles (generous, moderately restrictive, and highly restrictive), primarily differentiated by the perceived generosity of current Belgian policy, access for same-sex couples and single mothers, and the acceptability of patient copayments. Parenthood experience and prior infertility were significant predictors of profile membership.
CONCLUSION: This study finds widespread public support for reimbursing fertility treatment within Belgian healthcare, but also for using eligibility criteria that extend beyond the currently used, sole criterion of maternal age. In the light of growing infertility rates, pressured ART budgets and the limited awareness of the current policy observed in this survey, these results underscore the need for further societal debate on priority setting in Belgian infertility care.

articles.title: A Canadian population-based observational cohort study of alpha and beta-thalassemia syndromes in pregnancy.
articles.authors: Auger N, Dubois D, Wei SQ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Beta-thalassemia can adversely affect pregnancy, but the impact of alpha-thalassemia is less studied. We assessed whether patients with symptomatic alpha-thalassemia have similar pregnancy outcomes as patients with symptomatic beta-thalassemia.
METHODS: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of 1,324,488 pregnancies in Quebec, Canada, between 2006 and 2022. The exposures were maternal symptomatic alpha-thalassemia, symptomatic beta-thalassemia, thalassemia trait, and other thalassemia syndromes. Primary outcomes were severe maternal morbidity, preterm birth, preeclampsia, and other pregnancy complications. We used log-binomial regression models to estimate adjusted risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the association between each thalassemia and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: In total, 825 patients had symptomatic alpha-thalassemia, 681 symptomatic beta-thalassemia, 1,749 thalassemia trait, and 2,377 other thalassemia syndromes. Compared with no thalassemia, alpha-thalassemia (RR 3.05; 95% CI: 2.36-3.94) and beta-thalassemia (RR 2.52; 95% CI: 1.84-3.45) were associated with a greater risk of severe maternal morbidity. However, alpha-thalassemia was additionally associated with preterm birth (RR 1.45; 95% CI: 1.16-1.82), preeclampsia (RR 1.67; 95% CI: 1.27-2.20), and gestational diabetes (RR 1.79; 95% CI: 1.52-2.09). Beta-thalassemia was not associated with these outcomes, and associations were weak for thalassemia trait and other thalassemias.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that symptomatic alpha-thalassemia is associated with a wider range of pregnancy complications than symptomatic beta-thalassemia and other thalassemia syndromes. However, symptomatic alpha and beta-thalassemia are both associated with severe maternal morbidity.

articles.title: Cost-Consequence Analysis Comparing Originator r-hFSH-alfa and Biosimilars for =4 Complete Ovarian Stimulation Cycles During Assisted Reproductive Technology Treatment: A Multi-Country Perspective.
articles.authors: Roeder C, Longo R, Luyten J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) demand is increasing, raising questions about the cost-effectiveness of ovarian stimulation (OS) treatments. This study evaluates the clinical and economic outcomes of originator recombinant human follicle-stimulating hormone (r-hFSH-alfa) compared with its biosimilars across multiple ART cycles and countries.
DESIGN: A cost-consequence analysis was conducted using a decision-tree model simulating up to four complete OS cycles in women undergoing ART across seven countries (Spain, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Denmark, Australia, and South Korea). The analysis incorporated both fresh and frozen embryo transfers within each cycle and included base-case and scenario analyses, including treatment-switching strategies.
PARTICIPANTS: Theoretical model corresponding to women undergoing ART and receiving originator r-hFSH-alfa or a biosimilar for OS.
METHODS: Clinical inputs were derived from published real-world data and a meta-analysis. Economic inputs were estimated from public payer perspectives and included drug acquisition, ART procedures, embryo transfer, pregnancy, and delivery costs. Outcomes included cumulative live birth rate (CLBR), total costs, and cost per LB. Base-case and scenario analyses, including treatment-switching strategies, were conducted alongside deterministic sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Originator r-hFSH-alfa was associated with a higher CLBR compared with biosimilars (58.2% vs 50.8%). This advantage persisted across scenarios and time horizons. Despite slightly higher drug acquisition costs, originator r-hFSH-alfa resulted in lower cost per LB across all countries, with savings ranging from approximately €2,900 to over €8,000 per LB. Strategies initiating treatment with biosimilars were consistently dominated (less effective and more costly) compared to strategies starting with r-hFSH-alpha. Results were robust to sensitivity analyses, with LB rate differences being the primary driver of outcomes.
LIMITATIONS: This model included limited national clinical data and reliance on modeled assumptions. Other studies are needed to further establish the robustness of the effectiveness data used here. Indirect societal costs and the emotional burden associated with unsuccessful ART cycles were not included. Additionally, costs related to ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome were excluded because rates are very similar between both treatment arms.
CONCLUSIONS: Across multiple countries…

articles.title: Understanding intravaginal practices for gynecologic health among Haitian migrant women: A mixed-methods analysis.
articles.authors: Guillaume D, Amédée LM, Alcaide M et al.
articles.abstract: Haitian migrant women in the U.S. experience disproportionate rates of cervical cancer. Intravaginal practices (IVPs) are widely used among Haitian women and have been linked to an increased risk of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although IVPs are well-documented in the Haitian community, little is known about Haitian migrant women's perceptions and motivations underlying their use. This exploratory sequential mixed-methods study examined Haitian migrant women's motivations for engaging in IVPs, products used for IVPs, and indications for their use. A convenience sample of Haitian migrant women in South Florida were recruited through active and passive recruitment approaches in community-based centers. Semi-structured qualitative interviews (n = 25) explored perceptions, motivations, and products used for IVPs. Qualitative results informed the development of survey items measuring IVPs, which were administered to participants (n = 151). Chi-square analysis with a Bonferroni adjustment examined associations between IVP products and IVP indications. All women in the qualitative sample (n = 25, 100%) confirmed IVP use compared to 68.9% (n = 104) of women in the quantitative sample. Qualitative interviews revealed that IVP preferences were rooted in cultural expectations with most women starting these practices either during puberty or after sexual debut. IVP products (e.g., plant and herbal agents, astringent washes, and antibiotics) were often chosen based on specific gynecologic indications, with this finding being consistent across both samples. Pigeon pea (pwa kongo) was the most frequently used IVP product in the quantitative sample (n = 74, 71.2%) and was associated with nearly all IVP indications (p ≤ 0.004). Given the high prevalence of IVPs in our sample, researchers and practitioners should further examine the meaningful health risks and protective effects associated with IVPs.

articles.title: Gynecological malignancy signal triage: A two-dimensional framework integrating US-derived FAERS data with comparative US-China GBD trajectories.
articles.authors: Ma Y, Li D, Duan J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-related adverse-event reports are difficult to interpret because statistical disproportionality, stimulated reporting, and background disease burden are distinct phenomena. To address this, we formalized a two-dimensional prioritization framework that combines FAERS signal credibility with independent GBD burden context. Because the FAERS dataset is overwhelmingly of US origin, we utilized China exclusively as a prespecified macro-epidemiological GBD comparator, strictly avoiding cross-national pharmacovigilance extrapolations.
METHODS: We analyzed FAERS reports (2004-2023) and female GBD 2023 estimates for China and the United States. Four disproportionality algorithms (ROR, PRR, IC, and EBGM) were evaluated for 150 high-frequency primary-suspect drug-event pairs (50 per cancer group). We report any-algorithm positivity and four-algorithm concordance alongside case-definition sensitivity analyses. GBD trends, age-period-cohort models, and exploratory projections to 2053 were integrated to provide population-level context, explicitly not as exposure denominators or for causal validation.
RESULTS: FAERS cohorts yielded 19,717 cancer-associated report records. Among 150 high-frequency candidate pairs, 42 met all four algorithmic thresholds. The top-50 candidate screen captured approximately 72.8%-75.8% of primary-suspect records, serving as a variance-reduction step rather than a complete all-drug screen. Drugs like ranitidine and talc demonstrated marked disproportionality but also exhibited reporter and temporal features heavily compatible with stimulated reporting. Time-to-onset distributions reflected recorded administrative reporting intervals rather than biological carcinogenesis. GBD estimates revealed divergent China-US trajectories, notably a rising baseline for US uterine cancer.
CONCLUSIONS: The formalized F × G framework operates as a transparent triage tool, not a causal classifier. FAERS disproportionality generates hypotheses; GBD trajectories indicate potential public-health priority. All prioritized signals-particularly those involving consumer products or immunosuppressants-require formal causal evaluation in longitudinal exposure-denominator datasets.

articles.title: Luminal B-like predominance in breast cancer: A 5-year institutional experience of 2271 women from a tertiary cancer center in South India.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer research and therapeutics
articles.authors: Sulakshana MS, Sreelakshmi S, Krishna KL et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy among women, surpassing cervical cancer. Classifying tumors based on surrogate molecular subtypes using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and in situ hybridization (ISH) for human epidermal growth factor receptor (HER2) is essential for guiding treatment decisions. This study aims to assess the prevalence of these molecular subtypes in a South Indian population.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included women diagnosed with invasive breast carcinoma between January 2019 and December 2023. Cases with incomplete biomarker data were excluded. IHC for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), HER2, and Ki-67 was performed, and HER2 IHC 2 + cases were further evaluated using fluorescence in situ hybridization. Tumors were categorized into surrogate molecular subtypes using established American Society of Clinical Oncology and College of American Pathologists and St. Gallen guidelines. Clinical and histopathological data were collected from hospital records.
RESULTS: A total of 2271 patients were analyzed (median age: 58 years; 73.6% postmenopausal). Luminal B-like tumors were the most common subtype (62.6%), followed by triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) at 16.4%, HER2-enriched (non-luminal) at 10.7%, and luminal A-like at 10.2%. Notably, the number of triple-positive tumors exceeded that of TNBC (23.38% vs. 16.4%). ER and PR positivity rates were 68.8% and 65.1%, respectively, and HER2 positivity was observed in 34.1% of cases. Invasive carcinoma of no special type constituted 95.5% of cases, with Grade 2 tumors being the most common (63.8%).
CONCLUSION: The distribution of menopausal status, molecular subtypes, and histologic features in our cohort closely resembled patterns reported in Western populations. These findings emphasize the heterogeneity of patients and the need for generating local data to effectively address breast cancer treatment.

articles.title: Study on the association between the low-density lipoprotein to high-density lipoprotein ratio and clinicopathological characteristics of breast cancer: A retrospective analysis incorporating subgroup evaluations by age, body mass index, and menopausal status.
articles.authors: Dong L, Liu C, Li L et al.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) represents the most prevalent malignant tumor among women globally, with its pronounced heterogeneity presenting significant challenges for precision diagnosis and treatment. Aberrant lipid metabolism, particularly the ratio of low-density lipoprotein to high-density lipoprotein (LHR), has garnered considerable interest in relation to BC development and progression. Nevertheless, the association between LHR and clinicopathological characteristics remains inadequately explored. To address this gap, the present retrospective study analyzed 583 BC patients who underwent surgical treatment at Qilu Hospital of Shandong University. Preoperative blood lipid profiles and clinicopathological data were systematically collected to investigate the association between LHR and critical features, including molecular subtypes. The findings indicated that LHR levels were significantly elevated in patients aged 46 years or older, postmenopausal women, and individuals with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or higher. Subgroup analyses incorporating age, menopausal status, and BMI suggested potential interactions between these clinical factors and LHR. Although univariate analysis demonstrated an association between LHR and certain clinicopathological features, multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that menopausal status, rather than LHR, was the sole independent predictor of ER-positive and PR-positive status. Therefore, LHR should not be considered an independent predictive biomarker for receptor status. In conclusion, although the LHR demonstrates statistically significant associations with certain clinicopathological characteristics, its modest effect sizes and discriminative ability close to chance indicate limited clinical utility as an independent biomarker. These preliminary findings highlight the need for future research focused on identifying reliable metabolic signatures. Such studies should consider utilizing multi-marker panels instead of relying exclusively on individual lipid metrics for risk stratification in breast cancer.

articles.title: Does time-lapse imaging (TLI) of embryos improve reproductive outcomes in in vitro fertilisation (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)? Individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Bhide P, Chan DYL, Kieslinger DC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Time‑lapse imaging (TLI) systems may improve the success of in vitro fertilisation (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) by enabling undisturbed embryo culture and/or providing morphokinetic data to refine embryo selection. Despite several trials and aggregate meta-analyses showing uncertainty of benefit, there is little translation of evidence into guidelines. Heterogeneity in participant populations and algorithms used for TLI, although acknowledged in aggregate meta-analyses, remains unaddressed.
OBJECTIVE AND RATIONALE: We conducted an individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis to assess whether TLI improves reproductive outcomes and if effects vary by women or intervention characteristics. Our IPD meta-analysis enhances statistical power, allowing precise estimation of treatment effects and identification of subgroup differences. It overcomes the limitations of aggregate meta-analyses by enabling harmonised adjustment by participant-level baseline risk, testing treatment-covariate interactions and provides a comprehensive evaluation of TLI by leveraging diverse datasets from multiple studies that assess both undisturbed culture and morphokinetic-based embryo selection. The study implements rigorous data integrity and consistency checks to enhance the reliability and trustworthiness of its findings.
SEARCH METHODS: We conducted an IPD meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) in women undergoing IVF/ICSI that used TLI systems. We evaluated overall TLI (undisturbed culture and morphokinetic-based embryo selection), undisturbed culture alone, and morphokinetic-based embryo selection alone. The primary outcome was live birth after a first fresh or frozen embryo transfer; other outcomes included clinical pregnancy, biochemical pregnancy loss, miscarriage, multiple pregnancy, minor and major congenital malformations, birth weight, and gestational age at birth. We included trials from the 2019 Cochrane review and updated searches of MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and CENTRAL from 7 January 2019 to 9 May 2025 and repeated the search on 28 July 2026. We requested IPD from the authors of included trials. We assessed study-level risk of bias using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for RCTs (ROB2) and undertook integrity assessment of included studies. We performed a two-stage IPD meta-analysis. Results are presented as adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals and adjusted absolute risk difference (aRD)…

articles.title: 2D perineal compared to 3D endovaginal ultrasound for evaluation of the levator ani muscles in women.
articles.authors: Trikhacheva A, Alcoba E, Karimi Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pelvic floor therapists are incorporating mid-sagittal two-dimensional (2D) perineal pelvic floor ultrasound (pPFUS) to augment their pelvic floor digital examination. Although the mid-sagittal plane gives crucial information about pelvic floor function, it does not allow the operator to directly ascertain the integrity and thickness of the levator ani muscle (LAM). We aimed to evaluate the correlation between LAM thickness obtained with 2D pPFUS in the coronal plane and three-dimensional (3D) endovaginal ultrasound (EVUS) in the axial plane in women without pelvic organ prolapse (POP) at or beyond the hymen to evaluate if 2D pPFUS is an effective tool for visualization of LAM.
METHODS: In a retrospective descriptive analysis, 2D pPFUS and 3D (EVUS) were compared to attempt visualization and quantitatively measure the puborectalis (PR), pubococcygeus (PC), and iliococcygeus (IC) within the same patient cohort. LAM thickness was recorded at mid-urethra, mid-vagina, and mid-anorectum coronal levels. Statistical analyses included comparing measurements and calculating predictive values and correlation between 2D pPFUS and 3D EVUS.
RESULTS: Coronal 2D pPFUS could not be used to discretely visualize the PC and IC in any patient. Comparison of PR thickness between 2 and 3D ultrasound at different levels showed positive predictive values ranging from 0.70 to 0.86, while negative predictive values ranged from 0 to 1.00 across all three levels. Moderate to high correlations were observed between measurements taken at the mid-urethra and mid-vagina using both ultrasound modalities. At the mid-anorectum level, correlation was weak and inconsistent between sides, with only a low positive correlation on the right and no significant correlation on the left.
CONCLUSIONS: Measurements of the LAM at the level of the PR obtained with 2D pPFUS show good correlation with those obtained using 3D EVUS at the mid-urethra and mid-vagina levels. However, 2D pPFUS is limited by its inability to visualize PC and IC muscles.

articles.title: Effects of Prebiotics, Probiotics, or Synbiotics on Health Outcomes, Sex Hormones, Oxidative Stress, and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A GRADE Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials, and Umbrella Review.
articles.authors: Dong Q, Chen H, Liu N et al.
articles.abstract: Numerous individual studies have examined the effects of biotics on isolated health outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). However, a comprehensive evaluation of their impact on the full metabolic panel and sex hormone profiles is lacking. Accordingly, this meta-analysis of RCTs and umbrella review attempted to form a complete picture of the overall efficacy of biotics on human metabolism and endocrine function. The PubMed, Scopus, Cochran, Web of Science, and Embase databases were used for conducting a comprehensive systematic search. Twenty RCTs were included in the meta-analysis and 11 meta-analyses were included for umbrella review. The pooled estimates of the studies evaluating the effects of biotics on anthropometric measurements indicated that biotics are associated with an improvement in weight (SMD: -1.21, 95%CI: -2.06, -0.36) and body mass index (BMI) (SMD: -0.77, 95%CI: -1.45, -0.10), waist circumference (WC) (SMD: -0.67, 95%CI: -1.18, -0.16), waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) (SMD: -0.84, 95%CI: -1.52, -0.15), glycemic control fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (SMD: -0.71, 95%CI: -1.19, -0.24), insulin (SMD: -0.64, 95%CI: -1.07, -0.21), and HOMA-IR (SMD: -0.78, 95%CI: -1.24, -0.32), total cholesterol (TC) (SMD: -0.69, 95%CI: -1.25, -0.13), low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL) (SMD: -0.71, 95%CI: -1.21, -0.20), high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL) (SMD: 0.39, 95%CI: 0.19, 0.60), triglyceride (TG) (SMD: -0.53, 95%CI: -0.95, -0.10), oxidative stress biomarkers such as malondialdehyde (MDA) (SMD: -0.96, 95%CI: -1.29, -0.63), total antioxidant capacity (TAC) (SMD: 0.59, 95% CI: 0.29, 0.89), testosterone (TT) (SMD: -1.29, 95%CI: -1.98, -0.68) level. However, umbrella review showed that biotics may contribute to an improvement in weight, BMI, WC, FPG, insulin, HOMA-IR, QUICKI, lipid profile, CRP, oxidative stress markers (MDA, TAC), TT and LH/FSH ratio too. In conclusion, this meta-analysis and umbrella review provide evidence that prebiotics, probiotics, or synbiotics may confer beneficial effects on a range of health outcomes among patients with PCOS.

articles.title: Data-driven reweighting of the Charlson and Elixhauser comorbidity indices using German claims data: development for in-hospital mortality only, external validation across clinical and health-economic outcomes.
articles.authors: Kaier K, Hazard D, Heidenreich A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comorbidity scores such as the Charlson and Elixhauser indices are widely used for risk adjustment in health-economic and clinical outcomes research. Yet the existing weighting schemes, originally designed for mortality prediction, may no longer reflect today's patient populations or perform equally well across diverse outcomes. This study aimed to reweight both indices using a data-driven approach and to evaluate their predictive validity for multiple clinical and health-economic outcomes.
METHODS: Using administrative data from a large tertiary care teaching hospital in Germany (N = 198,819 hospitalizations), we applied adaptive lasso regression to recalibrate the Charlson (Deyo weights) and Elixhauser (van Walraven weights) comorbidity indices. Reweighting was performed for in-hospital mortality as the development endpoint. Penalized coefficients were converted into integer-based weights. Model performance was assessed for three dichotomous endpoints (in-hospital mortality, severe bleeding, prolonged mechanical ventilation) and two continuous outcomes (length of hospital stay, total reimbursement). External validation was performed in three independent cohorts: Elective endometrial cancer (N = 85,204), interventional left atrial appendage closure (N = 28,039), and emergency ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI; N = 248,062). AUC, R², and RMSE were used as complementary measures of discrimination and predictive accuracy. Pooled relative improvements of AUC, R², and RMSE across the three validation cohorts was calculated using random effects meta-analyses.
RESULTS: Reweighting consistently improved predictive performance across endpoints and cohorts, with modest absolute gains for in-hospital mortality and more pronounced gains for severe bleeding and continuous outcomes. When analysing in-hospital mortality in the three validation cohorts, the reweighted Charlson improved AUC from 0.679 to 0.714 in left atrial appendage closure, 0.588 to 0.594 in STEMI, and 0.798 to 0.810 in endometrial cancer (pooled relative increase: 2.05% [95% CI 0.56-3.53]); the reweighted Elixhauser showed larger gains, particularly in STEMI (0.708 to 0.766) and left atrial appendage closure (0.780 to 0.818; pooled relative increase: 4.86% [0.07-9.65]). The Elixhauser reweighting demonstrated consistently larger gains for severe bleeding (pooled AUC increase: 6.57% [4.23-8.92]). For continuous outcomes, the reweighted Elixhauser index yielded the largest gains in…

articles.title: The Relationship Between Attitudes Toward Early Detection of Cervical Cancer, Religious Health Fatalism, and Hope levels in Women: A Cross-Sectional Study in Türkiye.
articles.authors: Özcan E
articles.abstract: A study was conducted on women's attitudes towards cervical cancer early detection with regard to dispositional hope and religious health fatalism. The study used a cross-sectional design. A total of 1635 female volunteers aged 18 years and older residing in Türkiye were included in the study, yielding a response rate of 95.6%. The data was gathered from December 2024 to January 2025. The personal information form, dispositional hope scale, religious health fatalism scale, and attitude scale for early detection of cervical cancer were used to gather data online. The analysis was done using IBM SPSS Statistics. It involved analysis of descriptive statistics, correlation tests, and multiple linear regression. The participants' mean age was 28.37 ± 8.94 years; 50.3% were unaware of the Pap smear test, and 77.3% had never been screened. Correlation analysis indicated a weak positive relationship between hope and religious fatalism, whereas attitudes toward early detection were negatively related to both hope and fatalism. Furthermore, participant characteristics (such as education, income, and Pap smear awareness) showed significant differences in study variables. In multiple regression controlling for these background characteristics, both dispositional hope (β = - 0.272, p < .001) and religious health fatalism (β = - 0.053, p = .024) significantly predicted attitudes toward early detection, explaining 11.2% of the variance in attitude scores. These findings suggest that early-detection behaviors may be improved by strengthening education and awareness interventions, while also addressing psychosocial dimensions such as hope and health fatalism in counseling and prevention strategies.

articles.title: Varicocele embolization using n-butyl cyanoacrylate glue: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Mac Curtain BM, Cronin P, Temperley HC et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Varicocele, a dilation of the pampiniform plexus, is a common and potentially reversible cause of male infertility, contributing to up to 50% of cases. Symptoms may include scrotal pain, heaviness, and cosmetic concerns. Percutaneous embolization is a minimally invasive treatment with high success rates. N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA)/N-butyl cyanoacrylate-methacryloxysulfolane (NBCA-MS) glue is increasingly utilized due to improved safety. This meta-analysis evaluates the technical and clinical success of NBCA/NBCA-MS embolization in varicocele-related disease.
METHODS: A systematic review and proportional meta-analysis was conducted per PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261332073). PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched up to March 4, 2026. Retrospective and prospective studies reporting NBCA/NBCA-MS embolization outcomes were included. Primary outcomes were technical and clinical success; secondary outcomes included recurrence. Proportions were pooled using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey transformation, and heterogeneity was assessed using I2.
RESULTS: Eleven studies (five prospective, six retrospective) composed of 548 patients (10 cohorts) were included for analysis. Technical success was 100% across nine studies, with recurrence (eight studies) reported at 1% (95% CI 0-5%; I2=72.35%), fertility improvement (three studies) at 68% (95% CI 0.51-0.83; I2=70.3%), and pain improvement (three studies) was found to be 97% (95% CI 0.75-1.00; I2=79.8%) across reported cohorts..
CONCLUSION: Overall, embolization studies reported high technical success and low recurrence rates, as well as high reported rates of fertility and pain improvement; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of contributing studies and substantial between-study heterogeneity.

articles.title: Navigating result disclosure in the context of reproductive genetic carrier screening: an interview study of genetic healthcare professionals in Belgium.
articles.authors: Goossens K, Borry P, Dimitriadou E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since 2019, reproductive partners in Belgium have been able to access a reproductive genetic carrier screening (RGCS) test that screens for more than 1,000 genes associated with autosomal recessive and X-linked conditions.
OBJECTIVE: This study explored Belgian genetic professionals' views on reporting individual versus couple-based results, as well as the management of additional findings (AFs) and variants of uncertain significance (VUSs) in the specific context of RGCS.
METHODS: Between December 2023 and April 2024, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 18 trained genetic professionals working across six Belgian Centers for Human Genetics, including clinical geneticists, genetic counsellors, and laboratory staff. Participants were predominantly female (n = 14/18) with a mean age of 44 years (range 30-61). All interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Most participants favored couple-based reporting and supported reporting AFs with clinical utility, while opposing the disclosure of VUSs. While views diverged on whether to use opt-in or opt-out approaches for reporting individual results, there was greater consensus on their application to AFs. Participants' perspectives were shaped by the perceived objectives of RGCS, the availability of qualitative pre-test counselling, and practical implementation considerations.
CONCLUSION: Our findings highlight broad support for current reporting practices in Belgium, while identifying remaining challenges such as the need to expand counselling capacity to ensure responsible and sustainable implementation of RGCS in Belgium.

articles.title: Chemical genetic screens combine target dependence with efficacy: discovery of a MAP3K1 degrader (HBC-8) with anticancer activities.
articles.authors: Umeta LT, Mallareddy JR, Singh S et al.
articles.abstract: Heterobifunctional compounds (HBCs) that facilitate target protein degradation (TPD) by recruiting an E3 ligase complex have emerged as therapeutic options for cancer. Current screening approaches often prioritize protein degradation over anticancer activity, potentially missing therapeutically relevant compounds. To address this, we developed a viability-based screening strategy using isogenic wild-type, MAP3K1-knockout, and CRBN-knockout cell lines to identify HBCs with target- and E3-ligase-dependent anticancer effects. This approach identified HBC-8, which is > 30-fold more potent than the parent MAP3K1 inhibitor and induces S-phase arrest, growth inhibition, and apoptosis in a MAP3K1- and CRBN-dependent manner. HBC-8 degrades MAP3K1; however, proteome-wide, genome-wide, and large-scale viability-based screens indicate that the anticancer activity of HBC-8 also relies on the disruption of the ubiquitin-proteasome system and protein translation machinery, extending beyond MAP3K1 degradation alone. Target dependence of HBC-8 was established using a large-scale viability screen in 869 cancer cell lines, and the anticancer effects correlated with the expression levels of the target (MAP3K1) and E3 ligase (CRBN). Furthermore, HBC-8 showed antitumor effects in an in vivo orthotopic ovarian cancer model without observable toxicity, supporting the use of isogenic cell lines for chemical genetic screens as a rapid, holistic approach to identify therapeutically relevant HBCs that also degrade the target protein.

articles.title: Moderate-to-late preterm birth, common respiratory pathogens, and severe lower respiratory tract infections across childhood.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Feng L, Yang Z et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Children born moderate-to-late preterm (MLP; 32 to < 37 weeks) are at increased risk of respiratory morbidity. We aimed to evaluate the association between MLP birth and the severity of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) across age groups, and to characterize interactions between MLP status and respiratory pathogens. This 11-year retrospective study included children hospitalized with LRTIs at Tongji Hospital, Wuhan. The primary outcome was a composite clinical severity measure. Stratified analyses were performed across infancy, early childhood, and middle childhood/early adolescence using multivariable modified Poisson regression models. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline covariates before comparing pathogen positivity rates. Additive interactions were quantified via relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) and attributable proportion (AP). Of 65,859 patients, 1,453 (2.21%) were born MLP. In the fully adjusted model, MLP birth was associated with an increased risk of composite severity outcomes (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] = 1.19, 95% CI 1.11, 1.28). In age-stratified analyses, the corresponding aRRs were 1.08 (95% CI 0.99, 1.17) in infants, 1.19 (95% CI 1.03, 1.38) in early childhood, and 1.42 (95% CI 1.16, 1.74) in middle childhood/early adolescence (p for interaction = 0.843). No significant differences were detected in pathogen positivity rates between matched MLP and full-term children. Notably, a significant synergistic additive interaction was identified between MLP status and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection (RERI = 0.37, 95% CI 0.10, 0.64; AP = 0.22, 95% CI 0.09, 0.35).
CONCLUSIONS: MLP birth is associated with severe LRTI outcomes that extend beyond infancy into early and middle childhood. Although no significant differences were detected in pathogen positivity rates between children born MLP and their full-term counterparts, MLP birth showed a significant synergistic additive interaction with RSV infection in relation to greater disease severity.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Moderate-to-late preterm (MLP) birth was associated with increased respiratory morbidity, with evidence primarily restricted to early infancy.
WHAT IS NEW: • The increased risk of severe lower respiratory tract infections associated with MLP birth extended beyond infancy into middle childhood, without a significant age-related effect modification. • Although no significant differences were detected in pathogen positivity…

articles.title: Methyl aminolevulinate-PpIX mediated fluorescence-guided mapping of high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: a pilot prospective clinical trial (PhotoDiVin).
articles.authors: Hejl L, Helle M, Leufflen L et al.
articles.abstract: The worldwide prevalence of vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is increasing and is characterized by the high risk of recurrence and evolution towards vulvar cancer. Positive margins following surgical excision are the most important criteria of recurrence risk. We conducted a pilot clinical study to assess the fluorescence-based cartography of VIN lesions using methyl aminolevulinate (m-ALA), which is a prodrug of the fluorophore protoporphyrin IX (PpIX). A prospective, single-center, single-arm clinical trial included 17 women with histologically confirmed high-grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (dVIN or vHSIL). Following topical methyl aminolevulinate application, fluorescence-guided examination under 405-nm light was performed. Targeted biopsies from fluorescent and non-fluorescent areas were compared with histopathology to assess concordance and the ability of fluorescence to accurately identify high-grade lesions. Among 34 biopsies, histopathological findings were concordant with fluorescence in 91% of cases. The procedure correctly identified intraepithelial neoplasia areas in 14 patients, yielding a success rate of 82% (95%CI 56-96%). Sensitivity and specificity were 93% (95%CI 68-100%) and 89% (95%CI 67-99%), respectively. The tolerance of the procedure was excellent with no pain and no side effects neither after cream application nor after illumination. This pilot study suggests that fluorescence imaging is a workable technique to mark VIN lesions with m-ALA cream. Further studies are needed to improve the reproducibility and ease of use of this method.

articles.title: Scaling up primary HPV DNA screening and self-sampling for cervical cancer in Peru: Coverage, cost-utility, and budget impact analysis using public data sources.
articles.authors: Vera-Ponce VJ, Ballena-Caicedo J, García-Rodríguez M et al.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesTo estimate cervical screening coverage and inequities among Peruvian women aged 30-49 years and evaluate lifetime cost-utility and 5-year budget impact of scaling up HPV DNA testing, including self-sampling.SettingPeru, using national ENDES (Demographic and Family Health Survey) data and public sources.MethodsWe linked a cross-sectional ENDES 2015-2024 analysis to a public-payer decision model. Up-to-date screening was Pap or visual inspection with acetic acid within 3 years, or molecular HPV testing within 5 years. A screening decision tree and lifetime state-transition (Markov) model compared current practice with HPV self-sampling, clinician-collected testing, and hybrid expansion. We estimated costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), sequential incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), probabilistic optimality, and budget impact at S/ 25,007 (Peruvian soles) / QALY.ResultsIn 2024, 63.6% were up to date, 36.4% underscreened, 15.0% never screened, and 12.9% reported recent molecular HPV testing. The efficiency frontier was current practice, hybrid expansion to 90%, and clinician-collected HPV testing at 90%; sequential ICERs were S/ 5434 and S/ 10,982/QALY. In 5000 simulations, clinician-collected 90%, self-sampling 90%, and hybrid 90% had optimal-strategy probabilities of 69.46%, 15.46%, and 13.38%. Annualized budget impact was S/ 24.44 million for hybrid 90% and S/ 67.17 million for clinician-collected 90%.ConclusionsClinician-collected HPV testing at 90% maximized expected net monetary benefit under modeled assumptions, while hybrid expansion required less short-term expenditure. Policy should balance lifetime efficiency, feasibility, affordability, and linkage to diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Diagnostic performances and longitudinal trajectories of gene expression profiling and donor-derived cell-free DNA in pediatric kidney transplant recipients with rejection.
articles.authors: Kizilbash S, Sebastian A, Jensen C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely diagnosis of allograft rejection is crucial for preventing premature graft loss. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of blood gene expression profile (GEP) and donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) in detecting rejection in pediatric kidney transplant recipients.
METHODS: We prospectively recruited pediatric kidney transplant recipients (<21 years) who underwent a for-cause biopsy (August 20, 2023-February 6, 2025). Blood samples for GEP and dd-cfDNA were collected at biopsy (week 0) and at weeks 4 and 8. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize cohort characteristics. Diagnostic accuracy of biomarkers (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value [PPV], and negative predictive value [NPV]) was calculated against the gold-standard biopsy.
RESULTS: Our pilot study included 27 biopsies performed in 23 recipients. The median age of participants was 6.1 (IQR: 3.9, 13.7) years; 55.6% were male, and 92.6% were white. At week 0, GEP detected rejection with 40.0% sensitivity, 82.0% specificity, 57.0% PPV, and 70.0% NPV. A GEP score >0.4 yielded higher sensitivity (86% vs. 43%) and NPV (80% vs. 67%) compared to a score >0.5. Using a dd-cfDNA threshold of >1.0%, dual-positivity (positive dd-cfDNA and GEP) yielded a 33.0% sensitivity, 94.0% specificity, 75.0% PPV, and 73.0% NPV. Overall, the combined AUC of dd-cfDNA and GEP probability scores was 0.62 (95% CI, 0.31-0.93). Unlike serum creatinine, GEP probability scores and dd-cfDNA trended toward quiescent levels on serial assessment.
CONCLUSION: Combining GEP and dd-cfDNA improved their diagnostic performance. GEP and dd-cfDNA levels showed a downward trend after rejection treatment initiation.

articles.title: RPL22 suppresses tumor growth in undifferentiated/dedifferentiated endometrial carcinoma through IFIT3 downregulation.
articles.authors: Chao A, Lin CY, Tang WJ et al.
articles.abstract: Undifferentiated/dedifferentiated endometrial carcinoma (UDEC) represents a rare but aggressive subtype of endometrial cancer characterized by chemoresistance. Notably, a considerable proportion of patients with UDEC who exhibit mismatch repair deficiency respond favorably to immunotherapy. Here, we identified mutations in the ribosomal protein L22 (RPL22) gene in 42% (11/26) of UDEC samples - which occurred predominantly in mismatch repair-deficient tumors. Functionally, we demonstrated that RPL22 increased the sensitivity of UDEC cells to cisplatin and lenvatinib, while promoting T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity in the presence of combined lenvatinib and pembrolizumab. RNA sequencing revealed that RPL22 overexpression in UDEC cells downregulated interferon signaling pathways, including interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 3 (IFIT3). Further analyses supported a potential regulatory relationship between RPL22, IFIT3, and JAK/STAT1 signaling. In xenograft experiments, RPL22 overexpression reduced tumor growth, and concurrent IFIT3 overexpression attenuated this suppressive effect at the final time point. Collectively, these findings identify RPL22 as a potential regulator of drug sensitivity and immune responses in UDEC. We propose that the RPL22-IFIT3-JAK/STAT1 axis may offer opportunities for developing personalized therapeutic strategies in UDEC.

articles.title: Validation of the Turkish version of the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Overactive Bladder.
articles.authors: Tas IS, Evruke I, Ulusoy HE et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The aim was to enable the use of International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire Overactive Bladder (ICIQ-OAB) module in Turkish-speaking women, questionnaires were translated into Turkish, and validity, reliability, and sensitivity to change were evaluated in women suffering from overactive bladder syndrome.
METHODS: After obtaining permission from the ICIQ Advisory Board, the English version of the questionnaire was translated into Turkish, back-translated into English, and subsequently modified in accordance with the Board's recommendations. Pilot testing was then conducted with 10 women, after which validity (content/face validity and discriminant validity), reliability (test-retest reliability and internal consistency), and sensitivity to change were evaluated.
RESULTS: This study included 92 women (47 with overactive bladder and 45 controls) who applied to the urogynecology outpatient clinic. All women completed the same questionnaire 15 days later. More than 90% of women found the questions clear, unequivocal, and comprehensive. Missing data constituted less than 1%, indicating adequate content/face validity. Cronbach's α coefficient for this questionnaire was 0.73, which indicates adequate internal consistency. The intraclass correlation coefficient and the kappa values for individual items were > 0.7, indicating adequate test-retest reliability. Symptomatic and asymptomatic women's questionnaires were compared using the area under the ROC curves for discriminant validity, which showed good discriminant validity. Thirty-nine women in the symptomatic group were treated, and the results after 3 months of treatment were analyzed for sensitivity to change. The questionnaire showed a significant improvement in correlation with pre- and post-treatment bladder diary results, indicating good sensitivity to change.
CONCLUSIONS: The Turkish version of the ICIQ-OAB demonstrated strong validity and reliability, supporting its use among Turkish-speaking women worldwide in both clinical and research settings.

articles.title: Does blastocyst transfer have a higher live birth rate than cleavage-stage embryo transfer in patients with delayed in vitro blastocyst development?
articles.journal: Journal of assisted reproduction and genetics
articles.authors: Gao J, Li H, Li X et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: When embryo cohorts exhibit delayed blastocyst development, with only slow-developing day 6 (D6) blastocysts available for transfer, does blastocyst transfer achieve a higher live birth rate (LBR) than cleavage-stage embryo transfer?
METHODS: A modified blastocyst culture strategy was applied in freeze-all cycles. Specifically, one or two good-quality embryos were cryopreserved on day 3 (D3) as a backup, while an equal or greater number of good-quality embryos were cultured to the blastocyst stage. Among freeze-all patients managed with this strategy, 275 patients were identified who had only D6 blastocysts available for transfer, with no transferable day 5 (D5) blastocysts following extended in vitro culture. Cumulative LBR after one oocyte retrieval over 2 years and pregnancy outcomes in the first frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET) cycles were compared between groups with priority transfer of backup D3 cleavage-stage embryos versus top-graded D6 blastocysts.
RESULTS: The cumulative LBR was not significantly different between the group with priority transfer of backup cryopreserved D3 embryos and the group with priority transfer of top-quality D6 blastocysts [50.6% vs. 48.4%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 0.759; 95% CI, 0.384-1.499; p = 0.427]. In the first FET cycles, transfer of top-graded D6 blastocysts did not yield a higher LBR compared with transfer of backup cryopreserved D3 embryos [36.3% vs. 43.5%; aOR, 0.601; 95% CI, 0.299-1.208; p = 0.153]. Subgroup analyses showed no significant differences in LBR between the two groups following either single embryo/blastocyst transfer (SET/SBT) (37.0% vs. 36.4%; aOR, 0.922; 95% CI, 0.234-3.634; p = 0.907) or double embryo/blastocyst transfer (DET/DBT) (35.4% vs. 44.6%; aOR, 0.493; 95% CI, 0.213-1.138; p = 0.097). No statistically significant differences were observed in clinical pregnancy rate, obstetric complications, or neonatal outcomes between the two groups in the first FET cycles.
CONCLUSIONS: When embryo cohorts exhibit delayed development at the blastocyst stage, blastocyst transfer does not result in a higher LBR and therefore may not confer an advantage in achieving live birth sooner compared with the transfer of good-quality cleavage-stage embryos.

articles.title: The Experience of Urinary Incontinence and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms on Work Participation: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Verbeek M, Bye R, Strassmeir L et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Urinary incontinence (UI) and lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are largely invisible to others. Managing these conditions can restrict participation in life roles, particularly those involving community life, such as participating in work occupations. The purpose was to describe existing and emerging evidence on the experience of UI/LUTS on participation in work.
METHOD: A scoping review, using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology, was conducted. Six academic databases plus supplementary web-based search engines were systematically searched to locate evidence. Records describing the experience of UI/LUTS on work participation, available in English and full text, published in or after 2002 were included.
RESULTS: The review included 39 records. Most evidence collected data via self-report on quantitative instruments measuring the impact of UI/LUTS on work participation, revealing sparse research exploring the experience in work of individuals with UI/LUTS using qualitative methodologies. UI/LUTS limited work participation for individuals of all ages, and sex. Individuals with increased UI/LUTS severity reported greater cognitive, physical and psychosocial impacts on work participation. UI/LUTS were exacerbated by job type, specific work activities, inflexible work scheduling, and workplace design, for example, restricted bathroom access, breaks, or relief workers. Individuals with UI/LUTS employed varied management strategies including delayed voiding, fluid restriction, and wearing incontinence products at work.
CONCLUSION: UI/LUTS impacts work participation with the burden for managing symptoms falling heavily on individuals. A deeper understanding of the impact on work from individuals living with UI/LUTS is needed to guide practice, design, and policies to increase inclusion and participation.

articles.title: Combining Quantitative Measurement Tools with Theoretical Frameworks to Examine Structural Determinants on Reproductive Decision Making Among African American Women.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.authors: Strickland Denson JD
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Racial disparities in sexual and reproductive health are an ongoing injustice in the US, affecting pregnancy and maternal and infant health. This exploratory study sought to use Intersectionality and Critical Race Theory as theoretical frameworks to examine a sample of African American women's experiences with trauma, stress, depression, discrimination, and reproductive decision-making, and to examine their experiences relative to income level.
METHODS: This cross-sectional community survey study included African American women from lower and higher income strata and compared their scores in key measures of mental health and discrimination: Adverse Childhood Experiences Questionnaire (ACE), the Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2), the Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10), and the Everyday Discrimination Scale (EDS), and their experiences with pregnancy and birth control and demographic data collected from the Family Planning Study of African American Women (FPSAAW) questionnaire used in this study.
RESULTS: The mean ACE, PHQ-2, and PSS-10 scores were higher for the lower income group, and the EDS mean score was higher for the higher income group, though none of these differences reached between-group statistical significance. The FPSAAW found non-significant differences in contraceptive preferences and use and decision-making agency between income groups.
CONCLUSIONS: African American women's reproductive decisions are shaped by the intersection of micro-level and macro-level factors. Examining context, including mental health history, discrimination, and the intersection of their identities and social context provides important insight for reproductive planning. It is necessary to examine the needs of African American women using theoretical frameworks that center their experiences, particularly related to their mental health and reproductive health care.

articles.title: Obesity and perioperative outcomes of robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Gong J, Zhang M, Chen Y et al.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer in obese versus non-obese patients, as classified in the source studies. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for comparative studies of robotic-assisted surgery for endometrial cancer. Obesity was defined as BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² according to each study. The included data were not uniformly restricted to BMI < 40 kg/m²; consequently, the analysis does not represent class I-II obesity alone. Eight retrospective studies involving 1,879 patients were included. No statistically significant differences were detected in operative time (MD, - 9.02 min; 95% CI, - 21.25 to 3.20; p = 0.15), estimated blood loss (MD, 35.69 mL; 95% CI, - 40.54 to 111.93; p = 0.36), or length of stay (MD, - 0.25 days; 95% CI, - 0.61 to 0.10; p = 0.16). Pooled complication estimates were also nonsignificant. These findings do not establish equivalent safety. In the included retrospective studies, obesity as classified by the original reports was not associated with statistically significant differences in the assessed perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted surgery. The estimates are imprecise and potentially confounded; they do not establish equivalence or demonstrate superiority over other surgical approaches.

articles.title: TP-PCR combined with long-read sequencing for screening of fragile X syndrome carriers.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.authors: Yujiao C, Shanshan L, Meng Z et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To accurately screen Fragile X syndrome (FXS) carriers during pregnancy, number of CGG repeats for full mutation (FM), low-proportion mosaicism, the presence of AGG interruptions, and microdeletions were identified.
METHODS: Long-read sequencing (LRS) was developed and evaluated premutation (PM) by comparing to triplet repeat-primed PCR (TP-PCR). In the follow-up, pregnancy outcomes in carrying FMR1 expanded alleles and the screening of their newborn offspring were inquired.
RESULTS: The results showed that LRS could accurately detect CGG repeats in clinical samples (blood and amniotic fluid samples) with premutation (PM). Furthermore, LRS could directly determine that mosaicism in FXS (29/48/77 repeats), offering a mosaicism ratio of 3%. The results of CGG repeats of FMR1 by LRS demonstrated that a history of infertility had PM alleles (29/71 repeats). In addition, LRS demonstrated a 71 bp deletion exon 1 of FMR1 in carrying PM, whereas CGG repeats was lower than 0 via detecting by TP-PCR.
CONCLUSION: Our study provides the first evidence of low-proportion mosaicism and microdeletion via LRS method, which may prove to be an option for the additional cases of FXS during pregnancy.

articles.title: Women's health in osteogenesis Imperfecta: a scoping review.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.authors: Amstrup AK, Folkestad L, Gregersen PA et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI) is a group of connective tissue disorders most often caused by quantitative or qualitative changes in type I collagen. The clinical phenotype is heterogeneous. Women's health in OI has been very sparsely investigated, and whether periods of skeletal stress throughout adulthood come with an increased risk of fractures and other complications due to OI is unknown. The present review covers the current literature on menarche, pregnancy and menopause, and periods of skeletal stress in women with OI.
METHODS: Over 1300 articles published between 1967 and 2026 were identified and screened for relevance.
