RESULTS: The literature suggests that the age of menarche reflects the general population. Fertility may be preserved - especially in the milder affected phenotypes. Most pregnancies are successful; however, data suggest that they may be associated with a higher risk of complications and fractures compared to the general population. Likewise, caesarean section is chosen more frequently in women with OI compared to the general population. Menopause is sparsely described, and it has not been investigated whether the consequences of and symptoms associated with menopause are different in women with OI compared to the general population. The current evidence is often limited by small study size and OI subtypes.
CONCLUSION: Overall, the evidence to guide clinicians in monitoring and treatment of women's health in OI is limited, and more studies are needed. As women with OI present as a very heterogeneous group, managing pregnancy and menopause requires individualized monitoring with focus on known complications.

articles.title: A randomized phase III study optimizing adjuvant osimertinib for resected EGFR-mutant stage II-III non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer: OASIS trial (JACTOP-01).
articles.authors: Onodera K, Okada Y, Kudo Y et al.
articles.abstract: The OASIS trial [Japan Cancer Treatment Optimization group (JACTOP)-01] is a multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase III study optimizing adjuvant osimertinib therapy for patients with completely resected, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated (exon 19 deletion or L858R) stage II-III non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer. Based on the ADAURA trial, the standard adjuvant dose of osimertinib is 80 mg/day, which often causes significant adverse events and financial toxicity. This trial evaluates the non-inferiority of a reduced dose of 40 mg/day of osimertinib compared to the standard 80 mg/day. A total of 420 patients will be randomized (1:1) to receive either osimertinib 80 or 40 mg/day orally for 3 years. The primary endpoint is disease-free survival. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, central nervous system disease-free survival, safety, and quality of life. If non-inferiority is confirmed, osimertinib 40 mg/day will establish a new optimal adjuvant strategy, improving patient quality of life and reducing medical economic burdens.

articles.title: A Feasibility Trial Examining Acupressure Wristbands in Ambulatory Surgery Patients at Risk for Post-Discharge Nausea and Vomiting.
articles.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
articles.authors: Tagami A, Henry S, McGillion M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (NV) can lead to complications like pain and bleeding. In ambulatory surgery patients, post-discharge NV impacts 40% to 80% of patients undergoing laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy (LAVH). Pericardium 6 (PC6) acupressure may prevent postoperative NV in hospital, but little is known regarding its effect on post-discharge NV. The purpose of this study was to examine the feasibility of a trial to test the effects of bilateral PC6 acupressure wristbands plus usual care versus placebo plus usual care on post-discharge NV.
DESIGN: A parallel-arm feasibility randomized controlled trial was employed.
METHODS: Primary outcomes included rates of consent, randomization, intervention/placebo delivery, continuous wristband wear, and retention. Twenty participants undergoing ambulatory LAVH were randomized to either a) usual post-discharge NV care plus bilateral PC6 acupressure wristbands, or b) usual care with bilateral placebo wristbands. Wristbands were placed on arrival to the recovery room and worn until 24 hours after discharge. Follow-up calls were made to gather outcome data.
FINDINGS: Three a priori criteria for feasibility success were met: rates of randomization, continuous wear, and retention.
CONCLUSIONS: It was feasible to conduct a trial where a registered nurse delivered acupressure wristbands versus placebo wristbands to patients in the recovery room following LAVH under general anesthesia. Post-discharge symptom management is an important component of nursing practice. If acupressure wristbands are found to be effective at preventing post-discharge NV in larger trials, registered nurses are well-positioned to educate patients about a cost-effective intervention with minimal risk of side effects.

articles.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Pretreatment Evaluation and Follow-Up of Endometrial Cancer: 2026 Update.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
articles.authors: Expert Panel on GYN and OB Imaging, Sertic M, Venkatesan AM et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecologic malignancy in the United States, and accurate pretreatment evaluation is essential for risk stratification, treatment planning, and detection of recurrent disease. This evidence-based review summarizes imaging recommendations for patients with established endometrial cancer undergoing pretreatment assessment, surveillance, or evaluation for suspected recurrence. MRI pelvis without and with intravenous contrast is usually appropriate for assessment of local tumor extension across histologic subtypes and grades. For aggressive histologic tumor types, or when metastatic disease is suspected, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous contrast and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for evaluation of nodal and distant metastases. Routine imaging surveillance is usually not appropriate for asymptomatic patients with treated low- or intermediate-risk disease, whereas CT may be appropriate in selected asymptomatic high-risk patients. MRI pelvis, CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and FDG-PET/CT are usually appropriate for suspected recurrence. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision process support the systematic analysis of the medical literature from peer reviewed journals. Established methodology principles such as Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE are adapted to evaluate the evidence. The RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method User Manual provides the methodology to determine the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where peer reviewed literature is lacking or equivocal, experts may be the primary evidentiary source available to formulate a recommendation.

articles.title: Preterm Birth and Birth Weight and Cognitive Performance Among Males Eligible for Military Service.
articles.authors: Perälä J, Möttönen J, De Luca D et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Preterm birth and low birth weight are associated with adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in childhood, but their association with cognitive performance in young adulthood remains incompletely characterized at the population level.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether gestational age and birth weight are associated with cognitive performance during compulsory military service in young adult males.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide retrospective register-based cohort study included males born in Finland between January 1, 1987, and December 31, 1998 (N = 350 617), identified using linked national health and military registers. The dataset was based on cognitive testing conducted during military service at a mean age of 19 to 20 years. Preconscription deaths and individuals without military cognitive testing data were excluded. Data analysis was performed from June 1 to December 31, 2025.
EXPOSURES: Gestational age at birth and birth weight.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Cognitive performance was measured using the Finnish Defense Forces' cognitive basic test 1, consisting of verbal, numerical, and visuospatial subtests. Scores were standardized on a 9-point scale (mean [SD], 5.00 [1.96]), with the overall score calculated as the mean of the 3 subtests.
RESULTS: A total of 192 767 participants were included, of whom 10 016 (5.2%) were born preterm. Individuals born extremely preterm scored lower on the overall cognitive test compared with full-term individuals (mean difference, -0.78 [95% CI, -1.07 to -0.49] points). The groups born very preterm and moderately preterm showed progressively smaller deficits, while those born late preterm showed minimal differences compared with their peers born full term. Associations reached a plateau at approximately 36 to 38 gestational weeks. Similar dose-response associations were observed across birth weight categories, with individuals with extremely low birth weight scoring 0.89 (95% CI, -1.23 to -0.55) points lower than those with normal birth weight. Differences were most pronounced in visuospatial and numerical subtests, whereas verbal performance showed little or no association with gestational age or birth weight.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Lower gestational age and birth weight were associated with poorer cognitive performance in young adulthood in a dose-response pattern, with the largest differences observed among individuals born extremely preterm and with very low birth weight. Late…

articles.title: Evaluating cervical length as a predictor of preterm labour in women with congenital uterine anomalies - an observational study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.authors: Kadam N, Raouf S, Jones NW et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with congenital uterine anomalies (CUA) are at increased risk for spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB). Cervical length surveillance is commonly used to identify cervical shortening as a predictor of sPTB. However, evidence supporting its predictive value in women with CUA remains limited. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of cervical length surveillance in predicting sPTB in women with CUA.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included women with CUA diagnosed on imaging who attended the preterm birth prevention clinic between 2020 and 2024. Singleton pregnancies without additional risk factors for sPTB were included. Cervical length was measured by transvaginal ultrasound between 16 and 24 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was sPTB before 37 weeks' gestation. Logistic regression analysis and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to assess the association between cervical length and sPTB and its predictive value.
RESULTS: Of 502 women referred to the preterm birth prevention clinic, 49 had CUA as their only risk factor for preterm birth. Five women (10.2%) experienced sPTB, and all had normal cervical length measurements. Cervical shortening (<25 mm) was identified in only one woman (2.0%), who subsequently delivered at term following cervical cerclage insertion. The prevalence of sPTB was highest among women with a unicornuate uterus (33.3%), followed by those with a septate uterus (11.1%) and a bicornuate uterus (9.1%). Logistic regression analysis demonstrated no association between cervical length and sPTB (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.78-1.19; p = 0.75). ROC curve analysis showed poor predictive performance (AUC 0.57, 95% CI 0.31-0.84).
CONCLUSION: While cervical length surveillance showed limited predictive value of sPTB in this cohort, the low incidence of cervical shortening precludes definitive conclusions. Larger prospective studies are required to clarify the role of cervical length surveillance in this high-risk group.

articles.title: Ultrasonography (IOTA-ADNEX) vs magnetic resonance imaging (ADNEX MR) for diagnosing ovarian cancer in high-risk patients: a prospective study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Dueholm Hjorth IM, Ledger A, Møller C et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To systematically validate and compare ultrasonography, using the ultrasound-based International Ovarian Tumor Analysis - Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (IOTA-ADNEX) model, with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), using the MRI-based ADNEX MR scoring system, as second-line imaging modalities for estimating the risk of adnexal malignancy in patients identified as being at risk of malignancy on first-line ultrasound examination.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-center diagnostic accuracy study designed as a head-to-head comparison. All patients referred to a tertiary referral center at Aarhus University Hospital, Aarhus, Denmark, for suspected adnexal malignancy on first-line imaging between May 2021 and December 2022 were offered second-line diagnostic testing. This comprised both a systematic expert ultrasound examination, including IOTA-ADNEX risk estimation, and a systematic MRI scan with ADNEX MR scores assigned by expert radiologists. The imaging assessments were performed prospectively, with ultrasound examiners and radiologists blinded to the results of other imaging modalities and to the reference standard (tumor outcome). The reference standard was a histopathological diagnosis of the primary adnexal mass or, in a small number of cases, clinical follow-up. Borderline tumors, invasive adnexal malignancy and metastases to the adnexa were grouped as malignancies. Diagnostic performance of the IOTA-ADNEX model, ADNEX MR scoring system and CA 125 for predicting malignancy was evaluated using the area under the receiver-operating-characteristics curve (AUC), and AUCs were compared using DeLong's test. Diagnostic metrics were estimated at clinically relevant cut-offs and scores. Agreement between modalities was assessed for the identification of morphological features and overall risk estimation using Cohen's kappa statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman plots. For the IOTA-ADNEX model, calibration and the ability to discriminate between tumor subtypes were evaluated.
RESULTS: The included cohort comprised 342 patients (342 lesions analyzed). In the final cohort, 78.1% of patients were postmenopausal and the overall prevalence of malignancy was 58.8%. The AUC for distinguishing patients with benign tumors from those with malignant tumors was 0.96 (95% CI, 0.94-0.98) for the IOTA-ADNEX model (with or without CA 125) compared with an AUC of 0.93 (95% CI, 0.91-0.96) for ADNEX MR. Agreement…

articles.title: Impaired NK Cell-Mediated Tumor Surveillance in Atherosclerosis Due to Plaque-Induced PPARα Dysfunction.
articles.authors: Ren T, Yu S, Jiang X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis is frequently associated with both an increased incidence and accelerated development of cancer. However, the impact of atherosclerosis progression on the efficacy of tumor surveillance by cytotoxic immune cells, particularly natural killer (NK) cells, remains poorly understood. This study aims to explore how atherosclerosis affects NK cell-mediated tumor surveillance in both animal models and humans.
METHODS: We analyzed peripheral blood NK cells from patients with atherosclerosis with early-stage (<50% stenosis) versus advanced-stage (≥50% stenosis) coronary artery lesions by flow cytometry to assess NK cell frequency, PPARα (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha) expression, and IFN-γ (interferon gamma) production. In parallel, we used atherosclerotic plaque progression and regression models, including high-fat diet-fed Apo-/- mice and aortic arch transplantation into wild-type, Apoe-/-, Rag1-/-, and NK cell-specific PPARα knockout (Pparaflox/flox Ncr1Cre/+) mice. NK cell phenotype and function were evaluated by flow cytometry for immune checkpoint molecules (PD-1 [programmed cell death protein-1], TIM-3 [T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3], LAG-3 [lymphocyte activation gene-3], and TIGIT [T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain]) and effector cytokines (IFN-γ, GZMB [granzyme B]). Antitumor capacity was assessed in B16F10 melanoma and ID8 ovarian cancer models in atherosclerosis mice, with or without a PPARα agonist (oleoylethanolamide) or an mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin kinase) agonist (MHY1485) treatment. Mechanistic studies included immunoblotting for mTOR pathway components and transcriptomic correlation analyses (GSE94044, GSE24495).
RESULTS: We found that atherosclerotic plaques induced PPARα deficiency in NK cells, which impaired their cytotoxicity and weakened tumor immunosurveillance. Mechanistically, PPARα-deficient NK cells exhibited elevated immune checkpoint expression, an exhaustion phenotype, and markedly diminished mTOR signaling. Administration of the PPARα agonist oleoylethanolamide restored NK cell effector function and enhanced tumor-killing efficacy in vivo, whereas mTOR agonism partially rescued the defect caused by PPARα loss. These findings underscore the suppressive effects of arterial plaques on NK cell-mediated antitumor immunity and suggest PPARα compensation as a potential immunotherapeutic strategy.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study unveils a novel association between…

articles.title: Application of protein metabolism and nutritional intervention combined with lower segment circular suture in the treatment of placental caesarean section.
articles.authors: Chen W, Sun S
articles.abstract: Background: Perioperative protein metabolism disorder is the core pathophysiological change in patients with postpartum haemorrhage after caesarean section with placenta previa. Purpose: Protein metabolism nutrition intervention, as a core nutritional support strategy during the perioperative period of obstetrics, can provide systemic metabolic support for surgical hemostasis and postoperative recovery by regulating protein metabolism. Results: The results showed that protein metabolism and nutritional intervention established a stable metabolic foundation for both groups of patients. The observation group had significantly lower intraoperative bleeding volume, hemostasis time, hospitalisation costs, and hospitalisation time compared to the control group. The hemostasis effective rate (95.5%) was significantly higher than that of the control group (70.6%); Conclusion: The combination of the new surgical hemostasis scheme has a definite haemostatic effect, can reduce bleeding volume and transfusion requirements, shorten hospitalisation time, reduce medical costs, and has good safety. It is worthy of clinical promotion and application.

articles.title: Pregnancy considerations in women with uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Bhardwaj A, Balachandran DM, Vasudev I
articles.abstract: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, accounting for approximately 7-10% of all congenital cardiac malformations. Although early surgical repair has transformed its natural history in high-income settings, with contemporary long-term survival exceeding 90%, uncorrected TOF continues to be encountered in pregnancy, particularly in women from resource-limited regions or those with previously undiagnosed disease. The physiological adaptations of pregnancy, including reduction in systemic vascular resistance, plasma volume expansion, and a 30-50% rise in cardiac output, are poorly tolerated in the presence of a non-restrictive ventricular septal defect and fixed right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, leading to progressive cyanosis, right ventricular strain, and uteroplacental hypoperfusion. Current European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidance classifies unrepaired cyanotic heart disease without Eisenmenger syndrome as mWHO 2.0 class III, while Eisenmenger syndrome is classified as mWHO 2.0 class IV. Contemporary data from the ESC EORP Registry of Pregnancy and Cardiac Disease (ROPAC) report maternal mortality of 0.7% and heart failure in 8.7% of pregnancies with uncorrected congenital heart disease, with markedly worse outcomes in cyanotic subsets. This narrative review synthesizes the pathophysiology, risk stratification, obstetric management, intrapartum anesthetic considerations, comparative outcomes of uncorrected versus corrected disease, and key evidence gaps that continue to constrain care for this population, providing a physiology-driven framework for the pregnancy heart team.

articles.title: The gut-ovary axis in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Mechanisms, microbiome dysbiosis, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Debnath D
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently termed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), is a heterogeneous endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by reproductive, metabolic, and hormonal disturbances. Increasing evidence suggests that interactions between the gut microbiota and host physiology may be relevant to PMOS through pathways involving intestinal barrier function, inflammation, insulin sensitivity, steroid hormone metabolism, bile acid signaling, and gut-brain-ovary communication. This narrative review synthesizes current human and preclinical evidence on the gut-ovary axis in PMOS, with particular emphasis on microbial dysbiosis, proposed mechanistic pathways, microbiome-related metabolic and endocrine interactions, and emerging therapeutic approaches. Human studies generally report associations between altered microbial composition and metabolic or reproductive features of PMOS, although findings vary considerably according to population characteristics, bodyweight, diagnostic criteria, sequencing methods, and analytical approaches. Experimental studies provide additional support for potential roles of microbial metabolites, intestinal permeability, immune signaling, and metabolic pathways, but these mechanisms have not been established as causal in humans. Microbiome-targeted interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and dietary approaches, show potential, whereas fecal microbiota transplantation remains largely experimental. Conventional metabolic therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, should be considered separately from microbiome-targeted approaches. Overall, the gut-ovary axis represents a promising framework for understanding the systemic features of PMOS, but substantial heterogeneity, limited longitudinal human evidence, and underrepresentation of diverse populations currently limit translation into clinical practice.

articles.title: Association of fetal epicardial fat thickness with adverse perinatal outcomes and assessment of fetal cardiac function in fetal growth restriction.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Ozturk Agaoglu M, Bozkurt Ozdal B, Reyhan Toptas G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigates the association between fetal epicardial fat thickness (EFT) and adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies complicated by fetal growth restriction (FGR), and assesses changes in fetal cardiac function.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center, prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary referral hospital. A total of 120 pregnancies between 28 and 37 weeks of gestation were enrolled: 40 with FGR and 80 healthy controls. EFT, fetal cardiac function parameters, and perinatal outcomes were compared between the FGR and control groups, and the same parameters were compared between the early-onset and late-onset FGR subgroups. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the ability of EFT to discriminate composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO).
RESULTS: Epicardial fat thickness was significantly lower in the FGR group than in controls (P < 0.001). Among fetal cardiac function parameters, the modified myocardial performance index (Mod-MPI) and isovolumetric relaxation time were significantly higher in the FGR group (P = 0.002 and P = 0.001, respectively), whereas ejection time was significantly shorter (P = 0.013). EFT was significantly lower in early-onset than in late-onset FGR (P < 0.001). Mod-MPI and isovolumetric contraction time were significantly higher in early-onset FGR (P < 0.05 for both). The rate of CAPO was higher in the FGR group (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, reduced EFT was associated with FGR and with impaired fetal cardiac function. EFT is a simple, non-invasive parameter that might help identify FGR pregnancies at increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes; however, larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and to validate the proposed cut-off value.

articles.title: Serum sex hormone and triglyceride-glucose index in postmenopausal women: A population-based study from NHANES.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Gu H, Liu J, Zhao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The association between sex hormones and insulin resistance (IR) in postmenopausal women remains unclear. This study investigated the association between sex hormones and the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG).
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) during the 2013-2016 cycles. The associations of log2-transformed estradiol, total testosterone, bioavailable testosterone, total testosterone-to-estradiol ratio, and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) with TyG were evaluated and verified by weighted linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 474 postmenopausal women with complete laboratory data for sex hormones and TyG calculation were included. After full adjustment for prespecified covariates, only SHBG showed an independent association with the TyG index when sex-hormone indicators were modeled continuously: a log2-unit rise in SHBG predicted lower TyG (β = -0.25, P < 0.001), whereas other sex hormones had no significant independent associations. When modeled as tertiles, SHBG remained negatively associated with TyG (P for trend <0.001), while bioavailable testosterone showed a positive association (P for trend = 0.020). RCS analyses confirmed a linear association for SHBG (P overall <0.001, P nonlinear = 0.852) and a nonlinear association for bioavailable testosterone (P overall = 0.008, P nonlinear = 0.010). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses further validated these findings across multiple covariates.
CONCLUSION: SHBG and bioavailable testosterone were associated with IR among postmenopausal women in this cross-sectional study. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.

articles.title: Comparison of self-sampling versus clinician-sampling HPV DNA cervical cancer screening in South African women living with and without HIV.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Snyman LC, Visser C, Dreyer GJ et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Human papilloma virus (HPV) testing is the preferred primary screening method for cervical cancer, and HPV self-sampling has the potential to improve screening uptake. We compared the test performance and agreement of self- and clinician-sampling HPV in women living with HIV (WLWH) and HIV-negative women in Gauteng and Western Cape Province, South Africa.
METHODS: Cervical cancer screening was performed in previously unscreened women using cytology, self- and clinician-collected HPV (Hybrid Capture 2 assay). Screen-positive participants underwent colposcopy and biopsy, and a random sample of negative screens had punch biopsy regardless of colposcopy findings. Performances of screening tests were evaluated against histology results adjusted for verification bias. The kappa statistic for HPV concordance between self- and clinician-collected HPV was also calculated.
RESULTS: Included for analysis were 903 women with a mean age of 41.5 years, of which 43.3% were WLWH. In WLWH/HIV-negative women, the sensitivity of self-sampling HPV was 74.7%/67.4% and of clinician-sampling HPV was 77.1%/59.2% to detect cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade3+, whereas the specificity for clinician-sampling HPV was 75.0%/86.8% compared with 70.3%/79.8% for self-sampling HPV to detect CIN2+. In both HIV groups, Cohen's kappa agreement between the two sampling methods was good (0.63 and 0.62, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Self-collected HPV sampling is an acceptable and viable option for primary cervical cancer screening in all women given the superior sensitivity to cytology. The statistically significant difference in HPV test performance among HIV-negative women according to sampling method confirms the benefit of a further triage test when self-sampling is used for HPV-base cervical screening, especially in HIV-negative women.

articles.title: Maternal nutritional screening and risk of small-for-gestational-age birth in Vietnamese pregnancies: A prospective comparison of the FIGO nutrition checklist, pre-pregnancy BMI, and mid-upper arm circumference.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Nguyen TTL, Nguyen PT, Pham VA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vietnam bears a substantial burden of small-for-gestational-age (SGA) births, contributing to neonatal mortality, stunting, and long-term developmental impairment. In Southeast Asia, practical nutritional screening tools that predict objectively defined neonatal growth outcomes are poorly evaluated. We aimed to compare the predictive validity of the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) Nutrition Checklist, pre-pregnancy body mass index, and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) for SGA birth outcomes in pregnant Vietnamese women and to identify the FIGO checklist items most strongly associated with distinct SGA phenotypes.
METHODS: In this hospital-based cross-sectional study with prospective ascertainment of neonatal outcomes, 818 mother-newborn pairs were enrolled at a national tertiary obstetric center in Hanoi, Vietnam, between June and December 2024. FIGO score (0-9), pre-pregnancy body mass index, and MUAC were assessed at the antenatal birth registration visit (mean gestational age 36.1 weeks). SGA-weight and SGA-length were classified independently as birth weight or birth length below the sex- and gestational-age-specific 10th percentile using INTERGROWTH-21st Newborn Size Standards. Predictive performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with DeLong pairwise comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression with bootstrap confidence intervals (1000 resamples).
RESULTS: SGA-weight occurred in 81 neonates (9.9%) and SGA-length in 39 (4.8%). The FIGO score demonstrated a significantly higher AUC than MUAC for SGA-length (0.706 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.627-0.785] vs. 0.564 [95% CI 0.465-0.662]; ΔAUC +0.142 [+0.023 to +0.261]; P = 0.028); no significant pairwise differences were observed for SGA-weight. FIGO at-risk status (score <5) was independently associated with SGA-weight (adjusted odds ratio 3.46 [95% CI 1.17-10.24]; P = 0.025) and SGA-length (adjusted odds ratio 4.03 [95% CI 1.03-15.84]; P = 0.046). Pre-pregnancy underweight was also independently associated with both outcomes. Fish intake and folate supplementation showed SGA-length-specific associations, whereas fruit/vegetable intake and reduced packaged snack consumption were associated with both SGA phenotypes.
CONCLUSION: The FIGO Nutrition Checklist demonstrated superior predictive validity over MUAC for impaired fetal linear growth and provided independent risk identification beyond anthropometric…

articles.title: Association of preoperative uterine artery Doppler with persistent intertwin size discordance in twin-twin transfusion syndrome treated with fetoscopic laser surgery.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Daxböck A, Kush M, Johnson J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the influence of preoperative uterine artery (UtA) Doppler abnormalities on disease severity, intertwin fetal-size discordance and perinatal outcomes in cases of twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) treated with fetoscopic laser surgery.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of TTTS pregnancies that underwent fetoscopic laser surgery using data that had been collected between August 2014 and July 2025. Inclusion required prelaser UtA Doppler examination and available neonatal outcomes. Preoperative ultrasound biometry, maternal and fetal Doppler data and Quintero staging were reviewed. UtA pulsatility index (PI) Z-scores were calculated; abnormal UtA Doppler was defined as mean UtA-PI ≥ 95th percentile and/or UtA notching. The primary outcome was the distribution of UtA Doppler abnormalities across TTTS stages. Secondary outcomes included the relationship between UtA Doppler findings and survival, gestational age at intervention, intertwin fetal-size discordance and intertwin birth-weight discordance. Analyses included non-parametric tests and regression models to identify predictors of intertwin size discordance.
RESULTS: Of 509 treated cases, 378 pregnancies were included. Abnormal UtA Doppler occurred in 23.5% of pregnancies and was most frequent in those with Stage-III TTTS (32.4%; P = 0.004). Abnormal UtA Doppler findings were associated with lower maternal age, Stage-III TTTS and greater intertwin size discordance. Patients with UtA Doppler abnormalities had earlier laser surgery (median, 18.4 vs 19.4 weeks; P = 0.008) and exhibited greater prelaser intertwin fetal-size discordance (median, 23.9% vs 18.9%; P = 0.012), with higher proportions of intertwin discordance ≥ 25% before laser surgery (49.4% vs 33.2%; P = 0.006) and at birth (28.4% vs 13.9%; P = 0.004) compared to those without abnormal UtA Doppler. However, immediate post-laser survival and overall perinatal survival did not differ by UtA Doppler status. Multivariable linear regression analysis identified umbilical artery Doppler parameters as the primary determinant of intertwin size discordance, while abnormal UtA Doppler remained independently associated with intertwin size discordance both at the time of laser surgery and at birth. However, receiver-operating-characteristics-curve analysis showed that abnormal mean UtA-PI Z-score alone did not predict intertwin birth-weight discordance of ≥ 25%.
CONCLUSIONS: Abnormal preoperative UtA Doppler was not a…

articles.title: Factors associated with severe postpartum hemorrhage in women with posterior low-lying placenta and prior cesarean: A prospective population-based study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Pinton A, Deneux-Tharaux C, Seco A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to conduct an exploratory assessment of the incidence and factors associated with severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in women with posterior low-lying placenta and prior cesarean without prenatal suspicion of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS).
METHODS: The study population was derived from the PACCRETA population-based study conducted in the 176 maternity units of 12 French regions from November 2013 through October 2015. All women with posterior low-lying placenta and prior Cesarean without prenatal suspicion of PAS were included in this analysis. The main outcome measure was a composite criterion of severe PPH defined by either estimated blood loss of ≥1500 mL, transfusion of 4 or more units of packed red blood cells, embolization, or surgical treatment.
RESULTS: Of the 520 114 women in the source population, 75 met the inclusion criteria (0.14 per 1000 women; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.11-0.18). Among these women, severe PPH occurred in seven (i.e., severe PPH incidence of 9.3% [95% CI 4.2-18.9]). Unsuspected PAS was diagnosed at delivery in four women of the study population (5.3%). Without these cases of PAS, the severe PPH incidence was 7.0% (95% CI 2.6-16.3). Factors associated with severe PPH were unsuspected PAS diagnosed at delivery (severe PPH incidence of 50% vs. 7%, P = 0.04) and placenta-os distance 1-9 mm compared with 10-19 mm (severe PPH incidence of 19% vs. 0%, P = 0.03).
CONCLUSION: About 1 in 11 women with posterior low-lying and prior cesarean without antenatal suspicion of PAS has severe PPH. Factors associated with severe PPH are unsuspected PAS diagnosed at delivery and 1-9 mm versus 10-19 mm placenta-os distance. These associations should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Interpregnancy interval and adverse live-birth outcomes after a non-live-birth prior pregnancy: A 2024 U.S. population-based analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Sebag M, Balayla J
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether the association between interpregnancy interval and adverse live-birth outcomes differs by the outcome of the preceding pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study of singleton live births in the 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia in 2024 (final Natality Public Use File) with at least one previous pregnancy and a classifiable most recent prior pregnancy outcome (live birth vs other outcome). Derived interpregnancy interval was categorized as <6, 6-11, 12-17, 18-23 (reference), 24-59, and ≥60 months. The primary outcome was preterm birth (<37 weeks); secondary outcomes were low birth weight, very low birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and a composite adverse outcome. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) and tested the interval × prior-outcome interaction.
RESULTS: Of 1 995 754 births, 420 882 (21.1%) followed a non-live-birth outcome. The association between interval and preterm birth differed by prior outcome (interaction P < 0.001). After a prior live birth, risk was U-shaped (<6 months: aRR 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.57-1.66; ≥60 months: 1.30, 1.27-1.33). After another outcome, intervals <6 months were not associated with increased risk (aRR 0.90, 0.87-0.94), although risk exceeded that after a live birth at every interval of 6 months or longer. Findings were similar for secondary outcomes and robust in sensitivity analyses, including adjustment for parity.
CONCLUSION: The association between interpregnancy interval and adverse outcomes of the subsequent live birth depends on the outcome of the preceding pregnancy and should not be interpreted uniformly across prior pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Gender-based violence in obstetric and gynecologic care: Secondary victimization, ethics, and trauma-informed practice-scoping review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Motiwala ZY, Sharma I, Choudhari S et al.
articles.abstract: Domestic, sexual, and gender-based violence (DSGBV) affects between 27% and 35% of women worldwide. The rate of this type of violence is higher in many low- and middle-income nations, and it exceeds 37% for women living in those countries. Many DSGBV survivors begin their healthcare experience at an obstetrics or gynecology (OB-GYN) office. Survivors might experience several barriers to receiving appropriate OB-GYN treatment because of failures to screen, secondary victimization, provider behavior, ethical dilemmas, and structural barriers; these barriers can affect the survivor's ability to disclose to a care provider, receive continuous care, and achieve long-term health outcomes. A search of the scientific literature was performed using PubMed and Scopus databases, gathering peer-reviewed articles that focused on DSGBV epidemiology, reproductive health outcomes of victims, secondary victimization in healthcare environments, trauma-informed care, ethical principles, and factors related to institutions that provide OB-GYN services to women. This review followed a scoping review methodology. The authors used a dual-reviewer systematic search, screening, and data-extraction process, which has been described in the methods section. Collected data were thematically synthesized to understand the power imbalance between OB-GYN practitioners and their patients, the professional behaviors of OB-GYN providers, the privacy dilemmas that exist between OB-GYN providers and their patients, how the training models for OB-GYN practitioners in high-income settings are applied to low-income and middle-income settings, and the adaptation strategies that can be implemented to provide trauma-informed care in low-income and middle-income settings. Domestic, sexual, and gender-based violence (DSGBV) exposure is related to an increase of 1.5 to 2.0 times in unintended pregnancy, 1.7 times in unsafe abortion, and approximately 2.0 times in high-prevalence areas HIV risk. This type of intimate partner violence during pregnancy is found in 3-9 percent of women, and it is linked to both late antenatal booking and poor attendance of antenatal visits. Less than one out of every four survivors reports violence in healthcare settings globally. Negative institutional responses occur in 30%-60% and are associated with more severe post-traumatic symptomatology and, in multi-country data, with most survivors never consulting formal health care or social services at all. The…

articles.title: Single-incision mini-sling (SIMS) under local anesthesia for stress urinary incontinence: A single-center prospective cohort study-12 months of follow-up.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Tsiapakidou S, Theodoulidis I, Grimbizis G et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is a prevalent and costly condition, with an estimated lifetime risk of surgery reaching 20% by the age of 80 years. Single-incision mini-slings (SIMS) represent the latest advancement in midurethral sling technology, offering a minimally invasive alternative to traditional retropubic and transobturator tapes (TOT). Studies indicate comparable subjective and objective cure rates between SIMS and TOT, with potential advantages in postmenopausal women owing to earlier mobilization and reduced morbidity. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of SIMS under local anesthesia in the management of SUI.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted in a tertiary academic urogynecology unit from December 2019 to December 2024. Consecutive patients meeting the inclusion criteria were enrolled following a standardized diagnostic and treatment protocol. Informed consent was obtained, and ethical approval was granted by the institutional review board. All patients underwent SIMS placement (Altis©, Coloplast) performed by two experienced urogynecologists under local anesthesia. Sling tensioning was performed via a standardized cough stress test at bladder volumes equal to normal voiding volume, as per pre-operative urodynamics. Patients were followed for 3 weeks and 12 months post-surgery. Data analysis was conducted using Microsoft Excel. Descriptive statistics were applied, and paired t-tests compared pre- and post-operative results. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 124 women underwent SIMS for SUI, with a mean age of 63.8 ± 11.1 years and a body mass index (BMI, calculated as weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters) of 29.0 ± 4.3. Among them, 21.8% had severe and 78.2% had moderate SUI, while 30.6% presented with mixed urinary incontinence (MUI). Pre-operatively, mean International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) Urinary Incontinence Short Form (ICIQ-UI-SF) and Female Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (ICIQ-FLUTS) scores were 14.3 ± 2.4 and 19.0 ± 6.0, respectively. All surgeries were performed in an ambulatory setting, with 95.2% discharged the same day. The mean surgical time was 31.5 ± 8.0 min, and peri-operative pain was 2.8 ± 1.8/10. At discharge, all but one patient had a negative stress test, and 99.2% would recommend the procedure. At 12 months, the composite outcome was successful for 103 (83.1%) patients, with an objective cure…

articles.title: From menopause to meaning: Women's reflections on navigating midlife.
articles.authors: Ness MM, Watts A
articles.abstract: Midlife has been framed through biomedical deficit narratives that emphasize decline, alongside a competing healthy-aging narrative that casts decline as something to be managed through individual effort; yet emerging scholarship calls for more inclusive, embodied, and intersectional approaches that center women's lived experiences. This qualitative study challenges deficit-based narratives of midlife by exploring how women negotiate between these narratives as they navigate this transition. We interviewed 27 women aged 39-57 using semi-structured interviews. Thematic analysis revealed three central themes: (1) reimagining 'midlife' - revealing tensions between societal expectations and personal agency, (2) embodied experiences of aging -navigating bodily changes while confronting medical dismissal and gender bias, and (3) evolving relational roles across diverse family structures. Participants actively negotiated deficit and healthy-aging narratives, describing midlife not as inevitable decline but as a period of profound reflection and redefinition. Many contested the 'midlife' label itself, challenged ageist and sexist expectations, and reclaimed bodily autonomy despite healthcare systems that frequently dismissed their embodied knowledge. These findings demonstrate how midlife is shaped by intersecting systems of power-ageism, sexism, and medical authority-yet also reveal possibilities for resistance and renegotiation. This research offers a more specific account of how midlife women negotiate between deficit and healthy-aging narratives, while also navigating broader relational narratives of family, gender, and caregiving, contributing a starting point for the new narratives on aging women this literature has called for. Future research must prioritize intersectional approaches with racially, economically, and culturally diverse samples to fully capture the complexity of midlife transitions.

articles.title: Lower and earlier diurnal cortisol signatures of psychological trauma versus comparable physiological stress: one day post-exposure.
articles.authors: Huang J, Liu Y, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Traumatic events engage stress physiology, with the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis and cortisol central to adaptation. In naturalistic trauma, physical injury and psychological distress often co-occur, complicating interpretation of acute cortisol changes. Stillbirth offers a natural contrast: it is physiologically similar to live birth but constitutes traumatic bereavement. This study tested whether psychological trauma elicited by stillbirth is associated with acute alterations in diurnal cortisol rhythm versus comparable physiological delivery stress. Fifty-seven postpartum women were included (stillbirth, 24; live birth, 33). Saliva samples were collected at seven fixed time points across the day following childbirth. Cosinor curve fitting yielded the midline estimating statistic of rhythm, amplitude, and acrophase. Traditional indices included area under the curve with respect to ground, area under the curve with respect to increase, and the cortisol awakening response. Group differences were tested using analyzes of variance. Both groups showed a coherent diurnal pattern. Compared with live birth, stillbirth was associated with a lower area under the curve with respect to ground, a lower area under the curve with respect to increase, and a lower midline estimating statistic of rhythm. Stillbirth was also exhibited associated with an earlier acrophase. Compared with comparable physiological delivery stress, stillbirth is linked to reduced total cortisol secretion, lower mean levels, and an advanced circadian phase in the acute postpartum period, suggesting that the psychological trauma of stillbirth may involve alterations in hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis regulatory patterns and providing preliminary evidence for future work on early biological markers and supportive interventions.

articles.title: Consensus and persistent uncertainty in fetal ventriculomegaly: Delphi study mapping unresolved clinical domains and research priorities.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Pagani G, Salomon LJ, Prefumo F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Fetal ventriculomegaly (VM) is a common prenatal finding with heterogeneous etiology and unpredictable outcome, yet its management remains among the least standardized in fetal medicine. This study aimed to establish expert consensus on key decision points in the prenatal management of fetal VM, and to systematically map the domains of persistent uncertainty as a structured framework for future research priorities.
METHODS: A two-round modified Delphi study was conducted with an international panel of experts in fetal medicine, selected through a systematic review of publications that included more than 50 cases of VM over the preceding decade. Round 1 comprised 39 multiple-choice questions, with consensus achieved when ≥ 75% of panelists selected a single answer option; items that did not reach consensus were reformulated into Likert-scale statements for Round 2, which comprised 60 statements rated on a 9-point Likert scale. In Round 2, consensus was defined by two simultaneous criteria: ≥ 75% of valid respondents scoring in the agreement (score, 7-9) or disagreement (score, 1-3) zone, with an interquartile range of ≤ 2. Non-consensus domains were classified using a post-hoc taxonomic framework into three categories: absent evidence (Type 1), divergent clinical frameworks (Type 2) and undefined construct (Type 3), which could occur independently or in combination.
RESULTS: Of 56 experts who completed Round 1, 45 (80%) also completed Round 2. In Round 1, consensus was reached on 20/39 (51%) questions. In Round 2, 6/60 (10%) statements reached positive consensus and four (7%) reached negative consensus; 50 (83%) did not reach consensus. Over the two rounds, consensus was achieved on standardized measurement technique, three-tier grading, comprehensive neurosonographic and investigative work-up, individualization of the timing of fetal magnetic resonance imaging, stepwise neurosurgical referral and delivery management of fetal VM. Classification of non-consensus domains identified 15/50 (30%) items as Type 1, 16/50 (32%) as Type 2, 4/50 (8%) as Type 3 and 15/50 (30%) as Type 1+3. Ventricular asymmetry, the largest non-consensus cluster with 12 items, was classified as Type 1+3 in 11/12 (92%) statements, reflecting the simultaneous absence of prospective outcome data and of a universally accepted operational definition.
CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi study provides structured expert-derived guidance, primarily applicable to specialist and referral…

articles.title: Gold-molybdenum disulfide functional nanocomposites for cervical cancer therapy: in vitro anticancer activity and modulation of pro-apoptotic markers.
articles.authors: T SF, M R, Packirisamy V et al.
articles.abstract: This study aims to develop the functional nanocomposites (Au-MoS2) for biomedical applications potentially for anticancer activity. The nanocomposite was synthesized via chemical method by integrating gold nanoparticle onto exfoliated MoS2 nanosheets. Scanning electron microscopy analysis revealed irregular, aggregated MoS2 nanosheets with a porous and rough morphology, decorated by uniformly distributed spherical shaped Au particles. Energy-dispersive X-ray analysis confirmed the presence of Mo, S, and Au, indicating the successful formation of the high purity hetero-structured nanocomposite. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the key functional groups and interfacial interactions between the components, while X-ray diffraction pattern showed the crystalline nature of both MoS2 and Au nanoparticles. The biological evaluation indicates moderate cytotoxic activity with an IC50 of 181.7 µg/mL. Morphological observations and fluorescence staining confirmed apoptotic features including chromatin condensation, membrane blebbing, and nuclear fragmentation. Further, the gene expression analysis revealed upregulation of pro-apoptotic markers (Bad and caspases), and downregulation of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, highlighting the activation of mitochondrial-mediated apoptosis. The Au-MoS2 nanocomposite demonstrated combined effects, structural stability, and controlled cytotoxicity, highlighting its potential as an effective platform for targeted cancer therapy and other biomedical applications.

articles.title: Maternity versus non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.authors: Cryns N, Schroer J, Noel-Storr AH et al.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Substantial uncertainty exists regarding how healthcare system factors, especially care setting types, affect the uptake and implementation of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy screening in practice. Evidence suggests that the care environment may influence diagnostic processes.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of maternity and non-maternity healthcare settings for the diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus or diabetes in pregnancy.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) up to April 2026, and for controlled non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs) up to December 2025. We also searched CENTRAL to identify ongoing trials.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included RCTs and planned to include cluster-RCTs and NRSIs, but we did not find any. Eligible participants were pregnant women being screened for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) or diabetes in pregnancy. We defined maternity healthcare settings as those specialising in care for pregnant, birthing, and postpartum individuals, with appropriate screening protocols, and non-maternity healthcare settings as general medical environments lacking a focus on pregnancy and women's care. We considered any screening format (e.g. risk-factor-based screening) and any diagnostic test (e.g. one- and two-step oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT)).
OUTCOMES: Critical health service outcomes were compliance with screening and follow-up guidelines, diagnosis of gestational diabetes or diabetes in pregnancy, maternal emergency department visits during pregnancy, maternal antenatal hospitalisation, length of maternal hospitalisation, length of neonatal hospitalisation, and care accessibility. Critical maternal outcomes included hypertensive disorders, maternal death, intensive care admissions, hyperglycaemia requiring pharmacological treatment, infections, and postpartum glucose intolerance, including progression to diabetes, within 15 years after birth. Critical child-related outcomes encompassed perinatal death, neonatal intensive care admissions, preterm birth, neonatal hypoglycaemia, large-for-gestational-age, shoulder dystocia, and birth trauma. Further critical and important outcomes not included in the summary of findings tables can be found in the full text.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs. We had planned to use ROBINS-I…

articles.title: Placental small-RNA sequencing reveals a distinct microRNA signature and its functional relevance in a preeclampsia rat model.
articles.authors: Vaka R, Amaral LM, Chambers CL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite extensive investigations over the last few decades, molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of preeclampsia remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests that microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate key pathological processes in preeclampsia including endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress. However, a comprehensive profiling of miRNA expression has not been previously carried out. Thus, using reduced uterine perfusion pressure (RUPP) model of preeclampsia, we performed placental miRNA sequencing to identify functional relevance of abnormally expressed miRNAs.
METHODS: Blood pressure was measured via carotid catheterization on gestational day (GD)19. Placental small-RNA sequencing was performed using Illumina NextSeq2000 sequencer.
RESULTS: Our analysis identified 142 differentially regulated miRNAs (40 up- and 102 down-regulated) in placenta from RUPP rats. The top upregulated miRNAs included miR-211-3p, miR-628, miR-6324, miR-363-5p, and miR-6329, while miR-3587, miR-29b-3p, miR-3556a, miR-29a-3p, and miR-21-3p were the most downregulated. Functional annotation revealed associations with immune response (miR-363, miR-21, miR-29), B-cell differentiation (miR-628), T-cell activation (miR-21), adipogenesis, and lipid metabolism (miR-211, miR-29, miR-21), and angiogenesis (miR-363, miR-21). Further, gene ontology analysis revealed significant enrichment in biological processes; regulation of transport, cell-cell signaling, and calcium-dependent exocytosis, cellular components; synaptic vesicles, perinuclear cytoplasm, and clathrin-coated vesicles, and molecular functions; glycoprotein binding, protein dimerization, and myosin binding.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that robust miRNA dysregulation in RUPP rats may underlie disease pathogenesis.

articles.title: Social-ecological factors shaping women's postpartum permanent contraception decision-making: Qualitative insights from a multi-site study.
articles.authors: Rangaswamy DD, Arora KS, Bullington BW et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe clinician-patient relationship is known to impact contraceptive care utilization, but less studied is how factors external to the clinician-patient relationship, such as prior experiences seeking reproductive healthcare or family dynamics and social networks, matter to patients' postpartum contraceptive decision-making.ObjectiveOur objective was to examine factors external to current patient-provider relationships that contribute to women's decision-making surrounding postpartum permanent contraception (PC).DesignThis was a qualitative study at four U.S. healthcare systems with 75 postpartum women who had a documented plan for PC.MethodsWe conducted semi-structured interviews between March 2022 and June 2023. We employed a modified grounded theory approach to codebook thematic analysis.ResultsPatients described experiences across four key domains: individual, family, social networking, and policy ecologies. Individual-level influences included prior experiences with clinicians, health concerns, miscarriage experiences, future life goals, and apprehension toward medical procedures. Family-level influences centered on maintaining family wellbeing and accommodating partner preferences. Social networks shaped decisions through information and experiences shared by relatives, friends, community members, and social media. Policy-level influences included concerns regarding abortion access and parental leave policies.ConclusionWomen's decisions regarding postpartum permanent contraception are shaped by a complex interplay of personal experiences, family priorities, social networks, and policy contexts. Contraceptive counseling that acknowledges these influences may better support reproductive autonomy, address misinformation, and facilitate patient-centered decision-making.

articles.title: Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Zreid H, Vlaming-van Eijk LE, Drakesmith H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant (n = 97) and nonpregnant (n = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available.
RESULTS: Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity (p < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, p < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, p = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant (p = 0.015) and non-pregnant (p = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, p < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, p = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, p = 0.003) compared with moderate illness.
CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

articles.title: Age and frequency of clinical contraceptive coercion: An analysis of age-based differences in upward and downward clinical coercion in a national sample.
articles.authors: Pleasants E, Whitfield B, Cannon LM et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundClinical contraceptive coercion-pressure from healthcare providers to use (upward) or not use (downward) contraception-threatens reproductive autonomy. Adolescents and young adults (AYA) may be at heightened risk of clinical contraceptive coercion due to age-based clinical biases and post-Dobbs shifts in clinician counseling practices, but quantitative evidence comparing AYA and adult experiences is limited.ObjectivesTo assess the frequency of upward and downward clinical contraceptive coercion among AYA (ages 18-25) and adults (26-49) and examine age-based differences.DesignIn 2023, we surveyed 1,500 respondents of reproductive age assigned female at birth in the United States. Using the Coercion in Contraceptive Care Checklist, participants reported experiences of coercion during their most recent contraceptive counseling, categorized as any, upward, and downward coercion.MethodsChi-square tests and Poisson regression models with robust error variance assessed associations between age and clinical contraceptive coercion, adjusting for sexual identity, socioeconomic status, race and ethnicity, ever being pregnant, relationship status, and how long ago they spoke to a clinician about contraception.ResultsAYA included in this analysis (n=1,169) were significantly more likely than adults to report experiencing any clinical contraceptive coercion (25.6% vs. 15.8%, p<0.001) and upward coercion (21.5% vs. 13.0%, p=0.001). Adjusted models confirmed these associations (any coercion: aRR=1.53, 95% CI: 1.14-2.06; upward coercion: aRR=1.58, 95% CI: 1.13-2.21).ConclusionsAYA more commonly reported clinical contraceptive coercion than adults, particularly upward coercion. This pattern suggests that pregnancy prevention may be disproportionately emphasized in clinical encounters with younger patients, potentially at the expense of AYA reproductive autonomy. These findings underscore the need for person-centered contraceptive counseling that safeguards reproductive autonomy across the life course, especially for younger patients navigating care in a shifting post-Dobbs landscape.

articles.title: Behçet's disease and pregnancy: retrospective study and updated review of the literature.
articles.authors: Briante M, Scattone M, Matys V et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Behçet's disease (BD) is a rare, chronic-relapsing multisystem vasculitis of unknown aetiology, typically presenting with bipolar aphthosis (oral and genital), cutaneous lesions, and ocular involvement. It is most often diagnosed during reproductive age and its coexistence with pregnancy is therefore not uncommon. The interaction between BD and pregnancy is complex and bidirectional: pregnancy can modulate disease activity, while the disease itself may influence maternal, foetal, and neonatal outcomes. Current literature remains limited and frequently yields inconsistent conclusions regarding this relationship. In light of these considerations, this study aims to evaluate the impact of BD on pregnancy outcomes and to characterise the disease course during pregnancy in a cohort of affected patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed data from 25 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of BD and a total of 48 pregnancies, followed at the outpatient clinics of Policlinico Umberto I, Rome, Italy. Clinical records were reviewed and supplemented with telephone interviews to ensure accuracy and completeness of information. Additionally, a literature review wasconducted using major databases such as PubMed, Cochrane and Google Scholar to provide context and comparison with previously published findings.
RESULTS: Contrary to the prevailing consensus in the literature, which often reports increased disease activity during pregnancy, our findings indicate that in 80% of cases it remained stable, with no significant differences compared to the pre-pregnancy period. When flares did occur, they primarily involved oral aphthosis, aligning with previously reported patterns. Pregnancy outcomes were generally favourable, with an overall live birth rate of 89.58%. Complications were observed in 13 pregnancies (27.08%), mostly in pregnancies that occurred before BD diagnosis (21%). The most common were spontaneous miscarriage and deep vein thrombosis. Other complications, each occurring in one case, included threatened miscarriage, preterm delivery, low birth weight, gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and premature rupture of membranes.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that Behçet's disease does not usually worsen during pregnancy and that favourable pregnancy outcomes are achievable. Nonetheless, the risk of complications, although relatively low, supports the need for preconception counselling and close multidisciplinary monitoring. This study…

articles.title: Perspectives of Women Who Have Migrated from Sub-Saharan Africa to Paris, France on PrEP Outreach and Education.
articles.authors: Miller K, Devlin SA, Zamudio AR et al.
articles.abstract: Women who have migrated from sub-Saharan Africa to France face a disproportionate risk of HIV acquisition yet remain underrepresented among pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) users. Barriers to PrEP use have been identified including low awareness of PrEP due to limited outreach from providers and ineffective advertising campaigns. This study builds on our previous work demonstrating interest in PrEP among this population by examining how to best engage these women through PrEP education and advertising. We conducted 6 focus groups with 25 women who migrated from sub-Saharan Africa recruited from the Lariboisière Hospital Family Planning Center in Paris between October 2024 and October 2025. Using a semi-structured focus group guide, we explored participants' knowledge and perception of PrEP and responses to advertisements. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic coding in Dedoose. Most participants (80%) had never heard of PrEP, but responses were positive when it was described. Participants identified health care providers as a trusted information source and social media as a promising channel for community outreach. Women preferred detailed, accessible medical content. Campaigns featuring Black women exclusively prompted concerns about stigmatization. Safety from HIV acquisition, especially in the context of relationship structures, was consistently cited as a motivator for PrEP use. Outreach strategies should leverage trusted provider relationships and peer networks. Content of educational initiatives should include accessible medical information and feature diverse representation without stigmatizing vulnerable groups. Framing of PrEP in advertisements should consider structural differences affecting a specific population, based on the circumstances surrounding their unique risks for HIV acquisition.

articles.title: Examining the Association Between Food Insecurity and Pregnancy Outcomes.
articles.authors: Lee KM, Thoma ME, Steinberg JR et al.
articles.abstract: Food insecurity (FI) is a critical yet under-identified social determinant of health among pregnant populations. Prior research links FI to adverse perinatal outcomes, but few studies have examined whether these associations are modified by participation in food assistance programs such as the USDA's Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). This study assessed the association between prenatal FI and four perinatal outcomes-postpartum depression (PPD), gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, and gestational weight gain (GWG)-and examined whether prenatal WIC participation moderated these relationships. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using state-representative data from Phase 8 of the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS). Ten states with relevant data were included. The sample was limited to WIC-eligible mothers (income < 185% of the federal poverty level or Medicaid enrollment). Logistic regression models estimated associations between FI and each outcome in unadjusted and adjusted models, with interaction terms used to assess moderation by WIC participation. Models adjusted for sociodemographic and pregnancy-related characteristics. Among WIC-eligible mothers, 13.65% reported FI during pregnancy. After adjustment, FI was associated with higher odds of PPD (OR: 2.47, 95% CI: 2.16-2.82), gestational diabetes (OR: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.00-1.49), gestational hypertension (OR: 1.38, 95% CI: 1.18-1.60), and GWG below recommendations (OR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.09-1.52). Adjusting for depression before and during pregnancy attenuated associations. WIC participation did not significantly moderate these relationships. Prenatal FI remains associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, suggesting that while WIC provides nutritional support, additional stressors linked to food insecurity may persist.

articles.title: Factors Impacting Continuation of Onabotulinum Toxin Therapy for Idiopathic and Neurogenic Urgency Urinary Incontinence.
articles.authors: Sadeghi Z, Bethel EC, Daignault-Newton S et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We investigated demographic, diagnostic, and socioeconomic variables associated with continuation and discontinuation of onabotulinum toxin (BTX) therapy in adult patients treated for idiopathic and neurogenic urgency urinary incontinence (UUI).
METHODS: Patients who initiated BTX for UUI between 2015 and 2018 at a tertiary academic referral center were identified from CPT codes and followed through 2020 (n = 723). The cohort was divided into patients who continued BTX therapy (received ≥1 BTX treatment within 2 years of initial injection) (Group A), and patients who stopped BTX (received no additional BTX for at least 2 years after the last injection) (Group B). Demographic variables were extracted using chart review and administrative data. Socioeconomic differences were estimated using affluence index (AI) and disadvantage index (DI) from their last botox injection, calculated using U.S. census tract indicators. AI factors include household income, professions of household members, and educational background. DI factors include neighborhood proportion of female-headed households, receiving public assistance or not, household income level, and level of employment. Indexes ranged from 0.0 (least affluent or disadvantaged) to 1.0 (most affluent or advantaged).
RESULTS: The mean cohort age (n = 723) was 57% and 69% were female. After the initial injection, 40% received additional injections within 2 years (Group A) and 60% did not (Group B). There were no demographic differences between groups. Univariate comparison of affluence and disadvantage indexes revealed Group A affluence was not significantly different (AI = 0.38 vs 0.37, p = 0.2) but was slightly less disadvantaged (DI = 0.072, vs. 0.081; p = 0.036) than Group B. Multivariable analysis including demographic and socioeconomic factors demonstrated that higher affluence index was associated with lower odds of BTX discontinuation (OR = 0.90 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI: 0.82-0.99, p = 0.029), while there was insufficient evidence of an association between disadvantage index and discontinuation (OR = 1.23 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI: 0.99-1.54, p = 0.06). After adding neurogenic versus non-neurogenic etiology of UUI, the socioeconomic associations were no longer significant. Patients with a non-neurogenic diagnosis had significantly greater odds of BTX discontinuation than patients with a neurogenic diagnosis (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.35-2.89, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Approximately 40% of…

articles.title: Efficacy of Rajahpravartini Vati in Adolescent Girls and Young Women With Primary Dysmenorrhea: Protocol for a Prospective, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.authors: Kumar A, Bhuyan G, R VL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary dysmenorrhea is a prevalent menstrual disorder affecting adolescents and young women worldwide and is associated with substantial impairment in daily functioning, academic performance, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life. Conventional treatments, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory and hormonal therapies, often provide temporary symptomatic relief but may cause adverse effects with prolonged use. Rajahpravartini Vati, a classical Ayurvedic herbomineral formulation traditionally indicated for painful menstruation, has shown preliminary therapeutic potential but lacks evaluation in a rigorous placebo-controlled clinical trial.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of Rajahpravartini Vati in adolescent girls and young women aged 12 to 24 years with primary dysmenorrhea.
METHODS: This study protocol describes a prospective, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial to be conducted at the Regional Ayurveda Research Institute, Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, India. A total of 100 eligible participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either Rajahpravartini Vati (500 mg twice daily) or a matched placebo for 3 consecutive menstrual cycles. Treatment will begin 3 days before the expected onset of menstruation and continue until 3 days after onset, followed by 1 observational cycle. The primary outcome is the change in dysmenorrhea severity measured using the Working Ability, Location, Intensity, Days of Pain, Dysmenorrhea score. Secondary outcomes include pain intensity and duration, rescue medication use, psychosomatic symptoms, and perceived stress. Both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses are planned.
RESULTS: The study was sanctioned in July 2025, and the first installment of funds was released in September 2025. Ethics approval was obtained on July 16, 2025 (IEC-RARI/2025-26/02), and the trial was prospectively registered with the Clinical Trial Registry-India (CTRI/2025/07/091892) on July 28, 2025. Participant recruitment began in June 2026, and is ongoing. To date, 15 participants had been screened, 6 enrolled, and 9 were classified as screen failures. Data analysis has not yet commenced, and results are expected to be available for publication in 2028.
CONCLUSIONS: This trial is expected to generate evidence regarding the efficacy of Rajahpravartini Vati in managing primary dysmenorrhea among adolescent girls and young women and may help inform future…

articles.title: From Delays to Systems in Maternal Healthcare Utilisation: A Conceptual Framework Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Ekpenyong MS, Matheson D, Serrant L
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop an operational, systems-oriented framework for analysing sustainable maternal healthcare utilisation, grounded in Nigerian evidence and intended for contextual adaptation and testing.
DESIGN: Conceptual framework study using narrative synthesis, structured comparative evidence synthesis and independent face and content appraisal.
SETTING: Nigeria, with consideration of applicability to other maternal healthcare settings.
POPULATION OR SAMPLE: Purposively selected peer-reviewed Nigerian maternal healthcare studies; three independent external appraisers comprising two maternal-health researchers and one healthcare professional.
METHODS: We synthesised empirical evidence into linked domains and hypothesised relationships, compared it with established maternal-health and health-systems frameworks and challenged it against additional Nigerian studies. Appraisers assessed relevance, clarity, completeness, cross-domain plausibility, and practical utility.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Conceptual coherence, domain relevance, completeness, explanatory plausibility, practical utility, and candidate indicators of sustainable maternal healthcare utilisation; no patient-level clinical outcomes were measured.
RESULTS: We specified six linked domains: policy and governance, health-system capacity, community engagement, equity, quality of care, and monitoring, evaluation and learning.
