Governance provides structural conditions; capacity, quality and community engagement interact; equity modifies pathways; and monitoring supports feedback and adaptation. External appraisal offered qualified support and identified boundaries requiring refinement.
CONCLUSIONS: The framework offers a testable systems structure for diagnosing interacting barriers and guiding context-appropriate indicators and multilevel interventions. Prospective testing is needed to establish construct validity, responsiveness and transferability.

articles.title: A Korean national birthweight reference for singleton live births.
articles.authors: Jung E, Son WJ, Im DH et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a national birth weight reference for singleton live births in Korea using nationwide data, provide sex-specific percentile charts, and compare the Korean reference with widely used international birth weight references.
METHODS: Nationwide birth registration microdata for singleton live births between 2019 and 2023 were used. The data were obtained from Statistics Korea and accessed through the MicroData Integrated Service. Smoothed gestational age (GA)-specific birth weight percentile curves were generated overall and separately for male and female neonates. The Korean reference curves were compared with the United States national birth weight reference and INTERGROWTH-21st standards.
RESULTS: 1) A total of 1,158,083 singleton live births were included in the analysis. Smoothed GA-specific birth weight percentile curves were generated overall and separately for male and female neonates. 2) Male neonates had consistently higher birth weights than female neonates across GAs, with a median difference of approximately 100 g from the third trimester onward. And 3) the Korean national birth weight reference was compared with the United States national birth weight reference and the INTERGROWTH-21st standards. The United States national reference classified 66.6% of neonates classified as large for GA by the Korean reference as appropriate for GA, whereas INTERGROWTH-21st classified 65.6% of neonates classified as small for GA by the Korean reference as appropriate for GA.
CONCLUSION: This study reports a nationwide Korean birth weight reference for singleton live births. The Korean birth weight reference differs from the widely used international references, supporting the need for population-specific charts for size assessment in Korean fetuses and neonates.

articles.title: Long-Term Reproductive and Obstetric Outcomes After Barbed Versus Monofilament Uterine Closure Strategies at Primary Term Caesarean Delivery: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Alessandri F, Centurioni MG, Olcese F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare outcomes after barbed versus monofilament uterine closure strategies at primary term caesarean delivery.
DESIGN: Retrospective, single-centre, 1:2 matched cohort study.
SETTING: Tertiary university hospital in Genoa, Italy.
POPULATION: Women with at least 36 months of follow-up after caesarean delivery for a term singleton pregnancy.
METHODS: Women receiving continuous, unlocked, double-layer barbed closure were matched 1:2 to women receiving monofilament closure by labour, second-stage caesarean, and temporal proximity. Records and structured interviews provided long-term outcomes. Cox models stratified by matched set evaluated time from the reported start of active attempts to conception.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was time to first conception from the start of active attempts; secondary outcomes included conception, live birth, and subsequent pregnancy and delivery outcomes.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 486 women (162 barbed; 324 monofilament). Among 205 women attempting conception, 62/73 (84.9%) and 114/132 (86.4%) conceived; median time to conception was 11 and 9 months. The adjusted hazard ratio for time to conception was 0.72 (95% CI 0.39-1.31). Confidence intervals for conception within 12-24 months and live birth all included the null value. Among 148 subsequent deliveries, gestational age, trial of labour, vaginal birth after caesarean, and other maternal and neonatal outcomes showed no consistent pattern across groups. Placental and uterine-scar complications were infrequent, resulting in imprecise between-group estimates.
CONCLUSIONS: Barbed closure was not clearly associated with different reproductive or obstetric outcomes. Operator-strategy confounding and imprecision limit interpretation; equivalence and comparative safety remain unestablished.

articles.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome research in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review on current status and future directions.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Hatoum S, Amiri M, Makwe CC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most prevalent disorders affecting women. The status of PCOS research in sub-Saharan Africa is unknown, where non-communicable diseases are prevalent but often underrecognized. To assess current knowledge about PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa and identify gaps in the literature.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and African Journals Online through 9 August 2026 to identify original studies on PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa. Original research studies involving sub-Saharan African populations, without age-related constraints, were eligible. We excluded non-original studies and studies that did not focus on PCOS. Three independent reviewers (S.H., M.A., and C.C.M.) performed the searches.
RESULTS: Of 1973 retrieved records, 40 studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly from Nigeria, with additional contributions from South Africa, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Benin, Kenya, and Ethiopia. Most studies were observational and primarily focused on PCOS in the context of infertility. No population-based prevalence studies were identified; however, 13 studies reported PCOS prevalence, mostly in clinically selected populations.
CONCLUSIONS: PCOS remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa, with substantial gaps in population-based epidemiology, diagnostic practices, phenotype distribution, management, and metabolic outcomes. Addressing these gaps through larger, well-designed studies is critical to accurately assess the disease burden, inform clinical guidelines, and optimize management strategies. Additionally, overcoming barriers such as cultural attitudes, cost, and limited accessibility to diagnostic tools and treatment options remains essential to improving PCOS care and research across the region.PROSPERO registration ID CRD420250649730 - 13 March 2025.

articles.title: Non-Hormonal Treatments for Vasomotor Symptoms of Menopause: An Up-to-Date Review.
articles.authors: Farhan AS, Farhan HS, Dinfash MT
articles.abstract: Treatment of vasomotor symptoms, sweating, and hot flashes after menopause is important to improve the quality of life in this population because of the burden and disruption that these features exert on daily life activities. In recent times, there has been a focus on non-hormonal modalities for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms because of the elevated concern about the adverse effects of hormonal treatment and the presence of contraindications to its use in some patients. Therefore, our objective in this review is to focus on non-hormonal options and their efficacy and effectiveness in managing vasomotor symptoms. To improve the quality of life for women going through menopause, this review summarizes recent research on menopausal vasomotor symptoms, including the physiology and pathophysiology of menopause and most non-hormonal methods for treating these symptoms. Improving life quality in menopausal women by relieving the troublesome vasomotor symptoms during this period of life is essential, so searching for new modalities of treatment that are safe and well tolerated is important. There are many non-hormonal options for treating the vasomotor symptoms in menopause, with variable effects and potency as well as fewer side effects and contraindications than hormonal types. These options include non-drug-like psychotherapies, herbal supplements, and drugs that have relative safety and more tolerability than hormonal options.

articles.title: Infertility Among Men Living with HIV in Sub-Sahara Africa; Bridging Evidence and Practice Gaps.
articles.authors: Adeniyi IA, Shehu UU, Ikuomola EO et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Male infertility is an important component of the global burden of infertility and remains an under-addressed reproductive health concern in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). The increasing number of men living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) following expanded access to antiretroviral therapy (ART) has heightened the need to address their reproductive goals and fertility-related needs. However, the intersection of HIV, male infertility, and access to fertility care remains inadequately characterized in the region. This review examined the biological, clinical, sociocultural, economic, and health-system factors influencing the management of male infertility among men living with HIV (MLWH) in SSA and identified key gaps in evidence and service delivery.
METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online (AJOL) for studies published between 2000 and 2026. English-language studies addressing male infertility in the context of HIV, including biological, clinical, sociocultural, economic, or health-system factors, were considered. Studies were screened by title and abstract followed by full-text assessment. Findings were thematically synthesized across biological and ART-related reproductive effects, diagnostic and treatment limitations, sociocultural barriers, economic constraints, and health-system challenges. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, outcomes, and settings, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: The review identified interacting biological, social, economic, and health-system factors that complicate infertility management among MLWH in SSA. HIV infection has been associated with alterations in semen quality and reproductive function, although findings are heterogeneous and do not establish that HIV or ART uniformly causes male infertility. Evidence regarding ART remains inconsistent and may vary according to regimen, treatment duration, and study population, with limited evidence from contemporary regimens and few longitudinal male-focused studies from SSA. Major barriers to care include HIV- and infertility-related stigma, gendered perceptions of infertility, limited male engagement in reproductive healthcare, fragmented HIV and fertility services, inadequate diagnostic and laboratory capacity, shortages of trained healthcare professionals, limited availability and affordability of assisted reproductive…

articles.title: Carbohydrate Quality Versus Quantity in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus While Considering Randomized Dietary Interventions: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Aggarwal S, Chawla GK, Gupta R
articles.abstract: Medical nutrition therapy is the first-line treatment for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), but whether carbohydrate quality or quantity should be prioritized is unclear, as dietary interventions often change amount, glycemic quality, fiber, fat, protein, and food pattern together. We systematically reviewed randomized trials of carbohydrate quality or quantity in diagnosed GDM. PubMed and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 19, 2026, with citation searching. Two human reviewers screened the records and extracted the data with artificial-intelligence assistance. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2), and the findings were primarily synthesized narratively using the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) approach, with limited random-effects meta-analysis for clinically compatible insulin-related outcomes. From 981 records, 34 reports representing 25 independent randomized studies were included; they differed markedly in construct, achieved carbohydrate separation, rescue treatment, and analysis population. In an exploratory, treatment-threshold analysis, lower-glycemic-index assignment reduced the proportion meeting insulin-start criteria (two trials, 159 participants; risk ratio [RR] 0.43, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.75), but rescue switching removed the difference in actual insulin use. Lower-carbohydrate assignment did not reduce insulin initiation (three trials, 248 participants; RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.76-1.35). This finding remained essentially unchanged after excluding the trial in which the intended difference in carbohydrate intake was not achieved. With only two or three small trials per pool, I² = 0% does not indicate homogeneity. Fiber, staple-quality, and provided-diet interventions improved selected postprandial measures, but obstetric, birth-size, and neonatal-adiposity benefits were not established, and certainty was low or very low. Carbohydrate quality is a plausible route to postprandial improvement without aggressive restriction, but current randomized evidence does not establish a universal quality-over-quantity rule or support lower carbohydrate intake as superior. Carbohydrate amount should be individualized while prioritizing nutrient-dense, lower-glycemic-index, fiber-rich sources.

articles.title: Dietary supplements are commonly used for menopause symptoms amid concerns about hormone therapy: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Mitschke S
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Many women use dietary supplements to manage menopause symptoms, yet patterns of use, perceived effectiveness, and information sources remain incompletely described in contemporary literature. This cross-sectional study assessed current dietary supplement use, including use specifically for menopause symptoms, and perceptions of menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) among symptomatic menopausal women aged 45-65 years.
METHODS: An online questionnaire was administered to a self-selected sample of 226 perimenopausal or postmenopausal participants recruited through online health forums, social media, menopause support groups, and newsletters. Survey items captured sociodemographic characteristics, health, supplement use, perceived effectiveness, information sources, and MHT awareness and concerns. Associations were examined using cross-tabulations, chi-square and exact tests, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression.
RESULTS: Current use of at least one dietary supplement, for any purpose, was reported by 138 participants (61.1%; 95% CI 54.6-67.2). Self-reported use of supplements specifically to manage menopause symptoms (menopause-targeted use) was reported by 65 participants (28.9%; 95% CI 23.4-35.1). Among supplement users, the most frequently reported products were multivitamins (55.8%), vitamin D (52.9%), magnesium (51.4%), and probiotics (41.3%). MHT awareness was high (n = 187, 82.7%) and increased with income. Concerns about breast cancer (47.8%), blood clotting (44.7%), stroke (40.7%), and heart disease (37.2%) as risks of MHT were frequently reported. Healthcare providers and online sources were the leading sources of information, and social media influencers were rated least trustworthy. Former smokers (adjusted OR 2.98, 95% CI 1.21-7.34) and never smokers (adjusted OR 3.92, 95% CI 1.59-9.65) had higher odds of any supplement use than current smokers; this association was not observed for menopause-targeted use.
CONCLUSION: In this self-selected online sample, current dietary supplement use for any purpose was common, although fewer than half of supplement users reported using supplements to manage menopause symptoms. Concerns about MHT persisted despite high awareness. These estimates should not be generalized to the broader population of midlife women. Future studies using probability-based samples and validated symptom measures are needed to characterize menopause-targeted supplement use and to inform clinical strategies that…

articles.title: Decision-Supported Collaborative Care for Gestational Diabetes: A Narrative Review of Development Pathways and Evaluation in Routine Clinical Practice.
articles.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
articles.authors: Yan Y, Yang M, Wang L et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) requires frequent glucose monitoring, rapid behavior adjustment, and timely escalation within a short pregnancy window, yet routine care is often episodic and fragmented across teams. Digital tools have improved data capture, but many systems still stop at logging and messaging and do not consistently translate patient-generated data into clinical action. This review frames decision-supported collaborative care for GDM as a workflow-centered care model that links glucose and clinical context to interpretable decision logic and role-based team processes for triage, escalation, and closed-loop feedback. We conducted a structured narrative review of English-language studies indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science from database inception to 2026, supplemented by manual screening of relevant reference lists. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in intervention design, clinical settings, and reported outcomes, the evidence was synthesized narratively. We summarize key system components, outline a practical development pathway from defining actionable use cases to embedding safety guardrails and workflow integration, and propose a multidimensional evaluation approach that combines clinical outcomes with process, implementation, and system-level measures. We also discuss major barriers to scale, including alert burden, role accountability, data governance and privacy, and digital equity. This framework may support clinicians, healthcare organizations, and policymakers in designing, implementing, and evaluating safe, equitable, and workflow-compatible GDM services.

articles.title: Localisation of Bladder Incontinence Based on History and Examination for First-Year Neurosurgical Residents.
articles.journal: The Malaysian journal of medical sciences : MJMS
articles.authors: Shareef IJ, Abdullah JM, Zakaria Z et al.
articles.abstract: When a patient presents with urinary incontinence, the goal is to quickly localise the cause of it, so that further imaging workup and targeted management can be initiated at the earliest. In this review, we look at established functional magnetic resonance imaging data and activation likelihood estimation analysis to pinpoint specific areas of the nervous system causing urinary incontinence. These can range from the cortex and the pontine micturition centre to the spinal pathway and peripheral nerves. By using basic history-taking and examination techniques, the five main types of urinary incontinence can be localised to specific anatomical locations.

articles.title: Cellular origins and evolutionary dynamics of plasma cfDNA in solid tumors: integrating germline, tumor-derived, and hematopoietic variation for MRD and treatment guidance.
articles.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
articles.authors: Zhao Q, Wu C, Huang X et al.
articles.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a heterogeneous and rapidly changing biological pool derived from malignant cells, normal tissues, and hematopoietic cells. The abundance and molecular composition of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) are determined not only by tumor burden but also by tissue architecture, vascular access, cell-death programs, chromatin organization, nuclease processing, systemic clearance, treatment exposure, and clonal evolution. These biological determinants shape the mutation, methylation, fragmentation, nucleosomal, and temporal features exploited by contemporary liquid-biopsy assays. Accurate clinical interpretation therefore requires both sensitive detection and reliable source attribution, particularly the distinction of tumor-derived variants from constitutional germline alterations and clonal hematopoiesis. In this review, we integrate the biological origins and processing of plasma cfDNA with analytical strategies for low-tumor-fraction detection and critically evaluate the evidence supporting postoperative molecular residual disease (MRD), recurrence surveillance, treatment-response assessment, resistance monitoring, and ctDNA-guided therapy across solid tumors. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing prognostic validity, treatment-predictive value, and demonstrated clinical utility. Current evidence is strongest in colorectal cancer and, more recently, ctDNA-selected urothelial cancer, whereas routine ctDNA-directed intervention in resected non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer remains insufficiently validated. By linking cfDNA biology to an explicit hierarchy of clinical evidence, this review defines both the established applications and the major limitations that must be addressed before broader implementation of ctDNA-guided precision oncology.

articles.title: Diminished ovarian reserve in systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical, immunological, viral, and therapeutic determinants in a 24-month prospective study.
articles.authors: Rizzo M, Beltrami S, Ruffilli F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) predominantly affects women of reproductive age; however, the impact of the disease, chronic inflammation, and its treatments on ovarian reserve remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve in SLE and to evaluate the longitudinal associations of clinical characteristics, therapeutic exposures, and herpesvirus serologies with Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) levels.
METHODS: This observational prospective monocentric study followed 80 premenopausal women (18-45 years) with SLE for 24 months. Clinical data, treatments, AMH levels, and herpesvirus serologies were collected every 6 months. Patients were stratified by diminished ovarian reserve (AMH <1 ng/mL). Longitudinal AMH trajectories and the impact of covariates were evaluated using repeated-measures analyses and linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: The cohort exhibited a high prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve (45% of the study population), associated with older age (37 ± 7 vs. 34 ± 7 years, p = 0.041), longer disease duration (14 ± 9 vs. 10 ± 6 years, p = 0.026), higher cumulative damage (p = 0.007), and lupus anticoagulant positivity (14% vs. 39%, p=0.009). Disease activity was comparable across groups. Hydroxychloroquine use was more frequent in women without diminished ovarian reserve (89% vs 69%, p = 0.033). Over 24 months, AMH levels remained stable with no progressive decline. Belimumab exposure did not adversely affect AMH trajectories, and viral serologies showed no direct long-term impact on AMH levels.
CONCLUSIONS: This prospective longitudinal study highlights that diminished ovarian reserve is common in women with SLE. AMH levels remained stable over 24 months, with no adverse longitudinal association with belimumab exposure. Hydroxychloroquine use was associated with a lower prevalence of diminished ovarian reserve and warrants further investigation. Serial AMH assessment may support personalized reproductive counselling in women with SLE.

articles.title: Laparoscopic and Robot-Assisted Surgery for Gestational Trophoblastic Disease: A Scoping Review of Patient Selection and Intraoperative Precautions.
articles.authors: Gou R, Yuda M, Fukasawa H
articles.abstract: Guidelines for gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) state when hysterectomy is indicated, but say little about the operative route or what should be recorded during the operation. We conducted a Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review, reported to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), of laparoscopic and robot-assisted operations that resected or biopsied GTD tissue to establish which patients undergo these operations and what intraoperative precautions the reports contain. PubMed (August 18, 2026; 449 records) and Ichushi-Web (August 20, 2026; 329 records) were searched without language or date restriction, and backward citation chasing added two reports. The review maps what is reported; it estimates neither safety nor effectiveness, and no meta-analysis was performed. In total, 64 original reports describing 67 operations entered the main analysis, alongside 24 Ichushi-Web conference records as a supplementary layer; 54 were case reports, and the literature spans 1995 to 2026. GTD had been diagnosed before 38 of the 67 operations; before the other 29, it had not. The details needed to study intraperitoneal containment were rarely described: use or non-use of a uterine manipulator in five of 36 evaluable reports of operations on a retained uterus, morcellation in three of 36, a retrieval bag in two of 50, peritoneal washing cytology in six of 53, and pneumoperitoneum pressure in none of 52. A mechanical containment token was present in 17 of 57 evaluable reports, but of the 16 that could also be assessed for wording, 12 never used the words spillage, seeding, dissemination, or port-site. Port-site events were charted as an outcome and were not reported in 43 of the 49 reports in which that field was evaluable. Laparoscopic and robot-assisted surgery for GTD has been reported since 1995, mainly as single cases and in a preoperatively mixed population, and the intraoperative detail that would allow containment to be studied is usually absent. The gap this review identifies is one of reporting rather than of technique.

articles.title: Fetal and neonatal outcomes in planned versus unplanned pregnancies in people with spina bifida.
articles.authors: Berndl A, Condran G, Kfouri J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is limited information on the impact of pregnancy planning on neonatal outcomes in people with spina bifida (SB).
METHODS: This study is a sub-group analysis of The Spina Bifida Reproductive Health and Pregnancy Study, an online international cross-sectional survey. Pregnancy, birth and neonatal data were assessed using descriptive and chi-squared analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 209 pregnancies were included: 108 planned and 101 unplanned. The unplanned group included a greater risk of miscarriage/ectopic pregnancy (30%), unplanned fetal loss (34%), intrauterine growth restriction less than 5th percentile (16%) and babies with congenital anomalies. There was no statistically significant difference between unplanned and planned pregnancies in terms of admission to neonatal intensive care unit or risk of preterm birth.
CONCLUSION: People with SB have rates of unplanned pregnancy similar to the general population. Unplanned pregnancies appear to have increased fetal and neonatal risks. Findings suggest that pregnancy planning is a modifiable factor, which may improve outcomes.

articles.title: Function-preserving plasma kinetic enucleation of the prostate with bladder neck and 12 o'clock urethral mucosal preservation for large-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia: a single-center retrospective case series.
articles.authors: Yan W, Jia J, Huo Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-volume benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) poses a significant surgical challenge, as conventional transurethral resection yields suboptimal tissue removal efficiency and high rates of ejaculatory dysfunction. While endoscopic enucleation techniques (e.g., HoLEP and PKEP) offer improved efficacy, the systematic preservation of functional anatomical structures - particularly the bladder neck and anterior urethral mucosa - remains inadequately addressed in current practice.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and functional outcomes of function-preserving plasma kinetic enucleation of the prostate (FP-PKEP) - a modified technique incorporating systematic preservation of the bladder neck circular fibers and the 12 o'clock urethral mucosal strip - in patients with large-volume BPH.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective case series included 52 consecutive patients with large-volume BPH (prostate volume >80 mL, International Prostate Symptom Score [IPSS] > 20, maximum urinary flow rate [Qmax] < 10 mL/s) who underwent FP-PKEP between January 2025 and December 2025. The primary outcome was the change in IPSS at 3 months postoperatively; secondary outcomes included Qmax, post-void residual urine volume (PVR), quality of life (QoL) score, perioperative safety parameters, and functional preservation outcomes (urinary continence and ejaculatory function at 6 months).
RESULTS: All 52 patients (mean age 67.8 ± 7.2 years; mean prostate volume 93.7 ± 15.2 mL) successfully underwent FP-PKEP without conversion. Mean operative time was 72.5 ± 15.8 min; postoperative hemoglobin decrease was 9.8 ± 4.2 g/L; catheterization duration was 2.8 ± 0.9 days; and hospital stay was 4.2 ± 1.3 days. At 3 months, IPSS decreased from 26.1 ± 3.0 to 6.8 ± 2.6 (P < 0.001), and Qmax increased from 7.2 ± 1.6 to 21.2 ± 4.5 mL/s (P < 0.001). Transient stress urinary incontinence occurred in 4 patients (7.7%), all requiring no more than one pad per day and resolving within 1 month without surgical intervention. Among the 16 patients who were sexually active before surgery, antegrade ejaculation was preserved in 14 (87.5%) and suspected retrograde ejaculation was recorded in 2 (12.5%). No clinically apparent cases of permanent urinary incontinence, bladder neck contracture, or urethral stricture were observed during the 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In this uncontrolled case series, FP-PKEP showed a favorable safety profile and achieved significant relief of bladder…

articles.title: Mechanistic ODE modelling of ovarian tumour microenvironment dynamics under hesperidin exposure.
articles.authors: Dzik R
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer progression is driven by complex interactions among tumour, immune, stromal, metabolic and angiogenic processes. Although hesperidin exhibits anti-cancer and immunomodulatory activities, its integrated effects on the tumour microenvironment (TME) remain insufficiently understood. This study presents a mechanistic ODE-based framework integrating tumour growth, immune regulation, macrophage polarization, cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-mediated extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling, hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) - 1 α / vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-dependent angiogenesis, glucose-lactate metabolism and redox signalling within a hypothetical ovarian TME centred on PA-1 cells. Simulations across multiple hesperidin concentrations predicted dose-dependent suppression of tumour growth, reduced HIF - 1 α accumulation, angiogenesis, ECM stiffening and lactate production, accompanied by enhanced anti-tumour immune activity. Local one-at-a-time (OAT) and global Sobol' sensitivity analyses identified tumour growth kinetics, CAF-ECM interactions, metabolic regulation and selected hesperidin-response parameters as principal determinants of system behaviour. Although not calibrated for quantitative prediction, the proposed framework provides mechanistic insight into how hesperidin-mediated perturbations propagate through interconnected tumour-immune-stromal networks. The model should be regarded as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating platform supporting future experimental validation of hesperidin-mediated mechanisms in ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Sexual Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Men in a Tribal Community in Tamil Nadu: A Descriptive Phenomenological Study.
articles.authors: Beraro I, Gopalakrishnan R, Rose A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexual health is strongly influenced by sociocultural beliefs, yet evidence on sexual knowledge, attitudes, and practices among tribal men in India remains limited. This study explored these aspects among men from the Jawadhi Hills, a tribal community in southern India.
METHODS: A descriptive phenomenological qualitative study was conducted using seven focus group discussions involving 55 men aged 18-60 years, including migrant workers, teachers, and community representatives. Participants were recruited through multistage and purposive maximum variation sampling. Discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed, translated, and analyzed manually using inductive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Mobile phones and social media were the predominant sources of sexual information. Participants demonstrated basic awareness of contraception and sexually transmitted infections but held several misconceptions regarding semen, masturbation, menstruation, fertility, and male contraception. Traditional gender norms, menstrual restrictions, and community sanctions against extramarital relationships strongly influenced attitudes and practices. While digital media had increased access to sexual information, it also appeared to reinforce myths and misinformation. Limited privacy within households and conflicting beliefs about substance use and sexual performance further shaped their sexual behaviors.
CONCLUSIONS: Sexual knowledge among tribal men reflects a complex interplay of traditional cultural beliefs and expanding digital exposure. Persistent misconceptions and gaps in reproductive health literacy highlight the need for culturally appropriate, community-based sexual health education that addresses local beliefs while promoting evidence-based practices.

articles.title: Perineal Body Reconstruction for Anal Sphincter Insufficiency Following Obstetric Perineal Body Injury: Morphology-based Classification and Type-stratified Outcomes in 42 Cases.
articles.journal: Journal of the anus, rectum and colon
articles.authors: Murakami K, Nishimura Y, Mizukuro T
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Post-obstetric fecal incontinence is multifactorial, and structural aspects related to the perineal body may not be fully characterized within current frameworks. We propose a three-type morphology-based classification and report type-stratified outcomes after perineal body reconstruction, in which the lateral extensions of the perineal body (LEPB) are reapproximated without direct sphincter manipulation.
METHODS: Forty-two consecutive female patients (July 2022-December 2025) with post-obstetric anal sphincter insufficiency (Wexner ≥ 4) underwent perineal body reconstruction and were classified as Type 1 (rectovaginal fistula, n = 20), Type 2 (sphincter insufficiency without fistula, n = 14), or Type 3 (cloaca-like deformity, n = 8). The primary outcome was the 6-month change in Wexner score; clinical improvement was defined as a decrease ≥ 4 points. Post-operative scores were compared by Kruskal-Wallis and post-hoc Mann-Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction (adjusted α = 0.0167).
RESULTS: The overall Wexner score decreased from 11.4 ± 4.7 to 3.4 ± 4.3 (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.92), with a 95.2% clinical improvement rate (40/42) and 50.0% complete remission (21/42). Post-operative scores differed among types (Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.010); after Bonferroni correction, only Type 1 vs Type 2 remained significant (raw p = 0.003; adjusted p = 0.009). Type 1, 2, and 3 improvement rates were 100%, 85.7%, and 100%.
CONCLUSIONS: The morphology-based classification linked preoperative assessment to type-specific surgical considerations and outcome expectations. Perineal body reconstruction, which targets the connective-tissue scaffold rather than the sphincter muscle, may complement muscle-level sphincteroplasty and neuromodulation; prospective comparative evaluation is warranted.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of ultrasonography-based risk models in differentiating between benign and malignant ovarian tumors in a Chinese cohort.
articles.authors: Li W, Sun Z, Huang Q et al.
articles.abstract:
​​BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-based risk models provide a valuable tool to support non-expert clinicians in evaluating adnexal masses, potentially reducing unnecessary surgeries for benign conditions. However, their implementation in clinical practice across China remains suboptimal, and direct comparisons of their diagnostic accuracy within this specific population are still needed.
​OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of three ultrasonography-based risk models-the International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) Simple Rules (with expert adjudication for inconclusive cases), the IOTA Assessment of Different Neoplasias in the Adnexa (ADNEX) model, and the Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS)-for distinguishing benign from malignant adnexal lesions in a Chinese cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective diagnostic study was conducted at a single Chinese academic medical center and included consecutive patients aged 18 to 89 years with adnexal masses that were managed surgically between January 2023 and December 2024. Each adnexal lesion was systematically evaluated using the IOTA Simple Rules, ADNEX model, and O-RADS classification. The diagnostic performance of these models was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and likelihood ratios, using surgical pathology as the reference standard. A secondary analysis evaluated the models' performance stratified by menopausal status. An additional analysis was to evaluate the supplementary value of tumor markers for the O-RADS model.
​RESULTS: A total of 459 female patients with a 15.5% malignant tumor prevalence were included. Mean age was 43.0 (15.2) years overall, with 40.7 (14.4) in benign and 55.3 (13.3) in malignant cases. Overall, 121 (26.4%) patients were postmenopausal. The AUCs for discriminative performance of the ADNEX and O-RADS models were 0.95 (95%CI, 0.93-0.97) and 0.96 (95%CI, 0.94-0.97), respectively. After converting the ADNEX continuous individualized risk into the discrete ordinal categories of O-RADS, the ADNEX performance was reduced to an AUC of 0.92 (95%CI, 0.90-0.95). The AUC of the Simple Rules was 0.95 (95%CI, 0.93-0.97) and yielded a sensitivity of 95.8% (95%CI, 88.1%-99.1%), specificity of 94.3% (95%CI, 91.5%-96.4%). For a binary comparison of all models (benign vs malignant), a uniform 10% risk threshold (O-RADS score of 4-5) was used. The sensitivity…

articles.title: Effective doses of propofol and oliceridine fumarate for painless hysteroscopy: a two-phase dose-finding study using Dixon's up-and-down method.
articles.authors: Chen J, Shao Y, Sun H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Painless hysteroscopy is widely performed in gynecological practice, yet achieving an optimal balance between anesthetic safety and patient comfort remains challenging. Combining propofol with oliceridine may mitigate respiratory depression and injection pain associated with conventional regimens, though the effective doses for this combination have not been established. This study sought to identify the optimal dose combination of propofol and oliceridine for use in painless hysteroscopy.
METHODS: Fifty-one women scheduled for elective painless hysteroscopy were enrolled in this prospective, two-phase dose-finding study. In Phase I, all patients received a fixed 1 mg dose of oliceridine at induction; propofol was subsequently titrated from an initial 2 mg/kg using Dixon's up-and-down sequential method in 0.1 mg/kg intervals. Probit regression modeling was used to derive propofol ED50 and ED95, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) obtained via the delta method; isotonic regression served as sensitivity analysis. In Phase II, propofol was fixed at the Phase I ED50, and oliceridine was titrated from 1 mg in 0.1 mg increments, with ED50 and ED95 determined identically. An effective response was defined as no body movement, no frowning, and a Ramsay Sedation Score ≥5 during cervical dilation and hysteroscope insertion. Secondary outcomes included Nociception Level Index (NOX), Cerebral State Index (CSI), hemodynamic parameters, and adverse events.
RESULTS: The ED50 and ED95 of propofol were 1.818 mg/kg (95% CI: 1.696-1.940) and 2.223 mg/kg (95% CI: 1.840-2.605), respectively. For oliceridine, the corresponding ED50 was 0.663 mg (95% CI: 0.605-0.720) and ED95 was 0.813 mg (95% CI: 0.692-0.934). Pearson goodness-of-fit tests confirmed adequate model fit for both phases (propofol: P = 0.755; oliceridine: P = 0.899), and isotonic regression yielded ED50 estimates within 3% of probit-derived values. Hemodynamic parameters remained stable throughout sedation, with no serious adverse events observed.
CONCLUSION: The propofol-oliceridine appears to be a feasible option for painless hysteroscopy, with an acceptable safety profile provided that continuous airway monitoring is maintained. The ED50 and ED95 values observed in this study offer preliminary dosing guidance for outpatient practice.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=241260, identifier ChiCTR2500102118.

articles.title: Association between serum estradiol levels on the hCG trigger day and euploid blastocyst rate in preimplantation genetic testing cycles: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Shuai J, Liu W, Sun X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While serum estradiol (E2) predicts ovarian response and endometrial receptivity, its role in embryonic development remains unclear. This study assessed the association between E2 levels on the day of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) trigger and the euploid blastocyst rate (EBR) in preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) cycles.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 3,082 couples who underwent PGT between 2017 and 2022, comprising 18,036 oocytes and 5,009 blastocysts screened using next-generation sequencing. Oocytes were stratified into tertiles based on serum E2 levels on the hCG trigger day: Group 1 (<3149 pg/mL), Group 2 (3149-4725.66 pg/mL), and Group 3 (≥4725.67 pg/mL). Associations between serum E2 levels and both blastocyst formation rate (BFR) and EBR were assessed using univariate stratified analyses and multivariable generalized estimating equation (GEE) models (crude, Model I, Model II) accounting for patient-level clustering. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis with three knots, collinearity diagnostics (variance inflation factor, VIF), and formal E2 × total gonadotropin (Gn) dose interaction tests were additionally performed.
RESULTS: Univariate stratified analyses showed subgroup-specific patterns: higher E2 generally correlated with lower blastocyst formation rate (BFR) yet higher EBR. In fully adjusted GEE Model II, E2 was not associated with BFR (Group3 vs Group1: aOR 1.050, 95%CI 0.910-1.212, P = 0.502; P-trend=0.653), while high E2 was associated with higher EBR (aOR 1.295, 95%CI 1.028-1.631, P = 0.028; P-trend=0.047). RCS revealed no significant overall E2-BFR (P-overall=0.107; P-nonlinearity=0.055) or E2-EBR associations (P-overall=0.100; P-nonlinearity=0.119), although the EBR curve showed an upward high-E2 trend consistent with tertile results. No multicollinearity was detected (all VIF <6, range 1.137-5.399), and no significant E2-Gn interactions existed (all P>0.05). Sensitivity analysis excluding oocyte number yielded consistent EBR estimates (aOR 1.232, 95%CI 1.006-1.508, P = 0.044).
CONCLUSION: In PGT cycles, elevated hCG-trigger-day E2 was not associated with BFR but was modestly associated with higher EBR. These observational findings require prospective validation and should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal or protective effect of E2 on embryonic chromosomal integrity.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture improves endometrial receptivity and pregnancy outcomes in controlled ovarian hyperstimulation rats by restoring Per2 circadian rhythm.
articles.authors: Zhu Q, Li Q, Zan Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) is a critical step in in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer (IVF-ET). However, the decline in endometrial receptivity caused by COH severely restricts the success rate of implantation. Previous studies mostly focused on static molecular events, lacking a systematic exploration from the perspective of dynamic rhythms. This study aims to explore whether electroacupuncture (EA) can improve endometrial receptivity and pregnancy outcomes by repairing the disordered rhythm of the core clock gene Per2 in the endometrium caused by COH from the perspective of chronobiology.
METHODS: A COH model was established using 126 Sprague - Dawley (SD) rats. Following EA intervention, dynamic sampling was conducted during the implantation window to assess clock gene rhythmicity, the expression of receptivity - related factors, and uterine morphological changes. Per2-/- mice were used to preliminarily investigate whether Per2 participates in mediating the effects of EA.
RESULTS: COH induced an abnormal increase in serum progesterone, leading to desynchronization of the endometrial clock gene network. Among them, the peak delay of the core clock gene Per2 was highly coupled with the abnormal peak of progesterone in time, and presented an anti - phase oscillatory pattern with the expression of the angiogenesis factor Vegf. During the implantation window, the expression of Vegf and integrin αvβ3 was down - regulated, the development of pinopodes degenerated, and the pregnancy rate was significantly reduced. EA could correct the abnormal progesterone level, repair the rhythm parameters of Per2, up - regulate the expression of Vegf and integrin αvβ3, improve the development of pinopodes, and significantly increase the pregnancy rate. In Per2-/- mice, the up - regulating effect of EA on Vegf and Integrin αvβ3 was significantly weakened, preliminarily suggesting that Per2 may participate in mediating the effects of EA on endometrial receptivity.
CONCLUSION: This study provided preliminary evidence for a novel mechanism by which COH impairs endometrial receptivity from the perspective of dynamic circadian rhythm, providing experimental evidence for EA as an adjuvant intervention strategy based on circadian clock regulation in IVF-ET cycles.

articles.title: The PCOS-to-PMOS shift in the broader history of nomenclature changes and its uncertain impact on clinical practice.
articles.authors: Aleksejeva-Zagura E, Laudański P, Acharya G et al.
articles.abstract: Proposed renaming of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) aims to broaden multidisciplinary care. However, it may obscure reproductive manifestations and introduce phenotypic ascertainment bias. Historical examples of nomenclature changes suggest that clinical benefits depend heavily on diagnostic, therapeutic, and etiological advances and education. Although formal cost-effectiveness analysis of nomenclature changes are lacking, our preliminary estimates suggest that implementation may entail substantial cost and healthcare resource requirements, while its clinical benefits remain uncertain.

articles.title: Genetic and genomic medicine across the lung transplant continuum: inherited disease, pharmacogenomics, and molecular surveillance.
articles.authors: Katpally RR, Pena T, Klesney-Tait J
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genetic information is increasingly relevant across the lung transplant continuum. A molecular diagnosis of the recipient's native lung disease can refine candidate evaluation, identify extrapulmonary vulnerability, guide family counseling, and anticipate posttransplant complications. Pharmacogenetic and molecular biomarkers offer opportunities to individualize therapy and allograft surveillance. This review summarizes the clinical utility and limitations of these emerging approaches.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent literature highlights the importance of cystic fibrosis in the era of highly effective cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators, short telomere syndromes and hereditary pulmonary fibrosis, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, primary ciliary dyskinesia, pharmacogenomics, and molecular surveillance. Among these, recognition of short telomere syndromes before transplantation has the clearest implications for multidisciplinary risk assessment and posttransplant management. CYP3A5 can inform initial tacrolimus dosing, but therapeutic drug monitoring remains indispensable; thiopurine methyltransferase and Nudix hydrolase 15 are actionable when azathioprine is used. Donor-derived cell-free DNA is a promising, noninvasive marker of allograft injury and prognosis, yet it is not specific for rejection and cannot independently replace microbiologic assessment, donor-specific antibody testing, bronchoscopy, or biopsy.
SUMMARY: Genomic tools are most useful when applied selectively and interpreted within clinical context. A tiered implementation model offers a practical path for incorporating genomic tools, improving patient outcomes while limiting overinterpretation.

articles.title: ATR inhibitors and gemcitabine synergize to induce cell death in TP53-mutant, ATRX-wildtype uterine leiomyosarcoma.
articles.authors: Doherty ME, Malik M, Otsuka Y et al.
articles.abstract: Inactivating mutations in TP53 and ATRX are key alterations defining the genomic landscape of uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS), creating chronic replication stress and increasing dependency on Ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3-related kinase (ATR) signaling for survival. ATR-CHK1 signaling limits the efficacy of standard-of-care gemcitabine by facilitating the stabilization of stalled replication forks and preventing lethal DNA strand breaks in checkpoint-deficient cells. Here, we show that ATR inhibitors (elimusertib, ceralasertib, berzosertib) preferentially synergize with gemcitabine over docetaxel or doxorubicin, across a panel of TP53-mutant/ATRX-wildtype uLMS models. When simultaneously administered, gemcitabine/elimusertib demonstrated enhanced synergy and efficacy compared to standard-of-care gemcitabine/docetaxel. This combination benefit was absent in a TP53-wildtype uterine sarcoma control line, highlighting TP53 mutation status as a critical predictive biomarker. Combined gemcitabine/ATRi treatment demonstrated reciprocal potency enhancement at low-nanomolar concentrations and significantly increased apoptotic populations compared to monotherapy. Gemcitabine monotherapy induced CHK1 (S345) phosphorylation and a corresponding S-phase arrest. Elimusertib abrogated this checkpoint, transforming protective S-phase arrest into a cytotoxic response characterized by a marked increase in the sub-G1 population. This transition was driven by the inhibition of gemcitabine-induced CHK1 phosphorylation, resulting in marked accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage (γH2AX) and the induction of apoptosis as evidenced by cleaved caspase-3 expression. These findings demonstrate that elimusertib strongly potentiates gemcitabine-induced damage to kill TP53-mutant uLMS in vitro, outperforming standard gemcitabine/docetaxel when concurrently administered. This combination strategy broadens the clinical utility of ATR inhibitors to uLMS harboring the prevalent TP53-mutant/ATRX-wildtype genotype and supports the clinical evaluation of gemcitabine/ATRi combinations as a novel therapy for uLMS.

articles.title: The impact of midlife hormonal treatment on lower urinary tract symptoms.
articles.authors: Byrne EH, Von Bargen EC
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Women in midlife are increasingly interested in receiving menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) for symptom relief. Increased patient interest and MHT prescribing require a clinical understanding of the effect of hormonal treatment on lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), which often develop in midlife and worsen with age. This review summarizes the divergent LUTS effects conferred by hormone type and mode of delivery.
RECENT FINDINGS: Vaginal estrogen is well established to help alleviate LUTS, and recent data suggest that periurethral application is noninferior to intravaginal application. Many studies have shown that systemic estrogen results in new and worsening LUTS, and recent studies have begun to probe this opposing effect. Selective estrogen receptor modulators are less well studied but seem to have a less deleterious effect on LUTS than MHT.
SUMMARY: The mechanism of the divergent effects of estrogen on LUTS by route of administration remains unclear, but further research may help provide more individualized hormone therapy options for women in midlife experiencing systemic and/or LUTS.

articles.title: Subtle Alterations of Tidal Breathing Variables in Healthy Late Preterm Neonates at Term-Equivalent Age.
articles.authors: Ozan E, Öztürk S, Akcan AB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late-preterm birth is associated with increased respiratory morbidity, but tidal breathing at term-equivalent age remains incompletely characterized. We hypothesized that healthy late-preterm neonates would differ from term neonates, with the between-group difference in tPTEF/tE designated as the primary outcome.
METHODS: In this prospective cross-sectional study, 60 healthy late-preterm and 60 term neonates underwent tidal breathing analysis (MasterScreen PAED) at term-equivalent age (40 weeks' postmenstrual age) during natural quiet sleep without sedation.
RESULTS: Late-preterm neonates had lower tPTEF/tE (27.4 ± 7.0% vs. 31.2 ± 6.9%; Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = 0.028; Cohen's d = 0.544) and VPTEF/VE [28.6 (25.1-31.0)% vs. 32.1 (27.3-35.5)%; adjusted p = 0.028; Cliff's δ = 0.304] than term neonates. Respiratory rate was higher (53.2 ± 9.1 vs. 49.6 ± 9.5 breaths/min), but not significant after correction (adjusted p = 0.126). No other tidal breathing variables differed significantly after correction. In the primary multivariable model, each additional week of exact gestational age was associated with a 1.18-percentage-point increase in tPTEF/tE after adjustment for sex, body weight, and crown-heel length (B = 1.182; 95% CI, 0.540-1.823; β = 0.323; p < 0.001). When postnatal age replaced gestational age, the association was inverse (B = -0.167/day; 95% CI, -0.263 to -0.071; β = -0.306; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: At term-equivalent age, healthy late-preterm neonates had modestly lower tPTFEF/tE and VPTEF/VE than term neonates. These findings may reflect subtle maturational differences in expiratory flow dynamics associated with late-preterm birth.

articles.title: Surgical Outcomes and Recurrence-Free Survival After Laparoscopic Sacrocolpopexy, Laparoscopic Colposuspension Sec Shull, and Vaginal Colpohysterectomy and Colposuspension: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Romeo P, Ronsini C, Tassone A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare surgical outcomes and recurrence-free survival (RFS) among laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy (LSC), laparoscopic colposuspension sec Shull (LCSS), and vaginal colpohysterectomy and colposuspension (VCH) for pelvic organ prolapse involving the apical compartment.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients undergoing surgery for pelvic organ prolapse involving the apical compartment. Patients were divided into three groups according to surgical technique: LSC, LCSS, and VCH. The primary outcome was prolapse recurrence. Secondary outcomes included operative time, postoperative complications, and reoperation rate. RFS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models, with LSC as the reference. A predefined subanalysis was performed in patients with severe pelvic organ prolapse (Stage III-IV).
RESULTS: A total of 204 patients were included. Median follow-up was 25 months (IQR 16-43) after LSC, 24 months (IQR 15-29) after LCSS, and 31 months (IQR 29-48.25) after VCH. Twenty recurrences occurred: five after LSC, nine after LCSS, and six after VCH. Operative time differed significantly among techniques, while postoperative complication rates were comparable. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed worse RFS after LCSS. In Cox analysis, LCSS was associated with a higher recurrence hazard than LSC (HR 17.20, 95% CI 3.67-80.57; p < 0.001), whereas VCH was not (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.26-2.85; p = 0.80). Concomitant anti-incontinence procedures were performed in only five patients and were not associated with recurrence or reoperation (both Fisher's exact p = 1.00).
CONCLUSIONS: LCSS showed significantly worse RFS than LSC, despite similar complication rates and intermediate operative times. These findings may suggest reduced short- to mid-term RFS; however, they should be interpreted with caution given the retrospective, non-randomized design and potential treatment allocation bias. VCH showed the shortest operative times and no significant differences in recurrence risk compared with LSC.

articles.title: Metabolic effects of botryosphaeran, a (1→3)(1→6)-β-D-glucan, in a model of gestational obesity: maternal and progeny developmental impacts.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.authors: Silva DIFD, Fabiane IZ, Pio AA et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is associated with several disorders, and its neonatal impacts include macrosomia. Botryosphaeran, a (1→3)(1→6)-β-D-glucan, produced by the fungus Botryosphaeria rhodina exhibits antiobesogenic effects in rats. The objective of this work was to evaluate, for the first time, the effects of botryosphaeran on obese and non-obese rats during the pregnancy period and its effects on offspring. Female Wistar rats (n = 18) were separated into two groups: control, which received commercial ration and water; and obese, that received high-fat ration and water with sucrose (300 g/liter), for 8 weeks. In the 8th week, the rats were divided in the proportion of two rats to one breeding male. After confirmation of pregnancy, the females were subdivided into 4 groups: Pregnancy Control, Botryosphaeran Pregnancy Control, Pregnancy Obese, and Botryosphaeran Pregnancy Obese. In the last 2-thirds of gestation, rats of the botryosphaeran group received the -glucan solution (12 mg/kg/day, via gavage), the control and obese rats received saline solution. At the end of the experiment, the mothers and their offspring were evaluated. Obese mothers had fat accumulation, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. Botryosphaeran significantly reduced blood glucose, corrected insulin resistance and dyslipidemia. The female and male offspring of the obese group showed higher weight gain, adipose tissue accumulation, soleus muscle reduction, hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. Botryosphaeran was effective in correcting these parameters. In conclusion, botryosphaeran exerts significant and promising effects, including antiobesogenic, hypocholesterolemic, and insulin sensitizing action in mothers and their offspring, demonstrating botryosphaeran as a potential agent to prevent obesity and its comorbidities.

articles.title: The Influence of Type of Maternity Care Provider on Early Breastfeeding Rates. A Retrospective Cohort Study of All Women Who Gave Birth in Victoria, Australia 2010 to 2020.
articles.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
articles.ta: Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol
articles.authors: Johnsson M, Holmlund S, Augustsson I et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding plays a vital role in infant health and development. Maternity care providers are well-positioned to support breastfeeding during the postnatal period. In Australia, there are multiple options for public and private maternity care. To date, there is limited information on how caregiver and hospital type influence early breastfeeding.
AIM: To examine associations between type of care provider during antenatal and intrapartum care, hospital type and early breastfeeding rates in Victoria, Australia.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all live, singleton, term births in Victoria, Australia 2010-2020 (N = 638,809). We investigated associations between variables using bivariate and multivariable logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Most women (95.7%) initiated breastfeeding, and 77.1% provided the last feed before hospital discharge exclusively from the breast. About a quarter of infants (27.0%) received commercial milk formula while in hospital. Women who received antenatal or intrapartum care from a midwife or general practitioner were more likely to initiate breastfeeding, and their infants to have their last feed before discharge from the breast, and less likely to receive formula in hospital compared to those cared for by an obstetrician. Dyads who received care in public hospitals had better breastfeeding outcomes than those in private hospitals. The small proportion (0.2%) who received private midwifery care showed the most favourable breastfeeding outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Early breastfeeding outcomes in Victoria differ in relation to antenatal and intrapartum care provider and hospital type, and indicate disparities in supportive breastfeeding practices. Implementation of Baby Friendly Health procedures may help standardise care across these settings.

articles.title: BRCA1 Mutation-Recognizing Tetrahedral Framework Nucleic Acid Nanoplatform Enables Coordinated PARP/WEE1 Inhibition and STING-Associated Antitumor Immunity in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Wang C, Yao M, Xie J et al.
articles.abstract: Improving therapeutic efficacy and antitumor immune responsiveness in BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer remains challenging. Here, we developed a BRCA1 mutation-guided tetrahedral framework nucleic acid nanosystem, FBOA-tFNA, for coordinated intracellular delivery of the PARP inhibitor olaparib and the WEE1 inhibitor adavosertib. After folate receptor-mediated uptake, FBOA-tFNA recognizes BRCA1 mutant RNA through toehold-mediated strand displacement, enabling mutation-selective beacon activation, while drug release is independently regulated by reduction-responsive disulfide cleavage. Coordinated PARP/WEE1 inhibition amplified DNA damage, impaired G2/M checkpoint protection, and promoted tumor-cell killing in BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer models. Resulting DNA damage-associated intracellular dsDNA signals activated STING-associated signaling, type I interferon responses, immunogenic cell death (ICD)-associated stress, dendritic-cell maturation, and CD8+ T-cell activation. Engineered patient-derived ovarian cancer organoids expressing a BRCA12594delC-containing transcript further supported the mutation-selective recognition and therapeutic potential of FBOA-tFNA ex vivo. In vivo, FBOA-tFNA showed tumor-associated fluorescence accumulation, BRCA1 mutant-transcript recognition-associated beacon activation, enhanced antitumor efficacy, and preliminary repeated-dose tolerability. Moreover, FBOA-tFNA enhanced antitumor immune responses and improved the response to anti-PD-1 therapy, accompanied by increased effector and memory-like T-cell populations. This programmable DNA nanoplatform provides a personalized combination strategy for coordinated DNA-damage therapy and immunomodulation in BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Accessory Cavitating Uterine Masses/Malformation: An Important Differential in Women With Intractable Dysmenorrhea and Chronic Pelvic Pain Across All Ages.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Vatsa R, Dhiman S, Kulshrestha V et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Accessory cavitated uterine malformation or mass (ACUM) is a rare and under-recognized cause of dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain (CPP). Various diagnostic criteria have been proposed; patients may present with atypical features. This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and management outcomes of ACUM.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data was done at a tertiary care institution over 6 years. All women diagnosed with ACUM were included. Clinical presentation, imaging, preoperative diagnosis, intraoperative picture, and management outcomes were analyzed.
RESULT: Eighteen women were enrolled. The median age at presentation was 26.5 years (18-46), with 17 in the reproductive age group and one postmenopausal. The median duration of symptoms was 4 years (2 months to 11 years). Dysmenorrhea with prominent pain on one side, localized to the side of the lesion, was the predominant symptom, occurring in 17/18 (94.4%). Of these, 10/18 (55.6%) experienced both CPP and dysmenorrhea, 7/18 (38.9%) had only dysmenorrhea. Only CPP was reported in 1/18 (5.6%), woman with postmenopausal ACUM. On initial 2D-USG, one case was correctly diagnosed, while 5/18(27.8%) were misdiagnosed as rudimentary horn, 7/18(38.9%) as degenerated fibroid, 4/18(22.2%) as endometrioma, and 1/18(5.6%) as dermoid cyst. Diagnosis was confirmed on further imaging with 3D-USG or MRI in 11/18 (61.1%) cases. Seventeen women underwent surgical management, with 16/17 had excision, and one postmenopausal woman was treated by laparoscopic aspiration.
CONCLUSION: ACUM is an important differential of intractable dysmenorrhea or CPP, especially if pain is localized to either side, even in postmenopausal females.

articles.title: Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes and Early Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease Risk: Vascular and Inflammatory Markers.
articles.authors: Spiro L, Accortt EE, Kilpatrick S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) have a 2- to 8-fold increased risk of future atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), yet the mechanistic pathways are not well-defined. Potential vascular and inflammatory factors contributing to ASCVD are not known in women with a history of preeclampsia (PE) or spontaneous preterm delivery (sPTD).
OBJECTIVE: Describe the vascular and inflammatory factors of women with PE or sPTD and compare differences that may contribute to ASCVD risk.
METHODS: Women 18 years or older, 2-3 years postpartum, with a history of PE (N = 19) or sPTD (N = 13), and reference controls (N = 19; delivery ≥ 37 weeks' gestation without APO) were enrolled. All cohorts underwent phlebotomy to measure inflammatory biomarkers and SphygmoCor testing for vascular function, including augmentation index (AIx75), central pulse pressure (CPP), and pulse wave velocity (PWV).
RESULTS: Participants with sPTD had higher interleukin-8 concentrations of 6.6 pg/mL (interquartile range [IQR] 5.7, 8.7), compared with 4.7 pg/mL (IQR 2.2, 6.3) in controls (p = 0.0279). Brachial systolic pressure was higher in PE (120 [standard deviation or SD 12.01]) than in sPTD (110.9 [SD 13.8]) or controls (108.6 [SD 9.22], [p = 0.0071]). Central systolic pressure was higher in PE (109.8 [SD 11.4]) than in sPTD (99.3 [SD 13.88]) or controls (98.4 [SD 8.94], [p = 0.0069]). CPP was higher in PE (34.2, SD 3.62) than in sPTD (30.8, SD 3.34) and controls (30.3, SD 3.67 [p = 0.0027]).
CONCLUSIONS: Vascular and inflammatory markers in PE or sPTD 2-3 years postpartum are higher compared with reference controls. Future studies should investigate vascular and inflammatory function in larger cohorts and prospectively evaluate contribution to CVD risk.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Prescriptions for Prenatal and Postpartum Women in Japan: A Large Claims Database Study.
articles.authors: Obara R, Sakai T, Ishikawa T et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of antipsychotic prescriptions before, during, and after pregnancy in Japan, with a focus on new prescriptions and continuation after pregnancy confirmation. We conducted a claims-based analysis using a Japanese claims database (analytic period: 2010-2022). Antipsychotic prescription prevalence and new prescriptions were assessed from 180 days before pregnancy through 180 days postpartum. To assess continuation after pregnancy confirmation, prescription status was evaluated across gestational weeks 0-4, 5-13, and from 14 weeks to delivery. Among 120 735 women, 1698 (140.6/10 000 deliveries) received at least one antipsychotic prescription, including 809 (67.0/10 000 deliveries) during pregnancy. Prescription prevalence decreased during the first and second trimesters but increased postpartum. New prescriptions were less frequent during pregnancy but increased after delivery. Among 611 women prescribed antipsychotics during 0-4 weeks' gestation, 482 (78.9%) continued and 129 (21.1%) discontinued prescription during weeks 5-13; of those who continued prescription during 5-13 weeks, 334 (54.7%) continued until delivery. Evaluation of major indications showed that continuation until delivery was highest in those with schizophrenia (63.6%), followed by bipolar disorder (51.0%). This study provides the first comprehensive description of perinatal antipsychotic prescription trends in Japan. Substantial prescription discontinuation occurred after pregnancy confirmation. Increases in postpartum prescriptions might reflect new prescriptions or resumption among women who had discontinued treatment during pregnancy. These findings offer foundational epidemiological insights into real-world perinatal antipsychotic use.

articles.title: Aspirin Use for the Prevention of Preeclampsia, an Evidence-Based Review.
articles.authors: Patel D, Kallash M, Frishman WH
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that is defined by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation along with proteinuria or evidence of end-organ dysfunction. Affecting 2-8% of pregnancies worldwide, preeclampsia remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. This disorder originates secondary to defective placentation during the first trimester, causing incomplete remodeling of the uterine spiral arteries, resulting in placental hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and the release of anti-angiogenic factors into the maternal circulation. This pathophysiology provided researchers a rationale for the use of low-dose aspirin as a preventive strategy for preeclampsia. Early studies investigated low-dose aspirin initiated at variable gestational ages and failed to show significant reductions in the incidence of preeclampsia. However, over the years, multiple meta-analyses studying aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention revealed a consistent decrease in the incidence of preeclampsia with the use of low-dose aspirin initiated at or before 16 weeks of gestation, with the efficacy being largely dependent on the time of initiation. In 2017, a randomized controlled trial demonstrated a statistically and clinically significant reduction in the incidence of preeclampsia leading to preterm delivery with aspirin initiated before 16 weeks gestation in women identified as high risk by first-trimester algorithm-based screening. Based on the strong evidence in support of aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention, current guidelines recommend initiation of aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks and ideally before 16 weeks for all pregnant women at increased risk for preeclampsia.

articles.title: Beyond Blood Cultures and Echocardiography: Emerging Diagnostics for Infective Endocarditis.
articles.authors: Park H, Dhand A
articles.abstract: Management of infective endocarditis (IE) is often confounded by the presence of prosthetic valves, transcatheter prostheses, and cardiovascular implantable electronic devices, as well as by changing epidemiologic risks and antimicrobial resistance patterns. For the diagnosis of IE, blood cultures and echocardiography remain foundational, but important gaps persist, particularly in culture-negative and prosthetic/device-associated infections. Contemporary diagnostic criteria and guidelines now support a multimodality approach incorporating molecular microbiology and advanced imaging. This review summarizes emerging technologies including broad-range 16S/18S/28S rRNA polymerase chain reaction and sequencing, fluorescence in situ hybridization coupled with sequencing, targeted and shotgun metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), plasma microbial cell-free DNA, cardiac computed tomography, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron-emission tomography/computed tomography. We also examine the potential role of artificial intelligence in echocardiographic interpretation and of large language models in multimodal data integration. Current evidence suggests that tissue-based molecular testing generally provides greater microbiologic yield than valve culture in culture-negative IE, while blood-based mNGS and microbial cell-free DNA may extend pathogen detection after antibiotic exposure and reduce reliance on tissue-based diagnosis. However, heterogeneity in specimen handling, sequencing pipelines, contamination control, reporting thresholds, and clinical interpretation remains a major barrier to implementation. Future progress should move beyond pathogen detection toward rapid, reproducible, clinically actionable diagnosis that integrates organism identification, anatomic localization, disseminated disease, and personalized treatment. Prospective outcome trials, standardized workflows, cost-effectiveness studies, and multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team integration can help determine whether these technologies translate into better antimicrobial stewardship, procedural decision-making, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal Obesity Is Associated With Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Matched Electronic Health Record Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Roberts C, Smith R, Odeh S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to define the prevalence of obesity in the first trimester of pregnancy among women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk.
RESULTS: Overall, 22.6% (64/283; 95% CI 17.7%-27.5%) of pregnancies in women with IBD met ethnicity-adjusted criteria for obesity. Increasing obesity class was associated with stepwise increases in gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, venous thromboembolism (VTE), emergency caesarean section and high birthweight. Matching yielded 177 IBD pregnancies and 1062 controls. Obesity was independently associated with the composite adverse pregnancy outcome (OR 1.63; 95% CI 1.15-2.33; p = 0.007), whereas no statistically significant additional association was identified for IBD diagnosis alone (OR 0.74; 95% CI 0.53-1.03; p = 0.073). Among IBD pregnancies, aspirin was recommended in 39.3% (86/219). Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) was prescribed in 21.6% (19/88) of pregnancies classified post hoc as intermediate or high VTE risk.
CONCLUSION: More than one in five pregnancies in women with IBD were complicated by obesity. Obesity was strongly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas this study did not identify a significant additional effect attributable to IBD diagnosis alone. Preventive prescribing with aspirin and LMWH represents an opportunity for improved antenatal care.

articles.title: Association of third-trimester maternal lipid levels with adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus: a retrospective single-center study using intrapartum data.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.authors: Yang Y, Peng Y, Fan J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the relationships between maternal factors and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), as well as third‑trimester maternal lipids and adverse pregnancy outcomes among GDM patients.
METHODS: This study enrolled 3,973 pregnant women, divided into a control group (n = 3166) and a GDM group (n = 807). The GDM group was further divided into well-controlled (n = 152) and poorly controlled subgroups (n = 655). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with GDM risk. Baseline clinical/laboratory characteristics were compared across groups via parametric, nonparametric, and chi‑square tests to assess associations of third‑trimester maternal lipid levels with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated the predictive values of body mass index (BMI) and third‑trimester maternal lipid levels.
RESULTS: Age (OR = 1.069, 95% CI:1.050-1.087, p < .001), overweight (OR = 1.678 95% CI:1.396-2.013, p < .001), and obesity (OR = 2.018, 95% CI:1.511-2.677, p < .001) are key risk factors for GDM. Significant differences existed in age (p = .001), BMI (p < .001), fasting blood glucose (FBG, p < .001) and 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose (2hPPG, p = .001) across subgroups, as well as triglycerides (TG, p < .001), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C, p = .001), and free fatty acids (FFAs, p < .001) among the three groups. Subgroup analysis by lipid levels showed TG predominantly affected delivery mode (p = .031), neonatal birth weight (p = .005), and quantitative blood loss (QBL, p = .019) in GDM, while HDL-C mainly influenced fetal growth curve (p = .004) and neonatal birth weight (p = .002). Subgroup analysis by triglyceride-glucose index (TyG index) revealed significant differences in glycemic control (p = .002), delivery mode (p = .002), neonatal weight (p = .005), and QBL (p = .005). The area under the curve of pre-pregnancy BMI for GDM complicated by hypertensive disorders of pregnancy was 0.738, third-trimester BMI 0.720, and 0.709 for macrosomia prediction in non-advanced-age women with GDM.
CONCLUSION: Age, overweight, and obesity are independent risk factors for GDM. Among women with GDM, third-trimester lipid levels are associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Therefore, lipid levels should be considered in GDM clinical management, rather than focusing exclusively on glycemic control.

articles.title: The Impact of Delayed School Entry on Developmental Outcomes in Very Preterm Children: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Haefke A, Schedewi A, Mehring C et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate whether delayed school entry (DSE) is associated with everyday functioning and participation in children born very preterm to inform the evidence-based guideline of follow-up of preterm born children.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of the literature and analysed outcome data at 10 years of age of a prospective cohort study of 1620 children born in 2009-2016 at < 32 gestational weeks. Children with DSE were compared to those with age-appropriate school entry (ASE) regarding everyday functioning and participation, using standardized parent- and self-report questionnaires.
