RESULTS: In the cohort, DSE was associated with less favourable outcomes (mean [standard deviation]): participation (ASE 95.8 [8.5]; DSE 90.3 [14.0]; p < 0.001), attention (3.6 [1.2]; 4.1 [1.3]; p < 0.001), internalizing problems (4.5 [3.3]; 5.7 [4.0]; p = 0.01), executive function (52 [11]; 58 [13]; p < 0.001). The proportion of children with special educational needs was higher in the DSE group (9.8% vs. 34%; p < 0.001). After adjustment for confounders, no differences remained at 10 years. ASE based on chronological age was associated with delayed transition to secondary school.
CONCLUSION: After adjustment, DSE did not affect everyday functioning and participation at 10 years or the timely transition to secondary school. School entry should consider corrected age for prematurity. Further research should examine long-term academic outcomes.

articles.title: Simultaneous acquisition of maternal and dual-fetal electrocardiography with maternal haemodynamic monitoring in anaesthetized pregnant rats.
articles.authors: Pardun SP, Duff S, Ward P et al.
articles.abstract: Experimental approaches that acquire maternal haemodynamics together with direct cardiac signals from more than one fetus remain limited. We developed a standardized in vivo method for simultaneous acquisition of maternal ECG, maternal arterial blood pressure and ECGs from two fetuses in anaesthetized late-gestation Sprague-Dawley rats. The platform combines custom-fabricated needle electrodes with conventional cardiovascular instrumentation and PowerLab/LabChart acquisition. Stable, analysable maternal arterial blood pressure, maternal ECG and dual-fetal ECG were maintained for ≤5 h. The recordings supported beat-to-beat ECG interval and heart rate variability analyses. Fetuses had lower heart rates and longer R-R intervals than dams, and fetal root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), high-frequency power and standard deviation of RR intervals (SDRR) were lower than maternal values. As proof of recording responsiveness, maternal noradrenaline and verapamil administration produced readily resolved maternal haemodynamic changes together with time-aligned fetal heart rate responses. This protocol does not by itself demonstrate maternal-fetal cardiac coupling; rather, it provides synchronized high-resolution signals suitable for future analyses of dynamic maternal-fetal cardiovascular relationships and pharmacological responses.

articles.title: Factors for Long-Term Ritodrine Monotherapy in the Treatment of Preterm Labor: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Sasaki T, Tamura M, Saisyo A et al.
articles.abstract: Ritodrine is used to manage threatened preterm labor (TPL) in Japan. While short-term administration is recommended internationally, long-term administration remains the customary practice in Japan, creating a gap in clinical practice between Japan and other regions. This retrospective study aimed to identify the maternal factors associated with long-term administration of ritodrine monotherapy. We reviewed the records of patients who received ritodrine infusion for TPL at the Yamaguchi University Hospital between April 2017 and March 2023. Patients were classified into the long-term monotherapy group (n = 37) if they received ritodrine monotherapy for more than 2 weeks. The non-long-term monotherapy group (n = 102) included patients who received ritodrine monotherapy for less than 2 weeks, required additional tocolytic agents, or discontinued ritodrine due to adverse events. The analysis showed that the white blood cell (WBC) count at treatment initiation was significantly lower in the long-term monotherapy group (p < 0.05). A receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a WBC count of 8710 as the cut-off value for predicting long-term administration. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified a WBC count below 8710 at treatment initiation as an independent factor for the long-term administration of ritodrine infusion (odds ratio: 2.57; 95% confidence interval: 1.12-5.90). Although further validation is required, these findings suggest that the WBC count at the initiation of ritodrine infusion may serve as a potential indicator of long-term ritodrine monotherapy administration in pregnant women with TPL.

articles.title: Two-Stage Estimation for Causal Inference Involving Semi-Continuous Exposures.
articles.authors: Wang X, Cook RJ, Zhu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Methods for causal inference are well developed for binary and continuous exposures, but in many settings, the exposure has a substantial mass at zero-such exposures are called semi-continuous. We propose a general causal framework for such semi-continuous exposures, together with a two-stage estimation strategy. A two-part propensity structure is introduced for the semi-continuous exposure, with one component for exposure status (exposed vs unexposed) and another for the exposure level among those exposed, and incorporates both into a marginal structural model that disentangles the effects of exposure status and dose. The two-stage procedure sequentially targets the causal dose-response among exposed individuals and the causal effect of exposure status at a reference dose, allowing flexibility in the choice of propensity score methods in the second stage. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the resulting estimators, and characterize their limiting values under misspecification of the propensity score models. Simulation studies evaluate finite sample performance and robustness, and an application to a study of prenatal alcohol exposure and child cognition demonstrates how the proposed methods can be used to address a range of scientific questions about both exposure status and exposure intensity.

articles.title: Associations of sFlt-1 and PlGF levels with hematologic and biochemical parameters in normotensive pregnant women.
articles.authors: Kinugawa M, Kumasawa K, Nemoto K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia (PE) is characterized by hypertension accompanied by hematologic and biochemical changes. In PE, these changes are linked to soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and placental growth factor (PlGF), but their relationships during normotensive pregnancy remain unclear. We aimed to investigate the associations of sFlt-1 and PlGF with routine hematologic and biochemical parameters in normotensive pregnancy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 780 pregnant women who did not develop PE or superimposed PE by measuring sFlt-1 and PlGF at 18 + 0-21 + 6 weeks of gestation with same-day routine hematology/biochemistry results.
RESULTS: Spearman's rank correlations showed weak but statistically significant associations between sFlt-1 and aspartate aminotransferase (AST; ρ = 0.19), alanine aminotransferase (ALT; ρ = 0.16), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH; ρ = 0.15). In multivariable analyses, these associations remained independent of maternal characteristics.
CONCLUSION: Even within physiologic ranges, sFlt-1 may reflect subclinical hepatic or hemolysis-related responses, consistent with its pathogenic role in PE.

articles.title: Frequent blastocyst contractions with area reduction >30% are associated with reduced embryo quality but not IVF outcomes: A retrospective cohort study of fresh and frozen single embryo transfer.
articles.authors: Lee CC, Lee KS, Chiu CS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze the effect of blastocyst contraction on embryo quality and subsequent in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes in women undergoing fresh single embryo transfer (SET) and frozen SET.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 300 patients who underwent 343 oocyte retrievals at Mackay Memorial Hospital between February 1, 2022, and February 29, 2024. The oocytes were divided into two categories based on whether blastocyst contraction occurred. We further analyzed the blastocyst morphology grading and KIDScore. We also analyzed subsequent fresh and frozen SET outcomes. Furthermore, we conducted a subgroup analysis for the frequency of contraction number and embryo quality.
RESULTS: In all embryo analyses, the contraction group was associated with significantly lower morphology grading (good embryos 25.7% vs. 68.9%, fair embryos 27.4% vs. 4.3%, poor embryos 46.9% vs. 26.8%, p < 0.001) and lower KIDScore (≧8, 14.3% vs. 20.2%, ≧ 6 and < 8, 25.5% vs. 28.2%, <6, 60.1% vs. 51.6%, p = 0.020) compared to the non-contraction group. In the contraction number analysis, higher numbers (3-4 and ≧ 5 times) were associated with significantly poorer embryo quality than less numbers (1-2 times) (p < 0.001). However, in the fresh and frozen-thawed SET analyses, there were no significant differences in the clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, livebirth, and miscarriage rates between the contraction and non-contraction groups.
CONCLUSION: The occurrence of blastocyst contractions-particularly at higher frequencies-was associated with poorer embryo quality. However, in the analysis of fresh and frozen-thawed SET, the clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, livebirth, and miscarriage rates were not significantly different between both groups, indicating that although contraction may reflect underlying differences in embryo viability, its impact on IVF success is minimal when high-quality embryos are selected rigorously for transfer. However, large research is needed to validate this conclusion.

articles.title: Improving the physician-patient relationship through timely caring services in Taiwan's no-fault childbirth compensation system.
articles.authors: Huang MC, Shih CL, Lee HL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Malpractice pressure in obstetrics contributes to clinician burnout, defensive practice, and declining participation in high-risk maternity care. Taiwan's Childbirth Accident Emergency Relief Act (CAERA) integrates a national no-fault compensation system with mandated caring services, including early communication, emotional support, and administrative assistance after childbirth-related adverse events. This study is to evaluate the timeliness, content, and perceived effectiveness of caring services under CAERA and their association with patient satisfaction and physician-patient relationships.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed nationwide survey data from compensated families and medical institutions following childbirth-related adverse events. Perceptions of caring service timing and content were compared between patients and providers. Associations between service timeliness and satisfaction outcomes were examined using standard statistical methods.
RESULTS: A total of 1345 family and 1074 institutional responses were analyzed. Substantial perception gaps were identified. Only 38.6% of families reported receiving caring services within 2 days, compared with 82.4% of institutions. Families also reported lower rates of communication (44.0% vs 81.4%), procedural assistance (69.7% vs 93.6%), and emotional support (62.2% vs 95.0%) than providers reported delivering (all P < 0.05). Timeliness was strongly associated with outcomes: families contacted within 2 days reported significantly higher satisfaction with the compensation process, administrative procedures, and physician-patient relationships than those contacted later (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Substantial gaps exist between provider-reported and patient-perceived caring services. Early engagement is associated with higher satisfaction and stronger physician-patient relationships. These findings suggest that the success of no-fault systems depends not only on financial compensation but also on prompt caring services.

articles.title: Effectiveness of father skin-to-skin contact on supporting breastfeeding behavior post cesarean section.
articles.authors: Wang SL, Kuo SC, Yu PJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Paternal early skin-to-skin contact (SSC) following a cesarean section is increasingly recognized as a vital component of maternal and infant care. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of paternal early SSC on rooming-in practices and breastfeeding longitudinal outcomes up to three months postpartum.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental design featuring pre-test, post-test, and repeated measures was employed to assess the effects of paternal-infant SSC after cesarean delivery. Data were collected at four time points: hospital admission and at one, two and three months postpartum. The primary outcomes measured were the rates of parent-child rooming-in and breastfeeding prevalence to determine the efficacy of the SSC intervention.
RESULTS: A total of 72 parent-newborn dyads participated in the study, with equal allocation to the paternal SSC intervention group and the control group. Participants in the intervention group demonstrated a significantly higher rate of rooming-in compared to the control group (χ2 = 5.79, p < 0.05). Furthermore, the intervention group showed significantly higher breastfeeding rates at all follow-up intervals: one month (χ2 = 6.92, p < 0.05), two months χ2 = 7.41, p < 0.05) and three months (χ2 = 6.24, p < 0.05) postpartum.
CONCLUSION: Early paternal-infant SSC effectively increases rooming-in frequency during hospitalization and sustains higher breastfeeding rates throughout the first three months postpartum. These findings provide an empirical foundation for integrating paternal involvement into perinatal care protocols and breastfeeding support strategies.

articles.title: Application of array comparative genomic hybridization on the DNA extracted from neonatal buccal mucosal cells for the postnatal investigation of prenatally detected chromosomal mosaicism at amniocentesis.
articles.authors: Wu PS, Chen CP
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To study the application of aCGH analysis on the DNA extracted from neonatal buccal mucosal cells for the postnatal investigation of prenatally detected chromosomal mosaicism at amniocentesis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: From January 2023 to December 2025, a total of 50 neonates with prenatally detected chromosomal mosaicism involving autosome (n = 22), sex chromosome (n = 20), microduplication (n = 2), microdeletion (n = 2), and a small supernumerary marker chromosome (n = 4) were studied for the postnatal investigation of prenatally detected chromosomal mosaicism at amniocentesis by use of aCGH analysis on the DNA extracted from neonatal buccal mucosal cells. Of 50 cases, 47 had one study and three had two studies. The buccal mucosal cells were investigated by aCGH along with or without FISH and peripheral blood chromosomal examination. The neonatal ages studied ranged from 1-6 months (n = 23), 7-12 months (n = 17) to 13-53 months (n = 13).
RESULTS: All 53 aCGH examinations were successful. The buccal DNA yield ranged from 0.55 to 5.68 μg (2.32 ± 1.26 μg, mean ± SD, n = 53). The DNA yields (mean ± SD) in 1∼6 months old neonates, 7-12 months old neonates and 13-53 months old neonates were 1.92 ± 0.79 μg (n = 20), 2.38 ± 1.47 μg (n = 15) and 2.73 ± 1.41 μg (n = 18), respectively.
CONCLUSION: The application of aCGH analysis on the DNA extracted from neonatal buccal mucosal cells is a convenient and efficient method for the postnatal investigation of prenatally detected chromosomal mosaicism at amniocentesis.

articles.title: Metabolic markers for risk stratification of diabetic ketoacidosis and perinatal mortality in pregestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Fan YH, Chen CP, Sun FJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify metabolic markers associated with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in pregnant women with pregestational diabetes mellitus (PDM) and to evaluate their utility in risk stratification and the prediction of perinatal mortality.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2000 to 2022, including singleton pregnancies in women with PDM. Maternal metabolic parameters such as glucose levels, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), lipid profiles (high-density lipoprotein [HDL] and low-density lipoprotein [LDL]), arterial pH, electrolytes, and anion gap were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and logistic regression models were used to identify metabolic predictors of DKA and perinatal mortality.
RESULTS: Among 219 pregnant women with PDM, 21 (9.6%) developed DKA. Affected women had significantly higher glucose levels (395.33 vs. 126.91 mg/dL, P < 0.001), higher HbA1c (8.45% vs. 6.73%, P = 0.001), lower HDL (38.71 vs. 57.96 mg/dL, P < 0.001), and higher LDL (152.86 vs. 119.25 mg/dL, P = 0.012) compared with those without DKA. Perinatal mortality occurred in 6 cases (28.6%) and was associated with metabolic acidosis, including lower arterial pH (7.07 vs. 7.20, P = 0.030), lower bicarbonate (3.90 vs. 9.96 mEq/L, P = 0.001), and a wider anion gap (22.50 vs. 15.17 mEq/L, P = 0.014). Additionally, higher HbA1c (10.00% vs. 7.83%, P = 0.026) and hyperkalemia (5.77 vs. 4.23 mEq/L, P = 0.022) were associated with perinatal mortality. The ROC analyses demonstrated strong predictive value for DKA (area under the ROC curve [AUC] = 0.99) and perinatal mortality (AUC = 0.98) using combined metabolic markers. The logistic regression analyses identified higher HbA1c (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13-4.75), lower HDL (aOR 0.89, 95% CI 0.81-0.96), and higher glucose (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.05) as independent predictors of DKA. Lower bicarbonate (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.96) was independently associated with an increased risk of perinatal mortality. The Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated a significant association between bicarbonate <6.50 mEq/L and increased perinatal mortality (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Key metabolic markers can aid with risk stratification for DKA and perinatal mortality in women with PDM, supporting early identification and guiding targeted clinical interventions.

articles.title: Real-time artificial intelligence-assisted assessment in a home-based pelvic floor muscle training device for pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence: A single-center prospective study.
articles.authors: Horng HC, Chen JF, Chang CP et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) is the first-line conservative treatment of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) and stress urinary incontinence (SUI), but its effectiveness is often limited by poor adherence and performance. We developed a third-generation home-based PFMT device incorporating real-time artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of this device in women with POP or SUI.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-arm study was conducted at Taipei Veterans General Hospital. Women with stage I-II POP or SUI performed home-based PFMT using a noninvasive wireless pressure-sensing device with real-time AI-assisted assessment. Outcomes were assessed at baseline (M0), 1 (M1), and 2 (M2) months. Primary outcomes included the Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory-6 (POPDI-6), Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6), Incontinence Impact Questionnaire-7 (IIQ-7), and the 1-h pad test. Contraction patterns were analyzed and categorized as optimal or non-optimal.
RESULTS: A total of 27 women (mean age 59.0 ± 14.3 years) were enrolled and completed the study. POPDI-6 decreased from 8.6 ± 2.6 to 5.2 ± 3.0 (p < 0.01), and UDI-6 from 6.4 ± 4.9 to 3.4 ± 3.4 (p < 0.05). The 1-h pad test decreased from 30.9 ± 41.9 g to 14.3 ± 23.5 g (p < 0.01); IIQ-7 reduction was also significant. Subjective and objective improvement rates were 89% and 54%, respectively. Physician-directed pattern optimization significantly improved contraction patterns, with 52.9% of patients converting from non-optimal to optimal patterns and increased the optimal contraction rate from 37.0% to 70.4% (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Real-time AI-assisted PFMT significantly improved symptom scores, objective urinary leakage, and contraction quality in women with POP or SUI. While limited by a small sample size, a short follow-up period, and a single-arm design, this approach effectively identifies and optimizes dysfunctional contraction patterns to enhance pelvic floor rehabilitation.

articles.title: Changes in postpartum glucose testing behaviors after the implementation of a gestational diabetes mellitus screening policy.
articles.authors: Chen SW, Huang MC, Chen YY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: On July 1, 2021, Taiwan implemented a national policy incorporating gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) screening into routine prenatal care and adopted a standardized 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). This initiative aimed to normalize prenatal GDM screening; however, its impact on postpartum glucose testing behaviors remains uncertain. We assessed changes in postpartum glucose testing after policy implementation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database. We compared maternal records from 1.5 years before policy implementation (January 1, 2020-June 30, 2021) with those from 1.5 years after implementation (July 1, 2021-December 31, 2022). Outcomes included postpartum glucose testing, timing of testing, and follow-up specialty.
RESULTS: After policy implementation, the proportion of women who received postpartum glucose testing within 3 months of delivery increased by 12.10 percentage points. Testing shifted toward the first 3 months postpartum (overall χ2 (df = 2) = 53.83; p < 0.0001). Follow-up in obstetrics and gynecology increased by 3.02 percentage points, and follow-up in endocrinology increased by 1.74 percentage points (both p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: After GDM screening was incorporated into routine prenatal care, postpartum glucose testing occurred earlier and became more concentrated, with postpartum follow-up more frequently occurring in obstetrics and gynecology and endocrinology. Even in the absence of a specific intervention targeting postpartum glucose testing, changes in postpartum testing behavior were observed, suggesting a spillover effect from the integration of GDM screening into routine prenatal care.

articles.title: Cytogenetic analysis of couples with recurrent pregnancy loss in taiwan: A retrospective study of 451cases.
articles.authors: Wu FT, Sun FJ, Chen CP
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the independent impact of age and gender on the prevalence of clinically significant chromosomal abnormalities in couples with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and to provide Taiwanese clinicians with local genetic data for genetic counseling.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 5-year retrospective study of 451 individuals (239 females and 212 males) was conducted at a tertiary referral center in Taiwan from 2021 to 2025. Karyotyping was performed by means of G-banding with resolution >550 band level. Common polymorphic variants, such as inv (9) (p12q13) and inv(Y) (p11.2q11.2), were excluded to assess refined cytogenetic risks. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to calculate adjusted odds ratios (aOR).
RESULTS: The prevalence of clinically significant chromosomal abnormalities was 4.43% (20/451). Female gender was identified as a significant independent predictor of abnormality (aOR = 3.70, 95%CI: 1.206-11.346, p = 0.022) after adjusting for age. The distribution of chromosomal abnormalities in 4 different age groups (≦30, 31-35, 36-40, ≧40) did not show significance difference (4.69%, 5.33%, 3.87%, 3.66%. p = 0.909) Both numerical chromosomal aberrations (e.g., sex chromosome mosaicism) and structural rearrangements (e.g., reciprocal and Robertsonian translocations) were more prevalent among females. Notably, females exhibited a predominant higher risk of sex chromosome mosaicism compared with males (aOR = 11.518, 95%CI: 1.454-91.253, p = 0.021) even after adjusting for age.
CONCLUSIONS: Female gender is a predominant factor for chromosomal abnormalities in RPL, largely attributed to sex chromosome mosaicism and chromosomal translocations. These genetic risks are independent of reproductive age, highlighting the necessity of universal parental karyotyping for all RPL couples, regardless of age, to optimize clinical management.

articles.title: Is the preoperative routine blood test workable to distinguish early-stage from advanced-stage ovarian cancer?
articles.authors: Tjokroprawiro BA, Sulistya HA, Novitasari K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preoperative routine blood test, such as complete blood counts (CBC) and nutrition markers may be associated with outcome of patients with epithelial ovarian cancer (OC); however, the value of the aforementioned test associated with the stage of OC is uncertain. This study aimed to determine the association between ten routine laboratory-based indices and the early-stage or advanced-stage OC (easOC or adsOC), particularly in low-resource country.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional analysis enrolled 98 patients with histologically confirmed OC who were treated between 2022 and 2023. The 10 preoperative indices calculated from CBC and nutrition markers included platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score (HALPS), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), monocyte-to-albumin ratio (MAR), platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), white blood cell-to-hemoglobin ratio (WHR), monocyte-to-hemoglobin ratio (MHR), and hemoglobin-to-lymphocyte ratio (HLR). Group differences and discriminatory ability for easOC (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics [FIGO] I-II) versus adsOC (FIGO III-IV) disease were assessed using nonparametric tests and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses.
RESULTS: Most indices showed no significant variation across the FIGO stages. Patients with adsOC had significantly lower PNI (p = 0.013), whereas their MAR showed a borderline increase (p = 0.054). ROC analysis demonstrated modest performance; PNI achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC, 0.648; p = 0.009; specificity, 75.4%), and MAR showed an AUC of 0.615 (p = 0.048; sensitivity, 78%). All the other indices demonstrated limited discriminatory values (AUC, 0.51-0.60).
CONCLUSION: The value of the preoperative routine blood test, such as CBC and nutrition markers for distinguishing easOC from adsOC may be limited, although PNI and MAR showed the positive association. A large cohort study may be needed to clarify the association between preoperative routine blood test and staging OC.

articles.title: Struma ovarii: Diagnostic pitfalls, management strategies, and clinical outcomes from a tertiary medical center.
articles.authors: Cheng IN, Chen WA, Tseng YJ et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To summarize the clinical, imaging, pathological, and surgical characteristics of struma ovarii and evaluate outcomes from a 17-year single-center experience.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review of 35 patients with histologically confirmed struma ovarii treated at Cathay General Hospital between January 2008 and January 2025 was conducted. Clinical data, imaging features, surgical approach, frozen section use, pathology, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean age at diagnosis was 43.3 years. One-third of patients were asymptomatic; others presented with abdominal pain, distension, or pelvic mass. Mean CA-125 was 51.5 U/mL. Ultrasonography commonly revealed multiloculated cystic masses with heterogeneous echotexture and minimal Doppler flow; several cases exhibited the characteristic "struma pearl sign." Laparoscopic surgery was performed in 60% of patients, and frozen section in 57%. Pathology showed 18 benign pure, 15 benign impure, and 2 malignant cases with papillary thyroid carcinoma arising within struma ovarii. During a median follow-up of 18 months, no recurrence or metastasis occurred.
CONCLUSION: Struma ovarii is a rare ovarian teratoma with variable clinical and imaging presentations. The struma pearl sign, when present, may serve as a supportive sonographic clue, but its absence does not exclude the diagnosis. Frozen section may assist intraoperative decision-making in selected cases, although final diagnosis should rely on permanent histopathological evaluation. Long-term follow-up remains important, particularly for malignant or atypical cases.

articles.title: Protective effects of melatonin against bisphenol A-mediated endometrial tumorigenesis: An experimental study targeting COX-2-dependent MMP-9 expression.
articles.authors: Chen TM, Hsuan-Yu Lin S, Wang KH et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bisphenol A (BPA), a widespread environmental endocrine disruptor, contributes to the development of endometrial carcinogenesis by activating the cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2)/matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) axis. In this study, the protective effects of melatonin on BPA-induced protumorigenic alterations were evaluated in the human endometrial carcinoma cell line RL95-2.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: RL95-2 cells were treated with BPA (10-7 M) alone or in combination with varying concentrations of melatonin (10-10 to 10-4 M) for 24 h. An MTT assay was performed to assess cell viability. RT-PCR and Western blotting were performed to evaluate COX-2 and MMP-9 expression. Immunofluorescence and flow cytometry were performed to analyze protein localization and quantify the COX-2+/MMP-9+ cell population. Cells were treated with NS-398, a selective COX-2 inhibitor, to validate COX-2 dependency.
RESULTS: BPA significantly increased RL95-2 cell proliferation and upregulated COX-2 and MMP-9 expression. Melatonin cotreatment, particularly at 10-6 M, suppressed BPA-induced proliferation and attenuated both COX-2 and MMP-9 expression at the gene and protein levels. Flow cytometry revealed that BPA significantly increased the proportion of COX-2+/MMP-9+ cells. Both melatonin and NS-398 reversed this effect. These findings highlight the capacity of melatonin to mitigate BPA-induced proliferation and invasiveness by suppressing COX-2-mediated MMP-9 expression.
CONCLUSION: Melatonin effectively mitigated BPA-induced proliferation and proinflammatory and proinvasive RL95-2 phenotypes by targeting the COX-2/MMP-9 signaling axis. These findings support the potential of melatonin as a physiologically safe therapeutic agent for preventing endometrial tumorigenesis induced by environmental endocrine disruptors, underscoring its anti-inflammatory relevance in reproductive oncology.

articles.title: A pilot study of electromagnetic therapy versus biofeedback-based pelvic floor muscle training for pelvic organ prolapse: A mixed-methods approach.
articles.authors: Lin KY, Wang LY, Wu PC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This pilot study aimed to: (1) evaluate the effects of high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) therapy on pelvic organ prolapse (POP) symptoms and pelvic floor function; (2) compare outcomes across HIFEM, pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) with biofeedback and/or electrostimulation, and usual care; and (3) explore participant acceptability of the interventions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mixed-methods pilot study was conducted in women aged >20 years with stage I-III POP. Participants were randomized to HIFEM, PFMT, or usual care. The HIFEM group underwent twice-weekly 28-min sessions for eight weeks using a non-invasive electromagnetic chair. PFMT consisted of supervised sessions incorporating biofeedback and/or electrostimulation. Usual care included lifestyle advice. Outcomes were assessed using validated questionnaires for POP symptoms and pelvic floor distress, digital palpation, and transperineal ultrasound.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight women completed the study (HIFEM, n = 10; PFMT, n = 9; usual care, n = 9). Compared with usual care, HIFEM significantly improved pelvic floor muscle endurance (p = 0.001), whereas PFMT significantly improved muscle strength (p = 0.034), endurance (p = 0.023), and rapid contractions (p = 0.019). Only HIFEM demonstrated significant improvements in POP symptom severity (p = 0.015) and pelvic floor distress (p = 0.041). No serious adverse events were reported. Participant satisfaction was highest in the HIFEM group (100%). Qualitative analysis supported intervention acceptability, with participants reporting increased pelvic floor awareness, improved symptom control, and enhanced psychological well-being.
CONCLUSIONS: Both HIFEM and PFMT with biofeedback appear to be safe, acceptable, and effective non-surgical treatment options for women with POP. Although no significant differences were observed between the two interventions, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of the small sample size. Larger studies are needed to confirm comparative efficacy and inform clinical implementation.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06532292. URL OF THE REGISTRATION SITE: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06532292?cond=Pelvic%20Organ%20Prolapse&intr=high-intensity&rank=1.

articles.title: Learning curve and determinants of sentinel lymph node mapping outcomes in endometrial cancer: A single-center CUSUM analysis.
articles.authors: Chen WA, Tseng YJ, Ho CM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the learning curve of sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping in endometrial cancer and to identify predictors of mapping failure in a single-center experience.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 59 patients with clinically early-stage endometrial cancer who underwent minimally invasive staging with SLN mapping at Cathay General Hospital between August 2021 and February 2025. Cumulative bilateral detection rates and cumulative sum (CUSUM) analyses were applied to assess the learning curve. Clinical, surgical, and pathological factors associated with mapping failure were examined by univariate analysis.
RESULTS: Median age was 52 years and median BMI was 27.4 kg/m2. Endometrioid histology comprised 95% of cases, and 81% were 2023 FIGO stage I. The overall detection rate was 92.3%, with bilateral mapping in 69.5%, unilateral mapping in 23.7%, and complete failure in 6.8%. Bilateral detection improved from 65% in the early phase (cases 1-20) to 72% in the late phase (cases 21-59). CUSUM indicated proficiency after ∼38 cases, with stabilization projected at ∼65 cases. Observed mapping failures were often associated with inadequate dye migration or empty specimens. Adnexal adhesions showed a borderline association with bilateral mapping failure (p = 0.080), whereas age, BMI, histologic grade, lymphovascular invasion, and stage were not significant.
CONCLUSION: SLN mapping in endometrial cancer exhibits a distinct learning curve, with proficiency achieved after approximately 40-65 cases. Adhesions encountered during surgery, particularly adnexal adhesions, may represent a key technical barrier, underscoring the importance of structured training, standardized protocols, and meticulous surgical management to optimize mapping outcomes.

articles.title: Efficacy of estetrol (E4) 15 mg/ drospirenone (DRSP) 3 mg combination for the treatment of dysmenorrhea in women with recurrent endometriosis and/or adenomyosis.
articles.authors: Lo YS, Hsu LT, Wu HM et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a combined oral contraceptive containing estetrol (E4) 15 mg and drospirenone (DRSP) 3 mg in the treatment of dysmenorrhea associated with recurrent endometriosis and/or adenomyosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study reviewed the medical records of 23 women undergoing E4/DRSP treatment. Among them, 14 patients with recurrent endometriosis and/or adenomyosis who completed at least 16 weeks of treatment were analyzed. The primary outcome was the change in endometriosis-associated pain severity, assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included changes in serum estradiol and cancer antigen 125 (CA-125) levels, as well as patient-reported quality of life. Biochemical data were available for 11 patients. Statistical analysis was performed using paired t-tests, with significance defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: The mean baseline VAS score was 7.7 with 95% confidence interval (CI) 6.9 to 8.6, which decreased significantly to 3.3 (95% CI, 2.3 to 4.3) after treatment (p < 0.005). The average VAS responder rate was 55.8%, with 85.7% of patients achieving a ≥30% reduction and defined as responder. Serum estradiol levels significantly declined (p = 0.024), from 214 pg/ml (95%CI, 34.7-394.1 pg/ml) to 42.7 pg/ml (95% CI, 2.23-83.2 pg/ml), whereas CA-125 showed a nonsignificant downward trend. No serious adverse events occurred. A total of 86% of patients reported improved quality of life.
CONCLUSION: The E4/DRSP combination regimen appears to be an effective and well-tolerated treatment for dysmenorrhea in women with recurrent endometriosis and/or adenomyosis. It may serve as a viable long-term hormonal option, for those intolerant or have contraindications to conventional therapies.

articles.title: Association Between Acute Vulvar Ulcers and Gene-Based COVID-19 Vaccines.
articles.authors: Shozu M, Teramoto S, Osada H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute vulvar ulcers have been reported following gene-based COVID-19 vaccinations, though causality remains uncertain. This study aims to examine the association between vaccination and ulcer occurrence.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational study analyzed vulvar ulcer cases reported to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) from January 2002 to February 2022. Risk was estimated by comparing VAERS-reported ulcer cases with vaccine recipient data from the COVID Data Tracker. Causality was assessed using the Bradford Hill criteria.
RESULTS: From 2021 to 2022, the proportion of vulvar ulcers among reported adverse events exceeded the upper control limits for the first time since 2002. Most cases (134/137, 97.8%) were linked to COVID-19 vaccines. Ad26.COV2.S had the highest relative risk (2.72 vs. BNT162b2; 95% CI: 1.17-6.30). For two-dose vaccines, the second dose posed a higher risk (dose 2 vs. dose 1: RR 3.52; 95% CI: 2.06-6.02 for BNT162b2; RR 2.40; 95% CI: 1.82-3.18 for mRNA-1273). Ulcers appeared a median of 2 days post-vaccination (IQR: 1.25-2.75) and resolved after a median of 12 days (IQR: 7-18). Adolescent females aged 12-17 years had the highest risk (RR vs. age 25-39: 4.01; 95% CI: 2.67-6.05), with a 46.0-fold increased risk (95% CI: 11.2-188.9) compared to age-matched females who received HPV vaccines.
CONCLUSIONS: Vulvar ulcers were closely associated with COVID-19 vaccination, especially in adolescent females. While findings suggest a potential link, further research is warranted to determine causality.

articles.title: Risk factors for adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies with early- and late-onset extreme fetal growth restriction, estimated fetal weight ≤ 1st centile: A multicenter retrospective study.
articles.authors: Choi SR, Ko HS, Kim HS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the risk factors associated with adverse perinatal outcome in early-onset (<32 weeks) and late-onset (≥32 weeks) extreme fetal growth restriction (FGR), defined as estimated fetal weight (EFW) ≤ 1st centile.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective cohort study was performed on pregnancies complicated by early- and late-onset extreme FGR within a week of delivery between 2018 and 2021. Doppler indices were converted as percentile adjusted for gestational age (GA). Composite adverse perinatal outcome (APO) was defined as fetal or neonatal death or at least one of the after severe perinatal morbidities: respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, intraventricular hemorrhage, proven sepsis or necrotizing enterocolitis. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Overall, 261 cases were included: 135 cases of early- and 126 cases of late-onset extreme FGR. The perinatal mortality rate was 7.4% in early- and 1.6% in late-onset extreme FGR. Composite APO was 54.1% and 12.7% in the early- and late-onset extreme FGR groups, respectively. The risk factors for the composite APO were GA at delivery (aOR 0.52, 95% CI 0.36-0.74), the presence of non-reassuring cardiotocography (aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.12-0.95), and EFW within 1 week before delivery (aOR 1.003, 95% CI 1.000-1.005) in early-, and GA at delivery (aOR 0.79, 95% CI 0.64-0.98) and diabetes during pregnancy (aOR 1.87, 95% CI 1.47-9.58) in late-onset extreme FGR.
CONCLUSIONS: Composite APO in early- and late-onset extreme FGR were comparable. GA at delivery may be the significant risk factor for the composite APO in early- and late-onset extreme FGR.

articles.title: Myo-inositol in placental metabolism and function: Implications for gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.authors: Salehpour S, Hosseini S, Zarisfi Z et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is a prevalent metabolic disorder affecting approximately 14% of pregnancies worldwide, with increasing incidence linked to rising obesity rates among women of reproductive age. GDM significantly impacts placental structure and function, leading to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Inositols, particularly myo-inositol (myo-Ins), play important roles in cellular signaling, glucose homeostasis, and insulin sensitivity, making them relevant to GDM pathophysiology. Myo-Ins, the most abundant inositol stereoisomer, is obtained through dietary intake and biosynthesis, with its metabolism intricately linked to insulin signaling. This review explores the role of myo-Ins in placental metabolism and its potential implications for GDM management. We discuss the potential mechanisms by which myo-Ins might influence glucose homeostasis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and lipid metabolism in the placenta, highlighting potential protective effects against GDM-induced placental dysfunction. Some clinical evidence suggests that myo-Ins supplementation may reduce the risk of GDM, improve insulin sensitivity, and mitigate adverse pregnancy outcomes. However, the timing, dosage, and specific placental effects require further investigation to optimize therapeutic efficacy. This review underscores the potential of myo-Ins as an adjunctive therapy for GDM, emphasizing the need for further research to elucidate mechanisms of action and long-term benefits for maternal and fetal health.

articles.title: Postpartum Follow-Up for Cardiovascular Disease Provoked by Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Reiger S, Buber J, Albright C
articles.abstract: Pregnancy and the postpartum period are times of significant hemodynamic change and can cause new cardiac disease, highlight previously unknown cardiovascular disease (CVD) or exacerbate known underlying CVD. While cardiovascular events frequently occur during pregnancy, half of maternal deaths occur in the postpartum period. Postpartum monitoring needs to be individualized based on the underlying disease process and must include inpatient and outpatient management plans. Care by a multidisciplinary team, including a mindful transition from obstetrics (OB) to primary care and/or cardiology, is necessary to optimize future pregnancy and long-term health.

articles.title: Intrapartum Management of Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Klammer C, Lewey J, Hirshberg A
articles.abstract: The management of pregnant patients with cardiovascular (CV) disease is focused on optimizing maternal, obstetric, and fetal outcomes. In this article, we provide guidance on intrapartum care for patients with lower risk CV conditions who can safely deliver in lower-resource settings. This includes discussion of physiologic changes during labor and delivery, commonly used medications, proposed indications for telemetry monitoring, and individualized condition specific care recommendations.

articles.title: Anesthetic Considerations for Delivery of Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Thomas AT, Naoum EE
articles.abstract: Pregnant patients with cardiovascular disease benefit from early evaluation by a pregnancy heart team and formal risk stratification to guide delivery planning and determine the need for care at a tertiary center. Carefully titrated neuraxial anesthesia is preferred to reduce maternal catecholamines, decrease cardiac workload, and enable controlled hemodynamic management. From a cardiovascular standpoint, vaginal delivery is generally favored over cesarean delivery due to its more gradual hemodynamic changes and lower physiologic stress. Intrapartum management should be guided by lesion-specific physiology, with contingencies in place for obstetric and cardiac emergencies.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Diseases Requiring Referral.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Landres IV, Staniczenko AP, Gaur P et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease complicates a small proportion of pregnancies but remains the leading cause of maternal mortality in the United States. Early recognition, risk stratification, and timely referral by obstetric providers to specialized pregnancy heart teams are critical to improving outcomes. This article outlines which cardiovascular conditions require referral, when referral should occur, and how care should be coordinated. Emphasis is placed on the use of risk stratification tools, identification of red flag symptoms, and the role of multidisciplinary pregnancy heart teams in optimizing maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Hypertension in Pregnancy and Postpartum.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Hoppe KK, Thordsen S
articles.abstract: Suboptimal prepregnancy metabolic health predisposes women to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). Prevention of HDP starts with prepregnancy metabolic health optimization. If hypertension is present during pregnancy, adequate blood pressure control becomes crucial. Pregnancy and lactation safety should be considered when selecting an antihypertensive medication regimen. Aspirin prophylaxis is recommended for women at risk of preeclampsia. HDPs and other APOs increase the risk of future maternal cardiovascular events. Therefore, continued surveillance, screening, and cardiometabolic health optimization after pregnancy are essential to improving long-term health.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Huynh K, Olevsky O, Mok T
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Pregnancy is a hypercoagulable state that increases VTE risk due to physiologic and anatomic changes of pregnancy. A clear understanding of risk assessment, diagnosis, and management of VTE in pregnancy is essential to optimize maternal outcomes. Diagnosis of VTE in pregnancy is often challenging, as symptoms may overlap with physiologic pregnancy-related changes. Accurate diagnosis requires high clinical suspicion and an understanding of various imaging modalities in pregnancy. Anticoagulation is the primary form of management of VTE in pregnancy and requires close care coordination and multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Evaluation and Management of Syncope in Pregnancy and Postpartum.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Azeem N, Nunez-Pellot C, Crousillat D et al.
articles.abstract: Syncope and presyncope symptoms occur commonly in pregnancy. Evaluation of syncope should include careful history and physical examination to determine underlying etiology. Patients with concerns for cardiogenic syncope require cardiology evaluation and multidisciplinary management. Orthostatic hypotension, vasovagal syncope and orthostatic intolerance carry favorable prognosis in pregnancy. Careful attention to volume status and avoidance of triggers can lead to successful pregnancy outcomes. Refractory cases requiring medical management should undergo individualized discussion of risk and benefits of treatment to optimize pregnancy outcomes.

articles.title: Common Arrhythmias in Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Aladesanmi OA, Spiel MH
articles.abstract: Arrhythmias during pregnancy are increasingly recognized due to increased age, risk factors, and the physiologic cardiovascular changes of pregnancy. Premature atrial contractions, premature ventricular contractions, supraventricular tachycardia, and sinus tachycardia, are benign and often resolve postpartum, with management centered on reassurance, lifestyle modification, and occasionally medication treatment. However, sustained arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter require more comprehensive evaluation, rate or rhythm control, and potential anticoagulation. A structured approach emphasizing symptom assessment, electrocardiogram evaluation, and recognition of high-risk features helps clinicians distinguish benign rhythm disturbances from pathologic arrhythmias, enabling appropriate reassurance, management, and referral to cardiology/cardio-obstetrics teams when necessary.

articles.title: Tachycardia in Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Wiley RL, Herrick NL, Tarsa M
articles.abstract: Tachycardia is a common physiologic finding in pregnancy due to increased blood volume and sympathetic activity, with heart rate typically rising by 15 to 20 bpm and peaking in the third trimester. However, persistent tachycardia may signal underlying pathology, including cardiac, endocrine, infectious, or hematologic conditions. A resting heart rate above 110 bpm should prompt further evaluation. Because cardiac disease remains a leading cause of maternal mortality, distinguishing benign physiologic changes from clinically significant conditions is critical. This article outlines a structured approach to evaluating pregnant patients with tachycardia, emphasizing early identification, risk stratification to optimize maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Impact of Hypercholesterolemia on Pregnancy and Postpartum.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Goldstein AK, Fisher MB, Trivedi V et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of maternal mortality and is secondary to the rising rates of prepregnancy CVD risk factors. Pregnancy represents a unique physiologic state characterized by significant alterations in lipid metabolism, which supports placental steroidogenesis and fetal growth. This article reviews the physiology of lipid metabolism in pregnancy, the pathophysiologic mechanisms linking dyslipidemia to adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, and current evidence guiding clinical management throughout gestation and the postpartum period. Emphasis is placed on risk stratification, medication safety, monitoring strategies, and long-term cardiovascular implications, with the goal of integrating lipid management into contemporary cardio-obstetric care.

articles.title: Evaluation and Management of Modified WHO I and II Lesions in Pregnancy.
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Zayat N, Mendoza L, Gupta M et al.
articles.abstract: The modified World Health Organization (mWHO) risk classification provides a practical framework to stratify maternal cardiovascular risk in pregnancy. For general obstetric providers, particularly those practicing outside tertiary centers, this tool can guide management decisions across different health care settings, both urban and rural. The result is the opportunity for early identification of patients who will benefit from multidisciplinary input and require transfer of care. It also provides reassurance when routine obstetric care is appropriate. A structured yet flexible approach that combines mWHO classification, clinical judgment, and multidisciplinary collaboration is recommended to optimizing outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Preconception Evaluation for Cardiovascular Disease: Who, What, and Why?
articles.journal: Obstetrics and gynecology clinics of North America
articles.authors: Wilkie G, O'Day K
articles.abstract: Preconception counseling and evaluation for individuals with cardiovascular disease is essential to optimize maternal and fetal outcomes by identifying risk and stabilizing conditions before pregnancy. It should be offered to patients with structural heart disease, cardiomyopathies, arrhythmias, valvular disease, aortopathies, prior adverse pregnancy outcomes, or significant cardiovascular risk factors. Key components include risk stratification, targeted diagnostic testing, medication review, and counseling on pregnancy timing, expected course, and contraception when appropriate. This approach can reduce severe maternal morbidity, improve fetal outcomes, and enhance care coordination. Preconception evaluation enables informed decision-making and focuses care on prevention, improving pregnancy and long-term cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Foot and Ankle Surgery on Pregnant Patients.
articles.authors: Humbyrd CJ, Martin E
articles.abstract: Pregnancy results in major changes in a woman's body, including physiologic changes in the cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, urinary, and musculoskeletal system. In the musculoskeletal system, these changes include increased lordosis, increased joint laxity, postural changes, gait changes, and metabolic bone health disorders. Despite the link between pregnancy and musculoskeletal disorders, very little is written on the orthopedic management of pregnant patients. In this article, we will provide information on the physiologic changes of pregnancy, special orthopedic considerations in pregnant patients, and advice for the surgical management of these patients.

articles.title: Gait Changes in Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Meyers M, Durnwald CP, Baxter JR
articles.abstract: The pregnant population undergoes significant changes during pregnancy that ultimately leads to gait alterations, pain, and increased risk of falls. The goal of this literature review was to identify gait changes in pregnancy with specific interest in the lower extremities. We included 39 research articles in this review in which we analyzed their methods as well as results, finding reports of significant changes to spatiotemporal parameters, kinematics, kinetic, foot biomechanics, and dynamic balance and stability during pregnancy.

articles.title: Fertility Preservation for Female Surgeons.
articles.authors: Caro D, Kermanshahi N, Reyes CJ et al.
articles.abstract: As the number of women in medicine exponentially grow, their participation in surgical specialties remains disproportionately low. Among the contributing factors are challenges related to fertility, delayed childbearing, and difficulties in family planning. Research shows female surgeons face higher infertility rates and pregnancy complications. Fertility preservation options such as storing embryos, oocytes, sperm, and reproductive tissues are options for female surgeons, yet are still limited by institutional, financial, educational, and ethical barriers. This review has the objective of identifying the unique issues female surgeons encounter concerning motherhood and fertility, and aims to identify solutions and options regarding fertility preservation.

articles.title: Endometrial Biopsies in Patients with Infertility: An Update for Pathologists.
articles.authors: Parkash V, Niu N, Pal L
articles.abstract: Pathological evaluation of endometrial biopsies has been a clinically relevant tool in the management of patients with unexplained infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss. In this article, we provide a practical, morphology-based framework for the interpretation of endometrial biopsies in this population. Chronic endometritis (CE) has attracted the most clinical and investigative attention in recent years. The evolving clinical picture and histological criteria for CE and the significant unresolved questions surrounding diagnostic thresholds are discussed.

articles.title: STK11 Adnexal Tumor: Expanding the Spectrum of Female Genital Tumors in Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome.
articles.authors: Mirkovic J
articles.abstract: Serine-threonine kinase 11 (STK11) adnexal tumors are rare clinically aggressive neoplasms most commonly arising in the paratubal/paraovarian tissue. They are of uncertain histogenesis, characterized by STK11 genomic alterations, with a subset associated with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. The spectrum of morphologic appearances is wide. Most commonly, cords and trabeculae in myxoid stroma are seen in addition to other components. They exhibit polyphenotypic immunoprofile with frequent expression of epithelial, mesothelial, sex cord, and smooth muscle marker desmin as well as hormone receptors, and loss of cytoplasmic STK11 expression.

articles.title: Human papillomavirus-independent, TP53 Wild-type Vulvar Intraepithelial Neoplasia and Its Mimics.
articles.authors: Kang Y, Skala SL
articles.abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus-independent, p53-wild-type vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (HPVi(p53wt) VIN) is a squamous cell carcinoma precursor lesion with altered squamous maturation but minimal to no cytologic atypia. Use of p16 and p53 immunohistochemical stains is strongly encouraged for accurate subclassification of VIN lesions due to the potential for overlapping morphologic features. Additionally, there are a number of benign and inflammatory mimics of HPVi(p53wt) VIN. For lesions that cannot be definitively classified as either neoplastic or inflammatory/reactive/benign, descriptive diagnoses or "vulvar aberrant maturation" are appropriate.

articles.title: Vaginal Epithelial Pathology: A Review with Emphasis on Recent Developments.
articles.authors: Talia KL, Wong RW, McCluggage WG
articles.abstract: Primary vaginal carcinoma is rare and far less common than vaginal metastases, which usually originate from neighboring organs. Primary carcinomas are predominantly squamous in type and human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated while primary adenocarcinomas are mostly HPV-independent; as glands are normally absent in the vagina, a congenital or acquired glandular precursor lesion is a prerequisite for their development, although this is not always identified. A variety of rare benign squamous and glandular lesions may also occur at this site. In this article the spectrum of vaginal squamous and glandular neoplasia, precursor and rare non-neoplastic lesions is discussed, with emphasis on recent developments.

articles.title: Rhabdomyosarcoma of the Cervix/Vagina and Its Mimics.
articles.authors: Devins KM
articles.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcomas form a morphologically and genomically heterogeneous family of malignant mesenchymal tumors defined by skeletal muscle differentiation. In the gynecologic tract, the same morphologic subtypes defined at extragenital sites may be encountered, but there are unique genetic associations and differential diagnostic concerns which should be addressed. This article aims to clarify the pathologic assessment of gynecologic rhabdomyosarcomas and their mimics, particularly in the cervix and vagina.

articles.title: Uterine Adenosarcoma: Unusual Presentations and Mimics.
articles.authors: Dinh TA, Chapel DB
articles.abstract: Uterine adenosarcoma is an uncommon biphasic neoplasm composed of malignant stroma and benign non-neoplastic epithelium. Most adenosarcomas show canonical low-grade morphology, which must be distinguished from various benign uterine polyps. A subset of adenosarcomas shows sarcomatous overgrowth, myometrial invasion, vascular invasion, heterologous differentiation, or marked nuclear atypia. These findings are prognostically adverse and may raise the differential with other uterine sarcomas. This article provides an overview of the clinicopathologic features of uterine adenosarcoma, with a particular focus on challenging presentations and histologic mimics.

articles.title: DNA Methylation Profiling: Current and Emerging Uses in Gynecologic Pathology.
articles.authors: Gu W, Howitt BE
articles.abstract: DNA methylation profiling is emerging as a powerful ancillary molecular tool for tumor classification in gynecologic pathology. This article provides a practical overview of the technology and its emerging applications, with emphasis on diagnostically challenging settings including rare mesenchymal neoplasms (eg, uterine tumors resembling ovarian sex cord tumor, SMARCA4-deficient uterine sarcoma) and lineage-ambiguous tumors. Beyond classification, methylation profiling enables copy number analysis, tumor microenvironment deconvolution, epigenetic age estimation, and cell-free DNA-based detection, with growing relevance to gynecologic pathology, albeit mostly in research setting. Current barriers include limited access, incomplete classifier development for gynecologic entities, and the need for clinical validation.

articles.title: Pitfalls, Problems, and Dilemmas in Applying the FIGO 2023 Staging System for Endometrial Cancer.
articles.authors: Joehlin AS, McGregor SM
articles.abstract: The publication of FIGO 2023 staging for endometrial carcinoma (EC) fundamentally changed pathologic staging of EC by incorporating histologic subtypes, extent of lymphovascular space invasion, and molecular classification. In this article, the authors discuss the new staging system, the dilemmas with molecular classification, and clinical application details of histologic examination as they relate to the staging practices of surgical pathologists.

articles.title: An Atlas-Based Approach to Assigning International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics Stage to Different Presentations of Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Hodgson A, Park KJ
articles.abstract: The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) staging system for cervical carcinoma provides a globally accepted framework that guides treatment decisions and prognosticates disease. The 2018 update incorporates imaging and pathologic findings into the schema, reflecting advances in diagnostic modalities and improving stage accuracy. Despite these improvements, significant information gaps remain, and assigning an accurate FIGO stage may be challenging in several situations faced by pathologists. This article uses real world case examples for various clinical situations and presentations of cervical carcinoma, focusing on a practical approach and providing strategies to ensure accurate and clinically relevant FIGO stage designation.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Prognostic Roles of Universal Estrogen Receptor Testing in Endometrial Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Huvila J
articles.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER) immunohistochemical evaluation has emerged as a key variable in the risk assessment of endometrial carcinoma. In the most common molecular subtype of endometrial carcinomas, the no specific molecular profile, ER is used in conjunction with stage, grade, and lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) for risk assessment and guiding adjuvant treatments. Additionally, ER is a useful tool for aiding primary site and histotype assessment and has a role in predicting response to hormonal therapies for endometrial carcinoma. These applications of ER immunostaining will be reviewed.

articles.title: Predictive Biomarker Tests for Ovarian Cancer: A Primer for Pathologists.
articles.authors: Lawson BC, Hagemann IS
articles.abstract: Several biomarkers play a role in treatment selection for epithelial ovarian cancer. Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a biomarker reflecting predisposing germline genetic changes as well as somatically acquired changes. Tumors with HRD may be eligible for poly-ADP(ribose) polymerase inhibitor therapy in the maintenance or recurrent setting. Expression of HER2 (ERBB2 gene product) or folate receptor alpha (FOLR1 gene product), assessed using immunohistochemical assays, is a biomarker for therapy with antibody-drug conjugates. Although the biomarker landscape in ovarian cancer remains relatively limited, these markers provide meaningful diagnostic and therapeutic guidance.

articles.title: Attitude and acceptability of IVF add-ons to improve reproductive outcomes: a focus group qualitative study.
articles.authors: Khan K, Nicholson L, Osinibi M et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: What factors are important for patients when evaluating the efficacy, safety, cost, and acceptability of IVF add-ons?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Although efficacy is the most important factor for patients, interim markers of success can also be important.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: IVF add-ons are increasingly offered alongside assisted conception despite limited evidence of their efficacy, safety, or value for money. Capturing patient perspectives on their acceptability and outcome priorities is essential to guide ethical clinical practice and inform future research.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Three online focus groups were conducted with 12 people who had used assisted reproductive technologies and were not currently in treatment. The focus groups were conducted in small groups of three to five people with each focus group lasting ∼2 h.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Participants were recruited through fertility charities and patient advocacy groups. All 12 participants were women and lived in the UK. All were currently in a relationship, and most had prior experience of using IVF add-ons. Online focus groups were conducted to discuss views on the efficacy, safety, and acceptability of IVF add-ons, and to identify preferred outcomes.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Nearly all participants defined the most important outcome of using an add-on to be achieving a live birth. However, they recognized that a live birth could feel a distant endpoint within the IVF treatment and therefore valued interim milestones as indicators of success. The main theme found in relation to understanding the risks involved was the need for patients to balance risk with desperation to have a baby. In terms of cost, two themes emerged, the need to balance cost with needing money for future treatments and the differing views on what is an acceptable cost. When receiving information about add-ons, participants reflected on the importance of finding reputable sources while also having to navigate conflicting information. Overall, the effectiveness of an add-on was valued over cost and safety, although cost and the risk of regret remained important considerations in decision-making. Most participants would not regret using add-ons, although some said they may regret not having used them.
LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: All participants were women, and most were White. Findings may not be applicable to other populations.
WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS:…

articles.title: Third-Line Overactive Bladder Treatments: Cost-Benefit Analysis in an Australian Public Hospital.
articles.authors: Klein Nulend R, Rosario M, Wood D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To review the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of third-line overactive bladder (OAB) managements, including percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS), intravesical botulinum toxin A (Botox) and sacral neuromodulation (SNM) in the urology department of a tertiary public hospital.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective review was performed to determine the therapeutic outcomes of PTNS, Botox and SNM from 2019 to 2023. Costings data were obtained from the government healthcare portal to determine the overall cost and cost effectiveness of each treatment.
RESULTS: Twenty-Eight patients underwent basic SNM lead insertion trial during the study period, with a response rate of 84%. Twelve patients proceeded to full implant insertion. The cost of SNM insertion is AU$23736. Comparatively, intravesical Botox has a unit cost of AU$2105 per treatment, with 67% efficacy in our patient cohort. PTNS was performed on 27 patients, with observed efficacy of 42%, at a cost of AU$200 per session. Comparing SNM and Botox, it would take 11.3 Botox treatments to generate equivalent cost to SNM. The Medtronic InterStim II Neurostimulator has a median battery life of approximately 6.2 years; if Botox was given 9-monthly during this time it would require 8.3 treatments, with a cost saving of over AU$6000. Each treatment is cost-effective when compared to the economic burden associated with OAB, with Botox being most cost-effective.
CONCLUSION: OAB significantly impacts quality of life and has significant financial and economic burdens. Third-line OAB treatments including PTNS, Botox and SNM differ significantly in their cost, efficacy and durability of effect. The availability of SNM in public hospitals has long been limited due to perceived cost ineffectiveness. Our series suggests a high efficacy associated with SNM in a public hospital setting, and cost-effectiveness when compared to the economic burden associated with OAB. Botox remains the most cost-effective option at our institution.

articles.title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
articles.authors: Alfakhri A, Almadani O, Alsehli H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users.
METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score.
RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases.
DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users.
CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.

articles.title: Identification and risk prediction of cancer symptom clusters based on integrated Chinese-Western multimodal data: a prospective real-world study protocol.
articles.authors: Wang X, Wu J, Bi Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify stable cancer symptom clusters (CSCs) phenotypes and trajectories in patients with breast and ovarian cancer, examine associations with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndromes and develop prediction models.
METHODS: A multicentre, prospective, longitudinal real-world cohort will enrol 2000 patients with breast cancer and 1000 patients with ovarian cancer. Data include clinical characteristics, symptoms, TCM syndrome information and multiomics data from subgroups. CSCs will be identified using exploratory factor analysis with bootstrap resampling; associations and trajectories will be analysed using regression and mixed-effects models. Prediction models will use LASSO（least absolute shrinkage and selection operator）, random forest and XGBoost（extreme gradient boosting） with internal validation.
RESULTS: Expected outcomes include stable CSCs phenotypes and clinically useful prediction models.
DISCUSSION: This study integrates TCM syndrome differentiation to explore CSC heterogeneity and evolution in real-world settings.
CONCLUSION: Findings may support personalised symptom management and improve quality of life among patients with cancer.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2500111873 (Approval time: 6 November 2025); ITMCTR2025001939 (registration time: 17 July 2025).

articles.title: Immunostimulatory gene therapy with chemotherapy remodels pancreatic tumors and induces immune signatures associated with prolonged survival.
articles.authors: Wenthe J, Grauers Wiktorin H, Hahn A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune desert/excluded tumors remain a major immunotherapeutic challenge. Herein, we aim to describe mechanistic insights of LOAd703, a novel tumor microenvironment gene engineering therapy targeting CD40 and 4–1BB, in patients with advanced solid cancer commonly associated with unresponsiveness to immunotherapy.
METHODS: The study evaluated blood and biopsy samples from pancreatic (n=29), colorectal (n=5), biliary (n=3), and ovarian cancer (n=4), treated with LOAd703 in combination with chemotherapy in a Swedish phase I/II clinical trial (NCT032259899).
RESULTS: Transcriptomic profiling of tumors before and after treatment initiation revealed induction of signatures known to predict immunotherapy responses and an enrichment for adaptive immune response pathways encompassing antigen-presentation and T-cell activation. In pancreatic cancer subanalysis, adaptive immune responses together with increased CD40 expression were associated with longer survival and CD40 appeared as a central node among upregulated immune biomarkers consistent with the mechanism of action of LOAd703. Treatment benefit was further associated with reduced expression of immunosuppressive and tumor-promoting factors both in tumors and peripheral blood. Systemically, treatment generated a Th1 profile in plasma, accompanied by an increase in effector/effector memory T cells and a reduction of regulatory T cells.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support that intratumoral LOAd703 in combination with chemotherapy drives local and systemic immune remodeling in commonly immunotherapy-unresponsive tumors. Further, the treatment reprograms the tumor microenvironment to reduce tumor-promoting factors and immunosuppression.
ONE SENTENCE SUMMARY: Targeting CD40 and 4–1BB with gene therapy in combination with chemotherapy induces immune responses associated with longer survival in pancreatic cancer.

articles.title: Metabolic and hormonal heterogeneity in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome in a South Indian cohort identified by k-means clustering.
articles.authors: Nambiyar N, Elango N, Velvizhi S
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: In polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), conventional Rotterdam phenotypes may not adequately capture the multidimensional hormonal and metabolic heterogeneity of the disorder.
AIMS: To identify clinically meaningful PMOS subtypes using a data-driven clustering approach among infertile South Indian women.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 196 infertile women diagnosed with PMOS (Rotterdam criteria) at a fertility centre in South India. Unsupervised k-means clustering was performed and cluster stability was assessed using Jaccard bootstrapping.
KEY RESULTS: Three subtypes were identified: gonadotrophin predominant, body mass index (BMI) predominant, and intermediate. The gonadotrophin predominant cluster exhibited intermediate BMI with higher LH and FSH concentrations and the highest LH/FSH ratio. The BMI predominant cluster demonstrated the highest BMI with a relatively low LH/FSH ratio, while the intermediate cluster showed lean-to-normal BMI with the lowest LH, FSH, and LH/FSH ratio. Significant differences were observed between clusters in systolic and diastolic blood pressure and endometrial thickness. No significant between-cluster differences were found for anti-Müllerian hormone, estradiol, prolactin, thyroid-stimulating hormone and haemoglobin A1c.
CONCLUSIONS: Data-driven clustering using BMI, LH, and FSH identified three PMOS subtypes, demonstrating heterogeneity beyond the conventional Rotterdam phenotypic classification.
IMPLICATIONS: The identified subtypes enhance understanding of clinical heterogeneity of PMOS and provide a basis for potential application in personalized patient management.

articles.title: Hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence and survival of uterine sarcomas by histotype, race and ethnicity in the United States, 2000-2019.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Dave D, Arend RC, Leath CA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uterine sarcomas are rare but aggressive mesenchymal malignancies of the uterus, characterized by diverse histotypes and poor survival. However, little is known about the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of uterine sarcoma histotypes at the population level.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence rates and five-year relative survival by histologic subtype, stage at diagnosis, and race/ethnicity among U.S. individuals aged ≥20 years diagnosed with uterine sarcoma in the SEER 22 registries from 2000-2019.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective population-based study included microscopically confirmed uterine sarcoma cases registered in the SEER 22 database. Hysterectomy-corrected, age-specific incidence rates were calculated by histotype, stage at diagnosis, and race/ethnicity. Five-year relative survival was estimated using the Ederer II method in SEER*Stat software (version 9.0.42).
RESULTS: A total of 14,801 individuals aged ≥20 years diagnosed with uterine sarcoma were included. Leiomyosarcoma (LMS) were most common comprising 53.3% of the total cases (n=7883), endometrial stromal sarcoma (ESS) accounted for 26.7% of cases (n=3948), Adenosarcoma for 12.7% (n=1884), sarcoma not otherwise specified (NOS) for 5.7% (n=837), and undifferentiated sarcoma for 1.7% of cases (n=249). Incidence rates of uterine sarcomas increased until ages 50-54 and plateaued thereafter other than among Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) individuals, where incidence continued to increase until ages 65-69 years. LMS demonstrated the highest hysterectomy-corrected incidence (0.6 per 100,000), followed by ESS (0.3 per 100,000) and Adenosarcoma (0.1 per 100,000). NHB individuals had the highest incidence of uterine sarcomas across all histotypes. Overall, NHB individuals were more likely to be diagnosed with distant diseases compared with other groups. Among all individuals, five-year relative survival was 42.3% (95% CI: 41-43.5) for LMS, 70.2% (68.5-71.8) for ESS, and 78.3% (75.7-80.6) for Adenosarcoma.
