When categorized by stage at diagnosis, relative survival for localized disease ranged from 62% to 85% in all histotypes, vs. 13.5% to 34.7% for distant metastatic disease. Survival was lowest among NHB individuals, 41.9%, versus 55.4 % in Non-Hispanic White (NHW) individuals, across all histotypes and stage at diagnosis.
CONCLUSION: Uterine sarcomas exhibit pronounced heterogeneity, comprising distinct histotypes that demonstrate variable…

articles.title: Postpartum glycemic trends among people with gestational diabetes using continuous glucose monitoring.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.authors: Hersh AR, Gallagher AC, Ward L et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During the immediate postpartum period, glycemic changes among persons with gestational diabetes (GDM) have not been well characterized.
OBJECTIVE: Using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data, we sought to explore the differences in postpartum glycemic trends among people with GDM by patient-level characteristics.
STUDY DESIGN: This study was an exploratory secondary analysis of pregnant people with GDM randomized to using CGM versus capillary blood glucose during pregnancy. Participants without CGM data in the immediate postpartum period were excluded from analysis. Our primary outcome was mean glucose by hour from delivery through the first 48 hours postpartum. We performed additional analyses stratified by GDM type, mode of delivery and time in range during pregnancy (≥90% TIR, 63-140 mg/dL) to determine differences in postpartum glycemia among these cohorts.
RESULTS: Of the 111 participants in the overall trial, we included 79 participants with postpartum data in this secondary analysis, of which 22.8% had A1GDM and 77.2% had A2GDM. Overall, there was a slight downward trend in glucose values over the first 48 hours post-delivery. Participants with A1GDM had lower mean glucose by 48 hours compared to those with A2GDM, as did participants with high percent TIR (≥90%) compared with lower percent TIR during pregnancy. Participants with higher gestational mean glucose and percent time-above-range (TAR) had higher mean glucose during the 48 hours post-delivery compared to those with lower gestational mean glucose and time-above-range.
CONCLUSION: We found that postpartum mean glucose trended downward after delivery and varied by multiple pregnancy and delivery characteristics. Future studies should assess whether differences in postpartum glycemic parameters are associated with clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: Weight and Risk Adjusted Perioperative (WRAP) Bundle for Prevention of Cesarean Delivery Surgical Site Infection: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Scremin Souza SC, Walker HA, Bowie AC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Many individual interventions to reduce surgical site infection (SSI) risk after Cesarean delivery (CD) have been identified; however, their collective impact when used as a bundle is not well defined. This quality improvement initiative compared SSI rates before and after the implementation of a weight- and risk-adjusted perioperative (WRAP) bundle, developed to improve CD outcomes.
METHODS: The WRAP bundle was designed to standardize care by tailoring evidence-based interventions according to each patient's individual SSI risk category. Risk stratification was based on pre-gravid body mass index (BMI) and the presence of comorbidities associated with increased SSI risk. This quality improvement initiative adopted a before-and-after quasi-experimental design over two years. Post-CD telephone calls by clinical reviewers were made 30-42 days postpartum to identify CD-SSI incidence.
RESULTS: A total of 4014 CDs were performed between July 1, 2022, and March 1, 2024, with 1275 before WRAP bundle implementation and 2739 after. Maternal characteristics were comparable between pre- and post-WRAP bundle groups, except for hypertension in pregnancy, which was more prevalent in the post-implementation period (22.1% vs. 17.1%, P = 0.001). Across all BMI categories, a statistically significant reduction in overall CD-SSI incidence from 8.9% to 5.8% (P = 0.007) was observed. In the high-BMI group, the CD-SSI rate decreased from 13.9% to 6.9% (P = 0.03).
CONCLUSION: Tailored bundled interventions, such as the WRAP bundle may be effective in reducing the incidence of CD-SSI, particularly among high-risk individuals. Continuous monitoring of post-CD SSI is vital for quality improvement efforts aimed at optimizing postpartum outcomes.

articles.title: Access to Early Pregnancy Assessment Clinics and Guideline-Recommended Investigations for Recurrent Pregnancy Loss in Ontario.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.authors: Friedman C, Ellis S, Tunde-Byass M et al.
articles.abstract: Early pregnancy assessment clinics (EPACs) are key in managing early pregnancy complications, yet access across Ontario remains limited. Little is also known regarding EPACs' integration of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) care, impacting up to 5% of patients. We surveyed Ontario obstetrics and gynaecology chiefs (May-October 2025, 33 responses, 61% response rate), and found 50% had EPACs and 15% had RPL protocols. Access to RPL investigations varied: gynaecologic ultrasound (89%), antiphospholipid antibody testing (85%), products of conception testing (54%), parental karyotyping (39%), and 3D ultrasound/sonohysterography (31%). We advocate for greater EPACs access, and integrated RPL protocols to improve patient care.

articles.title: Perceived descriptive norms and actual rates of contraception and fertility discussion among adults in rural Uganda: A whole-population study.
articles.authors: Comfort AB, Baguma C, Branam LS et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Women in Uganda face challenges in meeting their reproductive needs. Communication about contraception is one pathway through which couples navigate these challenges. However, it is unknown how often discussions occur among couples and whether perceptions of others' discussion behavior shape discussion frequency. We examined associations between individuals' beliefs about how often peer couples discuss contraception and fertility intentions and frequency of personal discussion.
STUDY DESIGN: We collected data from all partnered adults of reproductive age living in a single parish in southwestern Uganda as part of a larger study focused on social connection and health. Participants reported how frequently they discussed contraception decisions and fertility intentions with a partner, and how often most other reproductive-aged couples in their village discussed these topics (i.e., perceived norms). We compared perceptions to reported communication frequency aggregated at the village level, and we used sex-stratified multivariable Poisson regression models with robust estimates of variance to estimate the association between personal behavior and perceived norms.
RESULTS: Of 908 participants (92% response rate), 560 (62%) frequently discussed contraception decisions and fertility intentions, 174 (19%) rarely did, and 174 (19%) never did. Regarding perceptions, 305 (34%) incorrectly thought most others rarely or never discussed these topics and 197 (22%) said they did not know. Individuals who did not know or who thought discussions rarely or never occurred were less likely to discuss these topics compared to individuals who accurately perceived the norm (e.g., among women, adjusted relative risk for not knowing the norm=0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.61-0.91; p-value =0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Inaccurate beliefs about local discussion norms were associated with a lower likelihood of personally discussing contraception and fertility intentions. Emphasizing actual rates of discussions through public messaging or through existing intervention strategies (e.g., couples-based counseling) might motivate discussions within couples and support reproductive autonomy.
IMPLICATIONS: Individuals' misperceptions of local discussion norms among peer couples about contraception and fertility intentions contribute to their own tendencies to engage in these discussions. Correcting misperceived norms and strengthening individuals' accurate beliefs about local…

articles.title: Postmenopausal estradiol levels and female sex modulate haemodynamic responsiveness in experimental portal hypertension.
articles.authors: Schachteli F, Klein S, Schierwagen R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Sex and 17β-estradiol (E2) influence outcomes of cirrhosis, yet preclinical studies in portal hypertension are conducted predominantly in males. We investigated sex and E2-dependent differences in G protein-coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1) signalling and portal pressure response to PDE5 inhibition (PDE5i) in experimental cirrhosis.
METHODS: We assessed sex inclusion in rodent studies by PubMed literature search and analysed human hepatic GPER1 expression by sex and age using bulk RNA-seq. Bile duct ligation was performed in male, ovariectomised (OVX) and sham-operated female rats. E2 was administered 24h before invasive haemodynamic assessment in males and OVX females. Acute PDE5i effects were investigated during haemodynamic measurement.
RESULTS: Of 510 rat and 1,657 mouse studies, 87.3% and 77.3% respectively included males only. Human bulk RNA-seq suggested lower hepatic GPER1 expression in cirrhotic females aged ≥ 50 vs. < 50 years. OVX reduced hepatic - but not aortic - GPER1 expression. E2 reduced portal pressure (mean +/- SEM; 22.6 +/- 1.4 vs. 14.3 +/- 1.1 mmHg, p = 0.009) by lowering hepatic portal vascular resistance (74.4 ± 12.7 vs. 25.4 +/- 3.1 mmHg·min·ml-1·g-1, p = 0.03) only in OVX females. PDE5i decreased portal pressure in males (21.3 +/- 1.2 vs. 16.9 +/- 1.8 mmHg, p = 0.03) irrespective of E2. OVX abolished the PDE5i response, which was restored by E2 (14.3 +/- 1.1 vs. 10.0 +/- 0.9 mmHg, p = 0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: In experimental cirrhosis, estradiol depletion in OVX females was associated with reduced hepatic GPER1 expression and a diminished portal pressure response to PDE5i. This highlights sex and menopausal status as key determinants of treatment response in portal hypertension and supports the need for sex-specific validation.
IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Sex and hormonal status likely contribute to clinically relevant variability in the pharmacology of portal hypertension. Our work highlights that haemodynamic drug response varies due to sex and estradiol status in pre- and postmenopausal females, yet preclinical studies predominantly rely on male models. Integrating sex and menopausal status into early drug development could improve translational accuracy and anticipate non-responder populations.

articles.title: Tumorigenic microenvironment alters N-terminal membrane protein topology via a mechanism consistent with the Charge Balance Rule.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.ta: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis
articles.authors: Savenkova D, Bulatova L, Kozlova A et al.
articles.abstract: The molecular mechanism of changing and varied antigenicity of membrane proteins during cancerogenesis, where changes in membrane lipid composition and abiotic tumor microenvironment occur regularly, is unknown. By challenging ovarian cancer cells to tumorigenic hypoxia and acidosis, we observed unexpected surface exposure of the Na+-dependent phosphate transporter (NaPi2b) N-termini (NT) previously hidden on the cytoplasmic side of "resting" cancer cells in the accordance with its predicted orientation, violating the Positive Inside Rule. Consistently with the Charge Balance Rule of membrane protein assembly, the reorientation of NaPi2b NT coincides with loss of asymmetry and surface exposure of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), while the coincident exposure of PE and NT of NaPi2b is prevented by knockdown of phospholipid scramblase 1 (PLSCR1). These dynamic topological events can lead to unmasking of previously hidden extramembrane domains (epitopes), which can be potentially used as a novel target for targeted anti-tumor immunotherapy.

articles.title: Beyond pyroptosis: Non-lytic functions of GSDMD in tumor immunity and cancer immunotherapy.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.ta: Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Basis Dis
articles.authors: Wang X, Du Q, Wu J et al.
articles.abstract: Gasdermin D (GSDMD) is classically defined as the pore-forming executioner of pyroptosis, but GSDMD activation does not invariably culminate in terminal lysis. Direct mechanistic studies show that limited GSDMD pores can support interleukin-1β (IL-1β), ATP, or interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15) release before overt plasma-membrane rupture, whereas Ca2+-triggered endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT)-III recruitment and ALG-2-interacting protein X (ALIX)-dependent endosomal clearance can limit or reverse membrane injury. Nerve injury-induced protein 1 (NINJ1) acts downstream of early pore-mediated permeability to execute terminal plasma-membrane rupture and macromolecular damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) release. Emerging evidence extends GSDMD activity to nuclear-envelope transport and extracellular-vesicle-mediated transfer of pore structures, although these mechanisms are model-specific and are not uniformly non-lytic. In tumor immunity, GSDMD has opposing compartment-dependent effects. In a B16F10 anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) model, GSDMD in Cx3cr1+ myeloid/antigen-presenting cell (APC) populations restricted a cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-dependent ISG program. In MC38 and KPC models, non-lytic GSDMD pores in CD4+ T cells amplified Ca2+-nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT)-IL-2 helper signaling. In selected colorectal cancer (CRC) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) models, distinct full-length, nuclear, or cleavage-associated GSDMD states regulated DNA repair, growth, metastasis, and immune exclusion. In selected pancreatic and ovarian cancer models, treatment-induced gasdermin activation contributed to immunogenic lytic death. This review distinguishes established basic mechanisms, model-defined causal evidence, retrospective associations, and hypothesis-generating translation. We propose cell-type- and state-resolved biomarkers and compartment-selective interventions as prospective research frameworks rather than clinically validated decision tools. Standardized functional assays, unified multicompartment models, selective delivery, and prospective human validation are required before GSDMD can be considered clinically actionable.

articles.title: The impact of anovulatory conception cycle on first-trimester uterine artery pulsatility index and preeclampsia risk.
articles.authors: Moeykens M, Van den Mooter E, Vesali M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether the relationship between uterine artery pulsatility index and preeclampsia outcomes differs in anovulatory cycles.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study.
SUBJECTS: 3,651 singleton pregnancies undergoing uterine artery Doppler assessment between 11 and 14+1 weeks of gestation at the University Hospital Brussels, May 2021 to December 2023.
EXPOSURE: Mode of conception, including without medical assistance, ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination, fresh embryo transfer, programmed-cycle frozen embryo transfer, and natural-cycle frozen embryo transfer.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Association between first-trimester uterine artery pulsatility index and preeclampsia by conception mode.
RESULTS: The association between first-trimester uterine artery pulsatility index and preeclampsia risk varied by conception mode, with a significant difference between pregnancies conceived without medical assistance and those following programmed-cycle frozen embryo transfer (interaction estimate=1.11, p=0.04). Higher uterine artery pulsatility index was associated with preeclampsia in pregnancies conceived without medical assistance (odds ratio; 95% confidence interval: 5.31, 2.83-9.87), but not following programmed-cycle frozen embryo transfer (1.75; 0.76-4.01). Uterine artery pulsatility index was lower after programmed-cycle frozen embryo transfer (median, interquartile range: 0.71, 0.55-0.92) compared to without medical assistance: (0.94, 0.74-1.15), ovulation induction/intra-uterine insemination: (0.89, 0.71-1.09), fresh embryo transfer (0.95, 0.78-1.19) and natural-cycle frozen embryo transfer: (0.93, 0.70-1.11) (p<0.001). Compared to programmed cycles, pregnancies without medical assistance and after natural-cycle frozen embryo transfer show reduced preeclampsia risk (odds ratio; 95% confidence interval: 0.37; 0.24-0.57 and 0.09; 0.01-0.69 respectively). In uncomplicated pregnancies, birth weight percentile was higher following programmed-cycle frozen embryo transfer compared to without medical assistance (β, standard error: -4.8, 1.4; p<0.001), ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination (-6.1, 3.1; p=0.04), and fresh embryo transfer (-12.4, 2.6; p<0.001). In preeclamptic pregnancies, a similar but non-significant trend between birth weight and conception mode was observed (p>0.05).
CONCLUSION: Unlike pregnancies without medical assistance, first-trimester uterine artery pulsatility index was not associated with…

articles.title: Reference ranges for early pregnancy hCG following embryo transfer: A cohort study of 4807 embryo transfer cycles leading to live birth at term.
articles.authors: Hofer N, Moykens M, Cools W et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish gestational day-specific reference values for serum hCG in early pregnancy following embryo transfer and identify maternal and treatment-related factors contributing to its variability.
DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study.
SUBJECTS: Singleton healthy term live births following single embryo transfer, with serum hCG measurements obtained between gestational days 25 and 65.
EXPOSURE: None.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Gestational day-specific serum hCG reference values and estimated effects of maternal and treatment characteristics on serum hCG concentrations.
RESULTS: We analyzed 4,807 embryo transfer cycles resulting in term singleton live births, comprising 14,109 serum hCG measurements obtained between gestational days 25 and 65 using a Roche cobas immunoassay. Gestational day-specific 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles were established. A linear mixed-effects model showed that serum hCG concentrations were significantly associated with embryo developmental stage, transfer cycle type, and maternal weight. Maternal weight exerted the strongest influence, with hCG concentrations decreasing by approximately 0.76% per kilogram increase in maternal weight. Oocyte donation, fertilization method, and preimplantation genetic testing were not significantly associated with hCG levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Gestational day-specific serum hCG reference intervals were established for pregnancies following embryo transfer. Maternal weight, embryo developmental stage, and transfer cycle type contributed to variation in serum hCG concentrations. These references may provide context for interpreting early serum hCG measurements and complement clinical assessment in early pregnancy, although potential inter-assay variability should be considered. Future studies should explore predictive models integrating hCG with maternal and treatment-related factors.

articles.title: SMAD family member 9 restrains MYC-associated zinc finger protein-driven Wnt family member 7A transcription in endometrial carcinoma.
articles.authors: Zhen J, Nie L, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is a common gynecological malignancy with increasing incidence and limited treatment options for advanced disease. The molecular mechanisms underlying its progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify SMAD family member 9 (SMAD9, also known as SMAD8) as a negative regulator of EC progression. Integrated analyses of clinical datasets and patient samples showed that SMAD9 is consistently downregulated in EC, and higher SMAD9 expression is associated with a more favorable prognosis. Functional assays showed that SMAD9 suppresses EC cell proliferation and cell-cycle progression, whereas its silencing enhances these phenotypes. Mechanistically, DNMT3B-mediated promoter hypermethylation contributes to reduced SMAD9 expression in EC. RNA sequencing and subsequent validation identified WNT7A as a downstream target of SMAD9. SMAD9 represses WNT7A expression and attenuates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, whereas MAZ binds to the WNT7A promoter and promotes its transcription. SMAD9 also associates with SMAD4, MAZ, and TOB1, accompanied by reduced MAZ occupancy at the WNT7A promoter. In addition, medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) increased SMAD9 expression and inhibited EC growth both in vitro and in xenograft models. MPA did not significantly alter SMAD9 promoter methylation using MethylTarget analysis, whereas PGR knockdown markedly attenuated the MPA-induced SMAD9 upregulation, suggesting that PGR signaling is required for MPA-induced SMAD9 expression. Together, these findings identify a DNMT3B-SMAD9-MAZ-WNT7A regulatory network linking epigenetic regulation of SMAD9 with transcriptional control of Wnt signaling in EC.

articles.title: Jinfeng pills ameliorate levonorgestrel-induced ovarian injury by modulating ApoA1-associated cholesterol homeostasis and PI3K/Akt signaling.
articles.authors: Hu Y, Li G, Ni Q et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Jinfeng Pills (JFP, NMPA approval No. Z20064400) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula clinically used to regulate menstruation and support ovulation. It consists of nine medicinal materials: Epimedium brevicornu Maxim. (Yinyanghuo), Cervus elaphus Linnaeus (Lurong), Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. (Renshen), Equus asinus (EJiao), Ligustrum lucidum W.T.Aiton (Nvzhenzi), Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke (Heshouwu), Curculigo orchioides Gaertn (Xianmao), Cinnamomum cassia (L.). J.Presl (Rougui) and Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Yimucao). Previous studies have demonstrated the protective effects of JFP against ovarian dysfunction. However, the potential protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic exposure to levonorgestrel (LNG), a progestin commonly used in emergency contraception, and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of JFP against ovarian injury induced by chronic LNG exposure and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A rat model of chronic LNG exposure was established, and the efficacy of JFP was evaluated based on estrous cycles, serum hormone levels and ovarian morphology. Ovarian transcriptomic analysis and cholesterol-related biochemical assays were performed to investigate the alterations in ovarian cholesterol homeostasis. The role of apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA1) was further examined by using ApoA1 silencing in primary rat ovarian theca cells and intrabursal administration of ApoA1 in vivo. RT-qPCR and Western blotting were subsequently used to validate the key molecular changes and assess the effects of JFP on ApoA1expression, cholesterol homeostasis and the associated signaling pathways.
RESULTS: JFP significantly ameliorated LNG-induced ovarian injury, as evidenced by increased serum levels of FSH, LH and AMH, and decreased estradiol levels and the LH/FSH ratio, reduced cystic follicle formation, and attenuated follicular depletion. Transcriptomic analysis in ovarian tissues, together with cholesterol assays, RT-qPCR and Western blotting, revealed that LNG exposure disrupted ovarian cholesterol homeostasis, with alterations in cholesterol transport and increased ovarian ApoA1 abundance. Intrabursal administration of ApoA1 induced ovarian pathological changes and activated PI3K/Akt signaling in vivo, whereas ApoA1 silencing attenuated PI3K/Akt activation and inhibited the…

articles.title: Interfacility Variation in Diagnosis and Tocolysis for Threatened Preterm Labor and Its Association With Gestational Age Threshold for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Perinatal Centers in the Chugoku-Shikoku Region of Western Japan.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Yamane N, Teraoka Y, Mukai Y et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe interfacility variation in threatened preterm labor (TPL) management in a perinatal care network in western Japan and the association between the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission threshold and the long-term tocolysis policy.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, facility-level questionnaire survey was conducted for all 43 perinatal maternal and child health centers in the Chugoku-Shikoku region of western Japan in 2024. Centers reported diagnostic criteria for TPL, use of objective scoring systems, first-line intravenous tocolytic drugs, NICU admission gestational age threshold, and institutional policies regarding planned duration of intravenous tocolysis (short-term, ≤ 48 h; long-term, > 48 h). Factors related to the adoption of long-term tocolysis were evaluated using logistic regression.
RESULTS: Valid responses were obtained from 32 centers (74.4%). A long-term-only tocolysis policy was reported by 65.6% (21/32) of centers. Diagnostic criteria and thresholds for intervention varied widely, and only three centers (9.4%) used an objective severity score, such as the preterm labor index or tocolysis index. Ritodrine hydrochloride was used as the first-line intravenous tocolytic drug in 93.8% (30/32) of centers. The NICU admission threshold differed among centers. In multivariable analysis, centers with a higher NICU admission threshold were more likely to report a long-term-only policy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.38 per 1-week increase; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-1.83; p = 0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: Management of TPL showed marked interfacility variation in the regional perinatal care network. The NICU admission threshold was associated with the institutional tocolysis-duration policy, suggesting that regional perinatal system structure should be considered when discussing optimal tocolysis duration.

articles.title: Antinuclear antibodies and female reproductive health: Evidence, clinical implications and management.
articles.authors: Qiong L, Han J, Donglin H et al.
articles.abstract: Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) are biomarkers of immune dysregulation whose reproductive significance depends on the clinical setting and antibody profile. This narrative review synthesizes clinical and experimental evidence on ANA in infertility, assisted reproductive technology (ART), recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), recurrent implantation failure (RIF), endometriosis and pregnancy complications. Follicular-fluid studies and experimental models implicate oocyte maturation, embryo development, trophoblast function and placental immune regulation, providing biological plausibility without establishing ANA-mediated causation in human reproductive failure. Clinical studies show enrichment of ANA in infertility and RPL populations, whereas subsequent pregnancy prognosis, ART outcomes and perinatal associations vary with population, assay, titer and endpoint. We distinguish isolated ANA positivity from specific ANA-associated autoantibodies and established autoimmune disease because these findings carry different clinical implications. Disease-directed treatment for systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome is considered separately from empirical treatment in ANA-positive infertility patients. Some intervention studies report improved early reproductive outcomes, but current evidence does not support routine corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin or heparin solely on the basis of ANA positivity. ANA positivity is therefore best interpreted as a context-dependent marker that may guide targeted assessment rather than an independent therapeutic target. Prospective studies linking defined antibody profiles to tissue mechanisms, reproductive outcomes and treatment response are needed to establish clinically useful applications.

articles.title: Exploring the neural correlates of mental health: associations between cortical folding and mental health problems in youth with prenatal alcohol exposure.
articles.authors: Scholten C, Gilchrist C, Geeraert B et al.
articles.abstract: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) can alter neurodevelopment and cause health and behavioral effects. Mental health challenges disproportionately affect individuals with PAE and are related to brain alterations. Cortical folding (gyrification) is associated with mental health in clinical populations and may help understand mental health difficulties in individuals with PAE. 161 datasets from 125 youth (57 PAE, 59 females) aged 7-21 years were included. T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and the caregiver-report Behavior Assessment System for Children were collected at baseline and 2-year follow-up. Images were processed to extract local gyrification index (LGI) from 20 mental health-related regions. Linear mixed-effects models were used to test the effect of PAE on associations between LGI and mental health symptoms. Youth with PAE had more Externalizing Problems (60.7 ± 15.5) than unexposed youth (54.8 ± 11.1; p < 0.001). PAE moderated the relationship between Internalizing Problems and LGI in the left posterior orbital gyrus and the left subcallosal area, and between Externalizing Problems and LGI in the right frontal pole and left subcallosal area. Higher LGI was associated with higher Internalizing and Externalizing Problems in participants with PAE; this association was weaker or absent in unexposed youth. This indicates a potential neurobiological basis for mental health challenges in individuals with PAE.

articles.title: Association of birth plan use and respect with perceived obstetric violence, post-traumatic stress symptoms, and risk of postpartum depression: A cross-sectional questionnaire study.
articles.authors: Mazoteras-Pardo V, Ortiz-Esquinas I, Martínez-Galiano JM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Birth plans aim to promote respectful, woman-centered maternity care. However, evidence remains limited regarding whether maternal psychological outcomes are associated with birth plan use, the extent to which the plan is respected, and obstetric complications.
OBJECTIVES: To examine whether birth plan use and respect are associated with perceived obstetric violence, post-traumatic stress symptoms, and risk of postpartum depression, and whether these associations differ according to birth type.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional questionnaire study.
SETTING(S): Spain, 2023.
PARTICIPANTS: 2367 women aged ≥18 years who were between one and six months postpartum.
METHODS: Participants completed an anonymous online questionnaire. Birth plan status was classified as no birth plan, birth plan not respected, or birth plan respected in most aspects. Analyses were stratified by normal or complicated birth. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for maternal age, attendance at antenatal education, family income, parity, and previous caesarean section.
RESULTS: Overall, 1382 women (58.4%) had prepared a birth plan: 370 (15.6%) reported that it was not respected and 1012 (42.8%) that it was respected in most aspects. In bivariate analyses, women whose plans were not respected had the highest prevalence of perceived obstetric violence (normal birth: 35.2%; complicated birth: 45.3%), post-traumatic stress symptoms (25.9% and 40.5%, respectively), and postpartum depression risk (22.2% and 42.1%). Women whose plans were respected had the lowest prevalence of these outcomes. After adjustment, birth plan disrespect was strongly associated with perceived obstetric violence following normal births (adjusted odds ratio: 9.72, 95% confidence interval: 4.42-21.39) and complicated births (adjusted odds ratio: 7.99, 95% confidence interval: 5.60-11.40). Respectful implementation was associated with lower odds of post-traumatic stress symptoms after normal births (adjusted odds ratio: 0.18, 95% confidence interval: 0.07-0.47) and complicated births (adjusted odds ratio: 0.54, 95% confidence interval: 0.36-0.79). For postpartum depression, birth plan respect was associated with lower odds after normal births (adjusted odds ratio: 0.59, 95% confidence interval: 0.39-0.90), whereas birth plan disrespect was associated with higher odds after complicated births (adjusted odds ratio: 3.02, 95% confidence interval: 2.23-4.10).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal psychological…

articles.title: A novel BCB-based classification system reveals distinct chromatin and nucleolar signatures associated with oocyte developmental competence.
articles.authors: Stachovicova S, Benc M, Strejcek F et al.
articles.abstract: Oocyte maturity significantly influences developmental competence. Although individual aspects of oocyte quality have been relatively well characterized and supported by various methodological approaches, their interconnection and comprehensive evaluation are often lacking. On the one hand, cytoplasmic maturation plays an important role. On the other hand, chromatin configurational changes lead to the progressive silencing of transcriptional activity. Considerably less attention, however, has been devoted to the unique structure known as the nucleolus-like body (NLB), which plays a key role in chromatin organization and may significantly influence its remodelling during oocyte maturation. The present study introduces a novel three-category oocyte classification system based on modified native Brilliant Cresyl Blue staining and characterizes the individual categories according to their characteristic patterns of chromatin organization. The proposed classification distinguished BCB+, BCB+/- and BCB- oocytes and revealed category-specific patterns of chromatin organization associated with differences in developmental competence. We further investigated the relationship between this classification, oocyte developmental competence, and the functional relevance of the associated NLB. Micromanipulation transfer of NLBs from fully grown BCB+ oocytes markedly improved meiotic maturation of BCB+/- oocytes and partially restored their subsequent developmental performance. Together, these findings demonstrate that the proposed classification identifies oocyte populations differing in chromatin organization and developmental competence and provide further evidence of an association between NLB properties and the acquisition of developmental competence.

articles.title: Transrectal ultrasonographic assessment of the equine fetal distal limb beyond the first phalanx for predicting fetal age and bone development in Quarter Horses.
articles.authors: Renaudin C, Wensley F, Morgan J et al.
articles.abstract: In Quarter Horses (QH), fetal age can be predicted within 2 weeks prior to 200- days of gestation ultrasonographically; however, as pregnancy advances, accuracy decreases. Recently, fetal ultrasonographic measurement of the first phalanx length (P1L) was introduced as a novel biometric parameter during late gestation, and the timing of appearance and closure of P1 epiphyses has been identified as potential markers of bone development. The overall aim of this study is to describe distal limb bone development beyond the first phalanx. Ten healthy pregnant mares (9 QH and 1 Thoroughbred carrying a QH fetus) with known ovulation dates were used. Transrectal ultrasonography was performed every 2 weeks from 9 months of gestation until parturition. P2 length (P2L) correlated highly with days of gestation (p < 0.0001; r2 = 0.75). A correlation equation was established: y = 5.343 (±0.403) x +205.1(±6.99) (y = predicted value of gestational age in days; x = P2 length in mm). Ossification of distal MC3, P1 and P2 epiphyses, and sesamoid bones, appeared in a chronological order, with the distal MC3 epiphysis ossification center appearing first, followed by distal P1, distal P2, proximal sesamoid bones, and finally distal sesamoid bone. Distal limb ossification can be considered complete in QH when the distal MC3 epiphysis, proximal epiphyses of P1 and P2, and all sesamoid bones are present. Clinically, fetal ultrasonography of the distal limb may be used to assess fetal age and bone development.

articles.title: Menopause Education in Plastic Surgery Residency Training: A Competency-Based Framework.
articles.authors: Chakradhar A, Esmail K, Ranganathan K et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause is a major yet underrecognized determinant of plastic surgery outcomes and patient concerns. Women now spend more than 40% of their lives in menopause, and peri‑ and postmenopausal women represent a substantial and growing proportion of patients seeking cosmetic and reconstructive procedures. Estrogen loss affects many tissues central to plastic surgery practice, including skin, adipose tissue, breast tissue, hair, and vulvovaginal structures, influencing both patient presentation and procedural outcomes. Menopause-related conditions such as genitourinary syndrome of menopause may also drive demand for interventions offered by plastic surgeons. Despite the relevance of menopause to surgical decision-making, patient counseling, and perioperative management, formal menopause education is absent from plastic surgery residency training. We propose a competency-based framework to integrate menopause education into plastic surgery graduate medical education. Building upon Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education competency domains and contemporary competency-based education principles, we developed 4 menopause-focused entrustable professional activities (EPAs): (1) screening for menopause during preoperative consultation, (2) referral for evidence-based medical management before procedural intervention when appropriate, (3) counseling patients on hormone-related changes relevant to surgical outcomes and expectations, and (4) providing menopause-informed breast health counseling. We describe implementation strategies including Menopause Education Teams composed of menopause specialists and plastic surgery faculty, incorporation of menopause-focused didactics into existing curricula, EPA-based assessment, and electronic health record prompts to facilitate clinical learning opportunities. Importantly, our proposal is grounded in prior successful educational innovations, including women's health EPAs, menopause-focused residency curricula, and the Geriatrics-for-Specialists initiative, which collectively demonstrate that competency-based, specialty-specific educational interventions can successfully address longstanding gaps in clinician preparedness and patient care. This framework provides a scalable model for incorporating menopause education into plastic surgery training and may serve as a template for other surgical specialties.

articles.title: The Duffy-Null genotype and epithelial ovarian cancer survival in a cohort of Black women.
articles.authors: Schildkraut JM, Marks JR, Peres LC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Black women experience poor survival from epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) for all stages at diagnosis and histotypes. The contribution of an ancestry-related genotype in the Atypical Chemokine Receptor 1 (ACKR1) gene to mortality after an EOC diagnosis in Black women has not been previously reported.
METHODS: The relationship between the Duffy-null genotype (CC) in the ACKR1 gene and overall post-enrollment mortality in 408 Black women with EOC, including 275 with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC) was evaluated using Bayesian modeling approach to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% credible intervals (CI) adjusting for stage, age at diagnosis, socioeconomic factors, and ovarian cancer family history. Tumor immune and genetic features were generated from sequencing assays on subsets of the HGSC cases.
RESULTS: The CC genotype was associated with reduced all-cause mortality among EOC cases (adjusted HR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.99). Among HGSC, the CC genotype was associated with higher African origin, lower ACKR1 expression (p = 0.049), lower cytotoxic T cell abundance (p = 0.062), and a higher frequency of homologous recombination deficient (HRD) tumors (p = 0.051).
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, the Duffy-null CC genotype was associated with 40% lower EOC all-cause mortality in Black women. These are hypothesis-generating findings that require replication and further inquiry into mechanisms.

articles.title: Impact of air gaps on rectal dose in high dose rate intracavitary brachytherapy: Using Monte Carlo simulations.
articles.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
articles.authors: Jayakody M, Gabriel L, Jeyasugiththan J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: High dose rate intracavitary brachytherapy (HDR-ICBT) is widely used for cervical cancer treatment, delivering high radiation doses to tumor while sparing surrounding organs at risk. However, air gaps between the applicator and the rectal wall can alter dose distributions, thereby affecting treatment outcomes.
AIM: This study evaluated the dosimetric impact of air gaps between the HDR-ICBT applicator and rectum using Monte Carlo (MC) simulations and compared the results with Treatment Planning Systems (TPS) calculations.
METHODS: A custom-designed acrylic phantom replicating HDR-ICBT geometry was equipped with PTW 9112 rectal and PTW 9113 bladder semiconductor probes. Clinical HDR-ICBT treatment plans using a60Co source were reproduced. GEANT4 MC simulations were performed to estimate dose deposition at the detector locations with and without an air gap.
RESULTS: Without air gap, TPS calculations and MC simulations showed good agreement, with mean percentage deviations ranging from 1.02% to 2.08%. With air gap, rectal detector positions showed systematic dose increases of 5-6%, whereas bladder detector position showed a smaller deviation of 3.16%. Across rectal detector positions, deviations ranged from -6.32% to 4.96% without air gap and from -1.94% to 11.52% with air gap. Box plot analysis showed a positive shift and increased variability under the air-gap condition.
CONCLUSION: Air gaps between the applicator and rectum introduce significant spatially dependent dose perturbations during HDR-ICBT, which are not accounted for in conventional TPS calculations. These findings highlight the importance of tissue heterogeneities in brachytherapy and MC-based dose verification to improve treatment accuracy and patient safety.

articles.title: Birthweight discordance and within-pair clustering of severe neonatal morbidity in twins in the neonatal intensive care unit.
articles.authors: Xu D, Li S, Yang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Morbidity may cluster within twin pairs, but birthweight discordance (BWD) may relate differently to pairs with one or both twins affected.
AIMS: To quantify co-twin morbidity concordance and examine associations between BWD and pair-level outcome patterns.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective single-center secondary cohort analysis.
SUBJECTS: 742 complete co-twin pairs admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
OUTCOME MEASURES: A composite of neonatal morbidities classified pairs as both non-severe, discordant, or both severe. BWD associations were estimated using multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: There were 401 both-non-severe, 152 discordant, and 189 both-severe pairs. Cohen kappa was 0.55 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.49-0.61), and the co-twin recurrence risk ratio was 4.48 (95% CI 3.66-5.46). In the main model, adjusted odds ratios for BWD ≥25% were 2.70 (95% CI 1.31-5.57) for discordant pairs and 1.99 (95% CI 0.94-4.23) for both-severe pairs. The two associations did not differ statistically (ratio of odds ratios 1.36, 95% CI 0.68-2.72; P = 0.387). The affected infant was lighter in 50.3% of unequal-weight discordant pairs (95% CI 42.0-58.6%). Congenital malformation was associated with being the affected co-twin (conditional odds ratio 6.75, 95% CI 2.36-19.29).
CONCLUSIONS: Neonatal morbidity clustered within NICU-admitted twin pairs. BWD ≥25% was associated with discordant morbidity in the main model, but the association was not evident at the 20% threshold or after additional covariate adjustment. Congenital malformation, but not birthweight rank, was a within-pair correlate of morbidity.

articles.title: Recovering from stigmatised loss following child removal into state care: a realist synthesis of institutional mechanisms shaping maternal health and inequality.
articles.authors: McGovern R, Smiles C, Grant C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The removal of a child into state care is a profoundly traumatic event for mothers, with enduring consequences for mental health, wellbeing, and social marginalisation. Policy and intervention responses following child removal have largely prioritised the prevention of recurrent care proceedings or rapid repeat pregnancy, little is known about the mechanisms through which support may facilitate recovery, resist stigma, and shape longer-term trajectories.
METHODS: We conducted a realist synthesis to examine how, for whom and under what circumstances interventions may work (or not) to support mothers following child removal. Drawing on academic literature, service evaluations, and stakeholder expertise, we developed and refined programme theories through iterative searching, contextualised data extraction, and theory testing, in line with RAMESES standards. Analysis integrated sociological and psychological theory, including stigma, narrative identity, and bereavement.
FINDINGS: Child removal emerged as a form of stigmatised loss that disrupts maternal identity and constrains grief. Five interrelated mechanisms were identified through which interventions may support recovery: (1) compassionate responses at the point of removal enabling 'mothering from a distance'; (2) non-stigmatising relationships that reduce shame and isolation; (3) trusted support to make sense of care entry; (4) trauma-informed, post-removal engagement addressing unmet needs; and (5) future-oriented identity reconstruction beyond a spoiled maternal self. These mechanisms were highly contingent on relational quality, timing, and institutional context. Practices experienced as coercive, including mandated contraception, risked reinforcing stigma and undermining recovery.
CONCLUSIONS: By conceptualising child removal as a stigmatised loss and identifying the institutional mechanisms through which post-removal support shapes recovery, this study advances understanding of child removal as a health-shaping social process with implications for population health and health inequalities.

articles.title: Structural reproductive problems and risk of endometriosis: A population-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Gete DG, Doust J, Mortlock S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between structural reproductive anomalies and the risk of endometriosis.
STUDY DESIGN: This study used data from the Genetic variants, Early Life exposures, and Longitudinal Endometriosis symptoms Study (GELLES), a sub-study of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH). We included 8563 women from two population-based cohorts (born 1989-95 and 1973-78). Poisson regression with robust error variance was used to estimate relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for sociodemographic, lifestyle, and reproductive or health-related factors.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Endometriosis was identified using self-reported data from the GELLES survey and validated against linked health records.
RESULTS: In both cohorts, structural reproductive anomalies were associated with an increased risk of endometriosis. In the 1973-78 cohort, women with structural anomalies were more likely to have endometriosis, with adjusted RR = 1.88 (95% CI 1.53, 2.30); similar findings were observed in the 1989-95 cohort, 1.63 (1.25, 2.13). In site-specific analyses of the 1973-78 cohort, uterine 1.86 (1.48, 2.35), cervical 1.77 (1.20, 2.62), and vaginal 3.23 (1.39, 7.55) anomalies were each independently associated with a higher risk. Both congenital uterine anomalies 2.48 (1.72, 3.59) and uterine positional variants, such as a retroverted uterus 1.66 (1.25-2.20), were linked with endometriosis. Associations remained consistent, though slightly attenuated, after excluding women with corrective surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Structural reproductive anomalies are independently associated with a higher risk of endometriosis. Greater clinical awareness and targeted monitoring of reproductive tract anomalies may support earlier recognition and management, potentially reducing disease burden.

articles.title: Association of prenatal PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 exposure with early childhood hemoglobin levels and anemia: Identification of susceptibility windows.
articles.authors: Zhu Y, Zhao X, Ma Y et al.
articles.abstract: The effects of exposure to particulate matter (PM) during different gestational periods on childhood anemia remain unexplored. This study included 1235 mother-offspring pairs derived from the pediatric subcohort of the Fujian Birth Cohort Study. Maternal exposure to PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 was estimated using the ChinaHighAirPollutants dataset for four periods: the entire pregnancy and each of the three trimesters. We employed linear and logistic regression models to assess the effects of PM exposure on hemoglobin levels and anemia incidence, respectively. Additionally, distributed lag models were performed to detect the sensitive windows. PM exposure was associated with reductions in hemoglobin levels throughout the entire pregnancy, particularly during the first and second trimesters. During the entire pregnancy, each 1 μg/m3 increment in PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 exposure was linked to a decrease in hemoglobin levels of 1.02 (95% CI: -1.52, -0.53), 0.87 (95% CI: -1.28, -0.46), and 0.37 (95% CI: -0.56, -0.19), respectively. Regarding anemia risk, in the first trimester, each unit increase in PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 increased the odds of developing anemia with ORs of 1.23, 1.16, and 1.09. DLMs showed that the sensitive window for PM exposure was early-mid pregnancy for hemoglobin levels but was limited to the first trimester for anemia risk.

articles.title: Body mass index and major surgical complications in outpatient surgical abortion: an Australia-wide case-control study.
articles.authors: Drever N, Johnston L, O'Brien C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing evidence on the association between body mass index (BMI) and surgical abortion complications is inconclusive and derives exclusively from retrospective cohort studies conducted in the United States of America, often underpowered for uncommon surgical outcomes. In Australia, BMI is commonly considered when determining eligibility for outpatient surgical abortion, yet no Australian data have examined its association with major surgical complications.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case-control study across 10 oupatient surgical abortion clinics operated by MSI Australia between 2016 and 2024. Cases were procedures complicated by major surgical complications (haemorrhage ≥500 mL, uterine perforation, hospital transfer, laparoscopy, laparotomy, disseminated intravascular coagulation, intensive care admission, blood transfusion, or hysterectomy), identified through mandatory incident reporting. Four gestation-matched controls were selected per case. BMI was analysed as a continuous variable, as obesity (≥30 kg/m2), and by ordered categories. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for parity, gestational age and previous caesarean section.
RESULTS: BMI data were available for 775 of 795 individuals (159 cases, 636 controls). Mean BMI was slightly higher among cases than controls (25.9 vs 24.8 kg/m2; P = 0.017), but distributions were similar. Crude associations between BMI, obesity and complications did not persist after adjustment (per-unit increase: adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.01, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.04; obesity: aOR 1.24, 95% CI 0.78-1.96).
CONCLUSIONS: BMI was not an independent predictor of major surgical complications in outpatient surgical abortion within the BMI range represented. Risk stratification should prioritise gestational age, parity and previous caesarean section rather than BMI alone, noting limited data for very high BMI categories.

articles.title: In Vitro Fertilization or Intrauterine Insemination in Unexplained Infertility.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.authors: Prentice LR, Sadler LC, Anderson KL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited.
METHODS: We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points.
RESULTS: A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation.
CONCLUSIONS: In couples with unexplained…

articles.title: Effect of Solution-focused Outpatient Follow-up on Post-surgery Resilience and Sexual QoL in Cervical Cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of lower genital tract disease
articles.authors: Wang B, Chang Z
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer patients often experience impaired psychological adaptation and sexual quality of life after surgery, highlighting the need for effective follow-up interventions.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of an outpatient solution-focused follow-up intervention with postoperative psychological resilience, sexual quality of life, and related psychosocial outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 115 patients (42 control, 73 intervention) treated between 2023 and 2025. Primary outcomes were psychological resilience [Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC)], sexual quality of life [Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI)], and sexual distress [Female Sexual Distress Scale (FSDS)]. Secondary outcomes included anxiety and depression [Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)], overall quality of life [Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (QLQ-C30)], and self-efficacy (General Self-Efficacy Scale). Assessments were conducted before discharge and at 3 and 6 months postoperatively. Multivariable regression, linear mixed-effects models, and propensity score methods were applied.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. At 3 and 6 months, the intervention group showed higher CD-RISC and FSFI scores and lower FSDS scores. At 6 months, CD-RISC (72.6 vs 64.2), FSFI (26.9 vs 23.2), and FSDS (8.9 vs 12.1) significantly favored the intervention group. Multivariable analysis confirmed independent associations with improved outcomes. Secondary measures also showed consistent benefits.
CONCLUSION: Solution-focused follow-up is associated with improved psychological and sexual outcomes, supporting its clinical utility in postoperative care.

articles.title: Sensitivity of spontaneous abortion classification to hierarchical algorithm assumptions in US commercial claims data, 2018-2024.
articles.authors: Fuerst M, Schrote K, Rodriguez MI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying spontaneous abortion (SAB) and induced abortion (IAB) in administrative data compared to other pregnancy outcomes is challenging due to shared billing codes and lack of reimbursement by many insurers.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Merative MarketScan Commercial Database from 2018-2024. We adapted a previously published hierarchical algorithm to reduce the number of unknown or ambiguous pregnancy outcomes. We then tested the assumptions of the hierarchy by alternating the order of the diagnosis, procedural, and diagnosis-related group (DRG) codes within the algorithm for SAB and IAB.
RESULTS: Our dataset included 2,418,986 pregnancy episodes. Our modified algorithm improved the sensitivity for SAB, identifying a 17.5% incidence compared to 14.9% for previously published algorithms and reduced unclassified outcomes from 17.4% to 13.4%. Prioritizing IAB in the algorithm hierarchy over SAB identified an additional 8,623 IAB cases. However, IAB identification remained low at less than 5% of pregnancy episodes.
CONCLUSIONS: Following the Dobbs decision, it is critical that researchers accurately identify early pregnancy claims and remain transparent in their methodology. Our algorithm improved sensitivity for SAB and reduced unknown outcomes. However, claims-based analyses may systematically undercount IAB, with implications for research-informed reproductive health policy.

articles.title: A Randomized Trial of Multimodal Prehabilitation Before Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy to Improve Postoperative Quality of Life and Functional Outcomes.
articles.authors: Carbonell E, Dana F, Tena B et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) causes postoperative impairments. Although prehabilitation has shown benefits in surgical populations, data specific to RARP remain limited. We evaluated whether multimodal prehabilitation improves early postoperative health-related quality of life (HRQoL), functional recovery and mental health.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective, single-center randomized trial including men with prostate cancer scheduled for RARP (May 2022- September 2024). Participants were randomized to a 4-week multimodal prehabilitation program including physical and pelvic floor muscle training, nutritional counselling and psychological support or to usual care. The primary outcome was change in the EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status score from baseline to 1 month after surgery. Secondary endpoints included functional and perioperative outcomes at 1, 3 and 6 months.
RESULTS: Ninety-five of 100 randomized patients were analyzed (53 prehabilitation, 42 control). At 1-month post-operatively, global health status score was higher in the prehabilitation group (adjusted mean difference +15 points, 0-100 scale; 95% confidence interval (CI) 7-22; p<0.001). Improvements at 1-month were also observed in several HRQoL domains, mental health and urinary continence (mean difference in ICIQ-UI SF -2.7; p=0.032). No differences were detected in physical performance or erectile function. Prehabilitation benefits attenuated over time, with the global health status difference decreasing to +4.5 points at 6 months (-1.9 points/month; p = 0.024), whereas improvements in selected HRQoL domains, mental health, and ICIQ-UI SF were maintained throughout follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal prehabilitation before RARP is feasible and should be integrated into clinical practice, as it enhances postoperative recovery and patient-centered outcomes.

articles.title: MRI BRAIN lesions and growth after antenatal steroids in preterm infants: Does timing matter?
articles.authors: Malova M, Caruggi S, Pozzi F et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Antenatal corticosteroids (ACS) are widely used to improve outcomes in preterm infants, with known benefits on respiratory morbidity and intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH). However, the effect of ACS timing on brain injury and development remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the impact of a complete course of ACS (ccACS), with particular attention to timing, on brain lesions, growth, and neurodevelopment in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this historical cohort study, all VLBW infants admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between January 2019 and December 2021 were included. Clinical data, including timing of ACS administration, were collected. The primary outcome was the occurrence of brain injury on MRI at term-equivalent age, including IVH, white matter lesions (WML), and cerebellar hemorrhage (CBH). Secondary outcomes were brain growth and maturation on MRI and neurodevelopment at 2 years assessed using the Griffiths Mental Development Scales. Outcomes were compared between infants with and without ccACS and according to different administration-to-birth intervals.
RESULTS: A total of 189 infants were included, of whom 139 (73.5%) received ccACS. Infants exposed to ccACS had a lower incidence of WML (p = 0.02) and moderate/severe IVH (p = 0.04). In extremely preterm infants (<28 weeks), IVH was significantly less frequent when ccACS was administered within 7 days before birth (p = 0.006). No significant differences were observed in brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopmental outcomes at 2 years.
CONCLUSIONS: A complete course of ACS was associated with unadjusted lower rates of brain injury in VLBW infants, particularly when administered within 7 days before birth in extremely preterm infants, without adverse effects on brain growth, maturation, or neurodevelopment at 2 years.

articles.title: Estrogen Use and Porphyria Cutanea Tarda.
articles.authors: Erichsen PA, Heerfordt IM, Mogensen M et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Estrogen-containing therapy is considered a risk factor for porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT), but the evidence is limited to clinical series and case reports.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether estrogen-containing therapy is associated with incident PCT, overall and according to estrogen-containing therapy type and route of administration.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this matched case-control study using data from Danish nationwide registries conducted from January 1, 1995, through November 1, 2024, female individuals with a first-time hospital diagnosis of PCT were matched 1:100 with population control patients on age, sex, and index date.
EXPOSURE: At least 1 redeemed prescription of estrogen-containing therapy within 1 year before the index date.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for incident PCT were calculated from conditional logistic regression. Analyses were stratified by estrogen-containing therapy type and route of administration. Analyses were adjusted for PCT-related comorbidities: HIV infection; liver disease, viral hepatitis, or iron overload; smoking-related diagnosis or treatment; and alcohol or drug misuse diagnosis or treatment.
RESULTS: The study included 438 female case patients with incident PCT (median age, 61.16 years [IQR, 51.08-69.17 years]) and 43 800 age-matched female control patients. In total, 154 cases (35.16%) and 9433 control patients (21.54%) had been exposed to any estrogen-containing therapy within 1 year before the index date (adjusted OR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.66-2.49). Estrogen-containing contraceptives were associated with incident PCT (adjusted OR, 2.52; 95% CI, 1.67-3.82) as were estrogen-only therapy (adjusted OR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.23-2.03), and combined estrogen and progestogen therapy (adjusted OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.53-3.11). When stratified by route of administration, oral therapy was associated with PCT (adjusted OR, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.66-3.59), whereas nonoral routes were not.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This nationwide matched case-control study found that estrogen-containing therapy was associated with incident PCT. In route-specific analyses, only oral therapy was associated with PCT, suggesting that route of administration should be considered when evaluating estrogen exposure as a potential risk factor for PCT.

articles.title: Community Health Workers and Adolescent Health and Well-Being Across Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.authors: Lin Y, Adesina O, Asuma BS et al.
articles.abstract: Adolescence represents a pivotal stage of development. Community health workers (CHWs) may offer a valuable approach to addressing adolescent health challenges in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). This review systematically synthesized evidence on the effectiveness of CHW-led interventions to improve adolescent health and well-being in SSA. We searched 14 databases and 17 grey literature sources for studies published between January 2014 and October 2024. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024618546). Interventions were categorized by setting (community or school) and provider (lay or paraprofessional; peer-led or adult-led). Vote counting and meta-analyses were conducted, alongside risk of bias using Joanna Briggs Institute tools and evidence quality assessments using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Thirty-five studies were included spanning across 12 countries and 12 outcomes. All outcomes were summarized narratively. Meta-analyses showed very low-certainty strong evidence for increased modern contraceptive use (risk ratio: 1.50; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-1.99), low-certainty moderate evidence for reduced depression (standardized mean difference: -0.31; 95% CI, -0.61-0.00), and low-certainty weak evidence for improved human immunodeficiency virus viral suppression (risk ratio: 1.16; 95% CI, 0.99-1.36). No clear effects were observed for sexual health knowledge, unmet need for contraception, or adolescent pregnancy, all with very low certainty. CHW-led interventions show promise for improving adolescent contraceptive use and mental health in SSA. However, substantial heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation, and more rigorous evidence is needed across all health domains.

articles.title: Beyond reproduction: the emerging role of FSH in postmenopausal aging.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.authors: Vallejo MS, Paradas A, Neira H
articles.abstract: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is traditionally regarded as a biochemical marker of menopause and declining ovarian function. However, emerging evidence suggests that its role may extend beyond reproductive physiology. During the menopause transition, FSH concentrations rise progressively, initially due to declining inhibin B and later to loss of ovarian estradiol and inhibin production. Evidence of FSH effects in bone, adipose tissue, the cardiovascular system and brain has raised the possibility of broader physiological actions. Higher FSH levels have been associated with bone loss and hip fracture risk, adverse cardiometabolic and vascular changes, and cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease. Although these associations do not establish causality, they suggest that FSH may contribute to some consequences of reproductive aging rather than simply reflect ovarian failure. Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Toward a digital urinary biopsy for early risk stratification in diabetic kidney disease: Anchoring shed cells, vesicles, and cell-free DNA to spatial kidney cell states.
articles.authors: Wu J, Sheng P, Lu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease worldwide. However, albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which define and stage DKD, report established injury and do not resolve the cellular heterogeneity underlying variable progression. Urine, the only biofluid to traverse every nephron segment, carries shed cells, extracellular vesicles (EVs) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA), each retaining information about its cell of origin.
MAIN BODY: This review develops the concept of a digital urinary biopsy, in which the three compartments are read together against spatial single-cell kidney atlases to infer non-invasively which cell states are active and whether niche-associated programs are engaged, an approach we term atlas-anchored molecular profiling. For each compartment, we tabulate study population, sample size, processing, assay, performance and validation status. Because shed-cell RNA, selectively sorted vesicle cargo and cfDNA methylation differ in origin, measurement scale and bias, each requires its own reference matrix, sampling function and background terms. All three carry renal information in feasibility studies, yet none is a validated clinical assay in DKD. Moreover, a cfDNA methylation reference at the required resolution is lacking, and no named computational method has been tested on urine.
CONCLUSION: We therefore present the framework as a structured research hypothesis and define the required validation, from analytical and clinical validity to prospective demonstration of utility, with non-albuminuric DKD, which albuminuria-based screening misses, as the index use case. It offers a testable route to cell-resolved, non-invasive staging of DKD rather than a demonstrated capability.

articles.title: An open-label, Phase 1 study to evaluate the drug-drug interaction between ulonivirine and the combined oral contraceptive levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol in female participants without HIV.
articles.authors: Robinson M, Gillespie G, Kandala B et al.
articles.abstract: Ulonivirine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor in development as an oral, once-weekly treatment for HIV-1 in combination with investigational islatravir. The effect of ulonivirine on the pharmacokinetics of an oral contraceptive, levonorgestrel (LNG)/ethinyl estradiol (EE) was evaluated in females without HIV. In this Phase 1 study (MK-8507-009), postmenopausal or oophorectomized females received a single dose of LNG/EE (0.1 mg/0.02 mg), followed by a 5-day washout period. Participants then received ulonivirine 400 mg once-weekly for 3 weeks, and LNG/EE was co-administered with the third dose. Blood samples were collected for pharmacokinetics analysis. Safety and tolerability were monitored by clinical and laboratory assessments. Twenty adults (90% White; 100% Hispanic or Latina) were enrolled (median age, 56 years; range, 47-66 years). Two participants discontinued for reasons considered unrelated to ulonivirine. The geometric mean ratios ([LNG/EE + ulonivirine]/[LNG/EE]; 90% CI) for plasma AUC0-inf of LNG and EE were 0.88 (0.84-0.93) and 0.85 (0.82-0.89). Maximum plasma concentration of LNG and EE decreased (26% and 20%, respectively) with LNG/EE + ulonivirine versus LNG/EE alone. Ulonivirine pharmacokinetics were similar for LNG/EE + ulonivirine and LNG/EE alone. Four participants (20%) experienced ≥1 adverse event: 2 (10%) after administration of LNG/EE alone and 2 (10.5%) after co-administration of LNG/EE + ulonivirine. All adverse events were mild and considered unrelated to study intervention. Co-administration of ulonivirine 400 mg once-weekly with a single dose of LNG/EE had no clinically meaningful effect on the pharmacokinetics of LNG or EE in females without HIV and was generally well tolerated.

articles.title: Into women's hands? A transnational cartography of misoprostol in Burkina Faso and Senegal.
articles.authors: Suh S, Ndoye T, Sawadogo N
articles.abstract: In global reproductive health discourses, misoprostol is represented as a pharmaceutical panacea for maternal mortality reduction in sub-Saharan Africa. We locate misoprostol in transnational and postcolonial politics of pharmaceutical governance, whereby reproductive commodities are deployed to discipline African women's fertility, and Africa represents a global epicentre of pharmaceutical trafficking. Drawing on ethnographic research in Burkina Faso and Senegal, we show how misoprostol is manufactured and travels across continents and through pharmaceutical regulatory systems to distributors, health workers, vendors, and consumers. Misoprostol's availability, quality, authenticity, and price in official and unofficial circuits are deeply embedded in these transnational processes and are marked by inequities in access to medications. We disrupt the essentialisation of misoprostol as a life-saving medication for African women, or as a safe tool for reproductive self-care, and show instead how it falls short of delivering these promises.

articles.title: Gut-Mammary Axis-Mediated Improvement of Sialylated Milk Oligosaccharide Synthesis by Polygonatum sibiricum Polysaccharide and Probiotics in Mice with Gestational Metabolic Disorders.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.authors: Wang Y, Kang YL, Rui BQ et al.
articles.abstract: Milk oligosaccharides (MOs) are vital for infant health but vulnerable to gestational metabolic dysfunction. To explore a new microecological intervention strategy, we established a probiotic fermentation platform coupled with a mammary epithelial cell screening model to identify Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide (PSP) as a promising candidate. Murine models demonstrated that both PSP monotherapy and synergistic treatment with probiotics significantly mitigated gestational metabolic dysregulation and restored postpartum sialylated MOs. Mechanistically, the combined treatment outperformed single interventions by modulating glycerophospholipid (GPL) and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolism, mitigating mammary gland mitochondrial dysfunction and ATP deficiency, and significantly upregulating the mRNA expression of sialyltransferase gene ST3GAL1. Notably, ATP restoration improved precursor availability, while ST3GAL1 upregulation promoted terminal sialylation, jointly facilitating sialylated MO biosynthesis. Our findings provide novel insights into how maternal metabolic health governs sialylated MO biosynthesis via the gut-mammary gland axis and propose a synergistic microecological intervention strategy for gestational metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Chromosomal aberrations of reproductive dysfunction: An in-depth retrospective study of 1943 individuals with unexplained infertility.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Iravani F, Namjoo K, Montazeri F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fertility refers to the ability to achieve a clinically successful pregnancy. Chromosomal aberrations constitute a fundamental etiological factor in reproductive dysfunction, with prevalence rates substantially elevated in infertile populations compared to general demographic baselines. This comprehensive retrospective investigation aimed to elucidate the cytogenetic signatures underlying infertility pathogenesis through systematic karyotypic analysis.
METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated individuals referred to the Yazd Reproductive Sciences Institute between April 2016 and March 2025 for reproductive health concerns. Among 7768 individuals assessed during the study period, 1943 had infertility and underwent cytogenetic evaluation. Peripheral blood lymphocytes were analyzed using standardized Giemsa (GTG)-banding karyotyping at a resolution of 400-550 bands per haploid genome. Chromosomal abnormalities were classified according to the International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature (ISCN) 2020 guidelines, encompassing structural variants, numerical abnormalities, complex karyotypic alterations, and polymorphic heteromorphisms. The demographic characteristics of the patients were systematically evaluated and analyzed in correlation with their chromosomal abnormalities.
RESULTS: Among the 1943 individuals with infertility, chromosomal abnormalities were identified in 229 cases (12.0%), including numerical sex chromosome abnormalities (46.7%), chromosomal polymorphic variants (41.5%), structural abnormalities (9.2%), and complex karyotypes (2.6%). Males accounted for 83.8% of abnormal cases, with Klinefelter syndrome representing the most frequent abnormality.
CONCLUSION: This study highlights that detecting chromosomal abnormalities in infertile couples is crucial for elucidating infertility etiology align with optimizing treatment and genetic counseling.

articles.title: Integrating large language models and expert knowledge to identify risk factors and predict mode of delivery with machine learning.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Rashidi F, Qanbarzadeh S, Orooji A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurately predicting the mode of delivery is a significant challenge in obstetrics, with implications for maternal healthcare planning, resource allocation, and personalized patient counseling. While machine learning offers promising predictive capabilities, the selection of relevant clinical and socioeconomic risk factors from vast possibilities remains a critical and nontrivial step that directly affects model performance and clinical utility.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to (1) predict the mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) using machine learning algorithms and (2) identify the key risk factors influencing delivery mode prediction.
