METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on eligible pregnant women who delivered at Bent-Al-Huda Hospital in Bojnourd, Iran. A hybrid feature identification approach was employed: large language models (LLMs) initially proposed 63 potential risk factors. Through iterative refinement involving domain experts and assessment of data availability and frequency, this list was consolidated to 35 final variables for modeling. Machine learning algorithms, including multilayer perceptron (MLP), decision tree, naïve Bayes, and support vector machine (SVM), were applied to build predictive models.
RESULTS: Among all models, SVM showed the best performance using all features, achieving an accuracy of 94.8% and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94. Decision tree analysis identified previous cesarean section history, insurance type, and fetal presentation as the three most important predictive factors. After excluding 40 women with prior cesarean delivery, SVM maintained robust performance with accuracy of 94.3% and an AUC of 0.92. Using antenatal features only, MLP achieved the highest accuracy before and after excluding women with previous cesarean section (92.9% and 92.2%), while SVM also showed the highest discriminative ability (accuracy 92.4%, AUC 0.90 and accuracy 91.3%, AUC 0.87, respectively).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that combining expert knowledge with LLMs enables effective risk factor identification and that careful feature selection allows the proposed model to predict delivery type with high accuracy.

articles.title: Listeria monocytogenes favors the vacuolar compartment during ex vivo human placental infections.
articles.authors: McLeod PA, Ubhi JS, Vogl AW et al.
articles.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes poses a serious concern during pregnancy, as these microbes can cross the placental barrier to infect the developing fetus. The pathogen's intracellular lifecycle has been well characterized in cultured cells, where the internalized bacteria escape short-lived Listeria-containing vacuoles (LCVs), replicate in the cytoplasm, and recruit host actin to generate comet tails that enable their intra- and inter-cellular movement. Whether these events occur during intact human placental infections remains unknown. Through ex vivo placental infections, we characterized the spatiotemporal progression of L. monocytogenes in a physiologically relevant system. We found that the actin-rich structures, which are hallmarks of cultured cell infections, were essentially absent (<1% of L. monocytogenes were associated with actin-rich structures). Instead, the bacteria remained predominantly restricted within LCVs, where they also replicated. Quantitative histological and immunofluorescence analyses showed that 39% of wild-type L. monocytogenes remained within Rab5-positive vacuoles and 44% in Lamp1-positive vacuoles, whereas only 1%-4% were observed in cultured placental cells. Most vacuoles lacked the vATPase and cathepsin B, indicating that placental LCV vacuoles were non-acidified, non-degradative endosomal niches. These results closely phenocopied infections using Δhly-L. monocytogenes, which do not generate listeriolysin O (LLO), a bacterial toxin crucial for LCV escape. Together, our findings reveal that L. monocytogenes primarily reside within LCVs during ex vivo human placental infections, contrasting the classical in vitro models and emphasizing the importance of studying bacterial pathogenesis in intact human tissues.IMPORTANCEL. monocytogenes infection during pregnancy can result in miscarriage, stillbirth, or severe neonatal disease because the bacterium can cross the placental barrier. Current understanding of L. monocytogenes pathogenesis is largely based on cultured cell models, where bacteria rapidly escape vacuoles, replicate in the cytoplasm, and spread using host actin. By examining infections in intact ex vivo human placental tissue, we show that this paradigm does not accurately reflect a placental infection. Instead, L. monocytogenes remains predominantly within vacuoles that may support bacterial replication, while actin-based motility is rare. Our work provides new insight into placental listeriosis and highlights the…

articles.title: Clinical performance of sFlt-1/PlGF ratio triage in suspected pre-eclampsia: A prospective, observational multicenter diagnostic-triage study in South Africa (TsHEPPO study).
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Bhorat I, Soma-Pillay P, Chauke L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic and short-term predictive performance of the soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1/placental growth factor (sFlt-1/PlGF ratio) in South African women with suspected pre-eclampsia (PE), comparing thresholds of ≥ 33 and ≥ 38 in a predominantly African population.
METHODS: This was a prospective, observational diagnostic-triage multicenter study across four tertiary hospitals in South Africa. A total of 555 women with suspected PE with complete outcome data were enrolled from four study sites. The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio (Elecsys, Roche Diagnostics) was measured at presentation and comprehensive clinical and delivery outcome data were collected. Diagnostic and short-term predictive performance for sFlt-1/PlGF thresholds (≥ 33 and ≥ 38) were assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), receiver operating characteristics (ROC) and associated area under the curve (AUC).
RESULTS: PE was diagnosed in 349/555 women (62.9%). The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio showed moderate discrimination for PE (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.7-0.8) overall. Continuous-data ROC analysis in 418 women from Durban, Johannesburg and Pretoria yielded an AUROC of 0.8465 (95% CI: 0.8090-0.8841). In the all-site analysis, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and accuracy were 67.05%, 89.32%, 91.41%, 61.54% and 75.32% at ≥ 33, and 62.46%, 90.29%, 91.60%, 58.68% and 72.79% at ≥ 38, respectively. In short-term prediction, both thresholds showed high sensitivity (86.5%) for PE within 7 days while specificity/PPV were 77.3%/81.8% at ≥ 33 and 81.8%/84.9% at ≥ 38, with NPVs of 82.9% and 83.7%, respectively. By 28 days, NPVs declined to 62% and 64%.
CONCLUSION: The sFlt-1/PlGF ratio is a clinically useful biomarker primarily as a rule-in triage tool for suspected PE in South Africa. The ratio showed high specificity and PPV in this predominantly African cohort. The exploratory ≥ 33 threshold increased sensitivity relative to ≥ 38, with a small reduction in specificity in the all-site estimates. The findings support its evaluation as an adjunct to clinical assessment in women with suspected PE. Both thresholds showed limited rule-out performance beyond short follow-up supporting the need for reassessment and repeat testing where clinically indicated. These findings support consideration of region-adapted thresholds and highlight the value of…

articles.title: Difficult-to-Catheterize Continent Channel Revision: Techniques and Outcomes in an Adult Cohort.
articles.authors: Chao BW, Ratanawong JP, Demzik A et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Continent catheterizable channels allow patients who cannot void volitionally to maintain quality of life. However, catheterizable channels are susceptible to various pathologies, which may necessitate revision. Outcomes after catheterizable channel revision in adults are poorly described and are the focus of this investigation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of adult patients undergoing continent catheterizable channel revision at a single institution between 2011 and 2024. Indications for revision included stomal or channel stenosis, redundancy, false passage, and parastomal hernia resulting in difficulty catheterizing. Revisions performed solely for channel incontinence were excluded. Surgeries were categorized by repair type: (1) suprafascial, involving superficial revision with a local skin flap, (2) subfascial, requiring mobilization of the intraperitoneal channel, and (3) channel replacement with a new bowel segment. The primary outcome was freedom from reoperation for recurrent stenosis.
RESULTS: We identified 45 patients who underwent 54 revisions. Common surgical indications were stomal stenosis (24/54, 44%) and channel stenosis (27/54, 50%). Over a median follow-up of 46 months, 41/54 (76%) revisions were successful: 13/19 (68%) for suprafascial revision, 18/20 (90%) for subfascial revision, and 10/15 (67%) for channel replacement (p = 0.178). Eight patients (15%) developed new channel incontinence after surgery; two (4%) developed a parastomal hernia. Study limitations include its retrospective design.
CONCLUSIONS: Adult continent catheterizable channel revision can be accomplished with satisfactory success rates. When abdominal entry is necessary for reconstruction, efforts should be made to preserve the existing channel. Patients should be counseled about the risks of de novo stress incontinence and parastomal hernia.

articles.title: Cardiac Renin-Angiotensin Signaling and Susceptibility to Extracellular Matrix Remodeling in Male Mouse Offspring Conceived by In Vitro Fertilization.
articles.authors: Jiang W, Wang J, Wei L et al.
articles.abstract: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) has been associated with increased cardiovascular risk in offspring, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether alterations in the cardiac renin-angiotensin system (RAS) are associated with increased susceptibility to myocardial fibrosis in offspring conceived via in vitro fertilization (IVF). Bioinformatics analysis and in vivo experiments were integrated. Cardiac transcriptomic data from IVF offspring (GSE211597) were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses. An IVF mouse model was established and subjected to a high-fat diet (HFD) as "a second hit". Metabolic parameters, cardiac histology, and expression of RAS- and fibrosis-related molecules were assessed. The angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) antagonist Candesartan was used to evaluate the functional involvement of RAS signaling. Transcriptomic analysis revealed significant alterations in metabolic and extracellular matrix (ECM)-related pathways, with Agt identified as a central hub gene. Under HFD, IVF offspring exhibited aggravated metabolic dysfunction and increased myocardial collagen deposition. Increased expression of angiotensinogen (AGT), AT1R, collagen type I alpha 1 chain (COL1A1), and collagen type I alpha 2 chain (COL1A2) suggested alterations in cardiac RAS signaling accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Candesartan partially improved metabolic abnormalities and attenuated RAS- and fibrosis-related molecular changes. IVF is associated with increased susceptibility to cardiac ECM remodeling under metabolic stress, accompanied by alterations in cardiac RAS-related signaling. Pharmacological blockade of AT1R partially attenuated these changes, suggesting a functional contribution of RAS signaling. These findings provide mechanistic insight into developmental origins of health and disease (DOHaD)-related cardiovascular risk and suggest that RAS signaling may represent a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Multisystem Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Active Comparators in Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.authors: Vashisht R, Dhruva SS, Patel A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) beyond cardiometabolic outcomes are incompletely characterized against active comparators in type 2 diabetes (T2D). We compared GLP-1RA with sulfonylureas (SUs), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4is) in adults with T2D.
METHOD: In a multicenter target trial emulation across 5 University of California academic medical centers (2012-2025) using harmonized electronic health record data, adults with T2D newly initiating GLP-1RA, SU, SGLT2i, or DPP4i were propensity score-matched 1-to-1 within site via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (>11 000 covariates), with up to 5-year follow-up. We screened 181 prespecified incident outcomes across 15 body systems, pooling hazard ratios by random-effects meta-analysis. Robustness required leave-one-medical-center-out stability, E-value ≥1.5, and false discovery rate-adjusted P < .10.
RESULTS: Among 70 982 matched adults, 118 robust associations were identified (65 for reduced risk and 53 for increased risk). Risk reductions were most consistent for cardiovascular outcomes, including myocarditis/cardiomyopathy (summary hazard ratio, 0.38 [95% CI, 0.32-0.44] vs SGLT2i), acute myocardial infarction (0.53 [0.42-0.66]), heart failure (0.71 [0.58-0.88] vs DPP4i), and thromboembolism (0.69-0.72), and for nephritis/nephrosis (0.73 [0.67-0.79]), nutritional anemia (0.70-0.81), coagulation disorders (0.73-0.81), and tobacco-related disorders (0.60 [0.49-0.74]). Risk increases were found for musculoskeletal conditions (22 associations); osteoarthritis 1.48 (1.29-1.68), stress fractures 1.68 (1.15-2.47), diverticular disease (1.18-1.33), sleep-wake disorders (1.27-1.54), and menopausal disorders (1.32-1.52).
CONCLUSIONS: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist initiation was associated with reduced cardiovascular, renal, hematologic, and tobacco-related risk, consistent with outcome trials. Increased risks for musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, and sleep-wake disorders warrant monitoring as the clinical use of GLP-1RAs continues to expand.

articles.title: Evaluation of urinary iodine concentration, thyroid volume, and thyroid function in the first trimester of pregnancy.
articles.authors: Ozdemir N, Akcura C, Gelir Cavdar G et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Iodine is a crucial element for thyroid hormone synthesis and plays an important role in regulating the body's basal metabolism. The aim of our study was to evaluate iodine status, thyroid volume, and thyroid function in pregnant women during the firsttrimester of pregnancy.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study included 130 healthy pregnant women in their first trimester between November 2022 and May 2024. However, urinary iodine concentration (UIC) data could not be obtained for two participants, and urinary iodine/creatinine ratio datawere missing for four participants because of insufficient sample volume. Laboratory tests, including free triiodothyronine (fT3), freethyroxine (fT4), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and thyroglobulin (Tg), were performed. First-morning single-spot urine samples were collected, and urinary iodine and creatinine concentrations were determined. The urine iodine/creatinine ratio (μg/g) was calculatedusing the following equation: urine iodine (μg/L)/urine creatinine (mg/dL) × 100. The thyroid gland, including thyroid volume, wasevaluated using ultrasonography.
RESULTS: The median UIC was 107.00 μg/L, indicating mild iodine insufficiency at the population level according to the World Health Organization criteria for pregnancy. Analysis of the spot urine samples revealed that 90 samples had a UIC below 150 μg/L. When the relationshipbetween the urine iodine/creatinine ratio and the measured parameters was investigated, Tg levels (p = 0.006) and thyroidvolume (p = 0.039) were significantly higher in the group with a urine iodine/creatinine ratio below 50 μg I/g Cr.
CONCLUSIONS: The statistically significant associations between the urine iodine/creatinine ratio and both Tg and total thyroid volume suggest a potential relationship between these parameters and lower urinary iodine/creatinine ratios.

articles.title: The anthocyanin-rich extract of Hibiscus sabdariffa enhances nuclear area, stratum thickness, and dendritic spines of hippocampal pyramidal cells in ovariectomized Wistar rats.
articles.authors: Lorenzana-Martínez G, Santerre A, Aguirre López LO et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian hypofunction is associated with morphological alterations in the hippocampus, including a reduced nuclear area of pyramidal cells and changes in dendritic length and branching, which are linked to cognitive decline. Synthetic estrogens can partially mitigate these effects; however, their use is associated with adverse outcomes, such as increased cancer risk and cardiovascular complications. Therefore, natural alternatives such as phytoestrogens, particularly anthocyanins, have gained attention as potential neuroprotective agents against ovarian hypofunction and menopause-related neurodegenerative and cognitive impairments. We previously reported that the anthocyanin-rich extract from the calyces of Hibiscus sabdariffa (HSE) increases estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) levels, restores brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression, and improves spatial memory in ovariectomized Wistar rats. The present study evaluated the effect of HSE on the nuclear area, thickness of the stratum Oriens and stratum Radiatum, and spine number of hippocampal pyramidal neurons in ovariectomized Wistar rats. Adult female Wistar rats were ovariectomized, except for sham-operated and intact control groups, and treated with HSE in drinking water for six weeks (50 or 100 mg/kg body weight). Morphological parameters were analyzed and quantified using hematoxylin-eosin staining, while dendritic spine number was assessed by Golgi silver impregnation. HSE administration increased the pyramidal neuron nuclear area, thickness of the Oriens and Radiatum strata, and dendritic spine number in CA1 and CA3 regions of the hippocampus, counteracting the deleterious effect of ovariectomy-induced ovarian hypofunction. These findings support the therapeutic potential of H. sabdariffa as a natural strategy to prevent morphological alterations in hippocampal pyramidal neurons associated with ovarian hypofunction and menopause.

articles.title: Mothers' subjective retrospective view of previous pregnancies and risk classification in the German maternity record (Mutterpass): a nationwide survey from the FeMaR study.
articles.authors: Metz CK, Tabernig B, Sommer J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: High-risk pregnancy classification is associated with intensified antenatal surveillance, increased use of hospital-based services, and substantial healthcare costs. Classification may influence women's subjective perceptions of pregnancy and its care.
METHODS: This study assessed women's retrospective perspectives on their subjective risk classification, antenatal care, complications, and perceptions of risk in Germany using a nationwide online cross-sectional survey. Participants were grouped according to their self-reported high- or low-risk pregnancy classification. Data were based on subjective retrospective reports of pregnancies occurring ≤1 to ≥30 years ago.
RESULTS: A total of 2012 women participated (mean age 33.4 ± 4.6 years). Approximately half reported having had high-risk pregnancy, most commonly due to a maternal age ≥35 years. Among women who reported having been classified as high-risk, 54.4 % considered the classification appropriate, of whom 81.8 % also assessed their antenatal care as adequate. The perceived appropriateness of the risk classification corresponded with how women evaluated the adequacy of their antenatal care. Self-reported pregnancy- and birth complications were comparable between high-risk and low-risk groups, with fetal distress as the most frequently reported complication in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on retrospective self-reported data, women's perceptions of pregnancy risk classification were associated with their assessment of antenatal care. The findings highlight the importance of transparent, patient-centered communication regarding pregnancy risk classification and provide exploratory insights that may inform the future development of more individualized risk assessment approaches incorporating women's perspectives.

articles.title: Travel time modelling of access to surgical abortion services in Australia: A nationwide spatial analysis of distance, geographic, and socio-economic inequities.
articles.authors: Wood SM, Noonan A, Coffee NT et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundIn Australia, abortion is fully decriminalised in all states and territories. Despite advances in telehealth and the expansion of prescribers of medication abortion, surgical abortion services are scarce. The absence of national service-location data further limits both accessibility and assessment of service coverage.ObjectivesTo calculate private vehicle travel times from all private dwellings to their nearest surgical service to identify accessibility inequities by area-level remoteness and socio-economic status.DesignCross-sectional spatial analysis of publicly available data.MethodsA nationwide dataset of 83 public and private surgical abortion services (i.e. excluding medication abortion) was compiled and geocoded. Travel times were calculated from 10.6 million private dwellings to the nearest service along the road network. For each state and territory, the rate of public surgical abortion services per 100,000 reproductive-aged females was calculated. Analyses were stratified by remoteness using the area-level Modified Monash Model and Index of Relative Socio-economic Advantage and Disadvantage.ResultsNationwide median travel time from private dwellings to the nearest surgical abortion service was 19.6 minutes (IQR 11.9-35.3). Public-hospital-based services had a longer median travel time of 47.6 minutes (IQR 17.8-118.6) than private services, at 27.3 minutes (IQR 16.3-55.1). Public service provision varied across jurisdictions, ranging from 0.1 per 100,000 reproductive-aged females in New South Wales to 9.2 per 100,000 in the Northern Territory. Travel times increased with area-level socio-economic disadvantage and remoteness. An interactive web-based tool was developed to visualise these findings at national and local scales.ConclusionSpatial inequities in access to surgical abortion were evident, particularly outside metropolitan areas and in socio-economically disadvantaged areas. These findings highlight geographic barriers compounding existing financial and logistical challenges to care. This analysis was limited to publicly listed surgical abortion services and did not account for service capacity, affordability, or medication abortion access. Future analyses of medication abortion access, alongside improved national service location data, are needed to monitor changes in access and support equitable reproductive healthcare.

articles.title: Stress and menstrual cycle characteristics among adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic: An observational study using longitudinal app-tracking data.
articles.authors: Helmer CK, Shea AA, Vitzthum VJ et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundStress is linked to irregular menstrual cycles in adults, but little research has examined this relationship in adolescents. Adolescents may be particularly vulnerable because their menstrual cycles are still developing and more variable.ObjectivesTo investigate the association of stress and irregular menstrual cycle characteristics in adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic using data from the Clue menstrual cycle tracking app.DesignWe surveyed 13-18-year-old Clue app users (N = 6,486) in the United States about their perceived stress and linked responses to app-recorded menstrual cycle data.MethodsUsing mixed-effects models, we analyzed the association of overall stress and changes in stress during the pandemic with cycle and period length, dysmenorrhea, heavy flow, and three aspects of irregularity: short, long, and variable cycles.ResultsAdolescents reporting high perceived stress had higher odds of reporting dysmenorrhea (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.1, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.1-1.2, p = 0.001), and short cycles (<21 days) (aOR = 1.4, 95% CI: 1.1-1.8, p = 0.003), and had slightly longer periods (β = 0.1 days, 95% CI: 0.0-0.3, p=0.007) compared to those reporting low stress. Adolescents reporting that their stress levels had become much worse during the COVID-19 pandemic also had higher odds of reporting dysmenorrhea (aOR = 1.1, 95% CI: 1.1-1.2, p<0.001), and heavy flow (aOR = 1.2, 95% CI: 1.1-1.3, p<0.001) compared to those whose stress levels had not increased. Stronger associations between COVID-19 stress and report of dysmenorrhea were observed in users menstruating for <4 years (interaction p-value = 0.008).ConclusionIncreases in COVID-19 pandemic-related stress may have impacted adolescents' cycle characteristics, particularly among adolescents menstruating for <4 years.

articles.title: The Impact of Incretin-Based Therapies on Anthropometric and Metabolic Parameters in Women with Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome.
articles.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
articles.authors: Koceva A, Janež A, Jensterle M
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), affects 170 million women globally and is often accompanied by obesity and various levels of insulin resistance. Incretin-based therapies, including the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists liraglutide and semaglutide, and the dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) agonist tirzepatide, offer a biologically plausible mechanism for targeting metabolic dysfunction in PMOS. This review examines clinical trial evidence on the anthropometric and metabolic effects of incretin-based therapies in this population, including a focus on women of reproductive age, who face distinct challenges related to preconception planning, treatment duration, and post-discontinuation metabolic and weight management. Available literature shows that liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide produce clinically meaningful reductions in body weight, body mass index (BMI), and waist circumference, with some studies also confirming preferential effects on visceral and ectopic fat compartments. Glycaemic and insulin resistance outcomes vary across studies, while lipid and blood pressure effects remain incompletely characterized. Although emerging data suggest that higher-potency agents may yield more consistent weight-loss benefits, available PMOS-specific evidence does not establish comparative metabolic superiority among agents. Interpretation of the available evidence is limited by the predominance of short-term trials at sub-obesity doses, frequent co-administration with metformin, and the absence of phenotype-stratified data, leaving the full metabolic potential of these agents in PMOS incompletely defined. Larger, longer, and higher-dose trials are needed to fully characterize the anthropometric and metabolic potential of these agents in PMOS.

articles.title: Assessment of a direct fluorescence-based cell-free DNA assay for evaluating the extent of metastatic dissemination: An exploratory study.
articles.authors: Kim JJ, Lee Y, Hong YJ et al.
articles.abstract: Fluorescence-based cell-free DNA (cfDNA) assays quantify nucleic acids without the need for DNA extraction and amplification. The present study investigated whether cfDNA levels differed between patients with active cancer and those with no evidence of disease (NED). Blood samples from patients with metastatic cancer (Patient group) and from individuals with NED (patients that had completed curative-intent treatment and remained recurrence free for ≥1 year; NED group) were used to quantify cfDNA levels using PicoGreen™ reagent. In total, 124 participants were prospectively enrolled between January 2020 and August 2021 (Patient group, n=72; NED group, n=52). The median age was 69 years (range: 27-83 years) in the Patient group and 65 years (range: 34-81 years) in the NED group. In the Patient group, the pancreatobiliary (n=32, 44.4%), genitourinary (n=20, 27.7%) and gastrointestinal (n=6, 8.3%) sites were the most common primary cancer sites. The median cfDNA value in the Patient group (9.80 µg/ml, IQR 8.63-11.08) was significantly higher than that in the NED group (8.40 µg/ml, IQR 7.75-9.10, P<0.001). In addition, the median cfDNA levels were significantly higher in patients with a high extent of metastatic dissemination (defined as metastases in three or more organs) than in those with a low tumor extent (10.70 µg/ml, IQR 9.35-12.4 vs. 9.45 µg/ml, IQR 8.48-10.85, respectively; P=0.027). Notably, there was no significant correlation between cfDNA and conventional tumor marker levels, including carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels (P=0.468 and P=0.134, respectively). These findings indicated that cfDNA levels were elevated in patients with metastatic cancer compared with those with NED, particularly in those with a higher extent of metastatic dissemination. Additionally, cfDNA levels were not correlated with those of conventional tumor markers. These cross-sectional exploratory data highlight the potential utility of fluorescence-based cfDNA assays in assessing the extent of metastatic dissemination, and provide a foundational rationale for future longitudinal studies investigating treatment monitoring and prognosis.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Re attenuates severe acute pancreatitis-associated acute lung injury by inhibiting pancreatic necroptosis-driven cfDNA release and pulmonary cGAS-STING activation.
articles.authors: Hu C, Yang R, Luo W et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The high mortality of severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is primarily driven by multiple organ dysfunction, particularly acute lung injury (ALI), a condition for which lacks specific pharmacological therapy. Ginsenoside Re (Re) has documented anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, with preliminary evidence indicating its protective potential in pancreatic injury. However, its precise therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms in SAP, especially concerning the mitigation of systemic complications, remain incompletely understood.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of Re in SAP and to delineate the underlying mechanistic pathway connecting pancreatic acinar cell death to pulmonary injury.
METHODS: SAP was induced in mice by seven hourly cerulein injections followed by a final lipopolysaccharide challenge, and Re was administered intraperitoneally during the induction period. Primary pancreatic acinar cells (PACs) were isolated, and mouse pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (PMVECs) were cultured for in vitro studies. Underlying mechanisms were investigated through transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses, followed by molecular docking and experimental validation.
RESULTS: Re treatment significantly alleviated pancreatic injury in SAP mice, with a pronounced reduction in acinar necrosis. Integrated transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses identified necroptosis as a key target for these effects. Accordingly, Re inhibited RIPK3/MLKL-mediated necroptosis both in vivo and in vitro. The specific RIPK3 inhibitor GSK872 abolished cfDNA release from PACs, indicating that necroptosis is the primary source of cfDNA, and notably, Re mimicked these effects. Acinar cell-derived cfDNA was shown to induce pulmonary endothelial inflammation and barrier dysfunction via activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, effects that were abolished by DNase I. In addition, correlation analysis showed that mouse serum cfDNA levels were positively correlated with lung injury parameters. Further pulmonary transcriptomic analysis confirmed that Re treatment suppressed cfDNA-triggered activation of the cGAS-STING signaling in vivo, thereby contributing to the significant attenuation of lung injury.
CONCLUSION: Our study uncovers a novel pathological axis in SAP-ALI, wherein pancreatic necroptosis drives cfDNA release, which subsequently activates the pulmonary endothelial cGAS-STING signaling, ultimately leading to…

articles.title: The Association Between Glucose Intolerance and Longitudinal Fetal Growth in Nulliparas.
articles.authors: Mahdasian-Miller A, Peña A, Haas D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate fetal growth patterns and birth weight among individuals with normoglycemia, mild glucose intolerance, and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) from midgestation until delivery.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the NuMoM2b (Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-Be) prospective cohort of nulliparous individuals with singleton gestations. Maternal glucose tolerance was categorized as normal, mild glucose intolerance (one abnormal Carpenter-Coustan value), or GDM. Blinded ultrasounds at 16-22 weeks and 22-29 weeks provided fetal biometry z scores; suspected large for gestational age (LGA) was defined as an abdominal circumference or estimated fetal weight above the 90th percentile on ultrasound; LGA was confirmed as birth weight above the 90th percentile for gestational age and sex. Logistic regression and covariance pattern models assessed the association between glycemic status and LGA growth across time points.
RESULTS: Among 7,010 included participants, 175 (2.5%) had mild glucose intolerance, and 290 (4.1%) had GDM. Fetal biometry was similar across groups at 16-22 weeks. By 22-29 weeks, GDM was associated with accelerated fetal growth z scores, and both mild glucose intolerance and GDM were associated with increased odds of abdominal circumference above the 90th percentile (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.64, 95% CI, 1.08-2.50 and AOR 1.54, 95% CI, 1.10-2.16, respectively). By delivery, mild glucose intolerance carried a twofold increased risk for LGA birth weight (AOR 2.00, 95% CI, 1.29-3.10), whereas the LGA risk in those with GDM was similar to that in normoglycemic individuals (AOR 1.34, 95% CI, 0.91-1.98).
CONCLUSION: Fetal overgrowth associated with glucose intolerance emerges around the standard 24- to 28-week GDM screening window. Individuals with GDM had an LGA risk similar to those with normal glucose tolerance, consistent with the increased surveillance and clinical management associated with a GDM diagnosis attenuating the trajectory of excess fetal growth. Whether treatment of mild glucose intolerance can reduce LGA risk remains to be determined.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01322529.

articles.title: Psychological Impact of Fetal Echocardiography Referral on Pregnant Women With a Normal Routine Morphologic Ultrasound.
articles.journal: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease
articles.authors: Dufour C, Roy LO, Taillefer V et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal echocardiography (FE) is widely recommended in pregnancies at increased risk of congenital heart defects. Although FE is a safe diagnostic tool, its psychological impact on expectant pregnant women remains poorly understood.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study in 8 Canadian centers. Women aged ≥18 years with a normal second-trimester ultrasound between 18 and 26 weeks' gestation referred for an FE were compared with women who were not. Anxiety was assessed using the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory. The primary outcome was the difference between state and trait anxiety (net situational anxiety) after morphologic ultrasound but before FE (T0). Secondary outcomes included the proportion of participants with significant anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory ≥40) and anxiety trajectories after FE among referred participants.
RESULTS: Eighty-four women were included, of whom 38 were referred for FE. At T0, women referred for FE showed slightly higher median net situational anxiety compared with controls. In multivariable analyses, FE referral was associated with a modest increase although estimates were imprecise. A higher proportion of referred women reached a state anxiety score ≥40, though this association was weak after adjustment. Among the 14 women who completed post-FE questionnaires, anxiety trajectories were heterogeneous, with both increases and decreases observed after FE.
CONCLUSIONS: Referral for FE after a normal second-trimester ultrasound is associated with a small and variable increase in maternal anxiety. These findings suggest that FE referral may not be psychologically neutral and highlight the importance of considering maternal psychological responses as referral criteria broaden.

articles.title: Burden, Risk Factors, and Temporal Trends of Ovarian Cancer in Postmenopausal Women Aged 55 Years and Older: A Comparative Analysis in India, China, and the United States Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.authors: Wei T, Zheng H, Pei Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence remains limited on the ovarian cancer (OC) burden among women aged 55 years and older, used here as an operational proxy for the postmenopausal population, across India, China, and the United States.
METHODS: We extracted data on OC-related incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and relevant risk factors from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 for the period 1990-2023. We assessed age-specific patterns; temporal trends using the estimated annual percentage change and Joinpoint regression; age-period-cohort (APC) patterns and estimable functions; demographic decomposition; and DALY burdens attributable to high body-mass index (BMI) and occupational asbestos exposure. The Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model and Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model were applied to predict age-standardized DALY rates of OC through 2040.
RESULTS: Absolute incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased in all three countries, whereas age-standardized rates increased in India and generally declined in China and the United States. India had a comparatively greater burden in younger age groups within the study population, whereas the United States had the highest burden at older ages. In China, despite an overall negative net drift, local-drift point estimates were positive among women aged 85 years and older (0.03%-0.82% per year), although the 95% confidence intervals included zero. The proportion of DALYs attributable to high BMI increased in all three countries, and population growth was the principal positive driver of the rising absolute burden. Projections suggested a continued increase in India's age-standardized DALY rate and further declines in China and the United States through 2040.
CONCLUSION: Age-standardized OC burden increased in India but declined in China and the United States, whereas the absolute burden rose in all three countries; the non-significant positive local-drift point estimates among the oldest-old in China warrant monitoring. These ecological findings do not establish causality and support country-specific hereditary risk management and strengthened pathways for timely diagnosis and specialist referral.

articles.title: Prevalence and risk factors for stillbirths in India: secondary analysis of ICMR-Stillbirth Pooled India Cohort (ICMR-SPIC).
articles.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
articles.authors: ICMR-SPIC Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial reductions in stillbirth rate (SBR) over the past two decades, India continues to bear one of the highest burden of stillbirths worldwide. The available national evidence on stillbirth is fragmented, regionally variable, and often limited in scope. We aimed to determine stillbirth burden and risk factors leveraging a pooled cohort from ten prospective studies conducted across various settings in India.
METHODS: We established the Indian Council of Medical Research-Stillbirth Pooled India Cohort (ICMR-SPIC), combining individual-level data from ten prospective cohort studies conducted across multiple sites of India. The pooled dataset included prospective pregnancy cohort studies conducted across India between 1994 and 2023 from rural, urban, hospital, and community settings, with participant recruitment and follow-up periods varying across individual studies. After exclusions, 227,821 pregnancies were included. Harmonised analytical datasets were constructed, and weighted SBR was estimated. Multivariable mixed-effects modified Poisson regression was used to evaluate the association between stillbirth and independent maternal and antenatal risk factors. Population attributable fractions (PAFs) were calculated for modifiable exposures.
FINDINGS: A total of 3935 stillbirths occurred among 227,821 pregnancies, yielding a pooled weighted stillbirth rate of 14.8 per 1000 births (95% CI: 13.4-16.3). Independent risk factors included maternal age (>30 years) (aIRR 1.64, 95% CI: 1.55-1.72; PAF 3.23%, 95% CI: 2.97-3.48), informal maternal education (aIRR 1.45, 95% CI: 1.32-1.58; PAF 8.86%, 95% CI: 7.07-10.66), biomass fuel use (aIRR 1.37, 95% CI: 1.21-1.57; PAF 13.95%, 95% CI: 9.11-18.79), maternal height (<145 cm) (aIRR 1.32, 95% CI: 1.21-1.44; PAF 2.47%, 95% CI: 1.81-3.13), nulliparity (aIRR 1.36, 95% CI: 1.27-1.45; PAF 13.66%, 95% CI: 11.03-16.28), and previous history of stillbirth (aIRR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.15-3.97; PAF 2.13%, 95% CI: 0.97-3.29). Among obstetric complications, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (aIRR 4.18, 95% CI: 3.54-4.94; PAF 10.27%, 95% CI: 9.74-10.81) and antepartum haemorrhage (aIRR 12.12, 95% CI: 9.54-15.40; PAF 6.33%, 95% CI: 6.19-6.47) showed strong associations.
INTERPRETATION: Our study shows that stillbirth burden remains high and factors such as women's education, biomass fuel use, hypertensive disorders, and antepartum haemorrhage were associated with higher risk of stillbirths.
FUNDING: Indian Council…

articles.title: The impact of abortion denial on women's empowerment in Nepal (2019-2024): a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
articles.authors: Diamond-Smith NG, Foster DG, Puri MC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There has long been an interest in the association between family planning (contraception and abortion) and women's empowerment, with mixed evidence as to an association and most studies relying on cross sectional data. Within this body of work, less focus has been on how family planning impacts women's empowerment The aim of this study is to understand the impact of abortion denial resulting in having an unwanted birth on women's empowerment, measured by education, mobility and decision-making.
METHODS: In the Nepal Turnaway Study, we followed women seeking abortions from 2019 to 2020 in Nepal and assessed whether receiving versus being denied an abortion was negatively associated with women's empowerment over five years (longitudinal cohort). We used linear and logistic mixed effects regression models to assess the effects of obtaining an abortion compared to carrying an unwanted pregnancy to term on education, mobility outside the home and household decision-making power.
FINDINGS: We followed 1742 for 5 years and find that women who did not give birth were more likely to be in school (Risk Difference (RD) = 0.2 starting 18 months post-abortion seeking) and have greater decision-making power over five years (Risk Difference (RD) = -0.2 starting 12 months post-abortion seeking) and both of these continued for the remainder of the time period. We find no evidence that giving birth affects a woman's freedom to leave her home for shopping or connections to family and friends.
INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that being able to decide the timing and circumstances of childbearing has wide-ranging effects on women's empowerment (as measured by schooling and decision-making).
FUNDING: This study was supported by the National Institute of Health David and Lucile Packard Foundation.

articles.title: Antioxidants in male infertility: from empirical supplementation to phenotype directed therapy.
articles.authors: Zafar MI, Qu M
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress is a biologically plausible contributor to male infertility, and antioxidant supplementation has been investigated for decades. Yet clinical evidence has not converged on a reproducible benefit in reproductive outcomes. The 2025 World Health Organization (WHO) infertility guideline made no recommendation for or against antioxidant supplementation in men with infertility and one or more semen parameters outside WHO reference ranges, reflecting uncertainty rather than proof of universal inefficacy. A Cochrane review identified 90 randomized controlled trials involving 10,303 men, but live birth was reported in only 12 trials with very low certainty. Contemporary randomized trials have not resolved the uncertainty: MOXI found no improvement in semen parameters, sperm DNA fragmentation, pregnancy, or live birth with a multicomponent antioxidant formulation; FAZST found no benefit of folic acid and zinc on semen quality or live birth with an increase in sperm DNA fragmentation; and SUMMER found no improvement in ongoing pregnancy with a combined antioxidant supplement. These findings make routine empirical supplementation difficult to justify but do not establish universal inefficacy of redox modulating interventions. Most trials have enrolled men according to clinical infertility or semen criteria rather than a prospectively defined standardized redox phenotype and have rarely tested treatment effect modification. Biological and clinical heterogeneity, differences among interventions, physiological roles of reactive oxygen species, and reliance on surrogate endpoints may dilute true effects. Future trials should determine which biologically defined men, if any, benefit from which redox modulating intervention, using standardized phenotyping, target engagement measures, prespecified treatment by phenotype interaction testing, and clinically meaningful reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Atmospheric Pollution by Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) and Low Birth Weight: A Cross-Sectional Study in Binza Ozone Health Zone, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2022.
articles.authors: Valuvunina CM, Ngwimi MM, Konde JNN et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Air pollution is a major risk factor for perinatal health. PM2.5 can cross the placenta and induce oxidative stress and inflammation, promoting fetal growth restriction and low birth weight (LBW). Sub-Saharan Africa has the highest PM2.5 exposures in the world, but data on perinatal outcomes there are limited. In the DRC, urbanization and unregulated quarries degrade air quality. The Binza Ozone Health Zone in Kinshasa is home to the Carrigrès quarry within densely populated neighborhoods. No study in the DRC has evaluated the link between PM2.5 exposure and LBW. This study aimed to analyze the association between PM2.5 exposure, proximity to the quarry, and LBW.
METHODS: Cross-sectional study of 355 mothers who delivered between January and December 2021 in six healthcare facilities in Binza Ozone. Data were collected via interviews and reviews of antenatal care (ANC) and delivery registries. LBW was defined as a weight < 2500 g. PM2.5 was measured over 48-72 h per health area in September-October 2022 using calibrated PurpleAir PA-II-SD sensors. The PurpleAir PA-II-SD sensor is a low-cost optical particle counter that was calibrated against the Federal Reference Method (FRM) Beta Attenuation Monitor (BAM) in Kinshasa, as described by McFarlane et al. (2021); the calibration equation applied was as follows: PM2.5 (corrected) = 0.52 × PM2.5(raw)+3.2. Sites were classified as "highly polluted" > 75 μg/m3 or "polluted" ≤ 75 μg/m3 based on the median. Distance to the Carrigrès quarry was categorized as < 500 m and ≥ 500 m. Bivariate analysis was performed using the chi-square test. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), adjusted for age, parity, education level, maternal alcohol consumption, tobacco exposure (active and passive smoking), nutritional factors (dietary diversity score and mid-upper arm circumference), and gestational complications. The significance threshold was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Median age was 26 years (IQR: 20-36). 67.3% had a secondary education level. LBW prevalence: 12.96%, n = 46/355, 95% CI [9.7-16.9]. This prevalence is significantly higher than 7.8% reported for Kinshasa Province in the MICS-DRC 2017-2018 survey, confirming the existence of a local aggravating factor. PM2.5 levels ranged from 54.6 to 102.5 μg/m3, exceeding both the WHO annual guideline of 5 μg/m3 and the WHO 24-h guideline of 15 μg/m3. In bivariate analysis, residing…

articles.title: Persistent Pediatric Cervical Lymphadenopathy: A Case Report of Kikuchi-Fujimoto Disease Mimicking Infection and Malignancy.
articles.authors: Thomas M, Stevens D, Davis C et al.
articles.abstract:
CASE PRESENTATION: A 10-year-old female presented with 2 months of unilateral cervical lymphadenopathy despite several courses of oral antibiotics. She presented to the emergency department due to persistent pain and swelling along with new fever. On presentation, she was febrile to 39.0°C. Physical examination revealed significant left-sided cervical and submandibular lymphadenopathy with tenderness, warmth, and overlying erythema. Initial labs were notable for leukopenia (2.6 × 103/μL), thrombocytopenia (135,000/μL), and elevated liver enzymes. Computed tomography (CT) of the neck demonstrated necrotic left cervical lymphadenopathy with prominent right cervical lymph nodes. An infectious workup, including testing for Epstein-Barr virus, Cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus, coccidioidomycosis, tuberculosis, and microbial cell-free DNA sequencing, was negative. Initial fine-needle aspiration (FNA) and core needle biopsy showed predominantly necrotic tissue. Cultures obtained during the biopsy showed no growth, and flow cytometry was negative for leukemia/lymphoma markers. Intravenous (IV) ceftriaxone administration resulted in improvement in neck swelling and fever resolution. Histopathologic examination from excisional biopsy revealed histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis consistent with Kikuchi-Fujimoto (KFD) lymphadenitis. Comprehensive autoimmune serologies were negative. Naproxen was prescribed to help with residual inflammation.
DISCUSSION: KFD should be considered in children presenting with prolonged cervical lymphadenopathy refractory to antibiotics. This case illustrates several diagnostic challenges inherent in making this diagnosis. The patient's prolonged unilateral cervical lymphadenopathy, necrotic imaging findings, and transient improvement with antibiotics strongly suggested bacterial lymphadenitis or malignancy. However, the persistence of symptoms despite multiple appropriate antibiotic courses, the development of cytopenias and elevated liver enzymes, and ultimately nondiagnostic cultures represented key findings prompting reconsideration of the initial differential diagnoses. This case also highlights the importance of considering excisional biopsy when core biopsy is nondiagnostic.

articles.title: Personality beyond the brain: a new perspective on the brain-gut-gonadal axis and human fertility.
articles.authors: Doroftei B, Kamar AAM, Ciobica A et al.
articles.abstract: Despite major advances in reproductive medicine, many cases of infertility remain unexplained. Hormonal, genetic, anatomical, and environmental factors have been extensively investigated, whereas the possible contribution of personality characteristics to reproductive physiology has received little attention. Throughout this review, personality refers to relatively consistent individual characteristics and should not be confused with temporary emotional states or acute psychological stress. Published evidence reports associations between personality characteristics and measures of autonomic and neuroendocrine regulation, gastrointestinal symptoms or function, sexual function, and reproductive health. However, the strength and type of evidence vary across these domains, and most findings are observational or associative rather than causal. Established biological pathways should therefore be distinguished from reported personality-related associations and from the hypothetical cross-system links proposed in this review. This Mini Review examines current evidence linking personality characteristics with autonomic and neuroendocrine regulation, the brain-gut axis, the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, sexual function, and fertility. Rather than proposing that internal organs possess personalities, we propose that shared neurobiological and neuroendocrine mechanisms may produce parallel functional response patterns that reflect an individual's personality characteristics. Finally, we propose that integrating these previously studied relationships within a Brain-Gut-Gonadal framework may provide a new perspective on the possible links between personality traits, sexual function, reproductive physiology, and unexplained infertility. This perspective does not imply that personality traits cause infertility, but raises the novel and testable possibility that personality-related biological differences may contribute to individual variation in reproductive physiology and fertility.

articles.title: Policy-practice gaps and bottlenecks to postpartum family planning scale-up in the United Republic of Tanzania.
articles.authors: Kafaiya CB, Kilima SP, Mayige MT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unintended and closely spaced births remain important public health concerns. Postpartum family planning provides an opportunity to prevent unintended pregnancies and improve maternal and child health outcomes. However, evidence on the implementation bottlenecks affecting PPFP scale-up in Tanzania remains limited.
AIM: This study assessed implementation bottlenecks affecting the uptake, scale-up and sustainability of PPFP services in Tanzania and identified and prioritized potential actions to address them.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study employing a participatory mixed-methods approach was conducted using an adapted WHO PPFP bottleneck assessment tool, stakeholder survey, in-depth interviews, routine health information and population-based survey data, and review of national policies and guidelines. The online stakeholder survey included 477 invited participants, of whom 424 responded (88.9%). In-depth interviews were conducted with 34 stakeholders from regions representing high and low PPFP uptake. Findings from the different data sources were triangulated and presented during a stakeholder consensus meeting, where bottlenecks were ranked and prioritized and corresponding actions were identified.
RESULTS: Routine and survey data indicated substantial variation in PPFP uptake and an increase in postpartum FP counselling over time, but counselling did not consistently translate into PPFP uptake. The assessment identified gaps in provider capacity, motivation, financing, access to and awareness of updated policies and guidelines, referral systems, equitable access, and the scale-up of innovations. Policy reviews further identified gaps between national guidance and implementation, including limitations in dissemination, monitoring, and alignment with WHO recommendations. The consensus process prioritized actions addressing provider motivation, financing, dissemination of updated guidance and job aids, referral systems, equitable access, innovation scale-up, and provider capacity.
CONCLUSION: Tanzania has a supportive policy environment for PPFP, but implementation remains constrained by interconnected health-system, provider, and service-delivery barriers. Addressing these bottlenecks through coordinated investments in financing, provider capacity and motivation, guideline dissemination, referral systems, equitable access, and scale-up of effective innovations is essential to strengthen PPFP implementation and uptake.

articles.title: A model for prediction of a twin live birth following in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer in women of advanced age.
articles.authors: Xu S, Wang R, Zhang C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to construct a model for prediction of the probability of a twin live birth in women of advanced age in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer cycles.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 10,089 transfer cycles from women aged ≥35 years, stratified by whether they had a live twin birth. Taking a twin live birth as the positive outcome (Y = 1) and cycles with a singleton or no live birth as the negative outcome (Y = 0). A multivariate logistic regression analyses was built based on candidate variables, followed by nomogram construction. The discrimination ability of the model was assessed by the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve, with 500 bootstrap resamples for internal validation.
RESULTS: There were significant differences in age, endometrial thickness, number of usable embryos, number of embryos transferred, and embryo type between the groups (all P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified the following five predictors of a twin live birth: age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.69, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66-0.73, P < 0.001), endometrial thickness ≥7 mm (aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.30-5.99, P = 0.009), blastocyst transfer (aOR 1.88, 95% CI 1.36-2.60, P < 0.001), two good quality embryos (aOR 2.20, 95% CI 1.71-2.82, P < 0.001), and two embryos transferred (aOR 19.45, 95% CI 11.57-32.69, P < 0.001). The nomogram built on these variables yielded an area under the curve of 0.8462. Bootstrap internal validation (500 resamples) produced a corrected area under the curve of 0.8443.
CONCLUSIONS: The likelihood of a twin live birth correlated positively with two embryos transferred, two good quality embryos, blastocyst transfer, and endometrial thickness ≥7 mm, and correlated negatively with maternal age.

articles.title: ConvNeXt-KAN: a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network head for robust multi-class staging of Alzheimer's disease from brain MRI.
articles.authors: Islam K, Hossen B, Manjar MTA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which accurate, stage-wise classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can support earlier intervention. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) dominate this task, but their classifier heads rely on fixed activation functions and linear weights, which constrain the modelling of the subtle, highly non-linear atrophy and texture patterns that separate dementia stages. In addition, the widely used Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS) collection is severely imbalanced, and two common practices-undersampling every class to the smallest one, and splitting at the image (slice) level-respectively discard most of the data and inflate reported accuracy.
METHODS: We propose ConvNeXt-KAN, a hybrid model that couples a transfer-learned ConvNeXt-Tiny feature extractor with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) classification head whose edges are learnable spline activations implemented efficiently with Gaussian radial basis functions. The model is trained with a robustness-oriented recipe (MixUp and CutMix, label smoothing, decoupled weight decay, a cosine learning-rate schedule with warm-up, and test-time augmentation) and a data strategy that caps abundant classes and oversamples only the training partition, while evaluating on a fixed, balanced, leakage-controlled test set.
RESULTS: On the held-out test set the model attains 94.5% accuracy, a macro-averaged F1 of 0.944, and a mean one-vs.-rest ROC-AUC of 0.991, with an ablation confirming that pre-trained features and expanded data are the main drivers of performance. A head-to-head comparison under a matched protocol shows that the KAN and MLP heads are statistically indistinguishable (McNemar p = 0.52), while the proposed image-space resampling strategy outperforms focal loss, class-balanced cross-entropy and feature-space SMOTE. Evaluated without any fine-tuning on an independent four-class Alzheimer's MRI collection distributed on Kaggle, test-time-augmented accuracy is 61.6% with a macro-averaged F1 of 0.565.
DISCUSSION: The learnable-activation head improves the discrimination of the difficult non-demented vs. very-mild-demented boundary at negligible runtime cost, and the efficient formulation keeps the approach practical in standard deep-learning frameworks. A class-wise analysis of the external evaluation shows that moderate dementia continues to be recognized perfectly while the two clinically…

articles.title: Detection of prespecified CE-associated pathogen targets by quantitative polymerase chain reaction is associated with CD138-positive endometrium: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Nishii S, Iwami N, Kamiya H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We examined whether endometrial quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) detection of DNA from prespecified pathogen targets classically implicated in chronic endometritis (CE), from other reproductive-tract bacterial targets, or from Lactobacillus is associated with CD138-defined CE, independent of incidental endometrial polyps.
METHODS: We included 126 infertile women who underwent concurrent CD138 immunostaining and endometrial qPCR and who had also undergone hysteroscopy. Women with antibiotic use within 1 month before sampling, Lactobacillus probiotic use, insufficient samples for CD138 assessment, or no hysteroscopy were excluded. Robustness was evaluated by two prespecified polyp-exclusion analyses, by exclusion of women with endometriosis or adenomyosis, and by multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: CD138-positive endometrium was detected in 57 of 126 women (45.2%). Detection of CE-associated pathogen targets was associated with CD138 positivity (odds ratio 8.01, 95% confidence interval 1.70-37.85, P = 0.003; exact conditional odds ratio 7.89, 1.61-76.56), with specificity 97.1%, positive predictive value 84.6%, and sensitivity 19.3%, but this rested on only 13 target-positive women, of whom 11 were CD138-positive, so the estimate is imprecise. Other reproductive-tract bacterial targets were not associated with CD138 positivity (odds ratio 0.55, 0.25-1.22, P = 0.171). Lactobacillus detection was not significantly associated with CD138 positivity (odds ratio 0.54, 0.27-1.11, P = 0.107), although several analyses were directionally consistent with lower reported Lactobacillus values in CD138-positive women; this was suggestive rather than confirmatory. Conversely, 80.7% (46/57) of CD138-positive women had no detectable pathogen target. After polyp exclusion, the association was maintained (odds ratios 17.44 and 18.79), whereas the other categories remained nonsignificant. The association persisted after exclusion of women with endometriosis or adenomyosis (odds ratio 8.32, 1.75-39.60) and in the parsimonious multivariable model (adjusted odds ratio 8.94, 1.85-43.24; Firth penalized adjusted odds ratio 7.40, 1.67-32.90).
DISCUSSION: Detection of prespecified CE-associated pathogen targets, but not detection of other reproductive-tract bacterial targets, was associated with CD138-positive CE, independent of incidental polyps; the Lactobacillus findings were suggestive but not confirmatory. Because the panel provides no…

articles.title: A mobile health-assisted cardiovascular follow-up after pregnancy complications (MumCare): protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Staff AC, Sugulle M, Noll J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A history of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and/or gestational diabetes is associated with increased risk of long-term maternal cardiovascular (CV) disease. Despite recommendations for preventive strategies, few women receive CV follow-up postpartum. We have developed a personalized digital mobile Health companion, the MumCare (Mum's cardiovascular health for life) application, aiming at improving control of modifiable risk factors for CV disease and to bridge hospital and community health services. This paper describes the protocol for a MumCare randomized controlled trial in Norway.
METHODS: Study participation is offered to women at Oslo University Hospital with a diagnosis of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and/or gestational diabetes. Following informed consent (either during pregnancy or within 4 weeks postpartum), a block randomization process assigns participants to one of two groups (access to the Mum Care app or not). The app provides educational material, allows women to track modifiable risk factors, and prompts feedback to registered blood pressures. It also prompts the women to book the nationally recommended follow-up at their general practitioner's at 3-4 and 12 months postpartum. The primary study objective is to assess the effect of MumCare application access on 1-year follow-up rate with a general practitioner. Secondary objectives are to assess group differences at 14 months postpartum regarding: 1) satisfaction with the postpartum mHealth-assisted technology, 2) self-management evaluation, general self-efficacy; and at 14-18 months: 3) modifiable risk factors for CV disease (including hypertension, dyslipidemia, blood sugar control, smoking, weight and physical activity), CV non-invasive hemodynamics and CV-related biomarkers.
DISCUSSION: This randomized controlled trial tests the effect of a mobile Health-assisted follow-up of modifiable risk factors after pregnancy complications associated with premature CV disease in women. A study limitation is a risk of underrepresentation of recently immigrated women due to the restricted language options offered in the app.
STUDY PROTOCOLS REGISTRATION: NCT05835596.

articles.title: Accuracy of CSF tap test and lumbar infusion test in predicting shunt response in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Aliyar A, Dash D, Fasano A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) presents with gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary incontinence. The cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CSF-TT) and lumbar infusion test (LIT) are commonly used to predict postoperative improvement after shunt surgery; however, their validity remains debated.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the sensitivity and specificity of CSF-TT and LIT. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023454502). Reporting followed the PRISMA-DTA guidelines, and the certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Of 1,955 studies, 15 were included, reporting on 721 CSF-TT and 393 LIT patients, with shunt surgery as the reference standard. Nine CSF-TT studies (n = 700) and five LIT studies (n = 368) contributed to the primary meta-analysis. Considerable heterogeneity existed in test protocols, timing of assessment, and outcome measures. Several studies were retrospective with a high risk of bias. The pooled estimates were derived from a limited number of heterogeneous studies. Using a bivariate random-effects model, pooled sensitivity and specificity of CSF-TT were 64.1% (95% CI 49.2-76.6%, I 2 81.3%) and 54.8% (95% CI 41.8-67.2%, I 2 59.7%), respectively. The certainty of evidence was very low for sensitivity due to bias, inconsistency, and imprecision, and low for poor specificity due to bias and inconsistency. LIT showed a pooled sensitivity of 77.5% (95% CI 70.2-83.4%, I 2 14.7%) and a specificity of 28.3% (95% CI 19.0-39.9%, I 2 4.6%), with moderate certainty for sensitivity and moderate certainty for poor specificity.
CONCLUSION: Both CSF-TT and LIT show poor specificity for predicting shunt responsiveness in iNPH, with low-certainty evidence for CSF-TT and moderate-certainty evidence for LIT. A positive result from either test should not be used in isolation to guide surgical decisions. Standardized prospective studies with clearly defined patient selection criteria and outcome measures are needed to establish the true diagnostic value of these tests.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023454502.

articles.title: Maternal and Fetal Outcomes of Pregnant Women With Sickle Cell Disease: A Single-Center Canadian Study.
articles.authors: Lam WMJ, Rydz N, Soliman N et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sickle cell disease (SCD) increases the risk of complications during pregnancy. This study describes antenatal care patterns and maternal and fetal outcomes in pregnant women with SCD in a Canadian setting.
METHODS: Women with SCD receiving antenatal/perinatal care through the Southern Alberta Rare Blood and Bleeding Disorders program (January 2010 to January 2025) were identified. Antenatal care, and maternal and fetal outcomes were assessed in periods before (2010-2019) and after (2020-2025) local multidisciplinary protocols for SCD pregnancy management were updated.
RESULTS: 21 women (32 pregnancies; 31 neonates) were included. Most pregnancies were followed by maternal-fetal medicine (81.3%), had regular fetal growth assessments (84.4%), and had high-dose folic acid (90.6%) and acetylsalicylic acid (56.3%) supplementation; all were implemented more frequently following protocol update. Vaso-occlusive crises occurred in 56.3% of pregnancies, infections requiring intravenous antibiotics occurred in 21.9%, preeclampsia occurred in 6.3%, and peripartum/postpartum hemorrhages occurred in 28.1%. Transfusions were required in 62.5% of pregnancies. There was one intensive care unit (ICU) admission and no maternal deaths. No neonates had fetal growth restriction and 16.1% required neonatal ICU admission. One stillbirth occurred at 23 weeks (mother had hyperhemolysis).
CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary pregnancy management of women with SCD may improve antenatal care and maternal and fetal outcomes.

articles.title: Development and validation of a simple clinical prediction model for post-stroke seizures in critically ill patients: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Yang X, Kang Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke seizures (PSS) are common in critically ill stroke patients, but ICU-specific risk prediction tools are lacking, and the independent impact of PSS on mortality remains controversial.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort included 6,586 adult stroke patients from 208 US ICUs in the Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Patients were randomly divided 7:3 into training and internal validation sets. The primary endpoint was coded in-hospital post-stroke seizures identified via diagnosis codes during the index hospitalization. Candidate predictors were screened using logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were, respectively, evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration slopes and calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to evaluate the association between PSS and in-hospital mortality and length of stay.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of coded in-hospital PSS was 7.5%. Head-to-head comparison identified SOFA as the best-performing routine ICU severity score for coded PSS prediction, outperforming GCS, OASIS and APACHE II. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified five independent clinical predictors for coded in-hospital PSS: younger age, elevated admission body temperature, pre-existing hypertension, lower mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, and lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score. The model achieved AUCs of 0.702 in the training set and 0.713 in the validation set, with stable performance across age, gender, and stroke subtype subgroups. A three-tier bedside risk stratification was derived, with observed coded PSS rates of 3.4, 6.8, and 16.2% for low-risk, intermediate-risk, and high-risk groups. After PSM, coded PSS was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR = 0.84, p = 0.295) or prolonged hospital stay (mean difference = -0.30 days, p = 0.167).
CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a simple prediction model for coded in-hospital PSS in critically ill stroke patients. Coded PSS itself was not independently associated with increased mortality. This model remains a research tool that has not undergone external validation and cannot yet guide real-world clinical monitoring or pharmacological intervention. These findings are applicable to clinically evident,…

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
articles.authors: Qian Z, Li G, Tang J
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 409) and a validation cohort (n = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS).
RESULTS: The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs…

articles.title: Associations among quality of life, depressive symptoms, body shape concerns, anthropometric characteristics, and diet quality in women with PMOS: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Irmak E, Sanlier N
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a prevalent endocrine disorder associated with impaired quality of life, body image dissatisfaction, and psychological distress. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between quality of life, depression, body shape concern, and diet quality among women with PMOS.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted between July and December 2022 at a training and research hospital in Ankara, Türkiye, and included 247 women aged 19-40 years diagnosed with PMOS according to the Rotterdam criteria (2003). Participants were assessed using anthropometric measurements, Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Questionnaire (PCOSQ-50), Body Shape Questionnaire (BSQ-34), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Healthy Eating Index (HEI-2010), Carbohydrate Quality Index (CQI), and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII). Group comparisons, correlation analyses, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed to examine associations among the study variables.
RESULTS: Participants with minimal depressive symptoms reported significantly higher quality of life scores compared to those with mild or moderate-to-severe depression (p < 0.001). Higher BMI was associated with greater body shape concern (p < 0.001), and greater body shape concern was associated with lower PCOSQ-50 scores (p < 0.001). Significant negative correlations were observed between PCOSQ-50 scores and BSQ-34, BDI, and BMI (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate significant associations among quality of life, depressive symptoms, body shape concerns, and BMI in women with PMOS and underscore the importance of considering psychosocial and anthropometric factors alongside dietary characteristics in the comprehensive assessment of women with PMOS.

articles.title: Modulation of immune and inflammatory responses involving selected galectins and selected immune-inflammatory mediators in women with deep endometriosis coexisting with adenomyosis - preliminary study.
articles.authors: Wendlocha D, Smycz-Kubańska M, Kościelniak-Ziemniak M et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endometriosis is characterized by the presence of functionally active endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity, primarily within the peritoneal cavity. Its etiology and pathogenesis remain incompletely understood; however, endometriosis is considered a chronic inflammatory disease associated with immune system dysfunction. Galectins and other mediators of immune and inflammatory responses may play an important role in the pathogenesis of the disease. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of selected immune and inflammatory mediators in endometriosis by assessing the concentrations of galectin-1 (Gal-1), galectin-3 (Gal-3), galectin-8 (Gal-8), galectin-9 (Gal-9), asprosin, FSTL1, meteorin, neuregulin-4, isthmin 1, SFRP2, and TNF-α in the serum and peritoneal fluid of women with deep infiltrating endometriosis, deep infiltrating endometriosis coexisting with adenomyosis, and adenomyosis.
METHODS: The study included 33 women in whom endometriosis was diagnosed during laparoscopy and subsequently confirmed by histopathological examination. The reference group consisted of 14 women without endometriosis. Blood serum and peritoneal fluid samples were collected, and the concentrations of the investigated parameters were determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs).
RESULTS: In patients with deep infiltrating endometriosis coexisting with adenomyosis, alterations in the detectability of Gal-1, Gal-3, and Gal-9 were observed, suggesting a potential involvement of these galectins in the regulation of immune and inflammatory responses.
