Differences in the concentrations of asprosin, FSTL1, and TNF-α were also observed in this group, suggesting a possible association of these parameters with the inflammatory environment accompanying the disease.
CONCLUSIONS: The observed alterations in Gal-1, Gal-3, and Gal-9 levels in patients with deep infiltrating endometriosis coexisting with adenomyosis may indicate their involvement in the regulation of immune and inflammatory responses. Differences in the concentrations of asprosin, FSTL1, and TNF-α suggest their potential association with the inflammatory environment of the disease. Further studies in larger cohorts are needed to determine the biological and clinical significance of these parameters and their potential interactions.

articles.title: N-acetylcysteine ameliorates oxidative stress-induced decline in sex hormone-binding globulin in HepG2 cells and polycystic ovary syndrome rats.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Wang Q, Li S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) levels are a significant indicator of hyperandrogenism severity in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and are associated with an increased risk of reproductive and metabolic diseases. Oxidative stress suppresses the production and secretion of SHBG. However, the effect of the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) on hepatic SHBG expression remains unknown. This study investigated the effects of NAC on SHBG expression and the underlying mechanism in HepG2 cells and a rat model of PCOS.
METHODS: HepG2 cells were treated with testosterone propionate (TP), oxidized high-density lipoprotein (ox-HDL), oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL), and NAC. Female Sprague-Dawley rats aged 28 days were randomly allocated to eight groups: control, PCOS, and control and PCOS groups treated with NAC at 100, 200, or 400 mg/kg body weight. The PCOS rat model, induced by TP and a high-fat, high-sugar diet, was treated with different doses of NAC for 8 weeks. The expression of SHBG, hepatocyte nuclear factor 4α (HNF4α), chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter-transcription factor 1 (COUP-TF1), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) was assessed in HepG2 cells and rat liver tissue. Metabolic, hormonal, and oxidative stress indices were analyzed in the rat model.
RESULTS: In HepG2 cells, TP and oxidized lipoprotein treatments significantly suppressed SHBG and HNF4α expression, while NAC treatment reversed the inhibitory effects induced by ox-HDL and ox-LDL (P < 0.05). In PCOS rats, NAC intervention increased the mRNA and protein levels of SHBG by upregulating HNF4α and downregulating COUP-TF1 and PPAR-γ expression in the liver; increased serum SHBG; reduced hepatocytic reactive oxygen species levels (P < 0.05); and ameliorated obesity, estrous cycle abnormalities, hepatic steatosis, circulating sex hormone levels, and the lipid profile, with 200 mg/kg NAC showing the most favorable overall pattern among the three doses tested.
CONCLUSION: NAC treatment ameliorates oxidative stress-induced decreases in SHBG and HNF4α expression in HepG2 cells and may restore hepatocytic SHBG production by upregulating HNF4α and downregulating COUP-TF1/PPAR-γ expression in rats with PCOS.

articles.title: Beyond a single ratio: an adaptable deep learning approach to analyze the prognostic value of TSP distribution in ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Firmbach D, Kuritcyn P, Benz M et al.
articles.abstract: The tumor-stroma percentage (TSP) has been proposed as a prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. When assessed manually by pathologists, the TSP can be subject to significant inter-rater variability. Automated methods for TSP determination have recently been developed. Existing approaches typically yield a single TSP value for a relatively small region of interest in the slide, introducing bias through region selection and potentially overlooking the TSP distribution across the entire histologically examined area. We present an adaptable deep learning pipeline, efficiently fine-tuned for ovarian cancer tissue analysis using a few-shot learning approach, requiring only minimal new training annotations. Instead of calculating a single TSP value, our method quantifies the global TSP distribution across the entire tumor and therefore captures its spatial heterogeneity. To identify a prognostic biomarker, we systematically evaluated a panel of metrics describing this distribution in 98 patients. Our analysis revealed that the mean-median difference of the TSP distribution [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.46-0.79, p < 0.001], a quantitative measure of asymmetry, together with the mean TSP (HR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.43-0.97, p = 0.03), are biomarkers significantly associated with recurrence-free survival. By successfully adapting a pipeline for ovarian cancer, we demonstrate that automated analysis of the entire TSP distribution provides significant prognostic information superior to that obtained by manual assessment. Spatial heterogeneity of the TSP is a key prognostic factor. © 2026 Fraunhofer IIS and The Author(s). The Journal of Pathology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

articles.title: Focused ultrasound versus LEEP for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions: a retrospective cohort study of long-term effectiveness and obstetric outcomes.
articles.journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
articles.authors: Zhang M, Long F, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To compare long-term effectiveness and obstetric outcomes of focused ultrasound (FU) ablation versus loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) in reproductive-aged women.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included women treated with FU (n = 29) or LEEP (n = 32) for HSIL who subsequently delivered (2017-2023). A control group (n = 61) comprised healthy women with negative preconception HR-HPV/cytology. Outcomes were cumulative HR-HPV clearance, cervical length, pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: Both FU and LEEP demonstrated comparable long-term effectiveness: cumulative HR-HPV clearance rates did not differ significantly at any time point (p > 0.05). Post-intervention cervical length was significantly shorter in the LEEP group (24.79 ± 3.98 mm) than in both the FU (27.63 ± 2.80 mm) and control (28.26 ± 3.92 mm) groups (p = 0.003). Cervical insufficiency was more frequent in the LEEP group (15.63%) than in the FU (3.45%) and control (1.64%) groups (p = 0.019). The LEEP group also had higher rates of preterm birth (18.75% vs 3.45% in FU and 4.92% in controls; p = 0.039) and lower rates of vaginal delivery (15.63% vs 44.83% in FU; p = 0.025).
CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort of women with successful live births, FU may have comparable long-term effectiveness to LEEP for HSIL while potentially preserving cervical length and reducing adverse obstetric risks. These preliminary findings suggest FU may be a fertility-sparing option for appropriately selected HSIL women who are planning pregnancy.

articles.title: Impact of Reactive Temperament on Bull Fertility in Natural Service.
articles.authors: de Almeida Martin L, da Silva MKF, Sant'Ana Borges M et al.
articles.abstract: The study aimed to evaluate the influence of temperament on semen quality and fertility in Nelore bulls. Two groups were selected based on ethological analysis, consisting of animals with either calm temperament (CA, n = 8) or reactive temperament (RE, n = 8). All bulls underwent two semen collections for sperm evaluation (pre- and post-thawing), as well as serial blood collections for testosterone and cortisol measurements. Ejaculates recovered from the three most reactive and the three least reactive bulls were pooled to form two semen batches, which were subsequently cryopreserved and used for fixed-time artificial insemination (FTAI) to evaluate the fertility of semen from bulls with the two different temperament profiles. Additionally, each bull was housed in individual paddocks with cyclic cows (average of 20 cows per bull) for 90 days for a natural service capacity test. No differences were observed in sperm kinetic parameters, morphology and plasma membrane integrity for fresh or post-thaw semen when comparing the two experimental groups. Likewise, no effect of reactivity was observed on the fertility of calm and reactive bull semen in FTAI (p > 0.05). CA bulls showed lower average cortisol concentrations compared to the RE group during the second experimental routine, but there were no differences in testosterone values. CA bulls achieved higher conception rates in natural service (84.56%) compared to reactive animals (76.41%; p < 0.0001). In conclusion, no significant effects of temperament on fresh or post-thaw semen quality parameters were detected in Nelore bulls under the conditions of this study. However, bulls with a calmer temperament exhibited higher reproductive performance in natural service programs, supporting the hypothesis that behavioural mating efficiency rather than intrinsic gametic failure influences pasture breeding success.

articles.title: Targeting G2/M checkpoint vulnerability in homologous recombination-proficient tumors: lessons from ovarian cancer models.
articles.authors: Xi Q, Kunita A, Nagai S et al.
articles.abstract: Cell cycle dysregulation is a hallmark of cancer; however, tumors retaining homologous recombination (HR)-proficiency remain a major challenge. Although PARP inhibitors effectively target HR-deficient cancers, targeted therapies for BRCA1/2-wild-type, HR-proficient tumors are limited. High-grade serous ovarian cancer, approximately half of which is HR-proficient, illustrates that HR proficiency, together with replication stress and checkpoint dependence, may represent both a mechanism of therapeutic resistance and a druggable dependency on checkpoint-coupled DNA repair. This review synthesizes evidence that targeting either PLK1 or WEE1 independently exposes this vulnerability. PLK1 and WEE1 inhibition engage distinct mechanisms: PLK1 inhibition disrupts spindle assembly and HR competence, whereas WEE1 inhibition amplifies replication stress and forces premature mitotic entry. Nevertheless, both ultimately converge to compromise HR-associated repair, promote unresolved DNA damage, and trigger lethal mitotic catastrophe. Finally, we discuss biomarker-unselected trial failures, functional and replication stress-based patient stratification, and rational combinations with DNA-damaging agents and immunotherapy.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic changes and seizure outcomes in pregnant women taking second-generation antiseizure medications.
articles.authors: Hao N, Yi X, Zhao R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective seizure management in pregnant women with epilepsy poses significant clinical challenges. This study aimed to investigate the pharmacokinetic changes of second-generation antiseizure medications (ASMs) and their association with the deterioration of seizure control in Han Chinese women with epilepsy.
METHODS: Patient clinical data including oral daily doses and seizure frequency were acquired from routine clinical practice. Blood concentrations of ASMs determined by therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) were used to calculate apparent oral clearance (CL) at preconception and each trimester during pregnancy. The ratio of ASM concentration in each trimester to the preconception baseline concentration (RTC) was compared between patients experiencing seizure deterioration and those maintaining stability. Moreover, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to identify the threshold RTC value predicting increased seizure frequency.
RESULTS: A total of 52 pregnant patients with epilepsy were initially enrolled in this study. The apparent oral clearance of levetiracetam (LEV) and lamotrigine (LTG) showed a significant increase across all trimesters compared to the nonpregnant baseline. Peak clearance occurred in the third trimester for LTG with a 2.0-fold relative clearance (P < 0.05). Similarly, LEV displayed maximum apparent oral clearance increase during the third trimester, reaching 1.6 folds of baseline value (P < 0.05). As a result, serum concentrations of LEV and LTG significantly decreased during pregnancy compared to non-pregnant baseline levels (P < 0.05). However, the apparent oral clearance and the blood level of oxcarbazepine (OXC) remained stable throughout gestation compared to the preconception baseline. Moreover, the RTC values significantly differed between participants with and without seizure deterioration for all three ASMs, indicating that lower RTCs were associated with seizure worsening.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study revealed significant pharmacokinetic fluctuations of LEV and LTG in Chinese pregnant women. This highlights the necessity of early therapeutic drug monitoring for newer ASMs and dose adjustments to maintain blood concentrations near the non-pregnant baseline level in pregnant women with epilepsy.

articles.title: BMP4 as a Potential Molecular Link between Obesity and Female Fertility.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Zhang J, Chen G et al.
articles.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) is a member of the transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) superfamily. Accumulating evidence indicates that BMP4 is widely expressed in female reproductive tissues, including the ovary and endometrium. Therefore, this review summarizes the roles of BMP4 in regulating the physiological functions of the ovary and endometrium, including folliculogenesis, ovarian steroidogenesis, endometrial decidualization and regulation of maternal-foetal immunity. Notably, increasing studies revealed that BMP4 is also critically involved in obesity. Given the continuously rising prevalence of obesity worldwide, this review further summarizes emerging evidence on the role of BMP4 in adipogenesis, the shift between white adipose tissue (WAT) and brown adipose tissue (BAT) and metabolic dysregulation. To further elucidate the role of BMP4, we also summarize the expression patterns and potential mechanisms in reproductive disorders and obesity. We found that dysregulated BMP4 expression has been reported in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) and obesity, suggesting a potential molecular link between obesity and female fertility. Hence, the potential role of BMP4 between obesity and women's fertility is further discussed and may provide direction for further reproductive-related research. This hypothesis may guide further studies to explore the underlying mechanisms and their translational implications.

articles.title: Health-promoting behaviors in perimenopausal women based on the COM-B model: a latent profile analysis.
articles.authors: Fu Y, Jin L, Zhou Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perimenopause is a critical transitional stage in women's lives and is characterized by substantial physiological and psychological changes that may influence health behaviors and long-term health outcomes. Health-promoting behaviors play an important role in preventing chronic diseases and improving quality of life among perimenopausal women. However, these behaviors may vary considerably across individuals, and the psychosocial factors underlying different behavioral patterns remain unclear. Guided by the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviors (COM-B) model, this study aimed to identify latent profiles of health-promoting behaviors among perimenopausal women and to examine their associated factors.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 500 women aged 40-55 years who were recruited by convenience sampling from the gynecology outpatient clinic of Dongguan Maternal and Child Health Hospital, China. Perimenopausal status was determined by a gynecologist with reference to STRAW + 10 menstrual criteria, defined as a persistent difference of at least 7 days in consecutive cycle lengths or an amenorrhea interval of at least 60 days but less than 12 months. Health-promoting behavior was assessed using the revised Chinese Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II. Latent profile analysis was conducted using six dimension scores. Theory-informed ordinal logistic regression examined associations of eHealth literacy, Family APGAR score, general self-efficacy, and prespecified covariates with profile level; a sensitivity model additionally adjusted for self-rated health, sleep quality, and body mass index category.
RESULTS: Three ordered profiles of health-promoting behavior were identified: low-level (32.8%), moderate-level (46.4%), and high-level (20.8%). Their broadly parallel patterns across the six HPLP-II-R dimensions indicated primarily graded differences in overall health-promoting behavior. Higher eHealth literacy (OR = 1.266, 95% CI: 1.198-1.338), Family APGAR scores (OR = 1.137, 95% CI: 1.041-1.242), and general self-efficacy (OR = 1.125, 95% CI: 1.081-1.170) were associated with greater odds of membership in a higher-level profile.
CONCLUSIONS: Health-promoting behaviors among perimenopausal women show substantial heterogeneity. Higher eHealth literacy, Family APGAR scores, and general self-efficacy-reflecting selected aspects of psychological capability, social opportunity, and reflective motivation within the COM-B framework-were…

articles.title: Male partners' roles in women's contraceptive decision-making in Nigeria: a secondary qualitative data analysis.
articles.authors: Nmadu AG, Challa S, Okoli C et al.
articles.abstract: Male partners can play important roles in contraceptive decisions, especially in patriarchal societies like Nigeria, where restrictive gender norms influence women's reproductive choices. However, little has been explored about how women navigate male influences and its impact on reproductive autonomy. This study explores how Nigerian women perceive and navigate male partner influence in contraceptive decision-making. We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis of in-depth interviews with 60 women aged 15-45 from Enugu and Plateau States using data from the Innovations for Choice and Autonomy (ICAN) project and conducted in Nigeria as part of a multi-country study. Thematic analysis, guided by a pre-existing codebook examined decision-making, agency, and partner influence. Data were analysed using Dedoose software (version 9.0.62) with emergent themes refined through collaborative coding, independent review and memo writing. The process of contraceptive decision making occurred through three stages. 'Before' decision-making, societal norms shaped women's perceptions, reinforcing men dominance as the heads of the home expected to make decisions. 'During' the decision-making process, women used strategies such as persuasion, joint decision-making or third-party involvement to align their partners' views with theirs. However, male partners often asserted significant influence by insisting that women comply with their preferences, constraining women's agency. In the 'after' stage, supportive partnerships emerged when couples communicated openly and shared their views. In relationships with dominant gender roles, women often complied with husbands' preferences, and in some cases resorted to covert contraceptive use to avoid conflict. The process of contraceptive decision-making among Nigerian women is influenced by normative beliefs, negotiation strategies, and women's agency. While male dominance often constrains autonomy, some women navigate these barriers through persuasion, negotiation, or covert use to exercise reproductive autonomy. These findings highlight the need for gender-sensitive approaches that promote open dialogue, couple-based education and policies that support women's autonomy while fostering collaborative decision-making.

articles.title: Quercetin attenuates maternal respiratory virus-induced fetal neuroimmune dysregulation.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Xi S, Shi G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal respiratory viral infections during pregnancy are epidemiologically linked to increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in offspring, yet the causal immunological mechanisms that disrupt fetal neuroimmune homeostasis remain unclear.
METHODS: A murine pregnancy influenza model was established by intranasal inoculation of a sublethal dose of H1N1 (PR8) at embryonic day 9.5. Maternal immune modulation was performed using natural killer (NK) cell depletion and genetic deletion of granzyme B (Gzmb) in maternal NK cells, as well as quercetin administration during defined gestational windows. Fetal neuroimmune outcomes were assessed by immunostaining and quantitative analysis of macrophage activation in fetal brain barrier regions, complemented by single-cell RNA sequencing of fetal brain CD11b⁺ myeloid populations. Offspring behavioral phenotypes were evaluated in adulthood, and decidual transcriptomic profiling was performed to characterize changes at the maternal-fetal interface. In parallel, human decidual NK cells were stimulated in vitro with interferon-β with or without quercetin to examine conserved immunoregulatory effects.
RESULTS: Maternal H1N1 infection induced robust maternal lung inflammation and was accompanied by fetal neuroimmune dysregulation characterized by increased Iba1⁺CD68⁺ macrophage accumulation in the fetal choroid plexus and meninges. Depletion of maternal NK cells significantly ameliorated these fetal neuroimmune abnormalities, implicating maternal NK cells as key mediators. Quercetin treatment mitigated fetal neuroinflammation and improved autism-like behaviors in offspring. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis showed that quercetin reversed interferon-stimulated gene programs and attenuated infection-induced expansion of proinflammatory fetal macrophage subsets. Mechanistically, quercetin reduced NK-derived granzyme B while enhancing decidual Serpina3n and broader pregnancy-supportive molecular programs, and alleviated infection-associated fetal growth restriction.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify maternal NK cell-derived granzyme B as a central driver of respiratory virus-induced fetal neuroimmune disturbance and support quercetin as a dual-action immunomodulatory candidate capable of mitigating maternal immune dysregulation and fetal neuroinflammation.

articles.title: Hormone replacement therapy through the lens of epigenetic clock: estrogen signals, glycemic status, and lifespan.
articles.authors: Wei H, Kong C, Gao B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) is a critical biomarker of aging. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is commonly used to alleviate age-related diseases, while glycemic status also influences the aging process. We aimed to investigate the association between estrogen and EAA, and the effects of HRT, EAA, and glycemic status on mortality.
METHODS: Mendelian randomization (MR) established causal relationships between genetically predicted estrogen receptor expression and EAA markers (HorvathAA, HannumAA, PhenoAA, and GrimAA). Using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, we employed Cox proportional hazards models to analyze the association between HRT and mortality, exploring whether it was modified by EAA and glycemic status.
RESULTS: Elevated estrogen receptor α (ESR1) expression significantly decelerated PhenoAA (β -1.26; 95% CI: -2.16, -0.37; P = 0.005). HRT significantly correlated with a reduced risk of all-cause (HR: 0.65, 95% CI: 0.47-0.88; P = 0.006) and cardiovascular (HR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.28-0.95; P = 0.033) mortality. Additionally, there was a significant three-way interaction among HRT, two types of EAA (HorvathAA and PhenoAA), and abnormal glucose status. Stratified analyses showed no significant interaction in the normal glucose subgroup; however, a significant antagonistic interaction emerged between HRT and both HorvathAA and PhenoAA in the abnormal glucose subgroup. Consequently, although HRT exhibited a protective main effect in patients with abnormal glucose, its survival benefits were significantly attenuated as their epigenetic aging accelerated.
CONCLUSIONS: Estrogen may decelerate PhenoAA via the ESR1 pathway. In postmenopausal women, HRT is significantly associated with a reduced risk of mortality; however, this survival benefit is substantially modified by glycemic status. Future studies should evaluate whether incorporating EAA and glycemic status into HRT decision-making could optimize clinical outcomes.

articles.title: A prospective cohort study on ultrasound simulation training in gynecology and obstetrics using pelvic, fetometry, and breast models.
articles.authors: Tüscher L, Weyers S, Arslan M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound is an essential diagnostic modality in modern medicine due to its wide availability, safety, and versatility. However, its diagnostic accuracy is highly dependent on operator proficiency. Despite growing recommendations from professional societies for early and structured ultrasound education, training often begins late and predominantly in clinical practice. Simulation-based ultrasound training offers a safe and standardized learning environment, particularly for intimate examinations in gynecology and obstetrics. This study aimed to evaluate the educational effectiveness of a mandatory ultrasound simulation training integrated into an undergraduate medical curriculum.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, n = 143 fifth-year medical students enrolled in a mandatory obstetrics and gynecology module were allocated via a quasi-randomized approach to an intervention group or a waitlist-control group. The intervention consisted of three 20-min ultrasound simulation sessions using high-fidelity models for transvaginal sonography, fetometry, and breast ultrasound. Knowledge acquisition and self-efficacy were assessed using study-specific, pilot-tested pre- and post-intervention questionnaires. Group-level statistical analyses were performed to evaluate learning outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 126 students completed the post-test (waitlist-control group n = 55; intervention group n = 71). Baseline characteristics and pre-test knowledge scores did not differ significantly between groups. After the intervention, the intervention group demonstrated a significantly greater increase in ultrasound knowledge compared to the waitlist-control group (p = .005). Participants reported high satisfaction with the training and increased self-confidence in ultrasound application. The majority (87%) expressed a desire for extended training duration.
CONCLUSIONS: Mandatory ultrasound simulation training significantly improves undergraduate medical students' ultrasound knowledge and self-confidence, even after short training interventions. These real-life evaluation data support simulation-based ultrasound education as an effective and feasible component of competency-based medical curricula.

articles.title: Effect of mobile health application interventions on modern contraceptive use among women of reproductive age in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Adjei KK, Ganle J, Boadu I et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sustainable Development Goal 3, target seven, aims to ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health care services, including family planning information and education. Mobile health interventions may be an effective means to achieve this target. Mobile health (mhealth) involves the use of mobile phone applications (MPAs) and text messages (SMS) on devices such as cell phones to provide relevant information to improve well-being and health. Given the growing interest in the use of mobile health to improve healthcare delivery, especially in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), up-to-date information must be available to guide practice.
OBJECTIVES: To provide up-to-date evidence on the effectiveness of mhealth interventions in enhancing contraceptive use among women of reproductive age in SSA.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of the literature in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis guidelines. The review was guided by a protocol registered in PROSPERO and aimed to provide up-to-date evidence on the effectiveness of mhealth interventions in enhancing contraceptive use. The PICO framework guided the literature search, and the review was conducted with an information specialist. The literature search covered studies published from 1994 to 2022 in the following databases: Medline, CINAHL, PubMed CENTRAL, the Cochrane Library, and EMBASE. Two independent reviewers conducted the screening in three stages. The title, abstract, and full-text were screened to identify studies that met the inclusion criteria. Data were extracted using a standardised data extraction form, synthesised, and assessed for quality. The quality of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) was evaluated using the JBI critical appraisal tool for RCTs. The JBI critical appraisal tool for cross-sectional studies was used to assess the non-randomised studies. A meta-analysis was conducted for studies that met the meta-analysis criteria.
RESULTS: A total of 9,768 records were retrieved following the searches. Eight (8) studies were included in the final review: 6 RCTs, and 2 cross-sectional studies. A positive effect of mhealth on modern contraceptive use was reported in 4 out of the 8 studies, while the remaining 4 did not report any significant effect. A meta-analysis of data pooled from the 6 RCTs demonstrated a statistically significant effect of the intervention on contraceptive use (OR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.11-1.92), indicating…

articles.title: Brucella abortus RB51 vaccination: a comprehensive systematic review of safety, efficacy, and global field outcomes (1990-2025).
articles.authors: Dadar M, Arellano B, Gharekhani J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brucella abortus strain RB51 is a live attenuated rough vaccine developed to overcome the serological interference of conventional smooth vaccines. Since replacing strain S19 in the United States (1996) and globally thereafter, RB51 has been promoted as a DIVA (Differentiating Infected from Vaccinated Animals) vaccine for brucellosis control in cattle and other livestock. However, conflicting reports on its safety, efficacy, and adverse effects have generated ongoing debate.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. Six electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CAB Abstracts, Cochrane Library, SciELO) were searched from January 1990 to March 2025. Studies reporting original data on RB51 vaccination in animals or humans, including safety, efficacy, adverse events, or human health outcomes, were included. Due to extreme heterogeneity (I² > 94%), findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Ninety-four studies (189 individual trials, 8 host species, 25 countries) were included. Positive outcomes included DIVA capability (no serological interference in most experimental settings), consistent Th1-biased cell-mediated immunity (IFN-γ, CD4⁺/CD8⁺ T-cell responses), and efficacy against B. abortus challenge in controlled trials (up to 100% protection). However, substantial adverse effects were documented: abortion rates in cattle ranged from 0.5% to 50% (median 8.3%), with higher rates (6-88%) in bison and elk; placentitis, stillbirth, and premature birth were reported across multiple host species. Vaccine strain shedding in milk occurred in 1.8-6.1% of vaccinated cows and buffaloes (culture-confirmed median 4.0%). Diagnostic interference (atypical seropositivity on smooth-LPS tests) was observed under field conditions, particularly after revaccination. Efficacy limitations included failure to protect against B. melitensis, B. suis, and B. ovis, waning immunity (< 4 years), and no benefit from revaccination. Human health risks included occupational accidental exposures (USA, Brazil, Egypt) and raw milk-associated RB51 infections (USA), complicated by intrinsic rifampin resistance.
CONCLUSIONS: RB51 preserves DIVA capability and induces cell-mediated immunity under ideal conditions but carries significant risks, including vaccine-induced abortion, milk shedding, and incomplete cross-protection. Its safety and effectiveness are highly context-dependent, performing well in low-prevalence…

articles.title: The effect of pelvic floor muscle training on sexual function, depressive symptoms, and pelvic floor muscle performance in women with overactive bladder: a randomized controlled.
articles.authors: Yılmaz Aladağ F, Kızılkaya Beji N
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) improves urethral pressure, reduces detrusor muscle overactivity, and helps suppress the micturition reflex, thus contributing to symptom control. This study aimed to investigate the effects of pelvic floor muscle training on sexual function, depressive symptoms, and pelvic floor muscle performance in women with overactive bladder (OAB).
METHODS: This study was conducted with 64 women (32 women: intervention group, 32 women: control group) who applied to Erzurum City Hospital Urology Polyclinic between December 1, 2021 and December 1, 2024. The study data were collected by Personal Information Form, Urinary Diary Follow-up Form, Overactive Bladder Questionnaire (OAB-V8), Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), Sexual Quality of Life Scale-Woman (SQoL-F), Epidemiological Research Center Depression Scale (CES-D), Pelvic Floor Muscle Training Intervention Follow-up Form, Digital palpation (pelvic floor muscle strength measurement). In the intervention group, PFMT was performed for 6 weeks with biofeedback with the Simplex Device in accordance with the given PFMT intervention procedure.
RESULTS: Following the 6-week intervention, women receiving PFMT demonstrated significantly lower OAB symptom severity and depressive symptoms and significantly higher sexual function, sexual quality of life, pelvic floor muscle strength, contraction strength, and MVC% than women in the control group. They also showed significantly higher sexual quality of life, pelvic floor muscle contraction strength, maximum voluntary contraction (MVC%), and pelvic floor muscle strength (all p < 0.05). No significant between-group difference was observed in pelvic floor muscle relaxation values (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Women receiving PFMT demonstrated lower OAB symptom severity and depressive symptom scores and higher sexual quality of life and pelvic floor muscle performance measures. Because female sexual function (FSFI) was the predefined primary outcome, findings related to secondary outcomes should be interpreted as exploratory.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Trial Registration Number: NCT07030608 (ClinicalTrials.gov, May 30, 2025; retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Menopause and Alzheimer's disease: can hormone replacement therapy modify the risk? A narrative review.
articles.authors: Wang JY, Ansorge O
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) prevalence and lifetime risk are higher in women than men. This led to the hypothesis that menopause, with its associated changes in female hormone homoeostasis, may be an AD risk factor modifiable by hormone replacement therapy (HRT). However, HRT is not without its risks to women's health, and any recommendations must rest on sound evidence. Here, we critically review data concerning sex-specific epidemiological and biological parameters that may influence AD development. Recent epidemiological studies suggest that the age-adjusted incidence of AD is not higher in women than men. Whilst there is mechanistic experimental evidence that female sex hormones modulate the metabolism of β-amyloid and tau, the neuropathological hallmarks of AD, no clear conclusions can be drawn from studies conducted in humans. Exposure to HRT may modify the development of AD; however, data are weak and the influence of timing, duration, type of HRT, and ethnic, socioeconomic, educational and genomic factors such as APOE genotype, requires further clarification. Large prospective biobank studies in diverse populations, with long follow-up periods and application of biological consensus criteria for the diagnosis of AD provide opportunities to conclusively clarify the relationship between menopause, HRT therapy and risk for the development of AD. Based on current evidence, HRT cannot be recommended as a generic intervention for the reduction of AD risk in women. Any decision to take HRT must consider the individual circumstances and overall health of a woman.

articles.title: Expression and clinical significance of WBC, hs-CRP, and ROMA index, and tumor markers in endometriosis.
articles.authors: Li J, Wang K
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the expression and clinical significance of white blood cell (WBC) count, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) index, and tumor markers in patients with endometriosis.
METHODS: A total of 125 women with surgically and histologically confirmed endometriosis and 80 control women without clinical or ultrasonographic evidence of endometriosis were enrolled at the Affiliated Hospital of Putian University between August 2019 and March 2023. Fasting venous blood samples were collected preoperatively, prior to surgical intervention, to measure WBC, hs-CRP, CA125, HE4, and formula-derived ROMA index values. Statistical analyses included independent-sample t-tests and one-way ANOVA to compare biomarker levels between groups and across surgical procedures.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with endometriosis showed significantly elevated WBC, hs-CRP, CA125, HE4, and formula-derived premenopausal and postmenopausal ROMA index values (all p < 0.001). One-way ANOVA showed no significant differences in biomarker levels across surgical procedures. These findings suggest that inflammatory markers, tumor-associated biomarkers, and formula-derived ROMA values are elevated in patients with endometriosis; however, ROMA findings should be interpreted cautiously because menopausal status was not consistently available for patient-specific ROMA classification.
CONCLUSION: Elevated WBC count, hs-CRP, CA125, and formula-derived ROMA index values may reflect systemic inflammatory activation in endometriosis, while HE4 should be interpreted more cautiously as a nonspecific tumor-associated biomarker difference. Because menopausal status was not consistently available, ROMA findings should be interpreted as exploratory formula-derived values rather than patient-specific clinical ROMA classifications.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of initiating insulin versus metformin therapy for gestational diabetes mellitus in China: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Jiang L, Peng N, Xue M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While insulin is widely recommended as the first-line pharmacological therapy for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), the use of metformin is increasing in routine clinical practice. However, real-world evidence comparing their effectiveness and safety remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate glycemic control and adverse pregnancy outcomes between the insulin and the metformin initiation group in women with GDM in China.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from a provincial healthcare database in Eastern China. Women diagnosed with GDM between 2018 and 2025 were included. Patients were divided into the insulin initiation group and the metformin initiation group based on their first prescription. Propensity score overlap weighting (OW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Weighted linear and logistic regression models were used to assess glycemic outcomes, including the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level at the end of pregnancy, the change in HbA1c, and target achievement (HbA1c < 6.0%). Adverse pregnancy outcomes were evaluated using weighted Cox proportional hazards models with gestational age as the time scale.
RESULTS: Of the 7,397 women included, 6,922 (93.6%) initiated insulin and 475 (6.4%) initiated metformin therapy. After OW adjustment, no significant differences were found between the two groups in end-of-pregnancy HbA1c levels, HbA1c changes, or glycemic control rates. Compared with insulin initiation, metformin initiation was associated with significantly lower risks of cesarean delivery (HR: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.62-0.95; P = 0.017), premature rupture of membranes (HR: 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.93; P = 0.016), and macrosomia (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.40-0.93; P = 0.021). Risks for other adverse outcomes, including preterm birth and preeclampsia, were comparable. Sensitivity analyses, including per-protocol analysis, confirmed the robustness of these findings.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world Chinese cohort, the metformin initiation group achieved glycemic control similar to the insulin initiation group. In addition, the metformin initiation group had lower risks of cesarean delivery, premature rupture of membranes, and macrosomia. These findings suggest that metformin may be a viable and effective initial treatment option for selected women with GDM.

articles.title: Perception and coping with aging among middle-aged women: a qualitative study.
articles.authors: Lei Y, Li K, Zhuo H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Middle-aged women face distinct physiological, psychological, and social challenges during the transition from adulthood to later life. However, their perceptions of aging and the strategies they employ to cope with this process remain insufficiently understood. This qualitative study aimed to explore how middle-aged women perceive and respond to aging, with the goal of informing the development of future assessment instruments and targeted health interventions.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 middle-aged women aged 46-57 years in Changsha, Hunan Province, from April to June 2025. Participants represented diverse educational backgrounds, residential areas, and menopausal statuses. Thematic analysis was employed for data analysis, and the study adhered to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) checklist.
RESULTS: The perceptions and coping strategies of middle-aged women regarding aging were categorized into five themes, summarized as "1H4W": (1) H- "How am I aging": A three-dimensional experience of aging; (2) W1- "What does aging bring me": The dual impact of aging; (3) W2- "Why am I aging": Multidimensional attribution of aging; (4) W3- "What can I do": Dual trajectories of coping strategies and their perceived efficacy; (5) W4- "What prevents me from acting": Barriers to aging coping actions.
CONCLUSIONS: Middle-aged women experience complex and multifaceted perceptions of aging, encompassing physical, psychological, and social dimensions. Their perceptions reflect both threat and growth, and their attribution patterns influence their choices of coping behaviors. However, translating these perceptions into action faces significant barriers. These preliminary findings point toward the potential value of developing a validated tool to assess aging perceptions in middle-aged women, which may enhance self-awareness, promote proactive health behaviors, and support healthy aging.

articles.title: Prevalence of hepatitis B virus infection and associated factors among pregnant women attending antenatal care in public hospitals of the Eastern Zone of Tigray, Northern Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Gebretsadik A, Gebreegziabiher G
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global public health challenge, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where transmission occurs through exposure to infected blood and body fluids, sexual contact, and mother-to-child transmission. Chronic HBV infection can result in cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and premature mortality. Evidence on the prevalence of HBV infection and its associated factors among pregnant women in Ethiopia, particularly in the Eastern Zone of Tigray, remains limited. This study assessed the prevalence of HBV infection and associated factors among pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) services in public hospitals in the Eastern Zone of Tigray, Northern Ethiopia.
METHODS: An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 536 pregnant women attending antenatal care in four public hospitals in Eastern Tigray, Ethiopia, from January 1 to March 31, 2025. Hospitals and study participants were selected using simple random and systematic sampling techniques, respectively. Data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire. Hepatitis B virus infection status was determined using a single rapid hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) test (ABON™ Rapid Test), without ELISA or molecular (HBV DNA) confirmation. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 24. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with HBV infection. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: All 536 eligible pregnant women participated in the study, yielding a response rate of 100%. The mean age of participants was 27.9 ± 5.9 years (range: 16-48 years). The prevalence of HBV infection was 7.8%. Factors significantly associated with HBV infection were women aged ≥ 30 years (AOR = 2.72; 95% CI: 1.21-6.10), a history of multiple sexual partners (AOR = 16.12; 95% CI: 5.26-49.47), a history of hospital admission (AOR = 3.24; 95% CI: 1.92-15.32), and alcohol consumption (AOR = 5.42; 95% CI: 1.92-15.34).
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of HBV infection among pregnant women attending ANC services in public hospitals of the Eastern Zone of Tigray was 7.8%, indicating a high-intermediate level of endemicity. HBV infection remains a public health concern among pregnant women in the study area. Strengthening routine antenatal HBV screening and appropriate linkage to care and vaccination, enhancing infection prevention measures, and providing targeted…

articles.title: Serum neudesin is elevated in pregnancies complicated by pregestational type 2 diabetes: an exploratory cross-sectional controlled study : Neudesin in pregestational diabetes during pregnancy.
articles.authors: Köksal Z, Güçel F, Sarışen Ş
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neudesin has been linked to adipose tissue activity, glucose metabolism, and insulin resistance. Evidence on its behavior in diabetic pregnancies is limited, particularly in women with pregestational type 2 diabetes mellitus (PREGDM). This exploratory cross-sectional controlled study evaluated serum neudesin concentrations in pregnancies complicated by pregestational type 2 diabetes mellitus (PREGDM) or gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and in non-diabetic pregnant controls without major systemic disease, while examining the influence of gestational timing.
METHODS: This study included 90 pregnant women: 30 with PREGDM, 30 with GDM, and 30 non-diabetic controls without major systemic disease. Controls were recruited in two planned gestational-age strata, including early pregnancy and 24-28 weeks, to provide clinically relevant timing-aware comparisons. Serum neudesin concentrations were measured using a human neudesin enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit (BT LAB, catalogue no. E4258Hu) and reported as ng/mL. Overall group comparisons were supplemented by gestational-timing-aware analyses and exploratory multivariable log-neudesin regression.
RESULTS: Overall median serum neudesin was highest in the PREGDM group (5.67 [4.72-6.21] ng/mL), followed by the GDM group (2.80 [2.70-3.10] ng/mL) and controls (2.17 [1.77-2.89] ng/mL; p < 0.001). In gestational-timing-aware comparisons, PREGDM remained higher than early-pregnancy controls (5.67 [4.72-6.21] vs. 1.70 [1.37-2.15] ng/mL; Hodges-Lehmann difference, 3.70 ng/mL; 95% CI, 3.15-4.35; p < 0.001). In contrast, GDM did not differ from controls sampled at 24-28 weeks (2.80 [2.70-3.10] vs. 2.85 [2.28-3.03] ng/mL; Hodges-Lehmann difference, 0.04 ng/mL; 95% CI, - 0.20 to 0.40; p = 0.791). In the diabetic-only model adjusted for gestational age and age, the PREGDM-GDM contrast was attenuated (GMR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.61-2.85; p = 0.490). In the all-participant adjusted model, PREGDM remained associated with higher neudesin than controls (GMR, 3.11; 95% CI, 2.57-3.76; p < 0.001), whereas the GDM-control contrast was not significant (GMR, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.96-1.30; p = 0.149).
CONCLUSION: Serum neudesin was most consistently elevated in pregnancies complicated by PREGDM. The apparent overall GDM-control difference was not retained after timing-aware comparison or adjustment. Given the modest sample size, neudesin should be considered an exploratory complementary metabolic marker rather than a standalone…

articles.title: Sex-specific adverse neonatal outcomes and umbilical cord arterial ph at birth: a population-based cohort study.
articles.authors: Akel WN, Abdulilah S, Zaigham M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biological sex may influence neonatal vulnerability to adverse perinatal outcomes, but sex-related differences in these outcomes remain underexplored. Male neonates may be more susceptible to perinatal asphyxia, metabolic acidosis, preterm birth, and morbidity, possibly due to sex-specific placental differences and inflammatory responses. Umbilical cord arterial pH (UApH) < 7.05 is used in Sweden to define neonatal acidemia, associated with poor outcomes. This study aimed to investigate the association between neonatal sex and adverse outcomes, focusing on UApH.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study used data from the Swedish Perinatal Revision South Register (1995-2015). The cohort included live-born, singleton, vaginal births. Neonatal and maternal data were extracted, and logistic regression models compared outcomes between male and female neonates, adjusting for maternal age, gestational age, and birth weight.
RESULTS: Among 87 840 neonates, 51.6% were male. Male neonates had significantly higher adjusted odds of adverse outcomes compared with females: UApH < 7.05 (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.07-1.30; P < 0.001), Apgar score < 7 at 5 min (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.14-1.56; P < 0.001), CPAP use (OR 1.66, 95% CI 1.46-1.87; P < 0.001), NICU admission (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.43-1.60; P < 0.001), hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.29-3.90; P = 0.002) and central nervous system disease (OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.30-1.76; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Male neonatal sex was associated with several adverse perinatal outcomes, including acidemia and neurological complications. These findings contribute to the understanding of sex-related differences in neonatal vulnerability and warrant further investigation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Genetic and non-genetic contributions to early spontaneous miscarriage in women with PCOS undergoing PGT-A and single euploid blastocyst transfer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Bu Z, Ge X, Sun J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide an updated and comprehensive assessment of euploid embryo rates in polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) women compared with non-PCOS counterparts undergoing preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), and to evaluate early spontaneous miscarriage (ESM) rates across different PCOS phenotypes following single vitrified euploid blastocyst transfer cycles.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study (2017-2023) included women with PCOS and non-PCOS controls. Two cohorts were analyzed: first PGT-A cycles and first single vitrified euploid blastocyst transfers. ESM and euploidy rates were assessed, and regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with miscarriage.
RESULTS: In the PCOS group, a total of 1,274 blastocysts were biopsied, of which 580 were euploid, yielding a euploidy rate of 45.53% (580/1,274), which was significantly higher than the 39.86% (1,935/4,854) observed in non-PCOS women (P < 0.001). Additionally, 345 PCOS and 1,650 non-PCOS frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles involving the first single vitrified euploid blastocyst were included in the analysis. ESM rates were 14.48% (21/145) in the polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM)+ ovulation disorder (OD) subgroup, 18.75% (6/32) in the PCOM+ Hyperandrogenism (HA) subgroup, and 31.70% (13/41) in the PCOM + OD+HA subgroup. After adjusting for covariates, the PCOM + OD+HA phenotype remained an independent risk factor for ESM (adjusted OR: 2.164; 95% CI: 1.209-6.247; P = 0.036).
CONCLUSION: The high ESM rate observed in PCOS patients may be attributable to their endocrine abnormalities. These findings suggest that non-genetic, environmental factors-rather than genetic factors-warrant greater attention in future strategies aimed at reducing ESM in this population.

articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of postpartum anemia among women in Southeastern Iran: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Kashani ZA, Pirak A, Yazdkhasti M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postpartum anemia is a significant public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. In Iran, prevalence rates are higher in socioeconomically disadvantaged regions such as Iranshahr in Southeastern Iran, where nutritional deficiencies may further increase vulnerability. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of postpartum anemia and identify its associated factors in this underserved population.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study conducted from July to December 2023, 500 postpartum women were recruited from five comprehensive health service centers in Iranshahr, Iran, using proportional cluster sampling with systematic random sampling within each cluster. Socio-demographic, obstetric, and antenatal laboratory data were extracted from participants' medical records using a structured data extraction form. Postpartum hemoglobin was measured at the six-week postnatal visit using complete blood count (CBC). Postpartum anemia was defined as hemoglobin < 12 g/dL and classified as mild (11-11.9 g/dL), moderate (8-10.9 g/dL), and severe (< 8 g/dL). Anemia during pregnancy was defined as hemoglobin < 11 g/dL. Bivariate associations were assessed using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests, and independent predictors were identified using multivariable binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: The prevalence of postpartum anemia was 37.2% (95% CI: 33.0-41.4%), comprising 25.6% mild and 11.6% moderate cases; no severe anemia was identified. In multivariable logistic regression, anemia during pregnancy was the strongest independent predictor (AOR = 5.73; 95% CI: 3.81-8.61; p < 0.001), followed by postpartum hemorrhage (AOR = 2.41; 95% CI: 1.07-5.41; p = 0.033). Age, occupation, body mass index, economic status, educational level, and iron supplementation were not independently associated with postpartum anemia.
CONCLUSION: Postpartum anemia is common in this population, primarily predicted by anemia during pregnancy and postpartum hemorrhage. Routine hemoglobin screening from early pregnancy, education on correct iron supplement use, and regular postpartum monitoring are essential to reduce its burden in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Postoperative membranous urethral length and continence recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a Bayesian longitudinal meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Yadav S, Kairuz DN, Yadav A et al.
articles.abstract: Postoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-measured membranous urethral length (MUL) may reflect the functional urethral substrate preserved after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). We aimed to characterise how postoperative MUL influences the likelihood and timing of urinary continence recovery after RARP. This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261518338) searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL. Eligible cohort studies assessed postoperative MRI-measured MUL and urinary continence after RARP. Continence outcomes were synthesised using Bayesian longitudinal meta-regression. Time-specific continence probabilities, odds ratios per MUL increment, and modelled time to 50% continence probability were estimated. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using QUIPS and GRADE. Eight cohorts comprising 938 patients were included. At a reference postoperative MUL of 13.52 mm, modelled continence probabilities were 26.4%, 57.8%, 76.1%, and 88.1% at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively. Per-millimetre odds ratios for continence were 1.31 (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.04-1.67) at 1 month and 1.55 (1.21-2.03) at 12 months. Modelled time to 50% cohort-level continence probability was 2.32 months (95% CrI 1.12-4.71) at the reference MUL and a 1-mm increase was associated with a 22.3% (7.9-35.9%) shorter time.Excluding one influential study attenuated the association, with CrIs crossing 1. The overall certainty of evidence was rated as low. Longer postoperative MUL was associated with greater modelled continence probability and earlier modelled recovery. Prospective validation of the incremental predictive value of postoperative MUL beyond established predictors is required to justify routine postoperative MRI or guide individual prognostication.

articles.title: Revisiting menopausal hormone therapy for bone health: evidence, controversies, and clinical positioning in India in 2026.
articles.authors: Vaghasia N, Nagendra L, Kapoor N et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause is characterized by the rapid decline of estrogen exposure, resulting in accelerated bone loss superimposed on the gradual age-related decline in bone mass. This process is particularly relevant in India, where women experience menopause earlier than Western populations, thereby increasing lifetime fracture risk. Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) has been evaluated extensively over the years for skeletal health, with consistent evidence demonstrating preservation of bone mineral density and reduction in vertebral and hip fractures, especially when initiated early after menopause. Although multiple concerns arose following the Women's Health Initiative in terms of cardiovascular safety and breast cancer risk, leading to a decline in MHT use, subsequent analyses have supported a more favorable benefit-risk profile in appropriately selected younger postmenopausal women. Current evidence suggests that individualized MHT can also improve skeletal outcomes while benefiting menopausal symptoms and overall quality of life. This review revisits the evolving role of MHT in bone health in the Indian context.

articles.title: UNICAL: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Learning with MRI-Derived Synthetic Amyloid PET for Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.authors: Challapalli SSA, Bhattarai KM, Kamangar FA et al.
articles.abstract: Limited availability of amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) motivates imaging-informatics methods that derive complementary molecular-imaging representations from routinely acquired magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We developed UNICAL, an uncertainty-aware multimodal framework for Alzheimer's disease-spectrum versus cognitively normal classification that combines a self-supervised three-dimensional MRI encoder, Contourlet Wavelet Stationary Radiomics (CoWS-Rad) engineered MRI features, and MRI-derived synthetic 18F-florbetapir (AV45) PET. CoCoLIT generated four stochastic PET realizations per MRI; their mean and voxelwise variance were used for uncertainty gating before probability-anchored transformer fusion. Synthetic PET was validated in 228 paired OASIS-3 MRI-AV45 examinations, achieving a mean per-examination voxelwise Pearson correlation of r = 0.864 and strong cortical-composite SUVR agreement with acquired PET (Pearson r = 0.954). In the OASIS-3 development cohort (813 sessions from 811 participants), participant-grouped five-fold cross-validation repeated across 20 seeds yielded AUROC 0.868 and expected calibration error (ECE) 0.061. The OASIS-3 development endpoint used the manuscript's AD-spectrum reference standard, whereas ADNI3 used AD-versus-CN research-group labels, providing cross-dataset evaluation on a related but non-identical prediction endpoint. Without retraining, feature refitting, threshold optimization, or recalibration, the frozen framework was evaluated in an independent matched ADNI3 cohort of 261 participants (87 AD, 174 CN), achieving AUROC 0.836 (95% CI 0.791-0.876). ECE increased to 0.089 under external transfer, indicating that calibration was more sensitive to domain shift than rank discrimination. Ablation analysis and K-sample sensitivity supported the contributions of uncertainty gating, adaptive weighting, modality dropout, residual correction, and the K = 4 synthesis configuration. UNICAL therefore provides an uncertainty-aware MRI-derived multimodal representation for AD-spectrum classification that retains substantial cross-dataset discrimination while remaining distinct from acquired molecular imaging and not replacing amyloid PET as a clinical biomarker.

articles.title: Focal therapy vs radical prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer: a systematic review, meta-analysis, bayesian network, and trial sequential analysis.
articles.authors: Hinojosa-Gonzalez DE, Slawin B, Torres-Martinez M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer is a prevalent malignancy with procedural treatment strategies. These treatments are associated with significant quality of life impact, including erectile dysfunction and urinary incontinence. Focal therapy (FT) has emerged as an option that may minimize treatment-related side effects. Its efficacy in cancer control compared to standard strategies, such as radical prostatectomy (RP), remains controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis sought to compare the oncologic and functional outcomes of focal therapy versus radical prostatectomy (RP) for localized prostate cancer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive systematic search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Google Scholar in October 2025. The study followed PRISMA guidelines and included prospective and retrospective observational studies comparing RP with FT. Eleven studies met inclusion criteria providing a total of 8399 patients of which 4498 underwent RP and 3901 underwent FT. The coprimary endpoints were salvage treatment-free survival and failure-free survival, with secondary endpoints including continence, erectile function, and complication rate.
RESULTS: Oncologic outcomes revealed a statistically significant overall difference in salvage treatment-free survival and failure-free survival between FT and RP, with a HR of 2.05 (95% Cl 1.29-3.26, p=0.002) and 2.68 (95% CI 1.04-6.93, p=0.04), respectively. Differences in overall survival were not statistically significant HR 1.71 (95% CI 0.75-3.90, p = 0.20). Subgroup analyses showed varied results across different focal therapy approaches, with cryotherapy and combined approaches demonstrating higher treatment failure rates. Functional outcomes strongly favored FT, with significantly higher rates of continence and erectile function across all measured time intervals. At 12 months post-treatment, FT patients demonstrated substantially better continence (OR 3.45, p<0.00001) and erectile function preservation (OR 6.43, p<0.00001) compared to RP.
CONCLUSION: FT offers substantial quality of life benefits, particularly within the first 12 postoperative months, compared to RARP, however, at the cost of decreased oncologic treatment effectiveness. Differences in oncologic outcomes become attenuated in propensity-matched studies and trial sequential analysis yielded inconclusive results. Careful patient selection is paramount, and patients should be thoroughly counseled about potentially reduced…

articles.title: Minimal-volume single-mesh dual-cervico-vaginal wall fixation for abdominal sacrohysteropexy: preliminary outcomes of a novel technique with a standardized mesh configuration.
articles.authors: Çetinel B, Kalender G, Irmak F et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and effectiveness of a minimal-volume, single-mesh technique for dual-cervicovaginal wall fixation in abdominal sacrohysteropexy.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 38 patients who underwent abdominal sacrohysteropexy using a single specially designed mesh fixed to both the anterior and posterior cervico-vaginal walls and anchored to the sacral promontory were included and evaluated. Objective and subjective outcomes, as well as complications, were evaluated over a median follow-up of 17 months (range, 12-60).
RESULTS: The median age was 65 years (interquartile range, 58-72). Due to combined anterior-compartment defects and/or urodynamic stress urinary incontinence, bilateral paravaginal defect repair and anti-incontinence surgery (Burch colposuspension) were performed in 76.3% and 52.6% of patients, respectively. Among the 38 patients who completed at least 1 year of follow-up, no objective recurrence of apical prolapse and no other vaginal prolapse greater than Stage 1 were observed. Statistically significant improvements were found after surgery in some prolapse-related symptoms, such as bulge sensation or visualization, pelvic pressure, urinary frequency, sensation of incomplete bladder emptying, and urinary incontinence. All patients reported subjective improvement, with 30/38 (78.9%) reporting being "very much better," 7/38 (18.4%) "much better," and 1/38 (2.6%) "a little better". Postoperative complications were mostly minor. De novo stress urinary incontinence developed in two patients (5.2%); one was managed conservatively (2.6%) (Grade I), while the other required stress urinary incontinence surgery (2.6%) (Grade III). No cases of mesh erosion, mesh exposure, spondylodiscitis, sacral osteomyelitis, or middle sacral vein injury were observed during the perioperative or follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS: Dual-cervicovaginal wall fixation using a single minimal-volume mesh appears to be a safe and effective approach for abdominal sacrohysteropexy. This technique may reduce mesh burden without compromising clinical outcomes. Long-term follow-up findings and comparative studies with other techniques are needed.

articles.title: Latent Class Analysis Reveals Distinct Profiles Associated with Preeclampsia in Nulliparous Pregnancies.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.authors: Brown RE, Comeaux CR, Hill AV et al.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is a major cause of maternal illness and death, with poorly defined risk factors in nulliparous pregnancies. This study used latent class analysis to identify patterns of social, reproductive, health, and behavior factors associated with preeclampsia in 9809 nulliparous individuals who live in a large urban area in the Southeast US. Data were obtained from a perinatal administrative database (2011-2021). Latent indicators included maternal age, sociodemographic factors, foreign-born status, pregnancy intendedness, body mass index, mental and chronic health conditions, drug use, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Outcomes were gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia. Associations between latent classes and outcomes were examined with structural equation modeling. Of the pregnant patients, 49.1% were < 25 years old, 37.4% were foreign-born, 62.6% were married, 54.4% were on public insurance, 55.3% had unplanned pregnancies, 11.2% had mental health conditions, 5.4% had chronic health conditions, and 8.7% reported drug use. Three latent profiles emerged: Multidomain vulnerability (28%) included those more likely to be < 25 years of age with co-occurring social disadvantage, unplanned pregnancies, STIs, and drug use; social vulnerability (32%) included predominantly foreign-born patients with social disadvantage; health-behavior vulnerability (39%) included those with planned pregnancies and social advantage, but more health and behavior indicators relative to social vulnerability. Multidomain vulnerability (OR 2.0, 95% CI 1.67-2.46) and social vulnerability (OR 2.51, 95% CI 2.09-3.01) had higher odds of preeclampsia compared to the health-behavior vulnerability profile. Our latent class analysis revealed unique clustering of social, behavior, and health risk factors associated with preeclampsia among nulliparous pregnancies.

articles.title: Statins promote bone anabolism in estrogen deficiency by inducing osteogenic differentiation of skeletal stem/progenitor cells.
articles.authors: Yang M, Guo J, Ye J et al.
articles.abstract: Menopause-associated estrogen deficiency drives age-related bone loss in women. Statin use has been associated with higher bone mineral density in postmenopausal women, but whether menopause alters skeletal responses to statins remains unclear. Here, we show that statin use was associated with a slower annual decline in bone mineral density in postmenopausal women and that atorvastatin promotes bone anabolism specifically under estrogen-deficient conditions by inducing osteogenic differentiation of leptin receptor-expressing (LEPR+) bone marrow stromal cells, which include skeletal stem/progenitor cells. Atorvastatin increases osteoblast formation by restricting RAC1 prenylation and enabling nuclear factor kappa B-mediated Oln transcription. Estrogen acts on the same LEPR+ cells through estradiol-estrogen receptor-α signaling to promote Oln transcription. Thus, statins compensate for reduced estradiol-estrogen receptor-α signaling through a mechanistically distinct pathway. These findings reposition a major component of estrogen action to an earlier osteogenic stage and suggest broader implications for how statins influence stem/progenitor cell responsiveness beyond cholesterol management.

articles.title: Legal regulation of conscientious objection to abortion in Australia: qualitative study among key interest-holders.
articles.authors: Haining CM, Merner B, Willmott L et al.
articles.abstract: Conscientious objection (CO) provisions exist in abortion legislation in each Australian state and territory. These provisions embody a compromise approach to regulation-permitting conscientious objectors to opt out of abortion care they object to in certain circumstances, provided they fulfil prescribed obligations to facilitate abortion seekers' access to lawful abortion care. However, evidence suggests that, in practice, current regulatory approaches are not operating optimally or serving their policy goals. In this article, we report the findings from a qualitative study exploring the perspectives and experiences of 41 interest-holders about Australia's current approach to CO legal regulation in relation to abortion. Using framework analysis, we identified five themes: the desirability of protecting CO in Australian abortion law; boundaries placed on the scope of CO protections; striking a balance through the imposition of obligations; the limitations of current Australian CO legal provisions; and effective regulation of CO is beyond the contours of law. Our study found some support for a compromise approach to CO regulation, but identified a need to improve current regulatory approaches. While some improvements could be made to legislation, an effective regulatory response will likely need to be multi-pronged and consider the role of other regulatory instruments.

articles.title: Female Prune Belly syndrome: A social media survey report.
articles.authors: Amado N, Yong R, Johnson N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Given the extreme rarity of female Prune Belly syndrome (PBS), there is a scarcity of information on this population. With the rise of social media, these connected communities of female PBS patients provide an opportunity to identify medical and social challenges faced by them.
METHODS: A 26-question, non-validated REDCap survey was created, IRB approved and administered from Aug 1, 2022 to May 31, 2024. The survey link was circulated through the investigator's institutional social media page. Members of the PBS Network elected to share this social media-based survey to a private Facebook group. No medical records were reviewed on these anonymous subjects. Participants were queried as to whether they had a diagnosis of cloacal anomaly in addition to PBS. Self/family-reported long-term urinary/genital/sexual function outcomes of individuals aged ≤10 versus >10 years old were compared by Fisher's exact analysis with significance p < 0.05 (GraphPad software).
RESULTS: Twelve adults with PBS and 6 caregivers completed the survey for 18 PBS females (ages 2-66y [mean 28y], with n = 5 ≤ 10 years old and the remainder >20 years old). 61% prefer the term PBS over EBS. 38.9% reported diagnosis of PBS + cloacal anomaly. 71.4% of PBS + cloaca anomaly females (mean age 20.4y) manifest kidney dysfunction compared to only 27.8% of PBS patients (mean age 33y) without cloaca anomaly (p = 0.14). Overall rates included self-reported urinary incontinence (61.1%), CIC (38.9%), native kidney disease or failure (50%), and female reproductive anomalies (72.2%). Of the 12 females who are sexually active, 58.3% have cloaca, and 50% patients have successfully become pregnant, with 2 successful vaginal births, 2 successful cesarean section, 1 miscarriage, and 1 abortion. Self-reported challenges include multiple hospital admissions and surgeries, depression, lack of independence, body image issues, and fatigue. 93% of patients reported difficulties with physical activity (inability to run and play sports, wheelchair-bound, and minimal exercise limited by severe pain).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the utility of social media for characterizing patient-reported outcomes in female PBS, a rare and understudied condition. Female PBS is associated with a substantial lifelong physical burden extending beyond congenital genitourinary anomalies. Despite the high prevalence of Müllerian anomalies, many affected women reported successful pregnancies. These findings…

articles.title: Real-World Safety Profile of Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: A Population-Based Pharmacovigilance Study Leveraging FAERS and EudraVigilance Databases.
articles.authors: Cui Z, Song P, Xie D et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) is the first FDA-approved antibody-drug conjugate targeting folate receptor-α (FRα)-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Despite its clinical adoption, comprehensive post-marketing real-world evidence regarding its safety profile remains limited. This study aimed to systematically characterize the adverse event (AE) profile of MIRV in real-world settings and to identify potential safety signals using large-scale pharmacovigilance databases.
METHODS: A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis was conducted using adverse event reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS, 2022-2025). We excluded all reports submitted for male patients. Safety signals were assessed at the system organ class (SOC), standardized MedDRA query (SMQ), and preferred term (PT) levels. Disproportionality analyses were performed using 4 algorithms: reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). Time-to-onset (TTO) analysis was conducted to evaluate onset patterns. External validation was performed using the EudraVigilance database.
FINDINGS: A total of 1,249 MIRV-related reports corresponding to 2,577 AEs were identified in FAERS. At the SOC level, eye disorders were the most frequently reported AEs (n = 593) and demonstrated the strongest disproportionality signal (ROR: 13.79, 95% CI: 12.58-15.12). At the PT level, the 3 most frequently reported AEs were vision blurred (n = 97), neuropathy peripheral (n = 95), and cataract (n = 75). Among detected safety signals, the strongest disproportionality signals (ranked by IC025 value) were observed for keratitis (ROR: 390.64, PRR: 383.08, EBGM05: 269.06, IC025: 5.06), keratopathy (ROR: 487.9, PRR: 479.78, EBGM05: 323.68, IC025: 4.87), and pneumonitis (ROR: 56.93, PRR: 55.37, EBGM05: 43.35, IC0254.64). Overall, 44 positive PT-level signals were identified. Common labeled AEs included blurred vision, peripheral neuropathy, cataract, diarrhoea, and abdominal pain. Potentially novel (unlabeled) signals included blindness, colitis, pulmonary fibrosis, glaucoma, intestinal perforation, and astigmatism. Time-to-onset analysis showed that 42.9% of AEs occurred within the first month after treatment initiation, indicating an early-onset pattern. In the EudraVigilance database, 527 MIRV-related reports were identified. At the SOC level, eye disorders again demonstrated…

articles.title: Comparing the Risk of Maternal Complications and Adverse Infant Outcomes Among Pregnancies With and Without COVID-19 in the Sentinel System.
articles.authors: Shinde MU, Cosgrove A, Kempner ME et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, but knowledge about the timing of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy on these outcomes is limited.
OBJECTIVES: We implemented the CONSIGN protocol to examine the impact of COVID-19 on pregnancy-related complications and adverse infant outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: We identified eligible females with live-birth deliveries who had a COVID-19 diagnosis or a positive-confirmed test for SARS-CoV-2. Pregnancies with COVID-19 were propensity score (PS) matched 1:1 to pregnancies without COVID-19 during the 6 months prior to or during pregnancy.
RESULTS: From 2020 to 2023, we identified 69 901 pregnancies with COVID-19 and 1:1 matched pregnancies without COVID-19. Most pregnancies with COVID-19 were diagnosed in the third trimester (49%, 33 979/69 901) and < 5% (1860/69 901) were classified as severe. Pregnancies with severe COVID-19 in the first trimester had a higher rate of preterm delivery, and pregnancies with severe COVID-19 in the second trimester had a higher rate of cesarean section compared to those without COVID-19. No increased risk of adverse infant outcomes was observed among 22 865 linked mother-infant pairs with COVID-19 although a slightly increased risk of low birth weight was noted among pregnancies exposed to severe COVID-19 in the third trimester.
CONCLUSION: Among nearly 70 000 live-birth pregnancies with COVID-19, severe COVID-19 was associated with cesarean section and preterm delivery. No association with adverse infant outcomes was noted. Our study enabled assessment of the timing and severity of COVID-19 on adverse pregnancy outcomes, although changing treatment and prevention recommendations might impact trends of these outcomes.

articles.title: Gestational Alloimmune Liver Disease.
articles.authors: Conover KR, Taylor SA
articles.abstract: Gestational alloimmune liver disease (GALD) is a top cause of neonatal acute liver failure that is highly preventable in subsequent pregnancies after the index case. The understood mechanism involves placental passage of maternal antibodies targeting an unknown fetal hepatocyte antigen, leading to complement activation and extensive hepatocyte damage and fibrosis. This disease mechanism explains the clinical presentation of liver failure shortly after birth.
