Intravenous immunoglobulin and double volume exchange transfusion can improve neonatal outcomes, likely due to dampening the effect of circulating maternal antibodies. Early recognition of GALD depends on a high index of clinical suspicion.

articles.title: Retrospective Study of Pelvic Irradiation in Patients With Advanced Uterine Cervical Cancer.
articles.authors: Utsumi N, Kawamura H, Yamano T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: The clinical role of local therapy for advanced uterine cervical cancer remains unclear. While systemic chemotherapy is the standard treatment, pelvic radiotherapy may contribute to local control and potentially improve outcomes in selected patients. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of pelvic irradiation in patients with advanced cervical cancer with para-aortic lymph node (PAN) and/or distant metastases.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 35 patients with cervical cancer with PAN and/or distant metastases who underwent radiotherapy including whole-pelvic irradiation between 2009 and 2019. Patients were classified into a distant metastasis (DM) group and a PAN group. The DM group was further subdivided into patients with lymph node-only metastases (LY group) and those with organ metastases (OR group). Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards model.
RESULTS: The median OS for all patients was 2.22 years. The median OS was 1.76 years in the DM group and 3.02 years in the PAN group, with no statistically significant difference between the groups (p=0.838). Within the DM group, the median OS was 1.18 years in the OR group and 2.01 years in the LY group, with no significant difference (p=0.590). Treatment was generally well tolerated, with limited severe adverse events. In Cox proportional hazards analysis using the PAN group as the reference, neither the OR nor the LY group showed a statistically significant difference in OS.
CONCLUSION: Although limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, this study suggests that semi-definitive pelvic radiotherapy may be a reasonable treatment option for selected patients with cervical cancer with distant metastases.

articles.title: 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Michalski K, Kosmala A, Kohnle P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Detection of locoregional lymph node (LN) metastases is a critical prognostic factor in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is limited by insufficient specificity, potentially leading to overtreatment. We evaluated gallium-68 fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI-04) positron-emission tomography (PET)/CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in this setting, using CT as comparator.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT scans of 15 patients with gynecologic SCC (nine cervical, six vulvar carcinomas; mean age 56.3 years, range=38-86 years) were analyzed. PET/CT and CT were read independently by two blinded readers. Histopathology and/or clinical and radiological follow-up (12-18 months) served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was calculated on a patient-based level; maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were compared using Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test.
RESULTS: Histopathological confirmation was available in 12 patients; three were classified by follow-up. LN metastases were confirmed in five patients. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieved a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and accuracy of 100%. CT achieved a sensitivity and NPV of 100% but produced false-positive findings in three patients (specificity=70%, PPV=62.5%, accuracy=80%), caused by tattoo-associated lymphadenopathy, sarcoidosis and reactive nodal enlargement, none of which showed pathological tracer uptake. Metastatic LNs exhibited higher SUVmax (mean 23.2±6.0) than nodes false-positive on CT (mean 4.5±4.6; p=0.004 and p=0.036). Primary tumors were visualized in all patients undergoing initial staging; peritoneal nodules down to 7 mm were detected.
CONCLUSION: In this small cohort, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed a higher observed specificity than contrast-enhanced CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in gynecologic SCC, with no false-negative cases observed.

articles.title: PREGnancy, HEART Health and Cardiovascular Disease (PREG-HEART): protocol for a national, direct-to-participant prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Hunt K, Buchan R, Sheppard C et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality in the UK. Its prevalence in pregnancy continues to rise, driven by both improved survival of women with congenital and inherited heart disease into reproductive age and an increasing burden of acquired cardiovascular risk factors. However, its natural history and optimal management remain poorly defined. Current research is limited by small sample sizes, drawn from highly selected patient cohorts from individual units. The aim of the PREGnancy, HEART Health and Cardiovascular Disease (PREG-HEART) study is to develop a patient-driven, clinically relevant digital platform to understand the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease in pregnancy and support clinical trials of management strategies. This paper provides the protocol for PREG-HEART which will start with a 6-month pilot study.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PREG-HEART will use an online, direct-to-patient platform to enrol patients with cardiovascular disease in pregnancy alongside healthy pregnant controls. Enrolled women will be invited to provide self-reported demographic and clinical data and consent to linkage with national health records for long-term follow-up. We will also seek consent for storage and analysis of leftover clinical biosamples and to re-contact participants, enabling recruitment into sub-studies and clinical trials. Planned analysis for the pilot study at 6 months will assess feasibility, including recruitment rates, case-mix of cardiovascular diagnoses, and participant geographical, socio-economic and ethnic background, compared with the UK general pregnant population. Findings from the pilot study will inform subsequent phases of PREG-HEART, which will explore associations between different cardiovascular diagnoses and adverse cardiovascular, obstetric and neonatal events. We will work closely with patients and clinicians to define priority research questions and use the PREG-HEART platform to support a range of observational and interventional studies to address these.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Approved by the West Midlands Solihull Research Ethics Committee (IRAS 349694; REC 25/WM/0142). Findings will be returned directly to participants, disseminated to clinicians through professional societies and the National Institute for Health and Care Research-British Heart Foundation Cardiovascular Partnership, and to the public through partner charities, as well as by peer-reviewed…

articles.title: Multimodal preoperative risk stratification of pancreatic mass lesions using clinical variables, imaging radiomics and plasma cfDNA methylation: protocol for an ambispective multicentre diagnostic prediction model study.
articles.authors: Xue Z, Jia W, Weng X et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative risk stratification of pancreatic mass lesions is challenging because malignancies, premalignant, inflammatory and indolent lesions can overlap on conventional assessment. Clinical variables, imaging radiomics and plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation may offer complementary information. We aim to develop and externally evaluate a multimodal model for clinically high-risk lesions, define interpretable risk strata and assess whether cfDNA methylation adds value beyond clinical and CT-radiomics information.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This ambispective diagnostic prediction model study will include approximately 3000 adults at eight Chinese tertiary hospitals: 1500 at a lead development centre and 1500 at seven external evaluation centres. The primary target condition is a prespecified diagnosis-based composite, assigned independently of management and predictor values. A hierarchical reference standard prioritises surgical pathology, followed by definitive biopsy or cytology and blinded adjudication with longitudinal follow-up for non-operated participants. Predictors will comprise clinical variables, contrast-enhanced CT radiomics and plasma cfDNA methylation markers measured using a prespecified targeted methylation panel. The primary multimodal model will integrate these three domains using elastic-net logistic regression; MRI radiomics will be analysed in a separate secondary pipeline. Threshold-selection rules will be fixed before fitting; the final preprocessing pipeline, model and two cut-points will be locked before external evaluation. Performance will be assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis and model-based descriptive analyses. Predicted probabilities will define low-, intermediate- and high-risk strata for multidisciplinary assessment.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval has been obtained from three participating centres. Ethics approval, institutional authorisation or documented reliance will be obtained from the remaining centres before local prospective enrolment or data contribution, where required. Written informed consent will be obtained from prospectively enrolled participants; consent may be waived for eligible retrospective cases where permitted. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and conference presentation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07045571.

articles.title: Exploring patterns of acute and primary care utilisation before diagnosis, during treatment and for 3 years postcompletion of surgery and adjuvant treatment in women with endometrial cancer: a protocol for a Victorian data linkage study.
articles.authors: Kinnane N, Drosdowsky A, Allanson ER et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women with endometrial cancer have two to three times higher rate of pre-existing chronic cardiovascular risk factors including hypertension (59% vs 31%), obesity (34% vs 15%) and diabetes (26% vs 10%) compared with women without cancer. With a 5-year cancer-specific survival of 85%, these women are three times more likely to die of cardiovascular disease than they are to have a cancer recurrence. Surveillance for recurrence dominates post-treatment follow-up, a model misaligned with greatest health risks. Current approaches to endometrial cancer care may disrupt established management pathways for high-mortality risk chronic conditions and how best to manage chronic disease postcancer remains unclear. Women’s engagement with health services to manage chronic conditions before, during and after cancer treatment and what it means for long-term health is unknown. Linked data enables examination of healthcare utilisation across the care continuum.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This retrospective cohort study uses data accessed via the Victorian Comprehensive Cancer Centre (VCCC) Alliance Data Connect platform, an Australian platform that links Victorian general practice data: Primary Care Data Research Repository (PATRON); hospital data—Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED), Victorian Radiotherapy Minimum Dataset (VRMDS), Victorian Emergency Minimum Dataset (VEMD), Victorian Integrated Non-Admitted Health Dataset (VINAH); and clinical registry data—Victorian Cancer Registry (VCR) and Victorian Death Index (VDI), managed in the secure environment of the Centre for Victorian Data Linkage (CVDL). Data span 2008–2022. Healthcare utilisation across acute and primary care settings will be mapped across three phases: prediagnosis, during treatment and 3 years post-treatment. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics reporting frequency and percentage of encounters, mean and SD. Primary outcome is frequency and patterns of healthcare utilisation before, during and after endometrial cancer diagnosis and treatment. This includes frequency and type of cancer and non-cancer healthcare encounters, patterns of specialist versus general practice (GP) care, evidence of care associated with, or sought for, chronic diseases.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Study approved by the Office of Research Ethics and Integrity (Number 2025–23718-73133-20); Patron Data Governance (ID PAT 0001138), The University of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Results will be…

articles.title: Assessing awareness and use of Opill among Latine young adults in an agricultural setting in California.
articles.authors: Stoner MCD, Browne EN, Raymond-Flesch M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We assessed awareness and use of Opill, the first over-the-counter oral contraceptive pill, and identified correlates of awareness among Latine young adults in an agricultural setting in California.
STUDY DESIGN: Two annual visits from a prospective cohort study; A Crecer: Salinas Teen Health Study 2023-2025 (n = 344).
RESULTS: Awareness increased from 11% to 19%; only four participants (1%) accessed Opill. Females and participants with favorable birth control attitudes, recent sexual and reproductive health service use, and more of their information about sexual health coming from doctors had greater awareness.
CONCLUSIONS: Access expansion should be paired with targeted communication strategies.

articles.title: Genetic Analysis of Fetal Corpus Callosum Abnormalities: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
articles.authors: Xu Y, Deng L, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Corpus callosum abnormalities (CCAs) are an anomaly that can occur in fetuses during pregnancy. This retrospective cohort study included 86 fetuses with prenatally diagnosed CCAs. All cases underwent chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), with exome sequencing (ES) performed either concurrently (n = 73) or sequentially (n = 3). CMA identified two aneuploidies and 10 pathogenic or likely pathogenic copy number variants, yielding a diagnostic rate of 13.9% (12 of 86). Among the CMA-negative cases, ES data were available for 90.5% (67 of 74) of cases and provided an additional diagnostic yield of 26.9% (18 of 67). The detection rate of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants was higher in nonisolated CCA cases, especially within the subgroup with multisystem anomalies (53.8%), although this difference did not reach statistical significance. The pregnancy termination rate was significantly higher in cases of nonisolated CCAs compared with isolated CCAs (79.4% vs 52.2%; P = 0.013). Termination occurred in all cases with positive CMA results and in 94.4% of cases with positive ES findings. The current study shows that the combination of CMA and ES enhances the diagnostic yield for fetal CCAs. Implementing concurrent CMA and ES testing in cases of nonisolated CCAs, particularly those involving multisystem anomalies, is recommended to maximize diagnostic efficiency and support timely prenatal decision-making.

articles.title: Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms Associated With Intensive Care Unit Admission in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry
articles.authors: Murillo García JD, Loaiza Cardona LM, González AD et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) are a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, particularly in Latin America. Depression and anxiety are frequent during pregnancy and may influence HDP severity, yet their impact on clinical outcomes remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether depressive and anxiety symptoms are associated with obstetric intensive care unit (ICU) admission and hospital length of stay among women with HDP.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted at a Colombian tertiary-care referral hospital (July 2024-January 2025). Women aged ≥16 years in their third trimester hospitalized for HDP completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression and Cox regression models assessed associations with ICU admission and length of stay.
RESULTS: Among 234 participants (median age 25 years), 61.1% required ICU care; only 14 of the 143 ICU patients (9.8%) were assessed before ICU transfer. An Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale score ≥10 or a positive response to item 10 was independently associated with ICU admission (odds ratio 4.83, 95% confidence interval 1.56-14.94, P = 0.006) and longer hospitalization (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% confidence interval 0.48-1.00, P = 0.048). In an exploratory finding, a Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 score ≥10 showed an inverse association with ICU admission (odds ratio 0.29, 95% confidence interval 0.09-0.88, P = 0.029). Hemoglobin <11 g/dL and a post hoc mean arterial pressure threshold ≥102.5 mmHg were also significantly associated with ICU admission.
CONCLUSIONS: Depressive symptoms were associated with obstetric ICU admission and prolonged hospitalization in patients admitted for HDP, whereas anxiety appeared protective, which seems counterintuitive and requires future research to confirm its association; however, because most assessments took place after ICU transfer, causality could not be established. Integrating mental health screening into HDP management may improve maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical utility of plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing in adult immunocompromised patients: A real-world cohort study.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.authors: Charles DW, Alkabab Y, Sharma D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plasma metagenomic next generation sequencing (mNGS) enables noninvasive pathogen detection independent of organism viability. Although analytic performance has been described, the real-world clinical impact in immunocompromised hosts remains incompletely defined.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of immunocompromised adults undergoing plasma mNGS testing from January 2022 through November 2024 at the Medical University of South Carolina. Immunocompromised conditions included solid organ transplantation, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, active hematologic malignancy, HIV, or biologic immunosuppressants. Clinical impact was adjudicated by infectious disease physicians as positive, negative, or neutral. Positive results were classified as definite, probable, possible, or unlikely infectious based on clinical correlation and concordance with conventional microbiologic testing (CMT).
RESULTS: Ninety-eight patients were included (median age 60 years [range 18-76]; 63% male), including solid organ transplant (31%), hematopoietic stem cell transplant (8%), HIV (13%), active malignancy (42%), corticosteroids (3%), and biologic therapy (10%). At testing, 85% were receiving antimicrobials and 88% were hospitalized. Plasma mNGS was positive in 62% of cases, with CMT concordance in 30%. Thirty-two percent of tests had positive clinical impact, identifying unrecognized infection or antimicrobial optimization. Sixty-six percent had no treatment impact and 2% had potential negative impact. More than half of discordant positives were deemed possible or unlikely infections. False-negative cases included invasive mold and nontuberculous mycobacterial infections.
CONCLUSIONS: In this antimicrobial-exposed immunocompromised cohort, plasma mNGS frequently detected organisms but less often influenced clinical management. Discordant positives were common, and false negatives occurred in selected syndromes, supporting cautious interpretation and stewardship-guided use.

articles.title: Vaccination-driven suppression, stochastic variability, and contact saturation in HPV-cervical cancer transmission in India: A Black-Karasinski perturbation model.
articles.authors: Midhun TA, Murugesan K
articles.abstract: This study develops two stochastic models (one representing the pre-vaccination era and the other representing the vaccination era) describing human papillomavirus infection and its progression to cervical cancer in India. Both models incorporate Holling type-II incidence, with transmission dynamics perturbed by the Black-Karasinski stochastic process. A rigorous theoretical analysis is conducted for these models. The existence and uniqueness of global positive solutions are established, followed by the derivation of threshold quantities governing persistence and extinction. When Ris>1(i=1,2), each model admits at least one stationary distribution, indicating long-term persistence of infection. In contrast, when Rie<1(i=1,2), the infection undergoes exponential extinction. The non-vaccination model is fitted to annual cervical cancer incidence data from India for the period 2003 to 2017. Substituting the fitted parameter values within the specified time horizon implies that the system remains persistent under the current conditions. Subsequently, for the vaccination model, the remaining parameters are estimated from reliable scientific data, and simulations are carried out from 2025 onward. For the vaccination period, the estimated parameter values indicate eventual eradication of infection. Extensive numerical simulations support the theoretical findings. A global sensitivity analysis using Latin hypercube sampling and partial rank correlation coefficients identifies the most influential parameters. Finally, extinction time distributions and survival probabilities are examined to provide policy-relevant insights toward achieving an HPV-free India within the next 50 years.

articles.title: Sonographic Assessment of Cervical Length in Placenta Previa Compared With Normal Pregnancy During The Early Third Trimester.
articles.journal: Seminars in ultrasound, CT, and MR
articles.authors: Khan J, Yaqoob F, Rasheed A
articles.abstract: Placenta previa is a significant obstetric disorder linked to preterm delivery and antepartum hemorrhage. The importance of cervical shortening in early third trimester has not been adequately proven, also there is little evidence of early third-trimester monitoring using transabdominal sonography (TAS) at 28-32 weeks of gestation. To assess the cervical length in the placenta previa and normal pregnancy group at 28-32 and the prevalence of a short cervix (≤25 mm) in placenta previa with the use of TAS. The study was a comparative cross-sectional study conducted over 6 months in the Radiology departments of tertiary hospitals in Rawalpindi. The 70 pregnant women (35 with placenta previa; 35 with normal pregnancy) were sampled. TAS used in measuring cervical length measured the internal to external os in the sagittal plane of measurement, and these measurements were in millimeters. The mean cervical length was significantly lower in the placenta previa group than in the normal pregnancy group (24.37 ± 5.34 mm vs. 34.46 ± 4.07 mm; P < 0.001). Short cervix (≤25 mm) was observed in 51.4% of placenta previa cases and in none of the normal pregnancies (P < 0.001). These findings suggest an association between placenta previa and cervical shortening and may justify closer clinical surveillance in the early third trimester.

articles.title: Scinderin: a metastasis-associated biomarker identified in metastatic lung nodule interstitial fluid proteomics.
articles.authors: Guasch-Vallés M, Ribes-Santolaria M, Eritja N et al.
articles.abstract: The tumor microenvironment is a critical factor in understanding cancer progression and metastasis. In this context, isolating tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) is a powerful tool for detecting cancer biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In our study, we conducted a proteomic analysis of TIFs from metastatic lung nodules using a murine model. The TIFs from these lungs were enriched with actin-binding proteins, among other molecules. Notably, we identified Scinderin (Scin), an actin-binding protein secreted by tumor cells. Knockdown of Scin resulted in a significant decrease in the number and size of lung nodules, as well as a reduction, albeit to a lesser extent, in disseminated tumor cells (DTCs). Furthermore, silencing Scin inhibited cell and tumor growth in different cancer cell lines. In human tumors, Scin was detected in the tumor interstitial fluid (TIF) of endometrial cancer patients. Scin was expressed abundantly in serous endometrial carcinomas and in the secretory endometrium. Remarkably, a paired analysis using an endometrial cancer tissue-array revealed increased Scin expression in metastatic samples compared to their corresponding primary tumors. In addition, a retrospective study revealed that levels of Scin in plasma were significantly elevated in patients who developed metastases. These findings suggest that Scin plays a significant role in the metastatic process and may serve as a promising biomarker for tumor aggressiveness and metastatic potential.

articles.title: Total polyphenols from Hemerocallis citrina Baroni leaves improve sleep quality in mice with perimenopausal insomnia and are associated with altered expression of 5-HT1AR, ADCY5, PKA, and GABRA2.
articles.authors: Zhang Z, Wang Y, Meng Y et al.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni has a long history of dietary and medicinal use in China. Its dried whole herb is documented as an ethnic medicinal material in the 2003 edition of the Guizhou Provincial Quality Standards for Chinese Medicinal and Ethnic Medicinal Materials, while Hemerocallis flowers are traditionally used for "ye shao an mei" (), referring to reduced or disturbed sleep at night. Modern studies have demonstrated sleep-improving effects of the flowers, and previous work showed neuroprotective and antidepressant-like activities of total polyphenols from Hemerocallis citrina Baroni leaves (HLTP). However, the effects of HLTP on perimenopausal insomnia (PMI) remain unclear.
AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the effects of HLTP on sleep disturbances in mice exhibiting perimenopausal and insomnia-like features and investigate associated molecular changes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: HLTP was prepared using a previously reported procedure. Network pharmacology predicted candidate targets and pathways for 32 phenolic constituents identified in an earlier HLTP batch, while molecular docking assessed predicted binding to 10 core targets selected by protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis. A composite mouse model was generated using 4-vinylcyclohexene dioxide (VCD) to induce perimenopausal features, followed by para-chloro-DL-phenylalanine (PCPA) to induce insomnia-like disturbances. Seventy female C57BL/6J mice were randomized into seven groups (n = 10 per group): Control, Con + HLTP, Model, HLTP-L/M/H (10, 20, and 40 mg/kg, respectively), and zopiclone. Treatment began with model induction. Behavioral tests, pentobarbital-induced sleep testing, 24 h electroencephalographic/electromyographic (EEG/EMG) polysomnography, histopathology, biochemical assays, and Western blotting were used to evaluate pharmacological effects and associated molecular changes. 16S rRNA sequencing, serum untargeted metabolomics, and brain transcriptomics were additionally performed to characterize complementary changes in the gut microbiota, systemic metabolism, and central gene expression.
RESULTS: Network pharmacology prioritized the serotonergic synapse pathway for further investigation. HLTP improved behavioral and sleep-related abnormalities, with the most consistent effects at the high dose. EEG/EMG polysomnography showed a partial shift in sleep-wake distribution toward the Control pattern. During the inactive phase, high-dose HLTP shortened…

articles.title: Comparison of cPCR, PCR-HRM, qPCR, and microarray for detecting GSTM1 and GSTT1 deletions and copy number variations: agreement and practical considerations.
articles.authors: Fidelis GFS, Torso NG, Matos YG et al.
articles.abstract: Copy number variations (CNVs) are clinically relevant as they may influence gene expression, enzymatic activity, and interindividual variability in drug response. Among these, deletions affecting the Glutathione S-transferase (GST) genes GSTM1 and GSTT1 are of particular interest due to their potential implications for pharmacogenetic research. However, comparative evidence to guide the selection of the most appropriate method for CNV detection in different laboratory settings remains limited. Therefore, this study compared four molecular techniques, microarray, conventional PCR (cPCR), high-resolution melting PCR (PCR-HRM), and quantitative PCR (qPCR) for detecting CNVs in GSTM1 and GSTT1. Germline DNA samples from participants diagnosed with ovarian cancer were analyzed by all genotyping methods. A total of 80 participants were included for the cross-method agreement analysis. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa coefficient, with 95% confidence intervals estimated using the Wilson score method. qPCR and microarray showed perfect concordance for both GSTM1 and GSTT1 qualitative and copy-number (CN) assessment. PCR-HRM showed perfect qualitative performance for GSTT1, whereas cPCR exhibited slightly lower agreement for both genes, despite maintaining high overall concordance. For those two genes, cPCR had the lowest entry cost, PCR-HRM combined qualitative robustness with workflow simplicity, qPCR was the most suitable targeted approach for CN estimation, and microarray was most advantageous when broader pharmacogenomic profiling was also intended. These findings indicate that method selection should be guided not only by analytical performance but also by the intended analytical objective and the available technical and financial resources.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rg1 alleviates dehydroepiandrosterone-induced polycystic ovary syndrome by regulating granulosa cell glycolysis, proliferative activity, and apoptosis through the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway.
articles.authors: Wu Z, Mu L, Cheng S
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) represents a common endocrine-metabolic disorder. Mounting evidence has demonstrated that Korean red ginseng confers therapeutic advantages in PCOS; accordingly, this investigation sought to elucidate the therapeutic potential of its bioactive constituent, ginsenoside Rg1, in this pathological condition. A DHEA-induced murine PCOS model was generated for in vivo experiments. Serum hormonal profiles and insulin sensitivity were assessed. Ovarian histomorphological alterations were evaluated through hematoxylin and eosin staining. For in vitro studies, a PCOS-mimicking cellular model was constructed by exposing KGN cells to dihydrotestosterone (DHT, 500 nM) for 24 h. Cell viability was quantified using the CCK-8 assay. Apoptotic events were characterized through flow cytometric analysis and immunoblotting of Bax and Bcl-2. Expression patterns of glycolytic enzymes, alongside the proliferation marker PCNA, were examined. Rg1 administration ameliorated PCOS-associated phenotypes in mice, manifesting as reduced body mass, partly restored serum hormone concentrations, enhanced insulin responsiveness, and improved ovarian architecture. Rg1 potentiated glycolytic and proliferative activities while suppressing apoptotic processes in both PCOS mice and DHT-challenged KGN cells. Mechanistically, Rg1 triggered PI3K/Akt/mTOR cascade activation, evidenced by elevated p-Akt and p-mTOR expression, effects that were partially reversed by LY294002, a pharmacological antagonist of this pathway. Furthermore, LY294002 co-administration attenuated the protective actions of Rg1 against PCOS in both experimental paradigms. In conclusion, ginsenoside Rg1 exerts beneficial effects on PCOS by enhancing glycolysis and proliferative activity while attenuating apoptosis in ovarian granulosa KGN cells via PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway activation. These findings position Rg1 as a promising therapeutic candidate for PCOS management.

articles.title: TP53 Y220C hotspot mutation in clinically advanced ovarian carcinoma: Frequency and genomic features.
articles.authors: Avellanet Crespo NI, Corines J, Ross JS et al.
articles.abstract: Over 80% of cases of clinically advanced ovarian carcinomas (CAOC) contain inactivating genomic alterations in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene. Among these, the rare TP53 Y220C hotspot mutation can be potentially "reverted" to restore wild-type function using novel drugs, such as Rezatapopt (PC14586, Clinical Trial NCT04585750). This study builds on existing knowledge by exploring the molecular changes associated with TP53 Y220C-positive CAOC. A retrospective review of specimens from the Foundation Medicine database identified 29,365 cases of CAOC of various subtypes that had undergone hybrid capture-based comprehensive genomic profiling. Within the 29,365 cases, 854 (2.9%) featured a TP53 Y220C mutation (Y220C+). When compared with the 28,511 CAOC negative for TP53 Y220C mutations (Y220C-), the Y220C + patients had similar increased frequencies of genomic alterations in CCNE1, KRAS, PIK3CA, NF1, and BRCA1. CAOC features a 2.9% incidence of the potentially targetable TP53 Y220C mutation, making it one of the most frequent tumor types harboring this rare but recurrent mutation.

articles.title: Cervical cancer: national clinical practice guidelines from the French cervical cancer guidelines group.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Carcopino X, Ouldamer L, Huchon C et al.
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, cervical cancer management has evolved substantially, with major changes in surgical approach, surgical radicality, nodal staging, imaging, radiotherapy techniques, brachytherapy and systemic treatments. To harmonize practice and integrate new evidence into clinically applicable recommendations, the French Cervical Cancer Guidelines Group developed national clinical practice guidelines for the management of patients with cervical cancer. The guideline process was conducted under the auspices of the French National College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and involved a multidisciplinary expert panel representing the French scientific societies involved in cervical cancer care. Clinical questions were formulated using the PICO framework and addressed the full continuum of care, including initial assessment, imaging, diagnostic conization, surgical nodal staging, treatment, fertility preservation, response assessment, follow-up, recurrence and specific clinical situations. Evidence was reviewed and critically appraised according to the GRADE methodology, and all recommendations were based on the 2018 FIGO staging system. External validation was performed through a two-round Delphi process involving 87 independent reviewers. Overall, 130 PICO questions generated 158 recommendations, including 35 strong and 52 weak recommendations, while no recommendation could be issued for 71 questions. Key practice-changing recommendations include the role of diagnostic conization in early-stage assessment, avoidance of minimally invasive hysterectomy from stage IB1 disease, risk-adapted surgical radicality, sentinel lymph node biopsy with ultrastaging, image-guided brachytherapy after chemoradiotherapy, and integration of PEMBROLIZUMAB in selected locally advanced or metastatic settings.

articles.title: Risk-adapted surgical treatment of early-stage cervical cancer: tailoring radicality, ovarian preservation, and surgical approach in the post-shape and post-LACC era - A review from the French cervical cancer guidelines group✰,✰✰,★,★★.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Ouldamer L, Deberti M, Morineau F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exclusive surgical treatment remains a cornerstone of management for selected patients with early-stage cervical cancer. However, the traditional paradigm of radical hysterectomy with systematic parametrial resection has been challenged by contemporary evidence supporting risk-adapted surgical de-escalation. In parallel, randomized and real-world data have raised major concerns regarding the oncologic safety of minimally invasive radical hysterectomy.
METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted to summarize the available evidence on exclusive surgical treatment for early-stage cervical cancer. Predefined topics included the extent of hysterectomy and parametrial resection, ovarian preservation, surgical approach, and the comparative role of surgery versus chemoradiotherapy. Randomized trials, prospective studies, retrospective cohorts, meta-analyses, and relevant methodological reviews were included.
RESULTS: In early-stage cervical cancer, parametrial involvement is uncommon in well-selected low-risk patients. The SHAPE trial demonstrated the non-inferiority of simple hysterectomy compared with radical hysterectomy in low-risk disease, with lower urinary morbidity, supporting risk-adapted omission of parametrial resection. Ovarian preservation appears oncologically safe in young women with early-stage disease and no high-risk features, although caution is warranted in the presence of adverse factors such as uterine corpus involvement, lymphovascular space invasion, lymph node metastases, and non-squamous histology. Conversely, minimally invasive radical hysterectomy has been associated with inferior disease-free and overall survival compared with open surgery, despite reduced perioperative morbidity.
CONCLUSION: Exclusive surgical treatment for early-stage cervical cancer should be guided by individualized risk assessment, combining parametrial de-escalation in low-risk disease, ovarian preservation when appropriate, and open surgery when radical hysterectomy is required.

articles.title: Special situations in cervical cancer management: de novo metastatic disease, occult cancer after simple hysterectomy, and cervical stump cancer - A review from the french cervical cancer guidelines group.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Fuss E, Lecointre L, Gladieff L et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cervical cancer may present in uncommon and complex clinical settings, including de novo metastatic disease, occult cancer incidentally diagnosed after simple hysterectomy and cervical stump cancer after supracervical hysterectomy.
METHODS: A literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library and Scopus. English- and French-language publications available through September 2025 were qualitatively analyzed according to their methodological quality, level of evidence and clinical relevance.
RESULTS: In de novo metastatic cervical cancer, platinum-based chemotherapy remains the backbone of systemic treatment. BEVACIZUMAB and PEMBROLIZUMAB have improved outcomes in trials combining de novo metastatic, persistent and recurrent disease, although their specific benefit in the de novo subgroup remains less clearly established. Local treatment of oligometastases has been associated with prolonged survival in selected patients, but controlled comparative evidence is lacking. For occult cervical cancer after simple hysterectomy, favorable outcomes without additional treatment have been reported in selected patients with small tumors, limited stromal invasion, negative margins and no nodal involvement. Completion surgery and radiotherapy-based treatments have achieved disease control in patients with more extensive disease or adverse pathological features, but their comparative efficacy remains uncertain. In cervical stump cancer, historical series suggest that external beam radiotherapy combined with brachytherapy provides effective locoregional control. Evidence regarding contemporary image-guided brachytherapy is limited, while completion surgery after radiotherapy has been associated with substantial morbidity without demonstrated improvement in disease control.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence remains limited by heterogeneous populations, historical staging and treatment techniques, selection bias, and the absence of prospective controlled comparisons.

articles.title: Fertility-sparing surgery and ovarian transposition in cervical cancer - a review from the French Cervical Cancer Guidelines Group.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.authors: Margueritte F, Mathevet P, Diguisto C et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer often affects women of reproductive age, for whom treatment may compromise both fertility and ovarian endocrine function. Fertility-sparing surgery may preserve the ability to achieve pregnancy, whereas Ovarian Preservation (OP) during hysterectomy and Ovarian Transposition (OT) before pelvic radiotherapy may prevent treatment-induced premature ovarian insufficiency. However, the oncological safety and appropriate indications for these strategies require careful assessment. Despite the low certainty of evidence, conization with negative margins may be offered for FIGO 2018 stage IA1-IA2 disease, irrespective of lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI). Simple trachelectomy may be preferred for stage IB1 disease without LVSI, whereas evidence remains insufficient to choose between simple and radical trachelectomy in LVSI-positive disease. Routine cerclage at the time of trachelectomy is not supported by current evidence. Completion hysterectomy after childbearing provides no established oncological benefit and should not be systematically performed. For stage IB2 disease, neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by fertility-sparing surgery remains investigational because of uncertain oncological safety and a potential adverse effect on survival. OP appears oncologically acceptable in carefully selected premenopausal patients undergoing surgery, particularly those with early-stage squamous cell carcinoma. OT preserves ovarian function in approximately two-thirds of patients receiving pelvic radiotherapy, especially in women younger than 40 years when both ovaries are positioned above the radiation field. However, OP and OT must be balanced against the risk of ovarian metastasis and should be approached cautiously in patients with adenocarcinoma, advanced disease, or uterine corpus, parametrial, or lymph node involvement.

articles.title: Inflammatory Markers and Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index Predict Recurrence Patterns in Endometrial Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Kong R, Liu H, Zhang C et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammatory and host-related markers have demonstrated prognostic utility across multiple malignancies; however, their specific role in predicting recurrence patterns in endometrial cancer remains inadequately characterized. Notably, the Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index (ALI), a novel host-related biomarker, has not yet been evaluated in this context.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 687 patients with endometrial cancer treated between 2010 and 2020. Pretreatment inflammatory markers, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), and ALI, were calculated based on routine laboratory data. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the optimal cut-off values for these markers. Multivariate logistic regression and multinomial regression were employed to assess predictors of recurrence and recurrence patterns, respectively. The C-index was used to evaluate the discriminative ability of the prediction models.
RESULTS: Over a median 52-month follow-up, 127 patients (18.5%) recurred. Optimal cut-offs: NLR > 2.45, PLR > 158, LMR ≤ 3.85, NPAR > 11.2, ALI ≤ 45.6. Multivariate analysis identified NLR (OR = 2.18), PLR (OR = 1.67), LMR (OR = 1.75), and ALI (OR = 2.42) as independent predictors (all p < 0.008). NLR was more predictive in early-stage disease (interaction p = 0.032). Distinct patterns emerged: NLR predicted distant recurrence (RRR = 3.12), PLR was associated with local recurrence (RRR = 2.03), and ALI was associated with recurrence across all sites (local RRR = 1.82; regional RRR = 2.21; distant RRR = 3.45). The host-related biomarker model demonstrated superior discrimination (C-index = 0.821) versus FIGO staging alone (0.718, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-treatment inflammatory markers independently predict endometrial cancer recurrence with distinct site-specific patterns. ALI is a promising composite host-related biomarker that significantly improves risk stratification, offering a foundation for the design of prospective studies of personalized surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Prenatal phthalate exposure and early childhood asthma: a prospective birth cohort study from the Japan Environment and Children's study.
articles.authors: Oba K, Iwata H, Yamaguchi T et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal phthalate exposure has been associated with allergic outcomes; however, evidence linking it to childhood asthma remains inconsistent. Using data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS), we examined the association between prenatal phthalate exposure measured during the first and second/third trimesters and current asthma in early childhood.
METHODS: Among 9,707 mother-child pairs with urinary phthalate measurements in both the first and second/third trimesters, 8,554, 8,048, and 7,722 singleton children with available asthma data were analyzed at ages 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. Current asthma was defined as wheezing in the past 12 months together with caregiver-reported physician-diagnosed asthma during that period (or ongoing asthma treatment). In the primary analyses, first-trimester, second/third-trimester, and average concentrations were analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for maternal allergy or asthma history, smoking, education, household income, parity, and recruitment center, with multiple imputation and false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional analyses included sex stratification, generalized estimating equations, mutually adjusted trimester-specific models, alternative asthma definitions, and quantile g-computation.
RESULTS: Current asthma prevalence was 6.4, 5.8, and 4.4% at 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. In the primary analyses, no associations remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Similarly, generalized estimating equation and quantile g-computation analyses showed no significant overall associations after FDR correction. In additional analyses after FDR correction, the average monomethyl phthalate (MMP) concentration was positively associated with International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC)-defined asthma at age 2, while first-trimester and average MMP concentrations were positively associated with later-confirmed age-2 asthma. These findings were not consistently observed across ages or analytic approaches.
CONCLUSION: Prenatal phthalate exposure was not consistently associated with current asthma in early childhood in this large Japanese birth cohort. Although certain MMP associations emerged in secondary and sensitivity analyses, the overall pattern of findings did not support a robust association.

articles.title: Scottish health and social care professionals knowledge and attitudes towards prenatal alcohol exposure and fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
articles.authors: McDougall S, Brown RH, Shields J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Awareness and knowledge of FASD among health and social care professionals remains low. As Scotland integrates FASD into neurodevelopmental pathways, assessing staff knowledge is vital to guide future training and ensure equitable diagnostic access.
METHOD: An online survey was employed, assessing respondents' FASD-related knowledge and attitudes, was distributed to health and social care professionals across Scotland through NHS Health Boards and Health and Social Care Partnerships.
RESULTS: A total of 897 staff completed the questionnaire, of whom 60% reporting receiving no FASD training, with only 11% very familiar with FASD. Medical doctors and psychologists reported higher training rates. Training and direct experience with FASD correlated with greater knowledge and fewer stigmatising beliefs. Lack of training was associated with more negative attitudes.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant gaps in FASD knowledge persist, especially outside specialist groups. Targeted and widespread training is needed training is needed to identify potential cases, reduce stigma, and ensure equitable, informed care in Scotland.

articles.title: One size does not fit all: a qualitative descriptive study on Swedish midwives' perceptions of fertility education for young people.
articles.journal: Sexual & reproductive healthcare : official journal of the Swedish Association of Midwives
articles.authors: Stern J, Grandahl M, Cato K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fertility awareness is a cornerstone of public health. For young people, such awareness is essential for making informed sexual and reproductive choices, empowering them to use their rights in deciding if, when, and how to form a family. However, little is known about the challenges and opportunities related to fertility awareness among young people attending youth health clinics. Therefore, this study aimed to explore midwives' perceptions of fertility education directed at young people.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive design using focus group interviews (N = 5) with 23 midwives working at youth health clinics in Sweden.
RESULTS: The overarching theme "Fertility education for young people: a crucial piece of the puzzle - but 'one size' does not fit all" reflects midwives' perceptions regarding barriers and facilitators to fertility education among young people. It emphasises the importance of providing fertility education, while at the same time recognizing the varying receptivity and needs among young people. It highlights the essential role of empowering young individuals to make informed decisions and addressing knowledge gaps. Finally, it acknowledges the importance of tailored support for diverse groups of young people and the need for a delicate approach to fertility education.
CONCLUSION: Midwives considered fertility awareness among young people important at both individual and societal levels. Young people were described as wanting fertility education, and the midwives viewed this as a relevant and meaningful part of their professional role. Future research should explore long term outcomes and investigate best practises as well as strategies for effective implementation.

articles.title: Reference ranges of the fetal ductus arteriosus area by Three-Dimensional ultrasonography.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Simioni C, Peixoto AB, Callado GY et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine reference values for the fetal ductus arteriosus (DA) area using three-dimensional (3D) ultrasonography with spatio-temporal image correlation (STIC) in the rendering and multiplanar modes.
METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted with 322 cardiac volumes from normal fetuses between 20 and 33 + 6 weeks. DA area measurements were performed in the multiplanar (sagittal B-plane) and rendering modes. Polynomial regression models were fitted and assessed using the coefficient of determination (R2). Reproducibility was assessed by the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman plots, and agreement between modes by Bland-Altman analysis and least products regression.
RESULTS: Patient age ranged from 18 to 45 years, with a median of 29.0 years. The median gestational age at the time of the ultrasound examination was 26.6 weeks (20.0-33.9 weeks). A linear relationship and a significant strong positive correlation were observed between gestational age and DA area measurements in the multiplanar and rendering modes (R2 = 0.54 and 0.53, respectively). Mean DA areas in the multiplanar and rendering modes ranged from 0.06 to 0.32 cm2 and 0.07 to 0.37 cm2, respectively. Intra- and interobserver reliability was good (CCC ≥ 0.72), but relative limits of agreement were wide. The rendering mode yielded larger areas (mean difference -0.028 cm2).
CONCLUSION: Reference curves for the fetal DA area by 3D ultrasonography with STIC in the multiplanar and rendering modes were determined and showed a strong correlation with gestational age. These measurements showed good reliability but wide limits of agreement; the two modes are not interchangeable, and their clinical usefulness remains to be established.

articles.title: Follitropin delta versus human menopausal gonadotropin in progestin protocol cycles: a retrospective cohort study using inverse probability of treatment weighting.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Fujii T, Iwami N, Takimoto K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether follitropin delta (FD), administered using an individualized dosing algorithm, improves cumulative ongoing pregnancy compared with human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) in progestin protocol (PP) cycles.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of 716 progestin protocol (PP) stimulation cycles (382 FD, 334 hMG) at one center (oocyte retrieval April 2022-January 2024; follow-up to July 2024). All started cycles reached retrieval. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was the primary analysis; 1:1 propensity score matching was a sensitivity analysis. The primary outcome was cumulative ongoing pregnancy per retrieval (per started cycle) from all frozen embryo transfers (FET).
RESULTS: After IPTW, covariates were balanced. FD yielded more retrieved oocytes than hMG (adjusted mean difference 2.11; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.57-3.65) with lower gonadotropin consumption; mature (MII) oocytes, fertilized oocytes, and blastocysts did not differ. At first FET (n = 558), hCG positivity was lower with FD (65.0% vs 74.6%; odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.98; P = 0.041); clinical pregnancy (51.6% vs 61.4%; P = 0.057) and ongoing pregnancy (39.4% vs 46.7%; P = 0.175) were numerically lower but not significantly so. Cumulative ongoing pregnancy per retrieval was similar (50.2% vs 50.5%; OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.66-1.47).
CONCLUSION(S): FD gave a higher oocyte yield with lower gonadotropin consumption than hMG, without a significant increase in MII oocytes or blastocysts. FD was associated with lower hCG positivity and numerically lower clinical pregnancy after the first FET, whereas cumulative ongoing pregnancy per retrieval did not differ significantly. Caution is warranted; prospective studies with live birth endpoints are needed.

articles.title: Heterogeneity of folate receptor alpha expression and associations with molecular biomarker in ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma: A multicenter Chinese cohort study.
articles.authors: Li F, Li D, Xi Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) is an established therapeutic target in ovarian cancer, but information on its expression distribution, staining heterogeneity, and molecular context in Chinese patients remains limited. We evaluated these features in ovarian high grade serous carcinoma (HGSC).
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 1002 patients with resected HGSC from 14 Chinese hospitals. FRα expression was assessed using the VENTANA FOLR1 (FOLR1-2.1) RxDx Assay based on the percentage of viable tumor cells with moderate or strong (2+/3+) membranous staining. Intensity specific percentages were available for 992 tumors. Associations with clinicopathologic features and BRCA1/2, HRD, TMB, MSI, MMR, HER2, and PD-L1 were exploratory. Temporal concordance was evaluated in 53 paired primary and recurrent tumors.
RESULTS: High FRα expression, defined as 2+/3+ staining in ≥75% of viable tumor cells, was observed in 435 of 1002 tumors (43.41%). Among 992 tumors with intensity data, 972 (98.0%) contained at least two staining categories, and 924 (93.1%) contained both negative or weak and moderate or strong tumor cell populations. No significant associations were detected with age, FIGO stage, tumor size, or the biomarkers evaluated, although analyses were limited and underpowered. Paired tumors showed 71.7% categorical agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.44) and moderate correlation of FRα percentages (Spearman ρ = 0.59).
CONCLUSIONS: FRα expression showed substantial variation between tumors and frequent intensity admixture within specimens. Biomarker associations remain inconclusive because of limited testing. Moderate primary and recurrent concordance supports archival testing, while discordance suggests repeat testing at recurrence may be appropriate in selected patients.

articles.title: Effect of short-term storage prior to vitrification on pregnancy rates of dromedary camel embryos.
articles.authors: Mulligan BP, Skidmore JA
articles.abstract: Short-term storage of embryos prior to cryopreservation may improve the logistical flexibility of dromedary camel embryo transfer (ET) programs. However, the impact of such storage on embryo cryotolerance remains unclear. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the effect of storing dromedary camel embryos for 24 h at either room temperature (RT) or 4 °C prior to vitrification on subsequent pregnancy rates following ET. A total of 60 Day-7 in vivo-derived embryos were assigned to one of three treatment groups: immediate vitrification without prior storage (NS, n = 20), storage at 4 °C for 24 h prior to vitrification (4C, n = 20), or storage at room temperature (RT, n = 20) for 24 h prior to vitrification. Within each group, embryos were further categorised according to diameter (<500 μm or ≥500 μm). Following warming, embryos were transferred in pairs to synchronized recipients and pregnancy establishment was assessed between days 18-20 and day 60 of gestation. The transfer of NS embryos produced pregnancy rates of 60% (6/10) at 18-20 days and 50% (5/10) at day 60. Transfer of embryos in the 4C group resulted in pregnancy rates of 40% (4/10) and 30% (3/10), respectively. In contrast, embryos stored at RT prior to vitrification failed to establish pregnancies (0/10). These findings demonstrate that while short-term cooling may be compatible with subsequent vitrification, storage at room temperature could severely compromise embryo cryotolerance.

articles.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitors in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer: Clinical disappointments, biological lessons, and the reopening of therapeutic opportunities.
articles.authors: Giudice E, Spinazzola A, Floudas CS et al.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of several malignancies; however, their efficacy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) remains limited. The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in ovarian cancer constitutes a major barrier to effective antitumor immunity, prompting the development of various strategies to enhance responsiveness to ICIs. This narrative review examines current therapeutic approaches targeting the TME to overcome resistance to ICIs in PROC, with a focus on angiogenesis, innate immunity, and adaptive immune pathways. Despite a strong biological rationale, most chemotherapy-free ICI-based combinations targeting specific immune or stromal components have shown limited and inconsistent clinical benefit. The most notable clinical activity has been observed when ICIs are combined with chemotherapy, particularly in regimens that include anti-angiogenic agents. Recent positive results from a single phase 3 trial evaluating pembrolizumab in combination with weekly paclitaxel, with or without bevacizumab, mark a notable deviation from the predominantly negative outcomes of earlier studies. Nevertheless, it remains uncertain whether this result represents a true paradigm shift or a context-specific effect. Currently, no validated predictive biomarkers exist to reliably identify patients most likely to benefit from ICI-based strategies. The discrepancy between the isolated success of chemo-immunotherapy combinations and the failure of most previous trials highlights the need for further investigation into TME biology. A more comprehensive understanding of TME dynamics and the development of biomarker-driven patient selection strategies will be essential to define the role of ICIs in this challenging clinical context.

articles.title: Metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, a fatty-liver proxy, inflammation, and apolipoproteins in relation to breast cancer risk in young Korean women: A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Lee KH, Kim EY, Park CH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Greater adiposity is associated with higher postmenopausal but lower premenopausal breast cancer risk; whether its metabolic consequences - insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and atherogenic lipoproteins - follow the same pattern is unresolved. Apolipoproteins, which track with adiposity, have not to our knowledge been evaluated prospectively for premenopausal breast cancer risk in East Asia. We examined these markers in relation to incident breast cancer in Korean women.
METHODS: We followed 99,648 Korean women (91.3% premenopausal) without prior breast cancer attending health screening during 2011-2024. Prespecified exposures were metabolic syndrome component count, the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), a fatty-liver proxy, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and the apolipoprotein B (ApoB) to apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) ratio. Incident breast cancer was ascertained by registry linkage (ICD-10 C50 plus D05). Age-stratified Cox models used sequential adjustment; the primary model included reproductive, anthropometric, and lifestyle covariates.
RESULTS: Over a median 7.75 years of follow-up, 1094 incident breast cancers occurred (28.1% in situ). In the primary model, metabolic syndrome component count (hazard ratio 1.05 per component, 95% CI 0.97-1.14), HOMA-IR (1.01 per log unit, 0.91-1.12), and hs-CRP (0.98 per log unit, 0.90-1.06) were not associated with breast cancer risk; the fatty-liver estimate was uninformative (38 exposed cases). The ApoB/ApoA1 ratio (0.94 per 1 SD, 0.88-1.00) and ApoB (0.94, 0.88-1.00) were inversely but not significantly associated, both attenuating to the null in a 3-year landmark analysis (0.99, 0.92-1.07). ApoB and LDL cholesterol were near-collinear (r = 0.944), precluding specificity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and apolipoprotein markers were not associated with breast cancer risk in this predominantly premenopausal Korean cohort. These sequelae therefore do not appear to share the inverse association adiposity shows before menopause. These are, to our knowledge, the first prospective apolipoprotein data on premenopausal breast cancer risk in East Asian women.

articles.title: What are the barriers and facilitators to engagement with physiotherapy among women experiencing adverse effects associated with menopause?
articles.authors: Gross J, Stephens G, Soundy A
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Menopause typically begins in the 40 s (perimenopause) with adverse effects such as hot flushes, fatigue, and musculoskeletal (MSK) pain affecting 80% of women. Declining hormones during menopause can reduce bone density, muscle strength, and joint health, contributing to MSK pain, reported in up to 85% of women. Physiotherapists play a key role in the management of MSK pain; however, menopause-related effects including fatigue and low self-efficacy can hinder NHS physiotherapy engagement.
OBJECTIVES: To explore the experiences of women attending NHS physiotherapy in the UK for musculoskeletal pain while experiencing adverse effects associated with menopause, and to identify barriers and facilitators to engagement with physiotherapy.
DESIGN: A qualitative study utilising semi-structured interviews. Reflexive thematic analysis was performed.
SETTING: A single NHS elective orthopaedic hospital in the UK.
PARTICIPANTS: Twelve participants were recruited via an electronic poster and a staff menopause support group.
RESULTS: Two main themes were identified: Biopsychosocial impact of menopause-related adverse effects and considerations for physiotherapists. Common barriers to physiotherapy were fatigue, cognitive issues, low self-efficacy and negative language used by healthcare professionals. Participants identified direct enquiry about menopause and feeling listened to as facilitators of engagement. Individualised treatment strategies and education were reported as recommendations to foster rapport and engagement.
CONCLUSIONS: Women experiencing adverse effects associated with menopause and MSK pain often experience uncertainty about the causes of their health concerns and feel their needs are not fully met by physiotherapists. Direct enquiry, individualised care plans and education may improve engagement and enhance therapeutic relationships. Physiotherapists are well-positioned to support women through this important transition, but specific training may be required to enhance their knowledge and skills in supporting women experiencing menopause and MSK pain. CONTRIBUTION OF PAPER.

articles.title: National trends in menopausal hormone therapy use in Denmark, 1999-2025.
articles.authors: Socha PM, Pedersen AT, Christensen J et al.
articles.abstract: We describe trends in the use of menopausal hormone therapy in Denmark, using data on medication sales from all pharmacies, from 1999 to 2025. Between 2001 and 2013, the proportion of females aged 45-64 who purchased systemically-acting menopausal hormone therapies fell from 20% to 4%. After a decade of consistently low use, purchasing of systemically-acting therapies increased in 2024 and was 8% in 2025. Purchasing of locally-acting (i.e., vaginal) therapies increased throughout the study period, from 5% to 11%. We expect these upward trends to continue in response to growing interest as well as guidelines aimed at supporting decision-making.

articles.title: Association of sinonasal symptoms with health-related quality of life in peri- and postmenopausal women.
articles.authors: García-Alfaro P, Pérez-López FR, Solé GB et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The menopausal transition is characterized by a progressive decline in estrogen levels. This can trigger physiological alterations in the sinonasal mucosa and potentially lead to the development of sinonasal symptoms affecting women's quality of life. Our study examines associations between scores on the Sinonasal Outcome Test-22 (SNOT-22) and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in peri- and postmenopausal women without chronic rhinosinusitis.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey, conducted via the REDCap database, was offered by email to women aged ≥40 years. A total of 901 women were eligible for participation. The survey instrument covered: i) age, menopause status, age at menopause, smoking status, diagnosis of chronic rhinosinusitis or prior nasal surgery, use of medications (for arterial hypertension, hypothyroidism, depression, insomnia, allergies or asthma), use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs specifically, and use of menopausal hormone therapy; ii) the SNOT-22, which was included to evaluate sinonasal symptoms; and iii) the Cervantes Short-Form scale (Cervantes SF), to assess HRQoL.
RESULTS: The overall mean score on the SNOT-22 was 34.8 ± 18.7. There were significant differences in the SNOT-22 domains nasal (p = 0.003) and emotion (p = 0.008) between peri- and postmenopausal women. There were correlations between total SNOT-22 score and scores on the following Cervantes SF domains: 1, Menopause and health (r = 0.710; p < 0.001); 2, Psychological (r = 0.706; p < 0.001); 3, Sexuality (r = -0.091; p = 0.006); and 4, Couple relations (r = -0.129; p < 0.001). A higher SNOT-22 total score was independently associated with poorer HRQoL (β = 0.432; 95% CI = 0.399-0.465).
CONCLUSIONS: Both peri- and postmenopausal women without chronic rhinosinusitis had high scores on the SNOT-22 scale. There were differences between peri- and postmenopausal women in the SNOT-22 nasal and emotion domains. There was an independent association between a higher SNOT-22 total score and a poor HRQoL.

articles.title: Associations of longitudinal patterns of central obesity and chronic low-grade inflammation with incident frailty in middle-aged and older adults.
articles.authors: Chen X, Bu Z, Xu P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is a common geriatric syndrome associated with adverse health outcomes. Although central obesity and chronic low-grade inflammation have both been linked to frailty, their long-term patterns and combined effects remain unclear.
METHODS: Data were obtained from 7075 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Waist circumference measured in 2011 and 2015 was used to identify longitudinal patterns by K-means clustering, while C-reactive protein levels measured in 2011 and 2015 were classified as low-low, low-high, high-low, and high-high (with 2 mg/L as the threshold between low and high). Frailty was assessed in 2018 and 2020 using the Frailty Index. Logistic regression, cross-lagged analysis, and network analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Compared with low waist circumference, high waist circumference was associated with an increased risk of frailty (OR 1.44; 95% CI 1.20-1.72). Compared with the low-low C-reactive protein group, the low-high (OR 1.26; 95% CI 1.07-1.48) and high-high (OR 1.30; 95% CI 1.06-1.59) groups had higher frailty risks. Participants with high waist circumference combined with low-high or high-high C-reactive protein showed the greatest frailty risk. Cross-lagged analysis suggested a stronger temporal association between waist circumference to subsequent changes in level of C-reactive protein, while network analysis identified physical function and disabilities in activities and instrumental activities of daily living as the central frailty components.
CONCLUSION: Long-term high waist circumference and persistently or newly elevated C-reactive protein were independently and jointly associated with frailty. These findings highlight the importance of monitoring long-term changes in central obesity and inflammatory status for early identification of individuals at high risk of frailty.

articles.title: Exploring post-traumatic growth in women experiencing infertility: levels and mechanisms.
articles.authors: Niu C, Yu Y, Xie Y et al.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: Does post-traumatic growth occur in women experiencing infertility, and what mechanisms underlie its development, particularly regarding the roles of self-disclosure and rumination?
DESIGN: Mixed-methods design. Semi-structured interviews explored lived experiences of post-traumatic growth with 12 patients. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 258 women using the Chinese versions of the Post-traumatic Growth Inventory, Distress Disclosure Index and Event-Related Rumination Inventory. Group comparisons, multiple linear regression and Pearson correlation analyses were conducted. Structural equation modelling with bootstrapping tested the mediating role of deliberate rumination.
RESULTS: Qualitative analysis identified three main themes and seven sub-themes, encompassing emotional responses, factors that may create conditions for growth, and manifestations of post-traumatic growth. Quantitative findings indicated that overall levels of post-traumatic growth, self-disclosure and rumination were moderate, with deliberate rumination being particularly prominent. Age, educational level and self-perceived personality orientation (exploratory variable), along with monthly household income and co-residence with parents, were significantly associated with post-traumatic growth (each P < 0.05). Both self-disclosure and deliberate rumination were positively correlated with post-traumatic growth (P < 0.01). Multiple linear regression analysis further identified self-disclosure and deliberate rumination as significant positive predictors of post-traumatic growth (each P < 0.001). Furthermore, structural equation modelling revealed that deliberate rumination partially mediated the relationship between self-disclosure and post-traumatic growth, accounting for 10.54% of the total effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Women experiencing infertility can achieve post-traumatic growth despite psychological distress. Self-disclosure promotes post-traumatic growth directly and indirectly via deliberate rumination, highlighting modifiable cognitive mechanisms that may inform psychological interventions in reproductive care.

articles.title: LMOD1 expression and survival in uterine leiomyosarcoma: discordant results in tissue microarrays and whole sections.
articles.authors: Davidson B, Holth A, Horni Gløersen G
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leiomodin 1 (LMOD1) was previously reported to be associated with longer survival in leiomyosarcoma (LMS) in analysis combining uterine and non-uterine tumors. The objective of the present study was to analyze the expression and prognostic role of LMOD1 in a large series of exclusively uterine LMS (uLMS).
METHODS: LMOD1 protein expression by immunohistochemistry was analyzed in tissue microarrays (TMAs) from 244 uLMS and whole sections from 203 uLMS, of which 134 were included in both series. Expression was assessed for association with clinicopathologic parameters and disease-specific survival (DSS).
RESULTS: TMAs were informative in 221/244 (91%) tumors, of which 100 (45%) expressed LMOD1. No significant association with DSS was observed for 156 patients with clinical data. In the series stained using whole sections, LMOD1 was expressed in 142/203 (70%) tumors, and higher expression was associated with significantly longer survival (203 patients with survival data; p=0.007). Other parameters related to survival in the latter series were FIGO stage (p<0.001), tumor diameter (p<0.001), mitotic count (p<0.001), the degree of atypia (p=0.006) and lymphovascular invasion (LVSI; p=0.006). In Cox multivariate analysis, FIGO stage (p<0.001), mitotic count (p<0.001), tumor diameter (p=0.001) and LMOD1 expression (p=0.003) were independent prognosticators.
CONCLUSIONS: LMOD1 expression in whole sections is a new candidate marker of longer survival in uLMS. This study additionally highlights the limitations associated with use of TMA sections compared to whole sections in biomarker studies.

articles.title: Bisphenol A induces ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury: Implications for Hunner-type interstitial cystitis.
articles.authors: Wu W, Xu Y, Lu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Hunner-type interstitial cystitis (HIC) is an inflammatory subtype of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome marked by persistent urothelial injury and bladder dysfunction. Bisphenol A (BPA) can disturb redox and inflammatory homeostasis, but its relevance to HIC-associated urothelial vulnerability remains unclear. This study examined whether acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) contributes to BPA-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury. Among non-pregnant adult women, higher creatinine-corrected urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype predominantly characterized by urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), and the primary Mendelian randomization analysis suggested higher interstitial cystitis (IC) risk with genetically proxied BPA exposure. Integrated transcriptomic, BPA-target, and machine-learning analyses prioritized ACSL4 as a consistent HIC-associated candidate. HIC tissues showed higher ferro-aging-like transcriptional scores and ACSL4 expression; single-cell analyses further identified disease-associated urothelial cell-state remodeling, with higher ACSL4 expression and SenePy scores in HIC urothelial cells. Structure-based modeling suggested a plausible BPA-ACSL4 interaction, while cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) indicated BPA-associated thermal stabilization of ACSL4. In primary human urothelial cells, BPA increased ACSL4 mRNA and protein expression, lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, p21 expression, senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) positivity, inflammatory signaling, and barrier impairment, together with reduced Lamin B1 and ZO-1 expression and transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER). ACSL4 silencing and vitamin C attenuated these changes. In mice, PRGL493 and vitamin C each attenuated multiple BPA-induced bladder abnormalities. Together, these findings support an ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury phenotype involving iron-lipid stress, senescence-associated changes, inflammation, and barrier impairment, with relevance to selected features of HIC.

articles.title: PARP Inhibitors in the Management of Ovarian Cancer: ASCO Living Guideline, Version 2026.1.0.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.authors: Tew WP, Lacchetti C, Adams TS et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This living guideline provides recommendations on the use of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) in the management of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC).
METHODS: An Expert Panel developed recommendations based on a systematic review of randomized controlled trials, and cohort studies evaluating homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing and PARPi efficacy and safety.
RESULTS: The updated evidence base comprises 79 publications, including 18 studies evaluating 13 homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) assays and 31 pivotal trials assessing PARPi efficacy and safety. Frontline trials demonstrated progression-free survival benefits. However, later-line treatment and recurrent maintenance trials reported potential overall survival disadvantages.
RECOMMENDATIONS: All patients with newly diagnosed advanced EOC should undergo genetic testing, and HRD tumor testing if BRCA-negative, using FDA-approved or prospectively validated companion diagnostic assays. In advanced EOC, PARPi maintenance should be prioritized for the first clinical remission. Frontline PARPi monotherapy maintenance should be offered after platinum-based chemotherapy response to patients with germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations or HRD-positive disease. Olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance may be offered to patients responding to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy plus bevacizumab who have BRCA1/2 mutations or HRD-positive disease. PARPi maintenance therapy is not recommended for patients with non-BRCAmut HRD-negative tumors or early-stage EOC. In the recurrent setting, PARPi maintenance should be restricted primarily to PARPi-naïve patients with BRCA1/2 mutations responding to second-line or greater platinum-based chemotherapy. Monotherapy PARPi should not be offered for the treatment of recurrent EOC outside clinical trials.
