Furthermore, PARPi are not recommended for use in combination with chemotherapy, other targeted agents, or immune-oncology agents outside a clinical trial. Clinicians should monitor for serious adverse events, including myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, and pulmonary complications.

articles.title: Modeling the U.S. National Burden of Severe Hemolytic Disease of the Fetus and Newborn.
articles.authors: Abels EA, Louie JZ, Jacobs JW et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the national burden of severe hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) attributed to the three most clinically significant alloantibodies (anti-D, anti-K, and anti-c) using a large data set of prenatal antibody screens in U.S. pregnancies.
METHODS: Prenatal red blood cell alloantibody results were extracted from a national laboratory firm from 2010 to 2021 and normalized to the U.S. population race, ethnicity, and regional distributions based on Census data. Prevalence of critical alloantibody titers, pregnancy continuation rates, distribution of paternal race and ethnicity, allele prevalence of antigen in paternal race and ethnicity, and rate of disease were used to estimate the burden of disease using Monte Carlo simulations.
RESULTS: There were 8,809,993 pregnancies included in the cohort. Normalization of the cohort to U.S. births resulted in an estimated national prevalence of any high-risk antibodies of 686.5 per 100,000 pregnancies (27.9 per 100,000 for anti-c, 596.1 per 100,000 for anti-D, and 62.5 per 100,000 for anti-K), with 63.9 per 100,000 (1.9 for anti-c, 20.6 for anti-D, and 41.3 for anti-K) of those reaching critical levels. The estimated national burden of severe HDFN attributed to any high-risk antibody was 2.4 per 100,000 pregnancies (95% CI, 2.0-2.9). Among all pregnancies with critical titers, 3.8% (95% CI, 3.1-4.5) were estimated to result in severe HDFN.
CONCLUSION: This study provides contemporary national estimates of severe HDFN in the United States, demonstrating that, although alloimmunization is relatively common, progression to severe HDFN remains rare.

articles.title: Antidepressant Discontinuation During Pregnancy and Risk of Mental Health-Related Emergencies.
articles.authors: Zafman KB, Zhu Y, Kornfield SL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate contemporary patterns of antidepressant discontinuation during pregnancy and associated maternal mental health outcomes, including behavioral health-related emergency department (ED) visits, among patients with preexisting depression or anxiety.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of a state-based private insurance claims database in Pennsylvania. Patients who delivered between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, with a diagnosis of depression or anxiety before pregnancy and an active prescription for a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) in the 3 months before pregnancy were included. The exposure was antidepressant continuation compared with discontinuation during pregnancy, defined as no prescription fills or a gap of more than 60 days. The primary outcome was behavioral health-related ED visits during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Behavioral health-related ED visit rates were compared between patients who continued and those who discontinued antidepressants with appropriate bivariate statistical tests.
RESULTS: Among 3,983 patients with depression or anxiety, 1,462 (36.7%) entered pregnancy with an active SSRI or SNRI prescription. Of these, 260 (17.8%) had no medication fills during pregnancy, and 945 (64.6%) had a gap of more than 60 days. Among patients with a treatment gap of more than 60 days, discontinuation occurred most commonly in the first trimester (44.9%) followed by the third trimester (30.3%). Patients who continued and those who discontinued treatment had similar rates of outpatient and ED mental health visits before pregnancy. However, discontinuation was associated with a higher risk of mental health-related emergency visits during pregnancy, with peaks in the second month (58 vs 37/1,000, P=.027) and the ninth month (59 vs 29/1,000, P<.01) of pregnancy. This increased risk persisted postpartum, with higher rates of mental health-related ED visits within 8 months after delivery among those who discontinued treatment during pregnancy (32 vs 21/1,000, P=.02).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of privately insured patients with preexisting depression or anxiety, antidepressant discontinuation during pregnancy was common and was associated with increased risk of mental health-related ED visits. These findings underscore the need for clinical and policy strategies to support continuation of evidence-based treatment for perinatal mental…

articles.title: Anti-Müllerian Hormone Trajectories Across the Menopause Transition.
articles.authors: Acharya KS, Bozzuto L, Kaizer LK et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the trajectory of anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) decline leading to the final menstrual period, identify distinct AMH patterns, and assess their association with unique participant characteristics.
METHODS: SWAN (Study of Women's Health Across the Nation), a multisite, multiethnic perimenopausal cohort, was analyzed. Included participants had an observed final menstrual period and three or more measurements of AMH levels taken during perimenopause. Statistical modeling was used to identify AMH trajectory classes; participants were placed into predicted class based on best fit. Differences in baseline demographic and health characteristics were assessed by analysis of variance or χ2. Generalized estimating equation models were used to estimate the association between AMH trajectory class and outcomes, accounting for repeated measures.
RESULTS: A total of 1,131 women had at least three AMH measurements and an observed final menstrual period. Two AMH trajectory classes were observed: 448 participants (39.6%) with lower initial AMH and slower decline (low/slow [LS] group) and 683 participants (60.4%) with higher AMH and steeper decline (high/fast [HF] group). Participants in the LS group had a median AMH decline of 1.2 pg/mL/month; those in the HF group had a decline of 6.7 pg/mL/month. The LS classification was associated with baseline older age, higher body mass index (BMI), and non-White race and ethnicity. Trajectory classes did not differ by history of oligomenorrhea, presumptive polycystic ovarian syndrome, or smoking status. Participants in the LS group had worse postmenopausal cardiovascular risk profiles and were less likely to report frequent vasomotor symptoms after the final menstrual period.
CONCLUSION: Two different AMH trajectories to the final menstrual period were observed in a subsample of SWAN participants. Independent of a participant's premenopausal cardiovascular risk factors, lower starting AMH and slower decline were associated with higher postmenopausal cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Risk Factors and Associated Severe Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality at Cesarean Delivery for the Second Twin.
articles.authors: Attali I, Goffinet F, Sentilhes L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between cesarean delivery for the second twin after vaginal delivery of the first twin and severe neonatal morbidity and mortality in comparison with vaginal delivery, and, secondarily, to identify risk factors for second twin cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This was a planned secondary analysis of the JUMODA (JUmeaux MODe d'Accouchement) cohort, a national prospective population-based study of twin deliveries conducted from February 2014 to March 2015 in 176 French maternities. For this analysis, we included only second twins born after vaginal delivery of the first twin at a gestational of at least 32 weeks. The primary outcome was severe neonatal morbidity and mortality. The association of cesarean delivery for the second twin with severe neonatal morbidity and mortality in the total population was estimated from multivariate Poisson regression models. A sensitivity analysis limited to pregnancies that mirrored the Twin Birth Study low-risk population was conducted. Candidate risk factors were evaluated for cesarean delivery for the second twin.
RESULTS: Among the 3,905 second twins included in analysis, 124 (3.2%) were delivered by cesarean and 3,781 (96.8%) were delivered vaginally. Cesarean delivery for the second twin was associated with severe neonatal morbidity and mortality compared with vaginal delivery (n=11/24 [8.9%] vs n=95/3,781 [2.5%]; adjusted relative risk [aRR] 3.17, 95% CI, 1.58-6.40). Findings were similar in the low-risk population (n=8/106 [7.5%] vs n=62/3,230 [1.9%]; aRR 4.03, 95% CI, 1.97-8.24). Absence of locoregional analgesia (aRR 2.13, 95% CI, 1.18-2.86), transverse second twin presentation (aRR 2.11, 95% CI, 1.44-3.08), and delivery in centers that performed fewer than 50 twin deliveries per year (aRR 1.58, 95% CI, 1.01-2.48) were associated with increased risk of cesarean delivery for the second twin. Conversely, breech second twin presentation was a protective factor (aRR 0.47, 95% CI, 0.27-0.82).
CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of twin deliveries that involved vaginal delivery of the first twin, cesarean delivery for the second twin tripled the risk of severe neonatal morbidity and mortality when compared with vaginal delivery. Results should be interpreted with caution because of the small number of events and potential residual confounding.

articles.title: Evolving treatment approaches for postpartum depression: The role of neuroactive steroids.
articles.authors: Theroux JD, Carter C, Sayed F et al.
articles.abstract: This article embarks on a journey through recent advances in postpartum depression (PPD), specifically focusing on rapid-acting neuroactive steroids, the first medications approved specifically for PPD.

articles.title: Pregnancy Outcomes and Long-Term Kidney Function in Women with Primary Glomerulonephritis.
articles.authors: Gulseren UA, Mirioglu S, Oto OA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether pregnancy accelerates long-term kidney function decline in women with primary glomerulonephritis remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate maternal and fetal outcomes and the long-term course of kidney function in women with primary glomerulonephritis.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study analyzed 40 pregnancies in 31 women with biopsy-proven primary glomerulonephritis (1996-2022). A control group of nulliparous women with primary glomerulonephritis, matched for subtype, age at diagnosis, and disease duration, was included. Obstetric and neonatal outcomes were evaluated alongside longitudinal kidney parameters assessed before, during, and up to 60 months postpartum.
RESULTS: Common diagnoses were focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (32.3%) and IgA nephropathy (25.8%). Mean maternal age was 29.6±4.1 years. Preeclampsia occurred in 15% and preterm birth in 50% of pregnancies (mean birth weight: 2819±859 g). During pregnancy, serum creatinine decreased and eGFR increased (p<0.001). Postpartum, serum creatinine returned to baseline, showing no significant differences at 6, 12, or 60 months. Although eGFR at 60 months was lower than pre-pregnancy levels, serum creatinine remained comparable to baseline and no significant differences in kidney function parameters were observed between the pregnancy and control groups at 60 months. The clinical significance of the isolated reduction in calculated eGFR therefore remains uncertain.
CONCLUSIONS: In women with primary glomerulonephritis and predominantly early-stage kidney disease, physiological kidney adaptation during pregnancy is largely preserved. No clear acceleration in long-term kidney function decline was observed compared with matched controls; however, an adverse effect of pregnancy cannot be excluded. Preeclampsia and preterm delivery remain significant, requiring monitoring.

articles.title: Toward Safer Regenerative, Functional, and Aesthetic Gynecology: A Clinical Governance Framework for Patient Safety.
articles.journal: Journal of lower genital tract disease
articles.authors: Sánchez-Borrego R, Alinsod R, Bader A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Regenerative, functional, and aesthetic gynecology has expanded rapidly, yet discussions about complications remain focused on individual technologies rather than the clinical decisions that determine procedural safety. This review proposes a multidimensional clinical governance framework for complication prevention in this subspecialty.
METHODS: A narrative review was based on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase (January 2014-May 2026), supplemented by international guidelines, regulatory communications, and evidence syntheses. Forty-two sources were included in the final qualitative synthesis. Evidence was appraised by study design, methodological rigor, clinical relevance, consistency, and applicability. The preliminary framework underwent successive rounds of multidisciplinary expert review, substantive textual and conceptual revision, and approval by all authors.
RESULTS: Adverse outcomes arise from the convergence of 3 interdependent domains: patient-related factors (hormonal status, tissue quality, expectations, psychological context), clinician-related factors (diagnostic accuracy, anatomic expertise, endocrine competence, willingness to decline intervention), and procedural variables (technique, standardization, follow-up). When present, genitourinary syndrome of menopause represents a potentially modifiable biologic risk factor that should be identified and appropriately managed before restorative intervention is considered. A structured 5-component clinical evaluation framework integrating hormonal status, symptom profile, anatomic assessment, psychological context, and prior treatment history supports indication-based decision-making. Safety reflects both procedure-specific risk and patient-, clinician-, and protocol-related factors.
CONCLUSIONS: Complication prevention begins with clinical reasoning, not procedural selection. The credibility of this subspecialty will depend on rigorous patient selection, endocrine optimization when indicated, evidence-based indications, competency-based training, and robust clinical governance rather than on the continuous introduction of new technologies.

articles.title: First-trimester neurosonography of the fetal brain: when visualization outpaces biological interpretability.
articles.authors: Mace P, Meagher SE, Dawood Y et al.
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, first-trimester neurosonography has undergone a remarkable transformation. Advances in ultrasound technology, image resolution, transvaginal imaging, three-dimensional ultrasound, image post-processing, and operator expertise have considerably expanded assessment of the developing fetal brain between 11 and 14 weeks' gestation. Cerebral structures that were previously inaccessible can now be consistently visualized, extending the possibilities for earlier prenatal diagnosis (1). As imaging performance continues to improve, however, a new challenge has emerged. At this gestational age transient embryological structures coexist with definitive anatomy (2), and many cerebral structures can now be identified before they have reached sufficient anatomical maturity to allow reliable diagnostic interpretation. The question is therefore no longer simply how early the fetal brain can be imaged, but when developmental anatomy allows a structure that can be visualized to also be reliably interpreted, and when that interpretation becomes clinically actionable. This concept is illustrated throughout this review through three representative examples: first-trimester ventriculomegaly, the developing future cavum septi pellucidi, and cystic appearances of the posterior fossa. Although involving different anatomical regions, these entities share a common principle: the interpretation of early neurosonographic findings is intrinsically dependent on developmental stage and structural maturation. Rather than reviewing these entities as isolated diagnostic challenges, this article proposes a developmental perspective on first-trimester neurosonography. By integrating current imaging capabilities with the principles of embryological brain development, we explore how developmental biology increasingly defines the opportunities and the limits of early fetal brain assessment., and we propose practical points to guide assessment, follow-up, and counselling (Table 1).

articles.title: Projected obstetric risks in an aging maternal population in Taiwan: a Bayesian age-period-cohort analysis.
articles.authors: Chuang HM, Meng LC, Lai HY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed childbearing may alter maternal and neonatal risk profiles and potentially challenge current healthcare strategies. Therefore, we aimed to provide comprehensive Bayesian projections of pregnancy outcomes through 2050 to inform urgent healthcare system adaptation.
METHODS: We analysed all singleton pregnancies in Taiwan using linked data from National Health Insurance and Birth Certificate Application databases from 2004 to 2021. Temporal trends and age-stratified prevalence were assessed for maternal (gestational hypertension [GHTN], gestational diabetes mellitus [GDM], mortality, sepsis, and postpartum hemorrhage) and neonatal (stillbirth, preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age, and large for gestational age) outcomes. Bayesian age-period-cohort models were applied to project prevalence and absolute burden through 2050.
RESULTS: From 2004 to 2021, total pregnancies declined by 25.3%, while the proportion of pregnancies among women aged ≥35 years nearly tripled (11.8%-34.6%). GHTN prevalence rose from 0.4% to 2.1% and GDM from 2.0% to 9.3%. By 2050, GHTN and GDM are projected to reach 26.4% (95% credible interval [CrI], 5.2%-67.4%) and 60.9% (95% CrI, 28.9%-85.0%), respectively, while the GDM estimate should be interpreted in light of one-step screening adoption after 2010. Preterm birth and low birth weight are projected to increase modestly to 11.2% and 11.9%. BAPC modeling indicates these trends are associated with advancing maternal age and cohort patterns, reflecting evolving risk profiles shaped by shifting healthcare and behavioral practices.
CONCLUSIONS: Obstetric risk is shifting due to demographic and generational transitions, requiring prenatal care systems to adopt more proactive and routine management approaches.

articles.title: Aberrant mRNA 5-methylcytosine modification contributes to ovarian dysfunction in a rat model of polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.authors: Chen X, Lin J, Chi Z et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the altered landscape of messenger RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) methylation and the functional involvement of m5C-related regulators in a rat model of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
METHODS: A PCOS rat model was established by dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) induction, with the phenotype confirmed through estrous cycle monitoring, serum sex hormone analysis, and ovarian morphological assessment. Differentially m5C-methylated mRNAs were identified using an m5C epitranscriptomic microarray, and their associated biological pathways were predicted by KEGG analysis. Global m5C methylation levels and the expression and m5C enrichment of selected pathway-related genes were validated in ovarian tissues and isolated primary ovarian granulosa cells using dot blot, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation quantitative PCR (MeRIP-qPCR). The functional roles of TET2 and NSUN6 were further evaluated using shRNA-mediated knockdown, followed by analysis of PI3K/AKT-related signaling proteins, serum sex hormones, and ovarian histopathology.
RESULTS: m5C modifications were predominantly localized within coding sequences and 3' untranslated regions. Among 1,090 RNAs showing both differential m5C methylation and expression, 36 genes exhibited significant correlations between methylation and expression changes. Global mRNA m5C methylation was significantly elevated in the PCOS group. The m5C-related regulators Nsun6 and Tet2 showed increased m5C enrichment and significantly elevated protein expression. KEGG analysis linked the differentially modified transcripts to endocrine resistance and insulin-related signaling pathways. Tet2, Nsun6, Src, Pi3k, and Akt transcripts exhibited increased m5C enrichment in PCOS ovarian tissues and primary granulosa cells. Concurrently, SRC and PI3K protein expression was increased, whereas AKT protein expression was decreased in the PCOS group. Knockdown of TET2 and NSUN6 was confirmed at the mRNA and protein levels and differentially modulated PI3K/AKT-related protein expression and phosphorylation status, as assessed by PI3K, p-PI3K, AKT, and p-AKT levels. TET2 and NSUN6 knockdown also partially improved PCOS-associated abnormalities in serum FSH, LH, the LH/FSH ratio, testosterone, estradiol, and ovarian morphology.
CONCLUSION: This study reveals a significantly altered mRNA m5C methylation landscape in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model and primary ovarian granulosa cells. The…

articles.title: Causes of stillbirth in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia: Findings from Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance, 2016-2023.
articles.authors: Rahman A, Lee KH, Arifeen SE et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, an estimated 1.9 million stillbirths occur annually, yet significant knowledge gaps exist regarding the causes of stillbirths, particularly in high-burden regions. We investigated fetal and maternal conditions causing stillbirths in seven countries in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia and described missed opportunities for prevention.
METHODS: Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance (CHAMPS) identified stillbirths at sites in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Sierra Leone, and South Africa. We asked families for consent to conduct minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS) from December 2016 to December 2023. An expert panel reviewed test results, clinical information, and verbal autopsy data and assigned fetal and maternal conditions leading to stillbirths and identified missed opportunities for prevention.
FINDINGS: A cause of death (fetal or maternal condition) was determined for 94% (2342/2492) of stillbirths; the most frequent condition in the fetus was intrauterine hypoxia (75%, 1864/2492) across all sites, resulting from either maternal condition (49%, 922/1864) or placental causes (33%, 610/1864). Congenital infections were determined to be the cause of 9% (228/2492) of stillbirths, accounting for the highest proportion in South Africa (31%, 96/306). Group B Streptococcus, Escherichia coli, and Enterococcus faecalis were the most common causative pathogens. Congenital birth defects caused 9% (227/2492) overall and were most common in Ethiopia (24%, 136/568). Primary maternal conditions were identified in 72%, most often placental complications (18%, 446/2492) and maternal hypertension (17%, 414/2492). Complications of placenta, cord and membranes were more common in Mali (43%, 92/212) while maternal medical and surgical conditions were most frequently observed in South Africa (40%, 121/306) and Bangladesh (39%, 158/405). Most (72%, 1808/2492) causes of stillbirth were considered preventable, with heterogeneity observed across sites on the recommended prevention strategies.
INTERPRETATION: Complications of pregnancy or delivery accounted for most stillbirths across all sites, with intrauterine hypoxia identified as the predominant fetal condition highlighting widespread and persistent gaps in the timely identification and management of maternal and placental conditions during antenatal and obstetric care across sites in Africa and South Asia. At the same time, substantial geographic variation in causes…

articles.title: Factors associated with the optimal uptake of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine: The experiences of postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in three rural districts in the Western Region of Ghana.
articles.authors: Amugi G, Agudey DT, Gyimah NM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) is a key preventive strategy. However, optimal uptake remains inconsistent despite high antenatal care (ANC) attendance. This study assessed factors associated with optimal IPTp-SP uptake and explored the experiences of postpartum women in rural Ghana.
METHODS: A convergent parallel mixed-method study was conducted among 1,155 postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in Jomoro, Prestea-Huni Valley and Ellembelle districts of the Western Region of Ghana. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Qualitative data from in-depth interviews and focus group discussions were analysed thematically to explore women's experiences and perceptions.
RESULTS: Among the 1,155 women enrolled, 812 (70.3%) took three or more doses of IPTp-SP (IPTp3-SP). Knowledge of malaria in pregnancy was high, with 92.7% correctly identifying its mode of transmission and 91.7% identifying ways of preventing malaria during pregnancy. Factors independently associated with IPTp3-SP included age 10-19 years compared with 20-29 years (aOR 2.17, 95% CI 1.21-3.88), gravidity of three compared with one (aOR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.58-4.50), and gravidity of four compared with one (aOR 1.83, 95% CI: 1.02-3.28). Lower odds were observed among uninsured women (aOR 0.36, 95% CI: 0.20-0.64), single women (aOR 0.64, 95% CI: 0.42-0.97), and cohabiting women (aOR 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79). ANC attendance showed a strong association with IPTp3-SP: women attending <4 ANC visits had lower odds of receiving IPTp3-SP than those attending 10 or more visits (aOR 0.08, 95% CI: 0.04-0.15). Nausea, dizziness, weakness, abdominal discomfort, vomiting and difficulty chewing the tablets affected their experiences and, for some women, willingness to continue treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: IPTp-SP uptake was relatively high. Predictors of optimal uptake include age, education, marital status, gravidity, health insurance status, and number of ANC visits. Women with fewer ANC visits were less likely to receive three or more doses. Reported side effects posed barriers to adherence. Strengthening ANC attendance and counselling on IPTp-SP expected side effects may improve completion of recommended doses.

articles.title: Addressing unsafe abortion in India: A mixed-methods systematic review protocol.
articles.authors: Dhiman P, Gadapani Pathak B, Manna S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unsafe abortion remains a critical public health challenge globally and in India, despite the legal provision under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act for over 50 years. Multiple barriers -including limited access to trained providers, inequities in health facility readiness, stigma, poor awareness of legal entitlements, and widespread reliance on self-managed medical abortion- contribute to unsafe practices, which result in preventable maternal morbidity and mortality. Evidence on hazardous abortion in India is fragmented across facility-based studies, community surveys, and qualitative research. This protocol outlines methods for a mixed-methods systematic review integrating quantitative and qualitative data to comprehensively assess the prevalence of unsafe abortion, its determinants, associated morbidities, decision-making pathways, and the role of providers, methods, and settings.
METHODS: The review will include quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies conducted in India and published from 1972 onwards. Eligible quantitative designs include surveys, cross-sectional, cohort, case-control, quasi-experimental studies, randomised controlled trials, and hospital series with at least ten instances. Qualitative designs will include studies using interviews, focus groups, ethnography, or participatory approaches. Mixed-methods studies will be eligible if India-specific results can be extracted. The electronic databases to be searched include PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL supplemented by grey literature from WHO, UNFPA, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and other national sources. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data, and appraise quality. The Newcastle - Ottawa Scale will be used for observational studies, the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for trials, the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) or Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists for qualitative studies, and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) for mixed-methods studies. Quantitative data will be synthesised using random-effects meta-analysis, while qualitative findings will be analysed through thematic synthesis guided by abortion decision-making trajectories. Integration will follow a convergent segregated design.
DISCUSSION: This review will generate an integrated synthesis of unsafe abortion in India, including prevalence, morbidities, determinants, women's decision-making, and the contextual role of…

articles.title: Long-term abortion and birth rates for 14- to 25-year-olds before and after the implementation of prescription-free emergency contraceptives in Finland.
articles.authors: Luukkonen J, McEvoy O, Martikainen P et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Public health interventions increasing access to emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been deemed mostly unsuccessful in preventing abortions. However, the assessment of these interventions has mostly ignored potential variation in responses by age at intervention or socio-economic background.
METHODS: We used Finnish-population register data to assess annual abortion and live-birth rates for women aged 14-25 years during 1994-2010 by age and parental education. Changes in rates were assessed around the introduction of prescription-free ECs in 2002 with interrupted time-series regressions. We also assessed cohort-wise hazards of abortions and births by age 25 years for cohorts of 1980-94 (aged 8-22 years at the time of intervention).
RESULTS: After the introduction of prescription-free ECs, the increasing annual rates of abortions and live births turned into a clear decline for ages 15-19 years, with a less consistent decline for young people whose parents had low educational attainment. Conversely, the abortion rates continued to increase for ages 20-24 years, with larger increases by lower parental education. Comparing cohorts exposed to the intervention at different ages, we observed lower abortion and live-birth risks by age 19 years among the cohorts who were ≤15 years old at the time of the intervention.
CONCLUSION: The clear reversal in adolescent abortion rates suggests the prescription-free ECs worked as intended, but the intervention was far less successful among young adults and those with lower socio-economic background. Evaluations of public health interventions need to consider population subgroups.

articles.title: Chemotherapy-induced ovarian failure in females with Hodgkin lymphoma: current evidence and fertility preservation strategies.
articles.authors: Georgopoulou AN, Vassilakopoulos TP, Markantes GK et al.
articles.abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a highly curable malignancy and increasing survival rates have shifted attention towards long-term treatment-related complications, particularly infertility among young women of reproductive age. Chemotherapy-induced ovarian damage is a multifactorial process that may lead to diminished ovarian reserve, premature ovarian failure, and impaired fertility. Several distinct mechanisms contribute to ovarian injury. Direct DNA damage to primordial follicles is the best-characterized pathway, resulting in apoptosis and irreversible depletion of the follicular pool. Chemotherapy also affects granulosa cells and ovarian stromal tissue, disrupting the microenvironment necessary for follicular growth and hormone production. In addition, vascular injury characterized by endothelial dysfunction, reduced ovarian perfusion, and cortical fibrosis may compromise follicular survival and contribute to long-term ovarian dysfunction. More recently, dysregulation of the PI3K/PTEN/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway has emerged as an important mechanism, promoting accelerated activation and premature exhaustion of primordial follicles, a phenomenon known as the "burnout effect." These mechanisms frequently coexist and their relative contribution depends on treatment intensity, cumulative drug exposure, and patient-specific factors. Current fertility preservation strategies include oocyte, embryo, and ovarian tissue cryopreservation, while the uncertain efficacy of pharmacological ovarian suppression in HL highlights the need for further research into effective gonadoprotective approaches. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the biological mechanisms underlying chemotherapy-induced ovarian damage in women with HL and discusses their implications for fertility preservation and long-term reproductive health.

articles.title: Evaluation and Disposition of Potential Candidates for Uterine Transplantation: Experience From a Large Referral Center.
articles.authors: Ciomperlik HN, Alexander MV, Reding A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uterine transplantation (UTx) is an emerging surgical treatment for absolute uterine factor infertility. Given its complexity, careful patient selection and counseling are essential. We aimed to characterize patients expressing interest in UTx and identify common reasons for exclusion at a large referral center.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of individuals who self-referred for UTx and completed a standardized intake survey between April 2022 and April 2025 at a large academic center. Demographic, reproductive, medical, and psychosocial data were collected. Applications were reviewed by the transplant team, with additional phone screening when needed. The primary outcome was reason for exclusion from UTx candidacy.
RESULTS: During the 3-year study period, 371 intake surveys were received; 3 (0.8%) were incomplete. Causes of infertility included prior hysterectomy (79.6%), congenitally absent uterus (16.3%), and other etiologies (4.1%). Among 368 complete applications, 96.0% (353/368) were excluded. Reasons included age ≥ 40 years, BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, tobacco or illicit substance use, medical contraindications, severe mental health conditions, reproductive contraindications, self-withdrawal, and inability to comply with study requirements. The most common exclusions were medical contraindications (34%), age (18%), and BMI (17%).
CONCLUSIONS: Fewer than 2% of interested applicants ultimately qualify for UTx. While many criteria are nonmodifiable, addressing modifiable factors may improve candidacy and support informed counseling.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registration number- NCT05263076.

articles.title: Developmental Perturbation of the Kynurenine Pathway Shapes Adult Sensorimotor Processing and Behavioral Responses to Cannabinoid Receptor Activation.
articles.authors: Edoardo T, Bilel S, Bassi M et al.
articles.abstract: The kynurenine pathway (KP) plays a critical role in brain development by generating neuroactive metabolites that regulate glutamatergic and cholinergic neurotransmission. Although developmental disturbances of KP metabolism have been associated with long-term neurobehavioral abnormalities, it remains unclear whether early-life KP perturbation produces persistent alterations in adult sensorimotor function and behavioral responses to pharmacological challenges. In this study, we combined constitutive kynurenine 3-monooxygenase (KMO) deficiency with prenatal kynurenine (KYN) exposure to investigate their long-term effects on brain kynurenic acid (KYNA) concentrations, acoustic startle reactivity and prepulse inhibition (PPI) following acute administration of the cannabinoid receptor agonist JWH-018 in adult male wild-type (WT) and Kmo-/- mice. Constitutive KMO deficiency markedly increased adult brain KYNA concentrations, whereas prenatal KYN exposure (10 mg/dam/day) did not produce sustained elevations in whole-brain KYNA. Nevertheless, prenatal KYN exposure was associated with long-lasting alterations in sensorimotor function. Kmo-/- mice exhibited enhanced baseline acoustic startle reactivity and higher baseline PPI compared with WT mice. Prenatal KYN exposure attenuated the elevated baseline startle response observed in Kmo-/- mice, whereas its influence on baseline PPI was more limited. Following acute JWH-018 administration, changes in acoustic startle reactivity differed according to prenatal treatment, whereas changes in PPI were primarily associated with genotype, with WT mice generally exhibiting larger positive changes than Kmo-/- mice. The intensity-dependent profile of PPI changes was also influenced by prenatal treatment. Together, these findings indicate that transient prenatal KP perturbation can be associated with persistent alterations in adult sensorimotor function even in the absence of sustained elevations in whole-brain KYNA. They further suggest that developmental KP history and constitutive KMO deficiency are associated with distinct patterns of behavioral changes observed following cannabinoid receptor activation, highlighting the complex relationship between developmental metabolic perturbations and adult sensorimotor processing.

articles.title: Anatomical and Histological Analysis of the Urethral Vascular System in Female Rats.
articles.authors: Mu J, Xu S, Guo H et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: There exists a complex vascular structure within the female urethra, and these structures may be closely related to urinary continence. Therefore, the overall anatomical structure of the urethra at the macroscopic scale still requires further clarification. We hypothesized that a specialized musculo-vascular complex exists within the female mid-urethra, which could be visualized and characterized using advanced 3D imaging techniques.
METHODS: Nine Sprague-Dawley rats (6 females, 3 males for preliminary comparison) and 2 canines were used. The primary aim was to provide a high-resolution 3D anatomical description of the female rat urethra, with a specific focus on the vascular-muscular system. To achieve this, we employed fMOST, Masson's Trichrome staining, 3D immunolabeling, vessel labeling, tissue clearing, light-sheet microscopy, and immunofluorescence staining.
RESULTS: The vascular architecture of the female rat urethra demonstrates remarkable complexity. In the mid-urethral segment, a venous sinus forms an intricate reticular network. This vascular plexus exhibits two distinct structural components: one is enveloped by the surrounding striated musculature, whereas the other closely apposes the urethral lumen and is structurally positioned to potentially contribute to suggesting a potential contribution to urethral closure mechanisms, a hypothesis requiring functional validation. These components are interconnected via anastomotic reticular branches, forming a structurally integrated system that is anatomically poised to function as a unit. This specialized anatomical configuration may play a role in urinary continence, a hypothesis that now requires functional testing. Similar vascular architectures have been documented across mammalian species, suggesting evolutionary conservation of this structure-function relationship.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first 3D depiction of the urethral vascular-muscular complex, revealing a highly specialized anatomical structure in the female rat mid-urethra. Based on this novel anatomy, we propose the hypothesis that this complex could facilitate urinary continence via a hydraulic mechanism, a premise that now requires direct functional testing in future work.

articles.title: Brisk Walking- and Running-Induced Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Questionnaire in Runners: French Translation and Content Validity.
articles.authors: Proulx L, McLean L, Klahsen O et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Urinary incontinence (UI) during exercise is common among active females, with one in three runners experiencing symptoms. As UI can limit participation in sport, there is a need to understand exercise-specific symptoms and strategies used to mitigate them. Existing questionnaires do not assess UI that occurs specifically during exercise. The Brisk Walking- and Running-induced Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Questionnaire (BRUTS-Q) was developed in English using focus groups and a Delphi process and is currently under validation. A French version is needed for francophone populations. The objectives were to translate the BRUTS-Q into French and to assess the content validity of the translated version among females reporting running-related UI in terms of relevance, comprehensibility, and comprehensiveness.
METHODS: Following COnsensus-based Standards for the selection of health Measurement INstruments guidelines, a qualitative design using cognitive "think-aloud" interviews was conducted with French-speaking females who reported experiencing running-related UI. Iterative analyses were performed in sets of five interviews. Two researchers independently coded data to identify issues related to content validity, and the questionnaire was revised accordingly between rounds. The process continued until no new issues emerged.
RESULTS: The final French version of the BRUTS-Q demonstrated strong content validity, with participants reporting good clarity, relevance, and comprehensiveness for describing running-related UI in the francophone female population.
CONCLUSION: These findings support the strong potential of the French-language BRUTS-Q as a patient-centered outcome measure to assess symptoms of running-related UI and to inform the development of targeted interventions. Further studies are needed to evaluate its psychometric properties before it is used clinically or in research.

articles.title: Outcomes in patients stopping biologic during the first trimester of pregnancy: a retrospective monocentric study.
articles.authors: Monin L, Reenaers C, Grandfils S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend continuing biologics during pregnancy but patients remain concerned about foetal drug exposure. For women in sustained remission, discontinuing biologics before active placental transfer (≈GW20) may represent a compromise. We evaluated disease activity and pregnancy outcomes in this situation and measured biologic concentrations in cord blood to estimate foetal exposure.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study including all IBD pregnancies followed at the University Hospital of Liege (2010-2023). Disease flare was defined as the need for corticosteroids, start/resumption of biologics, or surgery. Preterm birth, caesarean section, low birth weight were recorded. Additionally, drug levels in paired maternal-cord samples (n = 5) were prospectively measured at delivery in women stopping biologic between GW12-20.
RESULTS: We analysed 185 pregnancies in 143 women. Ninety pregnancies began under biologics: 80 (88.9%) discontinued before GW20 and 10 (11.1%) continued treatment. Disease flare occurred in 14/80 (17.5%) and 4/10 (40%), respectively. Among the 80 who discontinued before GW20, 16/80 (20%) preterm births, 31/80 (39%) caesarean sections and 10/80 (12.5%) low birth weight were reported. Stopping treatment before GW20 was not associated with an increased risk of disease flare (p value = .11). Low residual levels were detected in cord blood in one ustekinumab-exposed case.
CONCLUSION: Discontinuing biologic therapy before GW20 in women with IBD in remission was associated with a relapse rate of 17.5%, suggesting this approach may be a safe option to minimise foetal drug exposure without significantly increasing relapse risk. Larger, prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings and refine treatment strategies during pregnancy.

articles.title: Hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium in routine clinical practice: a retrospective cohort study showing no improvement in pregnancy outcomes among predominantly frozen embryo transfer cycles.
articles.authors: Coştur Filiz P, Filiz S
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effect of hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (HETM; EmbryoGlue) on clinical pregnancy rates in a predominantly frozen embryo transfer (FET) cohort and to identify independent predictors of outcome.
METHODS: In this retrospective, nonrandomized cohort study, we analyzed 335 embryo transfer cycles at a university-based ART unit (June 2025-April 2026): HETM group (EmbryoGlue, n = 171) vs. control (Irvine NX medium, n = 164). Allocation to transfer medium was based on shared clinical decision-making. The primary outcome was clinical pregnancy rate per cycle. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors.
RESULTS: FET accounted for 87.5% of cycles. Overall clinical pregnancy rate was 56.7% (190/335). Rates were comparable between HETM and control groups (56.7% vs. 56.7%; OR = 1.00, 95% CI 0.65-1.54; p > 0.999). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in exploratory subgroups, including women aged ≥ 35 years, cycles with two or more previous transfer attempts, and blastocyst transfers (all p > 0.05). Despite a higher proportion of cycles with two or more previous transfer attempts in the HETM group (41.5% vs. 27.4%; p = 0.008), HETM was not an independent predictor of pregnancy (OR = 0.89, 95% CI 0.55-1.46; p = 0.652). FET (OR = 4.32; p < 0.001), blastocyst-stage transfer (OR = 2.96; p < 0.001), and younger age (OR = 0.92 per year; p = 0.001) were independently associated with clinical pregnancy.
CONCLUSIONS: HETM use was not associated with higher clinical pregnancy rates in this cohort. Transfer type, embryo stage, and patient age were independently associated with clinical pregnancy. These findings do not provide evidence supporting the routine use of EmbryoGlue in unselected FET populations.

articles.title: Process Evaluation of a Digital Smartphone Intervention (URApp) to Support Adherence to Bladder Training in Community-Based Specialist Pediatric Continence Care in England: Mixed Methods Study.
articles.authors: Beasant L, Ingram J, Richardson D et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Daytime urinary incontinence is a common childhood condition that can persist into adolescence, and it is associated with psychological distress, social and educational difficulties, and an increased risk of later mental disorders. The co-designed smartphone app "URApp" was developed in partnership with young people aged 10 to 18 years to support their self-management of bladder symptoms, but it is not yet used by community pediatric continence clinics to facilitate ongoing patient bladder training.
OBJECTIVE: The study aims to understand the barriers and facilitators to embedding a digital health intervention (URApp) designed to aid adherence to bladder training in children and young people with daytime urinary incontinence in community pediatric continence clinics.
METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods process evaluation using the Normalization Measure Development (NoMAD) questionnaire at 4 time points to measure behavior change in nursing teams at 6, 12, and 18 weeks. Teams' responses to questionnaire items were summarized as median scores and plotted at each time point using petal plots. Qualitative data were collected through focus groups and interviews and analyzed, drawing upon thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Twenty pediatric continence nurses from 5 National Health Service community pediatric continence clinics in England were recruited through purposive maximum variation sampling. URApp was well-received, and nurses were positive about introducing it to patients and felt that URApp's functionality aligned with existing bladder training provided by National Health Service community clinics. Nurses reported that URApp was easy to introduce, age-appropriate for children aged 10 to 18 years, and accessible to patients with neurodivergent conditions. However, community teams found integration into existing care pathways challenging and did not fully use URApp for urotherapy and bladder diary data collection. Teams lacked confidence in changing from paper to electronic bladder diaries, and although they were positive about young people taking ownership of their bladder condition, they struggled to encourage URApp uptake and were concerned about the lack of parental oversight of bladder diary data in URApp. Successful uptake and patient engagement with URApp were also negatively impacted by barriers in the school environment, such as lack of access to toilets and smartphones.
CONCLUSIONS: The successful integration of URApp into community…

articles.title: Long-term gynecological symptoms and ultrasound and reproductive outcomes after monofilament vs multifilament uterine closure at Cesarean delivery: secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.authors: Ziello C, Pacilio AM, Niccolini L et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term gynecological symptoms and reproductive and ultrasound outcomes among women originally enrolled in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing monofilament and multifilament sutures for uterine closure after Cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a RCT including women who underwent Cesarean delivery, who were originally assigned to monofilament or multifilament absorbable sutures for uterine closure. In this secondary analysis, participants were contacted 4-6 years after delivery and invited to a follow-up evaluation, comprising a clinical interview and a voluntary transvaginal ultrasound examination. The primary outcome was the presence of postmenstrual spotting at long-term follow-up. Secondary outcomes were other gynecological symptoms, reproductive outcomes and ultrasound outcomes. Analyses were performed according to the original randomized allocation. Effect estimates are reported as relative risk (RR) with 95% CI.
RESULTS: Of the 300 women included in the original RCT, 117 (39.0%) were included in the long-term follow-up analysis, comprising 51 in the monofilament group and 66 in the multifilament group. There was no significant difference in the primary outcome of postmenstrual spotting between the monofilament and multifilament groups (23.5% vs 22.7%; RR, 1.04 (95% CI, 0.53-2.01)). Similarly, no significant differences were observed between groups for other gynecological symptoms. Ultrasound data were available for 21 women, of whom 13 had a Cesarean-scar defect. The overall prevalence of Cesarean-scar defects was similar between groups, although defects ≥ 4 mm were more frequent in the multifilament group (RR, 0.42 (95% CI, 0.18-0.97); P = 0.04). Most reproductive outcomes, including infertility and pregnancy outcomes among women who conceived, were comparable between groups. However, subsequent pregnancy occurred more frequently in the monofilament group (29.4% vs 12.1%; RR, 2.43 (95% CI, 1.12-5.27)).
CONCLUSIONS: In this long-term follow-up of a RCT, monofilament and multifilament sutures for uterine closure were associated with similar long-term gynecological symptoms. Differences observed in selected ultrasound and reproductive outcomes should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size and exploratory nature of these analyses. Further studies are needed to better evaluate the potential impact of suture material on long-term reproductive outcomes and sonographic…

articles.title: The Impact of High Intensity Focused Ultrasound on Ovarian Reserve in Women with Uterine Fibroids and Adenomyosis: A Systematic Review and Single Arm Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
articles.authors: Karadeniz O, Kar E, Cicekyurt DT
articles.abstract: The aim of the study is to evaluate the effect of high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) treatment on ovarian reserve by synthesizing available evidence on post-treatment changes in ovarian reserve markers. Studies were eligible if they evaluated the impact of HIFU on ovarian reserve by reporting pre- and post-treatment ovarian reserve markers, including anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), antral follicle count (AFC), or gonadotropin levels. MEDLINE, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to January 5, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, assessed full texts, and evaluated risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool for randomized trials or the JBI critical appraisal tool for case series. Disagreements were resolved through discussion or consultation with a third reviewer. Of 2498 records identified, 1935 were screened after removal of duplicates, 24 articles underwent full-text review, and 10 studies were included in the systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis. This review included 2 randomized controlled trials and 8 case series (n = 667). The duration of follow-up after HIFU ranged between 3 and 24 months. Overall pooled analysis of all studies showed a small but statistically significant reduction in serum AMH levels (MD = -0.12 ng/mL; 95% CI = -0.20 to -0.04, I2 = 0%). Pooled analysis of AFC (2 studies, n = 140) revealed no statistically significant change after HIFU treatment (MD = -0.05; 95% CI = -0.28 to 0.19; I2 = 0%). The reduction in AMH persisted when the analysis was restricted to fibroid-only studies (MD = -0.13 ng/mL; 95% CI = -0.22 to -0.05), whereas data were insufficient for an adenomyosis-specific estimate. Pooled single-arm analysis showed a small but statistically significant reduction in serum AMH levels following HIFU treatment, with no significant change in AFC. This decline was associated with, rather than proven to be caused by, HIFU treatment, as the available evidence derives predominantly from uncontrolled pre-post studies that cannot establish causality. Therefore, evaluation of ovarian reserve after HIFU should not rely on AMH alone but incorporate AFC and clinical context. Pre-treatment counseling is particularly important in women with diminished ovarian reserve or of late reproductive age, in whom even minor reductions may be clinically relevant.

articles.title: Magnesium status in pregnancy: from deficiency to clinical management of preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Rondón LJ, Rojas D, Piña M et al.
articles.abstract: Magnesium is crucial for enzymatic and genetic functions, and demand increases for both the mother and the foetus during pregnancy. Inadequate magnesium intake is linked to adverse outcomes, including foetal growth restriction and preeclampsia. This narrative review characterizes the global prevalence of insufficient magnesium intake and status among pregnant women and examines its relationship with deficiency symptoms and preeclampsia. Current magnesium requirements based on recent studies and public health guidelines to identify new hallmarks for prevention and treatment are also assessed. A literature search over the past five years revealed evidence of widespread dietary magnesium inadequacy among pregnant populations. In the absence of a validated, pregnancy-specific biomarker, the true prevalence of physiological magnesium deficiency remains difficult to establish. Serum magnesium levels often appear normal despite this dietary shortfall, which may mask an underlying insufficiency. International guidelines differ on routine supplementation, and current evidence does not support universal supplementation for all pregnant women; targeted supplementation may be warranted for those with documented insufficiency or recognized risk factors, while ensuring adequate magnesium status through a varied diet remains the appropriate strategy for the broader population. Persistent dietary inadequacy nonetheless represents a significant public health concern. Current research confirms that magnesium sulphate (MgSO4) remains the cornerstone pharmacological intervention for preeclampsia with severe features and eclampsia, and its use has been associated with a significant reduction in maternal and foetal morbidity. Further prospective research is needed to clarify pregnancy-specific magnesium requirements, validate diagnostic biomarkers, and solidify clinical guidelines and best practices for pregnancy nutrition.

articles.title: An immune-inflammatory and thyroid function machine learning model for predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes: Development in a retrospective cohort and external validation in a prospective cohort.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Huang Y, Chen H, Xie X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maternal thyroid dysfunction is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, yet thyroid status alone stratifies individual risk poorly and the immune-inflammatory contribution is rarely incorporated into prospectively validated prediction tools. We aimed to develop and externally validate a model predicting a composite adverse pregnancy outcome from antenatal thyroid and cytokine markers.
METHODS: The model was developed in a retrospective cohort (n = 650; 131 events, 20.2%) and externally validated in an independent prospective cohort (n = 150; 26 events, 17.3%). Fifteen antenatal candidate predictors common to both cohorts were considered. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection; LASSO-logistic regression, random forest, extreme gradient boosting, and a support-vector machine were compared by repeated stratified cross-validation. Discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); calibration and clinical utility were also assessed, with internal-external cross-validation (IECV) as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: LASSO retained three predictors: thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-10 (IL-10). LASSO-logistic regression was selected (development cross-validated AUC 0.762, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.692-0.846). On external validation, the model achieved an AUC of 0.750 (95% CI 0.647-0.848), exceeding a thyroid group-only reference model (AUC 0.625); the Brier score was 0.127, and the calibration slope was 1.77. Random 10-fold IECV gave a pooled AUC of 0.761 (95% CI 0.720-0.800). Higher IL-6 was associated with increased risk and higher IL-10 with decreased risk.
CONCLUSION: A parsimonious three-marker model combining TPOAb, IL-6, and IL-10 showed moderate discrimination for adverse pregnancy outcomes and outperformed thyroid status alone. Calibration requires refinement, and validation in larger multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Prostaglandin-Endoperoxide Synthase 2 (PTGS2) Expression Is Increased in Chronic Asymptomatic Orchitis in the Dog.
articles.authors: Packeiser EM, Körber H, Morawietz J et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic asymptomatic orchitis (CAO) in dogs lacks effective treatment options. To elucidate the involvement of prostaglandin endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2), associated with inflammation and physiological steroidogenesis, testicular PTGS2 and StAR gene (via RT-qPCR) and protein expression (via immunohistochemistry) were analyzed in 11 canine CAO samples and compared to five normospermic control group (CG) samples. The percentage of immunopositive area (PIA) and mean gray scale (MGS) intensity were evaluated in the interstitial and tubular compartments. In CAO, PTGS2 and StAR gene expression levels were significantly increased compared to CG (p < 0.001 and p = 0.0034). Leydig cells and some peritubular cells stained immunopositive for PTGS2 and StAR and Sertoli cells positive for PTGS2. PIA and MGS for PTGS2 differed significantly between groups in the interstitial (PIA: p < 0.0001; MGS: p = 0.0051) and tubular (PIA: p = 0.0006; MGS: p = 0.0413) compartments. For StAR, PIA, but not MGS, was significantly higher in CAO (p = 0.0010). Except for PTGS2 gene expression, higher degrees of spermatogenetic impairment correlated with more prominent expression changes. This study demonstrates an association between increased PTGS2 expression and CAO. Further research is needed to investigate potential clinical benefits of selective PTGS2 inhibitors.

articles.title: Transcriptomic Identification and Functional Assessment of Candidate Host Factors Affecting Akabane Virus Replication.
articles.authors: Tan X, Zhang M, Li C et al.
articles.abstract: Akabane virus (AKAV) causes abortion, stillbirth, and congenital malformations in ruminants, yet the transcriptional response of Madin-Darby bovine kidney (MDBK) cells and the roles of infection-responsive host genes in AKAV replication remain incompletely characterized. We profiled AKAV-infected and time-matched mock-infected MDBK cells by RNA sequencing at 12 and 24 h post-infection (hpi). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were examined using Gene Ontology functional classification and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment analysis, six DEGs were evaluated by RT-qPCR, and OAS2 and ZBP1 were assessed by overexpression in BHK-21 cells. We identified 119 DEGs at 12 hpi (82 upregulated and 37 downregulated) and 149 at 24 hpi (85 upregulated and 64 downregulated). The DEG sets were associated with antiviral defense, interferon responses, pattern recognition receptor signaling, DNA replication, cell cycle regulation, chromosome organization, and metabolism. RT-qPCR measurements were consistent with the RNA-seq trends. OAS2 and ZBP1 transcripts were significantly upregulated at 12 hpi, while ZBP1 transcript levels remained significantly elevated at 24 hpi. Overexpression of either gene was associated with reductions in AKAV Gc protein abundance, viral RNA levels, and infectious titers. These results define transcriptional changes in AKAV-infected MDBK cells and nominate OAS2 and ZBP1 as candidate host factors for further investigation, while their endogenous roles in bovine cells remain to be established.

articles.title: Teratogenic Effects and Outcomes of Congenital Oropouche Virus Infection: Current Evidence, Pathophysiological Mechanisms, and Research Priorities.
articles.authors: Pomar L, Epelboin L, Hcini N
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oropouche virus (OROV), an Orthobunyavirus endemic to Latin America, has recently emerged as a pathogen of concern in pregnancy following reports of vertical transmission, fetal demise, congenital anomalies, and neonatal disease. The unprecedented 2023-2025 outbreaks in Latin America have expanded the geographic distribution of OROV and renewed concerns regarding its potential as an emerging human teratogen.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative comprehensive review of the literature focusing on epidemiology, maternal-fetal transmission, placental infection, experimental models, fetal and neonatal outcomes, and comparisons with other congenital arboviral infections.
RESULTS: Increasing evidence supports the ability of OROV to infect the placenta, cross the maternal-fetal interface, and invade fetal tissues. Human cases have documented miscarriage, stillbirth, fetal demise, microcephaly, ventriculomegaly, cerebral atrophy, corpus callosum abnormalities, posterior fossa defects, arthrogryposis, and neonatal death following maternal infection. Viral RNA and OROV-specific antibodies have been detected in placental, fetal, and neonatal samples, providing direct evidence of congenital infection. Experimental studies using trophoblast cultures, placental organoids, neural progenitor cells, brain organoids, and animal models have confirmed placental susceptibility, vertical transmission, fetal neurotropism, and disruption of neurodevelopment. The congenital phenotype shares important similarities with congenital Zika syndrome and other neurotropic arboviral infections.
CONCLUSIONS: OROV is newly and increasingly recognized as a vertically transmissible neurotropic arbovirus with potential teratogenic effects. Although biological plausibility is supported by converging clinical and experimental findings, prospective epidemiological studies are urgently needed to quantify risks, identify determinants of fetal injury, and define long-term outcomes among affected children.

articles.title: Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling of the Human Placenta in Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection: A Broad Antiviral Response with Concurrent Suppression of Trophoblast and Vascular Programs.
articles.authors: Atkinson SN, Miller HE, Jarzembowski J et al.
articles.abstract: Congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the most common congenital infection and a leading infectious cause of childhood hearing loss and neurodevelopmental disability. The cellular organization of the placental response to infection is incompletely defined. We applied Visium CytAssist spatial transcriptomics to formalin-fixed tissue from two CMV-infected and two uninfected late-gestation placentas and annotated the major maternal and fetal cell populations by reference-based label transfer. Across 16,074 spatial spots, the only significant compositional changes were increased T cell spots and decreased syncytiotrophoblast-enriched spots in CMV-infected placentas; the remaining populations showed similar changes but did not reach significance. Differential expression comparing CMV-infected to uninfected samples within each cell type identified two opposing programs. Infected placentas displayed a broad interferon-stimulated gene signature accompanied by induction of CXCR3-ligand chemokines, antigen-processing machinery, and the major histocompatibility complex class I transactivator NLRC5, classical-pathway complement components, and lymphocyte and plasma-cell markers, most pronounced in endothelial, stromal, and syncytiotrophoblast clusters and minimal in extravillous trophoblasts. Concurrently, infected placentas showed downregulation of trophoblast differentiation and syncytialization genes, including PAPPA2, pregnancy-specific glycoproteins, CGA, and GCM1, as well as vascular and hemostatic genes, including FLT1, VEGFA, PECAM1, and TFPI2. These data provide a cell-type-resolved molecular correlation of immune activation and placental dysfunction associated with congenital CMV. Together, the data indicate that congenital CMV infection is associated with a coordinated shift at the maternal-fetal interface, in which a broad interferon-driven immune response accompanies suppression of trophoblast-developmental and vascular programs, providing a cell-type-resolved reference for larger studies of placental CMV transmission. Future studies in larger cohorts will be needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Medicine-Food Homology Bioactives for Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: Multi-Target Mechanisms and Functional Food Translation.
articles.authors: Lv X, Long W, Hu Z et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) is characterized by insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, chronic inflammation, and oxidative stress, with a global prevalence of 10-13% and limited current drug treatments. Medicine-Food Homology (MFH) materials are rich in bioactive compounds such as polyphenols, flavonoids, and polysaccharides, offering potential multi-target nutritional interventions for PMOS, although safety data remain limited mainly to single compounds. A systematic search of the literature was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science CNKI, and Wanfang Data, spanning from database inception to August 2026, utilizing predefined search terms and inclusion/exclusion criteria. This review summarizes research on MFH-derived bioactive compounds in PMOS, covering active component identification, network pharmacology-based target prediction, key signaling pathways (PI3K/AKT, AMPK, NF-κB, Nrf2/HO-1), and formulation strategies including green extraction, nano-encapsulation, and controlled release. It further discusses functional food development from five perspectives: meal replacement powders, functional teas, fermented beverages, dietary supplements, and compound formulations. Key bottlenecks hindering commercialization are analyzed, including insufficient high-quality clinical evidence, unclear dose-response relationships, and limited long-term stability data. Future directions are proposed, such as organoids, organ-on-a-chip, AI-driven formulation optimization, and international multicenter trials. In summary, MFH bioactive compounds show potential as multi-target interventions for PMOS; however, most mechanistic evidence comes from non-PMOS metabolic models, and direct PMOS-specific evidence is limited. Their translation from empirical use to evidence-based intervention requires PMOS-specific preclinical validation, randomized controlled trials, safety assessments, bioavailability evaluation, and standardized product validation, alongside collaborative efforts across research paradigms, technology development, and industrial translation.

articles.title: Human Papillomavirus Prevalence and Genotype Distribution in Unvaccinated Women: A Gynaecology and Obstetrics Hospital-Based Retrospective Study in México.
articles.authors: Flores-Medina S, Sam-Soto S, Plazola-Camacho NG et al.
articles.abstract: In countries with suboptimal vaccination coverage, human papillomavirus (HPV) genital infections remain a public health problem. Furthermore, the prevalence of specific HPV genotypes in unvaccinated women is uncertain. Therefore, this study aimed to retrospectively evaluate HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among unvaccinated women attending a gynaecology and obstetrics hospital in Mexico, and to establish potential associations between HPV infection and the different pathologies affecting unvaccinated women. A single-centre, retrospective analysis of 347 unvaccinated women who underwent gynaecological examination and had an HPV test was conducted. HPV genotypes in cervical cells were determined using the CLART HPV4 system, which can detect 35 HPV genotypes. Overall, 124 (35.73%) women tested positive for HPV, which included single- and multiple-genotype infections. Oncogenic, high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) genotypes were detected in 74.19% of the HPV-positive women. Ranked by prevalence, HPV59 was the most frequent, followed by HPV16, HPV39, HPV31, and HPV42. Out of the 11 HR-HPV genotypes identified, 6 are targeted by the nonavalent HPV vaccine. In conclusion, this study reports the prevalence of HPV infection among unvaccinated women attending a gynaecological and obstetric centre and demonstrates that HR-HPV genotypes are the most prevalent in this population. These data may facilitate the design of organised screening and vaccination programmes to reduce genital infection and cervical cancer burden in México.

articles.title: Nelfinavir Synergizes with Cisplatin and Promotes GSDME-Associated Lytic Cell Death in Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer Cells.
articles.authors: Forgie BN, Prakash R, Marno D et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Platinum resistance limits the efficacy of ovarian cancer treatment and arises through multiple mechanisms, including enhanced DNA repair, activation of stress responses, and increased survival signaling. Nelfinavir (NFV), an HIV protease inhibitor with reported anti-tumor activity, is a candidate for drug repurposing, but its interaction with cisplatin (CDDP) in ovarian cancer has not been established. Here, we investigated whether NFV enhances CDDP cytotoxicity in platinum (Pt)-resistant ovarian cancer cells and characterized the associated cell death response. Methods: Drug interaction was assessed using cell vitality and viability assays and Loewe additivity modeling together with Bliss and ZIP analyses. Cell death was characterized by Annexin V/7-AAD staining, mitochondrial membrane potential analysis, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, immunoblotting, pharmacological caspase inhibition, and bulk mRNA sequencing with differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses. Results: NFV synergistically enhanced CDDP cytotoxicity across three Pt-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines, reducing CDDP IC50 values by 4.2-5.8-fold and producing mean Loewe synergy scores of approximately 25-30. Combination treatment increased LDH release and was accompanied by caspase-8, caspase-3, PARP, and the pore-forming death effector gasdermin E (GSDME) cleavage. Caspase inhibition attenuated viability loss and GSDME processing. Transcriptomic analysis identified enrichment of stress- and death-associated programs, including the unfolded protein response (UPR), apoptosis, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-associated signaling, and TNF/NF-κB signaling. Conclusions: Together, these findings demonstrate a reproducible synergistic interaction between CDDP and NFV in Pt-resistant ovarian cancer cells and characterize an associated lytic cell death phenotype involving apoptotic signaling and accompanied by GSDME processing. These findings support further investigation of NFV as a repurposed combination partner to enhance CDDP cytotoxicity in Pt-resistant ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Medication-Associated Xerostomia and Oral Symptom Burden in Midlife Women: A Drug Safety Perspective Across the Menopausal Transition.
articles.authors: Dragomir AC, Moleriu RD, Marin RC et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medication-associated xerostomia is a clinically relevant adverse effect, but its contribution to oral symptom burden in midlife women remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the association between xerogenic medication exposure and xerostomia burden across the menopausal transition and whether this association extended to broader oral symptoms. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 306 Romanian women aged 45-65 years. Medication exposure was assessed in two complementary ways: a medication-list-derived definition, in which reported medicines were coded into therapeutic classes with recognized xerogenic potential (n = 54; 17.6%), regarded as the pharmacological reference measure, and participant-reported use of medication potentially associated with dry mouth (n = 39; 12.7%), which additionally reflects patient recognition of xerogenic exposure. Outcomes were a six-item xerostomia symptom score (XSS-6; 0-18) and a nine-item oral symptom score (OSS-9; 0-27), both derived from the MMBQ-44. Associations were evaluated using two-part models adjusted for age, menopausal stage, body mass index, smoking, medication burden, and psychological symptom burden, with complementary sensitivity analyses. Results: Xerostomia symptoms were more frequent among women reporting xerogenic medication (94.9% vs. 71.5%; unadjusted OR 7.36, 95% CI 1.73-31.30), and participant-reported exposure remained associated with greater XSS-6 severity after full adjustment (+1.28 points, 95% CI 0.22-2.34). With the medication-list-derived definition, unadjusted associations were present (rate ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.08-2.10) but attenuated to near-null estimates after full adjustment (severity difference 0.06 points; rate ratio 1.17, 95% CI 0.79-1.71). Psychological symptom burden was independently associated with both outcomes, and no independent association with OSS-9 was observed for either exposure definition. Agreement between definitions was moderate (85.3%; Cohen kappa 0.43); only 24/54 (44.4%) women identified from medication lists recognized taking medication capable of causing dry mouth. Conclusions: Pharmacologically defined xerogenic exposure showed weak independent associations with xerostomia burden after full adjustment, whereas the stronger associations observed for participant-recognized exposure may partly reflect symptom-driven awareness and should be read as an upper bound. Limited recognition of xerogenic exposure points…

articles.title: Population-Specific Pharmacogenetic Variants Associated with Chemotherapy Response in the Bulgarian Population.
articles.authors: Miteva-Marcheva N, Ivanov H, Sotkova-Ivanova I et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pharmacogenetic variability influences the efficacy and toxicity of anticancer therapies. However, Eastern European populations remain underrepresented in pharmacogenetic databases. This study aimed to characterize pharmacogenetic variants relevant to chemotherapy response in the Bulgarian population and compare their allele frequencies with reference populations. Methods: Ninety individuals were included, comprising 50 patients with colorectal, non-small cell lung, or breast cancer and 40 healthy controls. Genomic DNA and circulating cell-free DNA were analyzed by next-generation sequencing targeting pharmacogenetic genes involved in drug metabolism, transport, and DNA repair. Allele frequencies were compared with gnomAD v2.1.1 reference data. Sensitivity analyses compared Bulgarian controls with Bulgarian non-cancer and combined Southern European, Northwestern European, and Other non-Finnish European non-cancer populations. Results: Twenty-three pharmacogenetic variants were evaluated. Six variants remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction in both Fisher's exact test and the two-proportion Z-test. Five variants-DPYD c.2194G>A, XPC c.2815C>A, EGFR c.1562G>A, XRCC1 c.1196A>G, and ERCC2 c.2251A>C-showed higher allele frequencies, whereas ERCC2 c.934G>A was less frequent in the Bulgarian cohort. DPYD c.85T>C remained significant after correction in the Z-test but not in Fisher's exact test. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the significance of XPC c.2815C>A in both reference-population comparisons, while DPYD c.85T>C remained significant only against the combined European reference population. Conclusions: Several pharmacogenetic variants showed distinct allele frequencies in the Bulgarian cohort. XPC c.2815C>A demonstrated the most robust population-specific pattern across sensitivity analyses. These findings highlight the value of locally derived pharmacogenetic data for precision oncology and pharmacogenetically guided treatment strategies.

articles.title: Early Revegetation Initiates Soil Physical Habitat Reconstruction and Microbial Community Reassembly Within the First Growing Season in an Alpine Mining Substrate.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Cai B, Zhao X et al.
articles.abstract: Ecological restoration of alpine mining areas is constrained by low temperature, infertile substrates, and limited water availability, yet the coordinated early responses of plants, soils, and microorganisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a 90-day in situ revegetation experiment in an alpine sand-and-gravel mine in Tibet using three native perennial grasses, Elymus nutans, Agropyron cristatum, and Festuca sinensis, established in monoculture and mixed-sowing treatments. Plant growth and physiology, soil physicochemical properties, nutrients, enzyme activities, and microbial communities were assessed.
