All three pioneer species established measurable biomass within the first growing season, although growth and physiological responses differed among planting configurations. Soil capillary porosity, moisture content, and water-holding capacity showed the most consistent improvements, whereas enzyme activities and nutrient responses were more treatment-dependent. Bacterial and fungal communities underwent significant reorganization, while inferred co-occurrence networks showed temporal topological restructuring and sensitivity to simulated targeted node removal. Mantel analysis showed that bacterial community variation was significantly associated with capillary porosity, non-capillary porosity, and total phosphorus, whereas fungal community variation was not significantly associated with the measured soil variables. Overall, 90 days of pioneer revegetation initiated measurable plant-soil-microbial recovery in the alpine mining substrate. Physical and hydrological properties showed clearer early responses than most nutrient indicators, while the observed associations between soil pore characteristics and bacterial community composition suggest a potential link between physical habitat changes and microbial community reassembly.

articles.title: Varied Mulching Practices Modulate Soil Hydrothermal-Nutrient Regimes and Root Yield of Indigowoad Root in an Oasis.
articles.authors: Zhou P, Wang Z, Wang Y et al.
articles.abstract: Water scarcity and plastic film pollution increasingly threaten the sustainable production of Indigowoad Root (Isatis tinctoria L.) in semi-arid regions. However, the mechanisms by which different mulching practices under flat planting regulate soil hydrothermal conditions, nutrient availability, and yield remain poorly understood. The study aimed to provide theoretical and technical support for water-saving and high-yield production of Indigowoad Root in oasis areas. Bare soil without mulching was used as the control (CK), and five mulching treatments were established: biodegradable white plastic film mulching (DW), biodegradable black plastic film mulching (DB), white polyethylene film mulching (PW), black polyethylene film mulching (PB), and straw mulching (SM). The effects of these treatments on soil water storage, soil temperature, soil organic matter, soil nutrient status, leaf area index, dry matter accumulation, and yield of Indigowoad Root were evaluated. The mulching treatments improved soil hydrothermal conditions and nutrient status and promoted plant growth and yield formation in Indigowoad Root. Compared with CK, DB significantly increased soil water storage and soil temperature. It also increased the contents of ammonium nitrogen, nitrate nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium, thereby promoting dry matter accumulation and yield formation. The PLS-PM results indicated that improved soil hydrothermal conditions enhanced soil nutrient availability, thereby promoting plant growth and driving yield formation (increased by 25%). Biodegradable black film mulching (DB) increased Indigowoad Root yield by improving soil hydrothermal conditions, enhancing soil nutrient availability, and promoting plant growth, thereby providing a promising water-saving and yield-enhancing mulching strategy for Indigowoad Root production in the semi-arid Hexi Oasis.

articles.title: Estrogen Receptor-Mediated Effects of a Phytoestrogen-Rich Soy-Based Diet on Metabolic Health Following Ovariectomy in Aged Mice.
articles.authors: Zidon TM, Padilla J, McCabe LT et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Loss of ovarian hormones leads to obesity and insulin resistance (IR), increasing the risk of cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. We previously showed that aged female ERa knockout (αKO) and ERb knockout (βKO) mice differentially respond to ovariectomy, with a greater adverse metabolic response in βKO mice. We later showed that young ovariectomized (OVX) βKO mice were somewhat resistant to exercise-mediated metabolic benefits including adipose tissue browning.
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: We tested the hypothesis that feeding a high phytoestrogen soy-based diet (SOY) would improve metabolic health in older OVX female mice and that αKO and βKO mice would differentially respond to the diet. Since phytoestrogens weakly bind ERs, and it is known that activation of ERa mediates insulin sensitizing and weight loss benefits, and ERb is known to improve adipocyte mitochondrial responses, we hypothesized that αKO mice would be less responsive to the systemic metabolic benefits of SOY, whereas βKO mice would be less responsive to adipocyte-specific benefits.
METHODS: We examined OVX and ovary-intact aged (~1 yr) wildtype (WT), αKO, and βKO female mice (n = 7-12/group). One week following OVX, mice were randomized to receive either SOY (585 mg phytoestrogens/kg) or a phytoestrogen-free diet (<15 mg/kg, CON) and were followed for 11 weeks. Mice were assessed for body composition (EchoMRI), energy expenditure (EE via Promethion metabolic cage system), glucose tolerance (i.p. glucose tolerance test), insulin sensitivity (HOMA-IR, Adipo-IR), adipose tissue gene and protein expression for insulin signaling markers, and fasting blood lipids. To provide additional mechanistic insight, primary adipocytes were treated with phytoestrogens and assessed for insulin-mediated phosphorylation of Akt.
RESULTS: Era mediated important metabolic benefits of SOY in aged OVX mice. OVX αKO mice were unresponsive to SOY-mediated improvements in body composition and glucose tolerance, whereas SOY improved those metrics, as well as increased spontaneous physical activity in OVX WT and βKO mice (all p < 0.05). Primary adipocyte cell culture experiments revealed that insulin-mediated phosphorylation of Akt occurred even with ERα-antagonization, with no effects of estrogen or phytoestrogen treatment, at least in the small set of experiments performed.
CONCLUSIONS: SOY improved body composition and glucose tolerance in old OVX mice, effects that were absent in ERα-null mice. Soy-based…

articles.title: Five-Year Trends in Dietary Intake by Gender Among Korean Preschoolers (2017-2021): Nationwide Survey-Based Surveillance Amid Rising Demand for Medical Care for Precocious Puberty.
articles.authors: Yang J, Lee J, Og H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Care-seeking for precocious puberty (PP) in South Korea has risen sharply, coinciding with dietary westernization among children. This study describes sex-specific and temporal dietary trends among Korean children aged 1-11 years, focusing on the 6-11-year band preceding the typical PP diagnosis threshold.
METHODS: Using KNHANES (2017-2021) dietary data and HIRA care-seeking counts with the sex-year aggregate, not the individual child. Sex differences were assessed using the Mann-Whitney U test, year-to-year patterns using a sex-by-year interaction model (n = 5 annual observations per sex), and dietary pattern structure using principal component analysis (PCA) on 12 food groups (n = 10 sex-year observations).
RESULTS: PP care-seeking rates rose in both sexes, substantially more in girls. Boys showed significantly higher intake of most food groups and macronutrients; within the 6-11-year band this held for meat, cola, and macronutrients (p = 0.008) but not legumes (p = 0.421). Macronutrient sex gaps numerically narrowed while meat and cola gaps widened over 2017-2021, though none reached significance. PCA identified a primary axis reflecting overall intake volume that separated boys and girls, and a secondary axis distinguishing a dairy/seaweed/beverage profile from a meat/egg/cola-dominant profile.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings describe sex-specific dietary patterns amid rising PP rates without establishing that intake volume explains the sex disparity, identifying candidate exposures for future research and cautioning against oversimplified dietary narratives.

articles.title: Melatonin and Female Fertility: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Supplementation, In Vitro Experiments, and Observational Evidence.
articles.authors: Ye H, Hu Y, Wang H et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Melatonin has been proposed as a potential strategy to improve female fertility, but existing evidence is dispersed across assisted reproduction, reproductive disorders, and in vitro studies. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the relationships of melatonin supplementation, in vitro melatonin treatment, and endogenous melatonin levels with female fertility. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, and EMBASE were searched from inception through February 2026. Randomized and non-randomized intervention studies, observational studies, and in vitro studies involving human oocytes or embryos were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Results: Thirty-six publications were included. Among women undergoing ART, melatonin supplementation increased the clinical pregnancy rate (RR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.23-1.94) and live birth (RR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.01-2.51). Melatonin supplementation also improved selected ovarian and embryological outcomes. In vitro treatment increased fertilization (OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.40-2.76) and blastocyst formation (OR = 2.00, 95% CI: 1.33-3.03). Observational studies showed higher morning serum melatonin levels in women with PCOS (MD = 7.83 pg/mL, 95% CI: 3.56-12.11). The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Conclusions: Melatonin supplementation may improve selected reproductive outcomes, including clinical pregnancy and live birth, although evidence for live birth remains limited. In vitro and observational findings further support a potential role of melatonin in female reproductive function, but its clinical value requires confirmation in high-quality studies.

articles.title: Enhanced Estrogenic Activity in Water-Soluble Silybum marianum Complex via Microwave-Assisted Steviol Glycoside-Based Formulation.
articles.authors: Kim JH, Jeong SH, Lee BW et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phytoestrogens are promising alternatives to menopausal hormone therapy, but their clinical application is limited by poor solubility and bioavailability. Silybum marianum (milk thistle) contains flavonolignans with reported estrogenic potential. However, its extract shows only modest estrogenic activity, and approaches to enhance its efficacy by improving solubility remain insufficiently explored.
METHODS: A water-soluble Silybum marianum complex (WS) was prepared using microwave-assisted processing with steviol glycoside (SG), and its phytochemical integrity was assessed by UPLC-QTOF-MS. Estrogenic activity was evaluated using cell-free ERα/ERβ competitive binding assays and, in MCF-7 cells, by assessing proliferation and ERα/ERK/AKT phosphorylation. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in a VCD-induced menopause model in female C57BL/6 mice by measuring plasma estradiol levels, uterine weight, and vaginal epithelial thickness.
RESULTS: WS retained major flavonolignans and incorporated SG-derived metabolites. WS bound both ERα and ERβ in cell-free assays. In MCF-7 cells, WS induced ERα, ERK, and AKT phosphorylation and cell proliferation; the proliferative response and ERK/AKT phosphorylation were abolished by the ER antagonist fulvestrant, and proliferation was comparable to that of genistein and daidzein. Neither Silybum marianum extract (SME) alone nor its simple physical combinations with SG reproduced the activity of WS, indicating that enhanced estrogenic activity was observed following microwave-assisted processing. In vivo, WS dose-dependently increased measured estradiol levels, increased uterine weight, and reversed vaginal atrophy.
CONCLUSIONS: Microwave-assisted processing with SG significantly enhances the estrogenic activity of Silybum marianum. Our findings suggest that WS may serve as a promising phytoestrogenic candidate for further evaluation in the context of estrogen deficiency.

articles.title: Lipid Indicators and Low Bone Mass Among Taiwanese Adults: A Cross-Sectional Association Study.
articles.authors: Ko HS, Chang CW, Bai CH
articles.abstract: Background & Aims: This study investigated the associations of lipid indicators, particularly the total cholesterol to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (TC/HDL-C), with low bone mass in adults. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 6389 participants aged ≥19 years from the Nutrition and Health Survey in Taiwan (2013-2020). Two study-defined low-bone-mass phenotypes were evaluated as research phenotypes rather than densitometric diagnoses: central-site low bone mass, defined as a T-score < -1.0 at either the lumbar spine (L1-L4) or the lower of the bilateral femoral neck T-scores, and total-body low bone mass, defined as a total-body T-score < -1.0. Multivariable logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline analysis were performed to examine associations of lipid indicators with low bone mass. Subgroup analyses by sex, age, and age-defined menopausal status were exploratory. Results: Among 6389 participants, 1069 had total-body low bone mass. Total-body low bone mass showed more evident associations with lipid-related markers than central-site low bone mass. Each 10 mg/dL increase in HDL-C was associated with higher odds of total-body low bone mass (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 1.080, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.018-1.147, p = 0.011). Although the linear association between TC/HDL-C and low bone mass was not statistically significant, spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear association with total-body low bone mass, with a turning point at 4.39 (p for nonlinearity = 0.016). Exploratory analyses suggested effect modification by age and age-based grouping. Conclusions: Total-body low bone mass showed more evident associations with lipid indicators than central-site low bone mass. HDL-C was linearly associated with low bone mass, whereas TC/HDL-C showed an exploratory nonlinear association, supporting its potential role as a readily available metabolic correlate of skeletal status.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome-Estrogen Axis in Menopause: Implications for Body Composition, Cardiometabolic Health and Nutrition.
articles.authors: Pătru O, Luca S, Păunescu A et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Menopause is associated with profound endocrine, metabolic, immune, and microbial changes that may contribute to accelerated biological aging and increased cardiometabolic risk. The gut microbiome represents a potential interface between estrogen biology, host metabolism, inflammation, and systemic organ function. This narrative review examines the role of menopause-associated gut microbiome remodeling in microbiome-mediated metabolic aging, focusing on the estrobolome, microbial metabolites, organ crosstalk, and microbiome-targeted interventions. Methods: Relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by reference-list screening. Human observational and clinical studies, mechanistic investigations, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant guidelines were critically evaluated and synthesized narratively. No formal meta-analysis was performed. Results: Menopause-associated changes in gut microbial composition and function may influence estrogen metabolism through the estrobolome and modify the production of short-chain fatty acids, lipopolysaccharides, trimethylamine N-oxide, and bile acid metabolites. These pathways may contribute to chronic low-grade inflammation, insulin resistance, endothelial dysfunction, dyslipidemia, hepatic metabolic dysfunction, adipose tissue inflammation, adverse changes in body composition, sarcopenia, neuroinflammation, and urogenital microbial instability. Dietary patterns, fermentable fiber, physical activity, probiotics, synbiotics, phytoestrogens, and menopausal hormone therapy may influence components of this network, although the strength of evidence remains variable. Current data do not support the use of microbiome characteristics to select or dose hormone therapy. Conclusions: The gut microbiome may act as a dynamic mediator linking estrogen decline with metabolic and systemic aging after menopause. However, causality, individual variability, and clinical translation remain insufficiently established. Longitudinal studies integrating shotgun metagenomics, metabolomics, hormone measurements, standardized hormone therapy exposure, and clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether microbiome-derived biomarkers can support risk stratification and personalized interventions for healthier aging in postmenopausal women.

articles.title: Efficacy of 5-Aminolevulinic Acid Photodynamic Therapy Versus Observation for Cervical Low-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions with High-Risk HPV Infection.
articles.authors: Wang X, Huang J, He Q et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of photodynamic therapy (PDT) compared to observation in managing low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSILs) with high-risk HPV infection. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 608 patients with pathologically confirmed LSILs and Hr-HPV infection, divided into PDT or observation groups based on clinical preference and evaluation. PDT was administered as a routine clinical treatment option at our center. Follow-up at 6 months included HPV testing, cytology, and colposcopy. Results: The PDT group exhibited significantly higher regression rates (92.5% vs. 48.3%) and complete HPV clearance rates (80.8% vs. 37.3%) than the observation group. Adverse effects from PDT were mild and transient, with no cervical scarring or skin photosensitivity observed. Ten patients conceived successfully post-PDT, with five uncomplicated deliveries to date. Conclusions: These findings suggest that PDT is an effective, non-invasive treatment for LSILs with Hr-HPV infection, demonstrating favorable regression and safety profiles while preserving cervical integrity, particularly in reproductive-aged women.

articles.title: The Interplay Between Oophorectomy and Alzheimer's Disease: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Xu S, Fu X, Zuo L et al.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and affects women more frequently than men. Although age remains the main risk factor, reproductive aging and changes in ovarian hormone exposure may also contribute to this difference. Premenopausal bilateral oophorectomy causes an abrupt loss of ovarian hormones, including estradiol, progesterone, and testosterone, and several observational studies have associated this change with a higher risk of later cognitive impairment or dementia, particularly when surgery is performed at a younger age. However, these studies have assessed different outcomes, including dementia, mild cognitive impairment, subjective cognitive changes, and AD-related imaging findings, and current evidence does not establish a direct causal relationship between oophorectomy and AD. Possible biological pathways include neuroinflammation, synaptic dysfunction, amyloid-β and tau-related changes, and cerebrovascular dysfunction, although much of the mechanistic evidence remains experimental or indirect. Genetic background, vascular health, age at surgery, and the duration of hormone deprivation may further influence individual risk. Hormone replacement therapy has an established role in the management of premature or early surgical menopause when there is no contraindication, but its effect on long-term AD prevention remains uncertain; the timing of treatment may be important, but current evidence does not confirm a preventive effect. This review summarizes current epidemiological, neuroimaging, and experimental evidence linking oophorectomy with cognitive health and AD, and discusses hormone therapy, pharmacological and non-pharmacological management, emerging research approaches, and remaining knowledge gaps. Future studies with detailed information on surgical timing, hormone exposure, genetic risk, vascular factors, longitudinal cognition, and AD-related biomarkers are needed to better define which women may be most vulnerable after premenopausal oophorectomy.

articles.title: The Role of Hysteroscopy in Reproductive Medicine and Subfertility: A Critical Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Tsonis O, Paschopoulos I, Paschopoulou KI et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Hysteroscopy permits direct assessment and treatment of the uterine cavity, but diagnostic yield does not necessarily translate into improved fertility. This narrative review examines its role in subfertility and reproductive medicine. Materials and Methods: The original literature search covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library through February 2026. Targeted checks during revision added the 2026 chronic endometritis consensus and the full CERM trial report; these updates do not represent a new comprehensive search. Evidence was interpreted by study design, population, outcome and precision, without formal risk-of-bias assessment or meta-analysis. Results: Large randomised trials do not support routine hysteroscopy before first IVF or after repeated IVF failure when ultrasonography is normal. Polypectomy has evidence of improved pregnancy rates in women planning IUI, although spontaneous pregnancies contributed to that result and live-birth benefit remains uncertain. Hysteroscopic myomectomy may improve clinical pregnancy in women with cavity-distorting fibroids; evidence for live birth is less secure. Adhesiolysis restores cavity anatomy, but reproductive estimates largely derive from observational series. The small TRUST trial did not demonstrate a live-birth advantage from septum resection and cannot establish equivalence. Hysteroscopy may guide biopsy for chronic endometritis but does not replace histological assessment. CERM found no improvement with doxycycline in its composite of cumulative live births and ongoing pregnancies at ≥24 weeks among women with recurrent miscarriage and CD138-defined endometritis. Fertility-sparing endometrial cancer treatment requires oncological selection, progestin therapy and histological surveillance. Conclusions: Hysteroscopy should address a defined diagnostic or therapeutic question. Decisions should distinguish spontaneous conception, IUI and IVF/ICSI and acknowledge uncertainty in live-birth outcomes.

articles.title: Association of FOXP3 Gene Polymorphisms with Skin, Vulvar and Ectocervical Squamous Cell Tumors.
articles.authors: Kotlica B, Stefanović K, Argenziano G et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Squamous cell tumors arise from squamous epithelial cells. Polymorphisms in the FOXP3 gene may influence malignancy susceptibility. This study evaluated the potential association of FOXP3 rs3761548 (-3279 A/C) and rs2280883 (IVS9+459 T/C) polymorphisms with preinvasive and invasive squamous cell tumors of sun-exposed skin, sun-protected vulvar skin, and the ectocervix. Materials and Methods: This comparative observational study included 135 women aged >18 years surgically treated for squamous cell tumors of the skin (actinic keratosis, Bowen's disease, squamous cell carcinoma), vulva (HSIL, differentiated VIN, squamous cell carcinoma), or ectocervix (LSIL, HSIL, squamous cell carcinoma). Sociodemographic, anthropometric, lifestyle, ultraviolet radiation exposure, reproductive, and sexual health data were collected. The FOXP3 rs3761548 and rs2280883 polymorphisms were genotyped; codominant, dominant, recessive, and overdominant genetic models were evaluated. Results: The three groups differed significantly in several sociodemographic, anthropometric, lifestyle, reproductive, and sexual health characteristics. No significant differences were observed for smoking, sun exposure, history of sunburns, contraceptive use, or history of abortions. The minor A allele frequency of rs3761548 was lower in the skin and vulvar tumor groups and slightly higher in the ectocervical tumor group than in reference populations; however, this difference was not significant (p = 0.066). None of the rs3761548 genetic models remained significant after LASSO regression. For rs2280883, the C allele frequency was lower in the skin and ectocervical groups but higher in the vulvar tumor group than the 46.0% reported in the reference population. The dominant model (CC + CT vs. TT) was associated with lower odds of skin tumors, whereas the recessive model (CC vs. TT + CT) was associated with higher odds (both p = 0.037). Conclusions: The distribution of the FOXP3 rs2280883 polymorphism differed according to tumor location. It was significantly associated with cutaneous squamous cell tumors under both dominant and recessive genetic models.

articles.title: Protective Effects of Prophylactic and Therapeutic Erythromycin Administration in Ovarian Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Rats.
articles.authors: Akyüz S, Taş NG, Günay M et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Ovarian ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury involves oxidative stress, inflammation, and structural tissue damage that may impair ovarian function. This study investigated the effects of prophylactic and therapeutic erythromycin administration on biochemical and histopathological injury in a rat model of ovarian I/R. Materials and Methods: Forty adult female Wistar albino rats were divided into five groups (n = 8 per group): sham (SG), I/R, erythromycin alone (E), prophylactic erythromycin plus I/R (I/R+ERP), and therapeutic erythromycin plus I/R (I/R+ERT). Ovarian ischemia was induced by clamping the right ovarian vascular pedicle for 3 h, followed by 3 h of reperfusion. Erythromycin (50 mg/kg, intraperitoneally) was administered 30 min before ischemia in the I/R+ERP group and at the onset of reperfusion in the I/R+ERT group. Inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in serum and ovarian tissue, serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels, and ovarian hemorrhage and necrosis were evaluated. Results: Compared with the sham group, ovarian I/R increased inflammatory and oxidative stress markers and histopathological injury, and decreased serum AMH and ovarian tissue glutathione (GSH) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) levels. Compared with the untreated I/R group, both erythromycin regimens were associated with lower serum and ovarian tissue tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and lower ovarian necrosis scores. The I/R+ERT group also had lower ovarian tissue interleukin-1β (IL-1β), higher ovarian tissue GSH and SOD levels, and a lower hemorrhage score than the untreated I/R group. In the direct comparison between the two erythromycin regimens, serum MDA was lower (false discovery rate [FDR]-adjusted q < 0.001), ovarian tissue SOD was higher (q = 0.014), and the ovarian necrosis score was lower (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) in the I/R+ERT group. Direct comparisons for serum TNF-α (q = 0.055), ovarian tissue IL-1β (q = 0.127), and ovarian tissue GSH (q = 0.105) did not meet the FDR-adjusted significance threshold. The hemorrhage score did not differ significantly between the two erythromycin regimens (Holm-adjusted p = 0.057). Neither regimen significantly increased serum AMH compared with the untreated I/R group. Conclusions: Erythromycin attenuated several biochemical and histopathological indicators of acute experimental ovarian I/R injury. Administration at the onset of reperfusion was associated with more…

articles.title: Early Outcomes of Dorsal Onlay Buccal Mucosal Graft Urethroplasty for Female Urethral Stricture Disease: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.authors: Sarı H, Karaburun MC, Huseynli A et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: To evaluate the surgical, functional, and perioperative outcomes of Dorsal Onlay Buccal Mucosal Graft Urethroplasty (DO-BMGU) in women with Female urethral stricture (FUS) disease. Materials and Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed including women who underwent DO-BMGU for FUS at a single tertiary referral center between January 2018 and October 2025. The primary outcome was freedom from reintervention for symptomatic recurrence. Secondary outcomes included perioperative outcomes, complications, and changes in maximum urinary flow rate (Qmax) and postvoid residual urine volume (PVR). Results: Twenty women with a mean age of 52.9 ± 14.7 years were included. The median stricture length was 2 cm (IQR 2-3), and all patients had undergone previous urethral dilatation. Median operative time was 65 min (IQR 60-80), with a median hospital stay of 3 days (IQR 3-4). During a median follow-up of 12 months (IQR 12-24), 18 patients (90%) remained free from reintervention for symptomatic recurrence. Two patients developed recurrent symptomatic narrowing and were successfully managed with urethral dilatation. At the 3-month objective functional assessment, mean Qmax improved significantly from 6.1 ± 2.3 to 20.4 ± 5.8 mL/s (p < 0.001), while median PVR decreased from 125 mL (IQR 94.5-155) to 10 mL (IQR 10-40) (p < 0.001). No patient experienced major bleeding or urethrovaginal fistula. One patient (5%) developed mild de novo stress urinary incontinence, and postoperative complications were generally minor and managed conservatively. Conclusions: DO-BMGU was associated with favorable early objective functional outcomes and a high rate of freedom from reintervention for symptomatic recurrence, with few clinically significant complications in this small cohort. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are warranted to confirm the long-term durability of this technique.

articles.title: Prophylactic Carbetocin Versus Oxytocin and Blood Loss After Vaginal Delivery: Agent Selection and Confounding by Indication in a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Tsui WL, Ding DC
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Carbetocin is increasingly used for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) prophylaxis, but its selection in routine practice may bias comparisons with oxytocin. This observational study examined the association between the agent received and blood loss after vaginal delivery. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort included 559 women delivering vaginally in 2022-2023 who received carbetocin 100 μg intravenously (n = 474) or oxytocin 10 IU by infusion (n = 85). Gravimetric blood loss was analyzed using linear (primary), robust and median (co-primary) regression, and propensity score methods. Results: Carbetocin recipients more often underwent induction (63.3% vs. 43.5%), vacuum extraction (26.8% vs. 15.3%), and epidural analgesia (76.2% vs. 29.4%). Blood loss was higher with carbetocin before adjustment (223.7 vs. 180.0 mL, p = 0.003) but not after adjustment (β 12.72 mL, 95% CI -50.19 to 75.64, p = 0.691; robust p = 0.479; median p = 0.354). Propensity score results conflicted: inverse probability weighting showed higher blood loss with carbetocin (47.84 mL, p = 0.002), whereas matching and trimmed weighting did not. PPH occurred in 2.7% vs. 0% (p = 0.234). Conclusions: Carbetocin was preferentially used in higher-risk labors, indicating confounding by indication. Adjusted blood loss did not differ significantly, although a modest increase could not be excluded. The study was severely underpowered for PPH.

articles.title: Personalized Management of Hydrosalpinx Before IVF: A Narrative Review of Reproductive Outcomes and Treatment Timing.
articles.authors: Mihoci EC, Socolov D, Socolov RV et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Hydrosalpinx is an important and treatable cause of impaired in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, but the optimal intervention and its timing remain uncertain. This narrative review evaluates contemporary evidence to support individualized management before IVF. Materials and Methods: Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE records and publisher websites prioritized systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized trials, cohort studies, and international guidelines published from January 2015 to September 2026, while retaining earlier landmark studies. Evidence concerning salpingectomy, laparoscopic proximal tubal occlusion (PTO), aspiration, sclerotherapy, ovarian reserve, and treatment timing was synthesized narratively. Results: Clinically significant communicating hydrosalpinx should generally be treated before embryo transfer. Salpingectomy remains the most established definitive intervention, whereas laparoscopic PTO appears to provide comparable clinical pregnancy outcomes and may reduce tubo-ovarian vascular disruption in selected patients. Evidence regarding ovarian reserve after salpingectomy is conflicting: total oocyte yield is often preserved, although some studies report lower anti-Müllerian hormone, antral follicle count, or ipsilateral follicular recruitment. Aspiration and sclerotherapy may be considered when standard surgery is not feasible, but recurrence and limited randomized evidence restrict routine use. Observational studies do not establish a universally superior sequence of surgery and oocyte retrieval. Conclusions: Management should move from a uniform procedure-centered approach toward patient-centered selection. Reproductive age, ovarian reserve, laterality, pelvic adhesions, surgical complexity, and treatment urgency should guide both the intervention and its timing, while effective hydrosalpinx treatment should precede embryo transfer.

articles.title: Pelvic Floor Myofascial Dysfunction and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Mechanism-Based Narrative Review and Proposed Neuro-Musculoskeletal Model.
articles.authors: Barber JD, Biancaniello C
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), such as urgency, frequency, and pelvic discomfort, are often attributed to bladder-centered mechanisms; nonetheless, several patients exhibit overlapping pelvic floor dysfunctions that existing urologic models do not fully explain. Evidence from the musculoskeletal and pain literature demonstrates that myofascial trigger points within the pelvic floor are prevalent in patients with pelvic pain and urinary symptoms, potentially contributing to symptom generation. In this narrative review, we synthesized the literature on pelvic floor myofascial dysfunction, referred pain patterns, and autonomic regulation of bladder function to develop an integrated neuromusculoskeletal framework. Materials and Methods: PubMed and the TRIP Database were searched, with Elicit used for multi-database querying, abstract screening, and assisted data extraction; the final search was performed on 7 April 2026. Eligible publications addressed myofascial trigger point physiology, pelvic floor dysfunction, lower urinary tract function, or mechanisms of central or cross-sensitization and were required to describe or propose a physiological mechanism. Case reports were excluded. Seventeen publications were included in the synthesis. Results: The reviewed evidence supports a pathway in which active myofascial trigger points generate sustained nociceptive afferent inputs that converge with bladder afferents in the sacral spinal cord, potentially facilitating cross- and central sensitization, lowering the threshold for bladder sensation, and altering micturition reflex processing. The resulting amplification of afferent signaling provides a mechanistic basis for urgency, frequency, and pelvic pain in the absence of primary bladder pathology. Conclusions: This model integrates musculoskeletal and urological perspectives and suggests that, in a subset of patients, LUTS may reflect the central processing of peripheral musculoskeletal input. Incorporating pelvic floor assessment into clinical evaluations may improve diagnostic accuracy and provide more targeted management. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate this integrated pathway and its therapeutic implications.

articles.title: Serum WISP-1 and CTRP1 Levels in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Associations with HOMA-IR and Glycemic Status.
articles.authors: Akin OD, Misirlioglu NF, Karalok MH et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is characterized by insulin resistance and metabolic dysregulation, in which adipokines may be involved. We evaluated serum Wnt1-inducible signaling pathway protein-1 (WISP-1/CCN4) and C1q/TNF-related protein-1 (CTRP1) in women with GDM and normal glucose tolerance and assessed their relationships with glucose-insulin homeostasis and cross-sectional discriminatory ability. Materials and Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional biomarker study with prospective obstetric follow-up included 100 pregnant women at 24-28 weeks of gestation (50 GDM and 50 controls). WISP-1, CTRP1, HOMA-IR, and GDM status were assessed during the same gestational period; therefore, the principal biomarker analyses were cross-sectional. GDM was diagnosed using the one-step 75-g oral glucose tolerance test criteria recommended by the American Diabetes Association Standards of Care 2026. WISP-1 and CTRP1 were measured by ELISA. Group comparisons, correlation analyses, ROC analyses, nested logistic regression, and bootstrap internal validation were performed. Results: WISP-1 was higher in GDM than in controls (422.80 [387.10-471.85] vs. 315.00 [288.30-351.55] pg/mL; p < 0.001), as was CTRP1 (34.13 ± 6.74 vs. 26.50 ± 5.65 ng/mL; p < 0.001). WISP-1 showed a higher apparent AUC than CTRP1 in the present cohort (0.908 vs. 0.802; DeLong p = 0.034). In the final model adjusted for maternal age and BMI, both WISP-1 (adjusted OR per 1-SD increase 7.53, 95% CI 2.95-19.21; p < 0.001) and CTRP1 (3.61, 95% CI 1.45-8.99; p = 0.006) remained associated with GDM status after adjustment for these covariates. Within GDM, the age- and BMI-adjusted association between WISP-1 and HOMA-IR remained significant (partial ρ = 0.574; p < 0.001), whereas CTRP1 was not associated with HOMA-IR. Conclusions: WISP-1 and CTRP1 were elevated in GDM, with WISP-1 showing a stronger association with HOMA-IR and a higher internally derived AUC in this cohort. These findings support further investigation of WISP-1 and CTRP1 as exploratory metabolic biomarkers associated with GDM but do not establish diagnostic or predictive utility. Independent external validation is required before any potential clinical application.

articles.title: Detection of Cytomegalovirus in Chorionic Villi for the Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Infection: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Test Accuracy.
articles.authors: Mappa I, D'Antonio F, Ciolli P et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection following primary maternal infection in the first trimester carries the highest risk of long-term sequelae, yet prenatal diagnosis depends on amniotic fluid polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which cannot be performed before 17 weeks. Detection of CMV in chorionic villi at 11-14 weeks has been proposed to bring this information forward and to exclude CMV-related embryopathy. We systematically reviewed the published studies that have evaluated this test in order to determine its diagnostic accuracy. Materials and Methods: We conducted a systematic review of diagnostic test accuracy (PROSPERO CRD420261482510), and reported according to PRISMA-DTA. Five databases were searched up to 19 August 2026 without language or date restrictions. Eligible studies enrolled pregnancies with documented primary maternal infection and allowed reconstruction of a two-by-two table against CMV DNA in neonatal urine and/or saliva within three weeks of birth (with fetal or placental tissue accepted for pregnancies ending in termination). Screening, extraction and QUADAS-2 assessment were performed in duplicate and blinded. Overlapping cohorts were reduced to the largest, most completely verified report. Wilson score confidence intervals (CIs) were used; pooling was pre-specified only for four or more independent datasets. Results: Of 704 unique records, three independent cohorts in three primary publications were eligible, contributing 340 villus samples. The largest cohort (n = 330) gave a sensitivity of 40.5% (95% CI 27.0-55.5), specificity of 99.3% (97.5-99.8), positive predictive value of 89.5%, and negative predictive value of 92.0% at a prevalence of 12.7%. The remaining cohorts contributed four and six samples in turn, all true negatives. No study was at low risk of bias in all four QUADAS-2 domains; the cohort carrying the sensitivity estimate was at high risk in two, including verification of terminated pregnancies on placental tissue, whose net effect on sensitivity cannot be determined from the published data. Certainty was very low throughout. Conclusions: CMV PCR on chorionic villi is highly specific but misses approximately three infected fetuses in five, so a negative result does not reliably exclude congenital infection, and the proposition that it excludes embryopathy is unevaluated. Based on current evidence, it should not be used as a standalone basis for first-trimester decisions about…

articles.title: Empirical Antibiotic Initiation for Suspected Early-Onset Neonatal Infection in the Setting of Maternal GBS Screening and Intrapartum Antibiotic Prophylaxis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Zmelonek-Znamirowska A, Świercz G, Mlodawski J et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Maternal Group B Streptococcus (GBS) screening and intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis have reduced early-onset GBS disease. However, suspected early-onset neonatal infection (EONI) remains a broader clinical challenge, as signs prompting empirical antibiotic treatment may also occur in non-infectious disorders of postnatal adaptation. Therefore, this study evaluated the frequency of systemic antibiotic initiation for suspected EONI and the utilization and microbiological yield of blood cultures in a single-center cohort managed with routine maternal GBS screening and intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 2010 mother-newborn dyads delivered between 2019 and 2022. The primary outcome was systemic antibiotic therapy initiated within the first 72 h of life because of suspected EONI. Blood culture utilization and microbiological yield were analyzed separately from the primary treatment outcome. Positive blood culture findings were interpreted descriptively because of the small number of isolates and the possibility of contamination. Results: Empirical systemic antibiotic therapy for suspected EONI was initiated in 71 neonates (3.53%). The observed treatment rates among neonates born to GBS-colonized and non-colonized mothers were 16/402 (3.98%) vs. 55/1608 (3.42%) (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.67-2.01; p = 0.59). In an exploratory multivariable analysis, the adjusted OR for maternal GBS colonization and antibiotic initiation was 1.33 (95% CI 0.68-2.60; p = 0.408). Lower gestational age was the strongest associated factor. Treated neonates were more frequently preterm and had more respiratory disorders, NICU admissions, pPROM, and lower Apgar scores. Blood cultures were obtained in 79 neonates, including 63 treated for suspected EONI. Nine sampled neonates had positive blood cultures, including seven treated neonates; several isolates were compatible with contamination. No GBS isolates were detected among the sampled neonates. Conclusions: Empirical systemic antibiotics were initiated for suspected EONI in 3.53% of neonates. This treatment frequency does not estimate early-onset sepsis (EOS) incidence. The study did not detect a statistically significant association between maternal GBS colonization and antibiotic initiation, but the wide confidence intervals do not exclude clinically relevant increases in treatment. Selective blood culture sampling, possible contamination, and…

articles.title: Menopausal Symptom Burden and Self-Reported Poor Sleep Quality Among Japanese Working Women Aged 40 Years and Older: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Arima M, Edagawa Y
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Sleep-related complaints are common among women in midlife and may reflect not only insufficient sleep duration but also broader menopausal symptom burden. Although menopausal symptoms and sleep problems are known to be related, less is known about how menopausal symptom domains are associated with self-reported sleep quality among working women, particularly when objective sleep duration is considered. This exploratory cross-sectional study aimed to examine the association between menopausal symptom burden and self-reported poor sleep quality among Japanese working women aged 40 years and older, while accounting for objectively measured sleep duration. Materials and Methods: Participants completed questionnaires on sleep quality and menopausal symptoms and underwent objective sleep monitoring using a wearable electroencephalography device. Self-reported sleep quality was assessed using an item corresponding to the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and dichotomized into poor and good sleep quality. Menopausal symptoms were evaluated using the Simplified Menopausal Index, including vasomotor, psychological, and somatic domains, with higher scores indicating greater symptom burden. Results: Among 79 participants, 43 reported poor sleep quality and 36 reported good sleep quality. Women with poor sleep quality had higher total and domain-specific SMI scores and shorter objective sleep duration. In logistic regression analyses adjusted for age and objective sleep duration, total SMI score and each symptom domain were associated with poor sleep quality. These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses excluding the sleep-related SMI item from the total score and psychological domain score. Conclusions: Self-reported poor sleep quality among Japanese working women aged 40 years and older may reflect menopausal symptom burden beyond objectively measured sleep duration. The consistency of the findings across sensitivity analyses supports the robustness of this association. Sleep complaints may therefore serve as an accessible signal for recognizing menopausal symptom burden in clinical and occupational health settings.

articles.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Hysteroscopic Endometrial Resection Versus the 52-mg Levonorgestrel-Releasing Intrauterine System for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Küçük Z
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: To compare the effectiveness, durability, and patient-reported outcomes of hysteroscopic endometrial resection (ER) and the 52 mg levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) in women with medically refractory heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) without structural uterine pathology. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 242 women treated between January 2021 and December 2024, of whom 117 underwent ER and 125 received a 52 mg LNG-IUS. The primary outcome was hysterectomy during follow-up. Secondary outcomes included bleeding-related symptoms, treatment satisfaction, the change in the Female Sexual Function Index-6 (FSFI-6) total score, LNG-IUS discontinuation/expulsion, and subsequent reintervention. Baseline bleeding severity was characterized using the Pictorial Blood Assessment Chart (PBAC), hemoglobin, and serum ferritin, and abnormal uterine bleeding etiologies were classified according to PALM-COEIN. To address non-randomized treatment allocation, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was performed using prespecified baseline covariates. Hysterectomy was further evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Cox proportional-hazards models. Results: Baseline PBAC, hemoglobin, ferritin, and PALM-COEIN distributions were comparable between groups, whereas age, gravidity, parity, and baseline FSFI differed. After IPTW, all prespecified baseline covariates achieved adequate balance (absolute standardized mean differences < 0.10). Hysterectomy occurred in 3.4% of women after ER and 16.0% after LNG-IUS treatment. In the IPTW-weighted analysis, LNG-IUS was associated with a higher risk of hysterectomy (RR = 8.9, 95% CI 2.8-28.4; p < 0.001) and any bleeding-related symptom (RR = 12.8, 95% CI 5.0-32.9; p < 0.001), while treatment satisfaction was lower (RR = 0.48, 95% CI 0.39-0.59; p < 0.001). Hysterectomy-free survival was lower after LNG-IUS treatment (log-rank p < 0.001); the age- and parity-adjusted Cox model showed an HR of 11.6 (95% CI 3.4-39.4; p < 0.001), and the IPTW-weighted Cox model showed an HR of 9.8 (95% CI 3.0-32.1; p < 0.001). Firth regression similarly demonstrated a higher adjusted odds of hysterectomy with LNG-IUS (aOR = 18.9, 95% CI 5.0-71.9; p < 0.001). The 12-month FSFI total score remained lower with LNG-IUS in the IPTW-weighted analysis (B = -2.1, 95% CI -2.5 to -1.6; p < 0.001). Among women initially treated with LNG-IUS, 39.2%…

articles.title: Shifting High-Risk HPV Genotype Patterns in Histologically Confirmed Cervical HSIL: Temporal Changes and Differential Distribution in Invasive Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Díaz Del Arco C, Ramírez Mena M, Rojas Calles S et al.
articles.abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) genotypes differ in their oncogenic potential and contribution to cervical precancer and invasive cancer. We investigated temporal changes in HR-HPV genotype patterns in histologically confirmed cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and differences between 2022-2025 HSIL and invasive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in an opportunistic screening setting in Spain. This retrospective study included 371 patients with HSIL from 2011 to 2016, 411 with HSIL from 2022 to 2025, and 65 with SCC from 2022 to 2025. Among HR-HPV-positive HSIL, HPV16/18 frequency decreased from 65.7% to 50.8% (p = 0.003), accompanied by a lower mean number of detected genotypes. After adjustment for age and cytological diagnosis, the 2022-2025 period was associated with lower odds of HPV16 (OR 0.59) and HPV18 (OR 0.36) detection. Compared with 2022-2025 HSIL, SCC showed higher HPV16/18 frequency (75.0% vs. 50.8%; p = 0.003), fewer multiple infections, and lower representation of other HR-HPV genotypes. Exploratory birth-cohort analysis showed lower HPV16/18 frequency in women born in or after 1994, with higher individual frequencies of HPV52 and HPV58. HR-HPV genotype patterns in histologically confirmed HSIL varied over time and between birth cohorts, while invasive SCC showed greater HPV16/18 representation and lower HPV diversity.

articles.title: Clinical Pregnancy Outcomes Following Blastocyst Transfer Using Media with Different Hyaluronan Concentrations:A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Özel MK, Şahin F, Aşir F et al.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Hyaluronan-enriched embryo transfer media have been proposed to improve implantation and reproductive outcomes; however, their clinical benefit remains uncertain, particularly in frozen embryo transfer cycles. This study aimed to compare clinical pregnancy outcomes following blastocyst transfer using two commercially available media with different hyaluronan concentrations. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 421 blastocyst transfer cycles performed at a single IVF center between November 2024 and April 2026. Seventy-two cycles used a hyaluronan-enriched transfer medium (EmbryoGlue), and 349 used a medium with a lower hyaluronan concentration (SAGE 1-Step). The primary outcome was clinical pregnancy, defined as an intrauterine pregnancy with fetal cardiac activity. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed adjusting for maternal age and transfer type. Results: Clinical pregnancy occurred in 21/72 cycles (29.2%) in the hyaluronan-enriched medium group and 127/349 cycles (36.4%) in the lower-hyaluronan medium group (p = 0.30). The use of the hyaluronan-enriched medium was not significantly associated with clinical pregnancy after adjustment for maternal age and transfer type (aOR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.44-1.34, p = 0.352). Increasing maternal age was associated with lower odds of clinical pregnancy (aOR = 0.95 per year, 95% CI: 0.91-0.98, p = 0.002), whereas transfer type was not (aOR = 1.14, 95% CI: 0.59-2.21, p = 0.688). No significant differences were observed in either maternal age subgroup. Conclusions: In this predominantly frozen blastocyst-transfer cohort, no statistically significant difference in clinical pregnancy rates was observed between the hyaluronan-enriched and lower-hyaluronan transfer medium groups. Given the retrospective, non-randomized design, differences in medium composition beyond hyaluronan concentration, and potential residual confounding, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence or as demonstrating the absence of a clinically relevant effect. Prospective randomized studies evaluating live birth are warranted.

articles.title: Associations of Adjunctive Multistrain Probiotic/Prebiotic Supplementation with Microbiological Eradication and Semen Parameters in Infertile Men with Male Tract Infections: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Grande G, Graziani A, Mazzilli R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male tract infections (MTIs) represent a relevant cause of male factor infertility, yet microbiological persistence after antibiotic therapy remains common. This retrospective observational cohort study evaluated whether adjunctive multistrain probiotic/prebiotic supplementation was associated with microbiological and seminal outcomes in infertile men with microbiologically confirmed MTIs.
METHODS: One hundred infertile men with confirmed MTIs received either antibiotic therapy alone (n = 50) or antibiotics plus sequential multistrain probiotic/prebiotic supplementation (n = 50). The primary outcome was microbiological eradication. Secondary outcomes included changes in sperm concentration and total sperm count. Multivariable analyses adjusted for infertility duration, female partner age, pathogen category, and baseline semen parameters.
RESULTS: Microbiological eradication was achieved in 92.0% of patients receiving combined therapy versus 56.0% receiving antibiotics alone (adjusted OR 7.29, 95% CI 2.19-24.23; p = 0.001). Combined therapy was associated with greater improvements in sperm concentration and total sperm count, both when defined as any increase and as a ≥50% increase from baseline (all p < 0.01). These findings remained consistent across continuous analyses, pathogen-specific subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses excluding mixed infections.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive multistrain probiotic/prebiotic supplementation was associated with higher microbiological eradication rates and greater improvements in semen quality than antibiotic therapy alone. Prospective randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and define the role of microbiota-targeted therapies in managing infertility associated with MTIs.

articles.title: Maternal Characteristics, First-Trimester Biomarkers and Cell-Free DNA Fetal Fraction: A Single-Center NIPT Cohort over Ten Years.
articles.authors: Mureșan MC, Mureșan MB, Biriș DD et al.
articles.abstract: The fetal fraction (FF) of cell-free DNA determines the reliability of non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT); whether first-trimester placental biomarkers add information beyond maternal factors is unclear. We linked NIPT samples from a single fetal medicine center over ten years (1162 pregnancies) to first-trimester screening records and modeled log FF with hierarchical regression (maternal/technical covariates → PAPP-A → free β-hCG), cluster-robust standard errors, and an order-independent bootstrapped partition of the biomarker contribution. In the primary complete-case model (n = 292), FF was 3.4% lower per kg/m2 of BMI (95% CI -4.4 to -2.3) and 24% lower after IVF/ICSI. Free β-hCG was independently associated with FF (+11.0% per doubling of MoM, 95% CI +5.3 to +16.9; semi-partial R2 = 0.046), whereas the PAPP-A association was weaker and less consistent (+4.8%, 95% CI -0.6 to +10.4; semi-partial R2 = 0.010). The β-hCG association persisted after excluding high-risk NIPT calls, documented multiple gestation and IVF/ICSI, within platform-restricted subsets and with a restricted documentation-to-draw interval. No independent association with gestational age was identified in the primary model; low-FF and no-call results were too few for adjusted inference. Free β-hCG carries independent information on FF, consistent with, but not proof of, a link to syncytiotrophoblast biology.

articles.title: Metabolomic Profiling of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Its Subtypes Among Chinese Pregnant Women.
articles.authors: Alifu X, Qiu Y, Wang B et al.
articles.abstract: Background: This study aimed to explore first-trimester metabolic profiles associated with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and its glycemic subtypes. Methods: This nested case-control study included 90 women with GDM, comprising 30 with isolated fasting hyperglycemia (IFH), 30 with isolated post-load hyperglycemia (IPH), and 30 with combined hyperglycemia (CH), together with 30 women with normal glucose tolerance (NGT). Untargeted UHPLC-MS metabolomic profiling was performed on fasting plasma samples collected during the first trimester. Exploratory metabolic features were compared between GDM or its subtypes and NGT, and Spearman correlation analyses were performed to examine associations between candidate metabolic features and maternal fasting blood glucose (FBG), BMI, thyroid-related parameters, parity, education, and gestational weight gain. Exploratory pathway analyses were conducted to characterize potentially related metabolic processes. Results: At the exploratory threshold of VIP > 1 and nominal p < 0.05, 107 candidate metabolic features were observed in the GDM vs. NGT comparison, with 89, 76, and 123 candidate features observed in the IFH vs. NGT, IPH vs. NGT, and CH vs. NGT comparisons, respectively. These candidate features were mainly annotated as organoheterocyclic compounds and lipids and lipid-like molecules, with differences in chemical-class distributions across subtype comparisons. Organosulfur-related annotations were observed among the IFH candidate features, whereas alkaloid-related annotations were observed among the CH candidate features. No individual feature remained statistically significant after multiple-testing correction. Correlation analyses identified FDR-adjusted associations between selected candidate metabolic features and maternal FBG, BMI, and thyroid-related parameters. Exploratory pathway mapping highlighted processes related to lipid, amino acid, carbohydrate, and nucleotide metabolism. Conclusions: This exploratory study suggests that first-trimester plasma metabolic patterns may differ among women who subsequently develop different glycemic subtypes of GDM. The observed candidate features, clinical correlations, and pathway-level patterns provide hypotheses regarding metabolic heterogeneity in GDM but should not be considered validated biomarkers or subtype-specific metabolic signatures. Further studies using targeted metabolomics and larger independent cohorts are needed to confirm these observations.

articles.title: Immune Response Gene Polymorphisms and Cervical Cancer Susceptibility.
articles.authors: Dwornik R, Cylwik D, Białkowska K
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer (CxCa) remains one of the most common malignancies in women worldwide. Although almost all cases are associated with chronic infection with oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) types, not every infected woman develops the disease, indicating a significant role of genetic factors. This study reviewed 131 studies on genes related to immune system function and their impact on the risk of developing cervical cancer. The majority of the studies analyzed were conducted in Asian populations, primarily Chinese and Indian. The analysis focused in particular on polymorphisms in genes involved in the antiviral response, inflammatory processes, antigen presentation, and regulation of lymphocyte activity. Most of the evidence points to the importance of human leukocyte antigens (HLA) genes, Toll-like receptors (TLRs), interleukins (ILs), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), and interferons (IFNs). Variants in these genes may influence the effectiveness of HPV clearance, susceptibility to persistent infection, and the risk of progression of precancerous lesions to invasive cancer. It is worth emphasizing that identifying genetic risk factors may, in the future, support the development of personalized prevention strategies, screening tests, and the assessment of the individual risk of disease. Nevertheless, most available findings warrant further validation in large and diverse populations. In summary, cervical cancer is the result of a complex interaction between HPV infection and the host's genetic predisposition. Research on immune response genes provides valuable information about the mechanisms of disease development, and may contribute to improved methods of prevention and early detection.

articles.title: USP30 Beyond Mitophagy: A Context-Dependent Deubiquitinase in Cancer Progression.
articles.authors: Liao W, Xu N
articles.abstract: Ubiquitin-specific protease 30 (USP30) is a mitochondrial outer membrane-associated deubiquitinase best known for antagonizing PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin-dependent ubiquitination and suppressing mitophagy. This established role has linked USP30 to mitochondrial quality control and neurodegenerative diseases. However, emerging studies in cancer have expanded the biological scope of USP30, revealing functions that cannot be explained by mitophagy regulation alone. USP30 regulates diverse cancer-associated substrates through deubiquitination, thereby affecting protein abundance, subcellular localization, protein interactions, and downstream transcriptional programs. These substrate-dependent effects influence mitochondrial dynamics, lipid synthesis, glucose and amino acid metabolism, redox homeostasis, apoptosis, ferroptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, T-cell exhaustion, and therapy resistance. Although most studies indicate tumor-promoting roles of USP30 in hepatocellular carcinoma, breast cancer, colorectal cancer, oral squamous cell carcinoma, ovarian cancer, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and leukemia models, context-dependent tumor-restraining activities have also been reported. In this Review, we examine cancer-associated functions of USP30 that extend beyond its established role in PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy, discuss the spatial and substrate-dependent mechanisms underlying these activities, and highlight opportunities and challenges for therapeutic targeting.

articles.title: Maternal Plasma Proteomic Signatures Distinguish Preeclampsia from Healthy Pregnancy but Not Early-Onset from Late-Onset Subtypes: A Leakage-Free Machine-Learning and Explainability Study.
articles.authors: Yasar S, Melekoglu R, Basak Turkmen N et al.
articles.abstract: Early-onset (EOPE) and late-onset (LOPE) preeclampsia are clinically distinct, but their molecular differences are incompletely defined. Using a strictly leakage-free pipeline, we re-examined maternal plasma proteomes of EOPE, LOPE, and healthy pregnancy (HP) and asked whether the subtypes are separable at the proteome level. Label-free LC-MS/MS proteomes comprising 370 proteins from 46 women (HP, n = 18; EOPE, n = 17; LOPE, n = 11) were analysed using limma and fully nested cross-validation, in which feature selection, class balancing, and tuning were confined to the outer training folds; model explanations used SHAP and feature-selection stability. Observed selection frequencies far exceeded a random-selection null (for example, complement factor D was selected in all 15 outer folds, Wilson 95% confidence interval 0.80 to 1.00, against an expected frequency of 0.07), indicating that the stability was not a chance artefact. Discrimination is summarised as the mean ± standard deviation across the 5-fold × 3-repeat (15) outer test folds; because the single best-performing classifier was chosen on outer-fold performance, the reported area under the curve is modestly optimistic (on average by 0.04, and by up to 0.10 relative to the median of the three classifiers), even though the leakage-free procedure was applied identically to each classifier. Disease-versus-healthy contrasts were strong and concordant, with 10 and eight differentially abundant proteins identified for EOPE and LOPE, respectively, and AUROCs ranging from 0.88 to 0.90. EOPE showed a complement/acute-phase/coagulation signature, whereas LOPE showed an apolipoprotein/lipid signature, with limma, stability analysis, and SHAP yielding convergent findings. By contrast, the EOPE-versus-LOPE comparison identified no differentially abundant proteins and showed no reliable multivariate separation. A post hoc sensitivity analysis (two-sample t-test, two-sided, α = 0.05) indicated that the discovery cohort (early-onset n = 17, late-onset n = 11) had 80% power only for very large per-protein standardised differences (Cohen's d ≥ 1.13, or d ≥ 2.10 after Bonferroni correction across the 370 proteins), and only 24% and 51% power to detect medium (d = 0.5) and large (d = 0.8) effects; the absence of a detectable early-versus-late difference is therefore consistent with limited power for small-to-moderate effects rather than proven biological equivalence. In an independent ELISA cohort (n = 87), EOPE…

articles.title: Neochloris sp. PA3, an Oligotrophic Desert Oasis Microalga, Exhibits Differential Cytotoxicity and Apoptosis-Associated Effects in Human Cancer Cells.
articles.authors: Castillo-Roque M, Ramos-Silva JA, Fuentes-Garibay JA et al.
articles.abstract: Microalgae are increasingly recognized as valuable sources of natural products with potential applications in cancer prevention and therapy due to their ability to produce structurally diverse bioactive metabolites. In the present study, methanolic extracts from microalgal strains isolated from the oligotrophic desert oasis of the Cuatro Ciénegas Basin (Mexico) were evaluated for their antioxidant activity and in vitro cytotoxic effects against human breast (MCF7), colon (Caco2), prostate (DU145), leukemia (MOLT-4), and ovarian (OVCAR-3) cancer cell lines. The isolates were identified by rbcL gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis as members of the genera Asterarcys, Chlorella, and Neochloris. Antioxidant properties were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays, whereas cytotoxicity was assessed using the MTT assay and apoptosis-associated cellular responses were investigated by morphological analysis, acridine orange/ethidium bromide staining, and measurement of executioner caspase-3/7 activity. Neochloris sp. PA3 showed the highest total antioxidant capacity and detectable ferrous ion-chelating activity, whereas Chlorella sp. PS exhibited the strongest superoxide radical scavenging activity. Among the evaluated strains, the methanolic extract of Neochloris sp. PA3 exhibited the most favorable overall antiproliferative profile, with IC50 values of 17.1, 19.0, and 19.1 µg/mL against MCF7, Caco2, and DU145 cells, respectively, while displaying markedly lower cytotoxicity toward the non-tumorigenic Vero and Detroit 548 cell lines, indicating differential cytotoxicity between the tested cancer and non-tumorigenic cell models. The extract induced time-dependent reductions in cell viability, morphological and nuclear alterations consistent with apoptotic cell death, and increased executioner caspase-3/7 activity. Collectively, these findings provide preliminary in vitro evidence of differential cytotoxicity and an apoptosis-associated cellular response in Neochloris sp. PA3-treated cancer cells.

articles.title: Exploratory Analysis of Selected MicroRNAs as Tissue-Based Candidate Biomarkers in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Kozłowski M, Borzyszkowska D, Lubkowski M et al.
articles.abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate the expression and exploratory diagnostic potential of selected microRNAs (miRNAs) in ovarian cancer tissue compared with benign ovarian lesions. Tissue samples from 24 patients with epithelial ovarian cancer and 22 patients with benign ovarian lesions were analyzed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Ten candidate miRNAs were assessed; six met the predefined detection criteria and were retained for analysis. Group differences were tested with non-parametric methods and false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and menopausal status. Survival analyses were exploratory. miR-381-3p was downregulated, whereas miR-582-5p and miR-425-5p were upregulated in ovarian cancer compared with benign ovarian lesions; all three differences remained significant after FDR correction. miR-425-5p showed the highest individual diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.854) and remained associated with ovarian cancer after adjustment for age and menopausal status (OR = 7.84; 95% CI = 2.05-29.97; p = 0.003). This association was also retained in Firth penalized logistic regression. An exploratory three-miRNA panel achieved an apparent AUC of 0.858 but did not significantly outperform miR-425-5p alone (DeLong p = 0.596); its optimism-corrected bootstrap AUC was 0.822. No significant associations with survival were identified. miR-425-5p was the strongest candidate biomarker in this exploratory tissue-based study. Independent validation is required before clinical application.

articles.title: Multiscale Interactome Analysis Prioritizes Candidate Herbs and Compounds for Diabetic Retinopathy.
articles.authors: Ahn YS, Chae JI, Han SH et al.
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a leading cause of preventable vision loss among working-age adults, arises from chronic hyperglycemic injury to the retinal microvasculature; current interventions such as anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injection are largely reactive, and mechanism-anchored herbal options remain undefined. We constructed a multiscale interactome and applied a biased random-walk diffusion model to prioritize herbal candidates, candidate compounds, and mechanisms for DR. Herb-ingredient records were drawn from OASIS; ingredient targets from DrugBank, TTD, and STITCH; and disease genes from DisGeNET. For each herb and compound, we computed diffusion profiles, correlated them with the DR profile, and assessed target-overlap significance by hypergeometric test. Eleven herbs combining high correlation (top 5%) with significant overlap (p < 0.05) were retained, led by Pini Koraiensis Semen (0.0263), Benincasae Exocarpium (0.0183), and Veratri Rhizoma Et Radix (0.0162); none had been previously investigated for DR. CASP3 emerged as a target shared by all eleven herbs, and enrichment analysis highlighted the advanced glycation end product-receptor for AGE (AGE-RAGE), TNF, IL-17, and NF-κB pathways alongside apoptosis and reactive-oxygen-species responses. Compound-level analysis recovered evidence-supported quercetin, resveratrol, oleic acid, luteolin, and diosgenin and nominated tectorigenin and cucurbitacins as novel candidates. This framework recapitulates known DR biology and elevates testable multi-target leads that warrant experimental validation for diabetic retinopathy.

articles.title: Endometriosis-Associated Infertility: Molecular Mechanisms and Evidence-Based Clinical Management.
articles.authors: Chang KJ, Lai TH
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, estrogen-dependent inflammatory disease and a major contributor to female infertility. Endometriosis-associated infertility arises from interacting anatomical and biological mechanisms, including pelvic adhesions and tubal dysfunction, reduced ovarian reserve, altered follicular and oocyte competence, oxidative stress, immune dysregulation, and impaired endometrial function. This narrative review integrates current concepts of disease pathogenesis with evidence-based fertility management. It first examines the molecular, cellular, and immune processes that support ectopic lesion establishment and may impair reproduction. It then discusses diagnostic phenotyping, infertility evaluation, prognostic tools, medical suppression, fertility-preserving surgery, intrauterine insemination, and in vitro fertilization. Particular attention is given to the strength and clinical relevance of current evidence, including surgery for ovarian endometrioma before assisted reproduction, prolonged gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist pretreatment, fresh versus frozen embryo transfer, and the use of intracytoplasmic sperm injection without male-factor infertility. Emerging anti-angiogenic, immunomodulatory, antioxidant, stem-cell, and gene- or epigenetic-based interventions remain investigational. Because neither a single treatment nor a single assisted-reproduction protocol is optimal for all patients, management should integrate age, ovarian reserve, symptom burden, disease phenotype, prior surgery, coexisting infertility factors, and reproductive priorities. Mechanistically informed clinical trials using live birth and patient-centered outcomes are needed to advance precision fertility care.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Predictive CSF Biomarkers in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (iNPH): A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Procopio E, Accattatis A, Stroscio CA et al.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a progressive disorder clinically characterized by Hakim's triad: gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary incontinence. iNPH treatment consists of neurosurgical implantation of a ventriculoperitoneal CSF diversion, whose outcome depends on an early and correct diagnosis. Currently, there is no specific diagnostic test to perform preoperatively. Still, the combination of neurological examination, gait analysis, neurocognitive evaluation, and the tap test is useful to suggest when surgery is indicated. Our systematic review aims to identify diagnostic and outcome predictor CSF biomarkers (BM) in iNPH. The present systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library databases were first consulted in April 2025 and updated in May 2026. Studies were selected using the terms "idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus" and "CSF biomarkers" under Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) as inclusion criteria. The eligibility of a record was defined according to the study title and abstract. The QUADAS-2, QUIPS, ROBINS-I V2, and RobVis tools were used to assess the risk of bias. Ninety-nine records were included in this systematic review. Amyloid proteins (Aβ40-42), followed by tau (τT, τP-181) and neuroinflammatory proteins were the most frequently CSF BM analyzed in patients with iNPH. ELISA was the most used method to measure BM in CSF samples. Forty-seven records investigated the potential diagnostic role of CSF BM; comparisons were frequently made among iNPH, Alzheimer's disease (AD), and healthy control CSF samples. Regarding outcome prediction, 28 records examined CSF BM, with heterogeneous comparisons such as lumbar versus ventricular CSF or shunted versus non-shunted iNPH CSF samples, including healthy controls and iNPH. Seven records proposed both the diagnostic and predictive role of some CSF biomarkers, especially for tau proteins and Aβ42. On the other hand, 17 records concluded that neither a diagnostic nor a predictive role could be proposed for the CSF BM they analyzed. However, these records increased knowledge about an iNPH CSF pattern. Collecting and analyzing CSF samples from iNPH patients can be advantageous in differential diagnosis with other similar neurodegenerative disorders, especially AD, and therefore a predictor of neurosurgical outcomes. Combined biomarker panels should be integrated in standardized protocols, measuring: Aβ42,…

articles.title: Molecular Genetics and Reproductive Genomic Medicine in Cleft Lip and Palate: Current Evidence, Preimplantation Testing, and Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Fan R, Shen H, Liu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Cleft lip and palate (CLP) is a common congenital craniofacial anomaly with heterogeneous clinical manifestations and complex etiologies. Current evidence indicates that CLP arises from the combined effects of Mendelian syndromic disorders, rare pathogenic variants, common susceptibility loci, non-coding regulatory variants, epigenetic regulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and maternal environmental exposures. Although reconstructive surgery and multidisciplinary care remain central to treatment, families with recurrent CLP or a family history of orofacial clefts increasingly seek reproductive counseling and genetic risk assessment before pregnancy. Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) may provide a clinically meaningful option when a pathogenic variant, chromosomal abnormality, or clearly defined familial haplotype is identified. However, most non-syndromic CLP cases are polygenic or multifactorial, and the application of preimplantation genetic testing for polygenic disorders (PGT-P) remains limited by modest predictive accuracy, population-specific transferability, embryo-number constraints, incomplete penetrance, variants of uncertain significance, and uncertain long-term clinical utility. This narrative review summarizes the clinical phenotypes and genomic architecture of CLP, evaluates the principles and current limitations of preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M) and PGT-P, and discusses psychosocial and ethical issues in reproductive decision-making. We propose that PGT for CLP should be positioned as part of a stepwise counseling framework rather than as a universal preventive strategy. Future progress will depend on standardized phenotyping, multi-ancestry genomic databases, functional validation of candidate variants, transparent risk communication, and shared decision-making that respects both reproductive autonomy and the uncertainty of genomic prediction.

articles.title: Reversibility of Male Factor Infertility: Mechanisms and Evidence from the Literature.
articles.authors: La Vignera S, Calogero AE, Cannarella R et al.
articles.abstract: Male factor infertility contributes to approximately 50% of reproductive failure in couples worldwide. We conducted a narrative critical review synthesizing evidence from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, and clinical practice guidelines on reversible and irreversible causes of male infertility, examining hormonal, surgical, pharmacological, lifestyle, and drug-induced etiologies. The majority of identifiable etiologies demonstrate some degree of reversibility. Varicocele (prevalence 25-40% in infertile men) achieves natural pregnancy rates of 30-40% after varicocelectomy. Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism responds to gonadotropin therapy with spermatogenesis induction in 90-95% of cases. Obstructive azoospermia achieves ductal patency rates of 85-97% with microsurgical reconstruction. Male accessory gland inflammation is reversible with prompt antibiotic therapy.
