Spermiotoxic drug exposures-including anabolic-androgenic steroids, sulfasalazine, and chemotherapy-show variable reversibility depending on agent and duration of exposure. Normogonadotropic normotestosteronemic oligozoospermia represents a commonly encountered phenotype that may respond to empirical medical therapy. Lifestyle modifications demonstrate measurable benefits in selected patients. Irreversible causes include Klinefelter syndrome, Y-chromosome AZFa/b microdeletions, and severe post-chemotherapy damage. Systematic andrological evaluation, including comprehensive drug history, is essential to identify treatable causes and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Integrated Network Toxicology, Molecular Dynamics Simulation and In Vitro Assays Identify EGFR, ESR1 and IGF1 as Core Mediators of Bisphenol S-Exacerbated Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
articles.authors: Liu J, Ye G, Liu X et al.
articles.abstract: Bisphenol S (BPS), an environmental endocrine disruptor, has been implicated in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), but its underlying molecular targets remain largely uncharacterized. Here, this study integrated network toxicology, molecular simulations and in vitro cellular assays to identify key mediators of BPS-associated PCOS. A total of 199 overlapping target genes between BPS exposure and PCOS were screened from public databases, predicted hub genes were extracted via protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and 30 core hub genes were enriched in oxidative stress, hormone response, inflammation, cell-cycle regulation, and PI3K-Akt, FoxO, AGE-RAGE, and endocrine resistance pathways by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis. Using molecular docking simulations found that the top 15 hub proteins exhibited favorable binding affinities for BPS, with binding free energies below -5.0 kcal/mol. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that BPS binding induced only minor conformational perturbations in EGFR and ESR1, with negligible effects on backbone stability, core domain flexibility, global compactness and surface properties. In contrast, BPS association effectively dampened global backbone fluctuations and the residue-level mobility of IGF1, and the intermolecular hydrogen bond strength followed the order IGF1 > EGFR > ESR1. In KGN cells, BPS suppressed cell viability and proliferation in a time- and dose-dependent manner while upregulating the protein levels of EGFR, ESR1 and IGF1; notably, IGF1 was most sensitive to low-dose BPS exposure. These findings suggest that BPS may exacerbate PCOS progression by upregulating EGFR, ESR1 and IGF1 to inhibit granulosa cell growth, and thereby disrupt ovarian oxidative homeostasis, hormone signaling, insulin metabolism and cell-cycle regulation via the PI3K-Akt and FoxO pathways. This study provides a theoretical framework for assessing the reproductive health risks of BPS, and lays a foundation for further experimental validation and population-based epidemiological research.

articles.title: The Impact of Vitamin E Intake on Cardiometabolic Outcomes of Testosterone Replacement Therapy in Men with Late-Onset Hypogonadism.
articles.authors: Krysiak R, Szkróbka W, Kowalcze K et al.
articles.abstract: Androgen deficiency is associated with an increased risk of cardiometabolic complications, whereas vitamin E may exert protective effects against cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. This pilot prospective cohort study examined whether cardiometabolic outcomes observed during exogenous testosterone therapy differed according to vitamin E intake in men with insufficient endogenous testosterone production. Three cohorts of men with late-onset hypogonadism (LOH) (n = 29 per group), matched for age, smoking status, body mass index, and baseline testosterone concentration, were classified according to vitamin E intake as low, adequate, or high; 29 men without LOH served as controls. Men with LOH received intramuscular testosterone injections every three weeks for six months. Cardiometabolic parameters were assessed before and after treatment, including biochemical markers, carotid intima-media thickness, retinal vascular sclerotic changes, and estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk. Compared with controls, men with LOH had higher HOMA-IR, LDL cholesterol, uric acid, fibrinogen, homocysteine, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), carotid intima-media thickness, and estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk. Elevations in homocysteine, hsCRP, and UACR were more pronounced in men with low or high vitamin E intake than in those with adequate intake. Testosterone levels increased during treatment in all groups. Improvements were observed in most cardiometabolic parameters in men with adequate vitamin E intake, whereas changes were limited to HOMA-IR in those with low intake. In men with high intake, no significant changes were observed except for a decrease in HDL cholesterol. At study completion, carotid intima-media thickness and retinal vascular sclerotic changes in men with adequate vitamin E intake did not differ significantly from those in controls. Changes in assessed risk factors correlated with increases in testosterone levels and mean daily vitamin E intake. These findings suggest an association between vitamin E intake and cardiometabolic outcomes observed during testosterone therapy in men with testosterone deficiency.

articles.title: Progesterone Beyond Pituitary Suppression in Assisted Reproduction: Peripheral Signalling, Gamete Biology, Endometrial Competence and Precision Therapeutic Use.
articles.authors: Łukaszuk A, Łukaszuk J, Wocławek-Potocka I et al.
articles.abstract: Progesterone is indispensable to assisted reproduction, yet the phrase "progesterone effect" collapses non-equivalent biological processes. Classical progesterone receptors (PGR-A and PGR-B), progestin and adipoQ receptor-family proteins, progesterone receptor membrane components 1 and 2 (PGRMC1/2), and an unresolved proximal sensor upstream of sperm CatSper operate over different timescales and with unequal evidence for direct ligand binding. In the ovary, PGRMC-associated complexes regulate granulosa-cell survival, mitosis and oocyte competence, although much causal evidence is non-human. In sperm, progesterone-evoked CatSper activation is robust, whereas the influential ABHD2 hydrolase model was challenged by human data in 2026. In endometrium, receptivity emerges from temporally ordered PGR-dependent epithelial-stromal, immune, metabolic and vascular programmes; "progesterone resistance" is therefore better treated as a family of molecular states than as a single diagnosis. Oral, vaginal, subcutaneous and intramuscular regimens generate different systemic and uterine exposures, and serum progesterone is an exposure marker rather than a direct assay of tissue response. We integrate these levels into an exposure-target engagement-tissue state-outcome framework. This framework explains why universal serum thresholds and unselected rescue strategies remain uncertain and defines the experiments and trials needed for mechanism-informed luteal support and frozen embryo transfer.

articles.title: Neuropelveology in Endometriosis: Pain Mechanisms, Diagnostic Implications, and Surgical Decision-Making.
articles.authors: Gabriela CH, Loza López EC, Bautista Gonzalez MF et al.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a systemic, estrogen dependent neuroinflammatory-mediated disease affecting approximately 10-15% of women of reproductive age. Clinical manifestations include chronic pelvic pain (CPP), dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, dyschezia, dysuria, and infertility. Endometriosis-associated pain is multifactorial and comprises overlapping nociceptive, neuropathic, and nociplastic pain phenotypes driven by persistent inflammation, neuroangiogenesis, peripheral nerve involvement, and central sensitization (CS). These mechanisms may sustain pain beyond lesion excision, highlighting the importance of pelvic nervous system (PNS) involvement. This narrative review examines the role of neuropelveology (NP) in endometriosis, focusing on pain mechanisms, diagnostic implications, and surgical decision making. NP integrates pelvic neuroanatomy and neurophysiology into structured neurological assessment, pain mapping, symptom localization, and nerve sparing surgery. Current evidence suggests that NP may complement conventional evaluation in selected patients with refractory pain, neuropathic symptoms, discordance between symptom severity and imaging findings, or suspected involvement of the sacral plexus or sciatic nerve. Recognizing distinct pain phenotypes may support individualized treatment planning by balancing lesion excision with neural preservation and identifying patients who may benefit from multidisciplinary pain management, rehabilitation, neurolysis, or neuromodulation. Although current evidence remains limited, NP should be considered a complementary framework rather than a replacement for established endometriosis management. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized diagnostic criteria and long-term functional outcomes are needed to define its clinical utility.

articles.title: Ebola Virus Disease in Pregnancy: Maternal-Fetal Outcomes, Vertical Transmission, and Implications for Vaccination-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Hashim KNH, Mustafa HM, Adam I
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ebola virus disease (EVD) during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal illness and exceptionally poor fetal and neonatal outcomes. However, pregnancy-specific evidence remains limited by small cohorts, heterogeneous outbreak settings, and the historical exclusion of pregnant women from clinical research. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes, placental involvement and vertical transmission, clinical management, and vaccination during pregnancy. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through May 2026 using predefined terms related to EVD, pregnancy, maternal and neonatal outcomes, placental infection, vertical transmission, and vaccination. WHO and CDC guidance documents and reference lists of relevant publications were also reviewed. Two reviewers independently screened records and assessed full texts. Data was extracted using a standardized template and independently verified by a second reviewer. A total of 55 publications met the inclusion criteria and were narratively synthesized. Results: Historical reports documented very high maternal mortality and pregnancy loss; however, more recent studies do not indicate that pregnancy independently increases maternal mortality among patients with EVD. A systematic review and meta-analysis estimated maternal mortality at 67.8% (95% CI 49.8-83.7), fetal loss at 76.9% (95% CI 45.0-98.3), and neonatal mortality at 98.5% (95% CI 84.9-100). Contemporary data from the 2018-2020 Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak similarly found no increased maternal mortality associated with pregnancy, although fetal and perinatal outcomes remained poor. Evidence supports placental involvement in EVD, but placental viral RNA detection should be distinguished from confirmed fetal or neonatal infection. Pregnancy-specific vaccine evidence now includes a Phase 3 trial of Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo in 2013 pregnant women, demonstrating favorable safety and immunogenicity profiles. Conclusions: EVD in pregnancy remains associated with substantial pregnancy loss and neonatal mortality despite improvements in maternal care. Important gaps persist regarding maternal-fetal transmission, long-term infant outcomes, and optimal management strategies, highlighting the need for further research.

articles.title: Channel-Focused Modified TURP for Post-Radiation Bladder Outlet Obstruction: A Case Series.
articles.authors: Lee JH, Kim JH, Oh KT
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bladder outlet obstruction (BOO) after prostate radiotherapy is surgically challenging because of radiation-induced tissue changes and functional complications. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of channel-focused modified transurethral resection of the prostate (RadTURP) for post-radiation BOO. Methods: This retrospective case series included 11 patients who underwent RadTURP for post-radiation BOO between 2014 and 2025. Outcomes included symptom scores, voiding parameters, and postoperative complications. Pre-post changes were assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Results: Median age was 75 years and median follow-up was 29 months. The median resection proportion was 24%. IPSS improved from 27 to 10 (p = 0.003), QoL from 5 to 3 (p = 0.007), OABSS from 12 to 6 (p = 0.016), Qmax from 6 to 17 mL/s (p = 0.006), and PVR from 59 to 0 mL (p = 0.047). De novo urinary incontinence occurred in four patients (36.4%), including two (18.2%) with persistent stress urinary incontinence requiring artificial urinary sphincter implantation. Among six patients undergoing symptom-driven postoperative cystoscopy, five (83.3%) had stone/calcification-related findings requiring energy-free endoscopic removal. One patient (9.1%) developed a urethral stricture requiring repeated dilation. Conclusions: In this small case series, channel-focused RadTURP was associated with improved urinary symptoms and voiding function after prostate radiotherapy. However, de novo urinary incontinence occurred in 36.4% of patients, highlighting an important postoperative safety concern for patient counseling and selection. Larger studies are needed to define durability and safety.

articles.title: Chronic Venous Disease in Pregnancy: Pathophysiology, Diagnostic Pitfalls, and a Trimester-Stratified Management Framework-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Stan Bran RS, Solomon Condriuc IP, Haba RM et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic venous disease (CVD) in pregnancy is common, poorly codified, and interpreted with diagnostic thresholds, severity instruments and treatment algorithms all derived outside pregnancy. This narrative review synthesises the mechanistic, epidemiological, diagnostic and therapeutic literature, keeping pregnancy-specific evidence separate from evidence extrapolated from non-pregnant populations. Gestational change is characterised principally by increased venous capacitance and vein-wall distension; ambulatory venous hypertension was not demonstrated in the two pregnancy studies assessing it; and new reflux develops in a minority, undetectable postpartum in the one study reporting it. Physiological adaptation, CVD and thrombotic pathology overlap clinically, deep vein thrombosis and superficial vein thrombosis being at once the principal differential diagnoses and potential complications. Management is correspondingly conservative: compression relieves symptoms but has not been shown to prevent varicose veins, routine initiation of venoactive drugs is not supported, and intervention is deferred other than in exceptional circumstances. A venous finding first detected in pregnancy warrants postpartum reassessment before it is taken for established disease. A trimester-stratified framework spanning preconception to late postpartum reassessment is proposed; it is evidence-informed rather than prospectively validated, and is not a guideline.

articles.title: Postoperative Opioid-Free Multistep Opiranserin Infusion Versus Fentanyl Patient-Controlled Analgesia After Breast or Minimally Invasive Gynecologic Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Kim Y, Park M, Choi S et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Women undergoing breast or gynecologic surgery face high postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) risk, which often prompts discontinuation of opioid patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). Since anticipated opioid use is an Apfel risk factor, we examined a postoperative opioid-free analgesic regimen using opiranserin, previously evaluated only as an adjunct. Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 150 women undergoing breast or minimally invasive gynecologic surgery received a multistep opiranserin infusion via a PCA pump without demand boluses (n = 77) or fentanyl demand bolus PCA (n = 73). The opiranserin infusion ended at 10 h; fentanyl PCA remained connected throughout. The primary outcome was resting numeric rating scale (NRS, 0-10) at 24 h, by which time the infusion had been complete for 14-15 h; secondary outcomes were post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) and 6 h NRS, PONV, and early discontinuation. Results: Resting NRS did not differ significantly during the infusion (PACU p = 0.965; 6 h p = 0.675), with a larger difference at 24 h. The adjusted 24 h difference was 0.58 points higher with opiranserin (95% CI, 0.04 to 1.12; p = 0.036) by covariance analysis on pre-treatment covariates and 0.55 (0.02 to 1.09) by inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting; the point estimates were below the minimal clinically important difference of 1 point, but the confidence intervals do not exclude a clinically relevant increase in pain, and the estimate was nonsignificant after adjusting for non-opioid adjuncts (p = 0.177). Moderate or severe pain at 24 h was more frequent with opiranserin (19.5% vs. 8.2%; adjusted odds ratio, 3.76; 95% CI, 1.34 to 11.82). PONV (9.1% vs. 11.0%), rescue analgesia (26.0% vs. 17.8%), and early discontinuation (10.4% vs. 9.6%) were similar. Rescue opioids were available to both groups but used by one fentanyl-group patient and by none receiving opiranserin. Conclusions: The regimen eliminated postoperative opioid exposure, with resting pain scores that differed by less than 1 NRS point on average, although a clinically relevant increase cannot be excluded. With coverage fixed at 10 h, the 24 h difference cannot be separated into a shortfall of the agent and a shortfall of coverage. The anticipated PONV reduction was not observed, possibly in the context of low event rates and routine antiemetic prophylaxis.

articles.title: Urinary Incontinence Among Community-Dwelling Older Women: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Characterization of Clinical Features, Urinary Habits, and Perceptions.
articles.authors: Cárcamo-Cid C, García-Tobar K, Fuentes-Ramirez A et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objective: Urinary incontinence (UI) negatively affects wellbeing. As it is often seen as a normal part of aging, management is frequently delayed or ignored, challenging healthy aging. This study aimed to characterize UI in community-dwelling older women by assessing sociodemographic aspects, symptoms, pelvic floor muscle strength, urinary habits, and perceptions regarding UI. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study in older women from four communities in Chile. After educational sessions on UI, women voluntarily enrolled. We applied the ICIQ-SF, and pelvic floor muscle strength was evaluated using the Modified Oxford Scale. We also collected information on UI-related topics. Results: Among 32 older women assessed, 40.6% had stress UI, 3.1% had urgency UI, and 56.3% exhibited mixed UI. The mean ICIQ-SF score was 13.75 ± 3.5, corresponding to severe UI, with a mean score of interference on daily life of 6.75 ± 1.92. Older women exhibited low pelvic floor muscle strength (Oxford: 1.97 ± 1.03), a high prevalence of cystocele (84.4%; n = 27), and coexisting fecal incontinence (40.6%; n = 13). An association between UI severity and pelvic floor muscle strength was evaluated (Spearman's ρ = -0.242, n = 32), but the weak inverse correlation was not statistically significant (p = 0.180). Conclusions: Community-dwelling older women with UI exhibited substantial symptom severity accompanied by low pelvic floor muscle strength, pelvic organ prolapse, coexisting fecal incontinence, and potentially modifiable UI-related habits and perceptions. Although these findings derive from an exploratory sample, they highlight opportunities for community-based education, early detection, and pelvic floor health interventions to support healthy aging.

articles.title: Comparison of Modified Natural Cycle Versus True Natural Cycle Frozen Embryo Transfer in Terms of Clinical Pregnancy and Live Birth Outcomes: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Yetkin Yıldırım G, Uzaldı İ, Yelke TV et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Natural cycle frozen embryo transfer (FET) has become an increasingly preferred approach for endometrial preparation in ovulatory women. Whether modified natural cycle (mNC) protocols incorporating human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) for ovulation triggering provide any reproductive advantage over true natural cycle (tNC) protocols remains controversial. This study aimed to compare pregnancy and live birth outcomes between mNC-FET and tNC-FET cycles. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analysed 256 frozen-thawed embryo transfer cycles in ovulatory women at a single tertiary centre between January 2014 and December 2024. Of these, 91 cycles used an mNC protocol (mNC-FET group) and 165 cycles used a tNC protocol (tNC-FET group). All transfers involved a single day-5 good-quality or top-quality blastocyst, with identical luteal phase support. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, ovarian reserve markers, and embryological parameters were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of live birth. Results: The mNC-FET and tNC-FET groups were comparable with respect to age (29.88 ± 4.28 vs. 29.96 ± 3.78 years, p = 0.880), body mass index (24.86 ± 5.27 vs. 23.73 ± 4.58 kg/m2, p = 0.145), anti-Müllerian hormone concentration (3.28 ± 2.86 vs. 3.05 ± 1.88 ng/mL, p = 0.850), and endometrial thickness (9.76 ± 1.55 vs. 9.32 ± 2.18 mm, p = 0.065). The mean number of cryopreserved embryos was slightly higher in the mNC-FET group (5.79 ± 3.47 vs. 5.00 ± 3.47, p = 0.050). Embryo quality distribution did not differ significantly between groups (top-quality blastocysts: 69.2% vs. 70.3%, p = 0.858). Clinical pregnancy rates were 58.2% (53/91) in the mNC-FET group and 55.2% (91/165) in the tNC-FET group (odds ratio [OR] 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68-1.90; p = 0.633). Live birth rates were 46.2% (42/91) in the mNC-FET group and 37.0% (61/165) in the tNC-FET group, without a statistically significant difference (OR 1.46, 95% CI 0.87-2.46; p = 0.151). Women who achieved live birth had a significantly higher number of cryopreserved embryos than those who did not (5.91 ± 3.68 vs. 4.86 ± 3.29, p = 0.024). In multivariable logistic regression, endometrial preparation protocol was not independently associated with live birth (OR 1.27, 95% CI 0.74-2.19, p = 0.394). Conclusions: True natural cycle and modified natural cycle protocols did not differ significantly in clinical pregnancy…

articles.title: Examining the Associations Between Menstrual Disorders and SARS-CoV-2 Exposure in Greek Adolescents: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Svigkou A, Stefanaki C, Kokkou E et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Exposure to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), whether via infection or vaccination, seems to influence the character of the menstrual cycle by disrupting hormonal and immune function. Methods: The main aim of this cohort study was to explore the association between exposure to SARS-CoV-2-through either vaccination or infection-and menstrual disorders in adolescent females. We also aimed at identifying the most prevalent menstrual disorders observed and assessing potential differences between the exposure groups that may contribute to these conditions. Results: This study included data from adolescent females who visited the Center for Adolescent Medicine and UNESCO Chair in Adolescent Health Care due to various menstrual disorders. Data from 92 adolescents, 77 participants exposed to SARS-CoV-2 and 15 controls, were retrieved. Significant associations were found between exposure to SARS-CoV-2 and abnormally frequent uterine bleeding (p = 0.032) and abnormal uterine bleeding (p = 0.025). Adolescents with a past confirmed case of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) demonstrated significantly lower serum concentrations of fibrinogen (p = 0.023) and iron (p = 0.03), as well as higher γ-GT concentrations (p = 0.028), than those who were non-infected, whereas vaccinated adolescents presented with significantly lower concentrations of coagulation factors VIII (p = 0.002), vWFAg (p = 0.023), and Rcof (p = 0.007) than those of their unvaccinated peers. Overall, adolescents exposed [infection (or/and) vaccination] to SARS-CoV-2 demonstrated increased estradiol (E2) concentrations compared to those of the controls. In conclusion, adolescent exposure to SARS-CoV-2 was strongly linked to abnormal uterine bleeding and polymenorrhea, potentially due to decreased coagulation factors or increased E2 concentrations. Conclusions: Further research involving larger samples and a more sophisticated design is needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Analgesic Prescribing in Medically Complex Adult Outpatients Aged ≥40 Years: A Hierarchical Analysis of Comorbidity-Associated Patterns.
articles.authors: Alqurain AA, Alshammari A, Alhomoud F et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Selecting appropriate analgesic therapy in patients with multimorbidity is increasingly challenging because clinicians must balance pain management against comorbidities, polypharmacy, and medication-related risks. However, evidence describing how analgesic prescribing patterns vary across patients with different multimorbidity profiles in routine outpatient practice remains limited. This retrospective cross-sectional study examined associations between multimorbidity and prescribing patterns across paracetamol, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and opioids, and identified clinical characteristics associated with different hierarchical analgesic exposure groups among adults aged ≥40 years in Saudi Arabia. Methods: Electronic health record data were analyzed for adults aged ≥40 years attending multiple clinics in the Eastern Region of Saudi Arabia between January 2020 and December 2021. Analgesic exposure at the index outpatient visit was classified using a hierarchical framework into mutually exclusive paracetamol-only, NSAID-priority, opioid-priority, or non-use groups. Multinomial logistic regression was performed to identify clinical characteristics associated with assignment to the hierarchical analgesic exposure groups. Results: Among 41,083 patients, 29,383 (71.5%) received at least one analgesic prescription at the index visit. The NSAID-priority group was the largest exposure category, followed by opioid-priority and paracetamol-only groups. Hierarchical analgesic prescribing patterns differed across patient clinical profiles, with prescribing observed across patients with cardiovascular, metabolic, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and neuropsychiatric disorders. In adjusted analyses, arthritis-related disease was associated with slightly higher odds of NSAID-priority assignment, whereas ischemic heart disease, gastritis-related disease, and respiratory disorders were associated with lower odds of NSAID-priority assignment. Constipation and urinary incontinence were associated with lower odds of opioid-priority assignment. Conclusions: Analgesic prescribing was common among medically complex adult outpatients aged ≥40 years, and hierarchical prescribing patterns differed across patient clinical and comorbidity profiles. The hierarchical framework provided a pragmatic approach for characterizing prescribing across major analgesic classes while accounting for concurrent exposure. Most disease-specific associations…

articles.title: Laparoscopic-Assisted Ovary-Sparing Surgery for Ovarian Torsion in Children and Adolescents: A Single-Center 6.4-Year Retrospective Analysis.
articles.authors: Liu M, Meng J, Wu X et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: To explore the surgical experience and clinical value of laparoscopic exploration with one-stage ovarian tumor enucleation and oophoroplasty for ovarian tumor pedicle torsion in children and adolescents. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 105 cases of ovarian torsion managed at the Department of Oncological Surgery, Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine from 1 January 2019 to 1 June 2025. All patients underwent emergency laparoscopic exploration with one-stage ovarian tumor enucleation and oophoroplasty. Postoperative ovarian Doppler ultrasound follow-up was performed at 1-3 months, 3-6 months, 6-12 months, and over 12 months, comparing the ovarian volume of the affected side with that of the contralateral ovary. Results: This study included 105 cases of ovarian tumor pedicle torsion. The patients ranged in age from 11 months to 14 years, with a median age of 8 years. The surgery was successfully completed in all 105 cases. Ovarian survival was achieved in 103 cases (98.09%), postoperative ovarian necrosis occurred in 1 case (0.95%), and the affected ovary and fallopian tube were removed due to malignant tumor in 1 case (0.95%); the overall complication rate was 13.3% (14/105). Comparison of ovarian volume between the affected side and the contralateral ovary at each postoperative follow-up time point: at 1-3 months postoperatively, the volume was 3.28 (1.33, 7.71) cm3 vs. 3.43 (1.38, 5.92) cm3 (p = 0.301); at 3-6 months postoperatively, the volume was 1.28 (0.76, 6.09) cm3 vs. 2.67 (1.23, 6.24) cm3 (p = 0.169); at 6-12 months postoperatively, the volume was 3.37 (2.04, 6.66) cm3 vs. 4.37 (2.02, 6.28) cm3 (p = 0.092); at more than 12 months postoperatively, the volume was 4.07 (1.10, 5.04) cm3 vs. 5.60 (1.02, 9.85) cm3 (p = 0.090). At all follow-up time points, the comparison of ovarian volume between the affected side and the contralateral ovary showed no statistically significant difference (all p > 0.05). Conclusions: Emergency laparoscopic exploration with concurrent tumor enucleation and oophoroplasty for ovarian tumor pedicle torsion in children and adolescents is safe and feasible. It reduces the need for a second surgery and effectively preserves ovarian tissue on the affected side.

articles.title: Irritability and Hormone Replacement Therapy in Women Attending a Menopause Clinic: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Olivola M, Agosta A, Consonni A et al.
articles.abstract: Background: The menopausal transition is frequently associated with affective symptoms, including irritability, which remains relatively understudied despite its clinical relevance. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may influence affective symptoms through hormonal and metabolic mechanisms, including modulation of oxidative stress. However, the relationship between HRT and irritability in menopausal women remains poorly understood. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 84 women attending a menopause clinic between 2020 and 2025. Irritability was assessed using the single irritability item of the Greene Climacteric Scale. Associations between HRT use and irritability were explored using descriptive statistics, multivariable logistic regression, and exploratory predictive modelling controlling for age and clinical variables. Results: Approximately 27% of participants were receiving HRT. Descriptive analyses suggested higher HRT use among women reporting irritability compared with those without irritability. However, multivariable models did not confirm a statistically significant association between irritability and HRT use (OR = 1.66, p = 0.244). Age was the only variable significantly associated with HRT use (OR = 0.89, p = 0.009). Exploratory differences in psychopharmacological prescribing patterns did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: In this clinical sample, irritability was a common symptom during the menopausal transition but was not significantly associated with HRT use. The medication-class findings were exploratory and did not establish an association with irritability. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the relationship between hormonal treatments and affective symptoms in menopause.

articles.title: Salivary Flow, Biochemical Profile and Selected Antibacterial Properties of Saliva in Menopausal Women.
articles.authors: Ciesielska A, Kusiak A, Grzybowska ME et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: The aim of this study was to estimate differences in selected physicochemical and antibacterial properties of saliva between menopausal and premenopausal women. Methods: The study population consisted of 30 menopausal women and 22 premenopausal women assigned to the control group. Laboratory analyses included the assessment of unstimulated salivary flow rate, pH, concentration of total protein, lactoferrin, lysozyme, immunoglobulin A (IgA), inorganic phosphates, and ionized calcium. Only participants with clinically healthy periodontal tissues were included in the study. Results: Among menopausal women, statistically significant differences were observed in values of salivary flow rate, total protein, inorganic phosphates, and ionized calcium; however, no statistically significant differences for pH, lactoferrin, lysozyme, and IgA values were found. The unstimulated salivary flow rate parameter in the study group was significantly lower than in premenopausal women. Concentrations of total protein, inorganic phosphates, and ionized calcium in saliva of menopausal women were distinctly higher than in the control group. Conclusions: The results of the present study demonstrate a distinct alteration in salivary homeostasis characterized by significantly reduced salivary flow and increased concentrations of calcium, inorganic phosphate, and total protein between menopausal and premenopausal women. It suggests that menopause may predominantly affect the quantitative secretion and physicochemical composition of saliva rather than causing a generalized impairment of its antimicrobial and immune components. Longitudinal studies that control for age and other relevant factors, including menopausal duration, hormone therapy, and periodontal status, and that evaluate both salivary concentrations and individual analyte output rates are needed to clarify which salivary changes are independently associated with menopause and to determine their clinical relevance to oral health.

articles.title: Effects of BeBo® Pelvic Floor Muscle Training with and Without Electromyographic Biofeedback After Vaginal Delivery and Cesarean Section: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Handzlik-Waszkiewicz P, Sulowska-Daszyk I, Suder A
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pelvic floor dysfunctions, including urinary incontinence (UI) and impaired sexual quality of life, are common postpartum complications. Although pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) is recommended as first-line treatment, evidence regarding the additional benefits of electromyographic (EMG) biofeedback, particularly after different modes of delivery, remains limited. The objective was compare the effectiveness of BeBo®-based PFMT performed with and without EMG biofeedback on pelvic floor muscle function, urinary continence, health-related quality of life, and sexual quality of life in women following vaginal delivery (VD) and cesarean section delivery (CD). Methods: This randomized assessor-blinded controlled trial was conducted at the University of Physical Culture in Cracow, Poland. A total of 120 primiparous women (29.0 ± 1.9 years), assessed 6-8 weeks postpartum after VD (n = 60) or CD (n = 60), were randomly allocated to BeBo® training, BeBo® training combined with EMG biofeedback, or a control group. Intervention groups completed a supervised 6-week BeBo®-based PFMT program with or without EMG biofeedback, whereas controls received standardized postpartum pelvic floor health education only. Primary outcomes were pelvic floor muscle strength and endurance assessed using perineometry and the PERFECT scheme. Secondary outcomes included urinary incontinence (UDI-6), health-related quality of life (KHQ), and sexual quality of life (SQoL-F). Results: Both intervention protocols significantly improved pelvic floor muscle function compared with controls, with the greatest improvements observed following BeBo® training combined with EMG biofeedback. Significant effects of time and intervention were demonstrated for muscle strength and endurance (p < 0.001). Both interventions reduced UI symptoms, particularly after VD, and improved health-related and sexual quality of life. Women receiving EMG biofeedback achieved superior muscle endurance and functional performance compared with controls and, for several outcomes, compared with BeBo® training alone. Greater UI severity was associated with poorer sexual quality of life. Conclusions: BeBo®-based PFMT effectively improves postpartum pelvic floor function and urinary continence. The addition of EMG biofeedback provides further benefits, particularly in muscle endurance and functional control, supporting its integration into postpartum urogynecological rehabilitation after both VD and CD.…

articles.title: Kidney Outcomes in Offspring Exposed to Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Xiong L, Zhang Y, Liao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) may impair placental function and disrupt foetal nephrogenesis, increasing kidney vulnerability in offspring. However, the magnitude and phenotype-specific pattern of offspring kidney risk remain uncertain. We aimed to systematically assess the association between maternal HDP and offspring kidney outcomes. Methods: PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Wanfang Data, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from inception to October 2025. Cohort and case-control studies evaluating maternal HDP and offspring kidney outcomes were included. Outcomes were grouped into three final categories, including chronic kidney disease (CKD), acute kidney injury (AKI), and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT). Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Pooled effect estimates were derived from random-effects meta-analysis using the generic inverse variance method, prioritising the adjusted estimates. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251175714). Results: Thirty studies (20 cohort and 10 case-control studies), including 10,954,573 participants, were included. Maternal preeclampsia was associated with an increased risk of offspring CKD (pooled adjusted relative effect 1.26, 95% CI 1.16, 1.37; I2 = 0%). Although crude analysis suggested a significant association between maternal HDP and offspring CAKUT (odds ratio [OR] 1.18, 95% CI 1.07, 1.31; I2 = 18%), the pooled adjusted estimate was not significant (adjusted OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.87, 1.31; I2 = 0%). A pooled adjusted estimate for offspring AKI was not derived, as this was reported in only 2 studies with considerable population heterogeneity. The overall crude risk ratio (RR) showed no statistically significant association but substantial heterogeneity (pooled crude RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.61, 1.10; I2 = 78%). Crude AKI RRs varied by criteria: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes 0.71 (95% CI 0.55, 0.91; I2 = 51%) versus Acute Kidney Injury Network 1.09 (95% CI 0.60, 1.96; I2 = 83%). Conclusions: Maternal HDP, particularly preeclampsia, was associated with elevated risks of offspring CKD; however, the pooled adjusted estimate for CAKUT was not statistically significant. Evidence for offspring AKI remains inconclusive, providing no reliable evidence for either an increased or decreased risk. Prospective studies using harmonised definitions and robust confounding control are…

articles.title: Early Discontinuation of Opioid-Based Intravenous Patient-Controlled Analgesia After Single-Port Adnexal Laparoscopy: Incidence, Reasons, and Postoperative Outcomes.
articles.authors: Paik ES, Jang Y, Kim H et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Opioid-based intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (IV-PCA) provides postoperative analgesia but can cause adverse effects that lead to early discontinuation. In relatively limited procedures such as single-port access (SPA) adnexal laparoscopy, the balance between analgesic benefit and opioid-related adverse effects remains uncertain. We evaluated the frequency of and recorded reasons for early IV-PCA discontinuation, associated factors, postoperative pain, and length of stay. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 431 patients who received IV-PCA after single-port access (SPA) adnexal laparoscopy at two institutions. Early discontinuation was defined as permanent cessation before completion of the planned course. Associations with demographic and operative factors, concurrent continuous wound infiltration, and treating institution were examined. Repeated-measures analysis accounted for discontinuation timing and repeated pain assessments. Results: IV-PCA was discontinued early in 13.9% of patients. Among patients who discontinued IV-PCA, 85.0% had nausea or vomiting recorded as the reason for discontinuation. Of 59 patients with valid timing data, 47 (79.7%) discontinued within 24 h. No measured factor was significantly associated with discontinuation after adjustment. Unadjusted mean pain scores were 0.30, 0.39, and 0.28 points higher at 6, 12, and 24 h, respectively, but these differences were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Repeated-measures analysis showed no overall pain difference (+0.09 points, 95% CI -0.21 to +0.39). A secondary analysis suggested variation over time, but no time-specific estimate was statistically significant. Length of stay was similar between groups. Conclusions: Early IV-PCA discontinuation after SPA adnexal laparoscopy was mainly attributed to nausea or vomiting. These findings do not establish whether opioid-based IV-PCA is necessary or should be avoided in this setting; rather, they highlight the need to balance its potential analgesic benefit against opioid-related adverse effects and to prospectively evaluate alternative multimodal analgesic strategies.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Myo-Inositol, Metformin, Berberine, and Combination Therapy on Metabolic, Anthropometric and Hormonal Parameters in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A 6-Month Observational Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Yanachkova V, Yordanov A, Yaneva A et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the most prevalent endocrine condition among women of reproductive age. It is marked by metabolic and reproductive irregularities and is often linked to insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and obesity. Diverse methods of treatment are employed to enhance metabolic and hormonal parameters, including inositol-based supplements, metformin, and novel compounds such as berberine. Objective: To describe changes observed over six months in anthropometric, metabolic, lipid, and hormonal metrics among women with PCOS undergoing myo-inositol, metformin, berberine, or a combination of metformin and berberine in standard clinical settings, and to investigate if disparities among treatment groups remained after controlling for initial characteristics. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study included 148 women with PCOS diagnosed according to the Rotterdam criteria who completed six months of treatment with myo-inositol (n = 38), metformin (n = 52), berberine (n = 28), or combined metformin-berberine therapy (n = 30). Anthropometric, metabolic, lipid, and androgen parameters were assessed at baseline and after six months. Within-group changes were evaluated with correction for multiple testing using the Holm method. Given the non-random treatment allocation and baseline differences among groups, supplementary baseline-adjusted analyses were performed for the continuous outcomes. Results: Treatment groups differed significantly in several baseline metabolic variables including body mass index (BMI), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting insulin and homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). After Holm correction for multiple testing, the metformin group showed significant reductions in BMI, FPG, markers of insulin resistance, lipid parameters, and androgen-related hormonal parameters, together with an increase in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). In the myo-inositol group, significant reductions were observed in fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), triglycerides, androstenedione, and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS). In the berberine group, significant reductions were observed in BMI, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and androstenedione. In the combined metformin-berberine group, significant reductions were observed in BMI, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, total cholesterol, LDL-C,…

articles.title: First-Trimester Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone Levels and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Şahin B, Gürbüz TB, Tatar F et al.
articles.abstract: Background: The clinical relevance of a mildly elevated first-trimester thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) concentration is uncertain, recent meta-analyses disagree, and few studies have directly contrasted a TSH of 2.5-4.0 mIU/L with a TSH above 4.0 mIU/L. Methods: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, 218 singleton pregnancies with a first-trimester TSH ≥ 2.5 and ≤10.0 mIU/L and a concurrent free thyroxine (fT4) measurement were classified as high-normal TSH (2.5-4.0 mIU/L; n = 168) or elevated TSH (>4.0-10.0 mIU/L; n = 50; subclinical hypothyroidism in 47 and biochemically overt hypothyroidism in 3). The primary outcome was gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM); secondary outcomes were a composite obstetric complication, individual obstetric and neonatal outcomes, and first- and second-trimester screening markers. Two logistic regression models adjusted for maternal age were fitted; because levothyroxine was started after the index TSH measurement, it was treated as a potential intermediate and examined only in post hoc sensitivity analyses. Results: GDM occurred in 7/50 (14.0%) women with TSH > 4.0 mIU/L versus 6/168 (3.6%) with TSH 2.5-4.0 mIU/L (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.013; unadjusted odds ratio (OR) 4.40, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.40-13.76; risk difference 10.4 percentage points, 95% CI 0.4-20.4). After adjustment for maternal age, TSH > 4.0 mIU/L remained associated with GDM (adjusted OR 5.24, 95% CI 1.60-17.16; p = 0.006), an estimate based on only 13 events; additional adjustment for levothyroxine use gave a similar estimate (adjusted OR 4.51, 95% CI 1.33-15.22). The composite obstetric complication did not differ (32.0% vs. 20.2%; χ2(1) = 3.02, p = 0.082; adjusted OR 1.95, 95% CI 0.96-3.98), nor did individual obstetric outcomes, neonatal outcomes or screening markers. Conclusions: First-trimester TSH > 4.0 mIU/L was associated with a higher frequency of GDM. Given the few events, the wide confidence interval, unmeasured body-mass index and thyroid-peroxidase-antibody status and the absence of a TSH < 2.5 mIU/L comparison group, the finding is hypothesis-generating and does not establish 4.0 mIU/L as a clinically discriminatory threshold.

articles.title: Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Systemic Inflammatory Markers in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome): A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Kececi Oguzhanoglu M, Oguzhanoglu K
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Low-grade chronic inflammation is recognized as part of the systemic profile of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, formerly polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS), although whether this inflammatory signal tracks insulin resistance, adiposity, or both remains unclear. This study evaluated whether the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a surrogate of insulin resistance, is associated with subclinical inflammation independently of body mass index (BMI) in women with PMOS.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study of 150 women with PMOS, the TyG index was calculated from fasting triglycerides and glucose. C-reactive protein (CRP; standard assay) and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were pre-specified primary markers; the neutrophil-, platelet-, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios (NLR, PLR, and MLR) and the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were secondary. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age and BMI, with component, extended-adjustment, tertile, and BMI-interaction analyses.
RESULTS: The TyG index correlated with the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) (rho = 0.45, p < 0.001) but not with BMI (rho = 0.03, 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.13 to 0.19, p = 0.71). After adjustment, each standard deviation (SD) increment in TyG was associated with a 21.7% higher SII (95% CI 17.0 to 26.6%; p < 0.001) and with a higher NLR, PLR, MLR, and SIRI (all corrected p ≤ 0.023), with no TyG × BMI interaction. Both triglyceride and glucose components contributed, fasting insulin was only weakly associated, and results were unchanged after further adjustment for hormonal and glycemic covariates. TyG was not associated with CRP (p = 0.53), which was associated only with BMI.
CONCLUSIONS: In PMOS, the TyG index was associated with hemogram-derived inflammatory indices independently of BMI, a signal attributable to its triglyceride and glucose components rather than to fasting insulin, whereas standard-assay CRP tracked adiposity. These cross-sectional findings are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: The Gut-Muscle Axis in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Proposed Mechanistic Roles of Intestinal Permeability, Bile Acid Signalling, and Skeletal Muscle Dysfunction.
articles.authors: Prasad A, Kishan A, Keezhadath S
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder diagnosed when at least two of three features-chronic anovulation, hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology-are present, according to the Rotterdam criteria endorsed by the 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline. Its metabolic burden extends well beyond reproduction. Insulin resistance, low-grade systemic inflammation, and central adiposity are common, and recent work links the composition of the gut microbiota and the integrity of the intestinal barrier to each of these features, the association between dysbiosis and the pathogenesis of the syndrome having been reviewed in detail. The same gut-related disturbances are now being connected to a second, less recognized consequence of the syndrome: impaired skeletal muscle health. In one cohort, an increased prevalence of sarcopenic obesity has been reported in PCOS despite the anabolic potential of androgen excess, and this review proposes that the two observations are mechanistically linked. Two candidate pathways connect the gut to muscle in PCOS. The first runs from increased intestinal permeability to circulating lipopolysaccharide, which activates Toll-like receptor 4 and a cascade of pro-inflammatory cytokines that blunt insulin signalling in skeletal myocytes. The second runs through bile acids: PCOS is characterized by a distinct circulating bile acid profile, currently described in a preprint that has not undergone peer review, while peer-reviewed profiling has confirmed altered circulating bile acid signatures and links to hyperandrogenism in women with PCOS. Signalling through the farnesoid X receptor and Takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 has been shown to regulate muscle insulin sensitivity, mitochondrial oxidative capacity, and protein turnover in experimental systems, although direct demonstration in human PCOS muscle is lacking. Both pathways are predicted to converge on the IRS-1-PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 axis, the signalling hub through which muscle cells normally translate insulin into glucose uptake and protein synthesis. After reviewing the evidence for gut barrier dysfunction and skeletal muscle impairment in PCOS, we propose a dual-axis model linking intestinal permeability, bile acid signalling, and sarcopenic obesity. We then consider the therapeutic potential of interventions targeting the microbiota, bile acid receptors, inflammation, and muscle function, and outline the study designs that could…

articles.title: Weight Regain After Discontinuation of GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Marchetti M, Campisano G, Paragliola RM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight regain and loss of cardiometabolic benefit commonly follow the withdrawal of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/GLP-1 receptor agonists, yet maintenance strategies are incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review reported according to PRISMA 2020 of primary studies in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes. PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to September 2026, supplemented by backward/forward citation searching and cross-checking of recent systematic reviews. Eligible reports quantified weight or cardiometabolic outcomes at least 12 weeks after planned or unplanned treatment cessation, or tested a post-cessation maintenance strategy. Randomized reports were assessed with RoB 2 and non-randomized reports with ROBINS-I. Owing to incompatible estimands, follow-up schedules, cointerventions and overlapping trial families, results were synthesized narratively without a new pooled estimate.
RESULTS: Eighteen reports representing 16 study families were included. Randomized withdrawal trials showed renewed weight gain after treatment cessation: +6.9% over 48 weeks after switching from semaglutide to placebo in STEP 4, and +14.0% over 52 weeks after switching from tirzepatide to placebo in SURMOUNT-4. In the STEP 1 extension, participants regained 11.6 percentage points over one year, approximately two-thirds of their prior loss, while several cardiometabolic measures moved toward baseline. Real-world estimates were smaller and more variable because discontinuation was often inferred from prescriptions, follow-up weights were missing, and many patients restarted or switched therapy. Cardiometabolic rebound was associated with the degree of weight regain, but clinical cardiovascular events were not evaluated. Evidence for maintenance strategies was sparse: one randomized post-treatment study supported supervised exercise, with the exercise-plus-liraglutide group retaining an additional 5.1 kg of weight loss one year after both interventions ended compared with liraglutide alone; a small pilot supported sitagliptin plus metformin after liraglutide in polycystic ovary syndrome. No eligible controlled trial isolated a specific diet after cessation.
CONCLUSIONS: Weight regain is frequent after stopping GLP-1-based therapy, although magnitude varies by drug, design, follow-up and…

articles.title: Linking Flaxseed Intake to Lipid and Metabolic Health: Associations with Metabolic Dysfunction Indices and LDL-Subfractions in Slovak Menopausal Women.
articles.authors: Lenártová P, Gažarová M, Ponichtera P et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The aim of the present study was to investigate the effects of flaxseed consumption on selected metabolic health indicators in menopausal women following an eight-week dietary intervention. Methods: The study cohort comprised 34 menopausal women aged 45-55 years who were voluntarily recruited from the general population. The intervention lasted for eight weeks, during which participants received 40 g of ground flaxseed daily. Biochemical blood parameters were measured using a BioLis 24i Premium automatic analyser. Body composition was assessed using an InBody 720 device. Lipoprotein subfraction analysis was performed using the LipoPrint® LDL System. Metabolic indices were calculated according to established equations. Results: Overall, the present findings suggest that the most pronounced changes following flaxseed supplementation occurred in selected lipid parameters, particularly LDL-C, total cholesterol, VLDL, IDL-A, and IDL-B. In contrast, HDL-C, TG, glucose, liver enzymes after multiple-testing correction, anthropometric measurements, and the investigated surrogate indices of adiposity and metabolic dysfunction did not show statistically significant changes. The calculated metabolic indices (C-I, BRI, HSI, LAP, TyG-I, TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, TyG-WHtR) suggest preferential visceral fat deposition and an alteration in adipose tissue distribution. Conclusions: Flaxseed supplementation produced a heterogeneous lipid response, with decreased LDL-C but increased total cholesterol, VLDL, and IDL. No significant changes were observed in other lipid, glycemic, anthropometric, or calculated metabolic parameters after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings do not support a uniformly favorable cardiometabolic effect and warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Adiposity, Body Composition, and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Women with and Without Gestational Diabetes.
articles.authors: Charakida M, Fernández CG, Mansukhani T et al.
articles.abstract: Aims: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with increased long-term cardiometabolic risk. The value of body composition measures in predicting adverse cardiometabolic outcomes after GDM remains uncertain. Methods: In this prospective observational study, 757 women (300 controls and 457 with GDM in their index pregnancy) attended a postnatal assessment at a median of 5.8 (IQR 5.1-7.1) months after delivery. Anthropometric measures, biochemical markers, cardiovascular assessments, and body composition by bioelectrical impedance analysis were obtained. Outcomes included dysglycaemia, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, metabolic syndrome and liver steatosis. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated associations and predictive performance. Results: Compared with controls, women with prior GDM had higher BMI, central adiposity, and fat mass (all p < 0.001). They also had a higher prevalence of dysglycaemia (42.9% vs. 16.7%), hypertension (30.2% vs. 18.7%), dyslipidaemia (6.3% vs. 3.0%), and liver steatosis (33.3% vs. 14%; all p < 0.05). BMI and waist-to-height ratio improved prediction of adverse outcomes beyond maternal characteristics alone. Body composition measures were associated with cardiometabolic outcomes but did not show superior discriminatory performance compared with conventional anthropometric measures. Conclusions: Women with prior GDM have a high burden of postpartum cardiometabolic abnormalities. While body composition provides additional biological insight, simple anthropometric measures remain the practical first-line tools for risk stratification.

articles.title: Ladybird (Coleoptera: Coccinellidae) Community Dynamics and Climatic Driving Factors in the Taklimakan Desert-Oasis Ecotone.
articles.authors: Rouzi A, Guo W, Xu Q et al.
articles.abstract: Ladybirds serve as crucial predators in agricultural ecosystems; however, their community dynamics in extremely arid regions are not well understood. We conducted a systematic survey of ladybirds across four habitat types-croplands, orchards, shelterbelts, and weedy margin-at 654 locations in the Taklamakan Desert-oasis ecotone in southern Xinjiang from May to September in 2018, 2019, and 2024. This was done using sweep-netting along with morphological and molecular identification methods. We collected a total of 5414 specimens, representing 23 different species. Hippodamia variegata and Stethorus punctillum were the most prevalent, making up 80.35% of the total individuals. The highest abundance and α-diversity were observed in June, which is significantly earlier than in temperate regions. Climatic factors alone accounted for the largest unique fraction of community variation (14.2%), followed by the shared habitat-month fraction (13.0%), with all predictor sets together explaining 32.5% of the variation. In this extremely arid region, climate accounted for the largest unique fraction among the measured predictor sets, while habitat and month jointly contributed, though 67.5% of community variation remained unexplained. Because climate was strongly confounded with month and geography, this fraction should not be interpreted as evidence of causal dominance. The assembly of ladybird communities was associated with the interaction of climate and habitat, but the relative importance of climate versus habitat requires further experimental validation. These results provide a correlational foundation for understanding ladybird community assembly in oasis agriculture, but further experimental work is needed before they can be translated into specific management actions.

articles.title: Regional Differentiation of Ground-Active Beetle Assemblages Across Contrasting Dryland Alfalfa Agroecosystems.
articles.authors: He Q, Luo Y, Liu X et al.
articles.abstract: Perennial crops can provide a shared habitat template for arthropods, but whether regional differentiation persists among fields of the same crop in drylands remains unclear. From 2020 to 2022, we surveyed ground-active beetles at 55 perennial alfalfa sites across mountainous, oasis, and desert regions of Ningxia, China. We compared beetle diversity and feeding-guild structure among regions and examined their relationships with climate, soil, and vegetation. A total of 48,093 individuals representing 105 species, 62 genera, and 10 families were recorded. Agroecological region explained 30.1% of compositional variation and was associated with differences in total assemblages and all guilds. Mountainous sites had higher overall species richness and were dominated by detritivores; oasis sites contained a greater proportion of herbivores despite similar herbivore activity density among regions, whereas desert sites were numerically dominated by carabids and predators but had lower richness and diversity within the predatory guild. Regional differentiation was more evident in richness, assemblage composition, and trophic organization than in Shannon and Simpson diversity. β-diversity was dominated by nestedness. Climate was associated mainly with activity density and alpha diversity, whereas vegetation showed more recurrent associations with beta diversity. Ground-active beetle assemblages therefore remained regionally distinct despite occurring in the same perennial crop, supporting biodiversity assessment that accounts for dryland regional context.

articles.title: Eleven-Year Trends in Stillbirth, Neonatal and Infant Mortality and Birthweight-Specific Risk: A BABIES Matrix Analysis from a Tertiary Maternity Center in Kazakhstan, 2015-2025.
articles.authors: Ayazbekov A, Khaidarov S, Nartayeva M et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-run facility-level perinatal data from Central Asia are scarce. We described eleven years of stillbirth, neonatal, infant and perinatal mortality at one tertiary maternity center in Kazakhstan, and used the Birthweight and Age-at-death Boxes for Intervention and Evaluation System (BABIES) matrix to locate where feto-infant deaths concentrated. Methods: Retrospective ecological analysis of aggregated annual institutional records, 2015-2025: 102,481 total births, 101,544 live births, 937 stillbirths and 489 infant deaths. Rates were modeled by Poisson regression with the log birth denominator as offset, refitted as quasi-Poisson and negative binomial. Composite feto-infant mortality (antenatal and intrapartum stillbirth plus death at 0-27 days, per 1000 total births in each birthweight band) was examined by direct standardization and Kitagawa decomposition, using the nine years whose matrix cells reconciled with the registry. The study was not preregistered. Results: Infant mortality fell from 7.07 to 3.57 per 1000 live births (rate ratio 0.50, 95% CI 0.33-0.77) and stillbirth from 10.07 to 5.42 per 1000 total births (0.54, 0.38-0.76), an average annual decline near 8% for neonatal and infant mortality. Antenatal stillbirth declined; no clear change was detected for intrapartum stillbirth (1.11 to 1.04 per 1000; 0.94, 0.38-2.32). Births below 2500 g were 5.9% of all births but 71.1% of composite feto-infant deaths (rate ratio 39). Decomposition placed the reduction within birthweight bands rather than in the birthweight distribution, in single-year and pooled-period versions. Conclusions: The design is ecological and descriptive: it shows where feto-infant deaths are concentrated, not why. Intrapartum stillbirth and births below 2500 g are the groups in which any further reduction would have to be found.

articles.title: Evaluation of Infertility-Related Mobile Applications Using an Adapted APPLICATIONS Scoring System and a Holistic Care Framework.
articles.authors: Yanik F, Tokat MA
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mobile health applications often focus on physiological tracking while neglecting the provision of holistic infertility care. This study aimed to evaluate the technical and usability characteristics and comprehensiveness of holistic care provided by infertility-related mobile applications using the adapted APPLICATIONS Scoring System. Methods: This descriptive, cross-sectional study systematically searched the Apple App Store and Google Play Store at five intervals between 2021 and 2025. English and Turkish keywords were used to screen 2108 applications, with 79 meeting the inclusion criteria. The original APPLICATIONS Scoring System was adapted by combining its 13-point Technical and Usability Component with a researcher-developed 16-point Infertility-Specific Holistic Care Component, resulting in a 29-point adapted APPLICATIONS Scoring System. Results: Among the 79 applications analyzed, the mean score for the Holistic Care Comprehensiveness Component was 6.63 ± 3.50, and that for the Technical and Usability Component was 7.33 ± 2.07. The overall mean adapted APPLICATIONS score was 13.96 ± 4.95 (range, 7-28), with only 7.6% (n = 6) of applications providing comprehensive holistic care content. The physiological dimension was the most frequently represented (n = 65, 82.3%), whereas the psychological dimension (n = 11, 13.9%) was the least frequently represented. Only 39.2% of the applications referenced scientific literature or evidence-based sources. Regarding developers, the developer was unknown for 35.5% of the applications. Regarding the target audience, 48.1% of the applications were designed for couples, 44.3% for women, and 7.6% specifically for men. Conclusions: Mobile applications are increasingly used in infertility care; however, most lack a holistic perspective. To provide high-quality support, infertility applications should incorporate evidence-based content and professional guidance that address the multidimensional needs of both partners.

articles.title: Prevalence and Blood Biochemical Parameters Associated with Sarcopenia Among Korean Postmenopausal Women Aged 50 Years and Older: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: Kim S
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sarcopenia is a growing health concern from midlife, but evidence on its biochemical correlates among postmenopausal women younger than 65 years remains limited. This study aimed to estimate sarcopenia prevalence and explore associations with blood biochemical parameters among Korean postmenopausal women aged ≥50 years using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 age-specific diagnostic criteria. Methods: We analyzed 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data from 1157 postmenopausal women aged ≥50 years with complete muscle and biochemical measurements. The 13 biochemical parameters were glycated hemoglobin, total cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, hemoglobin, creatinine, aspartate aminotransferase, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, parathyroid hormone, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D3. Complex sample logistic regression examined each parameter's association with sarcopenia, adjusting for age alone or age, body mass index (BMI), and age at menopause. Results: The weighted prevalence of sarcopenia was 10.5% overall and 9.7% among women aged 50-64 years. Triglycerides were not significantly associated with sarcopenia in the age-adjusted model. However, in the model adjusted for age, BMI, and age at menopause, each 10 mg/dL increase in triglyceride levels was associated with approximately 5.1% higher odds of sarcopenia (aOR = 1.051, 95% CI: 1.020-1.072, p < 0.001). Higher hemoglobin levels were associated with lower odds of sarcopenia in the age-adjusted model (aOR = 0.734, 95% CI: 0.599-0.901, p = 0.003). Both associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Conclusions: These findings highlight the importance of muscle health before older age in postmenopausal women. Biochemical parameters may have potential relevance to muscle health assessment, but their clinical utility requires further validation.

articles.title: Induced Abortion as a Family Planning Strategy in Romania: A Narrative Literature Review of Policy, Health Outcomes and Psychosocial Determinants.
articles.authors: Augustin FE, Hamoud BH, Ples L et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Induced abortion is a major component of reproductive health, with about one in four pregnancies worldwide ending in induced abortion and important implications for maternal morbidity and mortality. Romania's history of restrictive pronatalist policies, very high post-1989 abortion rates, and subsequent family planning reforms provides an informative case for understanding abortion as a family planning strategy. Objectives: This narrative literature review synthesizes evidence on induced abortion with emphasis on Romania. It describes the evolution of abortion law and policy, summarizes epidemiological and maternal health outcomes, examines sociodemographic and psychosocial determinants of induced abortion, reviews psychological and psycho-sexual consequences, and discusses the role of non-stigmatizing terminology in clinical communication. Methods: This narrative literature review was informed by a structured literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection conducted on 20 May 2026. Publications from January 1990 to September 2024 were searched using terms related to induced abortion, family planning, Romania, maternal mortality and morbidity, abortion policy, psychosocial determinants, psychological outcomes, and stigma. Predefined eligibility criteria were used to identify relevant peer-reviewed studies and major institutional sources; additional historical and legal documents were considered for contextual framing. Additional recently published studies relevant to the review themes were identified through targeted update searches and reference-list screening up to 20 May 2026. Results: Restrictive policies and contraceptive bans in Romania were associated with extremely high abortion-related maternal mortality, whereas legal liberalization and integrated family planning programs led to marked declines in abortion rates and deaths. Abortion decisions reflect age, partnership, parity, education, employment and legal status. Psychological studies and major reviews report heterogeneous post-abortion experiences. These outcomes appear to be influenced primarily by pre-existing mental-health vulnerability, pregnancy intention and circumstances, social support, stigma, and decisional autonomy, rather than by the procedure alone. Also, terminology and conscientious objection practices can contribute to stigma and access barriers. Conclusions: Ensuring equitable access to contraception, safe abortion services, nonjudgmental…

articles.title: Exploratory Interim Analysis of Serial Plasma and Single-Follicle Follicular Fluid Oxidation-Reduction Potential During Fertility Treatment.
articles.authors: Kaltsas A, Papaharitou S, Papanikolaou K et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: This exploratory interim analysis examined associations between serial plasma oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) and single-follicle follicular-fluid (FF) ORP during fertility treatment. Between-visit measurements and cycle-level outcomes were also described. Methods: In 31 cycles from 29 women, plasma was sampled prospectively at cycle day 2 (D2), D6, and pre-trigger, and FF from one follicle at retrieval. Fresh samples were measured in duplicate (MiOXSYS); only means were available. All analyses were post hoc and used Spearman correlations, an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and mixed models with within-family adjustment. Results: Plasma-FF correlations were 0.580 at D2 (n = 25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.178-0.839), 0.715 at D6 (n = 23; CI, 0.350-0.924), and 0.866 pre-trigger (n = 23; CI, 0.679-0.941). All Holm-adjusted p values were ≤0.0027. In 21 women with complete profiles, between-visit correlations were 0.703-0.856 (ICC, 0.788; CI, 0.617-0.872). The mixed-model pre-trigger minus D6 difference was 6.6 mV (CI, 0.6-12.6; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0939). No visit contrast or main ORP-outcome association met its adjusted threshold. Conclusions: Plasma and FF ORP were associated in this small interim cohort. Neither biological stability nor a true temporal change was established, and assay precision, agreement, and prognostic value remain unknown. Clinical application is not supported.

articles.title: Phenotypic Landscape of Programmed Death and TIGIT/CD155/DNAM-1 Pathways in NK Cells in Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Pawłowska-Łachut A, Skiba W, Pieniądz-Feculak P et al.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Ovarian cancer (OC) is the gynecological malignancy with the highest mortality rate. Preclinical studies have shown that dual blockade of immune checkpoint proteins (ICPs), such as PD-1 and TIGIT, may be beneficial for OC patients. Thus, the aim of this study was to evaluate the expression of PD-1, TIGIT, and DNAM-1 in NK cells in three OC environments-i.e., peripheral blood (PB), peritoneal fluid (PF), and tumor tissue (TT)-and their soluble forms in plasma and PF to explore their clinical significance. Methods: The expression of ICPs on NK cells was analyzed via flow cytometry. The concentrations of soluble forms of these ICPs were measured in plasma and PF via ELISA. The obtained results were correlated with the clinicopathological features of OC patients. Results: We observed an increased percentage of PD-1+ NK cells in tumor tissue (p < 0.05), as well as TIGIT+ (p < 0.001) and DNAM-1+ NK cells in PF of patients with OC (p < 0.05). Soluble PD-1 (sPD-1) concentration was higher in PF than in plasma (p < 0.0001) and higher in plasma of OC patients than in controls (p < 0.001), while soluble TIGIT (sTIGIT) levels were elevated in plasma of OC patients compared with controls (p < 0.05). NK cell phenotypic alterations were also associated with selected clinicopathological features of OC (i.e., FIGO disease advancement, tumor type according to Kurman and Shih, and grade). The percentage of NK cells in PF was positively associated with age (p < 0.01) and negatively associated with BMI (p < 0.05). Conclusions: OC is characterized by distinct compartment-specific patterns of PD-1, TIGIT, and DNAM-1 expression on NK cells, accompanied by altered soluble ICP profiles. These phenotypic patterns may help define the immune landscape of the ovarian cancer microenvironment.

articles.title: Temporary Uterine Artery Clamping During Laparoscopic Myomectomy and Perioperative Hemoglobin Decline: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Korkmazer E, Deniz R, Tigli A et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study was to evaluate the adjusted association of temporary uterine artery clamping with the absolute and percentage decreases in hemoglobin during the perioperative period in women undergoing laparoscopic myomectomy, and to evaluate this association after multivariable adjustment for patient and leiomyoma characteristics. Methods: This single-center, retrospective, comparative observational study included 118 patients who underwent elective laparoscopic myomectomy for uterine leiomyomas between January 2021 and January 2026 (65 with temporary uterine artery clamping and 53 controls). The decision to perform clamping was based on the surgeon's intraoperative assessment. The primary outcome measures were defined as absolute hemoglobin drop and percentage hemoglobin drop. The adjusted association of clamping with these measures was examined using multivariable linear regression models simultaneously adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), and tumor burden (evaluated as dominant diameter in Model 1 and specimen weight in Model 2), with baseline hemoglobin additionally adjusted in absolute decline models. Results: No significant differences were found between the two groups in terms of baseline clinical and leiomyoma characteristics (age, BMI, number of pregnancies, preoperative hemoglobin level, leiomyoma size, and weight) (all p > 0.05). Although the difference in postoperative hemoglobin levels did not reach statistical significance (9.59 ± 1.70 vs. 10.01 ± 1.45 g/dL; p = 0.153), both the absolute hemoglobin decline (controls vs. clamping: 2.20 ± 0.90 vs. 1.83 ± 0.88 g/dL; p = 0.027) and the percentage hemoglobin decline (controls vs. clamping: 18.84 ± 7.77% vs. 15.24 ± 6.61%; p = 0.008) were significantly lower in the clamping group. Evaluated as a composite safety outcome across all 134 surgical patients (transfusion or conversion to laparotomy), procedural safety events occurred in 18.5% (12/65) of controls compared with 5.8% (4/69) of clamping cases, demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in composite major surgical morbidity in the clamping cohort (Fisher's exact test p = 0.033; Relative Risk = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.11 to 0.92). In both the primary and sensitivity multivariable models, temporary uterine artery clamping demonstrated a significant adjusted association with lower values of approximately 0.38 g/dL in absolute hemoglobin decline (p = 0.015-0.016) and approximately 3.6 percentage points in…

articles.title: Peri-Ovarian Mitochondrial Administration Improves Surrogate Markers of Ovarian Function in Aged Rats: Free Versus Alginate-Encapsulated Mesenchymal Stromal Cell-Derived Mitochondria.
articles.authors: Halbutoğulları ZS, Utkan Korun ZE, Çelebi G et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Ovarian aging is driven in part by mitochondrial dysfunction, and transfer of exogenous mitochondria has been proposed as a cell-free alternative to stem cell therapy; whether the delivery format alters efficacy has not been tested directly. Methods: We compared free and alginate-encapsulated mitochondria isolated from rat bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (BM-MSCs) in aged rats. Mitochondria retained their membrane potential after encapsulation; approximately 35% of the encapsulated protein was released within 1 h in vitro, and release was complete by 24 h.
