Thirty-five female Wistar rats were allocated to five groups (n = 7): young control (Y-Ctrl), aged control (O-Ctrl), and three aged subgroups receiving empty capsules (Alg), free mitochondria (MSC-Mito), or encapsulated mitochondria (MSC-Mito@Alg), administered peri-ovarianly and evaluated on day 14. Results: Both treatments were associated with higher primordial and secondary follicle numbers, fewer atretic follicles, higher estradiol, higher Esr1, Fshr, and Sod2 expression, lower Casp3 and Mct4 expression, and lower Caspase-3 and higher Ki-67 immunoreactivity relative to aged controls. Anti-Müllerian hormone, Nrf2, and Tomm20 were higher only with MSC-Mito@Alg; corpus luteum counts were higher only with MSC-Mito. Although empty capsules were not inert, peri-ovarian mitochondrial administration improved follicular, endocrine, and molecular indices of ovarian aging. Conclusions: The encapsulated formulation was associated with additional effects on antioxidant and mitochondrial-mass endpoints but was not uniformly superior to free mitochondria.

articles.title: Transperineal Ultrasound Comparison of Longitudinal Sling Position and Dynamic Sling Configuration After Altis and MiniStop Single-Incision Mini-Slings for Stress Urinary Incontinence.
articles.authors: Ke LY, Long CY
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Direct imaging comparisons of single-incision mini-slings are limited. This study compared six-month three-dimensional transperineal ultrasound (TPUS) findings after Altis and MiniStop surgery. Methods: This retrospective cohort included 174 women with stress urinary incontinence who underwent Altis (n = 118) or MiniStop (n = 56) surgery. Sling position along the urethral length was expressed as a percentage from the bladder neck (0%) to the external urethral meatus (100%), with 20-60% defined as the midurethral region. TPUS also assessed sling-to-urethra distance, coronal sling angles, and sling kinking. Clinical outcomes and complications were evaluated as secondary outcomes. Results: Slings were located within the midurethral region in 82.2% of Altis and 50.0% of MiniStop patients (p < 0.001). Coronal sling angles were smaller in the Altis group at rest and during straining (both p < 0.001). Sling-to-urethra distance and sling kinking did not differ significantly. Baseline leakage severity was greater in the Altis group, whereas concomitant pelvic reconstruction was more common in the MiniStop group. Questionnaire scores decreased within both groups. Recurrence occurred in 5.1% and 7.1%, respectively. Conclusions: Six-month TPUS identified distinct postoperative sling positions and coronal configurations in the two cohorts, with Altis slings more frequently located within the study-defined midurethral region. These findings characterize anatomical differences in the context of baseline and procedural differences and provide a basis for investigating their relationship with clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Fetal Doppler Beyond Biometry for Adverse Perinatal Outcomes in Suspected Fetal Growth Restriction: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Taşdemir D, Haksever M, Kandemir S et al.
articles.abstract: Objective: To explore the incremental prognostic information of fetal Doppler measurements beyond maternal and fetal biometric characteristics for adverse perinatal outcomes in pregnancies with suspected fetal smallness. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 606 singleton pregnancies assessed for suspected or diagnosed fetal growth restriction. The principal analysis was restricted to 429 pregnancies with estimated fetal weight (EFW) or abdominal circumference (AC) below the 10th percentile at the index examination. A composite adverse perinatal outcome comprised five-minute Apgar score < 7, umbilical arterial pH < 7.10, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, respiratory support, neonatal death, or stillbirth. Baseline clinical-biometric, Doppler-integrated, and delivery-week sensitivity logistic models were assessed using stratified 10-fold out-of-fold predictions. Additional robustness analyses evaluated component frequencies, a hard-outcome sensitivity composite less directly influenced by clinical management, paired uncertainty in out-of-fold performance differences, and model performance across alternative cohort definitions. Results: Among 429 pregnancies in the principal cohort, 111 (25.9%) met the composite adverse perinatal outcome, and 206 (48.0%) had abnormal Doppler findings. Event rates were 85/206 (41.3%) among pregnancies with abnormal Doppler and 26/223 (11.7%) among those with normal Doppler. The baseline and Doppler-integrated out-of-fold areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.642 and 0.690, respectively; corresponding Brier scores were 0.183 and 0.174. Elevated umbilical artery pulsatility index with forward flow and absent or reversed end-diastolic flow (AEDF/REDF) were independently associated with the composite outcome, with adjusted odds ratios of 2.61 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.58-4.32) and 6.60 (95% CI, 2.40-18.18), respectively, compared with normal umbilical artery flow. The adjusted estimate for the AEDF/REDF subgroup was imprecise because this subgroup included only 19 pregnancies. The paired out-of-fold AUC increment for the Doppler-integrated model was 0.049 (95% CI, 0.005-0.094); the corresponding Brier-score improvement was 0.009 (95% CI, -0.0004 to 0.0179). Sensitivity analyses supported a modest incremental contribution but did not establish the superiority of the integrated model over alternatives based on the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR) or umbilical artery (UA)…

articles.title: Early-Diagnosed Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Molecular and Metabolic Evidence Before 24 Weeks of Gestation.
articles.authors: Bilyalova G, Baibusunova A, Boshanova A et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is conventionally diagnosed at 24-28 weeks of gestation, although hyperglycaemia may be detected earlier. Early gestational diabetes mellitus (eGDM), defined here as hyperglycaemia diagnosed before 24 weeks in the absence of overt diabetes, is characterised by limited but emerging molecular and metabolic evidence. In women with eGDM diagnosed before 20 weeks, DALI phenotyping identified insulin-resistant, secretion-dominant and mixed phenotypes using HOMA-IR and the OGTT-derived Stumvoll first-phase index, with greater obstetric risk in the resistance-dominant group. In the TOBOGM cohort, eGDM was associated with higher diacylglycerol and fatty-acid species, which remained associated with eGDM and glycaemic indices after adjustment for clinical risk factors. Early-pregnancy SHBG provides additional evidence, with a further reduction reported in women diagnosed before 20 weeks. The principal limitation is that eGDM-specific evidence remains sparse. Most early-pregnancy biomarker studies measured women before 24 weeks but diagnosed GDM later and therefore describe antecedents of subsequent disease rather than eGDM diagnosed before 24 weeks. Most mechanistic evidence also derives from conventional-window GDM or placental tissue obtained at delivery, preventing determination of whether reported abnormalities precede, accompany or result from early hyperglycaemia. Longitudinal studies with early diagnosis, concurrent assessment of insulin sensitivity and secretion, adjustment for adiposity and independent validation are therefore needed to define the molecular phenotype of eGDM.

articles.title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma for Endometrial and Ovarian Dysfunction: Mechanistic Insights and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.authors: Qin X, Yang T, Bai L et al.
articles.abstract: Although assisted reproductive technology (ART) has been widely applied worldwide, thin endometrium (TE), diminished ovarian reserve (DOR), and other conditions remain the core bottlenecks of refractory infertility, and existing therapies fail to effectively preserve tissue and prevent functional damage. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP), as an autologous regenerative agent, has demonstrated promising application potential in reproductive medicine due to its multi-targeted regulatory capacity. Therefore, this review is intended as a narrative overview that aims to systematically elucidate the possible mechanisms by which PRP improves the endometrial microenvironment and ovarian function, integrate the latest clinical evidence to evaluate its therapeutic efficacy, analyze translational challenges such as the lack of standardization, and provide an evidence-based basis for its standardized clinical application.

articles.title: Oxytocin Signalling in Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Associated with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and Overactive Bladder Syndrome: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Badshah M, Ibrahim J, Elnahriry KA et al.
articles.abstract: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTSs) associated with benign prostatic disease and overactive bladder syndrome (OAB) substantially impair quality of life. This narrative review evaluates oxytocin receptor (OXTR) localisation, signalling, and contractile responses in prostate and bladder tissue, with anatomical and pharmacological context restricted to interpretation of these findings. Experimental receptor expression and antagonist responses provide mechanistic plausibility, but species differences, vasopressin receptor cross-reactivity, and inconsistent human tissue responses limit translation. Preclinical effects on tissue contractility and reproductive endpoints are distinguished from clinical urinary outcomes. OXTR antagonism remains investigational for LUTSs and OAB; clinical efficacy and safety require validation. Proposed artificial intelligence applications are limited to experimental receptor localisation, contraction analysis, and phenotyping.

articles.title: Urinary and Sexual Function Outcomes After Ultrasound-Guided High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound for Uterine Fibroids: Associations of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms with Fibroid Location and Uterine Morphology.
articles.authors: Long CY, Jeng CJ, Ke LY
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Uterine fibroids may contribute to lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) through pelvic mass effects, but urinary and sexual outcomes after ultrasound-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (USgHIFU) and their anatomical correlates remain unclear. We evaluated 6-month urinary and sexual outcomes, described urinary changes by dominant fibroid location, and explored associations between uterine morphology and baseline urinary symptom burden. Methods: This retrospective study included 75 women with paired baseline and 6-month urinary assessments (anterior, n = 45; non-anterior, n = 30). Measures included the Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS), Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6), Incontinence Impact Questionnaire-7 (IIQ-7), International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form (ICIQ-UI SF), and Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI; n = 63); pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characterized uterine anatomy. Results: At 6 months, OABSS decreased from 3.51 ± 3.07 to 2.57 ± 2.29 (p = 0.005); UDI-6, IIQ-7, and ICIQ-UI SF also improved (all p ≤ 0.009), and OABSS ≥ 3 prevalence declined from 53.3% to 40.0% (p = 0.002). Mean urinary symptom scores decreased in both location groups. The larger longitudinal-diameter subgroup had higher baseline OABSS (4.20 vs. 2.71; p = 0.034) and OABSS ≥ 3 prevalence (70.0% vs. 34.3%; p = 0.003), whereas the corresponding comparisons for uterine volume and anteroposterior diameter were not significantly associated. The mean FSFI total score increased from 21.6 ± 5.8 to 26.5 ± 6.6 (summary-derived conservative p-value bound, p < 0.005). Conclusions: USgHIFU was associated with improved urinary symptoms, urinary symptom-related quality of life, and sexual function. The exploratory association between the longitudinal-diameter groups and baseline overactive bladder symptom burden warrants confirmation using continuous measurements and adjusted analyses.

articles.title: Effects of Melatonin Dose Regimens on Follicular Development and Oocyte Developmental Competence in FSH-Superovulated Ewes: Redox and Molecular Responses.
articles.authors: Aihemaiti A, Niyazi A, Zhu K et al.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress impairs gamete development and embryonic competence in female mammals. We compared four melatonin (MT) dose regimens (vehicle control and 20, 40, and 80 mg per injection) in FSH-superovulated ewes during in vivo ovum pick-up. The 40 mg regimen significantly reduced follicular atresia and increased high-quality oocytes and transferable blastocysts. Pregnancy and lambing rates after in vivo embryo transfer were numerically higher in the 40 mg group but did not reach statistical significance. The favorable responses observed with the 40 mg regimen were not maintained at the 80 mg dose. Oocyte transcriptomics and follicular fluid metabolomics revealed multilevel molecular responses associated with MT treatment. Systemically, 40 mg MT was associated with changes in serum reproductive hormones, including significant increases in MT, E2, and IGF-1. At the cellular and molecular levels, MT treatment was associated with changes in follicular development and oocyte quality, together with altered redox status and candidate changes in energy metabolism; MT1-related signaling was identified as a candidate pathway. MT treatment was associated with increased MT1 and Ki-67 expression in granulosa cells, an increased Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and reduced follicular fluid ROS and MDA levels, indicating improved redox homeostasis and granulosa cell proliferation. MT treatment was associated with altered redox status, including significantly increased GSH and reduced intracellular ROS, while ATP and mitochondrial superoxide showed non-significant changes. Hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1) signaling and the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle were identified as candidate pathways potentially associated with follicular energy-redox remodeling. These observations provide a basis for further investigation of MT dose regimens to mitigate disadvantages associated with FSH superovulation in ewes and other species.

articles.title: Differential Susceptibility to Heavy-Metal-Induced Injury in a Human Testis Tissue Equivalent (hTTE): Implications for Oxidative Stress.
articles.authors: Cohen AB, Hingu J, Udaiyar A et al.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Oxidative stress driven by environmental and occupational exposure to heavy metals is increasingly recognized as a central, modifiable contributor to male infertility. Yet, the lack of physiologically relevant human models has limited mechanistic insight. We have previously described a three-dimensional Human Testis Tissue Equivalent (hTTE) that recapitulates the cellular composition and stem cell niche of the seminiferous tubule and is more resistant than two-dimensional (2D) culture to gonadotoxic chemotherapeutics. Here, we used the hTTE platform to compare heavy-metal cytotoxicity, cell-type-associated transcript responses, and exploratory microRNA (miRNA) profiles elicited by three prototypical pro-oxidant heavy metals: mercury (Hg2+), thallium (Tl+), and lead (Pb2+).
BACKGROUND AND AIM: To determine whether the hTTE model exhibits greater resistance to heavy-metal cytotoxicity than matched 2D cultures and whether cell-type-associated responses differ following heavy-metal exposure within the established redox biology of these toxicants.
METHODS: Adult human testicular cells from three donors were expanded, characterized by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry, and assembled into hTTEs alongside matched 2D cultures. Cultures were exposed for 48 h to Hg2+, Tl+, or Pb2+ across graded concentrations; IC50 values were derived from ATP-based viability assays and used for selected downstream exposure concentrations. The relative abundances of cell-type-associated transcripts were profiled by digital PCR for ZBTB16 (spermatogonia), STAR (Leydig), SOX9 (Sertoli), and CD34 (peritubular cells), and global miRNA expression was quantified using the NanoString nCounter Human v3b miRNA panel (827 miRNAs). Exploratory Ingenuity Pathway Analysis of miRNA data was used to identify predicted mRNA associations with a testis/reproductive disease filter.
RESULTS: hTTEs exhibited significantly greater IC50 values than matched 2D cultures for all three metals (p < 0.05), demonstrating greater resistance to acute heavy-metal cytotoxicity in the hTTE culture system, consistent with enhanced antioxidant buffering in the 3D microenvironment. Metal-associated changes in cell-type marker transcripts were distinct: Hg2+ produced broad reductions in markers associated with all four populations; Pb2+ produced greater reductions in Sertoli and peritubular cell markers while relatively preserving spermatogonial and Leydig cell markers; and Tl+ reduced somatic support cell markers…

articles.title: Biochemical Endocrine and Skeletal Findings in Adults with Fabry Disease: A Descriptive Single-Center Study.
articles.authors: Ozturk S, Kocar IC
articles.abstract: Background: Endocrine and skeletal findings have previously been reported in Fabry disease (FD), but their interpretation alongside Fabry-specific biochemical markers and multiorgan disease burden remains uncertain. This study descriptively characterized biochemical endocrine findings, vitamin D status, and age-appropriate DXA measurements in adults with FD receiving enzyme replacement therapy (ERT). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study screened 29 patients evaluated between January 2020 and December 2025, of whom 21 adults with genetically and/or enzymatically confirmed FD were included. Biochemical thyroid findings and HbA1c-defined dysglycemia were summarized separately as descriptive measures; no prespecified primary endpoint, composite endocrine outcome, or confirmatory outcome hierarchy was defined. A post hoc exploratory comparison was performed between patients with HbA1c-defined dysglycemia (HbA1c ≥ 5.7%; n = 7) and those without HbA1c-defined dysglycemia (HbA1c < 5.7%; n = 14). Vitamin D status and DXA findings were evaluated using age-, sex-, and menopausal-status-appropriate criteria. Exploratory analyses incorporated effect sizes, bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation tests, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Results: The mean age was 40.7 ± 14.5 years, and nine patients (42.9%) were male. The cohort was genetically concentrated, with c.851T>C (p.M284T) identified in 12/21 patients (57.1%). An elevated-TSH/non-elevated-FT4 biochemical pattern was observed in 2/21 patients (9.5%), and HbA1c-defined dysglycemia in 7/21 (33.3%). Vitamin D concentrations were <20 ng/mL in 16/21 patients (76.2%). DXA data were available for 20 patients. Among four postmenopausal women and four men aged ≥50 years, 5/8 (62.5%) had a minimum T-score within the osteoporosis range. Among seven premenopausal women and five men aged <50 years, 7/12 (58.3%) had a minimum Z-score ≤ -2.0, indicating BMD below the expected range for age. None of the 14 post hoc subgroup comparisons or 48 exploratory correlations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Conclusions: Thyroid, glycemic, vitamin D, and age-appropriate DXA measurements were descriptively characterized in this small, ERT-treated FD cohort. In the absence of an age-, sex-, and clinically matched comparator, the observed distributions cannot be interpreted as abnormalities attributable specifically to FD or as occurring more frequently than in an appropriate reference population.…

articles.title: Testosterone Impairs Endometrial Receptivity Markers and Trophoblast Spheroid Attachment In Vitro: Reversal by Flutamide in a Model of Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome.
articles.authors: Harper CV, Reeves BJ, Elliott CS et al.
articles.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; previously termed polycystic ovary syndrome, PCOS) is a multi-faceted reproductive and endocrinological condition that affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age. It is typically characterised by chronic anovulation and elevated levels of the androgen testosterone, which have been linked to reduced implantation rates and fertility outcomes. In this study, we investigated whether increased testosterone treatment affected attachment of trophoblast spheroids to an endometrial cell monolayer and the expression of genes known to be involved in the attachment process. Attachment of BeWo spheroids to Ishikawa endometrial cells was significantly reduced when Ishikawa cells were pre-treated for 24 h with pathological and suprapathological doses of testosterone compared to the results for the untreated control, with no significant effect measured following treatment with a physiological testosterone dose (1 nM). Expression of the transcription factor gene HOXA10; integrin β3 (a component of the αVβ3 molecule) and SPP1 (the gene expressing the ligand osteopontin), were significantly decreased in Ishikawa cells following treatment with 10 nM testosterone, along with αVβ3 protein. Treatment with the nonsteroidal antiandrogen flutamide (1 µM) rescued the testosterone-induced decrease in BeWo spheroid-endometrial cell attachment and associated decreases in gene expression. These results suggest that increased levels of testosterone decrease endometrial receptivity and downstream embryo attachment through negatively affecting the expression of genes required for the success of these processes. This testosterone-induced decrease can be reversed in vitro with flutamide treatment. These results highlight the importance of considering endometrial receptivity in the treatment of PMOS-induced infertility.

articles.title: Melatonin and Glutathione Co-Supplementation Improves Redox Homeostasis and Developmental Competence in Sheep Oocytes.
articles.authors: Li X, Zhang J, Su L et al.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress is a major factor limiting oocyte quality during in vitro maturation (IVM) and subsequent embryonic developmental competence. This study investigated the effects of combined melatonin (MLT) and glutathione (GSH) supplementation on sheep oocyte quality and the potential regulatory mechanisms involved. Sheep oocytes were assigned to Control, MLT, GSH, and MLT+GSH groups, and oocyte maturation, redox homeostasis, and mitochondrial function were evaluated by assessing cumulus expansion, first polar body extrusion, F-actin organization, ROS- and GSH-associated fluorescence, JC-1 staining, and MitoTracker signals, while subsequent developmental competence was assessed following in vitro fertilization (IVF). SMART-seq2 transcriptomic analysis, Nrf2 immunofluorescence, antioxidant-related gene expression analysis, and pharmacological inhibition of Nrf2 with ML385 were further performed to explore the underlying mechanisms. MLT and GSH, either alone or in combination, improved multiple indices related to oocyte maturation, redox status, and mitochondrial function, with the MLT+GSH group generally showing the most favorable numerical changes. MLT+GSH treatment was associated with greater cumulus expansion, a higher first polar body extrusion rate, improved F-actin organization, reduced ROS accumulation, increased GSH-associated fluorescence, a higher JC-1 red-to-green fluorescence ratio, and enhanced mitochondrial-associated fluorescence. However, for some endpoints, the numerical improvement observed with MLT+GSH did not differ significantly from the corresponding single treatment. Following IVF, MLT+GSH treatment increased cleavage and blastocyst formation rates and improved subsequent developmental outcomes. Mechanistically, MLT+GSH treatment was accompanied by increased Nrf2 immunofluorescence intensity and altered expression of NFE2L2 and several Nrf2-related antioxidant genes, including NQO1, HMOX1, GCLC, GCLM, and GPX4, suggesting the involvement of an Nrf2-associated antioxidant regulatory network. Addition of the Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 to the MLT+GSH treatment increased ROS levels and reduced JC-1 and other redox- and mitochondria-related indices, while partially attenuating improvements in oocyte maturation and embryonic development. Overall, MLT and GSH co-supplementation was associated with improved redox homeostasis, antioxidant capacity, mitochondrial function, and subsequent developmental competence in sheep oocytes, with…

articles.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Copper Metabolism Heterogeneity and Phenotypic Remodeling in Vaginal Anterior Wall Stromal Cells in Pelvic Organ Prolapse.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Huang S, Hu M et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common disease characterized by disordered extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling of pelvic support tissues. Copper dysregulation drives fibrosis in multiple diseases, whereas its function in POP remains unclear. We analyzed single-cell transcriptomes of 90,578 cells from 21 vaginal wall samples (5 controls, 16 POP). ECM remodeling was the most robustly upregulated module in POP fibroblasts, accompanied by decreased copper metabolism and senescence scores. Fibroblasts resolved into nine subpopulations, with copper metabolism activity decreased in eight, most prominently in p53/senescence-like states. High-copper fibroblasts were enriched for TNFα/NF-κB, inflammatory, hypoxic, and EMT programs. Copper metabolism correlated with senescence (rho = 0.56, p = 0.010) but not ECM remodeling (rho = -0.02, p = 0.92). Smooth muscle cells shifted toward a synthetic phenotype, negatively correlating with copper metabolism. CellChat and trajectory inference revealed ECM ligand-driven interactions and temporal copper-ECM gene dynamics. Elesclomol reduced fibroblast viability and induced apoptosis and senescence in a copper-dependent manner. These findings suggest that copper metabolism dysregulation contributes to POP stromal remodeling and may serve as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Programmed Frozen Embryo Transfer in the Absence of Corpus Luteum: Impact on Maternal Cardiovascular Adaptation, Endothelial Function and Risk of Preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Gerede A, Gkaitatzi F, Oikonomou E et al.
articles.abstract: Programmed frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles are an integral part of assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs). They rely exclusively on the administration of exogenous estrogens and progesterone to prepare the endometrium, and they are characterized by the absence of a functional corpus luteum (CL). Pregnancies resulting from FET cycles have been associated with an increased risk of complications related to placental dysfunction, such as preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction (FGR). Besides progesterone production, the CL secretes vasoactive and angiogenic factors essential for the regulatory mechanisms that occur during the early stages of pregnancy. Its absence results in a different endocrine environment, which may be associated with differences in normal maternal cardiovascular remodeling. In pregnant women without CL function, reduced vasodilation, increased systemic vascular resistance, altered cardiac output, and inadequate renal adaptation have been reported. In addition, disturbances in angiogenic balance and trophoblast invasion may contribute to abnormal placentation and the development of preeclampsia. Accordingly, the absence of the CL in programmed FET cycles may represent a critical endocrine disorder, predisposing patients to maternal cardiovascular disturbance and adverse obstetric outcomes. Recognition of this potential endocrine and vascular interaction has important implications for cycle selection, risk stratification, and preventive strategies in the implementation of assisted reproduction protocols.

articles.title: Sex-Based Differences in Cognitive Performance in Patients with Cardiovascular Diseases.
articles.authors: Prentakis AG, Fragoulis CI, Theleritis CG et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) share common risk factors with cognitive decline. The scope of this cross-sectional study was to evaluate sex-based differences in cognitive capacity in patients with CVDs. Methods: We evaluated cognitive performance in 246 patients with CVDs using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Other risk factors, comorbidity with depression and anxiety disorders, and frailty score were evaluated, and patients were stratified by sex and age. Results: Age and hypertension were associated with lower MoCA scores for both sexes. However, diagnosis of depression, dyslipidemia, higher Body Mass Index (BMI), and fewer years of education were associated with a lower MoCA score only in female participants. No statistically significant difference was found in mean MoCA scores between male and female subjects of the same age groups. Conclusions: Sex-based differences and shared risk factors may be taken into account when evaluating cognitive performance, especially in patients with CVD.

articles.title: Prognostic Significance of Amino Acid Transporters in Endometrial Cancer.
articles.authors: Zaborowski MP, Ciecierski Ł, Tyburski P et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Identification of high-risk patients with endometrial cancer (EC) remains challenging despite advances in molecular profiling. Methods: We comprehensively analyzed the RNA expression of 18 amino acid transporters (AATs) in 373 EC samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Results: Our clustering analysis based on AAT expression identified a patient group with a significantly worse prognosis. Sideroflexin family (SFXN1, SFXN5), glutamine (SLC38A1, SLC38A3), glycine (SLC6A9) transporters, and the heavy-chain subunit of heteromeric AATs (SLC3A2) were elevated in poorly differentiated tumors. In contrast, the transporter of small neutral amino acids (SLC1A4) and proline/imino-acid transporter (SLC6A20) were enriched in lower-grade disease. SFXN1 and SLC38A1 were also higher in advanced (III/IV) FIGO stages. AAT expression differed across molecular subtypes, with SFXN5, SLC38A1, SLC38A3, and SLC3A2 associated with the copy-number-high profile. In survival analysis, we demonstrated that SLC38A3, SFXN4, and SLC3A2 were associated with shorter disease-free survival, and SLC38A1, SLC38A3, and SFXN1 with worse overall survival, whereas SLC1A4, SLC6A20, and the taurine transporter (SLC6A6) were related to favorable outcomes. Conclusions: These findings highlight AAT expression as a potential marker of EC aggressiveness and prognosis and suggest that integrating metabolic features with molecular classification may improve risk stratification and identify potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: FragMIL: A Fragment-Token Multiple-Instance Learning Framework for Cancer Detection from Cell-Free DNA Fragmentomics.
articles.authors: Bui TD, Lin YF, Nguyen MH et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (lcWGS) is a promising approach for non-invasive cancer detection. However, most existing methods summarize millions of cfDNA fragments into handcrafted sample-level features before classification, potentially discarding informative patterns carried by individual molecules. We aimed to develop and benchmark a framework that learns directly from fragment-level signals. Methods: We developed FragMIL, a fragment-token multiple-instance learning framework that represents each cfDNA molecule as a learnable token integrating end-motif, genomic-position, and fragment-length information, and aggregates thousands of fragment tokens into a patient-level cancer score. FragMIL was evaluated on 934 samples from three public lcWGS cohorts (pan-cancer, lung cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma) using five repeated subject-level splits, a 288-configuration design-space benchmark, and comparison with four established fragmentomic approaches (coverage, DELFI, end motif, and fragment size). Results: FragMIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) in every cohort, with 0.963 ± 0.009, 0.802 ± 0.009, and 0.910 ± 0.015 in the DELFI/Cristiano 2019, LUCAS/Mathios 2021, and Jiang 2015 cohorts, respectively. End-motif encoding provided the strongest standalone discriminative signal, whereas the optimal fragment pool was cohort-dependent, with open chromatin region fragments performing best for pan-cancer detection and tumor-enriched fragments for disease-specific cohorts. Performance was retained across cancer stages and cancer types. Conclusions: Preserving molecule-level fragmentomic information improves cancer detection, supporting fragment-token learning as a promising framework for next-generation cfDNA fragmentomics.

articles.title: Sex Hormone Estrone Sulfate Serendipitously Downregulates Intercellular Tunneling Nanotube Conduits, EMT, and Migration in Breast and Pancreatic Cancer Cells.
articles.authors: Wahab I, Li Y, Szewczuk MR
articles.abstract: Aim: Estrone (E1) is of particular interest as most breast cancers are diagnosed after menopause, the period in which E1 becomes the dominant estrogen. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly invasive cancer that lacks hormone receptors for estrogen (ER), progesterone (PR), and HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor-2). TNBC management remains clinically challenging despite recent advances in targeted and immunotherapeutic approaches. This study investigated the effects of the estrogen hormone estrone sulfate (E1S) on cancer cells. Here, E1S engages in non-classical biased G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) signaling in TNBC MDA-MB-231 cells, estrogen receptor-positive MCF-7 breast cancer cells, and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cells, which express estrogen, progesterone, and androgen receptors. Methods: We performed sialidase and colocalization assays in breast MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 cells and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cells. An epithelial-to-mesenchymal (EMT) transition, a tunneling nanotube assay, and a scratch wound assay were conducted to elucidate the cellular behaviors of E1S. We used a RawBlue reporter macrophage cell line to measure NFκB activity using the secreted embryonic alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) assay, and we measured cellular viability and metabolic activity using the AlamarBlue assay. Results: E1S induced NMBR/MMP9/Neu1 signaling in MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, PANC-1 and RawBlue cells. E1S increased E-cadherin expression, reduced N-cadherin and vimentin expression, decreased tunneling nanotube density, and reduced scratch wound migration. E1S increased SEAP activity, suggestive of increased nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) and activator protein-1 (AP-1)-mediated transcription. E1S treatment did not affect cell viability and metabolic activity in triple-negative MDA-MB-231 breast cells using the AlamarBlue assay in a dose-dependent manner. Conclusions: E1S binding to GPER potentiates a biased heterodimerization with the GPCR neuromedin B receptor (NMBR) to activate matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9) and neuraminidase 1 (Neu1), a signaling paradigm with previously established receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) and Toll-like (TLR) receptors. Biased, temporal GPER signaling has significant implications for breast and pancreatic cancer cellular behavior, which may be leveraged to inform therapeutic strategies for aggressive forms of breast and pancreatic cancers. This research study is mechanistic in nature and may have potential translational…

articles.title: Comparative Neoplasm Risk of Mirabegron and Antimuscarinic Therapy in Overactive Bladder: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
articles.authors: Yen FS, Wei JC, Hsu CC et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Aims: Mirabegron, a selective β3-adrenergic receptor agonist used to treat overactive bladder (OAB), can promote adipose tissue browning and alter systemic metabolism, raising interest in its potential relationship with cancer development. However, clinical evidence regarding cancer risk remains limited and inconsistent. We compared the risks of obesity-related and site-specific cancers between patients with OAB initiating mirabegron and those initiating antimuscarinic medications. Methods: We conducted a multicenter emulated target trial using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults aged ≥20 years with OAB or related symptoms who newly initiated mirabegron or an antimuscarinic medication were included using a new-user, active-comparator design. Patients with pre-existing malignancy were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed 1:1, and a 1-year lag period after treatment initiation was applied for cancer outcomes to reduce potential reverse causation from occult malignancy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) under an intention-to-treat analog. Results: A 365-day lag/landmark period was applied before propensity-score matching. Patients with a recorded neoplasm or death during this period, or without follow-up extending through day 366, were excluded. Subsequent 1:1 propensity-score matching yielded 106,500 patients in each treatment group. Mirabegron initiation was not associated with the composite of obesity-related neoplasms compared with antimuscarinic initiation (HR, 1.011; 95% CI, 0.954-1.071). The individual neoplasm outcomes also showed no significant between-group differences. However, among patients eligible for the 1-year landmark mortality analysis, mirabegron initiation was associated with higher subsequent all-cause mortality (HR, 1.083; 95% CI, 1.044-1.124). Exploratory negative-control analysis of Hodgkin lymphoma showed no significant association. Conclusions: Among patients with OAB, mirabegron initiation was not associated with a significant difference in overall obesity-related neoplasm risk compared with antimuscarinic initiation. The observed associations with all-cause mortality should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design, multiple comparisons, and potential residual confounding. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Bile Cell-Free DNA as a Liquid Biopsy for Biliary Tract Malignancies: A Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Dhir A, Martins B, Yeung ZP et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Biliary tract cancers (BTCs) carry a poor prognosis driven by frequent diagnosis at advanced or metastatic stages. Inadequate tissue sampling impedes biomarker-directed selection of therapy that could potentially improve outcomes over limited chemotherapeutic options. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) yields limited sensitivity. However, given its direct contact with the tumor, bile holds promise as a locally enriched source of tumor-derived cfDNA for evaluation. Methods: Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE without date restrictions. Seventeen primary studies of bile cfDNA in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), gallbladder carcinoma (GBC), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) were synthesized narratively. Results: Compared to plasma cfDNA, Bile cfDNA was isolated at higher concentrations and in longer fragments than plasma cfDNA; bile cfDNA demonstrated higher concordance with matched tumor tissue, capturing more actionable alterations. Pairing it with serum CA19-9 or newer bile-derived markers improved performance. Emerging data suggest a role in early detection of CCA during PSC surveillance. Conclusions: Bile cfDNA as a liquid biopsy medium offers analytic advantages over plasma for detecting and profiling biliary malignancy. Standardized collection, extraction, and reporting protocols and prospective multicenter validation are needed before routine use.

articles.title: Multimodal Hyperspectroscopy with LuViva® for Detection of CIN2+ in Women Referred for Colposcopy: A Prospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
articles.authors: Millert-Kalińska S, Pruski D, Przybylski M
articles.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of multimodal hyperspectral spectroscopy (MHS) using the LuViva® Advanced Cervical Scan for the detection of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) in women referred for further cervical assessment. Methods: This prospective, non-randomized diagnostic study included 77 women examined between September 2025 and April 2026. Participants were referred because of abnormal liquid-based cytology (LBC), high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection, or other indications for colposcopy. LuViva examination was performed before colposcopy with cervical biopsy. Histopathological diagnosis based on biopsy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure specimens was used as the reference standard. The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy were calculated for HR-HPV testing, LBC, and different LuViva positivity thresholds. Results: The mean age was 39.0 ± 8.4 years. The final histopathology showed no lesions in 30 women, LSIL in 18, HSIL in 28, and cervical cancer in one. For CIN2+ detection, HR-HPV testing demonstrated a sensitivity of 93.1% and specificity of 29.2%, whereas LBC had a sensitivity of 82.8% and specificity of 39.6%. LuViva testing showed sensitivities between 82.8% and 100%, and a specificity-when comparing with LBC-of 45.8% but 20.8% in LuViva alone. LuViva results differ significantly between women with CIN2+ and those with LSIL or no lesions. Conclusions: LuViva showed potential as an adjunctive triage tool, as no CIN2+ lesions were observed among women with a low-risk result; however, the small number of negative tests and wide confidence intervals preclude safely deferring colposcopy. The AND strategy showed a modest numerical improvement in specificity and overall accuracy compared with LBC alone but did not show an increase in sensitivity; this finding should be considered exploratory.

articles.title: Species Distribution, Antifungal Susceptibility, and Factors Associated with Recurrence in Vulvovaginal Candidiasis.
articles.authors: Özmen E, Yardımcı AC
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a common condition in clinical practice, and the absence of standardized diagnostic criteria based solely on clinical findings remains a challenge. This study aimed to evaluate the distribution of Candida species, antifungal susceptibility patterns, recurrence rates, and clinical factors associated with recurrent disease.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 345 VVC episodes from 325 patients in whom Candida species were isolated from vaginal cultures. Demographic and clinical characteristics, identified Candida species, antifungal susceptibility test results, and recurrence patterns were analyzed. Associations with recurrent VVC were evaluated using univariable analyses and multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: Candida albicans was the most frequently isolated species, accounting for 85.2% (n = 294) of cases, followed by C. glabrata (9.6%; n = 33) and C. krusei (1.7%; n = 6). Fluconazole susceptibility patterns did not differ significantly between patients with ≥3 recurrent episodes and those with <3 recurrent episodes (p = 0.493). Similarly, no significant difference was observed for voriconazole susceptibility (p = 0.116). High in vitro susceptibility rates were observed for caspofungin, amphotericin B, and micafungin in both groups. Multivariable Firth logistic regression analysis demonstrated that smoking (OR = 3.83; 95% CI: 1.81-8.81; p < 0.001), intrauterine device use (OR = 16.77; 95% CI: 4.13-153.53; p < 0.001), and antibiotic use (OR = 7.81; 95% CI: 3.90-17.30; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with recurrence, whereas pregnancy was not significantly associated with recurrence (OR = 2.05; 95% CI: 0.78-5.66; p = 0.147).

articles.title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of an AI Chatbot-Based Psychosocial Self-Management Program for Women with Infertility: A Non-Randomized Feasibility Study.
articles.authors: Lee J, Park S, Nam SH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women undergoing infertility treatment experience elevated perceived stress, anxiety, and difficulty identifying and describing their emotions (alexithymia), yet access to conventional psychological care is constrained by stigma, time, and cost.
OBJECTIVE: To develop an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot-based psychosocial self-management program for women with infertility and to examine its feasibility and preliminary patterns of change in perceived stress, depressive symptoms, state anxiety, and alexithymia. Feasibility was the primary objective; the four psychological measures were secondary and are reported as exploratory.
METHODS: A non-randomized, two-group pretest-posttest feasibility study was conducted with 37 women recruited sequentially from a single infertility centre in the Republic of Korea; the comparison group was recruited and assessed first (n = 19), followed by the intervention group (n = 18). The intervention group completed six chatbot sessions over two weeks. Outcomes were the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-State subscale (STAI-S), and the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20).
RESULTS: Feasibility indicators were favourable: retention was 92.5% overall (37/40) and 90.0% in the intervention group (18/20), and all retained intervention participants completed all six sessions (108/108, 100%). The groups differed at baseline in age (33.33 ± 3.36 vs. 35.84 ± 4.00 years, p = 0.047). Group × time interactions favoured the intervention group for perceived stress (F(1, 35) = 14.37, p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.29), state anxiety (F(1, 35) = 4.40, p = 0.043, ηp2 = 0.11), and alexithymia (F(1, 35) = 6.92, p = 0.013, ηp2 = 0.16), but not for depressive symptoms (F(1, 35) = 3.66, p = 0.064, ηp2 = 0.09).
CONCLUSIONS: The program was feasible in terms of retention and adherence, with all retained intervention participants completing all six sessions. Because allocation was non-random and confounded with calendar time, and because the sample was small, these findings describe preliminary patterns of change and do not establish effectiveness. An adequately powered randomized trial with concurrent recruitment, an attention-matched comparator, and follow-up assessment is required.

articles.title: Haitian Mamas: The Development and Two-Year Implementation of an OB/GYN-Based Preventive Behavioral Health Group in a Safety-Net Hospital Setting.
articles.authors: Sokoto KC, Milord J, Taknint JT et al.
articles.abstract: Perinatal mental health conditions are among the leading causes of maternal mortality in the United States. However, 50% to 70% of perinatal mental health cases go undiagnosed, and of those diagnosed, fewer than 30% receive treatment. At Boston Medical Center, a large safety-net academic medical center in the northeastern United States (US), this treatment gap became apparent when new Refugee Women's Health Clinic patient visits increased by 138% following an influx of Haitian forced migrants starting in 2021. In response, we developed and implemented Haitian Mamas, a same-day access preventive behavioral health group within the Obstetrics and Gynecology department. This quality improvement study evaluates the development of Haitian Mamas from August 2023 to 2025, using four Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles. We evaluated the feasibility of this program across six domains: reach, engagement, integration of measurement-based care, financial viability, adaptability, and provider-perceived acceptability. Over two years, 196 women participated in the group, with an average of eight members per group, and there was a progressive improvement in integrating measurement-based care, which rose from 11.5% in Cycle 1 to 67.4% in Cycle 4. 35% screened positive for moderate to server mental health concerns. A thematic analysis of qualitative data from providers' weekly post-group reflections identified implementation barriers and facilitators for Haitian Mamas. Our findings suggest that the development and implementation of a same-day access, OBGYN-based preventive behavioral health group for perinatal patients in a safety-net hospital setting is operationally feasible.

articles.title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Single-Cell Analysis Prioritizes YWHAB Within Ubiquitination-Related Transcriptional Programs in Endometrial Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Wang J, Zhu H, Li Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ubiquitination-related transcriptional programs may help characterize epithelial heterogeneity in endometrial carcinoma (EC). We aimed to identify candidates associated with these programs and epithelial plasticity.
METHODS: We integrated a 43,613-cell atlas from five endometrioid EC samples and two normal endometrial samples with bulk transcriptomic, genetic-association and protein-expression data. Five scoring methods defined a consensus expression score, with HIGH and LOW quartiles defined within the Epithelial + EMT_like lineage. Differential expression and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) identified candidates for exploratory Mendelian randomization (MR) and survival-based prioritization among 541 patients from The Cancer Genome Atlas Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (TCGA-UCEC) cohort. Repeated nested cross-validation and cross-model feature support were used to evaluate internal performance and candidate stability. Pseudobulk, independently curated ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) gene sets and scSurv input masking provided sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The lineage-restricted screen identified 444 candidates, including 412 detectable in TCGA. GeneCards and curated Reactome and KEGG UCell scores were positively correlated (ρ = 0.519 and 0.579). YWHAB ranked fourth among 412 genes in the top-10% workflow analysis and fifth in the top-20% sensitivity analysis. Among the 12 nominal MR-associated genes, it had the highest machine-learning priority. Its single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) MR estimate was nominal (odds ratio (OR) = 1.732, p = 0.0488) and did not survive multiple-testing correction. Higher bulk YWHAB expression was associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 2.188, 95% CI 1.559-3.072). Western blotting showed higher YWHAB protein expression in EC than controls (nine versus nine tissues, p = 0.0027), consistent with descriptive Human Protein Atlas (HPA) staining. Single-cell analyses associated YWHAB with RNA processing, proteostasis-related expression and epithelial-state heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: Lineage-restricted discovery and cross-model prioritization identify YWHAB as an exploratory candidate associated with ubiquitination-related transcriptional programs in EC. Protein-expression evidence supports its further investigation, while causal function and clinical prognostic utility require independent validation.

articles.title: Clinical and Molecular Spectrum of 1q21.1 Copy Number Variations: A Case Series.
articles.authors: Esen TE, Celik LY, Aydin Gumus A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 1q21.1 copy number variations (CNVs) are recurrent rearrangements with a clinical spectrum, from neurodevelopmental disorders and congenital anomalies to apparently unaffected carrier status, reflecting incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.
METHODS: Our chromosomal microarray (CytoScan HD) database was retrospectively screened for pathogenic or likely pathogenic 1q21.1 CNVs.
RESULTS: Twenty probands from 19 families (14 postnatal, 6 prenatal) carried 21 CNV events: 11 deletions (52.4%) and 10 duplications (47.6%). Of these, 16 (76.2%) were confined to the distal segment, 3 (14.3%) to the proximal segment, and 2 (9.5%) spanned both. One proband carried coexisting proximal duplication and distal deletion, both inherited from an apparently unaffected father. Of the 17 probands (85%) with parental testing, 7 (41.2%) had de novo and 10 (58.8%) inherited CNVs. Distal CNVs were mostly observed in probands with neurodevelopmental or cardiac phenotypes, whereas bilateral upper extremity anomalies were observed in both prenatally ascertained fetuses with isolated proximal deletions. Corpus callosum atrophy and choanal atresia were infrequently reported co-occurring findings, whereas prenatal intracranial hemorrhage was potentially novel; each occurred in one proband. Given the small proximal subgroup and differing ascertainment, these segment-associated trends are descriptive.
CONCLUSIONS: This series highlights the relevance of segment localization and parental segregation data in interpreting 1q21.1 CNVs.

articles.title: Early Amniocentesis Versus Transabdominal Chorionic Villus Sampling for Early Invasive Prenatal Diagnosis: A 15-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Podobnik P, Meštrović T, Podobnik M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Two sampling routes are available when definitive genetic testing is required in the first trimester: early amniocentesis (EA) and transabdominal chorionic villus sampling (TA-CVS). Direct comparisons of the two at 11 to 14 weeks of gestation are, however, few. Our aim was to place the techniques side by side in terms of the genetic information they yield, the chromosomal abnormalities they uncover and the pregnancy outcomes that follow them.
METHODS: This single-operator, prospective cohort study evaluated singleton pregnancies between 11 and 14 weeks of gestation across 15 years (2010-2024), comparing TA-CVS with EA. Fluid for EA was withdrawn by amniovacucentesis (3-5 mL of amniotic fluid) through a 22-gauge needle, while villus tissue was taken with a 20-gauge needle, both with the ultrasound image visible throughout. Color Doppler assessment of the uteroplacental and fetal vessels and of the fetal heart rate preceded and followed every procedure. Material obtained by either route underwent cytogenetic testing, and targeted copy-number variant (CNV) analysis was added whenever ultrasonography had shown a major structural abnormality.
RESULTS: Of 3238 singleton pregnancies, a cytogenetic result was achieved in 1611 of 1613 (99.9%) EA and in 1622 of 1625 (99.8%) TA-CVS cases. An abnormal chromosome finding was present in 138 cases (4.3%), while pathogenic CNVs emerged in 5 of 35 (14.3%) fetuses with structural abnormalities. Spontaneous abortion affected 4 of 1613 EA pregnancies (0.25%) and 3 of 1625 TA-CVS pregnancies (0.18%; difference 0.06%, 95% CI -0.32 to 0.47%; p = 0.73). Talipes occurred in two EA cases and none after TA-CVS, whereas hemangiomas occurred in two TA-CVS cases and none after EA. Premature rupture of membranes, preterm delivery, neonatal respiratory distress and neonatal anomalies did not differ between the groups. Doppler pulsatility indices were essentially unchanged after both procedures; small changes reached statistical significance only in the umbilical (p = 0.032) and middle cerebral (p < 0.001) arteries, and all were transient and unaccompanied by clinical complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Fetal-derived material adequate for first-trimester genetic diagnosis was obtained by both routes, with cytogenetic results in more than 99% of pregnancies. Beyond the conventional chromosomal abnormalities, targeted CNV analysis added clinically meaningful diagnoses in fetuses with structural anomalies. Invasive fetal sampling…

articles.title: Beyond the Embryo: Rethinking the Genetics of Recurrent Implantation Failure in the PGT-A Era.
articles.authors: Voros C, Chatzinikolaou F, Papadimas G et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) affects many women undergoing IVF, but its genetic basis remains poorly defined. Most studies linking genetic or chromosomal factors to RIF were conducted before preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) was widely used, when embryonic aneuploidy could not be reliably excluded. This review asks whether that evidence still holds now that PGT-A allows embryo aneuploidy to be excluded, at least analytically, as the default explanation for failed transfers.
METHODS: We reviewed the literature on parental karyotype abnormalities, chromosomal microarray findings, thrombophilia-related gene variants, and endometrial receptivity testing in women with RIF, comparing pre-PGT-A and post-PGT-A era studies where available.
RESULTS: Most foundational data on RIF genetics predate PGT-A and likely overstate the embryo's contribution to implantation failure relative to maternal factors. Very few studies have re-evaluated RIF using strict, PGT-A-confirmed criteria for "true" implantation failure. Evidence for thrombophilia gene variants remains inconsistent across populations, and endometrial receptivity testing still lacks well-established genetic correlates.
CONCLUSIONS: The genetic evidence base for RIF needs updating for the PGT-A era. A clear, PGT-A-confirmed picture of the genetic and chromosomal contributors to true implantation failure is still missing. Closing this gap should be a priority for future research in reproductive genetics.

articles.title: CRISPR/Cas-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Intestinal Parasites: From Proof-of-Concept to Point-of-Care Testing.
articles.authors: Alsaady IM
articles.abstract: Intestinal parasitic infections remain a significant global public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective disease management and control. Although conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopy, antigen detection, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR), are widely used, each possesses inherent limitations related to sensitivity, turnaround time, laboratory infrastructure, or point-of-care applicability. Recent advances in clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)/CRISPR-associated (Cas) systems have led to the development of highly sensitive and rapid molecular diagnostic platforms suitable for decentralized testing. This review summarizes current applications of CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics for intestinal and foodborne parasitic infections, with particular emphasis on assays developed for Giardia duodenalis, Cryptosporidium parvum, Clonorchis sinensis, Fasciola hepatica, and Schistosoma spp. Published studies have predominantly employed Cas12a, with additional applications of Cas12b and Cas13a and, more recently, a type I-A Cascade-Cas3 system, generally coupled with isothermal amplification methods such as recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) or recombinase-aided amplification (RAA), enabling highly sensitive detection within 60-90 min using fluorescence or lateral-flow strip readouts. The available evidence indicates high analytical sensitivity and specificity, with several assays demonstrating substantial agreement with conventional molecular methods and potential for point-of-care development. However, current CRISPR-based assays remain limited by dependence on nucleic acid extraction, relatively small clinical validation cohorts, lack of standardized protocols, and the persistence of false-negative results associated with low parasite burdens and pre-analytical variables. Emerging strategies, including simplified or extraction-free sample preparation, one-pot sample-to-answer platforms, and detection of parasite-derived cell-free DNA, may further enhance the clinical utility of CRISPR diagnostics. Overall, CRISPR/Cas-based technologies represent a promising next-generation approach for intestinal parasite diagnosis, although large-scale clinical validation and workflow optimization are still required before widespread implementation in routine clinical and field settings.

articles.title: Diagnostic Assessment of Tamoxifen-Associated Endometrial Pathology: A Narrative Review of Biomarkers, Risk Models, and Translational Gaps.
articles.authors: Hakami MA
articles.abstract: In tamoxifen-related endometrial alterations, a challenge arises due to the similarity between clinically significant diseases and both benign proliferation and benign polyps. This narrative review examines the clinical assessment, imaging, tissue sampling, biomarkers, and prediction models for women taking tamoxifen. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and selected articles from reference lists up to August 2026, focusing on human studies reporting diagnostic performance, biomarkers, sampling limitations, or clinical prediction. Evidence was divided into three groups: tamoxifen-specific clinical studies, external studies of endometrial cancer, and mechanistic investigations; however, the heterogeneous populations and endpoints prevented pooled accuracy estimates. Although thickening of the endometrium is associated with an increased risk of abnormal bleeding, the finding when there is no abnormal bleeding is not significant enough to warrant routine surveillance of asymptomatic users. Representative histopathology remains the key, especially if hysteroscopy is used for sampling, particularly if the area is focal or if a diagnosis is not reached. These tissue markers primarily reflect the biology of exposure and show promise in methylation, cytology, serum-marker, and prediction studies, mostly in populations that are not tamoxifen-validated. Thus, reported discrimination does not provide sufficient reassurance to exclude atypical hyperplasia or carcinoma in tamoxifen users. The priorities are prospective validation in well-defined symptomatic patient groups, independent validation of locked assays or models against clinical baseline, and a focus on missed significant disease, avoided procedures, and patient outcomes. The current evidence favors a cautious diagnostic evaluation and does not define a biomarker-based screening or surveillance approach for women taking tamoxifen.

articles.title: Extravascular Cyanoacrylate "Embolization" for the Treatment of Vesico-Vaginal Fistula: A Minimally Invasive Alternative.
articles.authors: Vizzuso A, Bazzocchi MV, Spina A et al.
articles.abstract: Vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF) is a debilitating complication commonly occurring after gynecologic surgery and frequently associated with significant morbidity and impaired quality of life. Although surgical repair remains the standard treatment, management strategies remain heterogeneous, while conservative approaches often require prolonged urinary diversion with variable success rates. We report a case of persistent post-surgical VVF successfully treated with image-guided embolization using N-butyl cyanoacrylate methylsulfone (NBCA; Glubran 2, GEM; Viareggio, Italy) through a transvesical catheter-based approach after failure of conservative management. This case illustrates the potential role of interventional radiology in the management of selected VVFs, suggesting that image-guided fistula embolization may represent a minimally invasive treatment option when conservative management fails and surgical reintervention is undesirable or can be deferred.

articles.title: Plasma and Serum Metagenomic Sequencing of Microbial Cell-Free Nucleic Acids for Suspected Central Nervous System Infection: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Bratosin F, Branea HS, Hogea E
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Untargeted metagenomic sequencing of microbial cell-free DNA or RNA in plasma or serum offers pathogen detection without lumbar puncture or biopsy, but its value in suspected central nervous system (CNS) infection is uncertain. We reviewed diagnostic yield, agreement with CNS-site testing, clinical impact, and failure modes. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched with seven documented strings (inception to 2 September 2026), supplemented by citation and web searching. Eligible reports were primary human studies of untargeted plasma or serum metagenomic sequencing with a separable result in patients with suspected or confirmed infectious CNS syndromes. Selection, extraction, and design-specific risk-of-bias appraisal followed PRISMA 2020 and were performed independently by two authors with disagreements resolved by discussion; the search was restricted to PubMed/MEDLINE and no protocol was registered. Synthesis was narrative because designs and reference standards were incompatible. Results: Of 190 reports assessed, 69 studies were included (18 denominator-based cohorts, 8 small series, 43 case reports; 51 from the United States). Positive CNS-specific clinical impact in commercial assay cohorts ranged from 0 of 24 adult to 5 of 24 pediatric meningoencephalitis tests. Among 51 case-level reports, the plasma or serum result was concordant with CNS-site testing in 28, positive when CNS-site testing was negative in 5, unconfirmed in 12, and negative or missed the pathogen in 6. All five plasma-only detections came from single case reports, which contributed to no yield or agreement denominator; excluding the four abstract-level case reports moved no proportion by more than 1.3 percentage points. RNA viruses, low-burden focal mould disease, and chromosomally integrated HHV-6 were recurrent sources of false-negative or misleading results. Conclusions: Plasma or serum metagenomic sequencing is a useful adjunct in selected difficult CNS infections, particularly disseminated, fungal, amoebic, or fastidious bacterial disease, but it does not replace CNS-site diagnostics.

articles.title: Subclinical Cardiovascular Adaptation in Uncomplicated Monochorionic Twin Pregnancies: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Biomarker Findings.
articles.authors: Campillo Ajenjo M, Herrero Ruiz B, Sotillo Mallo L et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Although cardiac involvement is well characterized in complicated monochorionic (MC) pregnancies, whether subtle cardiovascular changes occur in uncomplicated pregnancies remains unclear. We characterized fetal and neonatal cardiovascular adaptation using echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers. Methods: In this prospective longitudinal cohort, 76 dichorionic (DC) and 68 uncomplicated monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twins underwent fetal echocardiography at 28 weeks and neonatal echocardiography within 72 h after birth. Cord blood N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP) were assessed at delivery. Analyses used generalized estimating equations to account for within-pregnancy clustering and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Associations between cardiac biomarkers and fetal echocardiographic parameters and interactions with chorionicity and gestational age at birth were also evaluated. Results: MCDA fetuses showed trends toward a higher cardiothoracic ratio, lower right ventricular fractional shortening and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, and a higher prevalence of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) compared with DC fetuses. In the early neonatal period, nominal differences in interventricular septal thickness and tissue Doppler indices did not persist after FDR correction. Cord-blood hs-cTnI (21.83 vs. 12.29 pg/mL; p = 0.015, FDR-adjusted p = 0.027) and NT-proBNP (1327.6 vs. 887.6 pg/mL; p = 0.018, FDR-adjusted p = 0.027) concentrations were higher in MCDA twins. After gestational age adjustment, the association with hs-cTnI remained relatively stable, whereas that with NT-proBNP was attenuated; neither remained significant after FDR correction (p = 0.116 for both). The TR-hs-cTnI association differed by chorionicity (p for interaction < 0.001, FDR-adjusted p < 0.004) and persisted after adjustment for gestational age at birth. Conclusions: Conventional echocardiographic measures of cardiac structure and function appear to be largely preserved in uncomplicated MCDA twins during fetal life and the early neonatal period. Higher cord-blood hs-cTnI and NT-proBNP may suggest subclinical myocardial stress associated with monochorionicity, although gestational age-adjusted findings warrant caution.

articles.title: Uterine Fibroids in Pregnancy: Maternal, Obstetric, and Neonatal Outcomes in a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Martire FG, d'Abate C, Costantini E et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Uterine fibroids are the most common benign tumors in women of reproductive age, and their coexistence with pregnancy is becoming increasingly frequent as maternal age at first pregnancy rises. Objective: The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of uterine fibroids on obstetric and neonatal outcomes and, secondarily, the effect of pregnancy on fibroid growth. Study Design: This retrospective observational study included 1512 pregnant women, 136 of whom had uterine fibroids, who were followed at a university hospital. Ultrasound examinations were performed before pregnancy (T0) and during the first (T1), second (T2), and third (T3) trimesters. Fibroid number, size, location, and ultrasound characteristics according to FIGO classification were recorded. Obstetric complications, mode of delivery, and neonatal outcomes were analyzed according to fibroid type and size. Fibroid growth throughout pregnancy was also evaluated. Results: Among 1512 pregnant women followed between 1 January 2024 and 30 November 2025, 136 patients (9.0%) had uterine fibroids. A positive family history of fibroids was identified in 36% of cases. Gestational complications were infrequent overall, although gestational hypothyroidism was significantly more common among women with fibroids, whereas preeclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage were significantly less frequent in univariable analysis. Vaginal delivery was less frequent in the fibroid group, while operative vaginal delivery and cesarean section were significantly more common. Fetal growth restriction (FGR) and umbilical venous pH also differed significantly between groups. In multivariable analysis adjusted for maternal age, BMI, parity, ART, smoking, chronic hypertension, and diabetes, the association with cesarean section was attenuated (aOR 1.47, 95% CI 0.93-2.32), whereas lower PPH rates persisted (aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.14-0.84) and a slight inverse association with umbilical venous pH remained detectable (β -0.01, p = 0.01). Exploratory stratification according to FIGO classification (3-4 vs. 5-7) showed significant differences in PPH, cesarean section, FGR, and LGA. Repeated-measure analysis demonstrated progressive fibroid growth in maximum diameter during pregnancy compared with preconceptional measurements (T0) (p < 0.001), with substantial enlargement already observed by the second trimester and fibroids ≤5 cm exhibiting greater relative growth at T2 compared with T0 than larger lesions (+18% vs.…

articles.title: Cell-Free DNA-Based Blood Tests for Colorectal Cancer Screening: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
articles.authors: Alkhawlani G, Alsanea N, Alharbi R et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major cause of rising global rates of cancer-related morbidity and mortality. CRC rates are particularly increasing among younger populations; however, the implementation of effective CRC screening programs remains limited. Colonoscopy, the gold standard CRC screening technique, is restricted by complex procedures, invasive methods, and low patient adherence. Therefore, non-invasive screening through circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-based blood tests is emerging as an effective alternative. Methods: This narrative review summarizes recent advances in cfDNA-based blood tests for colorectal cancer screening and early detection. Relevant English-language publications from 2021 to 2025 were searched on PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases, supplemented by examination of reference lists. The study evaluated various diagnostic performance measures [sensitivity, specificity, and AUC (area under the curve)] and compared cfDNA-based approaches with previously established screening methods. Results: CRC detection and diagnostic efficacies of cfDNA-based technologies (mutation analysis, fragmentomics, integrated multi-omics approaches, and methylation profiling) have been reported in several recent studies. Fragmentomics and integrated multi-omics strategies have reported high diagnostic accuracy in a small number of heterogeneous, non-pooled studies. During a large-scale ECLIPSE study, involving an average-risk screening population, the Shield blood-based assay demonstrated 83.1% sensitivity for CRC, whereas the sensitivity for advanced precancerous lesions was only 13.2%. However, lack of assay standardization, low sensitivity for advanced precancerous lesions, methodological heterogeneity, and the need for prospective validation before routine clinical implementation remain major limitations. Conclusions: cfDNA-based non-invasive screening tools offer promising colorectal cancer detection accuracy. However, prospective validation, standardization, and optimization of analytical workflows are mandatory for the widespread clinical implementation of these techniques.

articles.title: Comparative Detection of IDH1 R132H and TERT Promoter Mutations in Plasma and Cerebrospinal Fluid of Patients with Glioma Using Targeted Droplet Digital PCR.
articles.authors: Jain M, Rahmatullin T, Alexeev I et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular profiling is essential for glioma classification, but in some cases tissue sampling may be limited, whereas reported detectability of cell-free tumor DNA (cftDNA) in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) varies considerably. The aim of this study was to compare the detection rates and concentrations of cftDNA carrying IDH1 R132H and TERT promoter C228T/C250T mutations in paired plasma and CSF samples, as well as to examine associated clinical characteristics. Methods: 66 patients with WHO grade 1-4 gliomas were enrolled before surgery. Preoperative plasma and lumbar CSF were collected before tissue-damaging procedures. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was isolated from 5 mL of plasma and 2.5-5.0 mL of CSF and analyzed using mutation-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) assays. Results: cfDNA was available from 65 CSF and 63 plasma samples. Total cfDNA concentration was lower in CSF than in plasma (medians: 434.1 vs. 1240.3 copies/mL; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, cftDNA carrying at least one of the assayed mutations was detected in 14/65 CSF samples (21.5%) and in 0/63 plasma samples (0.0%) (p < 0.001). IDH1 R132H was detected in 4.6% of CSF samples, and TERT promoter mutations were detected in 16.9%. Every CSF mutation with available paired tissue data was also identified in the corresponding tumor. Glioma grade 4 and contrast-enhancing tumors were associated with higher CSF cfDNA, cftDNA carrying at least one of the assayed mutations, and mutant allele fraction values (p < 0.05), whereas tumor size and localization were not significantly associated with these parameters (p > 0.05). Conclusions: With the presented targeted ddPCR workflow, lumbar CSF was substantially more informative than plasma for detecting the selected glioma-associated mutations. CSF cftDNA analysis may complement tissue profiling, although broader panels and larger prospective studies are needed to establish its clinical sensitivity.

articles.title: Predicting MCI-to-Alzheimer's Conversion: A Systematic Benchmark of Classical, Machine Learning, and Deep Survival Models.
articles.authors: Santa NA, Daza-Santacoloma G, Serna WS
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting time-to-conversion from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a critical clinical challenge. Most survival analyses rely on static baseline variables, ignoring the temporal dynamics of serial neuroimaging. We benchmark seven survival model families using a novel temporal MRI descriptor pipeline on ADNI. Methods: A cohort of 661 MCI patients (250 conversion events, 37.8%, median follow-up 42.0 months) was constructed from ADNI. FreeSurfer volumetrics of six brain regions were summarised into three time-based descriptors each (atrophy rate, trajectory variability σ, and time-weighted cumulative mean μ) under strict anti-leakage constraints, yielding 18 neuroimaging features which, combined with six clinical variables (age, sex, education, MMSE, ADAS-13, and APOE-ε4), form a 24-dimensional covariate vector. Cox PH, Weibull AFT, Exponential, RSF, GBST, DeepSurv, and DeepHit were evaluated under stratified 5-fold cross-validation and assessed on an independent OASIS-3 cohort (n=78) as an exploratory analysis. Results: All seven models achieved C-index 0.853-0.863 (Δ=0.010), with Cox PH reaching 0.863±0.027 using only routine structural MRI. Time-dependent AUC ranged from 0.856 (12 months) to 0.938 (48 months). Risk stratification by quartile yielded highly separated Kaplan-Meier curves (log-rank p<0.001). On OASIS-3 (n=78, exploratory), classical models showed preliminary cross-cohort consistency (Weibull AFT 0.760±0.063, RSF 0.759±0.049), while deep learning degraded substantially (DeepSurv 0.551±0.116); these results are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as confirmatory given the small per-fold sample size (EPV ≈ 1). Conclusions: The temporal MRI descriptor pipeline achieves a C-index of 0.863 using only routine structural MRI, without PET or CSF biomarkers, demonstrating strong discriminative performance on ADNI MCI-to-AD conversion. The narrow performance band (Δ=0.010) suggests that, within this feature-engineering paradigm, no clear performance separation was observed among the evaluated model architectures; this convergence may reflect feature-level rather than architecture-level constraints, although the underlying cause cannot be established from discriminative performance alone. Classical models showed more stable cross-cohort behaviour under data-scarce conditions; prospective validation on larger cohorts with full covariate parity is required before clinical translation…

articles.title: Ectopic Adrenal Cortical Tissue in the Ovary: A Rare Incidental Histopathologic Finding.
articles.authors: Song DH, Cho IA, Baek JC
articles.abstract: Ectopic adrenal cortical tissue (EACT) is an uncommon developmental heterotopia and is exceptionally rare in the ovary of adult women. A 52-year-old woman, 6 years after menopause, was evaluated for progressive enlargement of a uterine leiomyoma and postmenopausal spotting. Transvaginal ultrasonography and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated multiple uterine leiomyomas but no adnexal mass or endometrioma. During total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, dense adhesions between the sigmoid colon and posterior cul-de-sac were unexpectedly encountered. Histopathologic examination of the adhesion-related tissue revealed neither endometriosis nor significant inflammatory change. Microscopic examination of the ovary identified a 1.9 mm, sharply circumscribed nodule composed of clear, vacuolated zona fasciculata-like cells and compact eosinophilic zona reticularis-like cells. The lesional cells showed diffuse Melan-A immunoreactivity and focal-to-patchy inhibin-α positivity, supporting adrenocortical differentiation. The findings established a diagnosis of ovarian EACT. This case emphasizes that microscopic ovarian adrenal rests may be radiologically occult and should be distinguished from ovarian steroidogenic neoplasms by integrating clinical, morphologic, and immunohistochemical findings.

articles.title: Cytokine Profiles in Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia: Associations with Lesion Severity and Exploratory Treatment Response.
