articles.authors: Major AL, Riger A, Kharchenko N et al.
articles.abstract: Background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the principal cause of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). Cytokines regulate antiviral immunity and tissue remodeling, and cytokine profiling may provide additional information about the biology of cervical lesions. Objective: To characterize cytokine profiles in cervical mucus and serum across grades of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Methods: The study included 90 women aged 18-80 years: 30 HPV-negative women with negative cytology (Control) and 60 HPV-positive women with histologically confirmed low-grade (LSIL, n = 30; Gr-1) or high-grade (HSIL, n = 30; Gr-2) squamous intraepithelial lesions. Participants were also stratified by minor (grade 1) or major (grade 2) colposcopic findings. An exploratory subgroup of 15 women with HPV16/18-positive HSIL received antiviral and immunomodulatory therapy. Concentrations of 27 cytokines (pg/mL)-FGF, eotaxin, G-CSF, GM-CSF, IFN-γ, IL-1ra, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IL-9, IL-10, IL-12(p70), IL-13, IL-15, IL-17A, IP-10, MCP-1, MIP-1α, MIP-1β, PDGF-BB, RANTES, TNF-α, and VEGF-were measured in serum and cervical mucus using the Bio-Plex Pro Human Cytokine 27-plex assay (Bio-Rad, USA) on a Luminex 200 platform. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 23.0 and Microsoft Excel 365. Results are reported as medians and interquartile ranges [Q1-Q3]. A two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Exploratory multivariate analyses identified IL-1β, IP-10, MCP-1, and FGF as the cytokines most strongly associated with lesion severity and colposcopic findings. In cervical mucus, HSIL was associated with the highest IL-1β concentration (0.83 pg/mL [0.18-4.91] vs. 0.30 pg/mL [0.04-0.69] in controls; p < 0.001) and the lowest IP-10 concentration (3.07 pg/mL [1.02-13.16] vs. 25.12 pg/mL [5.01-42.40]; p < 0.001). The highest mucus FGF concentration was observed in LSIL (1.73 pg/mL [1.33-2.27] vs. 0.32 pg/mL [0.17-0.59] in controls; p < 0.001), whereas MCP-1 was lower in LSIL than in HSIL (2.38 pg/mL [1.57-3.54] vs. 5.38 pg/mL [3.12-10.55]; p < 0.05). Similar patterns were observed in serum, except that IL-1β was lower than in controls. After treatment, HPV was undetectable in 10 women and remained detectable in 5. The overall cytokine profile changed only modestly. Among the five women with persistent HPV infection, cervical mucus MCP-1 was lower after treatment than before…

articles.title: The association between inflammation and pubertal development: Insights from NHANES and Mendelian randomization analyses.
articles.authors: Chen D, Qian L, Mei P et al.
articles.abstract: Our research seeks to elucidate the interplay between inflammation and pubertal development using association and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses, aiming to uncover the underlying potential causal relationship. Using data from the 2013 to 2016 and 2021 to 2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles, we assessed 3571 children and adolescents. To evaluate associations with pubertal status, logistic regression was performed for a panel of immune-inflammatory biomarkers: platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic inflammation response index, systemic immune-inflammation index, and pan-immune-inflammation value. Bidirectional 2-sample MR analysis was conducted: genetic instruments for exposures were from a published genome-wide protein quantitative trait locus study (91 inflammatory proteins), and outcomes were precocious puberty (PP) summary statistics from the FinnGen consortium R11 database to infer causality. The median age of participants was 10.00 years, with 1838 males (51.47%) and 1733 females (48.53%). In association analysis, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio showed a significant positive association with pubertal status across all models (fully adjusted: odds ratio [OR] = 1.198, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.095-1.311, P < .001). Systemic inflammation response index and systemic immune-inflammation index presented significant positive associations only in the fully adjusted model. Forward MR analysis suggested that genetically predicted higher levels of matrix metalloproteinase-10 (OR = 2.213, 95% CI: 1.218-4.024, P = .009) and osteoprotegerin (OR = 2.010, 95% CI: 1.082-3.734, P = .027) were associated with increased risk of PP, while higher tumor necrosis factor-β (TNF-β, OR = 0.678, 95% CI: 0.479-0.959, P = .028) decreased it. Reverse MR showed PP was positively associated with C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 1 (CXCL-1), fibroblast growth factor 5 (FGF-5), fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF-19), interleukin-7, interleukin-15 receptor subunit alpha, neurturin, and negatively associated with tumor necrosis factor-related activation-induced cytokine. Inflammatory processes may contribute to PP pathogenesis via pathways influencing pubertal timing and progression, providing new insights into pubertal development mechanisms and a scientific basis for future interventions.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and recovery impact of implementing enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathway in elderly patients with gynecological malignant tumors.
articles.authors: Wang A, Ying L, Sun X et al.
articles.abstract: Perioperative management is critical for optimizing recovery outcomes in elderly patients with gynecological malignant tumors, a demographic often facing significant health challenges. The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway has been proposed as a multifaceted approach designed to enhance recovery and minimize complications during the perioperative phase, particularly in vulnerable populations such as the elderly. Patients who underwent traditional perioperative management at the affiliated hospital of Chengde Medical University between January 2011 and December 2018 were selected as the conventional group. Patients who underwent ERAS perioperative management between January 2019 and July 2025 were selected as the ERAS group. Postoperative recovery and complications were then compared between the groups. The ERAS and control groups involved 149 and 90 patients, respectively. Patient characteristics were not significantly different between the 2 groups (P > .05). However, the ERAS group showed a lower volume of intraoperative fluid rehydration and a shorter time to first postoperative flatus, time to first defecation, duration of postoperative hospitalization, and interval time between surgery and the first postoperative chemotherapy session. The Visual Analogue Scale score at 24 hours postoperatively was also significantly lower in the ERAS group (P < .05). Meanwhile, there was no significant between-group difference in the incidence of postoperative complications and the 30-day readmission rate (all P > .05). Use of the ERAS pathway during the perioperative period does not increase the occurrence of postoperative complications and can accelerate recovery, shorten the postoperative hospitalization duration, and help with earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy in elderly patients with gynecological malignant tumors.

articles.title: Heterogeneity in nerve recovery patterns despite symptomatic improvement in paclitaxel-induced neuropathy: A longitudinal analysis.
articles.authors: Lim I, Moon YW, Suh M et al.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common and potentially persistent toxicity of paclitaxel. This prospective study aimed to characterize longitudinal changes in paclitaxel-induced CIPN by integrating serial neurophysiological and clinical assessments. Twenty-six patients receiving paclitaxel-based chemotherapy for breast, ovarian, or endometrial cancer were prospectively enrolled. Assessments were scheduled at baseline (T0), completion of chemotherapy (T1), 3 months posttreatment (T2), and 1 year posttreatment (T3) and included nerve conduction studies (NCS), the self-reported Leeds Assessment of Neuropathic Symptoms and Signs (S-LANSS), and Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading. Fourteen patients with available longitudinal outcome data were included in the analytic cohort. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and associations between NCS parameters and clinical measures were explored using repeated-measures correlation. S-LANSS scores increased from 1.29 ± 4.81 at T0 to 14.29 ± 4.23 at T1 and subsequently decreased to 4.86 ± 5.88 at T3 (overall P < .001), although they remained higher than baseline (P = .008). NCS amplitudes showed heterogeneous recovery patterns. Sural SNAP amplitude markedly decreased at T1 but recovered thereafter and was not significantly different from baseline at T3. In contrast, ulnar SNAP amplitude remained significantly reduced at T3 (P < .001), whereas tibial compound motor action potential amplitude was no longer significantly different from baseline (P = .060). NCS amplitudes were inversely associated with clinical measures, with the strongest association observed between ulnar SNAP amplitude and CTCAE grade (r = -0.720, P < .001). Paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy showed substantial symptomatic improvement after chemotherapy but heterogeneous electrophysiological recovery across peripheral nerves. Persistent abnormalities in selected nerves despite symptom improvement highlight the complementary roles of patient-reported outcomes and objective neurophysiological assessment in characterizing the longitudinal course of CIPN.

articles.title: Triple-Encoding Platform for Multiplexed In Situ Profiling of Extracellular Vesicle miRNAs Enables Precision Diagnosis of Ovarian Cancer.
articles.authors: Pei H, Kuang T, Dai Y et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer, the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, urgently demands early and accurate diagnostic methods. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tEVs) hold great promise as noninvasive biomarkers, yet their clinical translation is severely hampered by inherent heterogeneity and the inability of conventional assays to detect multiple types of biomarkers. To break this bottleneck, we developed a novel one-pot, triple-encoding platform that integrates size-fluorescence-encoded beads with a membrane fusion strategy. This enables simultaneous in situ profiling of 11 miRNAs across three distinct EV subpopulations defined by EpCAM/PD-L1 expression. Leveraging machine learning, an 11-miRNA logistic panel achieved tumor versus health discrimination (AUC = 0.995), and a combinatorial signature based on EV subpopulations and miRNA profiles enabled the classification of ovarian cancer subtypes, achieving 78.6% accuracy in the validation cohort. Our work provides a versatile and scalable approach for multiparameter EV analysis, enabling comprehensive EV miRNA profiling and ovarian cancer classification.

articles.title: Safe prescribing in pregnancy: Medication considerations for people with spinal cord injury.
articles.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
articles.authors: Koerber SN, Wood WJ, Shi E et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Pregnancy among individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) occurs at rates similar to the general population, yet reproductive care for this population remains underexamined. Pregnant individuals with SCI experience secondary complications including neurogenic bladder and bowel, spasticity, pain, venous thromboembolism (VTE), and autonomic dysreflexia that often require pharmacologic management. However, limited evidence exists regarding the safety of commonly prescribed medications during pregnancy, contributing to clinical uncertainty and disparities in maternal and fetal outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: Synthesize literature on the safety of frequently used medications during pregnancy for individuals with SCI to develop a pragmatic tool to facilitate initial identification and discussion of medications that may be considered during pregnancy.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary team identified medications commonly prescribed for secondary complications of SCI. A literature review was conducted using PubMed, UpToDate, Briggs' Pregnancy and Lactation Guide, and the NatMed Pro Database. Medications were categorized by indication, evaluated for safety during pregnancy, and assigned a consensus recommendation based on available evidence through iterative discussion among the authors.
RESULTS: Several medications for SCI-related conditions appear generally safe during pregnancy, including polyethylene glycol, acetaminophen, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, low-molecular-weight heparin, insulin, and vitamin supplementation. Other medications, including anticholinergics, gabapentinoids, and some spasticity agents, have limited or mixed safety data.
CONCLUSION: Pharmacologic management of secondary complications during pregnancy in individuals with SCI requires shared decision-making with patients due to limited safety data, emphasizing the need for nonpharmacologic management when possible. This review provides a reference for clinicians and highlights the need for prospective research and disability-inclusive guidelines.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Associations of Gestational OPE Exposure with Offspring Digit Ratio: A Birth Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Lian H, Song X, Luan M et al.
articles.abstract: The effect of prenatal organophosphate esters (OPEs) exposure on offspring reproductive development and the potential role of the placenta remain unclear. We investigated the associations of prenatal OPE exposure with the second-to-fourth digit ratio (2D:4D) and the mediating role of placental DNA methylation (DNAm) levels of PPAR pathway genes. Maternal urine OPE metabolites at 12-16 gestational weeks were measured. Placental DNAm levels at birth and children's 2D:4D at ages 4 and 6 years were assessed. Multiple linear regression, BKMR, and causal mediation analyses were applied. We observed associations between prenatal exposure to BBOEP, BEHP, DBP, and DPP and increased 2D:4D in boys, whereas DBP and DCP were associated with decreased 2D:4D in girls. BKMR identified alkyl-OPEs, particularly BBOEP, as the primary contributors in boys. Moreover, hypermethylation of RXRA, ACAA1, and ACADM was associated with decreased 2D:4D in all populations. In girls, the associations among higher OPE exposure, increased ACAA1 methylation, and lower 2D:4D suggested a potential mediation pathway, while the mediation effects were not statistically significant. These findings suggest sex-specific associations between prenatal OPE exposure and 2D:4D. The potential role of placental PPAR-related DNAm in these associations warrants further investigation.

articles.title: PFAS in Follicular Fluid, Anti-Müllerian Hormone, and Oocyte Developmental Competence: A Prospective Study in GIVES.
articles.authors: Chu C, Zhou Y, Ma JH et al.
articles.abstract: In this prospective study based on the Guangxi In Vitro Fertilization and the Environment Study (GIVES) cohort, we measured poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the ovarian follicular fluid of 729 participants to investigate their association with oocyte developmental competence. The PFAS mixture was negatively associated with Metaphase II (MII) oocyte rate, with chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonic acids (Cl-PFESAs) identified as the primary contributor in Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models. Cl-PFESAs were negatively associated with oocyte maturation [relative risk (RR) = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.56-0.79], fertilization (RR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.67-0.90), blastocyst formation (RR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70-0.94), and high-quality blastocyst formation (RR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.41-0.58). Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) may act as a key modifier, with a stronger association observed in women with low AMH for MII oocyte rate [relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.12-0.54] and fertilization rate (RERI = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.003-0.49). Our findings indicate that PFAS, particularly Cl-PFESAs, in follicular fluid are linked to impaired oocyte developmental competence, with AMH serving as a potential modifier. Further studies are warranted to validate our findings and assess the implications of PFAS for reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: "Too hot to handle":A qualitative analysis of reddit platform data on the impact of menopause on career sustainability.
articles.authors: Grabarski MK, van der Heijden B, Mercer M et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMenopause is a biological process that women experience in midlife and is associated with various physiological and psychological symptoms. These symptoms impact their career sustainability, as reflected in their well-being and workplace performance.ObjectiveBuilding on the sustainable career framework, we aimed to explore how menopause manifests in the workplace and impacts the three core indicators of career sustainability, namely health, happiness, and productivity.DesignPublicly available data were collected from Reddit, an online anonymous discussion platform. We collected the data from threads on menopause and work using pre-defined keywords, resulting in 130 posts.MethodsWe used a qualitatively-driven approach, in which machine-learning techniques were used for preliminary text exploration, and for which qualitative template analysis, grounded in the sustainable careers framework, served as the primary analytical strategy.ResultsOur findings provide a deeper understanding of women's workplace experiences during menopause, which not only include negative aspects but also opportunities for adaptation and growth.ConclusionThis empirical work expands and enriches the knowledge of menopause in the workplace, which is an intersectional issue that has been historically taboo. In addition, we also provide empirical evidence supporting the theorizing behind the sustainable careers framework by demonstrating how its three indicators can overlap and interact with each other.

articles.title: An International Study of Pembrolizumab for Drug-Resistant Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia.
articles.authors: Ghorani E, Hayes EJ, Maher GJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data to guide use of anti-PD1 immunotherapy with pembrolizumab for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) that is chemotherapy-resistant or in adjuvant settings are limited. We conducted an international retrospective study of pembrolizumab in GTN, including patients with ultra-high-risk choriocarcinoma and poor-prognosis placental site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumors (PSTT/ETT), with up to 8 years of follow-up.
METHODS: We collected data on patients with GTN cases who received treatment with pembrolizumab between May 2015 and June 2023 from 20 centers in 16 countries. Cases were identified at Charing Cross Hospital, London; international centers with expertise in GTN were directly invited to identify and submit eligible cases treated during the study period. Clinical data were gathered from medical records using a standardized case-report form, curated centrally. Twenty-three samples were characterized by multiplex immunofluorescence, shallow whole-genome, and whole-transcriptome sequencing.
RESULTS: We identified 76 patients with drug-resistant GTN treated with pembrolizumab. This included 60 (78.9%) patients with GTN and measurable disease. Complete response was achieved in 71.7% (n=43 of 60; 95% confidence interval [CI], 60.3 to 83.1). Two-year overall survival (OS) was 85.6% (95% CI, 76.7 to 95.4), with median follow-up from pembrolizumab initiation of 25.4 months (range, 1.4 to 95.7). Sixteen (21.1%) received adjuvant pembrolizumab instead of high-dose chemotherapy, of whom 15 had poor-prognosis PSTT/ETT. No deaths were observed with median follow-up of 33.1 months (range, 7.7 to 68.6) from first remission. There were no identified grade 4 or worse immune-related toxicities. On multiplex immunofluorescence, the median fluorescence intensity between-group difference in cancer cell HLA-G expression (responders minus nonresponders) was 0.6 (95% CI, 0.3 to 1.0). Shallow whole-genome and whole-transcriptome sequencing suggested low HLA-G expression could be due to transcriptional control.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study without a control group, pembrolizumab was associated with durable responses in multidrug-resistant GTN and showed potential activity as adjuvant therapy for poor-prognosis PSTT/ETT. HLA-G expression warrants further exploration as a response biomarker. (Funded by Imperial College Experimental Cancer Medicine Centre and others.).

articles.title: Factors associated with receipt of prescription medication for menopause-related symptoms.
articles.authors: Cochrane AC, McAllister V, Jensen ET et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of patient- and clinician-level factors and receipt of prescription medication for menopause-related symptoms in a large academic health care system.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of women aged 40-55 years seeking care for menopause-related symptoms in any outpatient encounter with family medicine, internal medicine, endocrinology, and OB/Gyn from 2016 to 2023. Prescriptions associated with menopause-related ICD-10 diagnoses were extracted. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression were used to evaluate the association of patient- and clinician-level characteristics and receipt of prescription treatment.
RESULTS: We identified 5,491 women with an outpatient encounter with an associated ICD-10 code for menopause-related symptoms. Relative to White women, Black women were less likely to receive any prescription treatment for menopause-related symptoms (OR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.67-0.95), including systemic estrogen (OR: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.47-0.87); however, were more likely to receive SSRIs (OR: 1.49, 95% CI: 1.04-2.14). Relative to patients seeking care within OB/Gyn settings, patients were less likely to be prescribed any treatment by internal medicine (OR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.36-0.56), family medicine (OR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.14-0.40), and endocrinology clinicians (OR: 0.23, 95% CI: 0.14-0.40).
CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates differential prescribing patterns for menopause-related symptoms with respect to race, insurance status, and clinician specialty. Our results underscore the need for equitable care for women experiencing menopause symptoms.

articles.title: Deep Learning of Position-Aligned Dynamic Cell Deformation Trajectories for Ovarian Cell Phenotyping in Hyperbolic Microchannels.
articles.authors: Hu YB, Gao XL, Li HF et al.
articles.abstract: Cell deformation during microfluidic transport evolves continuously, whereas cell phenotyping commonly relies on geometric descriptors measured at one or a few predefined channel positions. Such fixed-position measurements capture selected deformation states but overlook how the cellular response progresses along the flow path. Combined with high-speed imaging, hyperbolic microchannels capture this progression as a continuous trajectory, enabling the shift from static morphological measurements to a dynamic response analysis. However, cell-to-cell differences in transit velocity cause equivalent image frames to represent different channel positions and hydrodynamic conditions, preventing a direct comparison of frame-indexed deformation trajectories. Here, we develop a trajectory-resolved framework that converts high-speed microfluidic image sequences into position-aligned dynamic cell deformation trajectories and uses deep learning to model their cell line-specific evolution for label-free ovarian cell phenotyping. Geometric and kinematic trajectories were extracted from three ovarian cancer cell lines (A2780, OVCAR-3, and SKOV-3) and one nonmalignant ovarian epithelial cell line (IOSE-80) at three flow rates. The trajectories were reparameterized by the axial position and resampled on a common spatial grid. Class-specific one-dimensional convolutional neural networks predicted downstream trajectories from the inlet state and flow conditions. An unknown cell was classified by comparing its measured trajectory with class-specific predictions, and prediction errors in the width, area, perimeter, and axial velocity were integrated by soft voting. The framework achieved 93.26% accuracy, 94.07% macro precision, 90.25% macro recall, and a 91.85% macro-F1 score on the held-out test data. These results support extending microfluidic cell phenotyping from isolated geometric states to the position-aligned analysis of dynamic deformation trajectories.

articles.title: Antenatal Screening for Sexually Transmitted Infections to Reduce Preterm Birth or Low Birthweight (Philani Ndiphile Study): A Randomized 3-Group Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.authors: Medina-Marino A, Babalola CM, Mdingi MM et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Trichomonas vaginalis are predominantly asymptomatic curable sexually transmitted infections (STIs) associated with adverse birth outcomes. Whether antenatal STI screening improves birth outcomes remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this randomized trial (NCT04446611), pregnant women ≥18 years were assigned before 27 weeks' gestation to (1) screening and treatment for C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae, and T. vaginalis at enrollment, with tests-of-cure (1-Time Screening); (2) screening and treatment at enrollment, repeated at 30-34 weeks (2-Time Screening); or (3) Standard-of-Care (syndromic management). The primary outcome was a composite of preterm birth (<37 weeks' gestation) or low birthweight (<2500 g); each component was evaluated individually as a secondary outcome.
RESULTS: Of 2247 enrolled, 1910 had live births. The composite outcome occurred in 22.9% of the 1-Time Screening (RR 0.99; 95% CI .81-1.21) and 20.6% of the 2-Time Screening groups (RR 0.89; 95% CI .72-1.09), compared with 23.2% of the Standard-of-Care group. Preterm birth occurred in 18.9% of the 1-Time Screening group (RR 1.00; 95% CI .80-1.26), 14.5% of the 2-Time Screening group (RR 0.77; 95% CI .60-0.99), and 18.8% of the Standard-of-Care group. Low birthweight occurred in 14.1% of the 1-Time Screening group (RR 1.10; 95% CI .83-1.46), 12.9% of the 2-Time Screening group (RR 1.01; 95% CI .76-1.35), and 12.8% of the Standard-of-Care group.
CONCLUSIONS: Neither STI screening strategy reduced the primary composite outcome or low birthweight alone. The 2-Time Screening strategy reduced preterm birth by 23%.

articles.title: Development, Validation, and Application of a Highly Sensitive RP-HPLC Method for the Determination and Release Profile Comparison of Levonorgestrel from Silicone-Based Contraceptive Implants.
articles.authors: Kabir AKL, Bachar SC, Moniruzzaman M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Levonorgestrel (LNG), a synthetic progestin containing implants, has emerged as one of the most reliable, effective, and long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) methods for preventing unintended pregnancies. The current study aimed to develop and validate a simple, rapid, and highly sensitive reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) technique for the quantification and release profile comparison of LNG from different silicone-based LARC implants.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: All the analysis was performed using HPLC equipped with UV/UV-VIS detector with the help of Waters C18 column of 250 × 4.6 mm dimension, 5 μm sized particle with mobile phase consisting of water and acetonitrile in the ratio of 30:70 (v/v%) at room temperature and 1 mL/minute flow rate, injection volume of 50 μl with the detection wavelength of 240 nm. The developed method was then validated as per International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) guidelines and then the validated method was used successfully to quantify LNG and for a comparative release profile study of two marketed implants, Femiplant and Sino-implant (II). The obtained release data were assessed and compared using fit factors (f1 & f2) to compare one formulation with another.
RESULTS: All parameters met the limits according to ICH guidelines. The total time needed for analysis was 12 minutes, having LNG eluting with a retention time of 5.8 min (± 0.2). The average LNG content was obtained to be 98.52 to 101.32% (± 0.05%). From the release kinetic study, f1 and f2 values of Femiplant against Sino-implant (II) determined was 10 and 62, respectively, both of which meet the acceptable limits.
CONCLUSION: The devolved method was straightforward and quick for any sample preparation, which could be used for routine analysis, in-process quality control analysis, and stability study analysis, among others. Moreover, Femiplant presented similar release kinetics compared to the World Health Organization prequalified implant Sino-implant (II), thereby having similar bioavailability and ensuring the consistent therapeutic effect of both implants.

articles.title: Microsurgical Varicocele Repair in Adults in the Era of Assisted Reproduction: An Evidence-Based Reappraisal Against Misinformation.
articles.authors: Paul GM, Pasqualotto FF, Radaelli MRM et al.
articles.abstract: Varicocele remains the most common correctable cause of male infertility and one of the few male-factor conditions in which targeted intervention may improve both sperm quality and reproductive outcomes. Despite a robust body of evidence supporting its clinical relevance, the role of varicocele repair has increasingly been challenged by the widespread dissemination of health misinformation through digital platforms. Simplified narratives frequently suggest that assisted reproductive technologies (ART) have rendered surgical correction obsolete, that varicocelectomy carries significant risk, or that its impact on fertility is minimal. These claims are not supported by contemporary evidence. Microsurgical varicocelectomy, particularly through the subinguinal approach, is associated with a favorable safety profile, including low recurrence rates, minimal hydrocele formation, and an exceptionally low risk of ischemic testicular injury when performed by experienced surgeons. In appropriately selected men with clinical varicocele, infertility, and abnormal semen parameters or elevated sperm DNA fragmentation, repair leads to clinically meaningful improvements in sperm concentration, motility, total motile sperm count, and genomic integrity. These biological changes translate into higher spontaneous pregnancy and live birth rates, as well as improved outcomes in ART, including fertilization, clinical pregnancy, and live birth. In addition to clinical outcomes, varicocelectomy may reduce the need for more invasive and costly reproductive interventions, reinforcing its role as a fertility optimization strategy rather than a competing alternative to ART. Evidence also supports a selective role for varicocele repair in non-obstructive azoospermia, where it may improve sperm retrieval or, in a minority of cases, restore sperm to the ejaculate. The persistence of misinformation highlights the need for critical appraisal and synthesis of the available evidence. This expert opinion provides a comprehensive, pathophysiologically grounded, and quantitatively supported reappraisal of microsurgical varicocelectomy in modern male infertility care, while addressing the impact of health misinformation in the digital era and emphasizing the role of the urologist in evidence-based patient counseling.

articles.title: National Activity Register - Spanish Fertility Society Register of IVF/ICSI and IUI: 2020 to 2022.
articles.authors: Vassena R, Granados LM, Tévar LG et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This report collects the IVF/ICSI and IUI records of the Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) National Activity Register - Spanish Fertility Society Reg¬ister (RNA-SEF Register) for the years 2020, 2021 and 2022. The report of the year 2020 is of particular interest as it reflects the initial COVID-19 pandemic year in Spain, a country that experienced very significant healthcare dis¬ruptions and where the provision of ART was affected both in the public and private sector for months. While the pan-demic was still ongoing, 2021 represented a year of con¬trolled and orderly activity, with recovery of most of the activity, and 2022 reflected a more stable activity pattern, with activity returning to pre-pandemic levels. This report serves the dual purpose of documenting the activity of one of the largest ART providers in Europe and of assessing the level of resilience and adaptation of the sector to an extraordinary public health challenge.
METHODS: The data collected for IVF/ICSI cycles carried out in 242 Spanish centers in 2020, 249 in 2021 and 248 in 2022 were analyzed. The registry records activity aggre¬gated at the center level for each calendar year rather than by individual cycle or patient. The following cycles were studied: IVF/ICSI cycles with fresh own oocytes (2020: 37,782; 2021: 46,224; 2022: 42,341); IVF/ICSI cycles with fresh donor oocytes (2020: 12,001; 2021: 13,287; 2022: 12,590); cycles with cryopreserved embryos (2020: 27,571; 2021: 37,310; 2022: 36,235); PGT (Preimplanta¬tion Genetic Testing) cycles (2020: 13,153; 2021: 17,828; 2022: 20,502) and cycles with cryopreserved oocytes (2020: 8,171; 2021: 11,179; 2022: 11,738). Intrauter¬ine insemination (IUI) cycles were also analyzed (2020: 24,816; 2021: 33,818; 2022: 31,635).
RESULTS: For IVF/ICSI with fresh own oocytes, a total of 5,434 clinical gestations were obtained in 2020, 6,353 in 2021 and 5,461 in 2022, representing a pregnancy rate per fresh embryo transfer of 34.5%, 34.4% and 34.6%, respectively. In 2020, 10.5% of these gestations were multiple, 10.0% in 2021, and 9.0% in 2022, confirming a decade-long trend of diminishing multiple-pregnancy rates; it was the first time that multiple pregnancies fell below 10% in patients using their own oocytes. For IVF/ICSI with fresh donor oocytes, 5,065 fresh transfers were performed in 2020, 5,730 in 2021, and 5,102 in 2022. In 2020 these resulted in 2,912 clinical gestations (57.5% per transfer), of which 10.3% were multiple…

articles.title: Reproducibility of "chaotic" embryo calls by non-invasive PGT-A: a prospective pilot study and implications for diagnostic validity.
articles.authors: Vagnini LD, Petersen CG, Massaro F et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the test-retest reproducibility of "chaotic" embryo calls (≥ 6 whole-chromosome abnormalities) by non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (niPGT-A) using cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from spent culture medium (SCM), by repeating niPGT-A after embryo warming and short-term reculture, and to discuss implications for diagnostic validity.
METHODS: This prospective pilot study included seven vitrified blastocysts previously classified as "chaotic" by niPGT-A. After warming, embryos underwent 4 to 8 hours of individual reculture to enable additional cfDNA release. SCM was collected and processed for repeat niPGT-A using the same whole-genome amplification method (MALBAC), sequencing platform (Illumina MiSeq), and bioinformatic pipeline (ChromGo) employed in the initial test.Laboratory staff were blinded to the original results. An embryo-free negative media control was processed in parallel to monitor environmental contamination. Agreement between the initial and repeat classifications was assessed descriptively.
RESULTS: All cfDNA samples were successfully amplified and generated high-quality sequencing libraries. On repeat analysis, 3/7 embryos (43%) yielded a euploid call. The remaining 4/7 embryos (57%) showed abnormal findings; however, their chromosomal profiles differed from the initial reports, indicating limited agreement for the "chaotic" designation and for individual chromosomal calls.
CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot cohort, embryos initially classified as "chaotic" by SCM-based niPGT-A showed substantial discordance upon retesting after warming and short-term reculture. These findings raise concerns about end-to-end reproducibility and support a cautious interpretation of "chaotic" results until larger studies clarify technical from biological sources of discordance and validate SCM calls against embryo tissue and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Endometriosis in IVF/ICSI: Clinical Outcomes, Cumulative Live Birth, and a Pragmatic Narrative Review for Patient Counseling and Management.
articles.authors: Dubovecak M, Pavelic TT, Tikvica AL et al.
articles.abstract: This pragmatic narrative review provides a phenotype-informed framework for counseling and managing women with endometriosis undergoing IVF/ICSI, with emphasis on cumulative live birth and preservation of ovarian reserve. A focused literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar, covering studies published from 2021 to 2026 and including selected earlier landmark studies when relevant. Evidence was synthesized according to disease phenotype, the presence of adenomyosis, prior surgery, and key reproductive outcomes, including ovarian response, embryo cohort size, implantation, and cumulative live birth. Endometriosis appears to act predominantly as a quantitative ovarian constraint, characterized by reduced anti-Müllerian hormone levels, lower antral follicle count, and decreased oocyte yield, particularly in women with ovarian endometrioma or prior cystectomy. Fertilization and embryo competence are generally preserved, suggesting that the main limitation is embryo cohort size rather than intrinsic embryo quality. Implantation may be modestly impaired in selected phenotypes, especially in the presence of adenomyosis, whereas live birth per transfer may remain broadly comparable after adjustment. Adenomyosis is heterogeneous, and its variable presentation may influence reproductive outcomes and treatment response. Endometriosis does not preclude successful IVF/ICSI. Counseling should therefore emphasize cumulative outcomes, preservation of ovarian reserve, and avoidance of unnecessary ovarian surgery within a pragmatic, phenotype-informed management strategy.

articles.title: Comparison of Clinical Pregnancy Rates Between Difficult and Easy Embryo Transfers: A Comprehensive Retrospective Study and Multi-Regional Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Alwan MA, Abduljabbar HH, Sabban H et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The impact of difficult embryo transfer (ET) on clinical pregnancy rate (CPR) remains uncertain, with prior studies reporting inconsistent findings. This study aimed to evaluate the association between difficult versus easy ET and CPR in patients undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Center, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between January 2022 and November 2024. Difficult ET was defined by procedural challenges such as resistance, need for force, or use of additional instruments. The primary outcome was CPR, defined as the presence of a gestational sac or fetal heartbeat on ultrasound following a positive β-hCG test. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: A total of 481 cycles were included, of which 442 (91.9%) involved easy ET and 39 (8.1%) difficult ET. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. The overall CPR was 31.6%, with no statistically significant difference between the difficult and easy ET groups (23.08% vs. 32.35%, p=0.282). In unadjusted analysis, difficult ET was associated with lower odds of CPR (OR 0.63, 95% CI: 0.29-1.36). After adjustment for confound¬ers, difficult ET remained associated with reduced odds of CPR (adjusted OR 0.49, 95% CI:0.22-1.11), although this did not reach statistical significance (p=0.087).
CONCLUSION: Difficult ET was associated with a nonsignificant trend toward lower CPR. These findings suggest a potential negative effect; however, larger studies are needed to confirm this association.

articles.title: Fertility knowledge in Portuguese adolescents: Findings from the serious game "MyFActs!".
articles.authors: Fontaine C, Gaspar N, Galhardo A et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fertility awareness has become crucial for informed reproductive decision-making in the context of rising infertility rates, delayed parenthood, and evolving social norms. Research shows that adolescents have limited fertility knowledge, which may lead to poorly informed future reproductive decisions, making adolescence a particularly important period for fertility education. This study assessed fertility knowledge among Portuguese adolescents using an innovative digital assessment tool, the 12-question serious game "MyFActs!". Patterns of fertility knowledge and demographic predictors across multiple fertility dimensions were examined.
METHODS: A total of 970 adolescents aged 15-18 years participated in this study. Data were analysed using analysis of variance (ANOVA), chi-square tests, and stepwise binary logistic regression models to examine demographic differences and relationships among fertility knowledge dimensions.
RESULTS: Participants answered a mean of 8.77 qutions correctly (SD=1.88). Significant gender differences were observed, with girls demonstrating greater knowedge than boys in some dimensions. Age-related diffeenes were also found, with older adolescents (17 and 18 years) demonstrating greater knowledge than youner paicipants (15 and 16 years). Binary logistic regrsion analses revealed strong associations among fertility knowledge dmensions.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that fertilty knowedge among Portuguese adolescents remains moeate, with persistent demographic disparities that rquire tareed educational interventions. The interconnected nature of fertility knowledge dimensions supports comprehensive rather than fragmented educational approaches. The sucessful use of the serious-game format demostrates the potential of digital platforms to engage adlecents with sensitive health topics and overcome tradtioal educational barriers.

articles.title: Vaginal-Endometrial Microbiome Synchrony as a Predictor of Implantation in Frozen Embryo Transfer Cycles: A Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Srivastava S, Misra M, Gujrati C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether vaginal-endometrial microbiome synchrony is associated with biochemical and clinical pregnancy outcomes in frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 100 women undergoing single Day 5 FET cycles. Vaginal and endometrial samples were collected during a mock FET cycle on progesterone day 5 and analyzed using a contamination-aware targeted 16S rRNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel optimized for low-biomass reproductive tract samples. A Synchrony Index (SI), a similarity metric analogous to Jaccard-type indices, was calculated based on shared dominant microbial taxa between vaginal and endometrial compartments. An SI cutoff of ≥0.7 was pre-specified prior to outcome analysis based on biological plausibility and accepted similarity thresholds in microbiome research. Biochemical pregnancy (β-hCG positive) and clinical pregnancy rates were compared between high and low SI groups. A randomly selected subset underwent next-generation sequencing validation.
RESULTS: Baseline demographic, ovarian reserve, embryo quality, and endometrial parameters were comparable between groups. Biochemical pregnancy rates were significantly higher in women with high SI compared with low SI (65.5% vs. 28.9%, p<0.001), as were clinical pregnancy rates (61.8% vs. 26.7%, p<0.001). On multivariable logistic regression adjusting for clinical confounders, SI remained independently associated with biochemical pregnancy (adjusted odds ratio 1.20 per 0.1 increase; 95% CI 1.06-1.36; p=0.004). PCR-derived SI demonstrated substantial agreement with sequencing-based validation.
CONCLUSION: Vaginal-endometrial microbiome synchrony is independently associated with biochemical pregnancy in Day 5 FET cycles. The PCR-based Synchrony Index warrants further evaluation as an investigational biomarker of reproductive tract receptivity in larger and independent cohorts.

articles.title: Access to Assisted Reproductive Technology Services in Brazil: A Descriptive Analysis of SisEmbrio Data.
articles.authors: Queiroz LA, Divino JMZ, Santos LCVD et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To conduct a descriptive analysis of data from the National Embryo Production System (SisEmbrio) to characterize access to assisted reproductive technology (ART) services in Brazil.
METHOD: Data from SisEmbrio for the period from 2020 to 2024 were used, along with data from the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics, Google Maps, and clinical guidelines on ART.
RESULTS: The data showed growth in the number of ART centers, as well as increases in the number of frozen embryos and completed cycles during the study period. Following the increase in embryo cryopreservation, a higher absolute number of ART procedures was observed among women aged ≥35 years. The analysis also showed that most clinics are privately operated and that their geographic distribution is concentrated mainly in large urban centers.
CONCLUSION: The findings indicate that access to ART services in Brazil remains limited. SisEmbrio data reaffirm barriers previously identified in the literature. These challenges restrict the expansion of access and underscore the need for structural changes to promote greater equity in care for the target population.

articles.title: Association of female obesity with ovarian response and IVF outcomes: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Attar SAEDIE, Mahmoud EMM, Shaker AN et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Excess body weight is associated with subfertility and delayed conception, yet its effect on in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes in women with preserved ovarian reserve remains uncertain. This study examined the impact of overweight and obesity on IVF outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 159 infertile women aged 20-35 years who underwent IVF between December 2022 and May 2025. All participants had adequate ovarian reserve (anti-Müllerian hormone ≥1 ng/mL and antral follicle count ≥5) and infertility due to polycystic ovary syndrome, mild male factor, tubal factor, or unexplained causes. Based on body mass index (BMI), women were classified as normal weight, overweight, or obese. All patients received a standardized long agonist ovarian stimulation protocol. Study outcomes included gonadotropin dose, stimulation duration, number and quality of oocytes and embryos, fertilization rates, clinical pregnancy rates per initiated cycle and per embryo transfer, and cycle cancellation rates. Multivariable regression analyses adjusted for age, AMH, and AFC were performed.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups. Obese women required significantly higher gonadotropin doses and exhibited poorer ovarian response, with fewer retrieved and mature oocytes, reduced high-quality embryo yield, and lower fertilization rates. Clinical pregnancy rates declined with increasing BMI, while cycle cancellation rates were significantly higher in obese patients. Overweight status showed no independent adverse effect after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: In women with preserved ovarian reserve, obesity independently impairs ovarian response, embryo development, and IVF success, whereas overweight does not. Weight optimization before IVF may improve treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Genomic Profile of Asian Women with Recurrent Implantation Failure: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Sini KPI, Temenggung NAA, Handayani N et al.
articles.abstract: Recurrent implantation failure is a major challenge in assisted reproductive technology, affecting up to 15% of women undergoing in vitro fertilization. Although several hypotheses for the pathogenesis of the condition have been proposed, many RIF cases remain unexplained. Studies have suggested potential genomic contributions to RIF. However, most studies have focused on non-Asian or mixed populations, leaving gaps in understanding population-specific genetic risks. This systematic review aimed to characterize the genomic profile of Asian women with RIF and identify candidate genetic variants associated with increased susceptibility. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, OVID, and ScienceDirect up to June 2025 for case-control studies analyzing genetic polymorphisms in Asian women diagnosed with RIF. Five eligible studies were identified, comprising 566 women with RIF and 732 fertile controls from East and West Asia. Variants in genes related to angiogenesis (VEGF), RNA interference (AGO2), lipid transport (APOE), folate metabolism (MTHFR, TYMS/TS), and DNA repair (MDM2) were identified. Consistent associations were observed for VEGF polymorphisms (rs833061, rs25648, rs1570360) and AGO2 rs4961280, reported up to two-fold higher risk of RIF, while APOE ε4 carriage was linked to a similar increase. Combined MTHFR and TYMS genotypes also showed additive effects on RIF susceptibility. Genetic variants affecting angiogenesis, RNA processing, and lipid metabolism may contribute to RIF pathogenesis in Asian women. VEGF emerged as the most consistently associated gene, highlighting the importance of endometrial vascular remodeling in implantation success. Larger, multi-ethnic genomic studies with functional validation, together with a standardized definition of RIF, are warranted to clarify these associations and advance personalized reproductive medicine in ART.

articles.title: Fertility Preservation in Oncology Patients: A Comparative Study of Outcomes and Embryo Disposition Preferences.
articles.authors: Ávila MJA, Cabrera JL
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the initial outcomes of a clinical program offering fertility preservation to women newly diagnosed with cancer and scheduled for gonadotoxic therapy. Fertility preservation has gained importance among women with cancer due to increasing survival rates. Oncologic treatments can compromise reproductive capacity, often resulting in insufficiency (POI). Fertility preservation should be offered to young patients wishing to retain reproductive potential.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included 46 cancer patients aged 18-40 years and 34 infertile women. Medical records were reviewed for cancer diagnosis, ovarian stimulation protocols, and assisted reproduction outcomes.
RESULTS: Eighteen cancer patients (39.1%) underwent fertility preservation-12 with embryo cryopreservation and 6 with oocyte cryopreservation. The control group consisted of 34 infertile women undergoing IVF. Oncology patients had a lower mean number of oocytes retrieved (6.0 vs. 10.3), though the number of zygotes was comparable (5.23 vs. 6.3; p=0.06). Cycle cancellation was more frequent among cancer patients (16.6% vs. 2.9%). Preferences for unused embryos differed: fewer oncology patients chose disposal (11.1% vs. 17.6%; p=0.002). Three oncology patients returned for embryo transfer, all resulting in ongoing pregnancies.
CONCLUSION: Fertility preservation using assisted reproductive technologies is safe and feasible for cancer patients. Despite eligibility, many declined treatment due to emotional, medical, or logistical factors. Cancer patients expressed distinct ethical views on embryo disposition, underscoring the need for individualized counseling and integrated oncofertility care.

articles.title: Early menarche in association with ovarian reserve and biological aging in young adults: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Liu W, Li Y, Yu Y et al.
articles.abstract: In brief: Age at menarche has declined worldwide, raising concern about its long-term consequences for women's reproductive health and aging. This study shows that early menarche is associated with only modest differences in ovarian reserve markers and biological age in young women, suggesting that early menarche alone may be of limited concern for future reproductive potential. Abstract: Age at menarche has declined in many populations, but whether earlier menarche is related to ovarian reserve markers and biological aging in young adulthood remains unclear. In this cross-sectional study, we compared 82 women with early menarche (<12 years) and 92 women with normal menarche (12-13.5 years), all aged 18-25 years, from Anhui Province, China. Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone and estradiol (E2) were measured; antral follicle count (AFC) and ovarian volume were assessed by transabdominal ultrasound; and biological age was estimated using the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM-BA) and Phenotypic Age (PhenoAge). After adjustment for potential confounders, early menarche was associated with lower AMH (-15.5%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -26.8% to -2.4%) and AFC (-6.2%, 95% CI: -11.4% to -0.8%), higher FSH (22.1%, 95% CI: 5.5% to 41.3%) and E2 (25.7%, 95% CI: 6.5% to 48.3%), and greater KDM-BA acceleration (0.75 years, 95% CI: 0.04 to 1.46), but not with PhenoAge acceleration. These associations were modest: menarche group explained only 1.4%-4.1% of the variance in these outcomes. Early menarche is associated with small differences in ovarian reserve markers and biological age in young women; however, on its own it is unlikely to indicate a clinically meaningful reduction in reproductive potential.

articles.title: Productive or Transforming? How Epithelial Compartmentalization of HPV DNA and E6/E7 Transcripts Shapes Cervical Screening Assay Performance.
articles.authors: Schichl K, Doorbar J
articles.abstract: The human papillomavirus (HPV) life cycle is linked to epithelial cell differentiation, with viral genome amplification, E6/E7 transcription, and virion assembly spatially compartmentalized within the cervical epithelium. This organization is disrupted in transforming lesions. These fundamental observations determine what 'bulk' nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) of cervical exfoliates allow us to establish. DNA-based assays sensitively report high-risk HPV genome presence, which includes transient infections and virus particles. RNA-based assays target the E6/E7 transcripts in transcriptionally active disease, which accounts for their slightly higher clinical specificity for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions. No single assay defines both viral presence and disease significance, however. Cytology, p16/Ki-67 dual stain, extended genotyping and host-cell methylation interrogate complementary axes of risk with strong biological rationale. The loss of spatial information that limits bulk NAAT approaches matters most in mixed-grade lesions and immunocompromised populations. Emerging spatial methods, AI-assisted cytology and cervical cell-lifts offer recovery of biological resolution.

articles.title: Postmenopausal Bleeding Risk after COVID-19 Vaccination: A Population-Based Self-Controlled Case Series Study.
articles.authors: Jeong NY, Park H, Cho S et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate whether COVID-19 vaccination increases the risk of postmenopausal bleeding requiring hospital care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a nationwide population-based study using the integrated database of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency COVID-19 registry and the National Health Insurance Service claims data. Women aged 56 years or older who received their first COVID-19 vaccine dose before December 2021 and were newly diagnosed with postmenopausal bleeding during the observation period were included. A self-controlled case series design was applied to compare the incidence of postmenopausal bleeding during predefined risk periods (1-30 days after each vaccine dose) with that during baseline periods within the same individuals. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using conditional Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: Among 8075792 women aged 56 years or older who received COVID-19 vaccination, 5716 were diagnosed with postmenopausal bleeding. There was no significant increase in the risk of postmenopausal bleeding within 30 days following vaccination (IRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.92-1.04). Results remained consistent in subgroup and sensitivity analyses across vaccine types, doses, and age groups.
CONCLUSION: COVID-19 vaccination was not associated with an increased risk of postmenopausal bleeding requiring hospital care. These findings provide reassuring evidence supporting the safety of COVID-19 vaccines in postmenopausal women with respect to bleeding risk.

articles.title: Analgesic Efficacy of Ropivacaine-P407 Gel vs. Bupivacaine in Single-Port-Assisted Hysterectomy: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.authors: Kim JC, Lee YJ, Nam EJ et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of ropivacaine-poloxamer 407 (P407) gel injection with that of bupivacaine injection in patients undergoing single-port assisted hysterectomy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed medical records from January to December 2023 at Severance Hospital, Yonsei University. A total of 209 patients undergoing minimally invasive hysterectomy with or without adnexal procedures were analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups: 42 received ropivacaine-P407 gel (Welpass), and 167 received bupivacaine alone. Demographic variables, intraoperative parameters, and postoperative pain scores were collected. Propensity score matching was applied to control for surgical complexity and baseline imbalances, yielding 31 matched pairs. Pain levels were assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at multiple time points up to 48 hours postoperatively.
RESULTS: Before matching, the ropivacaine-P407 gel group demonstrated significantly lower pain scores starting at 12 hours postoperatively compared to the bupivacaine group (NRS difference p=0.005 at 24 hours, p=0.020 at 48 hours). After propensity score matching, this difference remained significant: patients in the ropivacaine-P407 gel group continued to report reduced pain intensity at 24 hours [mean NRS±standard deviation (SD): 1.96±0.35 vs. 2.86±1.35, p=0.003] and 48 hours (1.88±0.49 vs. 2.65±1.12, p=0.014). Both groups showed similar safety profiles, with no severe adverse reactions related to the anesthetic agents reported.
CONCLUSION: Ropivacaine-P407 gel injection provides superior early postoperative analgesia compared to bupivacaine alone in minimally invasive hysterectomy.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics of End-Organ Failure as a Cause of Primary Amenorrhea: Multicenter Study in Korean Population.
articles.authors: Chung YS, Yun BH, Kim HJ et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary amenorrhea is defined as the absence of menstruation by the age of 13 years in the absence of secondary sexual characteristics or by age 15 in the presence of normal secondary sexual development. It has multiple potential causes, and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. This study aimed to provide insights into the incidence and distribution of primary amenorrhea due to congenital anomalies or disorders of sexual development (DSD) in Korea.
METHODS: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was conducted, analyzing data from January 2001 to December 2016. Patient history, clinical characteristics, and management approaches for primary amenorrhea were compared based on the underlying causes. The DSD group included individuals with XX DSD, XY DSD, and sex chromosome DSD. The Müllerian agenesis group consisted of 7 different types of anomalies: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome, uterine agenesis, cervical agenesis, cervicovaginal agenesis, vaginal agenesis, transverse vaginal septum, and imperforate hymen.
RESULTS: A total of 359 patients were enrolled in the study, including 73 patients in the DSD group and 286 patients in the Müllerian anomaly groups. The age at diagnosis differed significantly among the Müllerian anomaly groups (P < 0.001), while no significant age differences were observed among the DSD groups (P = 0.259). Treatment approaches varied depending on the type of anomaly: approximately 38.8% of patients with Müllerian anomalies underwent surgical procedures for vaginal construction, while 62% of patients with XY DSD underwent gonadectomy.
CONCLUSION: The findings from the past 16 years highlight key clinical characteristics of DSD and Müllerian agenesis in Korea.

articles.title: The fetal phenotype is a trajectory, not a snapshot.
articles.authors: Recker F, Walter A, Gembruch U
articles.abstract: The fetal phenotype is a trajectory rather than a fixed observation: features emerge, progress, or resolve across gestation, and the anomaly present at 20 weeks is often not the anomaly present at 32. Sequence variants, however, are interpreted against the phenotype supplied when the test is requested, and phenotypic specificity carries evidence weight in variant classification. A scoping review of 59 studies combining serial prenatal phenotyping with sequence-based testing found that a newly emergent phenotype led to a molecular diagnosis in 16 studies and a variant reclassification in 8; yet a gestational age for every phenotypic observation was reported in 2, a serial imaging protocol in 7, and a reclassification with both direction and evidence code in 1. The clinical signal is real, and the literature cannot quantify it. Five reporting practices are proposed, none of which requires new equipment or funding.

articles.title: Clinical Efficacy of Low-Intensity Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Male Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Retrospective Pilot Study.
articles.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association
articles.authors: Wakita H, Ishikawa K, Yoshino Y et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-intensity extracorporeal shock wave therapy (Li-ESWT) using the Morenova system in men with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), including chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS), and to identify pretreatment factors associated with post-treatment symptom severity.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 61 men treated with Li-ESWT. The treatment was administered once weekly for six consecutive weeks. Symptom severity was assessed before and one month after treatment using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS), Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Impact Index (BII), and National Institutes of Health Chronic Prostatitis Symptom Index (NIH-CPSI). Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify pretreatment factors independently associated with the post-treatment NIH-CPSI total score after adjustment for baseline NIH-CPSI.
RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed in total IPSS (from 11.1 to 7.3), OABSS (from 3.8 to 2.8), BII (from 4.9 to 2.7), and NIH-CPSI (from 11.8 to 7.0) (all p < 0.001). Notably, pain improved significantly in patients with baseline pain (from 4.1 to 1.8, p < 0.001). Post-micturition dribbling improved in approximately one-third of patients. Higher PSA and lower baseline OABSS were independently associated with lower post-treatment NIH-CPSI scores after adjustment for baseline NIH-CPSI. No adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Li-ESWT was associated with improvements across voiding, storage, pain, and QOL domains, with no adverse events observed. These findings suggest that Li-ESWT may have potential as a treatment option for male LUTS, although prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm its efficacy.

articles.title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals genetic etiology and pregnancy outcomes in fetuses with ultrasound-detected abnormalities at a tertiary center.
articles.authors: Cai M, Lin N, Huang H et al.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in prenatal diagnostics, the genetic causes underlying fetal ultrasound abnormalities remain poorly understood, with a significant proportion of cases lacking definitive molecular diagnoses. Invasive prenatal testing was performed in 179 cases, followed by whole-exome sequencing (WES) to identify genetic etiologies. Among 179 abnormal fetuses, 132 had single-system and 47 had multisystem abnormalities. WES identified pathogenic (P) or likely pathogenic (LP) variants in 33 cases (19 single-system, 14 multisystem), with skeletal (7), cardiac (5), and craniofacial defects (2) being most frequent. Thirty-four genes were involved, encompassing 41 variants (15 missense, 10 frameshift, 6 splicing, 6 nonsense, and 4 in-frame deletions). WES yielded a P/LP rate of 17.88% (32/179) for variants that explained the fetal phenotype, with an additional pathogenic finding (overall P/LP rate: 18.44%, 33/179). Inheritance patterns were autosomal dominant (19), recessive (12), X-linked (1), and mosaic (1). Family studies confirmed 27 variants (18 inherited, 9 de novo). Pregnancy outcomes included 60 terminations, 19 intrauterine deaths, and 8 postnatal abnormalities. Most fetal ultrasound phenotypes matched the disease-causing gene profiles. Combining molecular testing with ultrasound helps clinicians identify genetic causes, assess recurrence risk, and inform parents, enabling personalized management for high-risk families.

articles.title: Bioengineering strategies for next-generation female reproductive organoids: A roadmap to clinical translation.
articles.authors: Gao B, Gao J, Wei W et al.
articles.abstract: The human female reproductive system is characterized by highly dynamic tissue remodeling, cyclical endocrinology, and the precise orchestration of maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Historically, deciphering reproductive pathologies ranging from infertility to obstetric complications and malignancies has been hampered by the fundamental physiological and interspecies disparities inherent in 2D cultures and animal models. While three-dimensional (3D) organoid technology has initiated a paradigm shift, conventional static cultures relying on poorly defined, xenogeneic matrices (e.g., Matrigel) introduce profound immunogenic confounding factors and severe bioengineering bottlenecks. To bridge this gap, this review comprehensively delineates the advanced bioengineering strategies driving the next-generation of female reproductive models. We first outline foundational engineering pillars, highlighting the transition toward intelligent biomaterials, deterministic 3D bioprinting, and microfluidic microenvironments. Subsequently, we critically evaluate state-of-the-art organoid models across the ovary, fallopian tube, the maternal-fetal interface containing endometrium and placenta, cervix, and vagina. We emphasize how multi-lineage "assembloids" and multiorgan microphysiological systems successfully recapitulate transient implantation events and bidirectional endocrine crosstalk. Finally, we propose a strategic roadmap for the field, demonstrating how the integration of materials science, genetics, multi-omics, and engineering methods will overcome current limitations, ultimately accelerating the transition from benchtop in vitro models to standardized clinical diagnostics and reproductive regenerative therapeutics.

articles.title: Association between Plasma Short-Chain Fatty Acids and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Nested Case-Control Study.
articles.authors: Wang D, Wu L, Feng P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between plasma short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
METHODS: A nested case-control study was conducted comprising 387 pairs of HDP cases and non-HDP controls. The HDP group included 291 cases of gestational hypertension (GH) and 96 of preeclampsia (PE) or chronic hypertension (CH) with superimposed PE (PE/CH-PE). Seven plasma SCFA levels were assayed at gestational weeks 16-20, before HDP onset. The individual effects of the seven SCFAs on HDP risk were analyzed using logistic regression, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied to calculate adjusted P-values in multivariate analysis. The joint effects of the seven SCFAs were evaluated using weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression.
RESULTS: HDP cases exhibited significantly lower median (interquartile range) valerate levels than controls (9 (5-14) vs. 10 (6-18) ng/mL, P = 0.001). Among the seven analyzed SCFAs, isobutyrate and isovalerate demonstrated the highest correlation coefficient at 0.85 (P < 0.001). Each interquartile range increase in valerate content was associated with a low risk of HDP, yielding an adjusted odds ratio (aOR) of 0.699 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.516-0.946, FDR-corrected P = 0.047). Isobutyrate and hexanoate were also inversely associated with HDP after multivariate adjustment and FDR correction (both P = 0.047), with aORs of 0.899 (95% CI: 0.826-0.980) and 0.686 (95% CI: 0.508-0.927), respectively. WQS regression revealed that joint SCFA exposure was associated with a decreased risk of HDP (aOR: 0.230, 95% CI: 0.105-0.506) and GH (aOR: 0.740, 95% CI: 0.571-0.933).
CONCLUSION: Plasma levels of valerate, isobutyrate, and hexanoate are inversely associated with HDP risk. Furthermore, the combined effect of these SCFAs is linked to a lower incidence of both HDP and GH. These findings suggest that circulating SCFAs may serve as potential early biomarkers for HDP.

articles.title: Herpes Simplex Virus Perinatal Management.
articles.authors: Carey R, McCallion N, Eogan M et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) is a double stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) virus with 2 serotypes, HSV-1 and HSV-2. Neonatal HSV infection is uncommon due to evidence-based interventions for pregnancy, delivery and the newborn. The study assessed whether pregnant women with a history of genital HSV and their infants were managed according to best practice recommendations.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of pregnancies between January 2018 and December 2021. Included were women with documented HSV - either diagnosed, treated, or with positive laboratory testing.
RESULTS: 234 women with 261 pregnancies were identified. Mean maternal age was 32 (SD =/- 5.2). 110 (42%) pregnancies had visible lesions. 2 (0.07%) cases of primary HSV occurred within 6 weeks of delivery. 11 (4.2%) had lesions at labour onset - all were recurrences. Prophylaxis was prescribed in 178 (68%) pregnancies. 14 (5%) infants required evaluation, with only one yielding a positive swab requiring full acyclovir treatment.
DISCUSSION: Genital HSV prevalence in this population was 0.07% (2 cases), with incidence of 0.003% (1 case) of infant requiring treatment throughout this timeframe. Primary infection within 6 weeks of delivery was rare, with no cases at labour onset. Recurrent lesions were reported in under 50% (110 pregnancies). Requirement for infant evaluation was low (5%, 14 infants).

articles.title: Coccydynia as a Multimechanistic Pain Syndrome: A Narrative Synthesis and Proposal of the Coccyx Pain Phenotype Score (CPPS) for Mechanism-Based Clinical Phenotyping.
articles.authors: Khalfallah M, Savalli L, Khalfallah I et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To introduce the Coccyx Pain Phenotype Score (CPPS), a conceptual clinical phenotyping framework intended to characterize the proposed contribution of four pain mechanisms in coccydynia and to provide a basis for individualized, mechanism-based assessment and management.
METHODS: A narrative synthesis of the literature was conducted to identify clinical and pathophysiological features relevant to four proposed pain mechanisms in coccydynia: mechanical, myofascial, peripheral neural sensitization, and central sensitization. PubMed and Embase were searched without date restriction using terms related to coccydynia, chronic pelvic pain syndromes, pelvic floor dysfunction, neuropathic pain, peripheral sensitization, central sensitization, and nociplastic pain. Findings were organized across the four proposed domains and combined with recurrent clinical observations to construct a hypothesis-generating CPPS framework. No quantitative evidence synthesis or formal assessment of evidence quality was performed.
RESULTS: Weak radioclinical concordance, heterogeneous treatment responses, and persistent pain despite anatomically successful treatment suggest that mechanical lesions alone may not fully explain coccydynia. Four recurrent mechanisms emerge from the literature: mechanical, myofascial, peripheral neural sensitization, and central sensitization. Their relative contributions appear to vary among patients, and several mechanisms may coexist within the same pain presentation. The CPPS was developed to structure this multidimensional assessment by scoring each mechanistic domain independently.
CONCLUSION: Coccydynia may be more appropriately regarded as a heterogeneous, multimechanistic pain syndrome than as a purely anatomical condition. The CPPS provides a pragmatic conceptual framework for structuring diagnostic reasoning, informing personalized management, and improving the homogeneity of future research cohorts. Prospective validation is required before the score can be recommended for quantitative assessment, routine clinical decision-making, or research stratification.

articles.title: Ovarian Cancer Nanovaccines: Recent Strategic Advances from Antigen Selection to Carrier Design.
articles.authors: Tang X, Huang Y, Zhang X et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the most lethal gynecological malignancies. Its immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and peritoneal dissemination characteristics have severely limited the efficacy of existing immunotherapies. To overcome the poor immunogenicity of tumor antigens and the need for coordinated delivery of antigen and adjuvant, nanovaccines have emerged as a promising strategy. By co-delivering tumor antigens and immunologic adjuvants to antigen-presenting cells, nanovaccines can elicit specific antitumor immune responses. Recently, mRNA-2416, an mRNA-LNP vaccine encoding OX40L, completed a Phase I/II trial in patients with ovarian cancer, providing initial proof-of-concept for intratumoral administration of mRNA-based immunotherapy. This review summarizes antigen design strategies for ovarian cancer nanovaccines and compares the design principles and application progress of major carrier nanoplatforms including liposomes, polymers, inorganic nanoparticles, cell membrane-biomimetic systems, and novel smart responsive nanoplatforms. It further analyzes the core bottlenecks currently facing clinical translation and proposes potential future directions, with the aim of providing a reference for the rational design and clinical translation of ovarian cancer nanovaccines.

articles.title: The mind-body connection in women's reproductive health: how psychological stress shapes gut and ovarian function - a narrative review.
articles.authors: Yachanahalli Purushotham A, Shilpa BM, Sundaram D
articles.abstract: Psychological stress plays a critical role in modulating women's reproductive health through integrated neuroendocrine, immune, and microbiome-mediated pathways. Activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis leads to elevated secretion of corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH), adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), and cortisol, which suppress hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) pulsatility, thereby disrupting the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. This results in reduced secretion of luteinising hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), impairing folliculogenesis, ovulation, and menstrual cyclicity. Chronic stress further induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis in ovarian cells, thereby reducing oocyte competence and diminishing ovarian reserve. Additionally, stress-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis alters the composition of key microbial taxa, including Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, and Clostridium, disrupting the estrobolome and impairing oestrogen metabolism. This dysregulation increases intestinal permeability and promotes systemic inflammation, as evidenced by biomarkers including interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and C-reactive protein (CRP), which adversely affect endometrial receptivity and implantation success. Emerging evidence also indicates that microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, and serotonin play a crucial role in modulating neuroendocrine signalling and reproductive outcomes. Despite growing evidence, the lack of standardised biomarkers and well-designed clinical trials limits translation into clinical practice. Future research should focus on integrative, personalised therapeutic approaches combining psychological interventions, lifestyle modifications, and microbiome-targeted therapies to improve reproductive outcomes and overall well-being.

articles.title: Magnesium Sulfate, Nicardipine, and Volatile Anesthetics in Severe Preeclampsia: Clinical and Mechanistic Implications for Uterine Atony and Postpartum Hemorrhage.
articles.authors: Bouya MS, Hamdani Z, Bouhabba N
articles.abstract: Severe preeclampsia frequently requires the concurrent administration of magnesium sulfate, intravenous nicardipine, and volatile anesthetics during the peri-delivery period, exposing the myometrium to convergent inhibition of calcium-dependent contraction. We conducted a narrative review guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles framework. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE and screened reference lists through March 2026, prioritizing mechanistic studies, human myometrial experiments, clinical cohorts, randomized trials, meta-analyses, and contemporary obstetric anesthesia guidance. The evidence indicates that convergence occurs at multiple levels of the excitation-contraction coupling machinery, including L-type calcium channel influx, inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate-mediated intracellular calcium release, oxytocin receptor signaling, intercellular coupling through connexin-43 gap junctions, and calcium sensitization via the Ras homolog family member A (RhoA)/Rho-kinase pathway. Magnesium sulfate acts as a broad calcium antagonist, nicardipine blocks L-type calcium channels, and volatile anesthetics depress spontaneous and oxytocin-induced force generation. Clinical evidence is more heterogeneous: magnesium sulfate shows mixed hemorrhagic associations, direct postpartum hemorrhage data for nicardipine remain sparse, and general anesthesia is associated with greater hemorrhagic risk than neuraxial techniques. This "tocolytic triad" is therefore best viewed as a mechanistically grounded risk model rather than a validated clinical syndrome. We propose a graded exposure-burden care bundle, anchored in quantified blood loss assessment, to align hemorrhage preparedness with cumulative pharmacologic inhibition of postpartum uterine contraction.

articles.title: ELAVL1 overexpression potentiates cervical cancer malignancy via regulating the ACVRL1/CASP14 pathway.
articles.authors: Liu J, Wang J, Gao Y et al.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer is the fourth common gynecological malignancy.
