To explore new therapeutic targets, we found that the transcriptional and translational levels of ELAVL1 were markedly increased in SiHa and HeLa cells as well as cervical cancer specimens. Knockdown of ELAVL1 substantially suppressed the proliferation, invasion, and migration of cervical cancer cells, while inducing apoptosis. Conversely, overexpression of ELAVL1 resulted in a substantial increase in the proliferative, invasive, and migratory capacities of SiHa cells. Bioinformatics predictions, RIP-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assays indicated that ELAVL1 might interact with the 3'UTR of ACVRL1, and upregulate ACVRL1 and CASP14 expression. Co-transfection experiments and functional assays revealed that ELAVL1 might modulate malignant phenotypes of cervical cancer cells via the ACVRL1/CASP14 pathway. Furthermore, in vivo si-ELAVL1 administration significantly inhibited tumor growth in nude mouse xenograft models. ELAVL1 may promote cervical cancer progression, potentially through regulating the ACVRL1/CASP14 pathway, rendering ELAVL1 a potential candidate for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Long-Term Maternal and Offspring Adverse Effects of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.authors: Juan J, Tian Z, Lu Y et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) serves as a diagnostic "stress test" for maternal physiology, exposing underlying metabolic vulnerabilities that imply a potential lifelong cardiometabolic trajectory for both mother and offspring. Mothers with a history of GDM face a 6-to-10-fold increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus and a 1.4-to-2.0-fold higher risk of cardiovascular disease, chronic hypertension, and chronic kidney disease. These risks are further compounded by factors such as obesity, hypertension, or adverse postpartum weight gain. For offspring, in utero exposure to hyperglycemia is thought to contribute to developmental programming that increases obesity risk-rising from approximately 1.1-fold in early childhood to 2.0-fold by adolescence-and predisposes them to early-onset dysglycemia. Although modest associations between in utero GDM exposure and both neurodevelopmental disorders and early cardiovascular events have been documented, these outcomes appear highly dependent on the postnatal environment. Despite the heterogeneity in findings among observational studies and variations in GDM diagnostic criteria, GDM should be regarded as a critical marker of long-term intergenerational risk for these adverse cardiometabolic and developmental outcomes. This review advocates for a clinical paradigm shift, positioning GDM as a sentinel event that requires a transition from episodic pregnancy care toward sustained, life-course cardiometabolic surveillance and preventative strategies for both mother and offspring.

articles.title: Association Between Hydrosalpinx and Detection of Gram-Positive Anaerobic Cocci in the Endometrial Microbiota: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Okamoto R, Enatsu N, Shibahara H et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether hydrosalpinx is associated with alterations in the endometrial microbiota and detection of gram-positive anaerobic cocci (GPAC)-associated genera.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 236 patients who underwent endometrial microbiota testing by 16S ribosomal RNA gene sequencing: 90 with untreated hydrosalpinx diagnosed by hysterosalpingography and 146 without hydrosalpinx. GPAC positivity was defined as detection of at least one of Anaerococcus, Finegoldia, Peptoniphilus, Peptostreptococcus, or Parvimonas. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, antibiotic use within 3 months, and luteal-phase sampling. False discovery rate adjustment was applied across four exploratory microbiota outcomes.
RESULTS: GPAC-associated genera were detected in 23/90 patients (25.6%) with hydrosalpinx and 19/146 (13.0%) without hydrosalpinx. Hydrosalpinx was nominally associated with GPAC detection (adjusted odds ratio, 2.20; 95% confidence interval, 1.10-4.38; p = 0.025), but not after false discovery rate adjustment (q = 0.101). No clear associations were observed for the other microbiota outcomes. Similar estimates were obtained after additional adjustment for recurrent implantation failure and in post hoc sensitivity analyses using alternative GPAC definitions.
CONCLUSION: Hydrosalpinx was associated with more frequent detection of GPAC-associated genera in exploratory analyses. This finding should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory and requires independent prospective validation.

articles.title: Ebola virus disease and maternal-neonatal health: direct and indirect impacts and health system preparedness gaps.
articles.authors: Ahmed NS, Ibrahim FA, Ali OA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ebola virus disease (EVD) is a severe viral infection that can substantially affect maternal and neonatal health through both direct disease and disruption of essential health services. Pregnant women and neonates may experience serious adverse outcomes during outbreaks, yet pregnancy-specific evidence remains limited and maternal-neonatal health has historically received insufficient attention in Ebola preparedness and research.
METHODS: This narrative review synthesized evidence on Ebola virus disease and maternal-neonatal health from peer-reviewed literature, international guidance, and outbreak reports. Relevant literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar and through reference-list screening of key publications. Findings were synthesized narratively, with attention to study design, methodological limitations, and differences across outbreak settings.
FINDINGS: Available evidence indicates that EVD during pregnancy is associated with severe maternal complications and poor fetal and neonatal outcomes, although risk estimates remain uncertain because of small and heterogeneous studies. Placental infection and mother-to-child transmission have been documented. Ebola outbreaks also disrupt antenatal, delivery, immunization, and emergency obstetric services, contributing to additional maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Key preparedness gaps include limited maternity-specific IPC, inadequate pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, and insufficient evidence on vaccines and therapeutics in pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: EVD poses serious but context-dependent risks to maternal and neonatal health through direct disease and disruption of essential healthcare services. Preparedness should prioritize continuity of essential maternity and newborn care, maternity-specific IPC, pregnancy-disaggregated surveillance, and the responsible inclusion of pregnant and breastfeeding women in vaccine and therapeutic research and access.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Nanoplatforms in HPV-Associated Cervical Cancer: Reprogramming the Post-Infection Microenvironment.
articles.authors: Huang L, Hu Y, Yu Y
articles.abstract: The immunosuppressive post-infection microenvironment (PIM) shaped by persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection poses a significant obstacle to the treatment of cervical cancer. In this review, PIM refers to a cervicovaginal local microenvironment initiated and established after HPV infection through complex interactions among HPV-infected keratinocytes, immune cells, host stromal components, and their derivative mediators, including chemokines, cytokines, extracellular vesicles, and metabolites. Ultrasound-responsive nanoplatforms, leveraging their deep penetration and spatiotemporal controllability, can induce immunogenic cell death (ICD) via sonodynamic therapy (SDT) and synergize with targeted delivery and local immune modulation. This review summarizes HPV-driven immune escape, conventional nanomedicine strategies, and ultrasound-responsive platforms for reprogramming PIM in HPV-associated cervical cancer.

articles.title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
articles.authors: Wright NC, Hossain R, Bouxsein ML et al.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional.
PARTICIPANTS: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728).
EXPOSURE: CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3).
OUTCOME MEASURES: Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis.
METHODS: Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated.
RESULTS: Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women.
CONCLUSION: In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

articles.title: Population-Level Shifts in Cervical Cancer Stage Distribution in the United States Following Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine Implementation.
articles.authors: Koshy E, Son C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine introduction is associated with shifts in stage at cervical cancer diagnosis and to examine whether sociodemographic disparities and evolving imaging practices have influenced these observed trends.
METHODS: We analyzed 103,831 cervical cancer cases diagnosed between January 2004 and December 2022 from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Stage at diagnosis was classified as non-distant or distant disease and compared across sociodemographic subgroups, including age group at diagnosis (<40 vs. ≥40 years), race/ethnicity, income, and urban-rural status. Temporal trends in distant-stage disease were evaluated using a linear probability model including year of diagnosis, age group, and an age group-by-year interaction term.
RESULTS: Across the entire cohort (N = 103,831), 14,622 patients (14.1%) presented with distant-stage disease. Among patients <40 years, distant disease increased from 5.6% in 2004 to 9.2% in 2022, corresponding to an annual increase of 0.18 percentage points per year (95% CI 0.12-0.23, p < 0.001). Among patients ≥40 years, distant disease increased from 12.6% in 2004 to 20.4% in 2022, corresponding to an annual increase of 0.39 percentage points per year (95% CI 0.34-0.44, p < 0.001). The annual increase was 0.21 percentage points greater among patients ≥40 years (95% CI 0.14-0.29, interaction p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Over the past two decades, distant-stage cervical cancer increased in the United States, with a significantly steeper increase among women ≥40 years than among women <40 years. The comparatively smaller increase among younger women is consistent with a possible contribution of HPV vaccination at the population level; however, individual vaccination status was unavailable, and a causal relationship cannot be established. Persistent racial, socioeconomic, and geographic disparities in distant-stage presentation emphasize the ongoing need for equitable access to vaccination and screening.

articles.title: Spatial analysis of placentae during congenital cytomegalovirus infection suggests distinct cellular profiles in immune and trophoblast cells: an exploratory study.
articles.authors: Sintim-Aboagye E, Quach HQ, Mukherjee I et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Human cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the leading infectious cause of congenital birth defects worldwide. The placenta is a major route of vertical transmission, and both immune and trophoblast cells are susceptible to CMV infection. This study aimed to spatially characterize gene and protein expression changes associated with CMV infection in the human placenta.
METHODS: In this exploratory study, CMV+ and control placentae were analyzed using the NanoString GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler to assess compartment-specific transcriptomic and proteomic profiles in trophoblast and immune cell populations.
RESULTS: CMV+ placentae showed increased immune activation in both trophoblast and immune cells, including pathways related to immune-cell proliferation, differentiation, lymphopoiesis, and T-cell development. Infected placentae also showed altered tissue repair and remodeling pathways, along with changes in proapoptotic proteins and cell death-associated transcripts.
DISCUSSION: Given the limited sample size, these findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. They provide preliminary insight into CMV-associated placental immune dysregulation and identify candidate pathways for investigation in larger, prospective studies.

articles.title: Cervical cancer screening willingness and associated health beliefs among predominantly college-educated young women attending gynecology clinics in Shenzhen, China.
articles.authors: Li H, Ke Y, Wu M et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study examined cervical cancer screening willingness and its associations with Health Belief Model (HBM) constructs among predominantly college-educated young women attending gynecology outpatient clinics in Shenzhen, China.
METHODS: A cross-sectional convenience-sampling survey was conducted (May 2023-May 2026) among 2,317 young women recruited from gynecology outpatient clinics in Shenzhen, China. The primary outcome was personal willingness to undergo screening (single binary item). Self-reported screening within three years was an exploratory secondary outcome. Thirty-three Likert items measured seven HBM domains. Seven HBM domains were treated as investigator-constructed summary scores and examined only exploratorily.
RESULTS: Most participants were aged 18-24 years (96.8%), unmarried (97.1%), and college-educated (95.5%). Screening willingness was reported by 88.3% and screening within the previous three years by 9.5%. Because these indicators capture different constructs (future willingness vs. previous screening experience) and eligibility was not assessed, their difference was not interpreted as a willingness-behavior gap. Cronbach's α ranged 0.890-0.965. In adjusted models, perceived barriers were inversely associated with willingness (aOR = 0.454, 95% CI 0.375-0.550), while cues to action (aOR = 1.399, 95% CI 1.189-1.646), perceived severity (aOR = 1.257, 95% CI 1.038-1.523), perceived benefits (aOR = 1.194, 95% CI 1.017-1.402), and HPV vaccination (aOR = 1.576, 95% CI 1.161-2.137) were positively associated.
CONCLUSION: Willingness to undergo screening was commonly reported, whereas prior screening experience was limited. Perceived barriers and cues to action were key correlates. Findings support guideline-based prevention communication but are cross-sectional and limited by clinic-based convenience sampling in Shenzhen, China; causal effects cannot be inferred.

articles.title: Neurovascular Retinomics for Noninvasive Profiling of Cancer Risk: A Prospective Cohort Study in the UK Biobank.
articles.authors: Zhang SW, Yusufu M, Gong X et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To comprehensively evaluate the predictive value of neurovascular retinal measurements for incident cancer.
DESIGN: Population-based, prospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 41 424 participants with eligible color fundus photography and OCT data from the UK Biobank.
METHODS: Retinomics were derived from multimodal retinal imaging of the UK Biobank, comprising 156 retinal features. Four Cox regression models were developed: model 1 (age and sex), model 2 (model 1 + ethnicity and lifestyle factors), model 3 (model 1 + retinomics), and model 4 (full model). Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression was used to select relevant retinal biomarkers, tailored to each cancer type. Predictive performance was assessed via the concordance index (C-index), detection rate (DR), and positive likelihood ratio (LR+). Detection rate and LR+ were evaluated at a false-positive rate of 10%. Calibration was assessed by calibration slope and calibration-in-the-large (CITL). Hazard ratios (HRs) were used to stratify cancer risk between high- and low-risk groups identified by retinomics.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident diagnoses of any cancer and specific types: breast, uterine/endometrial, prostate, esophageal, lung, stomach, colon, rectal, skin, and other cancers.
RESULTS: Among 41 424 participants, 3633 (8.77%) developed cancer over 12.5 years of follow-up. Incorporating retinomics significantly improved the C-index, DR, and LR+ across most cancer types, with the C-index values for model 4 ranging from 0.581 to 0.885 across individual cancers. The largest gain was observed in uterine/endometrial cancer (ΔC-index = 0.220; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.119-0.327]; ΔDR = 40%; ΔLR+ = 4.003), although this finding is based on only 20 incident cases and should be interpreted with caution. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed risks across all models (slope range: 0.635-1.233; CITL near 0). The high-risk group identified by retinomics exhibited a 7% higher annual cancer risk (HR = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.06-1.08; P < 0.001), accumulating to a nearly threefold higher risk over 12 years.
CONCLUSIONS: Retinomics demonstrates predictive value for cancer incidence, with cancer type-specific biomarker selection enhancing accuracy. These findings highlight the transformative potential of retinal imaging as a scalable, noninvasive approach for early cancer risk profiling and proactive prevention.
FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES:…

articles.title: A novel CD40LG frameshift mutation in an Iranian family with X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome: A case report.
articles.authors: Farzi F, Panahi M, Sakhinia E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathogenic mutations in the CD40LG gene lead to X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome type 1 (X-HIGM1), a rare primary immunodeficiency marked by impaired class-switch recombination of immunoglobulins and frequent severe infections. Early molecular diagnosis is essential for appropriate management, genetic counseling, and prenatal diagnosis.
CASE PRESENTATION: We investigated a 5-year-old Iranian boy with recurrent otitis media and pneumonia since infancy, progressive inflammatory arthritis, and a striking family history of early male deaths suggestive of an inherited X-linked immunodeficiency. Baseline immunological evaluation before initiation of IVIG showed markedly reduced IgG (2 mg/dL) and undetectable IgA (0 mg/dL), while IgM remained within the reference range (114 mg/dL). Lymphocyte subset analysis showed no major abnormality in the distribution of conventional T-cell subsets. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) revealed a hemizygous frameshift mutation in CD40LG, c.127del (p.Ala43LeufsTer11), predicted to introduce a premature termination codon and result in loss of normal CD40LG function. Sanger sequencing confirmed the variant in the proband and identified his mother as a heterozygous carrier, with the segregation pattern in the tested family members consistent with X-linked inheritance. Prenatal testing further showed that the fetus did not carry the pathogenic variant.
RESULTS: According to ACMG/AMP criteria, the c.127del variant was classified as pathogenic based on predicted loss of function, absence from population databases, phenotype specificity, and segregation evidence (PVS1, PM2_supporting, PP1_supporting, PP4). This variant affects exon 1 of CD40LG, a less commonly reported region compared with the known mutational hotspot in exon 5.
CONCLUSION: We report a novel pathogenic CD40LG frameshift variant associated with X-HIGM1 in an Iranian family. This report broadens the CD40LG mutation spectrum and underscores the utility of WES for confirming diagnosis, identifying carriers, enabling genetic counseling, and directing prenatal diagnosis for families with suspected X-linked immunodeficiency.

articles.title: Association of HER2, p53, and lymphovascular space invasion with lymph node metastasis in endometrial cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Cai X, Zhu Y, Wang S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in endometrial carcinoma is critical for optimizing the extent of surgical resection and formulating individualized therapies. This study aimed to investigate the associated factors of the LNM in endometrial carcinoma.
METHODS: 438 patients with endometrial carcinoma who underwent primary surgical staging between June 2014 and June 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Clinicopathological data and immunohistochemical expression profiles of ER, PR, HER2, p53, Ki67, ERCC1, and GST-π were systematically collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent associated factors for LNM.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of LNM in the study was 10.27% (45/438). Univariate analysis revealed that menopausal status, histological grade, Bokhman pathological subtype, depth of myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), and the expression levels of ER, PR, Ki67, p53, and HER2 were significantly associated with LNM (all P < 0.05). Subsequent multivariate analysis identified each one-category increase in HER2 staining level was associated with higher odds of LNM (OR 3.859, 95% CI 2.314-6.436, P < 0.001), as was each one-category increase in p53 staining level (OR 1.932, 95% CI 1.212-3.082, P = 0.006). The presence of LVSI was also an independent associated factor for LNM.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher p53 and HER2 staining levels and the presence of LVSI are independently associated with LNM in endometrial carcinoma.

articles.title: KAZALD1 upregulation predicts poor prognosis in epithelial ovarian cancer: Clinical validation and immune correlates.
articles.authors: Zhao R, Hu Y, Wang J et al.
articles.abstract: Reliable biomarkers for accurate risk stratification in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) remain limited. While kazal type serine peptidase inhibitor domain 1 (KAZALD1), a secreted proteoglycan, has been implicated in numerous tumors, its clinical value in EOC remains unknown. The present study evaluated whether KAZALD1 is an independent prognostic biomarker in EOC and explored its associations with immune-cell infiltration and tumor microenvironment-associated pathways. KAZALD1 expression was analyzed using Gene Expression Omnibus datasets (GSE66957 and GSE140082) and validated through immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis in 136 EOC samples. The Cancer Genome Atlas-Ovarian Cancer cohort (n=307) was utilized to explore immune infiltration and functional pathways. KAZALD1 mRNA levels were found to be significantly elevated in ovarian cancer compared with non-carcinoma tissues (adjusted P<0.001). In GSE140082, KAZALD1 upregulation correlated with poor overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival. IHC analysis determined that high KAZALD1 protein expression was significantly associated with distant metastasis (P=0.002) and advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage (P=0.011). Patients with high KAZALD1 expression exhibited a significantly shorter median OS (45.0 vs. 77.0 months; P=0.015). Multivariate Cox regression identified KAZALD1 as an independent prognostic factor (hazard ratio: 1.09; 95% CI: 1.00-1.19; P=0.042). Exploratory bioinformatic analysis demonstrated that KAZALD1 expression inversely correlated with the estimated abundance of macrophage (r=-0.431; P=0.020) and dendritic cell (r=-0.486; P=0.008) infiltration. In addition, its co-expression network was significantly enriched in TGF-β and extracellular matrix organization pathways. In conclusion, KAZALD1 was found to be a candidate independent prognostic biomarker for EOC. The observed immune associations are correlative and require validation in functional studies, spatially resolved analyses, prospective cohorts and immunotherapy-treated populations.

articles.title: Nonlinear relationship between serum LH levels on hCG trigger day and live birth rates in patients with fresh embryo transfer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang Y, Xiao Y, Yang A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In assisted reproductive technology (ART), the assessment of sex hormones is indispensable. Maintaining an appropriate level of luteinizing hormone (LH) is crucial for ovarian and endometrial development. However, the relationship between LH concentrations on the hCG trigger day and pregnancy outcomes after fresh embryo transfer (ET) remains relatively unclear. The aim of our study was to explore the role of serum LH levels in live birth rates (LBRs) and its specific relationship.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 9,044 patients who underwent fresh embryo transfer from 2019 to 2024. A multivariate regression model was used to identify the relationship. Stratification analysis was performed to test for effect modification in subgroups. The generalized additive model (GAM) and two-piecewise model were employed to describe the nonlinear relationship.
RESULTS: We found a positive relationship between serum LH levels and LBRs when LH concentrations were lower than 4.31 mIU/ml (odds ratio [OR] = 1.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.00-1.12, P = 0.042). No significant relationship was observed when LH concentrations were higher than 4.31 mIU/ml. In the exploratory subgroup analyses, the similar association was identified in GnRH agonist cycles, with an inflection point at 4.09 mIU/mL. The significant interaction was also identified between infertility type and serum LH levels in relation to LBRs.
CONCLUSIONS: Our research found the nonlinear relationship between serum levels on the hCG trigger day and LBRs. We tentatively identified an inflection point at 4.31 mIU/ml, and further studies are warranted to validate its potential clinical utility.

articles.title: Surgery-related factors predisposing to uterine niche after cesarean section: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Mazur-Ejankowska NK, Abacjew-Chmylko A, Ejankowski M et al.
articles.abstract: Cesarean section is among the most common surgical procedures worldwide, with rates exceeding 48% in some European countries and continuing to rise for both primary and repeat cases. Multiple cesarean deliveries have become routine in many developed countries. This trend has increased the incidence of intrapartum and long-term complications, particularly cesarean scar defects, which are symptomatic in up to 40% of affected women. A cesarean scar defect, also known as a uterine niche or isthmocele, is one of the most critical conditions in modern obstetrics and gynecology, with continuously increasing prevalence, as 56%-84% of women who undergo cesarean section develop a niche. Judicious indication for cesarean delivery and an appropriate uterine suturing technique are key factors in minimizing post-cesarean complications, including uterine niches. Uterine niche epidemiology and risk factors are widely investigated with partially contradictory conclusions. In this systematic review, a detailed analysis of surgery-related factors connected to uterine niche formation is presented. Aspects of uterine suturing technique, including the number of suture layers, locked or unlocked suturing, inclusion of the endometrium, and the choice of suture material, are compared. The aspect of single- and double-layer uterine closure remains under debate, as most studies do not show the superiority of either technique with regard to uterine niche incidence. Optimizing the hysterotomy surgical technique may decrease the rate of cesarean scar defects and their complications, including pelvic pain, abnormal uterine bleeding, dyspareunia, placenta accreta spectrum disorders, and cesarean scar pregnancies. All patients undergoing cesarean delivery should be screened for cesarean scar defects and informed about the potential complications of cesarean section.

articles.title: A high-throughput 96-well plate method to measure human uterine contractility.
articles.authors: Huon E, Rayssac J, Lamau MC et al.
articles.abstract: Uterine smooth muscle dysfunction is a common factor in many gynecological conditions, such as endometriosis, adenomyosis, dysmenorrhea, infertility, and labor dystocia. Here, we present a novel high-throughput, optical, low-cost, 96-well plate-based method for measuring ex-vivo uterine contractility. We validate this new method on non-pregnant human myometrial samples obtained from hysterectomies by systematically comparing contraction frequency, amplitude, and duration with the standard isometric force transducer approach. We illustrate the potential of this method by screening 8 different compounds, including hormones and pharmacological agents. In particular, we found that antagonists of T-type calcium channels (Z944) and chloride channels (benzbromarone) both decreased contractility in the non-pregnant human uterus. This method will accelerate the pharmacological development of myometrium-specific relaxing agents and provide a powerful tool to investigate the dysregulation of myogenic contractility in gynecological pathologies.

articles.title: Evaluation of inflammatory status and macrophage polarization in premature ovarian insufficiency mice induced by chemotherapy.
articles.authors: Tang M, Zhao M, Yao Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With an increasing trend of cancer occurring in young women, chemotherapy, a commonly used anticancer method, often leads to premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and infertility. Until now, there has been, however, no available treatment to cure POI patients caused by chemotherapy. This highlights the urgent need to unravel the mechanism underlying chemotherapy-induced POI development.
METHODS: The POI mouse model was established with cyclophosphamide and busulfan. The levels of key pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines in ovaries were determined using qPCR or immunohistochemistry (IHC), while the levels of other pro-inflammatory cytokines in the serum were measured by ELISA. The macrophages (MΦs) populations and polarization within ovaries were analyzed using flow cytometry and immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: Initially, chemotherapy-treated mice exhibited ovarian dysfunction and a decline in ovarian reserve, characterized by disrupted hormone levels and follicular loss. Following chemotherapy, there was an increase of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including Il1b, Il6 and Tnfa in mouse ovaries. Similarly, a significant elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and IL-18 was observed in the serum of chemotherapy-induced POI mice. Moreover, we found that the proportion of CD11c+ M1-like MΦs was remarkably increased in ovaries of chemotherapy-induced POI mice compared to the controls. However, the proportion of CD206+ M2-like MΦs did not differ significantly between POI and control groups. Notably, ovarian MΦs exhibited differential distribution after chemotherapy. CD11c+ M1-like MΦs mainly localized around atretic follicles, while CD206+ M2-like MΦs predominantly accumulated in ovarian stroma, accompanied by increased fibrosis. However, the Pearson analysis revealed that within the POI group, there was no significant correlation among fibrosis area, CD206+ M2-like MΦs density and the levels of key pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α) in ovaries.
CONCLUSIONS: Our descriptive study indicates that exacerbated inflammation and stromal fibrosis, as well as increased CD11c+ M1-like MΦs polarization, occur in mouse ovaries during chemotherapy. Since these are associative findings, future interventional studies including MΦs depletion are required to examine whether a causal relationship exists between CD11c+ M1-like MΦs and ovarian damage or between CD206+ M2-like MΦs and ovarian fibrosis in chemotherapy-induced POI.…

articles.title: Impact of unilateral salpingectomy on ovarian reserve and long-term reproductive outcomes in reproductive-aged women.
articles.authors: Zhou Y, Yang Y
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the short-term impact of unilateral salpingectomy on ovarian reserve and to evaluate its comprehensive value regarding long-term reproductive outcomes in women of reproductive age.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 96 reproductive-aged women diagnosed with ectopic pregnancy (EP) were enrolled. Base on the surgical and therapeutic regimens, participants were allocated into a study group (undergoing laparoscopic unilateral salpingectomy, n = 48) and a control group (preservation of the fallopian tube, including either laparoscopic salpingostomy or systemic methotrexate [MTX] therapy, n = 48). Biochemical markers of ovarian reserve (anti-Müllerian hormone [AMH], serum follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH], etc.) and morphological parameters (ovarian volume and antral follicle count [AFC]) were dynamically monitored and compared between the two groups at baseline and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. All participants were followed up for 24 months to compare spontaneous ovulation rates, spontaneous pregnancy rates, and the incidence of recurrent EP.
RESULTS: The study group exhibited transient fluctuations in biochemical markers indicative of diminished ovarian reserve in the early postoperative period (1 month), which normalized by 6 months postoperatively. Regarding morphological compensation, the contralateral ovarian volume and AFC in the study group increased significantly at 1-3 months postoperatively compared with the control group (P< 0.05); however, these parameters converged between the two groups by 6 months (P>0.05). Over the 24-month follow-up, there were no statistically significant differences in spontaneous ovulation or spontaneous pregnancy rates between the groups (P>0.05). Notably, the recurrence rate of EP in the study group was 2.08% (1/48), significantly lower than the 16.67% (8/48) observed in the control group (P< 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Unilateral salpingectomy induces a transient early decline in ovarian reserve, counterbalanced by a distinct short-term compensatory response in the contralateral ovary. Crucially, this procedure does not compromise long-term natural conception potential while significantly mitigating the risk of recurrent EP. For patients with normal ovarian reserve and a healthy contralateral tube, unilateral salpingectomy represents a safe, effective, and optimal treatment strategy for maximizing protection against recurrent EP.

articles.title: S-adenosylmethionine ameliorates spermatogenic dysfunction and sperm DNA damage via transsulfuration pathway.
articles.authors: Deng C, Jin Z, Wu H et al.
articles.abstract: Male infertility is a global concern, with high sperm DNA fragmentation linked to oxidative stress. Untargeted metabolomics in 111 men revealed downregulated S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) in patients with high sperm DNA fragmentation index (DFI). In vitro experiments demonstrated that SAM supplementation effectively reduced oxidative stress-induced DNA damage of human sperm and restored motility. In vivo, SAM administration in cyclophosphamide-induced oligoasthenozoospermia mice improved testicular structure, sperm quality, and DNA integrity. SAM restored glutathione levels and upregulated the expression of key transsulfuration enzymes, cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) and cystine/glutamate transporter (xCT), thereby enhancing glutathione biosynthesis and mitigating oxidative stress. RNA sequencing and protein analysis further revealed that SAM attenuated the expression of proapoptotic markers caspase-3 and caspase-8 and reduced germ cell apoptosis. These findings suggest that SAM may alleviate spermatogenic dysfunction and DNA damage, an effect that may involve enhancement of the transsulfuration pathway and improved redox homeostasis. This offers mechanistic insights and supports further exploration of its therapeutic potential on male infertility.

articles.title: Maternal Microvascular Calcium Sparks Are Reduced in Preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Parnell LC, Tierney AL, Cottrell EC et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal microvascular dysfunction is a hallmark of the hypertensive pregnancy disorder preeclampsia, but the mechanism(s) have not been fully defined. Within vascular smooth muscle cells, the principal pressure-induced vasodilatory pathway depends on localized Ca2+-release events from the sarcoplasmic reticulum ryanodine receptors (Ca2+ sparks), which stimulate BKCa (large-conductance Ca2+-activated potassium channels) to cause spontaneous transient outward currents and vasorelaxation. Here, the Ca2+ sparks-BKCa axis is assessed in preeclampsia for the first time.
METHODS: Pressurized omental resistance arteries from normotensive pregnant women and women with preeclampsia were imaged by high-speed spinning-disk laser confocal microscopy to assess Ca2+ sparks (20-110 mm Hg) and caffeine-evoked Ca2+ release (10 mmol/L; 80 mm Hg). Electrophysiology was used to assess spontaneous transient outward currents (-60 to 0 mV) and BKCa currents (-100 to +100 mV) in isolated vascular smooth muscle cells. A liquid chromatography-selected reaction monitoring-tandem mass spectrometry assay measured SERCA2 (sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase-2) and unphosphorylated/phosphorylated proteoforms of regulatory PLN (phospholamban). Vasoactive effects of the BKCa-dependent vasorelaxant HBD2 (human β-defensin-2; 0.01-10 nmol/L) were assessed by wire myography.
RESULTS: In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there was reduced Ca2+ spark frequency (P=1.1×10-10) and spontaneous transient outward current frequency (P=0.023). There was also reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ release in response to caffeine (P=0.0013), reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum refilling (P=2.0×10-4), and decreased ratio of SERCA2 to inhibitory unphosphorylated PLN (P=0.030), implicating increased SERCA2 inhibition. HBD2 (0.01-10 nmol/L) caused BKCa-dependent relaxation (P=4.6×10-10) of omental arteries without affecting Ca2+ spark frequency.
CONCLUSIONS: In microvascular arteries from women with preeclampsia, there is a striking reduction in Ca2+ spark frequency and spontaneous transient outward currents, likely secondary to increased inhibition of SERCA2 by unphosphorylated PLN and reduced sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ load. These defects may provide novel therapeutic targets to restore physiological control of the vasculature. BKCa-mediated relaxation by HBD2 was independent of Ca2+ sparks, supporting vasodilatory strategies bypassing disrupted microvascular mechanisms…

articles.title: Reconfiguring Abortion Infrastructures: An STS Analysis of Trends in Medical and Surgical Abortion in Post-Legalisation Contexts.
articles.authors: O'Shaughnessy A
articles.abstract: The growing dominance of medical abortion in liberal and post-legalisation contexts raises important questions about patient choice, reproductive autonomy and the organisation of abortion care. Whilst existing scholarship has examined the sociotechnical implications of medical abortion, contemporary shifts in relation to surgical abortion remain comparatively understudied. This research note proposes the notion of 'abortion infrastructures' as a sensitising concept for examining how abortion technologies are embedded in, and recursively reconfigure, broader sociotechnical systems of care. Drawing on feminist science and technology studies (STS), it develops four interconnected analytical dimensions: the relational embeddedness of abortion methods within medico-legal systems; the emergence of new spatial, temporal and institutional norms of provision; the relational differentiation of medical and surgical abortion; and the classificatory work through which these methods acquire distinct meanings and institutional positions. This framework directs attention to how resource constraints, clinical protocols, professional practices and moral assumptions may privilege medical abortion whilst rendering surgical abortion increasingly inaccessible. It also problematises understandings of method 'choice' which overlook the infrastructural conditions shaping available options. By foregrounding the normative and relational dimensions of abortion provision, this note advances a feminist infrastructural approach to trends in abortion methods and identifies directions for future empirical research.

articles.title: Barriers and Opportunities in Therapeutic Development for Early-Onset Preeclampsia.
articles.authors: Massaro A, Karumanchi A, Chang C et al.
articles.abstract: Early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE) remains a major contributor to maternal and fetal/neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with delivery, frequently at early preterm gestations, remaining the only effective way to halt disease progression. Therapeutic development has been limited by disease heterogeneity, unpredictable conditions, a progressive course, ethical and safety concerns in pregnancy, and uncertainty over trial design and regulatory pathways. This document summarizes an international multidisciplinary convening of clinicians, trialists, pharmacologists, regulators, and global health experts who met to explore key challenges and emerging strategies for therapeutic development in EOPE. Discussion centered on EOPE, marked by abnormal placentation, pronounced angiogenic imbalance, and high maternal-fetal risk, viewed as a potentially tractable target for disease-modifying interventions. Key themes included trial eligibility and enrollment, use of angiogenic biomarkers for enrichment and monitoring, defining meaningful maternal and fetal end points, safety oversight in the dual-patient context, and the potential of adaptive trial designs. Participants also considered translational tools such as pharmacokinetic (physiologically based pharmacokinetic) modeling and placental transfer studies. Participants identified both areas of alignment and continued uncertainty. Biologically informed strategies, such as biomarker-supported enrollment and carefully designed early-phase studies were seen as helpful in reducing uncertainty, especially alongside early regulatory engagement. Although many developers are pursuing soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 as a therapeutic target for EOPE, participants stressed the need for further biomarker validation, careful maternal-fetal risk-benefit assessment, and globally feasible approaches. Though focused on EOPE, these discussions may inform future research on late-onset disease, given its distinct underlying biology.

articles.title: Shared Genetics of Hypertension and Preeclampsia Converges on Immune Regulation.
articles.authors: Farahat MA, Abbas M, Melese M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and preeclampsia are clinically distinct, yet biologically related conditions characterized by vascular dysfunction and elevated cardiovascular risk. Although genome-wide association studies have identified loci associated with blood pressure traits and preeclampsia, the functional mechanisms linking shared variants to gene regulation and clinical phenotypes remain unclear.
METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for hypertension, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and preeclampsia to identify shared variants (P≤1×10-4). Cis-expression quantitative trait loci analyses were performed in whole blood using RNA sequencing data from 180 Black women. Significant associations (false discovery rate ≤0.05) were evaluated for replication across vascular, metabolic, and endocrine tissues in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project. Associations between gene expression and blood pressure traits were also assessed.
RESULTS: We identified 4792 shared genome-wide association study variants, of which 4663 were tested in expression quantitative trait loci analyses, yielding 1837 significant variant-gene associations across 78 genes. Replication in the Genotype-Tissue Expression project confirmed 645 associations involving 24 genes, many showing cross-tissue regulatory effects. Three genes (C4B, HLA-C, and HLA-DQB1) demonstrated convergent evidence across genome-wide association study, gene regulation, and expression-trait analyses. C4B expression was positively associated with hypertension and systolic blood pressure, while HLA-C showed negative associations with hypertension, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure. HLA-DQB1 expression was specifically associated with diastolic blood pressure, suggesting trait-specific effects.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight immune-related pathways as key mediators linking hypertension and preeclampsia. Integrating genetic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic data provides a framework for identifying functionally relevant loci and advancing mechanistic insights into cardiometabolic and pregnancy-related disorders.

articles.title: Beyond analytical proficiency: information continuity gaps in human papillomavirus testing laboratories within China's national external quality assessment network.
articles.authors: Lin G, Zhang K
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: External quality assessment (EQA) emphasizes analytical proficiency, but actionable molecular testing also depends on extra-analytical processes that link results to unique patients and subsequent care. We assessed patient de-duplication and downstream-result retrievability in HPV testing laboratories, using EQA performance as an analytical-quality anchor, and explored these capabilities as candidate quality indicators for the total testing process.
METHODS: A voluntary institution-level web survey was embedded in the 2026 National Center for Clinical Laboratories HPV16/18 EQA network and collected 2025 operational data. Survey records were linked to 2025 EQA results. The primary outcome was any laboratory access to downstream cytology, colposcopy, or histopathology information after an HPV-positive result. Associations were examined using prespecified Firth logistic regression, with ordinal and narrower-exposure sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Among 957 unique invitation-frame laboratories, 111 valid responses were obtained; 109 matched the frame (response rate 11 %). Among 89 respondents with 2025 EQA records, 88 (99 %) had fully correct HPV16/18 results. In contrast, 65/111 (59 %) laboratories could retrieve any downstream information, 14/111 (13 %) reported near-complete access, and 41/111 (37 %) could fully de-duplicate repeated tests from the same woman. Clinical service integration was associated with downstream information availability (OR 4.01, 95 % CI 1.71-9.84; p=0.001); the association persisted when exposure was restricted to screening/clinical-reporting functions (OR 3.30, 95 % CI 1.40-8.20; p=0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: High analytical proficiency did not imply closure of the extra-analytical testing loop. Patient identity resolution and downstream-result retrievability merit further standardization and validation as candidate quality indicators for molecular diagnostics and EQA-linked quality improvement.

articles.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.authors: Perichart-Perera O, Hernández-Hernández L, Rodríguez-Cano AM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metformin is increasingly used to treat gestational diabetes mellitus and other insulin-resistant conditions during pregnancy. Because it crosses the placenta, concerns remain regarding its potential effects on offspring growth and metabolic programming. This systematic review evaluated the effects of prenatal metformin exposure on infant nutritional status and adiposity during the first year of life.
METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care during pregnancy. Eligible studies reported infant nutritional status or adiposity-related outcomes from birth to 12 months. Risk of bias was assessed, and results were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Eight publications from six randomized controlled trials were included. Birthweight and birth size classifications were the most frequently reported outcomes. Metformin was not consistently associated with differences in birthweight or other anthropometric measures. One trial reported lower birthweight, while two reported fewer large-for-gestational-age or macrosomic infants. No study assessed direct measures of infant adiposity.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

articles.title: Institutional and Demographic Barriers to Cervical Cancer Screening among Women in Rivers State, Nigeria.
articles.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
articles.authors: Ohaka N, Okere GN, Asuzu NC et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The global goal of reaching a 70% cervical cancer screening rate by 2030 can hardly be achieved in the presence of screening constraints, especially in low- and middle-income countries. This study investigated institutional and demographic barriers to cervical cancer screening among women in the Rivers East District of Rivers State, Nigeria.
METHODS: This community-based cross-sectional study sampled 1,200 respondents from a population of 3,871,377 women of reproductive age. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire with a reliability index of 0.83, obtained using Cronbach's alpha. Data collected from the 1,182 valid returned questionnaires were analysed using SPSS version 27, with descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) and inferential statistics (multiple regression) at α = 0.05.
RESULTS: The findings of the study revealed that all institutional factors independently reduced screening uptake, R² = 0.271, F(4, 1179) = 109.83, p < 0.001; standardized effects were largest for health personnel unavailability (β = -0.203) and inconvenient clinic hours (β = -0.189). Demographic determinants were positively associated with uptake, R² = 0.296, F(4, 1179) = 123.34, p < 0.001, led by location (β = 0.231), religion (β = 0.218), age (β = 0.204), and marital status (β = 0.089).
CONCLUSIONS: It was concluded that institutional and demographic factors constituted significant barriers to cervical cancer screening uptake among women in Rivers State and that government intervention is needed to increase staffing levels in screening centres and provide targeted outreach, especially in local communities.

articles.title: Physical Activity, Sedentary Behavior, Obesity and Perceived Stress in Relation to Breast Cancer Risk among Moroccan Women: A Case - Control Study.
articles.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
articles.authors: Khossossi H, Ahyayauch H, El Alami A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer among Moroccan women. Although certain lifestyle factors like physical activity, sedentary habits, obesity, and psychological stress are suspected to play a role, evidence from North African populations remains limited. This study investigates the association between these factors and breast cancer among Moroccan women.
METHODS: A case-control study was conducted in the Rabat region involving 148 women, with 74 newly diagnosed breast cancer cases and 74 controls. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, reproductive and hormonal history, and lifestyle behaviors. Physical activity was evaluated using the validated Arabic version of the International Physical Activity Questionnaire, sedentary behavior was based on daily sitting time, and stress was measured using the Arabic Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10). Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to calculate odds ratios (ORs) and their 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: High physical activity was associated with a lower risk of breast cancer, while sedentary behavior and high stress were associated with an increased risk. Women with high stress levels had a notably higher risk than those with low stress. A family history of breast cancer and using hormonal contraceptives were also independently linked to a higher risk. These findings held true even after accounting for potential confounding factors.
CONCLUSION: This study emphasizes how lifestyle and psychosocial factors like physical activity, sedentary habits, and psychological stress play a significant role in breast cancer risk for Moroccan women. Encouraging physical activity, reducing sedentary time, and managing stress could be vital in preventing breast cancer in this population.

articles.title: CD44-Targeted Antibody-Drug Conjugates Suppress Ovarian Tumor Progression and Remodels Cancer Stem Cell-Associated Molecular Programs.
articles.authors: Shrestha P, Giri A, Thi TL et al.
articles.abstract: Cluster of differentiation 44 (CD44) is highly expressed in ovarian cancer (OC) and plays a critical role in cancer stem cell (CSC) maintenance, tumor initiation, and chemoresistance, making it an attractive therapeutic target. Herein, a CD44-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), CD44-VC-DOX, is developed by conjugating doxorubicin (DOX) to an anti-CD44 monoclonal antibody using a cathepsin-cleavable MC-VC-PAB linker for selective intracellular drug release in CD44-positive tumor cells. Physicochemical characterization confirms successful conjugation, high stability, and an optimal drug-to-antibody ratio. CD44-VC-DOX exhibit selective binding and rapid internalization in CD44-overexpressing OC cells resulting in potent cytotoxicity, apoptosis induction, and G2/M cell-cycle arrest. Importantly, CD44-VC-DOX effectively suppresses CSC-associated phenotypes, including tumorsphere formation, tumor-initiating frequency, CD44+CD133+ CSC populations, ALDH-positive cells, and stemness-related gene expression. In addition, CD44-VC-DOX reduces hypoxia-associated HIF-1α expression, indicating disruption of the CSC-supportive tumor microenvironment. In vivo, CD44-VC-DOX demonstrates efficient tumor targeting, significant tumor growth inhibition, and minimal systemic toxicity. Transcriptomic profiling further reveals coordinated suppression of CSC-associated and oncogenic pathways, including PI3K/AKT, MYC signaling, E2F targets, DNA repair, and stemness-related transcriptional programs, supporting effective depletion of tumor-initiating CSC populations and reduced tumor adaptability. Collectively, these findings highlight CD44-VC-DOX as a promising precision therapeutic strategy for targeting CSC-driven OC.

articles.title: Stage IV Ovarian Cancer Is Not Uniformly Lethal: Two Subgroups With Stage II-Like Outcomes Identified in Large Retrospective Cohorts.
articles.authors: Fang C, Li J, Li Q
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) staging system for advanced ovarian cancer has remained largely static since 2014, with stage IV subdivided into IVA and IVB without further stratification. Emerging evidence suggests substantial prognostic heterogeneity within stage IV, yet large-scale validation remains limited.
METHODS: We analyzed 28,010 patients from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (2010-2022) and 1175 from the Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC) (2010-2026). Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced baseline characteristics. Overall survival (OS) was compared across subgroups. We defined IVA-T1a as patients meeting FIGO IVA criteria with intra-abdominal disease limited to one ovary (intact capsule). We defined IVB-ILNT2 as stage IVB with metastasis confined to a single extra-abdominal lymph node station and intra-abdominal disease ≤ T2. IVB patients were stratified by metastatic pattern and surgical outcome.
RESULTS: In SEER, IVA-T1a patients (n = 49) showed no OS difference versus stage II (HR 1.08, 95% CI: 0.95-1.23, p = 0.250), but significantly better survival than stage IIIA (HR 1.35, 95% CI: 1.08-1.62, p = 0.024). Findings were validated in SYSUCC (IVA-T1a n = 15; vs. stage II p = 0.638, vs. IIIA p = 0.026). Among IVB patients, those with single-station lymph node metastases achieving R0/R1 resection (n = 152) had median OS of 29.0 months, comparable to stage IIIC patients (HR 1.08, p = 0.872). In SYSUCC, IVB-ILNT2 subgroup (n = 65) demonstrated survival comparable to stage II (p = 4e-04 vs. other IVB) and significantly better than stage IIIA.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that such patients may have a more favorable prognosis than implied by their current stage designation and underscore the need for prospective validation to determine whether treatment de-escalation could be considered in these specific subsets without compromising outcomes. Future FIGO revisions should consider refined classification incorporating intra-abdominal tumor burden and metastatic pattern, pending consistent validation across multiple independent populations.

articles.title: Female infertility in the 21st century.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.authors: Huzarska MA, Vail M, Effendi A
articles.abstract: More than 12% of reproductive-age women in the United States seek infertility services each year. Infertility is commonly defined as failure to conceive after 12 months of regular, unprotected sexual intercourse. Common gynecologic causes of female infertility include endometriosis; diminished ovarian reserve; ovulatory dysfunction and anovulation; and other cervical, uterine, or tubal factors. Advances in medicine and assisted reproductive technology have expanded treatment options for women and couples experiencing infertility. This article provides an updated review of female infertility to support PAs in delivering informed patient counseling on treatment options, recognizing potential complications, and facilitating timely and appropriate referrals.

articles.title: Completion of human papillomavirus vaccination and its determinants among adolescents in Southern Ethiopia: a convergent parallel mixed-methods study.
articles.authors: Suwanbamrung C, Sherfa A, Haile D
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women in Ethiopia and is primarily attributable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Although HPV vaccination has been introduced, completion of the recommended two-dose schedule remains suboptimal. Existing evidence has largely focused on access and awareness, with limited attention to cognitive, sociocultural, and maternal decision-making factors influencing completion. This study assessed the magnitude and determinants of second-dose or complete HPV vaccination among adolescents in southern Ethiopia using a mixed-methods approach.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 832 mothers of adolescent girls aged 9-14 years, selected using a multistage sampling method. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed with IBM SPSS ver. 23.0. A binary logistic regression model was used to identify factors associated with vaccine completion. Additionally, in-depth interviews were conducted with 12 purposively selected mothers and analyzed thematically to explore perceptions influencing vaccine completion.
RESULTS: The proportion of adolescents who completed the HPV vaccination series was 26.3% (95% confidence interval, 23.3-29.3). Factors positively associated with complete vaccination included maternal education at the secondary or higher, shared or autonomous maternal decision-making, prior cervical cancer screening and good knowledge of HPV. Conversely, high information overload and decision fatigue were associated with lower odds of completing the vaccination schedule. Qualitative findings revealed that mothers' decisions were shaped by cultural beliefs, trust in health workers, peer and social media influences, and prior healthcare experience.
CONCLUSION: HPV vaccination completion was low and was associated with interacting cognitive, socio-cultural, and health-system factors. Interventions should move beyond awareness creation to address information burden, strengthen maternal decision-making autonomy, and improve trust through consistent counseling.

articles.title: Barriers and enablers to the integration of family planning, immunization, and nutrition services into RMNCAH-N services in primary health care settings in Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Sadamo FE, Adinew YM, Dake SK et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite national policies promoting integrated Family Planning, Immunization, and Nutrition services, implementation remains challenging in Ethiopia's diverse primary healthcare settings. This research aimed to identify the barriers and enablers of integrating family planning, immunization, and nutrition services into reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health and nutrition (RMNCAH-N) services in selected agrarian and pastoralist regions of Ethiopia.
METHODS: A qualitative case study was conducted in ten primary healthcare units located across three districts: one district in pastoralist Afar region and two districts in the agrarian regions of Oromia and Central Ethiopia. We conducted seven focus group discussions (FGDs), 18 In-depth interviews (IDIs), and 10 key informant interviews (KIIs) with a total of 91 participants selected purposively, including program managers and policy-makers, health workers, and clients. Data were analyzed using a combined deductive and inductive approach guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research Version 2.0 (CFIR 2.0).
RESULTS: 17 of 48 CFIR 2.0 constructs were identified as influencing the integration of Family Planning, Immunization, and Nutrition services into RMNCAH-N touchpoints. Key barriers included: within the inner setting (inadequate facility readiness and limited space, essential supply shortages, poor provider commitment, and negative provider perceptions towards service integration), the outer setting (rural residence and political instability), and individuals and sociocultural factors (male-dominance in healthcare decision-making and restrictive cultural and religious norms particularly in pastoralist communities). Key enablers included: the innovation relative advantage of integration (reduced missed opportunities, lower transportation costs, fewer facility visits, and time savings), supportive inner setting factors such as enhanced teamwork, and improved health-seeking behavior facilitated by integrated health communication.
CONCLUSION: Integration of Family Planning, Immunization, and Nutrition services into RMNCAH-N services is influenced by distinct contextual factors in agrarian and pastoralist settings. To enhance integration, we recommend: improving facility readiness (space and supplies), addressing sociocultural barriers through community engagement, including male involvement, particularly in pastoralist areas, ensuring supply chain reliability,…

articles.title: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma via a CACNA1E-SNTG1 cfDNA methylation signature.
articles.authors: Song C, Tang J, Wu H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is characterized by high mortality primarily due to late-stage diagnosis. While circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation offers a promising avenue for non-invasive screening, achieving high diagnostic sensitivity for early-stage disease using scalable clinical assays remains a technical challenge. This study aimed to identify robust methylation biomarkers and validate their diagnostic performance and biological relevance using a liquid biopsy approach and patient-derived models.
METHODS: Differentially methylated regions were identified through whole-genome enzymatic methyl sequencing (WEM-seq) of clinical ESCC tissues and matched normal adjacent tissues, integrated with public microarray repositories. Following a rigorous dual-filter strategy to eliminate normal blood background noise, two hypermethylated loci, CACNA1E and SNTG1, were prioritized. A targeted quantitative methylation-specific PCR (qMSP) assay was developed and evaluated in a plasma cohort of 355 individuals (215 ESCC patients across stages 0-IV and 140 healthy controls). Five independent ESCC patient-derived organoid (PDO) models were established to investigate the mechanistic coupling between promoter hypermethylation and transcriptional silencing through paired qMSP and RNA sequencing.
RESULTS: The CACNA1E/SNTG1 dual-marker cfDNA panel demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy. In the independent validation cohort, the combined classifier discriminated ESCC from healthy controls with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.918, yielding an optimal sensitivity of 90.5% and a specificity of 85.7%. For early-stage (Stage 0-I) ESCC, the panel maintained a highly robust AUC of 0.950 with 90.0% sensitivity and 87.5% specificity. In the PDO models, Actin-normalized qMSP analysis revealed intense promoter hypermethylation at CACNA1E and SNTG1, which strictly correlated with profound transcript depletion, providing direct in situ evidence of methylation-mediated gene silencing.
CONCLUSION: The CACNA1E/SNTG1 methylation panel, combined with a qMSP workflow, provides a highly sensitive and specific strategy for the non-invasive early detection of ESCC. The integration of PDO-based multi-omics validation confirms the biological relevance of these epigenetic alterations, supporting the panel's broad utility for scalable clinical screening programs.

articles.title: Genome-wide association study of human papillomavirus infection and persistence in women living with HIV in Rwanda.
articles.authors: Naluai ÅT, Uwamungu S, Andersson M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We conducted an explorative genome-wide association study (GWAS) in East Africa to identify host genetic variants associated with the acquisition and persistence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection.
METHODS: We genotyped 385 Rwandan women living with HIV and selected host biomarker assay signals from genital swab samples using qPCR. We compared women who cleared HPV over a two-year interval (operationally defined as persistent infection), with those who did not. Exploratory gene-based aggregation analyses of rare and low-frequency variants represented on the genotyping array were also performed.
RESULTS: In the primary cluster-stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel analysis, rs13158830 within PPARGC1B exceeded the conventional genome-wide significance threshold for persistent HPV infection. The nearby MIR378A gene-expression assay signal was higher in HPV-positive women but did not distinguish clearance from persistence.
CONCLUSIONS: We identified an exploratory host genetic association with persistent HPV infection and several additional candidate loci. The lead rs13158830 signal remained evident in Fisher exact testing and PC-adjusted Firth regression, but the small number of carriers produced substantial uncertainty. These findings require replication in independent cohorts.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Expectant management of asymptomatic diaphragmatic endometriosis: a cross-sectional retrospective study.
articles.authors: Haghgoo A, Faegh A, Maghsoudi R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to introduce 55 patients with diaphragmatic endometriosis (DEM) who managed by pelvic endometriosis resection without resection of DEM. Also, tries to identify the most appropriate theory of DEM pathogenesis by multivariant analysis.
METHODS: 55 patients who underwent diagnostic and therapeutic laparoscopic endometriosis surgery and were diagnosed with DEM during the operation were included. Only one of the patients had symptoms of DEM and another 54 were asymptomatic. The #ENZIAN classification was used to better describe pre-operative imaging and surgical findings. During the follow-up period, all patients were asked for any DEM symptoms. Also, a second-look exploratory laparoscopy was performed on four patients with severe DEM. No patient recieved post-operative hormonal therapy after pelvic endometriosis resection.
RESULTS: The mean age was 32.7 years. Dysmenorrhea was the most common symptom among patients (81%). 94.5% had co-existing endometrioma, and 98.2% had deep pelvic endometriosis. Also, 75% of patients had evidence of ovarian chocolate cyst leakage. The present study revealed that DEM laterality was significantly associated with right-sided endometrioma and rectovaginal endometriosis size, as patients with bilateral DEM were more likely to have larger right-sided endometrioma and rectovaginal endometriosis. During a mean follow-up period of 34 months, none of the asymptomatic patients developed symptoms, while one symptomatic patient reported an improvement in chest pain. Also, the second laparoscopic exploration was performed in four patients, and it revealed improvement of DEM implantations in three and progression in one.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, DEM is a rare presentation of endometriosis that does not have a standardized diagnosis and treatment protocol. According to cases of DEM, which can be asymptomatic, subphrenic space exploration with appropriate exposure is necessary. In our opinion, the key point of the DEM treatment in asymptomatic patients is the current treatment of pelvic endometriosis. With pelvic endometriosis resection, DEM regresses spontaneously. In our study population, no patients with expectant management of the DEM mentioned related symptoms of DEM in follow-up visits. The results of this study emphasize the need for further studies on the expectant management of DEM.

articles.title: Socioeconomic and contextual determinants of high-risk fertility behavior among women in somalia: evidence from a multilevel analysis of nationwide survey.
articles.authors: Guled AM, Nuh AM, Mohamed MA et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk fertility behaviour (HRFB), characterised by early or advanced maternal age at childbirth, short birth intervals, and high parity, remains a major public health concern because of its strong association with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Somalia, a fragile and conflict-affected setting with persistently high fertility and maternal mortality rates, lacks comprehensive multilevel evidence on the determinants of HRFB. This study examined the socioeconomic and contextual factors associated with HRFB among women of reproductive age in Somalia.
METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the 2020 Somalia Demographic and Health Survey (SDHS). The weighted sample included 12,796 women aged 15-49 years with a history of childbirth. HRFB was defined as the presence of at least one risk condition: maternal age < 18 or > 34 years at birth, birth interval < 24 months, or birth order ≥ 3. Multilevel binary logistic regression models were fitted to identify individual-, household-, and community-level determinants, accounting for clustering at the community level. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported.
RESULTS: Overall, 70.5% of women experienced at least one high-risk fertility condition. Older maternal age was strongly protective against HRFB ([AOR] = 0.33, 95 CI: 0.28-0.38, p < 0.001). while limited healthcare decision-making autonomy increased risk (AOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03-1.35, p < 0.01). Women in the middle wealth quintile and those with primary education had higher odds of HRFB compared with the poorest and uneducated groups (AOR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.01-1.30, p = 0.03) and (AOR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.00-1.34, p < 0.01) respectively. Multiple births substantially increased the likelihood of HRFB, whereas health facility delivery reduced the odds.
CONCLUSION: HRFB is highly prevalent among women in Somalia and is shaped by intersecting individual, socioeconomic, and contextual factors. Interventions should prioritise delaying early childbearing, strengthening women's autonomy in reproductive health decisions, expanding access to quality maternal and family planning services, and addressing marked regional inequalities. Targeted, context-specific strategies are essential to reduce fertility-related risks and improve maternal and child health outcomes in Somalia.

articles.title: Multifactorial analysis of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis progression: the potential role of trunk skeletal muscle mass.
articles.authors: Watanabe K, Ohashi M, Tashi H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brace treatment can contribute to the progression of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) along with skeletal maturity and curve severity. However, other contributing factors remain unclear. We aimed to identify factors associated with the progression of AIS, focusing on skeletal muscle mass.
METHODS: The inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) female patients, (2) Risser grade 0-2 at the initial examination and ≤ 2 years postmenarche, (3) major Cobb angle of 10°-39° at baseline, (4) Risser grade ≥ 4 and ≥ 2 years postmenarche at final evaluation, and (5) follow-up of ≥ 2 years. In total, 149 patients with AIS were included. The assessed variables included major curve Cobb angle, age, height, age at menarche, extracurricular sports involvement, family history of scoliosis, curve type, Risser grade, body mass index, appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI), trunk skeletal muscle mass index (TSMI), and brace compliance. Skeletal muscle mass was measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis of skeletal maturity. Patients were classified into the progression (≥ 10° Cobb increase; n = 61) and nonprogression (n = 88) groups for comparison.
RESULTS: Significant differences (p < 0.05) were observed between the nonprogression and progression groups in height increase (6.9 cm vs. 10.8 cm), age at menarche (11.6 years vs. 12.2 years), curve type (major thoracic scoliosis: 67% vs. 92%), Risser grade (grade 0: 33% vs. 57%), ASMI (6.13 kg/m² vs. 5.92 kg/m²), TSMI (7.27 kg/m² vs. 6.97 kg/m²), and major Cobb angle at final examination (30.0° vs. 44.4°). Multivariate analysis identified major thoracic scoliosis (odds ratio [OR] 4.9, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.535-15.175), height increase (OR 1.2, 95% CI 1.031-1.360), and TSMI (OR 0.3, 95% CI 0.101-0.914) as factors associated with curve progression.
CONCLUSIONS: Although skeletal maturity largely determines AIS progression, trunk muscle mass may also play a role during growth. Future studies should explore targeted interventions to improve muscle condition for better scoliosis management.

articles.title: Association between maternal thyroid function in early pregnancy and neurodevelopment in children aged 0-24 months: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wu C, Yu Y, Liang H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the influence of maternal thyroid function in early pregnancy on offspring neurodevelopment outcomes.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 20,855 mother-offspring pairs from Shenzhen, China, with delivery dates between February 2016 and May 2024. Maternal thyroid hormone levels were measured at 7-13 gestational weeks. Neurodevelopment outcomes were assessed using the Ages and Stages Questionnaire-Third Edition (ASQ-3) at 0-24 months of age.
RESULTS: Compared with euthyroid mothers, overt hypothyroidism was associated with an increased risk of gross motor delay (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.14; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.17-3.63). Subclinical hypothyroidism was linked to a higher risk of delay in the problem-solving domain (aOR 1.63; 95% CI 1.03-2.49). Hypothyroxinemia was associated with increased risk of delays in both the gross motor (aOR 1.73; 95% CI 1.04-2.70) and fine motor domains (aOR 1.69; 95% CI 1.01-2.66). Subclinical hyperthyroidism was associated with an elevated risk of gross motor delay (aOR 1.97; 95% CI 1.14-3.18). Maternal thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels exhibited a U-shaped relationship with the risk of neurodevelopmental delay in the gross motor domain. (P-overall = 0.012; P-nonlinear = 0.003) CONCLUSIONS: Maternal overt hypothyroidism, subclinical hypothyroidism, hypothyroxinemia, and subclinical hyperthyroidism in early pregnancy are associated with neurodevelopmental delays in children. Notably, this association exhibits a U-shaped pattern, whereby both low and high TSH levels are linked to an increased risk of neurodevelopmental delay.

articles.title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a retrospective cohort study comparing coloanal and colorectal anastomosis.
articles.authors: Sahin K, Colak T, Güler E et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although anastomotic level after low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer is largely determined by tumor location, its relationship with postoperative bowel function and quality of life remains clinically important. This study compared functional outcomes, fecal continence, sexual function, and health-related quality of life between patients undergoing colorectal anastomosis (CRA) and coloanal anastomosis (CAA) after curative-intent LAR.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 126 patients who underwent LAR for rectal cancer between January 2019 and June 2024 (CRA, n = 84; CAA, n = 42). Health-related quality of life was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29 questionnaires, fecal continence using the Wexner score, and fecal incontinence-related quality of life using the FIQL scale in patients with Wexner scores > 8. Firth penalized logistic regression and multivariable linear regression were used to evaluate clinically significant fecal incontinence, Wexner scores, and selected EORTC domains, adjusting for age, sex, tumor level, neoadjuvant radiotherapy, diverting stoma, and time since surgery.
RESULTS: Global health status was comparable between groups. In unadjusted analyses, the CAA group had higher stool frequency, flatulence, and embarrassment scores and a higher prevalence of clinically significant fecal incontinence than the CRA group (28.6% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.004). After adjustment, anastomosis type was not independently associated with clinically significant fecal incontinence (adjusted odds ratio, 2.30; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-13.40; p = 0.261), Wexner score (adjusted β, 0.04; 95% CI, - 3.69 to 3.76; p = 0.984), global health status, or selected EORTC domains. No adjusted EORTC association remained significant after false discovery rate correction.
