Diverting stoma formation was independently associated with a higher Wexner score (adjusted β, 2.28; 95% CI, 0.61-3.95; p = 0.007). Sexual function did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Although patients undergoing CAA had worse bowel function in unadjusted comparisons, these differences were not independently attributable to anastomosis type after adjustment for relevant clinical and treatment-related factors. Global quality of life was comparable between groups. Postoperative functional outcomes after rectal cancer surgery appear multifactorial and should not be attributed to anastomosis type alone.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with maternal near miss in tertiary hospitals in Eskişehir, Türkiye: a case-control study.
articles.authors: Arslan Torba T, Önsüz MF, Metintaş S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal near miss (MNM) cases provide valuable insight into the quality and performance of maternal health services. Understanding the factors associated with MNM is crucial for developing effective public health interventions. This study aimed primarily to identify factors associated with MNM and secondarily to report the MNM ratio in tertiary hospitals in Eskişehir, Türkiye.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, case-control study was conducted at two tertiary hospitals in Eskişehir, Türkiye. The medical records of 10,360 women who gave birth between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023, were reviewed. A total of 53 MNM cases were identified based on the World Health Organization criteria defined by organ dysfunction and life-threatening conditions. For each case, three controls without serious complications were selected, resulting in 159 controls (1:3 ratio). Descriptive statistics, univariate analysis, and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with MNM.
RESULTS: The incidence of MNM was calculated as 5.18 per 1,000 live births. The most common maternal complications were severe postpartum hemorrhage (45.2%), uterine rupture (34.0%), and severe preeclampsia (17.0%). The most commonly performed critical interventions were blood transfusion (73.6%), laparotomy (45.3%), and intensive care unit admission (30.2%). Coagulation/hematological dysfunction (58.5%) and uterine dysfunction (47.2%) were the most frequently observed MNM criteria. Multivariate analysis identified anemia (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 16.57; 95% CI: 7.19-38.19), previous cesarean delivery (aOR = 6.22; 95% CI: 2.18-17.77), short interpregnancy interval of two years or less (aOR = 3.68; 95% CI: 1.63-8.32), absence of antenatal care (aOR = 4.69; 95% CI: 1.44-15.21), and presence of chronic disease (aOR = 4.83; 95% CI: 2.11-11.04) as independent risk factors, while preterm birth (aOR = 12.86; 95% CI: 5.95-27.78) emerged as a strong clinical indicator associated with MNM.
CONCLUSIONS: The results of this study underscore the importance of early identification and management of modifiable risk factors for MNM. Strengthening antenatal care services, improving anemia screening and treatment, promoting evidence-based cesarean delivery practices, and ensuring postpartum family planning support may help improve maternal outcomes and reduce preventable maternal morbidity.

articles.title: E-MPATHY: Development, validation, reliability, and acceptability of a decision-support tool for district-level maternal death review in Indonesia.
articles.authors: Cahyanti RD, Widyawati W, Hakimi M
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal Death Review (MDR), the cornerstone of Maternal Death Surveillance and Response (MDSR), generates evidence to inform strategies for reducing maternal death. However, MDR is often constrained by blaming cultures and the lack of structured approaches for systematic case review. These limitations hinder the objectivity identification of causes, contributing factors, and actionable recommendations. To address this gap, we developed a novel structured decision-support tool (DST) integrating scientific evidence and clinical standards to formulate evidence-based recommendation. This study aimed to develop a DST for district-level MDR and to evaluate its validity, reliability, and acceptability.
METHODS: The tool development comprised four steps: needs assessment, face and content validity, reliability, and acceptability assessment. We compared the review findings of 113 cases based on expert-decision constructed using a DST between district and provincial review teams in Central Java, Indonesia. Reviewers' acceptability was assessed through observations during the review and analyzed using the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability.
RESULTS: The needs assessment resulted in 1) naming the tool (E-MPATHY), reflecting a supportive learning environment, and 2) the development of a structured DST framework integrating scientific evidence with the three delays model across pregnancy periods. The tool guided reviewers in assigning underlying causes of death based on the International Classification of Diseases for Maternal Mortality (ICD-MM), assessing preventability, identifying contributing factors, and generating recommendations. Agreement between two reviewer teams was almost perfect for ICD-MM classification (κ = 0.86; 95%CI:0.76-0.96; p < 0.001). In the three delays assessment, the highest agreement observed in the postpartum period (κ = 0.58; 95%CI:0.42-0.74; p < 0.001), with substantial agreement in the third delay phase (κ = 0.61; 95%CI:0.46-0.75; p < 0.001). The reviewers' acceptability indicated the benefits of evidence-based review and encourages positive learning attitudes in their daily practices.
CONCLUSION: The E-MPATHY had almost perfect inter-rater reliability in assigning ICD-MM. In addition, there was convincing evidence of its validity and acceptability to be a support direct learning tool potentially applied to institutionalized workable district MDR in Indonesia. However, as the evaluation was conducted within one province,…

articles.title: Associated factors and machine learning-based prediction model construction for positive reproductive tract group B streptococcus screening in late-pregnancy women.
articles.authors: Liu F, Wu L, Li F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a key pathogen in perinatal health. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a risk prediction model for positive reproductive tract GBS screening in late-pregnancy women using routinely collected clinical data.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 363 late-pregnancy women who underwent combined vaginal-rectal GBS screening from January 2023 to May 2024. Data were split 7:3 into training (n = 254) and validation (n = 109) sets using stratified sampling. Predictive variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression combined with the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine learning models were developed in the training set. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: The GBS positivity rate was 25.1% (91/363). Feature selection identified seven predictors: education level, platelet count, lymphocyte count, vaginitis type, abnormal vaginal discharge, gestational thyroid disease, and gestational weight gain. The random forest model showed the best performance in the validation set, achieving an AUC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.811-0.922) and a Brier score of 0.153.
CONCLUSIONS: The random forest model, built from routinely available clinical data, demonstrated relatively favorable discrimination and calibration in internal validation for predicting positive GBS screening in late pregnancy. It may offer potential for risk stratification and screening adherence management, but it should not replace standard microbiological testing or clinical judgment. Multicenter prospective validation is required before clinical application.

articles.title: Factors associated with tubal obstruction and development of a preliminary prediction model following laparoscopic tubal fenestration and embryo removal in patients with tubal pregnancy: a single-center exploratory study.
articles.authors: Chen Y, Zhao W, Sun P et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with tubal obstruction following laparoscopic tubal fenestration and embryo removal in patients with tubal pregnancy, and to develop a preliminary prediction model based on these factors.
METHODS: Clinical data of 310 patients who underwent laparoscopic tubal fenestration and embryo removal for tubal pregnancy at the Third Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2020 and June 2025, and subsequently received hysterosalpingography, were retrospectively collected. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 217) and a validation set (n = 93) using a 7:3 ratio. Based on hysterosalpingography results, the training set was further divided into a patent group (n = 135) and an obstruction group (n = 82). Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify influencing factors for postoperative tubal obstruction. A nomogram prediction model for postoperative tubal obstruction was constructed using the R language, and its performance was evaluated through internal split-sample validation.
RESULTS: The preoperative β-hCG level (100 IU/L), maximum diameter of pelvic fluid (mm), and the proportion of pregnancies located in the interstitial and isthmic portions of the fallopian tube were significantly higher in the obstruction group compared to the patent group, while the diameter of the tubal mass was smaller. These differences were statistically significant (all P < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis indicated that preoperative β-hCG level (100 IU/L), site of tubal pregnancy, maximum diameter of pelvic fluid (mm), and diameter of the tubal mass (mm) were independently associated with postoperative tubal obstruction (P < 0.05). A nomogram was established using these factors. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for the training set was 0.824 (95% CI: 0.770-0.879), indicating promising discriminatory ability within this exploratory cohort.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative β-hCG level (100 IU/L), diameter of the tubal mass (mm), site of tubal pregnancy, and maximum diameter of pelvic fluid (mm) were identified as factors potentially associated with tubal obstruction in this single-center exploratory study. The nomogram developed from these factors demonstrated acceptable predictive performance in internal validation and may serve as a preliminary tool for preoperative risk estimation. However, external validation in independent multicenter cohorts is required before…

articles.title: Menopausal status modifies the association between migraine and cardiovascular disease risk: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of headache and pain
articles.authors: Kim DY, Han K, Lee JH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether menopausal status modifies the association between migraine and cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in women, using both relative and absolute risk measures.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service data. Women aged ≥ 40 years who underwent the 2009 health screening and had no prior CVD (myocardial infarction or stroke) were included. Migraine was defined by using ICD-10 diagnostic codes. Menopausal status was determined from questionnaire-based reproductive history and prespecified as an effect modifier. Incident CVD and cardiovascular death were ascertained. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Among 2,156,733 women, 923,517 were premenopausal and 1,233,216 postmenopausal. In premenopausal women, CVD incidence was higher in those with migraine than in those without migraine (2.22 vs. 1.38 per 1,000 person-years), with a higher risk after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.42-1.66). In postmenopausal women, CVD incidence was also higher among those with migraine (9.53 vs. 7.50 per 1,000 person-years), although the relative association was attenuated but remained significant (HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.17-1.23). Accordingly, the crude incidence rate difference associated with migraine was larger after menopause (2.03 vs. 0.84 per 1,000 person-years). The relative associations between migraine and cardiovascular outcomes were stronger in premenopausal women, whereas larger absolute risk differences were observed in postmenopausal women. This pattern was observed for CVD, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke, but not for cardiovascular death.
CONCLUSION: Migraine was associated with increased CVD risk in women. Relative associations were stronger before menopause, whereas absolute excess incidence was greater after menopause. These findings highlight the importance of considering migraine in cardiovascular risk assessment across the female life course, including after menopause.

articles.title: Maximum peri-prostatic anatomy preserving-robotic assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy with the da Vinci Si/Xi Surgical System: surgical learning curve evaluation and outcomes.
articles.authors: Liu L, Wang RL, Wu CY et al.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (RALP) is technically demanding, and anatomy-preserving modifications may further increase procedural complexity and prolong the learning curve. However, the case volume required to achieve stable operative efficiency with maximum peri-prostatic anatomy-preserving RALP (MPAP-RALP), and the clinical implications of the learning process, remain unclear. We therefore used cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis to evaluate the MPAP-RALP learning curve and compared perioperative, oncological, urinary continence, and quality-of-life outcomes between the learning and learning-completion phases. A total of 78 consecutive patients diagnosed with prostate cancer via biopsy were enrolled between June 2019 and June 2022. All procedures were conducted by a senior urological surgeon. CUSUM was used to analyze the operative time. Using the CUSUM inflection points, the phase division was established: the turning point in operative time CUSUM occurred at case 31, prompting the division of cases there. Significantly, the completion phase had a much shorter operative time than the learning phase, with medians of 250 and 333 min, respectively (p < 0.001). Follow-up of urinary continence was available in 58 patients. In both phases, urinary continence recovery was excellent, showing no significant differences at any time point (all p > 0.05), and all patients were continent by 12 months. A significant difference was observed (p = 0.041) in quality of life at 1 month, with more patients in the completion phase reporting "delighted" (24.2% vs. 0%). Urinary function at one month indicated a borderline non-significant difference (p = 0.079), with comparable patients reporting "no problem" in learning phase and completion phase (84.0% vs. 84.8%), whereas the learning phase had three cases of "problem". In this single-surgeon series, a measurable early learning curve was observed for MPAP-RALP. CUSUM analysis revealed that in this single-surgeon series, MPAP-RALP had a measurable operative-time learning curve, with relative stabilization after approximately 31 consecutive procedures. The shorter operative time was not accompanied by an obvious deterioration in perioperative safety, positive surgical margins, or urinary continence. However, this was a retrospective, single-center study with a small sample size, and platform-related confounding could not be excluded. The 31-case turning point should therefore be verified in larger…

articles.title: Length of stay and nhi-reimbursed expenditures after robotic-assisted surgery in taiwan: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.authors: Chen PD, Chung CH, Lu CY et al.
articles.abstract: Population-level evidence comparing robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with laparoscopic surgery (LS)/video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open surgery (OS) across multiple procedures from a payer perspective remains limited. This study aimed to compare postoperative length of stay (LOS) and insurer-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures among RAS, LS/VATS, and OS across representative procedures following the expansion of RAS reimbursement in Taiwan. This retrospective nationwide population-based cohort study was conducted using claims data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. We identified adults (age ≥ 18 y) who underwent 1 of 12 representative procedures spanning thoracic, hepatobiliary-pancreatic, colorectal, urologic, and gynecologic specialties between September 1 and December 31, 2024. Surgical approaches were classified as robotic-assisted surgery (RAS), laparoscopic or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (LS/VATS), or open surgery (OS) using the corresponding procedure and robotic-assistance codes in the NHI claims database. The outcomes were postoperative LOS and total NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials during the index hospitalization. Procedure-specific stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to each pairwise comparison. This study included 17 549 patients. Of these patients, 2900, 9763, and 4886 underwent RAS, LS/VATS, and OS, respectively. RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS than LS/VATS for lung resection, colectomy, partial nephrectomy, and nephroureterectomy and with lower reimbursed expenditures for lung resection, partial pancreatectomy, nephroureterectomy, and radical prostatectomy. Compared with OS, RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, with the largest difference noted for colectomy (8.38 vs. 14.80 d). Moreover, RAS was associated with lower reimbursed expenditures than OS for lung resection, minor hepatectomy, partial pancreatectomy, colectomy, and malignant hysterectomy. During the early period following the September 2024 expansion of NHI reimbursement for RAS in Taiwan, RAS was associated with shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, whereas differences in NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials varied by procedure and comparator. Given the observational study design, residual confounding, and limited…

articles.title: Arteriovenous Malformations as Neoplastic-Like Lesions: Molecular Underpinnings and Implications for the Interventional Radiologist.
articles.authors: Shashi KK, Gonzalez Garcia A, Sabado J et al.
articles.abstract: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are high-flow vascular anomalies traditionally treated as congenital structural lesions with embolization or surgical resection. However, recurrence after embolization alone exceeds 90%, underscoring incomplete understanding of their biology. Next-generation sequencing has identified somatic gain-of-function mutations in KRAS, MAP2K1, BRAF, and HRAS as drivers of sporadic AVMs. Confined to lesional endothelial cells, these mutations activate RAS/MAPK signaling and support a neoplastic-like rather than purely structural disease model. This has therapeutic implications: MEK inhibitors, particularly trametinib, have shown angiographic and clinical responses in refractory AVMs. Interventional radiologists can obtain draining vein liquid-biopsy samples during embolization for molecular genotyping; embolization may increase circulating cell-free DNA yield. This review summarizes the molecular rationale, targeted therapy evidence, and integration of genotyping into embolization workflows to enable combined treatment strategies.Level of Evidence: No level of evidence assigned (Review Article).

articles.title: The maternal-fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors.
articles.authors: Jain R, Tikoo S, Márquez-Burgoa C et al.
articles.abstract: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal-fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R+ erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4+CSF1R- Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4+ nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal-fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

articles.title: Risk of Preterm Birth, Congenital Structural Anomalies and Severe Postpartum Hemorrhage After Receipt of NVX-CoV2373 Vaccine During Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Gwak E, Choe YJ, Shin JY et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Information on maternal and neonatal outcomes following NVX-CoV2373 coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination in pregnant women is limited.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized National Health Insurance Service data, linking maternal and neonatal records with COVID-19 vaccination registries in South Korea. Eligible pregnancies included those with recorded births among 20-49-year-old women between February 1 and December 31, 2022, excluding pregnancies with first-trimester severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infections. Pregnant women who received NVX-CoV2373 during pregnancy were matched, 1:4, with COVID-19-unvaccinated women using propensity score methods to account for demographic and clinical variables. Adjusted risk ratios (aRR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) for preterm birth (PTB), congenital structural anomalies (CSAs) and severe postpartum hemorrhage (sPPH) were estimated using log-binomial regression models. To further characterize NVX-CoV2373 safety, a separate analysis estimated aRRs and 95% CIs comparing women who exclusively received either NVX-CoV2373 or BNT162b2 during pregnancy.
RESULTS: Among 484 NVX-CoV2373 recipients during pregnancy and their matched sample of 1930 COVID-19-unvaccinated women, there was no observed difference in risk of PTB (aRR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.75-1.21), CSAs (aRR = 0.57, 0.30-1.09) or sPPH (aRR = 0.65, 0.15-2.90) between groups. Between 476 NVX-CoV2373 and their matched sample of 1497 BNT162b2 recipients during pregnancy, there were no significant differences in risk of PTB (aRR = 1.01, 0.75-1.34), CSAs (aRR = 0.74, 0.42-1.29) or sPPH (aRR = 0.45, 0.10-1.97).
CONCLUSIONS: The risk of PTB, CSAs and sPPH was not statistically different between NVX-CoV2373 and BNT162b2 recipients during pregnancy and COVID-19-unvaccinated women, reinforcing the antepartum safety of NVX-CoV2373 and COVID-19 vaccines in general.

articles.title: Global disparities in prevalence, aetiology, motor impairment severity, access to health care, and mortality in childhood cerebral palsy: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Assan BR, Dossou MW, Agbodjogbé YA et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To map and synthesize the global literature on socioeconomic and structural inequalities in cerebral palsy (CP).
METHOD: A scoping review according to the framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley was conducted and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, World Health Organization Global Medical Index, African Journals Online, Scopus, Science Direct, Web of Science, and Wiley Online Library databases were searched. A manual search of Google Scholar was also conducted to capture grey literature. Observational studies reporting disparities in CP across high-income countries (HICs) and low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) were included. Data were extracted and synthesized narratively across five prespecified domains of inequality: prevalence, aetiology, severity, access to health care, and mortality.
RESULTS: Forty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Registry-based studies from HICs reported a birth prevalence of CP ranging from 1.4 to 2.5 per 1000 live births, most recently estimated at 1.6 per 1000 live births (95% confidence interval = 1.5-1.6). Registry-based prevalence in LMICs remained scarce, with estimates of up to 3.4 per 1000 live births and period-prevalence of 2.3 to 3.7 per 1000 children. A modelled estimate of 16.2 per 1000 children aged under 5 years has been reported in the World Health Organization African Region. Preventable causes, such as hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, kernicterus, and infection, were more frequently reported in low-resource settings, whereas preterm birth as a major risk factor was predominantly reported in HICs. Socioeconomic disadvantage, lower parental education, and minority ethnic status were associated with greater functional severity, higher comorbidity burden, and unmet health care needs. Physiotherapy was the main form of care reported in many LMICs. Studies from LMICs generally reported lower survival estimates and higher mortality rates than those from HICs. However, comparisons were limited by differences in study populations, severity profiles, and methodological approaches.
INTERPRETATION: This review identified pronounced disparities in CP across prevalence, severity, access to health care, and survival in diverse settings. The findings highlight important gaps in the evidence base and underscore the need for further research to better understand the mechanisms underlying these disparities and to inform equity-oriented health policies.

articles.title: Inter-reader agreement between expert and non-expert readers in the interpretation of placental MRI.
articles.authors: Coco A, Cho A, Weinstein R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) that are under reported in missed/under-classified cases, compare inter-reader agreement between subject matter experts (SMEs) and non-SME radiologists, and determine features most challenging for non-SME readers to detect.
METHODS: In this IRB-approved retrospective study, 59 patients with pathologically confirmed PAS who underwent cesarean hysterectomy (2008-2022) and preoperative MRI were included. Cases were classified as missed/under-classified (n = 17) or concordant/over-classified (n = 42). Original radiology reports were reviewed for key PAS features. Missed/under-classified cases were reinterpreted by two SMEs and two non-SME radiologists using a structured template. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and kappa statistics.
RESULTS: Missed/under-classified cases had significantly fewer reported imaging findings than concordant/over-classified cases (1.5 vs. 3.4, p < 0.001). Secondary SME review increased reported findings per case (5.3, p < 0.001), identifying overlooked features including placental bands and myometrial thinning or bulging. SMEs demonstrated higher concordance but more overestimation of disease severity, whereas non-SMEs had higher rates of missed diagnoses (p = 0.01). Placental bands and myometrial abnormalities were challenging features for non-SME readers to report. SMEs maintained improved feature documentation despite concerns of perceived suboptimal image quality.
CONCLUSION: In a selected pathology-positive cesarean hysterectomy cohort, missed/under-classified PAS cases were driven by under reporting of key imaging features by non-SME radiologists, highlighting the need for targeted education and structured reporting. SMEs improve documentation of PAS features and may partially compensate for suboptimal image quality, underscoring the importance of access to expert review.

articles.title: Impact of Trauma and Obstetric Conditions on Postpartum Mental Health in Veterans.
articles.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
articles.authors: Barbano AC, Serier KN, Thomas JL et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the impact of obstetric conditions (gestational diabetes and gestational hypertension), childhood trauma exposure, and their interaction on postpartum mood and anxiety disorders (PMADs) among women veterans.
METHODS: A total of 922 women veterans with 1,747 unique pregnancies completed surveys between September 2018 and June 2019. Average marginal effects (AMEs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) derived from generalized linear mixed effects models with a binomial link function estimated the effects of obstetric conditions and childhood trauma on PMADs at the pregnancy level.
RESULTS: Almost half of participants (41.9%) reported PMADs after at least one pregnancy. Obstetric conditions and childhood trauma exposure were associated with a 13.8-percentage point (pp) (AME = .138; 95% CI [.065, .215]) and 16.7-pp (AME = .167; 95% CI [.106, .228]), respectively, greater probability of PMADs in covariate-adjusted analyses. There was a significantly stronger effect of obstetric conditions on the probability of PMADs in the presence of childhood trauma (ΔAME = .181; 95% CI [.041, .32]). Among trauma-exposed women veterans, a 1-point increase in total childhood trauma was associated with a 3.2-pp (AME = .032; 95% CI [.018, .055]) greater likelihood of PMADs.
CONCLUSIONS: Obstetric conditions and childhood trauma exposure are associated with a greater probability of PMADs for women veterans. Exposure to even single incidents of childhood trauma may increase risk for PMADs. Pregnant veterans should be screened for exposure to childhood trauma and closely monitored throughout the perinatal period for the emergence of mental health problems.

articles.title: Cardiac and natriuretic peptide profiles by subtype and sex in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
articles.authors: Choi HI, Moon S, Kim YT et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) encompasses heterogeneous metabolic phenotypes. We examined associations of MASLD subtypes with epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) thickness, left atrial volume index (LAVI), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and whether these associations differed by sex.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In a cross-sectional analysis of 6181 adults undergoing concurrent abdominal ultrasonography and transthoracic echocardiography, participants were classified as No MASLD, Lean MASLD, Obese MASLD without diabetes, or Obese MASLD with diabetes (2023 Delphi criteria). Multivariable linear regression and sex-stratified analyses were used. Obese subtypes had greater EAT thickness, with the largest contrast in those with diabetes (β = 0.030 cm; p < 0.001). EAT associations were two- to three-fold stronger in women. Lean MASLD was associated with lower LAVI (β = -2.06 mL/m2; p < 0.001), predominantly in men. NT-proBNP was 25-39% lower across MASLD subtypes (all p < 0.001), including lean disease, and inversely associated with metabolic burden. Sex interactions were significant for all outcomes. Partial R2 was 3.0% for log NT-proBNP and 0.6-1.0% for structural outcomes. Estimates in women were similar after menopause adjustment.
CONCLUSION: MASLD subtypes were associated with different EAT, LAVI, and NT-proBNP profiles, with differences by sex. Structural contrasts were modest, whereas the association with NT-proBNP was larger. The clinical significance of these findings requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Irritant Contact Dermatitis Related to Fecal and Urinary Incontinence in the Critical Care Population.
articles.journal: Critical care nursing clinics of North America
articles.ta: Crit Care Nurs Clin North Am
articles.authors: Hutton JL
articles.abstract: Irritant contact dermatitis due to fecal, urinary, or dual incontinence is a common but often under recognized complication in critically ill patients that contributes to pain, skin breakdown, infection, and pressure injury risk. Despite advances in understanding its prevention and management, practice remains variable. This article contrasts traditional and evidence-based approaches, reviewing terminology, risk factors, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and interventions. A practical critical care application of the Manage→Clean→Protect→Restore care bundle, adapted from the 2026 Wounds International Best Practice Update, is presented to support standardized, proactive incontinence skin care, and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Severe maternal and neonatal hyponatraemia following excessive oral fluid intake during labour.
articles.authors: De Preux M, Michel J, Roth LA et al.
articles.abstract: Peripartum hyponatraemia is an under-recognised but potentially serious complication of pregnancy. We report a primigravid woman at 41 weeks gestation who developed severe acute-on-chronic hypo-osmolar hyponatraemia (111 mmol/L; osmolality 256 mOsm/kg) after drinking approximately 6 L of water during labour, without synthetic oxytocin nor hypotonic intravenous fluids during labour. Early maternal neurological symptoms were initially misattributed to labour. The diagnosis was only recognised after the newborn had a generalised seizure 3 hours after birth and was found to have hyponatraemia (118 mmol/L; osmolality 243 mOsm/kg). After delivery, maternal rapid spontaneous natraemia correction because of water restriction required treatment with desmopressin and 5% dextrose to prevent overcorrection. Both mother and neonate recovered without neurological sequelae. This case highlights that excessive oral water intake alone may cause severe maternal and neonatal hyponatraemia, and underscores the importance of fluid balance monitoring, rapid electrolyte testing and coordinated multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: What are the contraception access experiences of newcomer youth in Canada? Results of a qualitative investigation.
articles.authors: Khan Z, Seiyad H, Jacob K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite contraception care being recognised as a basic human right, it remains out of reach for many youth in Canada. Our knowledge of youth experiences of contraception, particularly newcomer youth, who may encounter additional challenges, is limited. The ‘Ask Us’ study aims to address this gap by identifying the contraception access, experiences, beliefs, attitudes, knowledge and needs of youth in Canada. This paper presents our analysis of 48 interviews with newcomer youth who participated in the ‘Ask Us’ study.
DESIGN: A qualitative study guided by constructivist grounded theory.
SETTING: National, Canada.
PARTICIPANTS: We conducted one-to-one qualitative interviews with youth aged 15 to 25 years residing in Canada. We defined newcomer youth as individuals who were born outside Canada or have a foreign-born parent. Our study involved youth research assistants who recruited participants and conducted and analysed interviews with youth.
RESULTS: Our analysis identified that newcomer youth’s views towards contraception are influenced by abstinence-based early education and parents’ attitudes towards premarital sex. Their attitudes may shift over time with access to new information and encounters with peers from diverse backgrounds. However, the perceived judgement and shame associated with contraception use persist despite this shift and lead to newcomer youth seeking contraception options that require minimal interactions with healthcare providers. Learning from the lived experiences of peers helps newcomer youth assess the suitability of a contraception method. Newcomer youth trust peer learning and conducted self-directed research to validate their learning.
CONCLUSIONS: There is a need for resources that will provide newcomer youth with information about what it is like to obtain and use a particular contraception method and support their self-directed research on contraceptive options. Knowledge translation interventions may address the information gaps that we identified and empower newcomer youth to choose contraception methods that best fit their needs.

articles.title: Community-based seek, test and treat intervention to reduce Chlamydia trachomatis among Black youth in New Orleans, Louisiana: an implementation study protocol.
articles.authors: Kissinger PJ, Sagoe M, Kandregula AR et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chlamydia trachomatis (Ct) is the most commonly reported bacterial sexually transmitted infection (STI) in the USA with over 1.8 million cases each year. Ct can cause genital symptoms, pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility and can amplify HIV risk. African Americans (AAs) are seven times more likely than White Americans to be infected. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends screening sexually active women under 25 years of age and men in high prevalence populations, yet many young people are not screened. We hypothesise that screening AA youth in the community will reduce Ct rates in the community in a feasible and cost-effective manner.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This implementation study will test 2322 AA youth aged 15–26 years in Orleans Parish, Louisiana, for genital and pharyngeal Ct and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (GC), syphilis and HIV. Individuals who test positive for genital Ct, genital GC or pharyngeal Ct will be offered expedited index and partner treatment for themselves and up to five sexual partners. Those who test positive for HIV, syphilis or pharyngeal GC will be referred to partnering clinics for treatment. The study will include two visits: baseline for all and 3 month rescreening for those who tested positive for Ct or genital GC at baseline. Using Medicaid data, we will compare the rate of Ct among women in the intervention parish with those in control parishes over the study period. Secondary aims will examine feasibility of mailing home testing kits, uptake of partner treatment and cost-effectiveness. We will track how many participants accept testing, expedited treatment for themselves and their partners, peer referral and how much the programme costs using time motion analyses.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This protocol is approved by the Tulane University Institutional Review Board (2024-377 SPHTM). Informed consent and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) attestation will be obtained from participants. Findings will be presented at scientific conferences and published in peer-reviewed journals as well as disseminated to patients and study partners in communities of interest.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06428643.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of electrical stimulation for post-stroke urinary incontinence: a protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Zhang L, Li Q, Li L
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Post-stroke urinary incontinence (PSUI) is a debilitating complication that affects approximately 38% of stroke survivors. It is characterised by urinary frequency, urgency and incontinence, with detrusor overactivity or detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia acting as the primary underlying urodynamic abnormalities. This condition elevates the risk of urinary tract infections, pressure ulcers, and renal impairment, as well as contributing to patients’ psychological distress and thereby impairing their quality of life and increasing caregiver burden. Although electrical stimulation has emerged as a promising non-invasive alternative to neuromodulation, there is, as yet, no consensus concerning which modality is most effective for this purpose. This study thus aims to systematically compare the efficacy of different electrical stimulation types in cases of PSUI by conducting a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
METHOD AND ANALYSIS: The proposed research will be based on a systematic search of several major electronic databases from their inception to 15 October 2026; these main sources are PubMed, Web of Science, Embase and the Cochrane Library. Additional Chinese databases will also be searched, namely China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang databases (Wanfang), VIP Database (VIP) and the China Biomedical Literature Database (CBM). Relevant clinical trial registries, including ClinicalTrials.gov, the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), will also be searched, and grey literature sources and forward and backward citation searching will be added to ensure full coverage. The search will, however, be restricted to studies published in English or Chinese. The primary outcome assessed will be the number of urinary incontinence episodes over 24 hours, with secondary outcomes based on the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Urinary Incontinence Short Form (ICIQ-UI SF) scores and adverse events. Pairwise meta-analyses will be performed using Stata V.17.0. The network meta-analysis will involve Bayesian analysis using R V.4.3.1 with the gemtc package V.1.1-2 and JAGS V.4.3.2 as a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) engine to use MCMC methods to compare the relative efficacy of the different electrical stimulation modalities. A random-effects consistency model will be used throughout. Study screening, data extraction, risk of bias assessment and…

articles.title: First trimester exposure to hydroxychloroquine during pregnancy and major congenital malformations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Cournand E, Teboul A, Costedoat-Chalumeau N et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) use during the first trimester of pregnancy and the risk of major congenital malformations (MCMs).
METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL, clinical trials registers and specialised databases from inception to 9 July 2025. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and comparative observational studies. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk of Bias in Non-Randomised Studies of Interventions or Risk of Bias 2. Primary outcome was any MCM. Meta-analyses used fixed-effects and random-effects models (REM) based on adjusted or crude ORs.
RESULTS: From 4311 records, we included 20 studies (18 cohorts, 1 case-control and 1 RCT) including 4260 HCQ-exposed and 361 802 unexposed-pregnancies. The risk of bias was serious (n=4), critical (n=15) and ‘some concern’ (n=1, RCT). A significant association was found between HCQ and any MCM (OR=1.27, 95% CI (1.11 to 1.45) for REM, I2=0.0%, Tau2=0, n=19 studies). The pooled association based on adjusted OR was also statistically significant (aOR 1.29, 95% CI (1.09 to 1.53) for REM, I²=0.0%, Tau2=0, n=8). The certainty of evidence was low.
CONCLUSION: A slight association between HCQ exposure and MCM was observed, with low certainty of evidence. Given the well-established maternal/fetal benefits of HCQ in systemic lupus erythematosus, these results do not support changes in current clinical practice regarding its use during pregnancy. For other indications where alternatives exist, its use during pregnancy should be considered on a case-by-case basis.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420250609725.

articles.title: Loop electrosurgical excision procedure with or without intraoperative iodine: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
articles.authors: Hecken JM, Romich FA, Tempfer CB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix during loop electrosurgical excision procedure is commonly used to better define surgical resection margins. No randomized head-to-head comparison of loop electrosurgical excision procedure with vs without intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix is available to inform clinical practice.
OBJECTIVE: To compare loop electrosurgical excision procedure with versus without intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix regarding rates of involved resection margins, patient satisfaction and procedure-related outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: Consecutive women referred to a university colposcopy unit were recruited and randomized 1:1 to loop electrosurgical excision procedure with intraoperative application of Lugol's iodine or loop electrosurgical excision procedure without intraoperative Lugol's iodine (control). The primary endpoint was the histopathological rate of involved resection margins. Secondary endpoints included patient satisfaction assessed on the day of surgery and 14 days thereafter using numerical rating scales (0-10) and procedure-related complications, pain, blood loss, and surgeon-reported assessments. Results were compared using nonparametric, chi-square, and t tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the influence of covariates on the primary outcome.
RESULTS: Between January 2022 and September 2025, we randomized 229 women, 114 in the intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix arm and 115 in the control arm. In an intention-to-treat analysis, rates of involved resection margins were 20/114 (17.5%) vs 8/115 (7.0%) (risk difference, 10.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval 2.1 to 19.3; risk ratio, 2.52; 95% confidence interval 1.16 to 5.49; P=.014). Post hoc analysis of 215 women showed lower main-cone depth measured after fixation in the group with intraoperative Lugol's iodine staining of the cervix (transformation-zone-adjusted mean difference, -1.47 mm; 95% confidence interval, -2.61 mm to -0.34 mm; P=.011). There were no differences in operative metrics including cone weight, cone fragmentation, procedure time, and time to complete hemostasis. Intraoperative complications were similar in both groups as were surgeons' ratings. Immediate postoperative pain and satisfaction did not differ significantly between groups. At 14-day follow-up, bleeding outcomes favored the iodine group. Bleeding intensity during the first 24…

articles.title: Digital health interventions for managing menopausal symptoms: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Cheon J, Hwang S, Won J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal symptoms significantly impair women's quality of life, and conventional menopausal hormone therapy carries risks of clinical contraindications and adverse effects. Digital health interventions (DHIs) are gaining attention as a promising non-pharmacological alternative for sustained symptom management. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the clinical efficacy of DHIs for peri- and postmenopausal women.
METHODS: We searched 6 databases for eligible clinical studies from inception to May 2025. The methodological quality of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. For non-randomized studies, the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions and the National Institutes of Health Quality Assessment Tool were used. The certainty of evidence for outcomes reported by RCTs was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
RESULTS: A total of 8 studies involving 17,420 participants were included. DHIs utilized various mechanisms, including cognitive behavioral therapy, hypnotherapy, biofeedback-based pelvic floor muscle training, cognitive training, behavior change and self-care models, and personalized healthcare. Overall, DHIs were associated with improvements in vasomotor symptoms, psychological distress, pelvic floor dysfunction, and cognitive decline. However, there was high methodological heterogeneity and study design limitations; both RCTs were rated as having "some concerns" regarding risk of bias. According to the GRADE assessment, the certainty of evidence was low for Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) and very low for Midlife Women's Symptom Index (MSI).
CONCLUSION: DHIs demonstrate clinical potential as a non-pharmacological alternative for managing menopausal symptoms. Large-scale, well-designed RCTs with longer follow-up are needed. Trial registration/Protocol registration: PROSPERO (CRD420251042496).

articles.title: Group logotherapy for psychological well-being in infertile women: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Shokoohifard M, Alizadeh A, Bahramkhani M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infertility can adversely affect psychological well-being and impose substantial emotional and existential challenges on women undergoing infertility-related care. Psychological interventions that address meaning, responsibility, choice, and adaptation to difficult life circumstances may provide an additional approach to supporting psychological well-being. This study evaluated the effectiveness of group logotherapy in improving psychological well-being among infertile women.
METHODS: 68 infertile women were randomized to a group logotherapy intervention (n = 34) or a control group (n = 34). Eight participants discontinued participation after baseline and before attending any intervention session, including four participants from each group. Thus, 60 participants (30 per group) completed all three assessments and were included in the complete-case analysis. The intervention consisted of eight weekly group logotherapy sessions, including one face-to-face session followed by seven online sessions. Psychological well-being was assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and two months later using the 18-item Ryff Psychological Well-Being Scale. Repeated-measures analysis of variance was performed, with Greenhouse-Geisser correction when required. The group-by-time interaction was considered the primary test of differential change between groups. Bonferroni adjustment was applied to the six subscale interaction tests.
RESULTS: A significant group-by-time interaction was observed for overall psychological well-being, F(1.692,98.151) = 533.156, P < 0.001, partial η² = 0.902. Significant group-by-time interactions were also observed for self-acceptance, F(1.985,115.132) = 135.974, P < 0.001, partial η² = 0.701; environmental mastery, F(1.854,107.535) = 168.697, P < 0.001, partial η² = 0.744; personal growth, F(1.998,115.863) = 129.569, P < 0.001, partial η²= 0.691; and purpose in life, F(1.836,106.462) = 307.461, P < 0.001, partial η² = 0.841. No significant group-by-time interaction was observed for autonomy, F(1.894,109.881) = 2.490, P = 0.091, partial η² = 0.041, or positive relations, F(1.935,112.230) = 0.586, P = 0.553, partial η² = 0.010.
CONCLUSIONS: Group logotherapy was associated with significant improvements in overall psychological well-being and four of its six dimensions among infertile women. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting group logotherapy as a potentially useful psychological intervention in…

articles.title: Differential modulation of PPAR-γ and aromatase by pharmacotherapeutics in Danio rerio ovaries: Mechanistic insights for PCOS therapy.
articles.authors: Gnana Thiraviam AI, Shanmugam A, Sankarganesh D
articles.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a multifaceted reproductive endocrinopathy characterized by oligo/anovulation, cystic ovaries, and disrupted steroidogenesis. Inhibition of aromatase during steroidogenesis may be linked to dysregulation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ), which could lead to aberrant estradiol synthesis and contribute to PCOS pathophysiology. Therefore, we speculate that activation of PPAR-γ with propionic acid may, in part, help restore normal steroidogenesis. However, the expression levels of aromatase and PPAR-γ were not clearly understood with the currently used drugs (for PCOS) and propionic acid. Therefore, this study investigated ovarian expression of PPAR-γ and aromatase in zebrafish (Danio rerio) treated with various drugs (metformin, letrozole, clomiphene citrate, and the novel molecule, propionic acid) under normal conditions. Fifty female zebrafish were divided into five groups and treated with DMSO (control), metformin, letrozole, clomiphene citrate, and propionic acid for 14 days, followed by analysis of aromatase and PPAR-γ expression using RT-qPCR. Metformin treatment downregulated aromatase expression and upregulated PPAR-γ, whereas letrozole-mediated regulation of aromatase and PPAR-γ was reversed. Clomiphene citrate treatment upregulated both PPAR-γ and aromatase. Notably, propionic acid also upregulated both PPAR-γ and aromatase, suggesting a potential role as an ovarian microenvironment modulator. Further, molecular docking analysis of all compounds with PPAR-γ and aromatase revealed differential binding affinities, with metformin and propionic acid forming more hydrogen bonds than letrozole and clomiphene citrate. Collectively, these findings suggest that propionic acid may modulate ovarian steroidogenesis by regulating aromatase and PPAR-γ.

articles.title: Subcutaneous progesterone versus vaginal progesterone supplemented with intramuscular progesterone every third day in programmed vitrified-warmed blastocyst transfer cycles.
articles.authors: Mumusoglu S, Ince O, Erden M et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare ongoing pregnancy rates between subcutaneous progesterone and vaginal progesterone supplemented with intramuscular progesterone every third day in programmed frozen embryo transfer cycles.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SUBJECTS: Six hundred twenty patients undergoing their first vitrified-warmed blastocyst transfer with a programmed protocol at a single tertiary center between March 2018 and June 2023; no exclusion criteria were applied.
EXPOSURE: After 10-12 days of estradiol valerate 6 mg/day, 451 patients received subcutaneous progesterone 25 mg every 12 hours, and 169 patients received vaginal progesterone gel 90 mg every 12 hours supplemented with intramuscular progesterone 50 mg every third day (days 1, 4, and 7 of progesterone start). The regimens were used during sequential, nonoverlapping calendar periods.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ongoing pregnancy rate. Serum progesterone was measured on the fifth day of progesterone administration (one day before transfer), 4-5 hours after the morning dose. Associations between serum progesterone and ongoing pregnancy were evaluated using regimen-specific percentile categories and continuous modeling. Adjusted risk ratios were estimated using modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: Ongoing pregnancy rates were 53.6% vs. 54.4% in the subcutaneous and vaginal plus intramuscular groups, respectively (crude risk difference: -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -9.5-7.9). After covariate adjustment, standardized risks were 53.6% and 56.2%, respectively (adjusted risk difference: -2.6 percentage points; 95% CI: -12.0-6.7; adjusted risk ratio: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.81-1.13). Median serum progesterone was 23.48 ng/mL (interquartile range, 18.72-29.46) vs. 22.90 ng/mL (interquartile range, 18.50-29.40), respectively. Neither the percentile-based analyses nor continuous modeling identified a clear association between serum progesterone concentration and ongoing pregnancy within the observed ranges.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in ongoing pregnancy was observed between subcutaneous progesterone 25 mg every 12 hours and vaginal progesterone 90 mg every 12 hours supplemented with intramuscular progesterone 50 mg every third day. Serum progesterone distributions overlapped between groups. However, the study design and statistical imprecision preclude causal inference and conclusions of equivalence or noninferiority.

articles.title: Clinical study of a frameless indomethacin-containing copper intrauterine device combined with levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system in the treatment of adenomyosis.
articles.authors: Li T, Wei J, Shi J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety and therapeutic efficacy of LNG-IUS alone versus LNG-IUS combined with frameless anchoring copper intrauterine device (IUD) (with or without indomethacin) in treating adenomyosis, and to explore the role of indomethacin in improving outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective study was conducted on 91 adenomyosis patients at Zhengzhou First People's Hospital (January 2022-January 2025), divided into three groups: Group A received LNG-IUS monotherapy alone (n = 29); Group B was treated with LNG-IUS combined with GyneFix® (GyneFix IN), a drug-free frameless copper IUD without indomethacin (n = 30); Group C received LNG-IUS paired with Jenefox (Jinizhimei), an indomethacin-loaded frameless copper IUD (n = 32).Baseline data, adverse events (complete expulsion, downward displacement and Removal), and efficacy indicators (uterine volume, hemoglobin [HGB], pictorial blood loss assessment chart [PBAC] score, visual analogue scale [VAS] score) were monitored during 12 months of follow-up.
SETTING: Single tertiary hospital gynecology department affiliated to Xinxiang Medical College, Zhengzhou, China.
PATIENTS: Women aged 30-52 years with ultrasonically confirmed symptomatic diffuse adenomyosis without fertility demands were enrolled. All subjects declined hysterectomy and long-term systemic hormonal medication, and agreed to complete all scheduled follow-up examinations. Patients with congenital uterine malformations, submucous fibroids, recent pelvic inflammatory disease, coagulation disorders, severe uncontrolled systemic diseases, or malignant gynecologic lesions were excluded. A total of 91 patients were allocated into three groups by treatment preference: Group A (LNG-IUS alone, n=29), Group B (LNG-IUS + GyneFix®, n=30), Group C (LNG-IUS + Jenefox, n=32). Baseline demographic and clinical parameters were balanced across the three groups (all P>0.05).
INTERVENTIONS: Placement of standalone LNG-IUS, combined LNG-IUS with indomethacin-free frameless copper IUD, or combined LNG-IUS with indomethacin-containing frameless copper IUD under transabdominal ultrasound guidance. The LNG-IUS was ligated to the anchoring knot of frameless copper IUD to form a dual-device system, which was anchored into the uterine myometrium during insertion; diagnostic hysteroscopy was performed immediately after placement to inspect the uterine cavity in combined-device groups.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable among…

articles.title: Association between elevated donor-derived cell-free DNA and donor-specific antibodies in heart transplantation: Antibody-mediated rejection and long-term outcomes.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.authors: Oren D, Moeller CM, Fernández-Valledor A et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) and donor-specific antibodies (DSA) are both used for non-invasive surveillance after heart transplantation (HT). Whether DSA provides incremental value beyond dd-cfDNA for detecting antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) and predicting outcomes is uncertain.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study of adult HT recipients with paired dd-cfDNA and DSA results (September 2019 to December 2024), biopsies within 30 days of sampling were paired for analysis. Significant rejection was defined as acute cellular rejection (ACR) grade ≥2R and/or AMR (pAMR ≥1). Associations were modeled among biopsy-paired samples using patient-clustered generalized estimating equations, and mortality using time-dependent Cox and Bayesian joint models.
RESULTS: We analyzed 2,856 dd-cfDNA/DSA pairs from 287 recipients, of which 763 were biopsy-paired. Elevated dd-cfDNA was more frequent in DSA-positive samples (19.3% vs 10.5%; p = 0.006). Among biopsied samples, AMR was associated with DSA (OR 5.93, 95% CI 1.82-19.26) and elevated dd-cfDNA (OR 6.21, 95% CI 2.07-18.60). Relative to negative concordance, the risk of significant rejection was similar with isolated DSA-positivity (OR 3.83) and isolated dd-cfDNA-positivity (OR 3.80) and was highest with double-positivity (OR 15.70, 95% CI 4.71-52.30). Adding DSA with MFI ≥4,000 to dd-cfDNA increased the AUC for AMR from 0.73 to 0.84 (p = 0.03). Among 15 deaths, dd-cfDNA, but not DSA, was associated with mortality (HR 2.12, 95% CrI 1.24-3.39).
CONCLUSIONS: dd-cfDNA and DSA carried similar, additive information for rejection, with double-positivity identifying the highest-risk phenotype. In exploratory analyses, DSA at MFI ≥4,000 added to dd-cfDNA for AMR, and dd-cfDNA was the only marker associated with mortality.

articles.title: Sociocultural Disparities in Diabetic Complications Within Canada: A Longitudinal Cohort Study of 680,000 Women Followed After Pregnancy.
articles.authors: Shrestha G, Taleb N, Brousseau É et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of sociocultural status on the risk of diabetes and diabetic complications among women from a large Canadian province.
METHODS: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study of sociocultural disparities in diabetes and diabetic complications among 681,875 women from Quebec, Canada, with pregnancies between 2006 and 2023. We measured sociocultural disparities using linguistic status, comparing the anglophone minority of Quebec with the francophone majority. Outcomes included diabetic cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications that led to hospital admissions at any time during follow-up. We accounted for patient characteristics and used Cox regression models to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each diabetic complication, contrasting anglophones with francophones.
RESULTS: Compared with francophones, anglophones were 1.27 times more likely to develop diabetes in the long-term period after pregnancy (95% CI: 1.15 to 1.39). Anglophones were more likely to be admitted for diabetic cardiovascular (HR: 1.94, 95% CI: 1.45 to 2.60), renal (HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.10 to 1.89), and metabolic complications (HR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.13 to 1.99). Anglophones with gestational diabetes (HR: 1.75, 95% CI: 1.16 to 2.66) and pre-existing morbidity (HR: 2.17, 95% CI: 1.11 to 4.27) were particularly at risk of developing cardiovascular complications. Anglophones who were socioeconomically disadvantaged were also at risk of diabetic cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Sociocultural disparities in the development of diabetic complications are present in Quebec, Canada, with anglophone women having a greater risk of cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications than francophone women in the long term.

articles.title: Prevalence, Types, Complications, and Determinants of Female Genital Mutilation Among Girls in Port Sudan, Sudan: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Malik AA, Algiritly AA, Rahamtalla BM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female genital mutilation (FGM) remains a widespread harmful traditional practice in Sudan, particularly in the eastern states, despite sustained elimination efforts. It is associated with substantial physical, psychological, and reproductive health consequences and continues to be reinforced by sociocultural and intergenerational norms.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence, types, complications, and factors associated with FGM among girls in Port Sudan.
METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 768 girls aged 1 month to 16 years in Port Sudan, Red Sea State, Sudan. Participants were selected using systematic random sampling from healthcare facilities. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and standardized clinical examinations based on the World Health Organization classification of FGM. Laboratory investigations and ultrasonography were performed when clinically indicated. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 28. As a hospital-based sample, findings may not be fully generalizable to the general population.
RESULTS: Overall, 220 (28.6%) participants had undergone FGM, while circumcision was planned for 217 (28.3%). Type III FGM (infibulation) predominated (85.5%), with Type I accounting for 14.5%. Grandmothers were the principal decision-makers (32.6%), and traditional midwives performed most procedures (59.5%). Higher parental education was associated with lower FGM prevalence. Clinical examination revealed discrepancies between caregiver-reported and observed FGM types. Complications included urinary tract infections, genital abnormalities, delayed wound healing, prolonged recovery, and two neonatal deaths attributed to severe hemorrhage.
CONCLUSION: FGM remains common in Port Sudan, with Type III infibulation predominating and associating with substantial morbidity. Its persistence is driven by entrenched cultural norms and intergenerational influences despite emerging attitudinal changes among educated families. Comprehensive, culturally sensitive, multisectoral interventions are urgently needed to accelerate elimination.

articles.title: Agreement between home sperm testing and computer-assisted and manual semen analysis for motile sperm concentration.
articles.authors: Puangsricharoen P, Tuntiviriyapun P, Ngeamvijavat J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the agreement of motile sperm concentration (MSC) measurements obtained using the YO Home Sperm Test compared with manual semen analysis and computer-assisted semen analysis (CASA), and to assess its potential utility as a home-based screening tool for male fertility.
METHODS: Semen samples from 40 men were analyzed using three methods: the YO Home Sperm Test, manual semen analysis with a Makler counting chamber, and CASA using the Integrated Visual Optical System analyzer. Agreement between methods was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: The three testing methods showed significant correlations (p<0.01), with an overall ICC of 0.902. Pairwise ICCs were 0.815 (95% CI, 0.651 to 0.902) between manual semen analysis and the YO Home Sperm Test, 0.793 (95% CI, 0.608 to 0.890) between manual semen analysis and CASA, and 0.944 (95% CI, 0.894 to 0.970) between the YO Home Sperm Test and CASA. Agreement was strongest between the YO Home Sperm Test and CASA, supporting the reliability of the home-based device for measuring MSC.
CONCLUSION: The YO Home Sperm Test demonstrated good agreement with both manual semen analysis and CASA, particularly with CASA, supporting its potential use as a convenient, accessible, and private screening tool for the initial evaluation of male fertility. However, as a screening device rather than a comprehensive diagnostic test, abnormal findings should be confirmed by standard laboratory semen analysis. Further studies in larger populations and across different smartphone platforms are warranted.

articles.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
articles.authors: Lorusso D, Martin-Babau J, Backes F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
METHODS: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall…

articles.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.authors: Slomovitz BM, Zhu J, Yin R et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
METHODS: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71…

articles.title: Amyloid-mediated RNA uptake by sperm for embryonic delivery.
articles.authors: Mallen WS, Zabello N, Brenner-Morton S et al.
articles.abstract: Seminal fluid (SF) RNA is essential for embryonic development, but the mechanism by which extracellular RNA is transferred from SF to sperm remains unclear. Here, we identify a role for functional amyloid fibrils in SF that bind and traffic RNA to mammalian sperm and, upon fertilization, to the zygote. We show that highly cationic peptides in SF phase separate with RNA to form amyloid fibrils. Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET), volume electron microscopy (volume EM), and fluorescence live-cell imaging reveal that these amyloid fibrils are internalized by mammalian sperm. Furthermore, biophysical and in vitro fertilization (IVF) experiments show that amyloid-bound RNA reaches the zygote, where molecular chaperones can control RNA dissociation from amyloid fibrils. Our work uncovers a mechanism for RNA trafficking from SF to the zygote, establishing amyloid fibrils as potential tools for RNA delivery during fertilization.

articles.title: Prepregnancy Prediabetes and Large-for-Gestational-Age Birth Independent of Gestational Diabetes Among Asian Women.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Inamura T, Tano S, Fujito S et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Prediabetes may increase the likelihood of adverse perinatal outcomes, but evidence regarding prepregnancy prediabetes remains limited. This study examined its associations with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and the delivery of a large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infant.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included women who delivered at 12 obstetric facilities in Japan between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2024, and had undergone hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) measurement within 1 year before conception. The primary maternal and fetal outcomes were GDM and LGA birth, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate each outcome, with adjustment for maternal age, assisted reproductive technology, prepregnancy body mass index, and primiparity.
RESULTS: A total of 282 pregnancies were included, of which 19 (6.7%) were complicated by prepregnancy prediabetes. Prepregnancy prediabetes showed a more than twofold increase in the estimated odds of GDM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.15; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-8.66), although the association was not statistically significant. In contrast, it was significantly associated with the delivery of an LGA infant (aOR, 3.48; 95% CI, 1.14-10.66). After women who developed GDM were excluded, 262 women remained, including 16 (6.1%) with prepregnancy prediabetes. In this subgroup, prepregnancy prediabetes remained significantly associated with the delivery of an LGA infant (aOR, 3.49; 95% CI, 1.09-11.57).
CONCLUSION: Prepregnancy prediabetes was independently associated with higher odds of delivering an LGA infant among Asian women, including those without a diagnosis of GDM. These findings suggest that preconception dysglycemia may help identify women at increased risk of excessive fetal growth beyond GDM diagnosis and warrant further evaluation in larger studies.

articles.title: Midline Angle as a Predictor of Neonatal Orbital Compression During Forceps Delivery in Occiput Anterior Presentations.
articles.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
articles.authors: Sayama S, Seyama T, Iriyama T et al.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the association between intrapartum transperineal ultrasonography findings obtained before forceps delivery and neonatal periorbital compression marks in occiput anterior presentations.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 166 term singleton forceps deliveries performed at the University of Tokyo Hospital between January 2019 and December 2022. Pregnancies with a non-cephalic presentation, congenital anomalies, or occiput posterior or transverse positions were excluded. Maternal and neonatal characteristics, together with intrapartum transperineal ultrasound findings, including the angle of progression and the midline angle retrospectively measured from ultrasound images acquired immediately before forceps delivery, were compared between neonates with periorbital forceps compression marks and those without compression marks. All neonates in the compression mark group underwent ophthalmologic evaluation.
RESULTS: The median midline angle was significantly greater in the compression mark group than in the control group (22.0° vs. 13.0°, p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between the two groups in maternal or neonatal characteristics or in the angle of progression. The cutoff value of 22° yielded a sensitivity of 47.8% and a specificity of 90.9% for predicting forceps-related compression marks. Nine of the 67 neonates with compression marks had confirmed ophthalmic findings: retinal hemorrhage (n = 1), corneal epithelial injury (n = 2), and subconjunctival hemorrhage (n = 6). All findings resolved spontaneously without intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: A midline angle of > 22° was associated with an increased likelihood of periorbital compression during forceps delivery in occiput anterior presentations. Midline angle assessment may be a useful adjunctive parameter for assessing the risk of periorbital compression marks.

articles.title: Cerebral palsy and intrapartum hypoxia: current evidence and the position of Korean Society for Maternal Fetal Medicine.
articles.authors: Ko HS, Oh SY, Choi CW et al.
articles.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) has long been associated with intrapartum hypoxia; however, contemporary evidence indicates that acute hypoxic-ischemic events during labor account for only a minority of cases. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and causation assessment of CP, focusing on the limitations of electronic fetal monitoring, umbilical cord pH, low Apgar scores, and cesarean delivery as predictors or preventive measures for CP. Prematurity, intrauterine infection and inflammation, placental pathology, perinatal arterial ischemic stroke, and genetic factors are important associated factors or contributory pathways in CP, although their population-attributable contributions remain uncertain.
