Recent genomic studies have identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in approximately one-quarter to one-third of affected children, challenging the traditional assumption that unexplained CP is attributable to intrapartum events. Current evidence indicates that isolated fetal heart rate abnormalities, acidemia, or neonatal encephalopathy alone are insufficient to establish intrapartum hypoxia as the cause of CP. The Korean Society for Maternal Fetal Medicine emphasizes that causation assessments should rely on strict criteria, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and integrated interpretation of antenatal, intrapartum, neonatal, neuroimaging, placental, and genetic findings. A multifactorial and evidence-based approach is essential for rational clinical assessment, appropriate counseling, and avoidance of unnecessary defensive obstetric practices.

articles.title: Incretin-based therapies in menopause: Current landscape.
articles.authors: Castaneda R, Pavlov K, Shufelt CL et al.
articles.abstract: The menopause transition is associated with substantial changes in body composition, including increased central adiposity and accelerated loss of muscle and bone mass, that heighten midlife women's risk of obesity and its cardiometabolic consequences. Incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide, have emerged as highly effective pharmacotherapies for obesity, and post hoc analyses of pivotal trials suggest that weight-loss efficacy is preserved across reproductive stages, with postmenopausal women achieving reductions in total body weight, waist circumference, and cardiometabolic risk factors comparable to those of premenopausal women. However, the same pharmacologically induced weight loss that drives these benefits raises concern for postmenopausal women, who already experience declines in muscle and bone related to estrogen deficiency that may be exacerbated by weight loss. Current evidence suggests that reductions in lean mass are generally proportional to the magnitude of weight loss but are often accompanied by improved patient-reported physical function. However, lean mass is not synonymous with skeletal muscle function, few trials have assessed muscle strength or objective physical performance as primary outcomes, and findings on bone mineral density and fracture risk remain inconsistent across studies. This review synthesizes current evidence on the use of incretin-based therapies by midlife and postmenopausal women. It specifically addresses weight-loss efficacy, cardiometabolic risk reduction, body composition, and skeletal health, while distinguishing menopause-specific from extrapolated evidence, and indicating the level of evidence supporting clinical considerations for nutrition, exercise, and musculoskeletal monitoring, to guide a menopause-specific approach to incretin-based therapies.

articles.title: Circadian syndrome as a multisystem risk factor for pain in older adults: Evidence from a cross-sectional and longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Zeng S, Peng X, Chen X et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circadian syndrome and pain are prevalent in aging populations, yet their relationship remains underexplored. This study investigates the cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between circadian syndrome and pain among older adults.
METHODS: Data were drawn from three prospective cohorts: the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, the English Longitudinal Study of Aging, and the US Health and Retirement Study. Pain severity was self-reported as mild, moderate, or severe. Multivariable logistic regression assessed cross-sectional associations, while generalized linear mixed models examined longitudinal relationships between baseline circadian syndrome and incident pain during follow-up. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to confirm the reliability of the findings.
RESULTS: At baseline, 18,719 participants were included, comprising 7219 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, 6063 from the English Longitudinal Study of Aging, and 5437 from the Health and Retirement Study. Cross-sectionally, individuals with circadian syndrome had significantly higher odds of prevalent pain than those without: the odds ratios were 1.68 (95% confidence interval 1.51-1.88) in the Chinese cohort, 2.24 (95% confidence interval 1.95-2.58) in the English cohort, and 1.71 (95% confidence interval 1.52-1.93) in the US cohort, suggesting a positive association between circadian syndrome and prevalent pain. In longitudinal analyses, baseline circadian syndrome predicted an increased risk of new-onset pain, with odds ratios of 1.26 (95% confidence interval 1.11-1.44) in the Chinese cohort, 1.62 (95% confidence interval 1.26-2.09) in the English cohort, and 1.22 (95% confidence interval 1.05-1.42) in the US cohort, providing stronger evidence for prospective prediction. Results remained robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: This large-scale multinational study establishes circadian syndrome as a significant correlate of both prevalent and incident pain in older adults, highlighting the importance of multisystem circadian health in pain risk assessment.

articles.title: Trends in utilization of cervical cancer screening and screening-associated services in a multi-organizational research network in Chicago, Illinois, US.
articles.authors: Holt HK, Ma W, Gordon HS et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chicago has a high degree of care fragmentation, with multiple large health systems and numerous safety-net systems. Fragmentation may be why the west and south areas of Chicago have high incidences of cervical cancer despite high self-reported screening rates. This study assesses utilization of cervical cancer screening-associated tests and procedures across seven health systems in Chicago between 2012 and 2022.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included females aged 15+ years enrolled in one or more health systems in the CAPriCORN network. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, geolocation, linear mixed-effects model, and Poisson regression. Proportions and trends in utilization by year of test modalities (cytology alone, cytology and human papillomavirus (HPV) test [cotest], HPV test alone, colposcopy, and cervical procedures [cone biopsy, loop electrosurgical excision procedure, and ablation]) were calculated and stratified by Chicago's six geographic zones. The time between screening utilization was compared by age, Chicago zone, and change in health system.
RESULTS: Of 1.20 million in the study cohort, 53.6% had only 1 screening test during the 11-year study period; 22.9% had 2 tests, and 22.9% had 3 or more. Individuals in Chicago who changed health systems between two consecutive screening tests had a longer median interval between tests compared with those who did not change (34 versus 15.4 months).
CONCLUSIONS: Over half of the cohort only had one screening test and may be underscreened. Switching health systems more than doubled the time interval between screening tests compared with patients who remained in the same system.

articles.title: Development and implementation of a transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation protocol for pediatric overactive bladder: A quality improvement initiative.
articles.authors: Gasiorek MA, Kieran K, Merguerian PA et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) is an established therapy for overactive bladder (OAB) that had not previously been offered in our pediatric urology clinic. We implemented TENS as an alternative second-line option for OAB refractory to standard urotherapy. Our objective was to develop a standardized protocol for TENS prescription and to increase advanced practice provider (APP) understanding and confidence with prescribing this therapy.
METHODS: Our quality improvement initiative was designed, conducted, and reported in accordance with the Standards for Quality Improvement Reporting Excellence (SQUIRE 2.0) guidelines. It consisted of two Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles: (1) protocol and resource development with small-scale testing involving two nurses and two APPs under physician oversight, and (2) broader protocol implementation through structured APP training. The primary outcome measures were APP understanding and confidence with prescribing TENS therapy, assessed via a survey administered before, immediately after, and 3 months following training. Our process measure was the number of TENS prescriptions following protocol implementation.
RESULTS: We developed a standardized protocol for TENS therapy in patients with OAB refractory to urotherapy, outlining inclusion and exclusion criteria, device specifications and settings, a multi-step evaluation schedule, and patient and provider resources. The protocol was implemented across seven clinical sites through an APP training webinar. Prior to implementation, 50% (5/10) of APPs were familiar with TENS as a treatment option for OAB, 10% (1/10) felt confident prescribing it, and 0% (0/10) felt confident managing it. Following implementation and at 3 months, 100% (10/10) of APPs reported understanding and confidence with prescribing TENS, and by 3 months, 100% (10/10) reported confidence with managing the therapy. Over the subsequent 5 months, 11 patients were initiated on TENS.
CONCLUSIONS: We successfully developed and implemented a standardized TENS protocol, leading to increased APP understanding and confidence in prescribing this therapy for patients with refractory OAB across multiple clinical sites.

articles.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of ferroptosis-related programs in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma.
articles.authors: Fu F, Zhang D, Zhuang S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) shows marked molecular and microenvironmental heterogeneity. How ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) relate to immune and metabolic states across bulk tumors and single cells is incompletely defined.
METHODS: We analyzed TCGA-OV RNA-seq data from 421 patients (419 evaluable for survival) using a curated 25-gene FRG panel, assessing expression, co-expression, survival, and immune/checkpoint associations. Single-cell data from GSE300897 (nine treatment-naive HGSOC donors; 16,939 cells after QC) scored FRG and pathway activity across nine subtypes and compared chemo-refractory versus chemo-sensitive tumors by donor-level pseudobulk analysis.
RESULTS: FTL, FTH1, RPL8, and LDHA were among the most highly expressed FRGs; inter-gene coordination was modest. The aggregate FRG score was not prognostic (log-rank p = 0.80; AUCs 0.52, 0.54, 0.46 at 1, 3, 5 years) but correlated with cytotoxic, CD8 T-cell, macrophage, and Treg signatures. At single-cell resolution, the FRG score was highest in myeloid cells, with enriched iron-metabolism gene expression. Refractory tumors showed higher myeloid and lower fibroblast/plasma-cell fractions, and malignant cells showed directional increases in GLS, CS, and TFRC with decreases in SLC7A11, HMOX1, and GPX4 (none surviving correction). The FRG score showed reproducible positive coupling with hypoxia, glycolysis, and NF-κB programs across platforms. qRT-PCR confirmed higher FTH1, FTL, GPX4, and SLC7A11 in SKOV3 and OVCAR3 versus IOSE80 cells.
CONCLUSIONS: Ferroptosis-related transcriptional programs in HGSOC are cell-type dependent and associate with immune infiltration and selected inflammatory/metabolic states, without independent prognostic value. These findings nominate myeloid iron-handling and antioxidant shifts in malignant cells as testable hypotheses for future validation.

articles.title: Prevalence and temporal trends of exposure to anti-obesity medications during preconception and pregnancy in a nationwide US claims database, 2018-2023.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
articles.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
articles.authors: Haynie C, Musty A, Choi H et al.
articles.abstract: Use of anti-obesity medications (AOMs) has increased among women of reproductive age, raising concerns about inadvertent fetal exposure. Using a retrospective cohort of approximately 2 million pregnancies identified in commercial claims data from the MarketScan database, this study investigated the prevalence and temporal trends of perinatal exposure to Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved AOMs from 2018 to 2023. Overall, 0.32% (n = 6179) of pregnancies were exposed to AOMs. Prevalence was highest among women aged > 40 years (1.1%) and those with pre-pregnancy obesity or type 2 diabetes (1.4% and 1.2%, respectively). Overall exposure increased modestly from 2018 to 2022, followed by a marked rise between 2022 (0.31%) and 2023 (0.58%). Prior to 2023, most exposures involved phentermine; in 2023, semaglutide accounted for the highest prevalence. The results highlight the need for further research to evaluate maternal and fetal outcomes associated with AOM exposure.

articles.title: TFAP2A-driven PTK6 promotes endometrial cancer progression through activation of the MEK/ERK signaling pathway.
articles.authors: Zhu A, Rao Y, Xia Q et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial cancer is an immune-responsive gynecological malignancy, but biomarkers linking oncogenic signaling with the tumor immune microenvironment remain limited. Protein tyrosine kinase 6 (PTK6), a non-receptor tyrosine kinase involved in tumor progression, remains insufficiently defined in endometrial cancer.
METHODS: Public transcriptomic and proteomic datasets were analyzed to evaluate PTK6 expression, prognosis, and pathway enrichment. Exploratory transcriptomic analyses examined associations between PTK6 expression and immune-related features. PTK6 protein expression was validated in clinical specimens by western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were performed to assess PTK6-mediated effects on cell proliferation, migration, and EMT-associated marker expression in vitro, and on subcutaneous xenograft tumor growth in vivo. The relationship between PTK6 and MEK/ERK signaling was examined by enrichment analysis, western blotting, and pharmacological inhibition. TFAP2A-mediated transcriptional regulation of PTK6 was investigated using JASPAR prediction, qRT-PCR, western blotting, and dual-luciferase reporter assays.
RESULTS: PTK6 was significantly upregulated in endometrial cancer and associated with poor overall survival. PTK6 knockdown inhibited cell proliferation and migration and altered EMT-associated marker expression in vitro. Subcutaneous xenograft experiments showed that PTK6 knockdown reduced tumor growth, whereas PTK6 overexpression enhanced tumor growth. PTK6 expression was associated with RAS/MEK/ERK pathway activation, and PTK6 inhibition reduced cell viability, migration, and MEK/ERK phosphorylation. Exploratory analyses of public transcriptomic datasets revealed associations between PTK6 expression and immune-related signatures. TFAP2A transcriptionally activated PTK6 and enhanced PTK6-driven tumor-promoting effects.
CONCLUSION: PTK6 promotes EC cell proliferation and migration in vitro and subcutaneous tumor growth in vivo. The findings implicate the TFAP2A/PTK6/MEK/ERK axis in EC progression and suggest PTK6 as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Progestin-only contraceptive use is associated with reduced sociosexual behavior of female zoo-housed bonobos (Pan paniscus).
articles.authors: Torfs JRR, Fodderie Z, Guéry JP et al.
articles.abstract: In female primates, sexual activity is modulated by the balance between progestins and estrogens and typically peaks around ovulation, when estrogens peak and the female is fertile. Yet, in many species, sexual activity also occurs outside the fertile phase and during pregnancy, raising questions about the hormonal mechanisms underlying non-reproductive sexual behavior. Bonobos (Pan paniscus) provide a valuable model for addressing this question, as females frequently engage in sexual interactions for social bonding, rather than reproduction. In zoo-housed populations, females often receive contraceptives with various hormonal compositions, including combined estrogen-progestin contraceptive and progestin-only formulations. This variation offers an interesting framework to investigate how ovarian hormones influence sociosexual behavior. We analyzed behavioral observations from 40 adult females across seven zoos and found that individuals receiving a progestin-only contraceptive exhibited significantly lower frequencies of sociosexual behavior compared to females receiving combined contraceptives or no contraception. Longitudinal data from 5 females further supported this pattern: sociosexual behavior substantially increased in females switching from progestin-only to combined contraception, nearly tripling their rates. Together, these findings show that the balance between estrogens and progestins modulates non-reproductive sexual activity in female primates, with important implications for understanding the impact of contraceptive use on social dynamics in managed populations.

articles.title: Blood lactate concentrations are associated with markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Pearson RC, Hamilton DP, Broskey NT et al.
articles.abstract: The ability to detect metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy can impact the health of mother and infant(s). Lactate may serve as a biomarker to predict metabolic dysfunction risk. The purpose of this study was to determine if fasting or postprandial blood lactate concentrations were related to established markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy. Overnight fasted healthy women between 32 and 38 wk of gestation underwent a high-fat meal test. Fasted and postprandial (1, 2, and 4 h) venous blood glucose, insulin, and lactate were collected. Fasted and postprandial (2 and 4 h) respiratory exchange ratios (RERs) were assessed by indirect calorimetry. Homeostatic model assessment-insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and Matsuda indexes were calculated. Participants were categorized into lean (18.5-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), or obese (≥30.0 kg/m2) based on prepregnancy body mass index. To determine the impact that weight status may have on postprandial lactate concentrations, a repeated-measures analysis of variance was performed on log-transformed data. Spearman's rank-order correlation coefficients were used to assess associations between outcome variables. Fifty-two participants were included in the analysis (lean, n = 29; overweight, n = 11; obese, n = 12). Postprandial lactate was higher in women with obesity compared with women who were lean (1 h, P = 0.024; 2 h, P = 0.025; 4 h, P = 0.010). Among all women, higher lactate area under the curve (AUC) was associated with higher insulin AUC, higher HOMA-IR index, lower Matsuda index, and higher RER AUC (P ≤ 0.003). These findings suggest that postprandially elevated lactate may serve as a useful biomarker for identifying metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Postprandial lactate concentrations were higher in late pregnancy among patients with obesity. Other markers of metabolic dysfunction, including insulin concentrations, HOMA-IR, Matsuda index, and respiratory exchange ratio, were also associated with postprandial lactate concentrations. Postprandial lactate may be a clinically useful biomarker for metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy.

articles.title: Automation of sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, and vitrification in IVF: insights from a proof-of-concept study.
articles.authors: Chavez-Badiola A, Valadez Aguilar A, Mendizabal-Ruiz G et al.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Can key embryological procedures, including sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, and blastocyst vitrification, be automated?
SUMMARY ANSWER: Individual automated systems enabling sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, and embryo vitrification demonstrated feasibility in a small proof-of-concept study.
WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Automated systems for specific IVF procedures have shown promise, with recent reports of successful births following automated gamete isolation and ICSI.
STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: Prospective proof-of-concept study evaluating five automated systems nicknamed 'Pearls'. Each system automated one of the following procedures: sperm preparation via swim-up (Pearl 1-SU); sperm preparation by a dish-based approach called horizontal swim-out (Pearl 1-HSO), oocyte retrieval, and denudation (Pearl 2); sperm selection and laser immobilization and piezo-ICSI (Pearl 3); and blastocyst vitrification (Pearl 5). The study enrolled patients undergoing treatment at Hope IVF, Guadalajara, Mexico, between October 2023 and October 2024, with data collection on pregnancy outcomes being completed in October 2025.
PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: Thirty-two patients or oocyte donors each underwent a single egg retrieval following minimal or mild ovarian stimulation. One patient was excluded from the study due to poor ovarian response. Oocytes were prospectively allocated to treatment with a single automated system: Pearl 1-SU (n = 20), Pearl 1-HSO (n = 37), Pearl 2 (n = 34), Pearl 3 (n = 57), with sibling oocytes treated manually per standard protocol. In the case of the automated vitrification system (Pearl 5), sibling blastocysts produced following manual ICSI were assigned to either manual or automated (n = 10) vitrification.
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: Pearl 1-SU and Pearl 1-HSO automated sperm preparation systems achieved fertilization rates of 90% (18/20) and 73% (27/37), and sibling oocytes injected with manually prepared sperm achieved 60% (6/10) and 75% (18/24) fertilization. Usable blastocyst rates were 55.5% (10/18) and 70.4% (19/27) for the automated systems, and 50% (3/6) and 66.7% (12/18) for manual preparation. Pearl 2 automated oocyte retrieval and denudation resulted in a fertilization rate of 79.4% (27/34) and a usable blastocyst rate of 48.1% (13/27); manual procedures achieved 66.7% (26/39) and 76.9% (20/26) fertilization and blastocyst formation rates,…

articles.title: Longitudinal analysis of skeletal muscle and cardiometabolic risk during the menopause transition.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Cabre HE, Falkenhain K, Smith SR et al.
articles.abstract: We assessed longitudinal changes in body composition and cardiometabolic risk in women with normal weight and women with overweight/obesity across the menopausal transition. We examined a 10-yr longitudinal analysis of 81 healthy women in the prospective Healthy Transitions cohort. Body composition measures were obtained via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Skeletal muscle was estimated using a validated prediction model: 1.12 × appendicular lean mass - 0.63. Serum sex steroid hormones and cardiometabolic factors were quantified in fasting blood. Participants were stratified by body mass index (BMI) into normal weight (n = 41) and overweight/obesity (n = 40) groups. Changes within and between BMI groups across the menopause transition were assessed with linear mixed models. At menopause onset, compared with those with normal weight, participants with overweight/obesity had lower sex hormone-binding globulin (-30.9 ± 10.3 nmol/L; P = 0.01), greater percent body fat (13.1 ± 1.3%; P < 0.001), greater skeletal muscle mass (2.5 ± 0.6 kg; P < 0.001), and worse cardiometabolic risk factors (P < 0.001). In the 5 years before menopause, participants with overweight/obesity gained skeletal muscle (+1.2 kg) and fat mass (+3.5 kg), whereas participants with normal weight increased percent body fat (+1.5%) only. At menopause onset, women with overweight/obesity exhibit distinct alterations in body composition, hormonal profiles, and cardiometabolic risk that exist in the years preceding menopause, highlighting the importance of early, targeted interventions to mitigate adverse health trajectories during the menopause transition.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study provides novel longitudinal evidence of changes in sex hormones, body composition, and cardiometabolic risk across 10 years of the menopause transition. By distinguishing skeletal muscle from lean mass and separating the sample by BMI, this work offers new insight into changes in skeletal muscle mass, adiposity, and metabolism during menopause. We show that independent of BMI, skeletal muscle mass remains stable when accounting for aging and lifestyle factors, despite hormonal shifts.

articles.title: Part 2: Impact of cardiovascular disease and health disparities in the obstetric population.
articles.authors: Takla TN, Mele M, Mulligan LJ
articles.abstract: Pregnant individuals represent a uniquely vulnerable population, as the physiological demands of pregnancy can unmask or worsen underlying conditions while simultaneously influencing fetal development. Building on prior discussions of cardiovascular adaptation during pregnancy, this review examines maternal and fetal health through a public health lens, emphasizing how social determinants of health shape obstetric outcomes. Although normal cardiovascular changes promote fetal growth, these shifts can exacerbate undiagnosed or poorly controlled conditions, leading to higher rates of complications. Research consistently shows that these negative outcomes are not equitably distributed. Significant disparities exist across racial and ethnic groups, reflected in metrics such as preterm birth, maternal morbidity, and cardiovascular complications. African American, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, and American Indian or Alaska Native populations experience markedly higher rates of adverse outcomes compared with White counterparts. These patterns reflect broader structural factors, including inequities in housing, access to care, environmental exposures, and socioeconomic status. Structural racism further compounds these disparities by influencing health behaviors, community resources, and clinical interactions. Understanding these themes provides essential context for addressing maternal health inequities. Through improved recognition of social determinants, clinicians and policymakers can implement targeted strategies aimed at prevention, early intervention, and equitable care delivery. The insights summarized here support efforts to reduce the disproportionate health burden borne by underserved communities and highlight the need for systemic change to protect maternal and child health.

articles.title: Osteopontin contributes to uterine artery dysfunction during chronic hypertensive pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.authors: Lave ML, Jones J, Patterson VS et al.
articles.abstract: Successful pregnancy requires maternal cardiovascular adaptation, including expansion and remodeling of the uterine arteries, to accommodate a progressive rise in uteroplacental blood flow. Chronic maternal hypertension is associated with impaired uterine artery adaptation and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including fetal growth restriction, yet the mechanisms driving these vascular changes remain incompletely understood. Osteopontin, a matricellular protein implicated in vascular pathology in hypertension, is a potential mediator of impaired uterine artery adaptation during pregnancy. In this study, we compared uterine artery remodeling in pregnant normotensive Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats and spontaneously hypertensive stroke-prone rats (SHRSP), a model of chronic hypertension. To investigate the contribution of osteopontin, we characterized an osteopontin-deficient SHRSP strain. Uterine artery hemodynamics were assessed by Doppler ultrasound, arterial structure was evaluated by histology, and molecular profiles were characterized by RNA sequencing. Fetal weight and length were measured at mid- and late gestation. We found that, compared with WKY, SHRSP fetuses were smaller and uterine arteries exhibited inward hypertrophic remodeling, including increased wall thickness, reduced lumen area, and an elevated resistance index. SHRSP uterine arteries also showed enrichment of pathways related to inflammation and vascular pathology. Among the most highly upregulated genes was Spp1, which encodes osteopontin. Compared with control SHRSP, osteopontin-deficient SHRSP had larger uterine artery lumen areas, lower resistance indices, and reduced expression of select inflammation-associated genes. Fetal growth trajectories were also improved. These findings identify osteopontin as a contributor to uterine artery dysfunction in chronic hypertensive pregnancy and demonstrate that osteopontin deficiency improves vascular adaptation and fetal growth.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study characterizes uterine artery dysfunction in a rat model of chronic maternal hypertension and identifies inflammation-related and matrix remodeling pathways associated with vascular pathology. We further demonstrate that osteopontin contributes to uterine artery dysfunction and introduce a novel osteopontin-deficient hypertensive rat model that exhibits improved uterine artery adaptation and fetal growth trajectory despite persistent maternal hypertension.

articles.title: Cell-free genome analysis reveals pathophysiological response to hypoxia at high altitude.
articles.authors: Choudhary R, Ali M, G KK et al.
articles.abstract: Extreme physiological stress induced by hypobaric hypoxia at high altitude (HA) alters nucleosome organization across the genome, affecting multiple tissues and cell types. Investigating hypoxic responses is essential to understand inter-individual differences in susceptibility, their impact on vital organs, underlying epigenetic modifications, and the clinical consequences of compromised oxygen delivery. Remarkably, the fragmentation pattern of cell-free (cf) DNA in high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE), a life-threatening, non-cardiogenic form of pulmonary edema that occurs in susceptible individuals traveling to altitudes >2500m asl, can identify disease-specific changes in nucleosome positioning attributable to hypoxia-induced gene activation or repression. The present case-control study profiled cfDNA fragmentation patterns in 42 healthy HA acclimatized sojourners designated as controls and HAPE patients, further subdivided into mild (n=40), moderate (n=40), and severe (n=37) categories. The windowed protection score employed for tissue deconvolution analysis showed a greater contribution of cfDNA fragments from immune cells, the adrenal gland, spleen, pancreas, liver, and the esophageal muscularis mucosa in HAPE, indicating the systemic impact of the disease, even though its main symptoms are localized in the lungs. In addition, severe HAPE patients exhibited tissue contributions from lung fibroblasts, renal epithelium, and thyroid tissue, suggesting extensive tissue damage in these patients. The positive correlations of cfDNA concentration, peripheral oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and pulse rate with tissue-specific fragmentation scores enhanced the translational value of the study. Furthermore, motif enrichment analysis, using HAPE-specific open chromatin regions and their integration with in-house RNA-seq data, revealed significant enrichment of oxygen-sensing, inflammatory, and immune-signaling pathways in HAPE.

articles.title: Beyond estrogen: aging and declining cardiac autonomic modulation are linked to longer QTc after menopause.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.ta: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
articles.authors: Kinaani F, Hadad O, Critz N et al.
articles.abstract: Women are more susceptible than men to QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias, yet how aging and cardiac autonomic control jointly affect the heart rate-corrected QT interval (QTc) in women, independent of fluctuating sex hormones, remains unclear. We hypothesized that QTc is longer in postmenopausal women than in young women, and that this difference reflects aging and age-related changes in cardiac autonomic control rather than sex-hormone levels. We studied 64 healthy menstruating women (median age 29.5 yr) in the early follicular phase, when estrogen and progesterone are low, and 35 healthy postmenopausal women (median age 67 yr). This design minimized acute hormonal differences. QT intervals and heart rate variability (HRV; power spectral analysis) were measured. QT, QTc, and corrected JT interval (JTc), the latter reflecting ventricular repolarization, were longer in postmenopausal women (P < 0.001; η2 ≥ 0.14). Postmenopausal women also had lower ln-transformed total power (P < 0.001), low frequency (LF) power (P = 0.006; η2 = 0.09), and high frequency (HF) power (P < 0.001; η2 = 0.17), and a higher LF/HF ratio (P < 0.001; η2 = 0.16). In postmenopausal women, QTc correlated modestly and negatively with total power and LF power (both P values = 0.02), but not in young women. Because acute hormonal differences were minimized, the longer QTc after menopause is more consistent with aging and reduced cardiac autonomic modulation than with the prevailing sex-hormone milieu. These findings suggest that age-related autonomic decline, together with a higher LF/HF ratio, may contribute to QT vulnerability in postmenopausal women, with implications for arrhythmic risk assessment and QT-prolonging drug prescription.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Studying young women in the low-hormone early follicular phase minimized acute sex-hormone differences. Postmenopausal women had longer QTc intervals and lower heart rate variability, and only in them was lower heart rate variability associated with longer QTc. These findings suggest that aging and the accompanying reduction in cardiac autonomic modulation, rather than acute hormone levels, may contribute to the longer QTc after menopause, with implications for arrhythmic risk and QT-prolonging drug use in postmenopausal women.

articles.title: Obesity and Cancer Risk in Young Adults in Korea : A Nationwide Health Screening Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Yun JS, Mun H, Jung JH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity and early-onset cancer are both increasing among young adults, yet evidence remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To assess associations between obesity and early-onset cancer risk in young adults.
DESIGN: Nationwide population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Korean National Health Insurance Service database, 2009 to 2021.
PATIENTS: 6 313 338 adults aged 20 to 39 years without prior cancer, from a national health screening program.
MEASUREMENTS: Body mass index (BMI) was categorized into 5 groups (underweight to class II obesity) according to Asian-specific criteria. The outcome was incident cancer.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 11.2 years, 151 893 cancer cases occurred. Ten-year cumulative incidence ranged from 1.84% (95% CI, 1.83% to 1.86%) in the normal-weight group to 2.24% (CI, 2.22% to 2.27%) in class I obesity and 2.62% (CI, 2.56% to 2.68%) in class II obesity, with absolute risk differences of 0.40% (CI, 0.39% to 0.41%) and 0.78% (CI, 0.73% to 0.82%). The relative association was more pronounced in men, and absolute risk differences were greater in women. In combined BMI-waist circumference analyses, people with class I obesity based on BMI and with abdominal obesity had higher 10-year cumulative incidence (2.45% [CI, 2.41% to 2.50%]) than those without abdominal obesity (2.13% [CI, 2.10% to 2.16%]), exceeding that of those with class II obesity without abdominal obesity (2.20% [CI, 2.03% to 2.36%]). The highest cumulative incidence was observed for thyroid, endometrial, and ovarian cancer. Obesity was not associated with higher risk for breast cancer diagnosed by age 50 years.
LIMITATIONS: Observational design; nonrepresentative sample limited to screening participants; and unmeasured confounding, including smoking burden.
CONCLUSION: Obesity in young Korean adults, measured by BMI and waist circumference, is associated with higher early-onset cancer risk persisting into midlife, with patterns varying by cancer type. Early weight management may be important for prevention.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: None.

articles.title: Dissociable contributions of cortical thickness and surface area to cognitive aging: evidence from multiple longitudinal cohorts.
articles.authors: Demetriou I, Correia M, Vidal-Piñeiro D et al.
articles.abstract: Cortical volume, a widely-used marker of brain aging, is the product of two genetically and developmentally dissociable morphometric features: thickness and area. However, it remains unclear whether these two features have dissociable consequences for cognitive aging. To address this, we analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal neuroimaging and cognitive data from one discovery cohort (Cam-CAN) and two independent, pre-registered replication cohorts (OASIS-3 and HABS-HD), leveraging wide age ranges across adulthood, different follow-up intervals and diverse population backgrounds. We show that thickness declines more steeply with age than does area, and shows stronger associations with longitudinal change in fluid cognitive abilities, fairly uniformly across the cortex. Cognitive change is also dependent on baseline thickness, independent of thickness change and independent of baseline cognitive ability. In contrast, area is comparatively stable across adulthood, at least until old age, and shows weaker and more heterogeneous associations with cognitive change. Together, these findings help to reconcile inconsistencies in the literature, and indicate that thickness provides a more sensitive marker of dynamic neurobiological processes underlying cognitive aging, whereas area seems to reflect primarily stable, trait-like variation in cognitive ability.

articles.title: Humid-heat shifts conceptions and increases pregnancy termination risks in Nigeria.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.ta: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
articles.authors: Brooks N, Tuholske C, McMahon K et al.
articles.abstract: Climate change is increasing the occurrence of dangerous heat events globally with immediate health consequences, particularly in the Global South. In this paper, we spatially integrate Demographic and Healt 9 h surveys with a high-resolution, blended remotely sensed and station-derived dataset of humid-heat events spanning 1983-2016 to examine the effect of humid-heat exposure on fertility in Nigeria, one of the largest and most climate-vulnerable countries in the world. We use discrete-time models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and conception probability and linear probability models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and pregnancy termination (spontaneous and induced). We find that a 1 °C increase in the current maximum wet bulb globe temperature decreases conceptions (0.2 conceptions per 1,000 woman-months, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.4), but exposure to hotter temperatures 1 to 2 mo prior increases conception probability. Exposure to hot-humid temperatures during pregnancy increases probability of pregnancy termination (1.73 terminations per 100 pregnancies, 95% CI: 0.7 to 2.7). The net effect is an increase in births, but the timing may be shifted. Subgroup analyses reveal that effects of humid-heat on conception were larger for women residing in rural areas or in northern districts, or who are Muslim or have lower educational attainment, while the association between humid-heat and pregnancy termination was larger for women in southern areas, older women, and Christian women. Differences in how humid-heat affects populations may exacerbate existing inequalities. Overall, our analysis contributes to a better understanding of how humid-heat exposure affects fertility and reproductive health among women in the Global South.

articles.title: Dual VEGF and PD-(L)1 Blockade: Facts and Hopes.
articles.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
articles.authors: Terme M, Bourhis M, Daban A et al.
articles.abstract: VEGF-A/VEGF-R axis is well recognized for its role in tumor angiogenesis as well as tumor-induced immunosuppressive mechanisms. Targeting this pathway can help to switch tumor microenvironment toward a more immune-permissive state. Inhibition of VEGF-A/VEGFR has emerged as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in some cancers leading to the approval of anti-VEGF-A/anti-PD(L)1 combinations in advanced renal cell cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and endometrial cancer. However, in other tumor types, and particularly in colorectal cancer or glioblastoma, results remain limited. In this review, we discuss the biological rationale underlying anti-VEGF-A/PD-(L)1 combinations, summarize the clinical evidence supporting their use across tumor types, discuss the disappointing results in colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, and highlight emerging strategies to improve their therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Impact of broadly targeted enhanced recovery after surgery protocols in hysterectomy versus other gynecologic surgeries.
articles.authors: Li T, Saroya H, Lu J et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The opioid epidemic in the United States poses a major public health challenge, with postoperative prescribing recognized as a significant source of initial opioid exposure. Midwestern states, including Iowa, have experienced substantial opioid-related morbidity and mortality, reflecting broader national trends of opioid misuse, diversion, and overdose. Excess postoperative opioid prescribing increases the availability of unused medications, which are often retained in households and pose ongoing risks for diversion and nonmedical use. These challenges highlight the need for effective, scalable strategies to reduce opioid exposure at surgical discharge. Accordingly, this study investigated the impact of a broadly targeted Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway on opioid prescribing at discharge for hysterectomy patients compared to other gynecologic procedures.
METHODS: A retrospective chart review was conducted across six Iowa hospitals implementing the "Billion Pill Pledge" ERAS pathway. Two groups of patients underwent surgery between November 3, 2022 and April 4, 2024: those undergoing hysterectomy (n = 63) and those undergoing other gynecologic surgeries (n = 30), including cervical hysteroscopy, cesarean section, endometriosis excision or ablation, and sterilization procedures. Pre-ERAS and post-ERAS implementation data from the postoperative period were analyzed between the two groups in terms of average opioid pill counts prescribed, percent reduction in pill counts prescribed after ERAS implementation, and percent of prescribed pills remaining unused.
RESULTS: Pre-ERAS data showed no significant difference in mean opioid pill counts prescribed at discharge between hysterectomies and other gynecologic surgeries (p = 0.3). Post-ERAS data displayed significantly higher mean pill counts for hysterectomies (23 pills) versus other gynecologic surgeries (16 pills) (p < 0.001). Patient-reported post-ERAS prescription quantities were significantly lower than surgeon-estimated pre-ERAS prescribing quantities for both hysterectomies (27 pills versus 23 pills) (p < 0.001) and other gynecologic surgeries (29 pills versus 16 pills) (p < 0.001). The hysterectomy group had a significantly smaller percent reduction in prescribed pill counts than the other gynecologic group (14% versus 40%) (p < 0.001). There was no significant difference in the proportion of prescribed pills left unused between the hysterectomy group (55%) and the other…

articles.title: E2 displacement of CIP2A from TOPBP1 activates the DNA damage response during papillomavirus life cycles.
articles.authors: Prabhakar AT, James CD, Nguyen AQ et al.
articles.abstract: The papillomavirus life cycle is linked to epithelial differentiation, and the virus manipulates differentiation to facilitate viral production. One such manipulation is the activation of the DNA damage response (DDR), which promotes viral replication via homologous recombination. Here, we show that the papillomavirus transcription/replication/segregation factor E2 activates the DDR. During differentiation, E2 attenuates sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) activity, enhances the acetylation of DDR factors, and displaces cancerous inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A (CIP2A) from DNA topoisomerase II-binding protein 1 (TOPBP1), resulting in CIP2A-mediated inhibition of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) and ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) activation. E2 associates with TOPBP1 and ATM while reducing TOPBP1-ATR complexes and ataxia-telangiectasia and Rad3-related (ATR) activation. This ATM-high, ATR-low DDR phenotype promotes viral replication and cell proliferation. We observe this DDR activation in E2-expressing keratinocytes, human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16)-positive cells, Mus musculus papillomavirus 1 (MmuPV1)-induced lesions, HPV-positive head and neck cancer cell lines, and HPV16-positive patient-derived xenografts. ATM inhibition preferentially kills E2-expressing cells, supporting ATM signaling as a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated disease retaining E2 expression and episomal genomes.

articles.title: Oral versus vaginal Lactobacillus supplementation for endometrial dysbiosis: A paired pre and post-endometrial microbiome study.
articles.authors: Hiratsuka D, Iki A, Kinoshita M et al.
articles.abstract: Infertility is a global health challenge, and impaired endometrial receptivity remains an important contributor to treatment failure. Endometrial dysbiosis, characterized by a low proportion of Lactobacillus in the endometrial microbiota, has been proposed as a potentially modifiable factor that may affect endometrial receptivity and fertility, and treatment with Lactobacillus-containing probiotics is emerging as a promising therapeutic approach. However, the optimal route of Lactobacillus supplementation remains unclear. We compared oral versus vaginal supplementation using the same Lactobacillus-containing formulation as an adjunct to standardized doxycycline/metronidazole therapy and continued oral lactoferrin in patients with baseline endometrial Lactobacillus <10%, based on paired microbiome profiling of endometrial samples (aspirated intrauterine fluid and endometrial tissue). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, thirty-two patients underwent paired endometrial microbiome testing before and after 30 days of supplementation (oral, n = 18; vaginal, n = 14). In the vaginal group, the median endometrial Lactobacillus proportion increased from 0.05% [0.00-0.20] to 99.15% [70.45-100.00] (p = 0.001), whereas in the oral group it increased from 0.00% [0.00-0.18] to 0.30% [0.03-66.33] (p = 0.005). The median change was greater with vaginal versus oral supplementation (+98.90% [70.45-99.80] vs + 0.25% [0.03-66.33], p < 0.001). Post-treatment Lactobacillus ≥80%, used as an exploratory marker of marked microbiota improvement, was observed in 9/14 patients (64%) in the vaginal group and 3/18 (17%) in the oral group (p = 0.010). Exploratory reproductive outcomes were limited by the small sample size and did not define a reliable clinical threshold. These findings suggest that, within this combined treatment regimen, vaginal Lactobacillus supplementation may provide a greater route-associated additional improvement in endometrial microbiota profiles than oral administration.

articles.title: Evaluating gain and loss-framed mobile messaging to improve maternal health service uptake: A cluster randomized controlled trial in Jimma, Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Duguma GB, Gutema H, Gerbaba M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality has declined in Ethiopia, yet rural areas still struggle with access to care. Mobile phone-based gain or loss-framed messaging-hold promise for improving maternal health outcomes. Evidence on the comparative impact of these framing strategies in low-resource rural settings remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of gain- versus loss-framed SMS messages in improving maternal health service utilization in Jimma Zone, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A three-arm cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted across 21 clusters, with clusters allocated to gain-framed messaging, loss-framed messaging, or control (usual care). A total of 588 pregnant women (16-20 GA) were recruited in March 2023 and followed from May to December 2023, with endline assessment in February 2024. Participants received 39 messages over a 6-8 month period, aligned with gestational age and postnatal timeline. Primary outcomes were at least one ANC, SBA, and PNC within 7 days. Secondary outcomes included knowledge, attitudes, self-efficacy, and self-reported morbidity. Analyses used generalized and linear mixed models with cluster-level adjustments.
RESULT: Both framing strategies improved service utilization compared to control. Gain-framed messages increased odds of ANC attendance (OR 5.40, 97.5% CI 1.95-14.94), SBA (OR 7.53, 97.5% CI 2.20-25.79), and PNC (OR 4.83, 97.5% CI 1.71-13.67). Loss-framed messages also improved ANC attendance (OR 7.14, 97.5% CI 2.40-21.26), Skilled Birth Attendance (SBA) (OR 7.31, 97.5% CI 2.13-25.09), and PNC (OR 4.07, 97.5% CI 1.46-11.39). Knowledge improved in both arms, attitudes improved only in the gain-framed arm, and self-efficacy showed no significant change. Self-reported maternal morbidity decreased in both intervention arms.
CONCLUSION: Both gain- and loss-framed mobile messages led to increased maternal health service utilization. Loss-framed messages were more effective for ANC attendance, knowledge, and morbidity reduction, while gain-framed messages showed greater impact on SBA, PNC, and attitudes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR), PACTR202201753436676, registered on January 4, 2022; https://tinyurl.com/ykhnpc49.

articles.title: Second-Generation Combined Oral Contraceptives Induce Early Cardiovascular Risk Through Inflammatory and Oxidative Vascular Remodeling.
articles.authors: Allen MO, Salami SA, Olumide OM et al.
articles.abstract: Second-generation combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs), particularly formulations containing ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel, remain widely used because of their effectiveness and affordability in middle and low-income countries. However, concerns persist about their cardiovascular safety. This study investigated the dose-dependent effects of a second-generation COCP on systolic blood pressure (SBP), inflammatory biomarkers, oxidative stress, vascular mediators, and vascular histology in female Sprague-Dawley rats. Twenty-four female Sprague-Dawley rats were acclimatized and randomly assigned to control, low-dose (1.1 µg/kg/day), and high-dose COCP (11 µg/kg/day) groups. Treatments were administered orally for six weeks. SBP and body weight were monitored before and after treatment. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP), tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and lipid profile were measured. Renal vascular homogenates were analyzed for nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), endothelin-1 (ET-1), nitric oxide (NO), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase, catalase (CAT), and glutathione. Histological examination was performed on the renal and thoracic arteries. The SBP increased by 4.6% in the low dose and 21.8% in the high dose (p < 0.05). High-dose treatment significantly increased CRP, TNF-α, and NF-κB levels, indicating enhanced systemic and vascular inflammation. Vascular MDA and CAT increased in both treated groups, suggesting oxidative stress with compensatory antioxidant activation. Low-dose COCP increased ET-1 levels, while the NO and lipid profiles showed no significant changes across the treated groups. Both doses produced marked structural alterations in the renal and thoracic arteries. The dose-dependent rise in vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, and SBP suggests early cardiovascular risk is mediated primarily by inflammatory vascular remodeling rather than by overt dyslipidemia.

articles.title: Do Religious Cultures Predict Fertility Desire? A Country-Level Analysis.
articles.authors: Malo JS, Andre N, Froese P
articles.abstract: The study examines whether religion influences ideal fertility at the country level. While global fertility rates have declined due to educational and economic development, technological change, and improved health care, ideal fertility-reflecting individual preferences-remains an important indicator of societal fertility norms. In particular, religious traditions and beliefs, which shape gender roles and family formation, may play important role in shaping these ideals. Using cross-sectional aggregate-level data on 123 countries from the Gallup World Poll, Pew Research Center, Economic Intelligence Units, Legatum Institute Foundation and World Inequality Database, this study analyzes the relationship between national religious traditions, levels of religiosity, and ideal fertility. The findings show that religiosity and religious composition remain associated with ideal number of children at the national level regardless of economic factors. Additionally, Muslim-majority countries have higher ideal fertility compared to Christian-majority countries. We also find that religiosity is positively associated with ideal fertility for both men and women, with largely parallel slopes, indicating similar responsiveness to religious context across genders. Overall, findings highlight the importance of considering religious cultural contexts in fertility-related research, policymaking, and family planning programs.

articles.title: Disparities in Environmental Chemical Concentrations and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes by Race and Ethnicity and Country of Birth: Examples from the MIREC Study.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.authors: Abdul-Fatah A, Marro L, Owen J et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Research investigating disproportionate exposure or susceptibility in racialized and immigrant pregnant people is limited. To address this gap, we quantified disparities in environmental chemical concentrations and pregnancy complications by two indicators: (1) race and ethnicity and (2) country of birth. Our objectives were to (1) quantify descriptive differences in chemical concentrations and prevalence of outcomes and (2) assess heterogeneity in the chemical-outcome associations by our two indicators of disparity.
METHODS: Using data from a pan-Canadian longitudinal pregnancy cohort study (2008-2011), we assessed disparities in three case studies based on prior publications that examined associations between: (1) arsenic and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (n = 1255), (2) lead and preterm birth (PTB) (n = 1847), and (3) perfluorohexane sulfonate (PFHxS) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) (n = 1739). Chemicals were measured in first trimester blood samples; lead was also measured in third trimester samples. Pregnancy complication data were extracted from medical charts. We calculated geometric mean (GM) chemical concentrations by each disparity indicator and assessed differences via one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). We calculated the prevalence of each health outcome by disparity indicator and assessed differences using Chi-square tests. Using multivariable models, we assessed heterogeneity by stratifying results and calculating measures of interaction on the additive (Relative excess risk due to interaction [RERI]) and multiplicative scales.
RESULTS: Compared to White participants, non-White participants had 16% higher GM arsenic concentrations and 15-20% higher GM lead concentrations lead. Foreign-born participants had 23% higher GM arsenic concentrations and 29-37% higher GM lead concentrations compared to Canadian-born participants. Prevalence of GDM was greater for non-White compared to White participants (14% vs. 7.2%) and for foreign-born compared to Canadian-born participants (11% vs. 7.9%). Foreign-born participants experienced heightened susceptibility to the effects of lead on risk of PTB (RERI: 0.67, 95%CI: 0.01-1.27). In contrast, PFHxS concentrations were lower in non-White (33%) and foreign-born participants (34%) relative to their counterparts. Prevalence of HDP was also lower in non-White compared to White participants (6.8% vs. 11%) and in foreign-born compared to Canadian-born participants (5.8% vs.…

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into polycystic ovary syndrome and periodontal disease: a systematic scoping review of inflammatory, oxidative stress, hormonal-metabolic, and microbial pathways.
articles.authors: Nassar M, Zatar Y, Sharikadze N et al.
articles.abstract: To identify critical evidence gaps, this scoping review mapped the extent and nature of published research exploring the biological links between polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and periodontal disease. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and a pre-registered protocol (OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/WE3XU) a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, EBSCO, and Google Scholar identified original human studies assessing clinical periodontal parameters and mechanistic biomarkers in PCOS patients. Screening and data extraction were conducted independently by two reviewers. Thirty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Mapping identified a synergistic pathophysiological network across four domains. The evidence reveals an elevated systemic inflammatory baseline marked by hyper-activated endothelial markers (Endocan) alongside elevated levels of Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and Interleukin-6 (IL-6), which appears to lower the threshold for local tissue destruction. This is coupled with a compromised antioxidant defense-notably nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) downregulation-and a "microbial dysbiosis" toward pathogenic microbial complexes. However, current data primarily identify mechanistic intersections rather than definitive causality, with the "PCOS-specific" impact often confounded by shared metabolic risk factors like insulin resistance and adiposity. Mapping this evidence reveals a profound overlap between PCOS and periodontitis through shared pathophysiological networks. Advancing this field requires a Core Outcome Set (COS) and well-designed randomized controlled trials. Clinically, recognizing periodontal disease as a potential contributor to the systemic inflammatory burden suggests that integrating routine.

articles.title: Postmenopausal Hormone Replacement Therapy is not Associated with Increased Postoperative Complications After Breast Surgery: A Propensity Matched Study.
articles.authors: Deng ES, Thomas C, Colarusso B et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast surgery and reconstruction rates in the USA continue to rise, with over 90% of new breast cancer diagnoses occurring in peri- or postmenopausal women. Despite the relevance of menopause to wound healing, postoperative outcomes in this population remain understudied. Estrogen hormone replacement therapy (HRT) may aid wound healing and menopausal symptoms, but carries prothrombotic risk. We investigate postsurgical outcomes after breast surgery and reconstruction among postmenopausal patients on HRTs compared to those without HRT use.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX database, we compared patients with and without HRT use within 1 year preceding breast reconstruction. Mastectomy and reconstruction procedures were identified using CPT codes. HRT use was identified using ICD-10 and RxNorm codes. Cohorts were propensity-matched for demographics and comorbidities. Risk differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for outcomes within 90 days postoperatively. Analyses were performed within TriNetX, with significance set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: Two cohorts were generated, with 3750 HRT+ and 75503 HRT- patients. After propensity matching, two cohorts of 3750 patients each were created. After propensity adjustment, there was no significant association between HRT use and postoperative mortality, VTE, or wound healing complications, which were comparably low across all surgery types. Among patients undergoing autologous reconstruction, 1-year revision rates were higher in the HRT+ cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Systemic hormone replacement therapy was not associated with an increased complications after breast reconstruction, including mortality, thrombosis, infection, and wound dehiscence. Further prospective studies across surgical populations are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Weight Stigma in Pregnancy: A Narrative Review of Consequences, Drivers, and Potential Solutions.
articles.authors: Hill B, Hailu H, Jenkinson B et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This narrative review summarises current knowledge of weight stigma in pregnancy including consequences, drivers, and potential solutions.
RECENT FINDINGS: Weight stigma in pregnancy has negative physical, psychosocial, and behavioural sequelae for mothers and their infants. It is an equity issue that compounds disadvantage experienced by marginalised communities. A focus on gestational weight gain in maternity care, particularly for women with a high body mass index has created an environment that perpetuates implicit and explicit weight stigma, negatively impacting women's care. The community, family members, and media are also key weight stigma perpetrators. This stigma pervades societal norms, influencing healthcare environments, practice, and policy. Tackling weight stigma in maternity care requires a shift from weight-centric, stigmatising approaches to more weight-inclusive, woman-centred, and holistic health-focused care. This should be supported by approaches addressing societal and cultural norms and policy change, ultimately leading to improvements in the health and wellbeing of women during pregnancy and beyond.

articles.title: Exposure to antidepressant and antipsychotic medicines in pregnant women and risk of gestational diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.authors: Zhao X, Hu Z, Chen C
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antidepressants and antipsychotics are commonly prescribed for psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and severe anxiety disorders. Psychotropic medications are increasingly prescribed during pregnancy to manage severe mental illnesses. Concerns have been raised about their metabolic side effects, including the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study aimed to systematically review and meta-analyze existing evidence on the risk of GDM development in pregnant women with prenatal exposure to two common psychotropics, antipsychotics and antidepressants.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Web of Science, up to June 2025, identifying observational studies reporting GDM outcomes following the use of psychotropic medicines during pregnancy. Eligible studies were reviewed, and pooled relative risks (RRs) were calculated using a random-effects model, with subgroup analyses based on medication classification.
RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included in this review and meta-analysis. The pooled adjusted RR for GDM among women exposed to any antipsychotics and antidepressants during pregnancy was 1.43 (95% CI: 1.17,1.69), and 1.19 (95% CI: 1.10,1.27). Second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) were associated with a significantly higher risk of GDM (RR = 1.6, 95% CI: 1.23, 1.97). First-generation antipsychotics showed no statistically significant association.
CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal exposure to antipsychotics, particularly SGAs, and antidepressants is associated with an increased risk of GDM. Clinicians should consider these risks when prescribing psychotropic medications during pregnancy and ensure appropriate metabolic monitoring.

articles.title: Candidate DNA methylation markers for gestational diabetes: findings from technical and biological validation in a South African population.
articles.authors: Dias S, Masete M, Adam S et al.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) increases risk of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Using Genome-wide Beadchip arrays, we previously reported differential methylation of 1046 CpG sites in women with GDM. This study aimed to validate three candidate CpG sites in an independent cohort of South African women with and without GDM. DNA methylation was assessed in maternal peripheral blood collected at < 28 weeks of gestation, at three top-most significant CpG sites within Calmodulin Binding Transcription Activator 1 (CAMTA1), Kelch domain-containing protein 3/ Male-Enhanced Antigen 1 (KLHDC3/MEA1), and Collectin Subfamily member 10 (COLECT10), using bisulfite pyrosequencing, in a technical validation group (12 GDM and 12 non-GDM), and an independent biological validation group (46 GDM and 135 non-GDM). Associations between differentially methylated CpGs and maternal clinical characteristics were assessed. Technical validation confirmed decreased methylation at cg23643951 (CAMTA1; -1.53-fold; p = 0.04) and cg21910650 (KLHDC3/MEA1; -1.57-fold; p = 0.004), and increased methylation at cg16306629 (COLECT10; 4.5-fold; p = 0.003) in women with GDM, consistent with the original array findings. No significant differences were observed in the biological validation group. Within the technical validation group, cg21910650 methylation was inversely correlated with fasting glucose (rho=-0.625; p = 0.015) and 1 h OGTT (rho=-0.555; p = 0.034), while cg16306629 was positively correlated with fasting glucose (rho = 0.709; p = 0.006). Technical validation confirmed differential methylation at three CpG sites, though these findings were not reproduced in the larger biological validation group, highlighting the need for validation in independent cohorts. Associations between CpG methylation with glucose concentrations suggest a potential association with glucose regulation during pregnancy, providing a foundation for future validation of these CpG sites as biomarkers for GDM.

articles.title: Patient Voices in a Digital Space: Thematic Analysis of YouTube Comments on Pelvic Floor Content.
articles.authors: Ngouonga AAN, Ibrahim Puri L, Van Kuiken M
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Women with pelvic floor disorders (PFDs), such as urinary urgency, pelvic organ prolapse, and pelvic pain, often benefit from pelvic floor physical therapy (PFPT). Barriers such as cost, location, and referral access limit utilization. YouTube has emerged as a platform offering freely available PFPT resources. This study evaluates the viewer engagement of popular PFPT videos addressing common PFDs.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional qualitative descriptive analysis of YouTube PFPT content. Searches included "pelvic floor exercises," "urinary incontinence exercises," "dyspareunia exercises," and "pelvic prolapse exercises." Channels were included if they featured exercise-based PFPT content. The first 20 channels were identified until search redundancy was reached, and the top three most-liked videos per channel were documented. The top 40 videos by viewer count were selected, and publicly available comments were extracted using an online scraper. A hybrid inductive-deductive process was utilized to identify themes until coding saturation was achieved.
RESULTS: Forty videos yielding 14.7 K comments were included in our analysis. Three major themes emerged: (1) Desire for Community-viewers shared personal experiences, tracked symptoms, and sought validation for stigmatizing conditions; (2) Healthcare Experiences-comments reflected medical mistrust, inadequate prior care, and reluctance to pursue medical intervention; and (3) Desire for Knowledge-viewers sought guidance on exercise safety, condition-specific adaptations, and management during pregnancy or with comorbidities.
CONCLUSIONS: YouTube serves as a vital resource for individuals with PFDs, especially those with limited access to care. Beyond education, the platform fosters community and empowerment that traditional healthcare settings fail to provide for stigmatizing conditions.

articles.title: Survey of Peritoneal Closure Practices During Minimally Invasive Sacrocolpopexy.
articles.authors: Weaver A, Lavelle ES, Sassani JC
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy (MISC) is a commonly performed surgery for pelvic organ prolapse. Peritoneal closure ("reperitonealization") after mesh placement is at surgeon discretion and not standardized. Our primary objective was to assess practice patterns regarding reperitonealization during MISC among urogynecologists.
METHODS: A survey was designed to assess reperitonealization practices. The survey was assessed for face validity by a group of urogynecologists and then underwent an iterative process to improve content and readability. The survey was distributed by the American Urogynecologic Society.
RESULTS: There were 291 survey respondents with a 34% response rate. The majority held primary certification by The American Board of Obstetrics and Gynecology (96.9%) and completed fellowship in Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery (82.1%). Most were moderate to high volume surgeons, with 37.1% performing 5-25 MISC yearly and 59.1% performing more than 25 yearly. Most participants reported "always" reperitonealizing in cases with and without concomitant hysterectomy (84.9% and 85.6% respectively). Only 2.8% reported never reperitonealizing during MISC with concomitant hysterectomy. Fewer respondents performed sacrohysteropexy but of those who did, 83.3% "always" reperitonealize mesh. Most providers reported using a running suture (88.9%) with a near-even mix between short-acting and delayed absorbable suture. Desire to avoid bowel complications was the most cited reason for mesh reperitonealization, endorsed by 91.3% of participants.
CONCLUSIONS: Most urogynecologists participating in this survey report always reperitonealizing during MISC, although differences exist in suture type and technique. As future evidence is available on best surgical practices, this survey may generate hypotheses for future work on this subject.

articles.title: Robot-Assisted Sacrohysteropexy Using Autologous Fascia Lata for the Treatment of Uterine Prolapse (SAFUP): Initial Experience and Outcomes.
articles.authors: Yong C, Boyens H, McKenzie D et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Sacrohysteropexy using synthetic mesh is an established uterine-preserving treatment for uterine prolapse; however, concerns regarding mesh-related complications have increased interest in mesh-free alternatives. We hypothesised that robot-assisted SHP using autologous fascia lata (AFL) would provide effective apical support with acceptable donor-site morbidity. This study describes the surgical technique and reports short-term anatomical, functional, and patient-reported outcomes.
METHODS: This combined retrospective and prospective single-centre study included consecutive women undergoing robot-assisted AFL sacrohysteropexy for symptomatic uterine prolapse between August 2022 and November 2024. A 12 cm × 3 cm AFL graft was harvested through a single lateral thigh incision and implanted in a hockey stick configuration. The primary outcome was POP-Q point C at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included objective success (POP-Q point C ≥2 cm above the hymen during maximal Valsalva), full POP-Q measurements, pelvic floor questionnaire scores, patient satisfaction, pain scores, and donor-site morbidity.
RESULTS: Twenty patients completed 12-month follow-up. Mean POP-Q point C improved from +3.25 cm to -7.25 cm at 12 months (mean change of 10.5 cm, 95% CI 8.97-12.03). Objective success was achieved in all patients at both 6 and 12 months. Mean prolapse symptom scores improved from 8.05 at baseline to 0.25 at 12-months (difference 7.8, 95% CI 5.80-9.80). Satisfaction remained high at both time points. Donor-site morbidity was mild and self-limiting, complete resolution by 12 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted AFL SHP appears feasible, with promising short-term anatomical and patient-reported outcomes and low donor-site morbidity. Larger comparative studies with longer-term follow-up are required.

articles.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts and immune evasion in endometrial cancer: current evidence and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.authors: Zhan J, Yan Z, Cao Z et al.
articles.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are potential contributors to tumor progression and immune resistance in endometrial cancer (EC), but the extent of EC-specific mechanistic and therapeutic evidence remains uneven. Studies using EC-derived fibroblasts support tumor-promoting paracrine activity and provide experimental evidence of altered natural killer cell function. Single-cell and spatial analyses further characterize stromal heterogeneity and candidate intercellular interactions. However, many proposed mechanisms of CAF-mediated immune exclusion and most CAF-directed therapeutic strategies are informed by studies in other malignancies. This review distinguishes findings obtained in EC patient samples and experimental models from evidence extrapolated from pancreatic, breast, gastric, and other cancers. We examine CAF heterogeneity, soluble signaling, matrix remodeling, and immune-cell interactions, while identifying where functional validation in EC is still required. Therapeutic approaches, including FAP-directed interventions, stromal reprogramming, and signaling blockade combined with immune checkpoint inhibition, are discussed as candidate research strategies rather than established EC treatments. Priorities include validating CAF-immune mechanisms in EC, developing reproducible stromal biomarkers, and testing treatment combinations in appropriate disease-specific models and clinical studies.

articles.title: Readability, understandability and actionability of BAUS and EAU patient education materials for common non-oncological urological conditions.
articles.authors: Ho HW, Biyani CS
articles.abstract: Background and AimsPatient education materials (PEMs) support patient understanding and engagement in care. This study evaluated the readability, understandability and actionability of non-oncological urological PEMs produced by the British Association of Urological Surgeons (BAUS) and the European Association of Urology (EAU), and explored agreement between human and AI-assisted PEMAT-P assessment.Methods and ResultsA cross-sectional descriptive analysis assessed eight matched PEMs relating to urinary tract infection, urinary incontinence, benign prostatic enlargement/lower urinary tract symptoms, and nocturnal polyuria. Readability was assessed using Flesch Reading Ease (FRE), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), and Gunning Fog Index. Understandability and actionability were assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT-P). Mean FKGL was 11.85 ± 2.77, SMOG 13.24 ± 2.39, Gunning Fog 14.09 ± 3.22, and FRE 48.5 ± 13.32. All materials exceeded the recommended reading level. Mean PEMAT-P understandability and actionability were 91.0% and 88.3%. Human-AI item-level agreement for understandability and actionability was 83.6% and 81.8%; Cohen's κ was 0.25 and 0.23, and Gwet's AC1 was 0.79 and 0.76.ConclusionThe materials exceeded recommended reading levels despite variable PEMAT-P scores. Human vs AI differences remained, requiring further evaluation of PEMs to establish the potential role of AI as an adjunct to human PEMAT-P assessment.

articles.title: Laparoscopic resection of pelvic retroperitoneal Castleman disease.
articles.journal: Clinical and investigative medicine. Medecine clinique et experimentale
articles.authors: Sun X, Ren Y, Yu S et al.
articles.abstract: Castleman disease (CD) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder with nonspecific clinical and imaging manifestations, making it easily confounded with other pelvic tumours. This article reports the case of a 43-year-old female who presented with a 4-year history of abnormal uterine bleeding starting in 2021. Pelvic ultrasound revealed a solid mass in the left adnexal region. The patient underwent laparoscopic resection of a left pelvic retroperitoneal mass, and postoperative pathological diagnosis confirmed hyaline vascular CD. The patient recovered well after surgery, and no recurrence was observed during follow-up at 1, 2, and 6 months postoperatively. This case suggests that although CD is rare, it should be given due consideration in the differential diagnosis of pelvic masses in female patients. Complete laparoscopic excision not only enables definitive diagnosis but also provides a curative outcome. Enhancing awareness of this disease may help prevent misdiagnosis and missed diagnosis and can serve as a valuable reference for the early identification and optimal surgical management of similar cases.

articles.title: Perianesthesia Nursing Considerations for the Patient with Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
articles.journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
articles.authors: Chichester M, Homan N, Austin A et al.
articles.abstract: Pregnant patients with Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) require complex care. Coordination and communication across the interdisciplinary team are vital for optimal outcomes. Familiarizing the perianesthesia nurse with concepts specific to this diagnosis greatly impacts mother-baby-family unit and can significantly reduce the risk of maternal morbidity. As the patient with PAS may require care outside the obstetric department, it is imperative to ensure the perianesthesia nurse has the requisite knowledge to serve as the hub of the interdisciplinary team. The purpose of this article is to review current information regarding patients with a diagnosis of PAS and to provide evidence-based interventions for holistic perianesthesia nursing care.

articles.title: Proposed Method for Mass Spectrometric Measurement of the Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonist Deslorelin.
articles.authors: Wei C, Buchweitz JP, Mani R et al.
articles.abstract: Deslorelin (C64H83N17O12) is a peptide GnRH agonist drug with monoisotopic mass 1281.64 Da applied as a drug-releasing implant in veterinary medicine for promoting ovulation and male/female contraception. Despite relative safety, it is suspected of reproductive toxicity and potential harm to unborn or breast-fed children. The compound was designed for high potency and prolonged half-life making it difficult to measure quantitatively in serum. A deslorelin LC-MS/MS method relies on detecting unmetabolized undegraded intact peptide, a crucial consideration since certain metabolites are thought to have activity.
