We propose a method for analyzing deslorelin indirectly by cleaving a unique portion of the carboxy terminus containing the modified proline ProNHEt (N-ethyl-2-pyrrolidine carboxamide), which can be removed by Clostridiopeptidase specific for arginine bonds. ProNHEt can be extracted from digested serum, reacted to an N-t-butyldimethylsilyl derivative and analyzed by GC-MS/MS. Settings were optimized for detectability to <1 ppb, and derivatization gave maximum yields by adjustment of solvent, reaction time, temperature and additives. MALDI-TOF applied to deslorelin revealed binding by copper. The proposed method can be used to measure deslorelin in serum samples from various zoo and small animals. Detection of deslorelin by examination of released ProNHEt is proposed to have applicability to other GnRH superagonists such as triptorelin and deslorelin breakdown products that exhibit the ProNHEt structure.

articles.title: Effects of a 12-Week Zumba Training Program on Estimated Aerobic Capacity and Exploratory Hematological and Inflammatory Outcomes in Overweight/Obese Postmenopausal Women: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Saadouni H, Marzouki H, Ouerghi N et al.
articles.abstract: This pilot randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of a 12-week Zumba training program on estimated aerobic capacity in overweight/obese postmenopausal women, while hematological and inflammatory outcomes were explored. Thirty overweight/obese postmenopausal women were randomly assigned to a Zumba group (ZG, n = 15) or a control group (CG, n = 15). Eight participants withdrew, and 22 completers (11/group) completed the study and were included in the per-protocol analysis. The ZG completed supervised 60 min sessions three times weekly for 12 weeks, whereas the CG maintained its usual lifestyle habits. Estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max), maximal aerobic speed (MAS), hematological parameters, and inflammatory biomarkers were assessed before and after the intervention. Intervention effects were assessed using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance (ANCOVA). Estimated VO2max was higher in the ZG than CG at follow-up (adjusted difference: 3.59 mL·kg-1·min-1; partial eta squared (ηp2) = 0.683). Exploratory differences were observed for mean platelet volume (0.701 fL; ηp2 = 0.400) and neutrophils (0.961 × 103/μL; ηp2 = 0.287), whereas no clear effects were identified for other hematological outcomes. Neither C-reactive protein nor erythrocyte sedimentation rate showed a clear effect. Zumba may improve estimated aerobic capacity, while the hematological findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Effect of a Whole-Body HIIT Session on Psychophysiological Responses, Muscle Damage, and Oxidative Stress in Healthy Young Men: A Pilot Study.
articles.authors: Zovico PVC, Lirio PHC, Rodrigues LCM et al.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Optimizing exercise prescription requires a comprehensive understanding of exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) kinetics. This study investigated the acute and 72 h recovery responses of psychophysiological markers, muscle damage, and oxidative stress following a single calisthenic high-intensity interval training (HIIT-C) session in healthy young men. Methods: Ten physically active healthy young men completed a HIIT-C protocol consisting of a 5 min warm-up followed by four blocks of five 30 s "all-out" bodyweight exercises (jumping jacks, burpees, mountain climbers, and jump squats) interspersed with 30 s passive recovery intervals. Perceptual, cardiovascular, functional, biochemical, oxidative stress, and circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) markers were assessed pre-exercise, immediately post-exercise, and at 24, 48, and 72 h post-session. Repeated measures were analyzed using a one-way ANOVA (p < 0.05). Results: The HIIT-C session elicited significant acute increases in heart rate, blood lactate, and perceived exertion (p < 0.001), accompanied by an immediate reduction in perceived recovery. Mood state analysis revealed immediate post-exercise increases in fatigue and decreases in vigor (persisting for 72 h), without alterations in depression and anger. Muscle soreness increased and general well-being decreased up to 48 h post-exercise. Nuclear cfDNA (n-cfDNA) was elevated immediately post-session and returned to baseline within 24 h, whereas mitochondrial cfDNA (mt-cfDNA) remained unchanged. Significant elevations in muscle thickness (biceps brachii, triceps brachii, rectus femoris), serum enzymes (CK, LDH, AST, ALT) and oxidative stress markers (TBARS, AOPP) were observed alongside reductions in the countermovement jump performance and pressure pain threshold. Most markers remained altered at 24 and 48 h; by 72 h post-exercise, all variables returned to baseline values except for the biceps brachii muscle thickness. Conclusions: A single HIIT-C session induces significant psychophysiological perturbations and systemic EIMD requiring a 48 to 72 h recovery period. These findings delineate the post-exercise recovery kinetics of bodyweight HIIT, providing empirical data to assist practitioners in optimizing training periodization and mitigating overtraining risks in young adult men.

articles.title: TORCH-Related Maternal Infections in a Tertiary Referral Center: Diagnostic Pathways and Prenatal Management in the Context of Canadian and European Recommendations.
articles.authors: Colomba C, Serra N, Giordano C et al.
articles.abstract: Maternal TORCH-related infections remain a major cause of adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes despite advances in prenatal diagnosis and prevention. We conducted a retrospective observational study of 71 HIV-negative pregnant women referred to the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit of a tertiary referral center in Palermo, Italy, between June 2020 and December 2024 for suspected maternal TORCH infections. Demographic, microbiological, clinical, therapeutic, and neonatal data were retrospectively collected to characterize referral patterns, diagnostic pathways, treatment uptake, and pregnancy outcomes. Overall, 43 women (60.6%) had a confirmed maternal infection; cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Toxoplasma gondii accounted for most confirmed maternal infections. Maternal treatment was administered to 12/23 (52.2%) women with confirmed CMV infection and to all women with confirmed toxoplasmosis (17/17, 100%), corresponding to significantly greater treatment uptake for toxoplasmosis (p = 0.0008). Maternal demographic characteristics, obstetric history, treatment, and neonatal outcomes showed no significant association with trimester at referral. Three newborns were diagnosed with congenital CMV infection. Most referrals followed uncertain serological findings rather than clinically apparent maternal disease. These findings highlight the role of specialist assessment in clarifying maternal infection status, counseling patients, and informing pathogen-specific prenatal management; prospective multicenter studies are required to assess its effects on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Thrombotic Complications in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies: Pathophysiology, Prevention, and Clinical Management-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Siniscalchi C, Delle Femine A, Di Gennaro C et al.
articles.abstract: Thrombotic complications represent uncommon but potentially life-threatening adverse events associated with assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs), particularly in the setting of controlled ovarian stimulation and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). The relationship between thrombophilia, infertility, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains complex and only partially understood. While antiphospholipid syndrome is a well-established acquired thrombophilic disorder associated with recurrent pregnancy loss, the association between common inherited thrombophilias and recurrent pregnancy loss is less consistent, and their contribution to primary infertility and implantation failure remains uncertain. Conversely, severe OHSS is consistently recognized as the principal treatment-related determinant of thrombotic events during IVF because of profound endothelial activation, hemoconcentration, and hypercoagulability. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation of thrombotic complications associated with assisted reproductive technologies, including deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebral venous thrombosis, upper-extremity thrombosis, splanchnic vein thrombosis, and arterial thrombotic events. Current recommendations for thromboprophylaxis, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic management are critically discussed, with particular attention to individualized risk assessment and the role of low-molecular-weight heparin in high-risk patients. Although routine thromboprophylaxis is not recommended for all women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF), careful evaluation of patient-specific thrombotic risk factors remains essential. Future prospective studies are needed to improve risk prediction, optimize preventive strategies, and establish evidence-based recommendations for women undergoing assisted reproduction.

articles.title: A Novel AI-Guided Hormone Replacement System Engineered to Maintain Physiologic Levels of 17β Estradiol and Progesterone.
articles.authors: Al-Reshawee F, Alburkat H
articles.abstract: Some cases of primary and secondary amenorrhea are associated with significant symptoms and an increased risk of multiple diseases, including cardiovascular disease (CVD), osteoporosis, genitourinary dysfunction (urinary urgency and incontinence), vasomotor symptoms such as hot flashes and night sweats, and central nervous system manifestations resulting from estrogen (17-Beta estradiol) deficiency. However, current hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has important limitations in reproducing the physiological actions of endogenous 17-Beta estradiol due to the route of administration, dosing patterns, and adverse effects of synthetic hormones. This paper proposes a novel therapeutic system designed to overcome these limitations. The system consists of two main components: (1) the production of human-identical 17β-estradiol and progesterone using genetically engineered yeast, and (2) the delivery of these hormones via a subcutaneous pump programmed to maintain physiologic pulsatile secretion. An AI model assists in determining the optimal hormone dose and timing for each patient based on individualized parameters such as body weight, SHBG levels, and overall health status.

articles.title: ADD-Net: An Adaptive Discriminative Network for Multiclass Lesion Detection in Hysteroscopic Images.
articles.authors: Lu Y, Shi S, Huang L
articles.abstract: Hysteroscopic lesion detection aims to automatically localize and classify lesions in hysteroscopic images, thereby facilitating intrauterine disease screening and clinical diagnosis. However, pronounced background clutter and interclass visual similarity in hysteroscopic images can impair feature discriminability. Although prevailing methods incorporate multiscale feature aggregation or local detail refinement, these operations rely on fixed processing schemes that constrain adaptive feature recalibration under varying imaging conditions, often resulting in representational instability and interclass confusion. To address this issue, we propose ADD-Net, an adaptive discriminative detection network tailored to multiclass hysteroscopic lesion detection. Specifically, a hybrid adaptive feature modulation strategy leverages an expert selection mechanism to dynamically recalibrate backbone features, improving model robustness under challenging hysteroscopic imaging conditions. A prototype confusion interaction mechanism enhances class discriminability by modeling class prototypes and interclass confusion relationships. In addition, the model uses lesion presence probabilities to improve detection stability. On the HS-CMU dataset, ADD-Net increases the three-run mean mAP@50 from 92.5% for Mamba YOLO-T to 93.3%, while reducing parameter count, computational cost, and inference latency by approximately 16.0%, 13.5%, and 33.3%, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that ADD-Net improves detection performance while maintaining high computational efficiency, highlighting its potential for computer-aided diagnosis.

articles.title: Maternal Obesity and Outcomes During Pregnancy and the Puerperium: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Ribeiro DS, Marques LFA, Marson FAL
articles.abstract: Background: Maternal obesity is associated with pregnancy complications and adverse perinatal outcomes, although observational associations may be influenced by confounding, exposure ascertainment, and missing data. This study investigated associations between recorded maternal body mass index (BMI) and maternal clinical conditions, obstetric complications, delivery characteristics, and perinatal outcomes in a referral center. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted using medical records of pregnant women at a referral center. Recorded maternal BMI categories were classified according to the World Health Organization. Database standardization harmonized equivalent diagnostic terms, preserved maternal clinical conditions and obstetric complications as separate domains, and grouped uncommon conditions for descriptive and exploratory analyses. Missing non-BMI variables underwent multiple imputation across 50 completed datasets; maternal BMI was not imputed. Twin pregnancies were excluded, and women with and without recorded BMI were compared before and after imputation. All singleton pregnancies with recorded BMI were included descriptively, whereas association analyses excluded women with underweight because of their small number and absence of recorded primary-outcome events. The primary composite perinatal outcome comprised neonatal intensive care unit admission, recorded fetal death or stillbirth, or a 5-min Apgar score <7 among liveborn infants. Logistic regression models compared overweight and obesity with normal weight, adjusting for maternal age and parity. Selected outcomes underwent additional adjustment for smoking, chronic hypertension, and pre-existing diabetes mellitus. Complete-case analyses assessed the sensitivity of the core findings. Results: The source database comprised 1012 records. After excluding 13 twin pregnancies, 999 singleton pregnancies remained; BMI was recorded for 787 women and missing for 212 (21.2%). Among women with recorded BMI, 27 (3.4%) had underweight, 282 (35.8%) normal weight, 210 (26.7%) overweight, and 268 (34.1%) obesity. Association analyses included 760 women. Compared with normal weight, obesity was associated with maternal clinical conditions (adjusted odds ratio, 3.04; 95% confidence interval, 2.06-4.49), chronic hypertension (8.96; 4.14-19.38), obstetric complications (4.12; 2.83-5.99), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (6.12; 3.60-10.40), gestational diabetes mellitus (2.43; 1.48-3.97), cesarean…

articles.title: Uterine Preservation and Maternal Outcomes Across FIGO Severity in Placenta Accreta Spectrum: A Six-Year Retrospective Cohort in Vietnam.
articles.authors: Huynh TN, Hoang TT, Dao DT et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Uterus-preserving management of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) is increasingly reported, but preservation rates are difficult to interpret without considering disease severity and maternal morbidity. We aimed to estimate short-term uterine preservation through hospital discharge and describe maternal outcomes by FIGO clinical severity. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 291 women with clinically diagnosed PAS and intraoperative FIGO grading who underwent cesarean delivery at Hung Vuong Hospital, a tertiary maternity referral hospital in Vietnam, from 2019 to 2024. The primary outcome was short-term uterine preservation through hospital discharge, defined as no hysterectomy during the index operation or before discharge. Secondary and exploratory analyses described hemorrhage and maternal morbidity across FIGO severity. Results: Short-term uterine preservation through hospital discharge was achieved in 282/291 women (96.9%; 95% CI 94.2-98.4), including 72/79 with FIGO grade 3 (91.1%; 95% CI 82.8-95.6). Major hemorrhage occurred in 81/291 (27.8%) and severe maternal morbidity in 25/291 (8.6%); no maternal deaths occurred. In FIGO grade 3, major hemorrhage occurred in 51/79 (64.6%), high-volume red-cell transfusion in 37/79 (46.8%), and severe maternal morbidity in 21/79 (26.6%). Conclusions: Most women retained the uterus through hospital discharge in this cohort, but women with FIGO grade 3 had high rates of hemorrhage, transfusion, and maternal morbidity. Without a concurrent planned-hysterectomy comparator, this study cannot compare the effectiveness of uterine preservation with hysterectomy.

articles.title: From Germ Cell Histogenesis to Precision Risk Stratification: Prognostic and Predictive Molecular Markers in Testicular Germ Cell Tumors-A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Cutitaru AB, Caruntu ID, Balan RA et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs) represent the most common solid malignancies in young adult men, with cure rates exceeding 95% under modern cisplatin-based therapy, yet a clinically relevant subset of patients still experiences treatment failure or long-term toxicity. This systematic review synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence, from database inception through 6 July 2026, on prognostic and predictive molecular markers in developmental and endocrine-sensitive testicular carcinogenesis. Methods: A PRISMA 2020-aligned search of MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Library was supplemented by registry-based evidence, reference-list screening, and contemporary guidelines to capture diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarkers in TGCTs. The strategy encompassed classical serum markers, tissue-based molecular and immunohistochemical markers, miRNA/cfDNA liquid-biopsy assays, immune and resistance-related features, and validated clinicopathological risk models. Results: The review integrates classical serum biomarkers, pluripotency transcription factors, surface and oncofetal antigens, yolk-sac and trophoblastic markers, circulating microRNAs, methylated cell-free DNA, immune features, and updated clinicopathological risk models. Markers are graded as established, validated research, or emerging candidates. miR-371a-3p shows a high accuracy for active non-teratomatous TGCT, with pooled sensitivity of about 0.90 and specificity of approximately 0.86, but is negative in pure teratoma. AFP, β-hCG, and LDH are still required for staging and IGCCCG risk assignment. Conclusions: Despite the growing promise of biomarker-driven approaches in TGCT, no single serum, tissue, liquid-biopsy, immune, or resistance-associated marker has yet demonstrated sufficient clinical utility to replace comprehensive evaluation based on morphology, staging, histology, imaging, standard serum markers, and established clinicopathological risk assessment.

articles.title: Exerkines During Pregnancy: Linking Maternal Exercise with Cardiometabolic Health-A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Sklempe Kokic I, Znika M, Brumnic V et al.
articles.abstract: Physical exercise during pregnancy is associated with important maternal and foetal health benefits. These include reduced risks of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), and excessive gestational weight gain. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain incompletely understood. Exerkines are exercise-responsive signalling molecules released from skeletal muscle and other metabolically active tissues and may contribute to metabolic, vascular, inflammatory, and mitochondrial adaptations. This narrative review critically examines current evidence linking exerkines with maternal exercise and cardiometabolic adaptation during pregnancy, with particular emphasis on GDM, HDP, maternal obesity, placental function, and maternal-placental-foetal communication. Evidence was identified through a comprehensive, iterative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science primarily covering literature published between January 2016 and July 2026. Priority was given to human pregnancy studies and clinically relevant outcomes. Pregnancy-specific evidence is currently strongest for irisin, although findings remain heterogeneous. Acute exercise studies also indicate transient changes in circulating fibroblast growth factor 21. Evidence for β-aminoisobutyric acid, apelin, adiponectin, chemerin, and interleukin-6 is more limited and frequently relies on experimental or non-pregnant populations. Overall, current evidence supports exerkines as plausible contributors to the cardiometabolic adaptations associated with maternal exercise, but does not establish them as causal mediators. Their principal value at present lies in providing a biological framework linking established clinical benefits of prenatal exercise with metabolic, vascular, inflammatory, and placental adaptations, while identifying specific pathways that require confirmation in pregnancy-specific longitudinal and intervention studies.

articles.title: Contemporary Approaches to Postpartum Hemorrhage with Focus on Uterine Compression Sutures-An Updated Comprehensive Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Ursache A, Socolov DG, Bujor IE et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Surgical management of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is essential when conservative measures fail, yet no clear hierarchy of effectiveness among interventions exists. Given the scarcity of the direct comparative studies and the substantial clinical and methodological heterogenicity of the available evidence, this systematic review aims to provide an updated and structured synthesis of the UCS for the management of refractory PPH. Methods: We reviewed studies published from January 2014 to December 2025 using keywords related to PPH and UCS. After excluding duplicates and applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, we selected 31 articles. Results: We grouped the selected articles into 4 sections: UCS alone; UCS versus uterine artery embolization (UAE) and versus Bakri balloon tamponade; newer UCS techniques; and articles on future fertility outcomes after UCS. Evidence on UCS alone was predominantly uncontrolled observational case series, with reported efficacy ranging from 73.9% to 100%. Newer UCS techniques use removable sutures to reduce side effects and complications. Although early results on subsequent fertility and menstrual function appear promising, the lack of large, well-designed randomized studies warrants caution in interpretation. Conclusions: Asian tertiary centers dominate the literature and report high uterine preservation rates, but retrospective design, small samples, lack of controls, inadequate adjustment for confounders, and heterogeneous techniques limit the strength of conclusions and generalizability. The predominance of cesarean section cohort further limits generalizability to vaginal births. UCS efficacy appears strongly influenced by bleeding severity and case complexity.

articles.title: Learning Curve and Detection Accuracy of Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy for Endometrial Cancer Staging: Experience from an ESGO & GESEA Certified Center.
articles.authors: Grimbizis G, Zouzoulas D, Theodoridis T et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pelvic lymphadenectomy has long been considered the gold standard for surgical staging in early-stage endometrial cancer. However, sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) with ultrastaging has emerged as a less invasive alternative. The aim of the study is to assess the detection rate, learning curve and diagnostic accuracy of SLNB in a cohort of patients with a high prevalence of obesity and early-stage endometrial cancer. Methods: This relatively small prospective single-center study included patients with presumed early-stage endometrial carcinoma who underwent laparoscopic hysterectomy, SLNB and bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy at the 1st Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology between 1 April 2023 and 31 May 2025. Results: Forty-one patients were recruited. The mean age was 64.3 years, and the mean BMI was 32.4 kg/m2. Bilateral and overall sentinel lymph node (SLN) detection was achieved in 27 of 41 patients (65.9%) and 85.4%, respectively. Concerning the learning curve, after the first 20 cases the bilateral detection rate was as high as 90.5% (p-value < 0.001). The median number of SLN for the left and right side were 1 (IQR: 1-2) and 2 (IQR: 1-3), respectively. The median number of lymph nodes dissected by lymphadenectomy was 7 (IQR: 5-8) for both sides. There were three patients with lymph node metastases, all of which were detected by SLNB. Conclusions: Bilateral detection of SLNs is technically feasible and requires a relatively short learning curve, under expert supervision in a high-volume, standardized training environment, even in patients with a high prevalence of obesity. The adoption of a standardized detection protocol is key to avoiding mapping failure.

articles.title: Bone Mineral Density in Women with Functional Hypothalamic Amenorrhea: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Sultanova Z, Issenova S, Dissyukeyeva Y et al.
articles.abstract: This study aims to quantitatively evaluate bone mineral density (BMD) in women with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (FHA), determine differences across skeletal sites, and summarise current evidence on the diagnosis and management of impaired bone health in this population. Methods: A systematic search of comparative studies evaluating BMD by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in women with FHA or anorexia nervosa (AN) and healthy eumenorrhoeic controls was performed. Eleven studies met the eligibility criteria, five of which were included in the meta-analysis. The quantitative synthesis comprised 14 group comparisons, with lumbar spine and hip BMD analysed separately. Effect sizes were pooled using Hedges' g with 95% confidence intervals (CI) under a random-effects model. Sensitivity analyses using REML estimation with Hartung-Knapp adjustment and leave-one-out analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the pooled estimates. Results: The narrative synthesis of 11 studies generally showed lower BMD in women with FHA or AN compared with healthy controls. In the meta-analysis, among women with FHA, hip BMD was significantly lower than in healthy controls (Hedges' g = -0.60; 95% CI -1.13 to -0.06; p = 0.030; I2 = 63%), while a moderate reduction was observed at the lumbar spine (Hedges' g = -0.68; 95% CI -1.48 to 0.13; p = 0.101; I2 = 83%). In women with AN, substantial reductions were observed at both the lumbar spine (Hedges' g = -1.66; 95% CI -2.28 to -1.04; p < 0.001; I2 = 71%) and the hip (Hedges' g = -1.37; 95% CI -2.33 to -0.42; p = 0.005; I2 = 89%). The lumbar spine reduction in AN remained statistically significant across sensitivity and leave-one-out analyses and was the most robust finding, whereas the statistical significance of hip BMD estimates in both FHA and AN and of lumbar spine BMD in FHA was sensitive to the analytical approach or exclusion of individual studies. The systematic review demonstrated that DXA with interpretation based on Z-scores remains the preferred method for skeletal assessment in premenopausal women with FHA. Bone health assessment is recommended after ≥6 months of amenorrhea or earlier in women with severe energy deficiency or a history of fractures. Restoration of energy availability, weight gain, and recovery of menstrual function remain the cornerstone of treatment. When amenorrhea persists and low BMD is confirmed, physiological transdermal 17β-estradiol combined with cyclic progesterone is the…

articles.title: Beyond Reported Rates: A Critical Narrative Review of the Risk Architecture, Early Recognition, and Prevention of Complications in Gynecologic Laparoscopy.
articles.authors: Maglic R, Ivanovic M, Lalic K et al.
articles.abstract: Reported complication rates in gynecologic laparoscopy are widely used as indicators of safety, yet they often describe fundamentally different clinical realities. Variations in definitions, severity classification, duration of follow-up, and procedural context mean that superficially similar outcomes are frequently not comparable. As a result, the literature is rich in data, but limited in interpretability. This review addresses that gap by critically examining complications not only as events but as phenomena shaped by methodological heterogeneity, procedural complexity, and the conditions under which they are recognized. A search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was performed, with additional manual reference screening. Given the predominance of heterogeneous retrospective series, cohort studies, registries, and targeted systematic reviews, a narrative synthesis was undertaken. Across studies, the most clinically significant complications remain hemorrhage, bowel injury, and urinary tract injury, while pneumoperitoneum-related events, vaginal cuff dehiscence, port-site complications, port-site metastasis, and morcellation-related dissemination represent rarer but disproportionately consequential outcomes. Importantly, complication risk consistently clusters around identifiable domains, including prior surgery and adhesions, procedural complexity, energy use, operative duration, surgeon experience, and center-level standardization. This review shows that complications in gynecologic laparoscopy cannot be meaningfully interpreted through incidence alone. Their true clinical significance lies in the interaction between risk architecture, intraoperative decision-making, and the timeliness of postoperative recognition. The principal contribution of this work is therefore not a single summary rate but a clinically oriented framework that integrates interpretation of the literature with practical principles of prevention and early diagnosis.

articles.title: Societal and Healthcare Costs of Post-IDFS Events Following Adjuvant Ribociclib Plus an Aromatase Inhibitor (AI) Versus AI Alone in Pre- and Postmenopausal Women with Early HR+/HER2- Breast Cancer in Canada.
articles.authors: Soliman D, Brezden-Masley C, Sehdev S et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent advancements in early breast cancer (EBC) for high-risk populations have significantly improved invasive disease-free survival (IDFS). While cost-effectiveness has been assessed, the broader societal impact of improved IDFS remains unstudied. A non-homogeneous semi-Markov model was developed to estimate total healthcare and societal costs after first-line treatment with ribociclib plus an aromatase inhibitor (AI) or, alternatively, AI alone in patients with hormone-receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) EBC.
METHODS: Using an incidence-based approach, the model calculated total expected annual societal costs of disease-related events after cessation of adjuvant treatment with ribociclib plus AI or AI alone for HR+/HER2- EBC. The model includes five states: IDFS, non-metastatic recurrence (NMR), distant recurrence (DR), secondary primary malignancy (SPM) and death, with a one-year cycle length, and a new cohort entering each year. Health state transition probabilities are based on a previously published cost-effectiveness model (CEM). Costs are tallied only after IDFS (after cessation of adjuvant treatment) and include direct costs of medical care as well as indirect costs related to employment, productivity, and wage loss.
RESULTS: At the 4-year NATALEE data cut-off (April 2024), ribociclib plus AI reduced the risk of an IDFS event by 28.5% versus AI alone (HR 0.715), corresponding in the model to 23% fewer non-fatal events (NMR, DR, and SPM), 18% lower mortality, 23% lower total direct costs (-$957,471,465), and 24% lower indirect costs (-$448,542,692) from the period of cessation of adjuvant therapy until death. Healthcare savings were driven primarily by fewer distant recurrences and deaths, while societal savings were largely due to reduced caregiver costs.
CONCLUSIONS: Treatments that reduce disease recurrence and mortality can significantly lower societal costs and alleviate burden on the healthcare system.

articles.title: Ovarian Somatic Cells: Cellular Heterogeneity and Functional Dynamics Across Health, Ageing, and Disease.
articles.authors: Rebuzzini P, Fantinato A, Brazzale G et al.
articles.abstract: The ovary is a highly dynamic organ in which the somatic cell population plays essential roles in coordinating folliculogenesis, steroidogenesis, and tissue homeostasis. Increasing evidence highlights substantial cellular heterogeneity and functional plasticity within the ovarian somatic compartment, which is dynamically modulated across the reproductive lifespan. The ovarian somatic cells exhibit distinct transcriptional profiles and functional states that evolve across developmental stages and throughout the reproductive cycle. During ageing, somatic cell composition and function are reshaped, promoting inflammatory responses, stromal remodelling, and reduced support for oocyte developmental competence. Dysregulation of their function and plasticity is also increasingly implicated in reproductive disorders (such as polycystic ovary syndrome, premature ovarian insufficiency and ovarian fibrosis). This review aims to consolidate emerging evidence of the central role of ovarian somatic cells and provides a unifying framework that integrates their roles in physiological ovarian function, ageing, and clinically relevant ovarian disorders.

articles.title: Transcriptional Regulation of the Meiotic Cohesin Subunit RAD21L by Methylation of Two CpG Islands in Its Promoter and Characterization of Its Interactions with Histones.
articles.authors: Dalai W, Saeki K, Jiya W et al.
articles.abstract: The meiosis-specific cohesin α-kleisin subunits REC8 and RAD21L regulate higher-order chromatin organization and germline-specific transcription in male germ cells. Rad21l exhibits high, testis-specific expression in mice, but the epigenetic mechanisms governing its promoter activity and those underlying its chromatin targeting and anchoring remain unclear. To address these questions, we investigated Rad21l using dual-luciferase reporter assays, in vitro methylation, bisulfite sequencing, molecular docking, transcriptome sequencing, and co-immunoprecipitation. We identified a distal regulatory region and mapped the core promoter of Rad21l to the -228 to -3 bp region. We further demonstrated that methylation of the promoter CpG islands represses its transcription. Molecular docking simulations suggested that KLF4 could bind a promoter sequence containing CpG5 and that methylation would not disrupt this interaction. Methylation was hypothesized to induce conformational remodeling of KLF4, shift its ability to recruit cofactors, and thereby enable bidirectional transcriptional regulation. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed the co-occurrence of α-kleisin proteins with the meiosis-specific histone H1t and histone H3, detected modified H3 forms including H3K9me1 and H3S10phos, and showed their association with HP1β. Histone modifications may regulate interaction affinity through long-range allosteric effects. This study proposes a working model for tissue-specific transcriptional regulation of Rad21l involving CpG methylation and KLF4 and establishes a hypothetical model of histone-dependent RAD21L chromatin anchoring, providing a basis for investigating male meiosis and identifying infertility-related targets.

articles.title: Can Thyroid Dysfunction Contribute to Infertility via Lipid Abnormalities?
articles.authors: Kelly RB, Hassoun AA, Stępniak J et al.
articles.abstract: Thyroid dysfunction alters lipid metabolism and may impair reproduction, raising the possibility that lipid abnormalities contribute to thyroid-related infertility. This review evaluates dyslipidemia as a potential mechanistic link between these conditions. Thyroid hormones regulate hepatic LDL clearance, triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism and HDL remodeling. Overt hypothyroidism commonly increases total and LDL cholesterol, changes that are partly reversible with levothyroxine, whereas lipid abnormalities in subclinical and central hypothyroidism are smaller and less consistent; hyperthyroidism generally lowers total and LDL cholesterol. Independently, adverse circulating lipid profiles are associated with reduced natural fecundability and poorer outcomes in selected assisted-reproduction studies. Experimental evidence identifies biologically coherent pathways involving ovarian steroidogenesis, follicular HDL function, oocyte cholesterol efflux and membrane signaling, endometrial receptivity and sperm membrane integrity. Human evidence supports both the thyroid-lipid and lipid-fertility relationships, but does not establish that lipid abnormalities mediate thyroid-related infertility. Interpretation is complicated by direct thyroid hormone effects, thyroid autoimmunity and metabolic confounding. Taken together, current findings support dyslipidemia as a biologically plausible potential contributor to thyroid-related reproductive dysfunction. Clinically, they suggest considering integrated assessment of thyroid and lipid status in reproductive-age adults and reassessment of the lipid profile after restoration of euthyroidism. Prospective preconception studies incorporating functional lipid measurements and formal mediation analyses are needed.

articles.title: Regulated Cell Death in Reproductive Biology: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.authors: Stavros S, Moustakli E, Kathopoulis N et al.
articles.abstract: Regulated cell death (RCD) has emerged as a fundamental determinant of cellular homeostasis and tissue remodeling, extending far beyond the classical concept of apoptosis. The identification of emerging RCD pathways, including ferroptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, cuproptosis, PANoptosis, and autophagy-dependent cell death, has expanded our understanding of reproductive physiology and disease. RCD mechanisms contribute to reproductive homeostasis and have been increasingly implicated in gametogenesis, folliculogenesis, embryonic development, implantation, placentation, and reproductive aging, while their dysregulation has been associated with infertility, recurrent implantation failure, recurrent pregnancy loss, pregnancy complications, endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), gynecological malignancies, and male reproductive disorders. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms governing RCD across reproductive physiology and disease, emphasizing the complex interplay between oxidative stress (OS), mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, immune regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and genetic and epigenetic networks. Particular attention is given to the contribution of emerging cell death pathways to reproductive disorders and their interactions with environmental and lifestyle factors, including endocrine-disrupting chemicals. In addition, current evidence regarding RCD-associated biomarkers, multi-omics approaches, and therapeutic strategies targeting specific cell death pathways is critically evaluated, with particular emphasis on distinguishing associative molecular signatures from functional evidence of RCD execution. By integrating recent advances from basic, translational, and clinical research, this review highlights the context-dependent role of RCD in reproductive biology and disease and identifies current limitations and future opportunities for RCD-informed diagnostics, patient stratification, and targeted therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine.

articles.title: Breastfeeding and Genitourinary Symptoms: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Illston JD, McMinn EK, McIlwraith CA et al.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Understanding genitourinary effects of breastfeeding allows for proactive treatments and quality-of-life improvements.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to estimate the effect of breastfeeding on genitourinary symptoms.
STUDY DESIGN: This prospective cohort study of breastfeeding (BF) versus non-breastfeeding (NB) primiparous women characterized genitourinary symptoms after singleton delivery at ≥34 weeks of gestation. Validated measures included the Urinary Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6), Incontinence Impact Questionnaire-7 (IIQ-7), Most Bothersome Symptom questionnaire (MBS), and Pelvic Organ Prolapse Incontinence Sexual Questionnaire, IUGA-Revised (PISQ-IR). Questionnaires were completed at baseline, 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months postpartum. The primary outcome was the UDI-6 score at 3 months. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were evaluated for group differences.
RESULTS: UDI-6 scores at 3 months were not different between groups (5.6±11.8 BF, 7±12 NB, P=0.43). Differences in IIQ-7 scores were not statistically significant (4.9±7.4 BF, 13.5±25.2 NB, P=0.07). Multivariable analysis for those not sexually active revealed better partner-related scores in the BF group (β, -0.85; 95% CI, -1.58, -0.12, P=0.024). Among those sexually active, the BF group had worse condition impact scores (β, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.11, 0.47, P=0.002). The three-month MBS revealed nearly a threefold likelihood of experiencing vaginal dryness in BF (adjusted odds ratio, 2.82; 95% CI, 1.19, 6.66, P=0.018). At 6 months, vaginal dryness was no longer different, but breastfeeding continued to affect sexual function.
CONCLUSIONS: At 3-months postpartum, there were no differences in lower urinary tract symptom severity between BF versus NB women. The BF group had increased bothersome vaginal symptoms and a mixed effect on sexual function. Awareness of these findings should lead to proactive assessment of symptoms and timely treatments.

articles.title: The remodeling of gut microbiota driven by changes in the living environment: a new perspective on the imbalance of the gut-bone axis in perimenopausal women.
articles.authors: Jin J, Wang X, Ma J et al.
articles.abstract: The perimenopausal period represents a critical transition stage during which female bone health shifts from a relatively stable state to accelerated bone loss. The development and progression of osteoporosis during this stage are influenced not only by estrogen decline but also by the gut microbial ecological background shaped by long-term environmental factors. With changes in modern dietary patterns, lifestyles, and environmental exposure profiles, the human gut microbiota undergoes continuous remodeling, which may disrupt the gut-bone axis regulatory network by affecting estrogen metabolism, immune-inflammatory homeostasis, and microbiota-derived metabolite production, thereby contributing to impaired bone metabolism in perimenopausal women. This review focuses on the research framework of "changes in the living environment-gut microbiota remodeling-osteoporosis" and systematically summarizes the theoretical basis of gut microbiota-mediated regulation of bone homeostasis. Furthermore, the potential mechanisms by which gut-bone axis dysregulation contributes to the development of osteoporosis during the perimenopausal period are discussed, and future research directions involving multi-omics integration, artificial intelligence, and longitudinal cohort studies are highlighted. Accordingly, this review proposes a conceptual framework linking long-term changes in the living environment, gut microbiota remodeling, and altered bone metabolism. This framework provides a new perspective for understanding how an environmentally shaped microbial background may contribute to changes in bone health during the perimenopausal transition.

articles.title: Early clinical experience with the OB balloon for prophylactic intrauterine tamponade during cesarean section for placenta previa: a prospective multicenter phase II study.
articles.authors: Tanaka M, Kato J, Hori Y et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Placenta previa is a major cause of severe postpartum hemorrhage, and effective intraoperative strategies to prevent bleeding during cesarean section remain an important clinical challenge. Intrauterine balloon tamponade has been reported as an effective strategy for hemorrhage control. We developed a novel double-balloon device, the OB balloon, intended for intrauterine tamponade during cesarean section in patients with placenta previa. This study evaluated the safety, feasibility, and clinical effectiveness of the OB balloon.
METHODS: In this prospective multicenter phase II study, 55 patients with placenta previa, including low-lying placenta, underwent cesarean section with prophylactic placement of the OB balloon. Perioperative outcomes, including blood loss, need for additional hemostatic interventions, and device-related complications, were analyzed.
RESULTS: Mean blood loss before balloon placement was 1306 g, whereas median blood loss after placement was 70 g. No patient required cesarean hysterectomy or additional surgical or interventional hemostatic procedures after balloon placement. The device was inserted directly through the uterine incision, and both balloons were inflated intraoperatively by the operating surgeon under sterile conditions. Median inflation volumes were 80 mL for the uterine balloon and 50 mL for the vaginal balloon. The balloon was maintained for 12-24 hours and removed without complication. Balloon prolapse occurred in 3.6% of cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic use of the OB balloon during cesarean section for placenta previa was safe, feasible, and associated with reduced blood loss in this cohort. The dual-balloon design provided stable tamponade with a low rate of prolapse and eliminated the need for additional hemostatic interventions.

articles.title: Circulating tumor DNA in breast cancer in 2027: advancing liquid biopsy and molecular monitoring.
articles.authors: Oliva GR, Cristofanilli M, Reduzzi C et al.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is increasingly used for molecular profiling in breast cancer, and its role as a longitudinal biomarker is expanding. This review examines recent evidence on serial ctDNA assessment, focusing on minimal residual disease (MRD) and molecular relapse in early breast cancer (EBC) and on molecular response and emerging resistance in metastatic breast cancer (MBC).
RECENT FINDINGS: In EBC, ctDNA dynamics and MRD detection carry prognostic value, and serial surveillance can identify molecular relapse before overt recurrence. However, molecular lead time is not necessarily a therapeutic interception window, and the benefit of treating molecular relapse remains unproven. In MBC, serial ctDNA analysis can capture tumor dynamics, clonal evolution, and emerging resistance. Emerging cell-free DNA methylation-based approaches may enable molecular breast cancer subtyping, complementing genomic profiling. Definitions of molecular response and progression lack standardization across assays, metrics, thresholds, and sampling schedules. Nevertheless, randomized evidence shows that adapting treatment to selected actionable resistance alterations detected before radiological progression can improve clinical outcomes.
SUMMARY: ctDNA monitoring is shifting liquid biopsy from a static molecular characterization toward the longitudinal assessment of disease evolution. Its future clinical value will depend on identifying molecular changes reliable and actionable enough to translate earlier detection into patient benefit.

articles.title: Joint Hypermobility and Female Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Kuroda K, Ito K
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To systematically evaluate the association between joint hypermobility and female lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS).
METHODS: A PubMed/MEDLINE search was performed, and eligible studies included original English-language studies evaluating women with joint hypermobility, benign joint hypermobility syndrome (BJHS), hypermobility spectrum disorder, or Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, including hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and reporting urinary outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, as appropriate. Owing to substantial methodological heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies met the eligibility criteria. Urinary incontinence (UI), stress urinary incontinence, urgency urinary incontinence, urinary frequency, nocturia, incomplete bladder emptying, and voiding symptoms were the most frequently reported outcomes. Comparative studies demonstrated higher rates of UI among women with BJHS, with increased voiding symptoms also reported in one cohort, whereas other studies found no significant association between joint hypermobility and specific UI subtypes or urodynamic abnormalities. Five studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, and considerable heterogeneity existed in hypermobility definitions, urinary outcome measures, and study design.
CONCLUSIONS: Women with joint hypermobility and related connective tissue disorders frequently experience LUTS, particularly UI and voiding symptoms. However, the available evidence remains heterogeneous and does not support a consistent independent association between joint hypermobility and specific lower urinary tract dysfunction. Standardized prospective studies using validated hypermobility classifications and objective urinary assessments are needed.

articles.title: Recombinant activated factor VIIa for severe postpartum hemorrhage in Africa: Evidence, appropriate use, and research priorities-A narrative review.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Mahlangu J, Rhemtula H, Zamparini J et al.
articles.abstract: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) accounts for 30%-50% of maternal mortality in Africa and occurs in the context of pre-existing anemia, limited blood product availability, delayed recognition, and constrained referral systems. Although bundle-based care (E-MOTIVE), early tranexamic acid (TXA), and uterotonics have substantially improved outcomes, a small proportion of women develop refractory hemorrhage despite optimal conventional management. This narrative review evaluates the role of recombinant activated factor VIIa (rFVIIa) in severe PPH within the African context. We conducted a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar, which was supplemented by manual review of international guidelines. We critically evaluated and synthesized data from clinical studies, systematic reviews, registries, consensus statements, and relevant African literature. The principal evidence derives from a French-Swiss randomized controlled trial demonstrating a 40% relative reduction in invasive procedures, supported by observational studies and expert consensus. In 2022, the European Medicines Agency approved rFVIIa for severe PPH after uterotonic failure, followed by South African approval in 2023. The indication remains unapproved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and is off-label in most other African countries. Efficacy depends on timely administration after definitive obstetric source control and correction of coagulopathy and physiological derangements. Current evidence supports rFVIIa as a protocolized rescue adjunct rather than routine therapy. In Africa, its use should be restricted to carefully selected women with refractory PPH managed in tertiary centers with multidisciplinary expertise. African registries, pragmatic implementation studies, and health-economic evaluations are needed to define its optimal role within resource-constrained healthcare systems.

articles.title: Birth satisfaction and resilience in the association between prenatal anxiety and postpartum depressive symptoms: A mediational analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Wang Y, Huang W, Xu X et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common mental health disorder among women after childbirth. This study aimed to examine whether birth satisfaction and resilience statistically mediated the association between prenatal anxiety and PPD.
METHODS: From February to August 2023, pregnant women in the third trimester were recruited using convenience sampling from three tertiary hospitals in Nantong, China. Prenatal anxiety was assessed using the anxiety subscale of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), and resilience was assessed using the 10-item Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10) during pregnancy. Birth satisfaction and postpartum depressive symptoms were assessed using the Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised Indicator (BSS-RI) and Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) at 6 weeks postpartum. Parallel mediation analysis was performed using PROCESS macro with 5000 bootstrap samples, adjusting for maternal age and physical discomfort.
RESULTS: A total of 635 participants completed two rounds of questionnaire surveys. Birth satisfaction and resilience showed significant indirect associations between prenatal anxiety and PPD. The indirect association through birth satisfaction was 0.047 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.025-0.073), accounting for 17.34% of the total statistical association. Furthermore, the indirect association through resilience was 0.082 (95% CI: 0.054-0.116), accounting for 30.26% of the total statistical association.
CONCLUSION: Prenatal anxiety was associated with postpartum depressive symptoms, with significant indirect associations through birth satisfaction and resilience. These findings highlight the potential relevance of psychological resources and childbirth experience in postpartum mental health and support further longitudinal and intervention research.

articles.title: Genetic Parameters and Genome-Wide Association Analysis of Reproductive Traits in Egyptian Buffalo.
articles.journal: Journal of animal breeding and genetics = Zeitschrift fur Tierzuchtung und Zuchtungsbiologie
articles.authors: Amin AMS, El Nagar AG, Khalil MH et al.
articles.abstract: Reproductive efficiency is a crucial factor in the sustainability and profitability of buffalo production systems. However, genetic improvement of reproductive traits is challenging due to low heritability, environmental sensitivity, limited recording, and shrinking reference populations caused by crossbreeding. This study aimed to estimate genetic parameters and detect the genomic architecture of key reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo using pedigree-based analyses and genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Over a 44-year period (1980-2024), reproductive records from five Egyptian experimental herds were analysed. The dataset comprised 2843 buffalo cows, sired by 140 bulls and out of 1328 dams. In total, 2359 records were available for age at first calving (AFC), 10,478 for gestation length (GL), 7966 for calving interval (CI), 6705 for days open (DO), and 12,909 for calving ease (CE) and stillbirth (SB). For genome-wide association analysis, 275 Egyptian buffaloes were genotyped using the Affymetrix Buffalo 90 K array, and 66,295 high-quality SNPs were retained after quality control. De-regressed proofs derived from pedigree-based genetic evaluations were used as response variables in a mixed linear model implemented in the rMVP package. Genome-wide association analysis identified putative genomic regions associated with GL, CI, CE, and SB, whereas no genome-wide significant associations were detected for AFC and DO. Functional annotation and QTL enrichment analyses were subsequently used to provide exploratory biological context for the identified genomic regions. Heritability estimates were generally low: 0.16 for AFC, 0.06 for GL, 0.02 for CI, 0.02 for DO, 0.18 for CE, and 0.06 for SB. Manhattan plots revealed that 15 genomic regions containing significant SNPs were identified on chromosomes 2, 4, 10, 12, 13, 15, 19, 20, and 25 for the reproductive traits of GL, CI, CE, and SB. These findings provide preliminary evidence of genomic regions potentially contributing to variation in reproductive traits in Egyptian buffalo, although the relatively small number of genotyped animals limits the power to detect and validate small effect loci. Seven significant genomic regions on chromosomes 10, 13, 15, 20, and 25 were associated with the GL trait. Additionally, three suggestive SNPs mapped to chromosomes 2 and 19 were associated with the CE trait, and three suggestive SNPs mapped on chromosome 12 were significantly associated with the SB trait. The…

articles.title: Small placental size is common in stillbirths, including unexplained late-gestation stillbirths.
articles.authors: Cheng M, Marsden T, Warrilow K et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study determined if placentas with low weight and/or abnormal size were associated with an increase in stillbirth incidence, and if the proportion of small placentas was greater in 'unexplained' late-gestation stillbirth.
METHODS: A total of 390 fresh, trimmed, placentas from stillbirths were weighed and measured. The Perinatal Society of Australia and New Zealand (PSANZ) Perinatal Death Classification (PDC) system (2018) was used for cause-of-stillbirth categories. A generalised linear model with a log link and a binomial distribution was used to assess how the risk of a small placenta varied according to potential explanatory factors.
RESULTS: Small placentas were 7-times more common in this stillbirth cohort when compared to livebirths. Babies who were stillborn at term were more likely than those born preterm to have a small placenta (RR 1.7; 95 % CI 1.1-2.4) and low placental weight to birthweight ratio (RR 2.7; 95 % CI 1.7-4.2). There were 117 (30.0 %) stillbirths classified as 'unexplained', and the adjusted RR (aRR) of having an unexplained stillbirth with a small placenta was 1.6 (95 % CI 1.1-2.2). Furthermore, there was a 20 % increase in the risk of small placenta for women who had a peripheral cord insertion (aRR 1.2; 95 % CI 1.0-1.3).
CONCLUSIONS: Stillbirths were associated with small placentas, low placental weight, low placental volume and low placental weight to birthweight ratio. Furthermore, we established a link between abnormal cord insertion and low placental weight in stillbirths, as well as between unexplained stillbirths and small placentas.

articles.title: Study on the molecular mechanism of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells inducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition in HPV-associated cervical cancer through activation of miR-129.
articles.authors: Ma N, Xu K, Wang Z
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HPV-associated cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related death in women worldwide. The role of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and miR-129 in tumor progression remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate miR-129 expression and its clinical significance in HPV-associated cervical cancer and to explore whether BMSCs regulate malignant phenotypes through miR-129.
METHODS: miR-129 expression was measured by qRT-PCR in 77 cervical cancer and 30 normal cervical tissues. Associations with clinicopathological features and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Diagnostic value was assessed by ROC curve. Rat BMSCs were co-cultured with SiHa and HeLa cells. Following miR-129 overexpression or knockdown, cell proliferation (CCK-8, colony formation), invasion (Transwell) and expression of E-cadherin, N-cadherin and MRP1 (Western blot) were examined.
RESULTS: miR-129 expression was significantly higher in cervical cancer tissues than in normal controls (3.24±0.56 vs. 1.00±0.32, P<0.05). High miR-129 expression correlated with tumor size ≥3 cm (P=0.009), FIGO stage III-IV (P=0.0034) and lymph node metastasis (P=0.038). High expression was associated with shorter OS (median: 28.4 vs. 46.2 months; HR=2.944, 95%CI:1.484-5.842, P=0.002). The AUC was 0.788 (95%CI:0.693-0.884), with a cut-off of 1.85 (sensitivity:76.9%, specificity:70.4%). BMSC co-culture upregulated miR-129 expression (SiHa: 3.52±0.42 vs. 1.00±0.08, P<0.01). miR-129 overexpression promoted proliferation, colony formation and invasion, while knockdown suppressed these phenotypes. Overexpression of miR-129 reduced E-cadherin (0.42±0.05 vs. 1.00±0.08, P<0.01) and increased N-cadherin (2.85±0.22 vs. 1.00±0.10, P<0.01) and MRP1 (2.46±0.18 vs. 1.00±0.09, P<0.01). Knockdown of miR-129 partially reversed BMSC-induced changes in these proteins.
CONCLUSION: miR-129 is significantly upregulated in HPV-associated cervical cancer and shows potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. BMSCs upregulate miR-129 in cervical cancer cells and miR-129 modulates proliferation, invasion, EMT marker expression and MRP1 expression. These findings suggest that the BMSCs/miR-129 axis may contribute to cervical cancer progression, but further in-vivo and mechanistic studies are needed.

articles.title: A dual-functional quinoline-coumarin receptor for the selective "turn-on" sensing of Cu2+ ions: environmental monitoring and cancer cell studies.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.authors: Riyazur Rahman F, Sangeetha NS, Kannan JC et al.
articles.abstract: The sensing of metal ions has become a major area of research due to their environmental and biological importance. Cu2+ ions were sensed using a probe ((E)-6-methyl-3-((2-(4-(2-oxo-2H-chromen-3-yl)oxazol-2-yl)hydrazono)methyl)quinolin-2(1H)-one) named as 6MeQOC. This was derived by appending quinoline and coumarin derivatives using the Hantzsch cyclization technique. Further, spectral characterizations were performed to confirm the formation of 6MeQOC. The sensing ability of 6MeQOC towards Cu2+ ions was determined using the spectrophotometric and spectrofluorimetric methods. Subsequently, the selectivity and sensitivity of 6MeQOC towards Cu2+ ions were evaluated. The limit of detection (LoD) and binding constant were found to be 13.7383 × 10-8 M and 7.43 ± 0.10 × 104 M-1, respectively, and the Job's plot analysis revealed a 1 : 1 (metal : probe) ratio. The practical application of 6MeQOC in real-sample analysis was examined by spiking Cu2+ into water samples collected from various sources such as tap water and drinking water. Further, the cytotoxic effects of 6MeQOC and 6MeQOC-Cu2+ in HeLa (human cervical cancer cell line) and A549 (human lung cancer cell line) cell lines were studied using the MTT assay. Conclusively, the probe has dual applications, both environmental and biological. This work presents its extended utility in both the environmental and biological domains.

articles.title: Obstetric violence and associated factors among postpartum women in Turkey: A cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Aslan M, Dinç Kaya H, Günaydın S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to determine the level of reported obstetric violence among women who had given birth in Turkey and to identify the factors associated with reported obstetric violence.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, descriptive study was carried out between October 1 and December 30, 2024. The sample comprised 286 women aged 18 years or older, within their first postpartum year, who had given birth in Turkey. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form and the Obstetric Violence Scale (OVS) and were analyzed with SPSS.
RESULTS: In unadjusted analyses, higher OVS scores were associated with unplanned pregnancy, cesarean birth, postpartum complications, inadequate information, lack of consent, and several intervention-intensive childbirth practices (P < 0.05). In multivariable negative binomial regression, postpartum complications (aIRR = 1.42, 95% CI = 1.01-2.00), lack of information during labor (aIRR = 2.40, 95% CI = 1.43-4.03), prolonged fasting (aIRR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.09-2.35), prolonged bed rest (aIRR = 3.07, 95% CI = 1.87-5.04), continuous non-stress test (NST) (aIRR = 1.56, 95% CI = 1.07-2.29), vacuum extraction (aIRR = 2.83, 95% CI = 1.18-6.80), and fundal pressure (aIRR = 2.29, 95% CI = 1.34-3.94) remained independently associated with higher total OVS scores.
CONCLUSION: Reported obstetric violence was independently associated with several care-related factors, particularly lack of information during labor and selected intervention-intensive practices. These findings underscore the importance of respectful maternity care, effective communication, and careful evaluation of obstetric interventions.

articles.title: Fetal head station and head circumference at second-stage onset and likelihood of vaginal delivery in nulliparous women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Gilboa I, Wertheimer KO, Gabbai D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to evaluate the combined association of fetal head station (FHS) at second-stage onset and fetal head circumference (HC) with the likelihood of spontaneous vaginal delivery (SVD) in nulliparous women.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included nulliparous women with singleton, vertex-presenting, term pregnancies (≥37 weeks) who reached the second stage of labor between 2013 and 2023 at a tertiary medical center. FHS was categorized as above, at, or below the ischial spines. HC, measured by ultrasound within 14 days before delivery, was dichotomized as <350 mm or ≥350 mm. Participants were classified into six FHS-HC groups. The primary outcome was SVD. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 4230 women, SVD rates ranged from 57.7% for FHS above the ischial spines with HC ≥350 mm to 88.7% for FHS below the ischial spines with HC ≥350 mm. Compared with the reference group (FHS below the ischial spines and HC <350 mm), the adjusted odds of SVD decreased with higher station: adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.73 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.60-0.88) for station at the ischial spines and 0.59 (95% CI 0.44-0.80) for station above the ischial spines. Among women with HC ≥350 mm, those with FHS above the ischial spines had the lowest likelihood of SVD (aOR 0.35; 95% CI 0.14-0.82). Higher FHS and larger HC were associated with longer second-stage duration (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: FHS at second-stage onset was more strongly associated with SVD than was HC. Combined FHS-HC assessment may help identify women at increased likelihood of operative delivery and support closer monitoring of labor progress.

articles.title: Urinary incontinence burden and phenotype transitions after colpocleisis in older women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Wang Q, Jiang X, Lin C
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study characterizes urinary incontinence (UI) burden and symptom-based UI phenotype transitions 1 year after colpocleisis in older women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included women aged 60 years or older undergoing colpocleisis for advanced or recurrent pelvic organ prolapse between August 2019 and May 2025. Paired analyses included women with 1-year urinary follow-up. UI burden was assessed using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF), and symptom-based phenotypes were classified as stress UI (SUI), urgency UI (UUI), or mixed UI (MUI).
RESULTS: Of 505 women, 495 completed 1-year follow-up; 258 had preoperative UI. Any UI decreased from 52.1% to 39.8% (paired absolute risk difference -12.3 percentage points, 95% confidence interval [CI] -17.8 to -6.7; P < 0.001). The median ICIQ-SF total score declined from 4.0 (interquartile range [IQR] 0.0-7.0) to 0.0 (IQR 0.0-5.0), with a Hodges-Lehmann paired estimate of -0.5 (95% CI -1.5 to 0.0; P < 0.001). UUI and MUI decreased, whereas SUI increased modestly. Among 237 women without preoperative UI, 65 (27.4%) developed de novo UI, of which 55.4% was slight and none was very severe. Baseline UUI most often transitioned to no UI, whereas baseline MUI showed the broadest postoperative distribution.
CONCLUSION: Colpocleisis was associated with reduced UI burden and distinct symptom-based phenotype transitions at 1 year. Descriptive transition patterns might inform preoperative counseling but should not be interpreted as an individual prediction tool.

articles.title: Liver function following preterm birth: long-term implications for metabolic health.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.authors: Yakubu I, Berry MJ, Dyson RM et al.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth affects one in ten infants and represents one of the major early life insults with long-term health implications. Among the organs most disrupted is the liver, crucial for metabolism, detoxification and general systemic function. While the early clinical signs like neonatal cholestasis are well documented, the molecular mechanisms underlying hepatic dysfunction remain poorly characterised. In this review, we explore the potential hepatic molecular alterations associated with preterm birth that may influence early life programming of metabolic dysfunction. First, we present normal liver function and the potential effect of preterm birth on liver development and function. Second, we review metabolic adaptation in the neonatal period following preterm birth and highlight findings of perturbed circulating and tissue metabolites in both preterm human cohorts and animal models. These altered metabolites are associated with disruption of glucose and insulin homeostasis; alterations in lipid metabolism and lipoprotein profiles; impaired bile acid metabolism; perturbations in amino acid and protein metabolism; oxidative stress and antioxidant imbalance; as well as hormonal, growth factor and immune dysregulation. Finally, we examine whether these metabolic perturbations resolve or persist during maturation and consider their potential contribution to adverse metabolic outcomes later in life. Although many of the metabolic perturbations appear to normalise, evidence suggests persistent alterations in insulin signalling and lipid metabolism. Despite growing evidence across the life course following preterm birth, the molecular mechanisms linking early hepatic alterations with later adverse metabolic outcomes remain poorly defined. Epidemiological studies nevertheless demonstrate increased risks of insulin resistance, dyslipidaemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and type 2 diabetes in individuals born preterm.

articles.title: The impact of pre-pregnancy underweight on the risk of perineal and anal sphincter injury in nulliparous women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Gabbai D, Dominsky O, Attali E et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perineal injury is a common complication of vaginal delivery with maternal consequences. Although the effects of obesity are established, the impact of underweight on perineal and obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI), remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to determine the association between pre-pregnancy underweight and the risk of non-severe perineal injury (NSPI) and OASI in nulliparous women.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single, tertiary medical center including nulliparous women aged 18-45 years with singleton term vaginal deliveries (≥37 weeks) and pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) <25 kg/m2 between 2012 and 2024. Women with diabetes were excluded. The cohort was divided into underweight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2) and normal BMI groups. The primary outcome was NSPI, and the secondary outcome was OASI. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess independent associations.
RESULTS: Overall, 32 112 women were included, 12.9% of whom were underweight. Underweight women had lower birthweights and lower rates of induction and occiput-posterior presentation (all P < 0.05). NSPI occurred slightly less frequently among underweight women than among women with normal BMI (81.5% vs 84.3%, P < 0.001), whereas OASI was more common (1.1% vs 0.8%, P = 0.033). In the fully adjusted model, underweight BMI was associated with slightly lower odds of NSPI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.905; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.825-0.994) and higher odds of OASI (aOR 1.641; 95% CI 1.179-2.286). Additional factors associated with OASI in the fully adjusted model included higher birthweight per 100 g increment (aOR 1.132; 95% CI 1.096-1.169), occiput-posterior presentation (aOR 2.815; 95% CI 1.806-4.386), prolonged second stage (aOR 1.590; 95% CI 1.158-2.182), and vacuum-assisted delivery (aOR 2.304; 95% CI 1.666-3.187).
CONCLUSION: Pre-pregnancy underweight was associated with slightly lower odds of NSPI but higher odds of OASI.

articles.title: Mid-trimester sum-estimated fetal weight and gestational diabetes risk in twin pregnancies.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.authors: Justman N, Carny DM, Beloosesky R et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is more prevalent in twin pregnancies, yet screening strategies remain largely based on singleton data. In the present study, we aimed to evaluate whether the mid-trimester sum of estimated fetal weights (sum-EFW) at the anatomy scan is associated with subsequent GDM in twin pregnancies.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of twin pregnancies undergoing routine mid-trimester ultrasound (2010-2025) at a tertiary center. Sum-EFW was calculated as the combined estimated fetal weight of both fetuses. The primary outcome was GDM. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed discriminative performance and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors.
RESULTS: Among 728 women, 70 (9.6%) developed GDM. Sum-EFW was higher in GDM pregnancies (1177 ± 187.9 vs. 1103 ± 178.8 g; P = 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated modest discriminative ability (area under the curve [AUC] 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.55-0.69; P = 0.001). After adjustment for gestational age, discrimination was similar (AUC 0.586; 95% CI: 0.518-0.655; P = 0.013), with sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 47.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) 12.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 93.1% at the optimal threshold. A cutoff of 1130 g identified a higher-risk subgroup (14.3% vs. 6.3%; P = 0.001). In multivariable analysis, maternal age ≥ 30 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.45; 95% CI: 1.10-5.45), body mass index (BMI) ≥30 (aOR 5.48; 95% CI: 2.33-12.85), and sum-EFW ≥1130 g (aOR 3.21; 95% CI: 1.41-7.34) were independently associated with GDM.
CONCLUSION: In twin pregnancies, a higher mid-trimester sum-EFW is independently associated with subsequent GDM. These findings suggest that combined fetal growth may reflect early metabolic alterations in twin gestations. Discrimination remains modest, limiting use as a screening or risk-stratification tool.

articles.title: Female Life Stages for Cardiovascular Disease Prevention and Management in Girls and Women: A Case-Based Approach.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.authors: Lau ES, Faubion S, Gangopadhyaya A et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death among women in the United States and worldwide, yet current approaches to prevention and management do not fully account for female-specific biology. To address this need, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, published a Presidential Advisory defining the Female Life Stage construct, which defines four distinct stages across the life course: Perimenarche (Stage 1), Ovarian Cycling (Stage 2), Perimenopause (Stage 3), and Postmenopause (Stage 4), with pregnancy including the time before and after (Peripregnancy period) recognized as a distinct life period when cardiovascular risk may be modified.1 To provide examples of how this framework and the accompanying consensus guidance published in an accompanying Scientific Statement can be translated into a personalized care approach, this special report presents six hypothetical cases spanning the Female Life Stages, including adolescence and young adulthood, the peripartum period, midlife, perimenopause, and postmenopause.2 These cases illustrate how a female-specific life course framework that reflects hormonally-mediated physiologic transitions can promote earlier recognition of cardiovascular risk, guide cardiovascular screening and inform cardiovascular management. The cases underscore how hormonal health (e.g., menstrual cycle assessment, pregnancy planning and prevention, assessing and managing perimenopausal and postmenopausal symptoms) and psychosocial health (e.g., anxiety, depression, disordered eating) have cardiovascular implications. Moreover, this approach integrates well-established female-specific cardiovascular risk factors (e.g., premature menopause and adverse pregnancy outcomes), in addition to less well-recognized risk factors (e.g., early menarche, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome). We also review key evidence to inform a patient-centered approach to exogenous hormone therapy and associated cardiovascular risks for a variety of indications, including management of abnormal uterine bleeding, ovarian suppression, pregnancy prevention, and menopausal symptoms. By contextualizing the Female Life Stage framework within practical case scenarios, this article provides clinicians with a structured, evidence-based approach to improve cardiovascular prevention and management for…

articles.title: Frailty Is Associated With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Adults With and Without HIV.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
articles.authors: Abelman RA, Ma Y, Margolick JB et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is a risk factor for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in older adults. People with HIV (PWH) have a heightened frailty burden, but the association of HIV and frailty with LUTS in people with and at risk for HIV is unknown.
