METHODS: Data from 1356 PWH (505 men, 851 women) and 820 without HIV (419 men, 401 women) enrolled in the MACS-WIHS Combined Cohort Study who completed the Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network 10-Item Symptom Index (LURN SI-10) from 10/2021 to 9/2022 were included. Frailty was determined using the Fried frailty phenotype (robust, pre-frail, and frail). Regression models stratified by sex evaluated the cross-sectional associations of HIV and frailty with LUTS severity, urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), and overactive bladder (OAB). Due to low prevalence in men, mixed urinary incontinence (MUI) was analyzed only in women. Effect modification by sex and HIV was tested using the interaction terms with frailty.
RESULTS: Mean age was 56 years (SD 11), and 58% of participants were Black. For women, 53% were pre-frail and 23% were frail. For men, 46% were pre-frail and 13% were frail. There was no association of HIV with LUTS. Among women, 21% reported UUI, 61% reported OAB, and 14% reported MUI at least weekly. Compared to robust women, frail women had higher LURN SI-10 scores (absolute difference = 3.3 (95% CI: 2.3, 4.3)). Similarly, frail men had higher LURN SI-10 scores than robust men (absolute difference = 1.6 (95% CI: 0.4, 2.9)). Frailty was associated with greater odds of UUI and OAB in women and men, and MUI in women. There was no evidence of effect modification by sex.
CONCLUSIONS: LUTS are common in people with and at-risk for HIV and are more severe among those who are frail. More research is needed to investigate the sex-independent mechanisms that underlie frailty and LUTS in this population.

articles.title: Alpha-mangostin combined with doxorubicin-loaded hydrogel for the treatment of ovarian cancer.
articles.authors: Liu X, Zhou W, Chen L et al.
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies of the female reproductive system and a gynecological malignancy with a high mortality rate. Alpha-mangostin is a xanthone derivative with anticancer activity that can increase the sensitivity of ovarian cancer cells to doxorubicin, and the combination of the two drugs exerts a synergistic therapeutic effect. However, the poor solubility of α-mangostin limits its application. To solve this problem, we prepared an α-mangostin nanoformulation via self-assembly using the film dispersion method. The formulation had a uniform particle size of approximately 58 nm, a stable nanostructure and good water solubility. Hydrogels, as good thermosensitive drug delivery systems, enable sustained and controlled release of drugs. Accordingly, we utilized the synergistic efficacy of the α-mangostin nanoformulation combined with doxorubicin and used a thermosensitive hydrogel carrier to jointly treat ovarian cancer. In vitro, the combined treatment achieved better effects than either drug alone in inducing ovarian cancer cell apoptosis, inhibiting ovarian cancer cell proliferation, and inducing cell cycle arrest. In vivo, this composite formulation effectively inhibited tumor growth by inducing ovarian cancer cell apoptosis, inhibiting tumor cell proliferation, and suppressing tumor angiogenesis, and effectively inhibited ascites formation, achieving a better antitumor effect than either drug alone. In summary, the composite hydrogel co-loaded with α-mangostin nanoformulation and doxorubicin represents a promising and effective strategy for the treatment of ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Fasting triglyceride-glucose index and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: an observational study of metabolic risk in singleton pregnancies.
articles.authors: Brenisin M, Lovasova E, Novakova J et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the fasting TyG index and gestational hypertension/preeclampsia (GH/PE) in singleton pregnancies.
METHODS: This observational study included 175 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies examined during routine antenatal care between 11 and 35 weeks of gestation from January 2023 to December 2024. Women with pre-existing hypertension, diabetes, renal disease, gestational diabetes mellitus or major systemic disorders were excluded. Clinical, anthropometric and fasting biochemical data were collected, and the TyG index was calculated as ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Group comparisons, correlation analyses, logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine women (22.3 %) developed GH/PE. Compared with women with physiological pregnancies, women with GH/PE had higher pre-gestational BMI, gestational weight change, blood pressure, fasting glucose, triglycerides and TyG index values (all p≤0.018). The TyG index correlated positively with mean arterial pressure (r=0.20, p=0.027) and gestational week at assessment (r=0.35, p<0.001). Higher TyG index values were associated with increased odds of GH/PE (OR=3.75, 95 % CI 1.79-7.85). A TyG cut-off of 8.6 showed 58.97 % sensitivity and 69.85 % specificity, with an AUC of 0.69 (95 % CI 0.59-0.79).
CONCLUSIONS: In this antenatal cohort, the fasting TyG index was associated with GH/PE and showed moderate discriminatory ability. The TyG index should not be used as a stand-alone diagnostic test, but it may complement BMI and routine clinical assessment in identifying women with increased metabolic susceptibility to hypertensive pregnancy disorders.

articles.title: Prevalence of bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis and vulvovaginal candidiasis among symptomatic women attending selected health centers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
articles.authors: Gesese YA, Abegaz WE, Mihret A et al.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSymptomatic vaginal discharge caused by bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, and vulvovaginal candidiasis is a common gynecological issue among reproductive-age women in Sub-Saharan Africa.ObjectivesThis study aimed to determine etiologies and associated risk factors in symptomatic women attending selected health centers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.DesignA cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2023 to October 2024, on 347 symptomatic women.MethodsSaline, KOH wet-mount and gram-stain microscopy was used to diagnose trichomoniasis, vulvovaginal candidiasis and bacterial vaginosis respectively. Descriptive analysis and multivariate logistic regressions identified factors associated with outcomes.ResultsThe overall prevalence of overall vaginal infection was 55.6%, led by bacterial vaginosis (44.4%), vulvovaginal candidiasis (20.6%) and trichomoniasis (12.7%). The most common co-infection was BV and VVC (10.1%), followed by BV and TV (4.9%) and VVC+TV (2.0%). Triple infection was detected in 0.9% (95% CI: 0.2-2.5%) of participants. Cigarette smoking was protective against bacterial vaginosis (AOR = 0.57, p = 0.029). Trichomoniasis risk lowered with increasing age (25-34 years: AOR = 0.29, p = 0.001; 35-44 years: AOR = 0.06, p = 0.006) and showed a frequency-dependent association with traditional "Weyba tis" use: protective at less than once monthly (AOR = 0.29, p = 0.007) but a risk factor for at higher frequencies (AOR = 4.01, p = 0.003). Vulvovaginal candidiasis showed lower odds in women with 3 to 5 lifetime sexual partners (AOR = 0.18, p = 0.005).ConclusionsOur study revealed relatively high prevalence vaginal infections highlighting the need for regular assessment and targeted reproductive health education. Larger studies with comprehensive behavioral assessment and etiologic testing are warranted to better elucidate the predictor variables.

articles.title: Time-varying association of first-line bevacizumab with progression-free survival in advanced ovarian cancer: A multicenter matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Katić K, Čerina Pavlinović D, Canjko I et al.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials have demonstrated that first-line bevacizumab extends progression-free survival (PFS) in advanced ovarian cancer. However, its long-term effectiveness in routine clinical practice remains unclear. This study investigated the time-varying association between first-line bevacizumab and PFS in patients newly diagnosed with advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer. Our retrospective cohort, drawn from four Croatian centers, included 249 eligible patients. After coarsened exact matching (CEM), 175 patients were retained: 102 received first-line bevacizumab, and 73 received no bevacizumab in either the first or second line. We used CEM-weighted, center-stratified Cox models to estimate log-time-varying and piecewise associations. A 2,000-replication full-process bootstrap determined 36-month restricted mean survival time (RMST) differences. Overall survival (OS) was a key secondary outcome. The PFS association varied significantly over time (interaction p < 0.001). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were: 0.12 (0.04-0.34) at 3 months, 0.69 (0.47-1.02) at 12 months and 2.81 (1.22-6.47) at 36 months. However, the piecewise HR beyond 24 months was 1.36 (0.61-3.05), influenced by sparse late risk sets. The 36-month PFS RMST difference was 3.42 months (95% CI, -0.18 to 7.40), and the OS HR was 1.15 (0.74-1.76). In a sensitivity analysis, where exposure was defined solely by first-line treatment, 217 patients were matched. Here, the 3-month PFS HR was 0.33 (0.14-0.78), the 36-month PFS RMST difference was 0.50 months (-3.02 to 4.14), and the OS HR was 1.47 (1.02-2.10). The 36-month OS RMST difference remained consistent with no significant difference. First-line bevacizumab was linked to a lower early risk of progression or death. However, this association diminished over time and was sensitive to how exposure was defined. Limitations such as calendar-period separation, sparse late follow-up data, and potential residual confounding prevent causal interpretation and do not establish definitive late benefit or harm.

articles.title: Mobile cervical screening: using an opportunistic screening service to increase uptake in underserved communities.
articles.journal: Nursing standard (Royal College of Nursing (Great Britain) : 1987)
articles.authors: West J, Green E
articles.abstract: Attendance rates for the cervical screening programme and the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme in England have fallen since 2022. Women and all people with a cervix from underserved communities are known to have lower screening attendance rates than other groups, so it is vital to address barriers to attendance to increase screening uptake. This article describes a service innovation pilot project in north west England involving the delivery of opportunistic cervical screening via a mobile screening unit sited in convenient community locations. The aim was to identify precancerous changes and promote early treatment for moderate-to-severe dyskaryosis by increasing attendance rates among underserved communities. A total of 2,283 clients completed a cervical screen during the pilot period (between July 2024 and March 2026). Analysis showed that a significant percentage (44%, n =994) of clients were from the two lowest deciles of the Index of Multiple Deprivation; half ( n =1,145, 50%) of completed screens were for clients designated as 'non-responders' to screening invitations; 101 (4%) clients were referred for colposcopy; and 18 (1%) clients were identified as having high-grade dyskaryosis. Patient experience feedback suggests that the opportunistic nature of the service was a significant incentive for clients to attend for screening. The project is ongoing and the service aims to expand to cover the whole of NHS England North West.

articles.title: A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
articles.authors: Khan SS, Grobman WA, Perak AM et al.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

articles.title: Brain Dead and Pregnant: The Moral Erasure of the Pregnant Person.
articles.authors: Johnson LSM
articles.abstract: When brain death/death by neurologic criteria occurs during pregnancy, unique and complex questions emerge concerning the ethical and legal status of the brain dead pregnant person, the continuation of life-sustaining treatment for the sake of a fetus, the posthumous exploitation of pregnant bodies, and potential conflicts between the preferences and interests of pregnant persons and others. In a setting of increasing restrictions on abortion and infringements of the medical and reproductive rights of pregnant persons, several states have enacted laws that prohibit the withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment from pregnant patients, resulting in cases of brain dead, pregnant persons being maintained without consent, against their own wishes and the wishes of their families. This paper considers the ethical implications of antiabortion laws and brain death guidelines for pregnant patients, and how both have the effect of erasing the pregnant person from ethical consideration.

articles.title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
articles.authors: Khan SS, Grobman WA, Angell S et al.
articles.abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

articles.title: Comparison of Growth Pattern in Children Conceived by Assisted Reproductive Technology with or without Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Bagheri-Lankarani N, Madani S, Shahsavand M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) has been associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) as well as various obstetric and perinatal complications. However, the long-term growth trajectories of children conceived via ART in the context of maternal GDM remain unclear. This prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the effect of GDM on growth parameters among children conceived through ART or spontaneous conception (SC).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The prospective cohort study enrolled 420 children aged 3-5 years, who were categorized into four groups: ART, ART-GDM, SC-GDM, and SC. Growth assessments included height, weight, and body mass index (BMI), which were extracted from medical records at birth and during follow-up visits at ages 3 and 5 years. Anthropometric data were standardized using age- and sex-adjusted Z-scores. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS and included Chi-square tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests for normality, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and post hoc comparisons.
RESULTS: Children in the GDM-exposed groups tended to be shorter at birth, with the ART-GDM group showing the highest prevalence of obesity by age 5. Children conceived by ART, particularly those exposed to GDM, were significantly heavier than their SC counterparts. At birth, mean height and weight in the ART, ART-GDM, and GDM groups approximated the 50th percentile. Catch-up growth was evident by age 3, and by age 5, all groups exhibited comparable mean height and weight, with no significant sex-based differences.
CONCLUSION: Despite being shorter and lighter at birth, children conceived via ART appeared to achieve growth parameters comparable to their peers by preschool age, suggesting compensatory growth. Nonetheless, further longitudinal research is warranted to clarify these findings. Healthcare providers should prioritize the monitoring and management of pregnancies complicated by GDM following assisted conception.

articles.title: Analysis of Trauma in Pregnancy in the State's Only Adult Level I Trauma Center.
articles.authors: Hope BC, Ounpraseuth S, Tyrer S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Trauma in pregnancy is an important determinate of maternal/perinatal morbidity and mortality. The study purpose is to evaluate all pregnant trauma patients presenting to the state's primary trauma center to develop a better understanding of the influence of trauma on pregnancy and identify improvement areas in maternal/perinatal outcomes.
METHODS: This is a retrospective study of all pregnant women who presented with documented trauma and on whom we had delivery information on mother and neonate from January 2015 through December 2022. Demographic and clinical characteristics, type of trauma, trauma-related outcomes, disposition, and mode of delivery were collected. Results are reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and statistical significance was defined as p-value less than 0.05.
RESULTS: There were 1143 patients identified. Mechanism of injury included falls (n=479, 41.91%), motor vehicle accidents (MVAs; n=464, 40.59%), assault (n=164, 14.35%) and other (n=164, 14.35%). Among patients kept for observation, the largest percentage followed MVA (n=131, 28.2%). Delivery was directly related to trauma in 28 pregnancies (2.45%). Overall, 147 neonates required NICU admission (12.88%), 27 required transport to higher-level of care (2.37%), and 26 deliveries resulted in stillbirth/neonatal demise (2.28%). After gestational-age group adjustment at the time of trauma, MVAs were associated with higher odds of trauma-related delivery (adjOR 8.00, 95% CI 2.59-24.72) and trauma-related complications (adjOR 7.24, 95% CI 2.90-18.07) compared with falls. Assault was associated with higher odds of trauma-related complications (adjOR 4.25, 95% CI 1.28-14.18), neonatal complications (adjOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.03-2.56), and NICU admission (adjOR 1.75, 95% CI 1.05-2.90) compared to falls.
CONCLUSIONS: Study results are consistent with published literature, demonstrating that a small subset will develop significant maternal/perinatal complications. This study supports the assumption that while most patients may be safely managed expectantly, those with higher-energy mechanisms may warrant increased clinical vigilance and potentially extended monitoring.

articles.title: Relationship Between Dominant Follicle Diameter on the hCG Trigger Day and Live Birth After Modified Natural Cycle Frozen Embryo Transfer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Huang C, Jiang Y, Liu J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of dominant follicular diameter at hCG trigger on live birth rate (LBR) in modified natural cycle frozen-thawed embryo transfer (mNC-FET) remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate this relationship and explore whether flexible triggering based on follicle size is acceptable.
METHODS: A retrospective study included 1669 mNC-FET cycles. The cycles were divided according to the dominant follicle diameter on the hCG day: ≥16 mm (n = 1439) and <16 mm (n = 230). The LBR was compared between the groups, and multivariate logistic regression was performed. A subgroup analysis stratified by maternal age (≥ 35 years) was conducted.
RESULTS: Overall, the LBR did not significantly differ between the <16 mm groups (49.0% vs 43.9%, P = 0.152; adjusted OR = 0.878, 95% CI 0.626-1.230). Among advanced-age women (≥35 years), the ≥16 mm group showed a significantly higher LBR (40.2% vs 28.0%, P = 0.048), but multivariate analysis revealed no independent association after adjusting for confounders (aOR = 0.963, 95% CI 0.517-1.791, P = 0.904).
CONCLUSION: Dominant follicular diameter on the hCG day was not independently associated with the live birth rate in mNC-FET. The crude difference seen in women aged advanced-age women (≥35 yeaadjustment and should be viewed as hypothesis-generating rather than effect modification. Flexible triggering may be acceptable, while maternal age remains a key clinical consideration in individualizing trigger timing.

articles.title: Emergent challenges: Eclampsia case series in primigravida Rohingya refugees of Malaysia.
articles.authors: Zakour Khadari M, Zainal H, Athirah Daud NA et al.
articles.abstract: Eclampsia, a serious and life-threatening complication of pregnancy, affects women in low-income and vulnerable populations. This case series describes the clinical management of two young Rohingya refugee women, aged 17 and 21, who presented with eclampsia at Seberang Jaya Hospital, Penang, Malaysia. Both patients reported prodromal symptoms of severe headache and visual disturbances before experiencing generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Treatment involved intravenous magnesium sulfate for seizure control and labetalol for blood pressure control, in accordance with local clinical guidelines. Notably, the 17-year-old patient's recovery was complicated by concurrent dengue fever, which presented additional management challenges. Neonatal outcomes varied significantly: the first infant had an Apgar score of 3 at 1 min and a birth weight of 1.7 kg, while the second infant had a healthier outcome, with an Apgar score of 9 and a birth weight of 3 kg. These cases emphasize the critical need for timely diagnosis, standardized treatment protocols, and comprehensive maternal and neonatal care in managing eclampsia among vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Perioperative Model for Predicting Early Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting After Gynecologic Laparoscopic Surgery.
articles.authors: Zheng Z, Wu Q, Zhou Y
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) is a frequent complication after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. The classic Apfel score is widely used for risk assessment, but its individual-level discrimination may be limited in this relatively homogeneous high-risk population.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center prospective observational model-development study of 487 patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia. Nineteen candidate predictors were considered. Exploratory univariable screening (P<0.10), followed by backward elimination using the Akaike information criterion, was used to derive the multivariable logistic model. The blood-loss cut-point was selected by comparing candidate cut-points that retained at least 10% of patients in each group. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples in which the complete screening, cut-point selection, and backward-elimination procedure was repeated.
RESULTS: Overall, 216 patients (44.4%) developed 0-24 h PONV. The final eight-predictor model had an apparent AUC of 0.706 and Brier score of 0.214. After bootstrap correction of the complete development procedure, the AUC was 0.666, the Brier score was 0.229, the calibration slope was 0.793, and the calibration intercept was -0.001. The apparent AUC exceeded that of the Apfel score (0.586; paired DeLong difference 0.121, 95% CI 0.070-0.171; P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: The perioperative model showed moderate apparent discrimination, which decreased after correction for model-development optimism. The model is preliminary and requires prospective external validation, recalibration where necessary, and clinical-impact evaluation before routine use.

articles.title: Burning Mouth Syndrome Among Postmenopausal Women: A Clinic-Based, Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.authors: S R A, Suragimath G, Suragimath DG
articles.abstract: Introduction Menopause is a physiological transition associated with several systemic and oral changes. Burning mouth syndrome (BMS), characterized by persistent or recurrent intraoral burning in the absence of an identifiable local or systemic cause, predominantly affects middle-aged and postmenopausal women. This study aimed to determine the clinic-based frequency of BMS and describe its demographic and clinical characteristics among postmenopausal women attending an oral medicine clinic. Materials and methods This cross-sectional observational study was conducted at the Department of Oral Medicine and Radiology of the School of Dental Sciences, Krishna Vishwa Vidyapeeth, Maharashtra, India. A total of 1,230 postmenopausal women were screened between January 2025 and December 2025, of whom 278 were excluded because they did not meet the eligibility criteria or declined participation. The remaining 952 eligible participants were included in the analysis. Data regarding demographic variables, systemic comorbidities, medication history, and clinical characteristics of BMS, as well as associated subjective symptoms like oral dryness and taste disturbances, were recorded. Descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi-square test were used for analysis, with a p value <0.05 considered statistically significant. Results Of the study participants, 26.5% (n=252) had BMS, with the largest proportion of women belonging to the age group of 55-59 years. Hypertension was the most prevalent systemic comorbidity, followed by diabetes mellitus. BMS symptoms were most commonly reported during the daytime, with the tongue being the most commonly affected site. Among women with BMS, oral dryness was reported most frequently in the age group of 60-65 years, whereas taste disturbances were most frequently reported in the age group of 55-59 years. Conclusion BMS was observed in one-fourth of the postmenopausal participants, with the tongue being the most commonly affected site and oral dryness and taste disturbances being frequent accompanying symptoms. Given the single-centre, cross-sectional design, the findings should be interpreted within the context of the study population and cannot establish causal relationships. Early recognition, exclusion of secondary causes, and appropriate multidisciplinary management may facilitate better clinical care for affected postmenopausal women.

articles.title: The Epidemiology and Associated Factors of Ectopic Pregnancy in Saudi Arabia: A Literature Review.
articles.authors: Alkathiri M, Almousa A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic pregnancy (EP) is a serious maternal complication with a worldwide prevalence of about 2%. It is defined as the implantation of the product of conception outside the uterine cavity. Patients with EP may present with a wide range of clinical symptoms, including abdominal/pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, missed menstrual cycle, and an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound. After diagnosing EPs, medical and/or surgical treatment options are available based on the patient's hemodynamic status, ectopic location, fetal cardiac activity, size of the gestational sac, level of β-HCG, and patient profile.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative literature review aims to summarize published primary studies on the epidemiology and reported associated factors of EP in Saudi Arabia between 2000 and 2024.
RESULTS: A total of 1342 EP cases were reported across the included studies. Reported prevalence estimates ranged from 0.23% to 1.20%. The reviewed studies were from different regions of the Kingdom, including Abha, Khamis Mushait, Yanbu, Makkah, Madina, Jeddah, Khobar, and Majmaah. The prevalence of EPs fluctuated between 2000 and 2019 and had three peaks: 1.13% (2012), 1.14% (2013), and 1.2% (2019). Multiple associated factors linked to EP were reported in this review, including a history of pelvic surgery, C-sections, previous EP, abortions, intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) use, and pelvic inflammatory diseases (PIDs).
CONCLUSIONS: EP is a serious complication that causes significant maternal morbidity and mortality and has a substantial burden on the healthcare system. In this review, eleven studies were reviewed regarding the epidemiology of EPs in the Kingdom. No clear pattern or trend in prevalence was identified, although the majority of studies reported lower EP rates than the worldwide prevalence. Several associated factors were reported across the included studies; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because most studies were retrospective and descriptive in nature.

articles.title: Recurrent belly dancer dyskinesia in pregnancy with postpartum resolution.
articles.authors: Henriques M, Ahmad A, Rodrigues S et al.
articles.abstract: Belly dancer dyskinesia (BDD) is a rare movement disorder characterized by involuntary, repetitive contractions of the abdominal wall. Pregnancy-associated BDD is exceptionally uncommon, and recurrence in subsequent pregnancies has rarely been reported. We describe the case of a 29-year-old woman in her first pregnancy who developed involuntary abdominal movements at 16 weeks. Her medical history included hypertension and multiple uterine fibroids. Neurological assessment, laboratory investigations, and spinal magnetic resonance imaging were unremarkable, and a clinical diagnosis of BDD was established. Symptoms persisted throughout pregnancy and resolved immediately after delivery. Two years later, during a second pregnancy, similar movements recurred at 15 weeks, again resolving completely after delivery. Recurrence during two consecutive pregnancies suggests a pregnancy-related trigger for BDD, and complete postpartum resolution highlights the self-limiting course of this benign condition.

articles.title: Relationship Between Psychiatric Drug Use and Cognitive Function in Women During the Menopausal Transition: An Analysis Based on the NHANES Database.
articles.authors: Jiang Y, Sun H, Ma H et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women during the menopausal transition often experience mood disorders, sleep disturbances, and cognitive decline, making the use of psychotropic drugs relatively common. However, the relationship between psychiatric drug use and cognitive function in menopausal women remains unclear.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study that included women aged 45-65 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2021-2023 cycle. Psychiatric drug use was defined based on prescription drug data, including antidepressants, benzodiazepines, and sedative-hypnotics. Cognitive function was assessed using the Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST). The Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression model was used to analyse the relationship between psychiatric drug use and cognitive function, with adjustment for potential confounders, including routine demographic characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 956 women during the menopausal transition were included in the analysis. As the number of psychotropic drugs used increased, cognitive function decline became more pronounced. Antidepressants and benzodiazepines played dominant roles in this association (posterior inclusion probability >0.9). The concurrent use of two or more psychotropic drugs was associated with an 11%-24% reduction in DSST cognitive scores. In the context of three-drug combinations, the cognitive impairment associated with antidepressants and benzodiazepines were amplified, resulting in an additional 5.1%-6.3% decrease in cognitive scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Psychiatric medication use showed a significant cross-sectional association with poorer cognitive performance among women undergoing menopausal transition, and polypharmacy regimens displayed stronger associations than single-drug regimens. Clinically, greater attention should be paid to the potential cognitive impact of psychiatric drug use in menopausal women, and polypharmacy regimens should be optimised.

articles.title: Development of an HPV Self-Collection Brochure for Unhoused Individuals Using Learner Verification and Revision.
articles.journal: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
articles.authors: Morenz AM, Inzunza-Uysal DJ, Robles-Morales R et al.
articles.abstract: Individuals who are unhoused face disproportionately high rates of cervical cancer incidence and multiple barriers to screening, yet tailored educational materials to support human papillomavirus (HPV) self-collection in this population remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a sequential, two-phased qualitative study using Learner Verification and Revision methodology to iteratively develop and refine an instructional brochure on HPV self-collection designed for, and with, individuals who are unhoused. We first conducted focus groups with community health educators (n = 6) and street medicine team members (n = 12), followed by semi-structured interviews with individuals who were unhoused (n = 19) and had participated in an HPV self-collection pilot study. Data collection assessed comprehension, attraction, cultural-linguistic acceptability, and persuasion of the brochure, with trauma-informed care as an additional domain, and transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis. Participants broadly found the brochure clear, visually appealing, and easy to follow, while identifying key areas for refinement, including greater brevity, more inclusive visuals, regional Spanish vocabulary adaptation, and language modifications to strengthen trustworthiness and empowerment. Street medicine team members emphasized that the brochure best complements verbal counseling rather than serving as a standalone resource. This community-engaged, iterative process yielded a tailored, trauma-informed educational tool which is publicly available and editable. As HPV self-collection expands across the United States, such materials will be valuable to support equitable access to cervical cancer screening.

articles.title: Mate Whenua-Follow-Up After Early Medical Abortion in New Zealand: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Wise MR, Knowles A, Talbot S et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate self-assessment with low sensitivity urine pregnancy test versus comparative serum bhCG in women having early medical abortion (EMA) for the outcomes of complete follow-up and ongoing live pregnancy.
DESIGN: Multi-centre parallel group randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: Six abortion services in Aotearoa New Zealand.
POPULATION: Pregnant women having EMA.
METHODS: Participants were randomised on a 1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, to a follow up protocol, self-assessment, or blood tests. Chi-squared tests, relative risks, and absolute risk differences (with 95% confidence intervals) were calculated.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome was complete follow-up (able to discuss follow-up test result within 6 weeks). Secondary outcomes were successful abortion; contraception; complications; and additional services.
RESULTS: There were 732 participants. More participants in the self-assessment group had complete follow-up compared to the blood test group (94.5% vs. 67.4%, p < 0.001; relative risk (RR) 1.41 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.30-1.52]). More participants in the self-assessment group had a successful EMA (89.0% vs. 81.0%, p = 0.002; RR 1.10 [95% CI: 1.03-1.17]) and more additional follow up investigations (17.3% vs. 11.1%, p = 0.017; RR 1.55 [95% CI: 1.08-2.24]). There were no differences between groups in contraception (61.0% vs. 56.0%; RR 1.09 [95% CI: 0.96-1.23]), additional health care visits (11.% vs. 10.3%; RR 1.06 [95% CI: 0.70-1.62]), community prescriptions (4.4% vs. 5.2%; RR 0.85 [95% CI: 0.44-1.63]) or complications (8.5% vs. 8.7%; RR 1.09 [95% CI: 0.96-1.23]). There was one ongoing live pregnancy detected after the first trimester.
CONCLUSIONS: The authors recommend self-assessment after EMA for improved follow-up. In addition to demonstrating clinical effectiveness and safety, the findings have important implications for improving reproductive health equity.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR): ACTRN12623000890639 (registered prospectively on 21/08/2023; https://anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=384373&isClinicalTrial=False).

articles.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
articles.authors: Kou H, Su M, Zhou J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.
METHODS: Transcriptomic, DNA methylation, and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas were integrated to construct a differentially methylated sites (DMSs)-lncRNA-mRNA network. After mapping DMSs to their corresponding differentially methylated genes (DMGs), the DMS-mediated network was further represented as a DMG-lncRNA-mRNA tripartite network. After removal of DMG nodes, a DMG-associated lncRNA-mRNA background network was constructed, and key lncRNA-mRNA pairs were prioritized according to their topological importance using weighted shortest-path calculation and PageRank-based random walk algorithms. The methylation-associated lncRNA- mRNA pair (MLMP) model was then established based on univariate Cox, LASSO Cox, and multivariate Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Eight DMG-associated lncRNA-mRNA pairs were selected to construct the MLMP model. Under a common analysis framework, the MLMP model achieved higher area under the curve (AUC) values than 17 previously published prognostic signatures for overall survival prediction. Patients in the low-MLMP group had significantly better overall survival than those in the high-MLMP group. Functional enrichment and immune microenvironment analyses indicated that the MLMP model was associated with immune-related pathways and distinct tumor immune microenvironment characteristics. Predictive analyses suggested that patients in the low-MLMP group exhibited higher predicted responsiveness to CTLA-4/PD-1 blockade and differential predicted sensitivity to several therapeutic agents.
CONCLUSIONS: The MLMP model may serve as a potential tool for prognostic stratification in EC and provide insights into methylation-associated lncRNA-mRNA interactions. The predicted associations with immunotherapy response and therapeutic sensitivity may generate hypotheses for future treatment-related studies. These findings require further validation in independent clinical cohorts and experimental studies before clinical application.

articles.title: LncRNA FLJ20021 Restrains Fibroblast Senescence and Matrix Remodeling in Pelvic Organ Prolapse by Promoting XRCC6-Dependent ADI1 Transcription.
articles.authors: Yang Y, Rui B, Rui G et al.
articles.abstract: Pelvic-organ prolapse (POP) is an age-associated disorder that is often accompanied by uterosacral ligament (USL) weakening and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation; however, the upstream regulators linking fibroblast aging to ECM remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify an uncharacterized long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), FLJ20021, as significantly downregulated in POP-derived USL tissues and primary human uterosacral-ligament fibroblasts (hUSLFs) compared with non-POP controls. FLJ20021 depletion reduces hUSLF proliferation and increases apoptosis and senescence, whereas FLJ20021 overexpression reverses these effects and shifts ECM-related markers toward a matrix-preserving profile. Mechanistically, FLJ20021 directly binds the DNA-binding domain (DBD) of X-ray repair cross-complementing 6 (XRCC6), facilitates XRCC6 occupancy at the ADI1 promoter, and promotes XRCC6-dependent ADI1 transcription. Gain- and loss-of-function as well as rescue experiments place XRCC6 downstream of FLJ20021 and support ADI1 as a required effector for FLJ20021-dependent cellular and ECM-related phenotypes. In POP-relevant murine injury models, XRCC6 and ADI1 are coordinately reduced with ECM-marker imbalance, and FLJ20021 overexpression partially restores ADI1 and ECM-related readouts in vivo. Together, these data support a model in which FLJ20021 interacts with XRCC6 to regulate ADI1 expression, thereby linking fibroblast-fate control to ECM homeostasis and providing mechanistic insight into POP-associated tissue degeneration.

articles.title: Oral Antihyperglycemic Agents Versus Insulin for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Societal Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of the SUGAR-DIP Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.authors: Broulikova HM, van der Wel AWT, Rademaker D et al.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the cost-effectiveness of treatment with sequential oral antihyperglycemic agents (OHA; metformin and glibenclamide) versus insulin for gestational diabetes (GDM).
DESIGN: Cost-effectiveness analysis from a societal and healthcare perspective alongside a randomized controlled trial (SUGAR-DIP).
SETTING: Twenty-five hospitals in the Netherlands.
POPULATION: Women with GDM and a singleton pregnancy, randomized to OHA (n = 409) or insulin (n = 411) between 16 to 34 weeks' gestation.
METHODS: Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. Differences in costs and effects were estimated using bivariate regression with bootstrapping to derive incremental cost-effectiveness ratios. Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves were constructed across a range of willingness-to-pay (WTP) thresholds.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Large for gestational age (LGA), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), costs and cost-effectiveness.
RESULTS: OHA slightly increased QALYs (0.009; 95% CI 0.004 to 0.014), corresponding to approximately 3 days in perfect health. There were no statistically significant differences in LGA avoided (-0.039; 95% CI-0.097 to 0.018) or societal costs (mean difference-€1004; 95% CI-€3503 to €1495). OHA were less costly and less effective than insulin for LGA, whereas for QALYs they were less costly and more effective. The probability of OHA being cost-effective at a WTP threshold of €0 was 79% for both outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: OHA have a high probability of being cost-effective compared with insulin for QALYs, although the QALY gain is small and of limited clinical relevance. For LGA, OHA were less costly but less effective, and cost-effectiveness depends on acceptable trade-offs between costs and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Investigating differential effects of interpregnancy interval on pregnancy complications by country development status: protocol for systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Wang RW, Ranganath A, Lee HL et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interpregnancy interval (IPI) has been reported to be associated with the risk of pregnancy complications. Short IPIs have been associated with higher risks of preterm birth, small for gestational age, low birthweight, fetal growth restriction, and perinatal mortality. However, there is limited information on how these associations differ according to the developmental status of a country. This review is therefore designed to examine the impact of the developmental status of a country on the relationship between IPI and perinatal complications.
METHODS: Studies will be identified through a comprehensive search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Global Health, LILACS, and African Index Medicus databases, using key terms including "interpregnancy interval", "birth interval", "preterm birth", "small for gestational age", "fetal growth restriction", and "perinatal mortality". Studies to be included will be screened for data reporting on IPI and relevant outcomes. The study population will consist of women with two or more singleton births. The exposure of interest is short IPI, categorised as (1) < 24 monthsmonths; ≤ 18 months; and ≤ 12 months between the birth of a child and conception of the next pregnancy. These exposure groups will be compared against the World Health Organisation recommendation of an IPI of at least 24 months. Co-primary outcomes are preterm birth, small for gestational age, fetal growth restriction, low birthweight, and perinatal mortality. The developmental status of study populations will be categorised according to the World Bank income-based country classifications for low-, middle-, and high-income countries. Studies will be included if they have an observational design and excluded if they are systematic reviews with no new data. All studies will be screened, data extracted, and bias assessed by two independent authors, with all discrepancies being resolved by consensus or the advice of a third author. If studies have a low heterogeneity (I2 < 50%), the Mantel-Haenszel method, with a fixed-effects model, will be used to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals. If studies have high heterogeneity (I2 ≥ 50%) a random-effects (inverse-variance) model will be used instead.
DISCUSSION: Results from this review have the potential to guide future recommendations on optimal IPI in both high and low-resource countries. Further, they have the potential to assist in developing health strategies to target specific…

articles.title: Predicting blastocyst viability: the role of post-vitrification re-expansion speed and its correlation with artificial collapse and preimplantation genetic testing.
articles.authors: Aizer A, Kaplan S, Noach-Hirsh M et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-thaw blastocyst behavior is clinically relevant and closely linked to implantation and pregnancy success after frozen embryo transfer. Re-expansion of the blastocyst after warming is recognized as an important indicator of embryo viability and has been associated with clinical outcomes, although it is not routinely evaluated in a dynamic manner. In addition, blastocysts undergo different laboratory procedures before vitrification, such as trophectoderm biopsy for genetic testing and artificial collapse, which may influence post-thaw re-expansion dynamics. Therefore, this study aimed to dynamically assess post-thaw blastocyst re-expansion and to evaluate its association with pregnancy outcomes, as well as to examine differences in re-expansion dynamics across different laboratory procedures.
RESULTS: A total of 463 frozen embryo transfer cycles were analyzed, including 170 cycles selected for detailed morphokinetic evaluation. Blastocysts were categorized according to pre-vitrification procedures into a Control group, a biopsy group, and an artificial collapse group. After thawing, the initial re-expansion ratio (T1) was slightly lower in the artificial collapse group compared with the Control and biopsy groups, although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.096). The artificial collapse group demonstrated a significantly higher maximal re-expansion ratio (p = 0.031) and a longer time to reach this maximum (p = 0.015). Re-expansion speed was highest in the artificial collapse group, followed by the biopsy group and the Control group, and showed a strong positive correlation with pregnancy outcomes (p = 0.011). Blastocysts in the highest Average Re-expansion Speed Rate (ARSR) quartile (≥ 5.1%) were more than three times more likely to result in pregnancy compared with those in the lowest quartile. The highest ongoing pregnancy rate was observed in the artificial collapse group (52.6%), followed by the biopsy group (41.7%) and the Control group (35.9%) (p = 0.033).
CONCLUSION: A dynamic assessment of post-thaw blastocyst re-expansion is strongly associated with pregnancy outcomes after frozen embryo transfer. Differences in re-expansion dynamics were observed between blastocysts subjected to different laboratory procedures, with artificial collapse before vitrification showing the most favorable profile. This approach may provide a useful tool for improving embryo evaluation and supporting clinical decision-making in IVF.

articles.title: Meeting report of the fifth symposium organized by the coalition to strengthen the HPV immunization community (CHIC): Nairobi, Kenya - advancing sustainable HPV vaccination programs in Africa.
articles.authors: Bolio A, Jennings MC, Burdier R et al.
articles.abstract: HPV vaccination coverage across Africa has improved substantially in recent years but remains below elimination thresholds, with persistent gaps in reaching hard-to-reach populations and growing uncertainty around future financing. This report summarizes proceedings from the fifth regional symposium of the Coalition to Strengthen the HPV Immunization Community (CHIC), held in Nairobi, Kenya, in October 2025 in collaboration with Kenya's Ministry of Health. The three-day symposium convened over 100 participants from 22 African countries, including national immunisation program managers, ministry officials, researchers, civil society representatives, and global partners (WHO, UNICEF, Gavi, PATH, the Gates Foundation). The agenda, developed through stakeholder interviews and prior scientific and advisory input, centered on six subthemes related to program sustainability. Plenary sessions addressed epidemiological trends, national policy updates including Kenya's transition to a single-dose schedule, and implications of Gavi's upcoming consolidated funding model (Gavi 6.0). Country snapshot presentations and service-delivery case studies facilitated cross-country peer learning. On day three, though an electronic poll of helped to prioritize 12 candidate implementation themes, which structured subsequent round table working groups. Countries then developed individual action plans identifying priority challenges, responsible stakeholders, and implementation timelines. Sustainable service delivery, financing, and data systems emerged as the highest-priority implementation themes. Country action plans most frequently targeted data systems strengthening, communication and community engagement, sustainable service delivery, and financing mechanisms, with additional attention to service integration, hard-to-reach populations, and target population expansion. Cross-cutting synthesis identified recurring concerns regarding HPV vaccination for people living with HIV, fragmented data systems, the role of program integration, financing sustainability under evolving donor models, and underrecognized risks from misinformation, including emerging AI-generated content. The symposium reinforced CHIC's role as a platform for peer-to-peer learning across countries at varying stages of HPV vaccine introduction, surfacing shared structural barriers to sustainability alongside country-specific action plans. Findings underscore the need for sustained political commitment, financing…

articles.title: Perinatal outcomes of growth -restricted fetus with abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform; a global systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Gashaw A, Ayele M, Abebe Y et al.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is associated with increased perinatal risks, including stillbirth, NICU admission, and neonatal complications. Doppler ultrasound helps diagnose abnormal fetal circulation in high-risk pregnancies, distinguishing IUGR from simple small-for-gestational-age fetuses. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to assess the perinatal outcomes of IUGR with abnormal umbilical artery Doppler findings, providing valuable insights for improving risk management and healthcare practices.
METHOD: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in adherence to the PRISMA guidelines. Comprehensive literature searches were performed across several global databases, including PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, Scopus, and African Online Journal databases. The pooled estimates were calculated using a weighted inverse variance random-effects model. To assess heterogeneity among the included studies, the Cochrane Q-test and I² statistics were utilized. Publication bias was examined using a funnel plot and Egger's test. All statistical analyses were performed using Stata version 17 software.
RESULT: A total of 1,003 articles were initially identified, from which 36 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final meta-analysis. Overall, data from 8,624 women were analyzed. The pooled perinatal mortality rate among fetuses with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) and abnormal umbilical artery Doppler findings was 16.54% (95% CI: 12.93-20.15). The pooled NICU admission rate among these neonates was 69.37% (95% CI: 58.52-80.21), indicating a substantial burden on neonatal care services. Furthermore, the pooled prevalence of reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF) in the umbilical artery among IUGR fetuses was 22.03% (95% CI: 13.44-30.62). Subgroup analysis revealed that the highest pooled estimates of perinatal mortality were observed in Europe and Asia, whereas the lowest rates were reported in Australia. In terms of REDF prevalence, the highest estimates were found in studies conducted in North America.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis identified perinatal death, NICU admission, and low APGAR score as the most common adverse outcomes associated with IUGR and abnormal Doppler findings. The pooled perinatal mortality rate was 16.54%, which is notably high compared to other causes of perinatal mortality.

articles.title: Telepharmacy-based mobile health for diabetes care: models, benefits, and barriers-a scoping review.
articles.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
articles.authors: Rumi A, Fitriawati MK, Haikal F et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) requires continuous care to prevent complications. Telepharmacy delivered via mobile health (mHealth) applications offers a potential solution, particularly in resource-limited settings. However, the roles of pharmacists within such applications have not been comprehensively mapped.
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aims to: (1) map existing models of telepharmacy-based mHealth applications for diabetes care, (2) describe the roles and functions of pharmacists within these models, and (3) synthesise the reported benefits and barriers associated with their implementation.
METHODS: The review followed the Arksey & O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to 20 May 2026. Studies were eligible if they involved pharmacists, used a mobile application for telepharmacy, and targeted any type of diabetes. Data extraction covered study characteristics, pharmacist roles, application features, benefits, and barriers.
RESULTS: Of 227 records, 6 studies (632 patients) met the inclusion criteria. Studies were conducted in Malaysia, China, Japan, Pakistan, Thailand, and Indonesia covering type 1, type 2, elderly type 2, and gestational diabetes. Pharmacist roles included digital coach, educational facilitator, clinical consultant, and therapy monitor. Key application features comprised electronic medical records, counselling dashboards, adherence and quality of life assessments, medication reminders, and lifestyle monitoring. Reported benefits included improved glycaemic control (HbA1c reduction up to 0.79%), blood pressure, medication adherence, and quality of life (p < 0.05 where reported). Barriers included low digital literacy, technical issues (data synchronisation), waning long-term motivation, and economic constraints (subscription costs).
CONCLUSION: Telepharmacy-based mHealth applications with active pharmacist involvement may contribute to improving comprehensive diabetes management. However, evidence is currently limited. Future applications should prioritise user-centred design, sustainable engagement strategies, and supportive policy frameworks.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Determinants of women's exposure to mass media and its influence on healthcare utilization in Somaliland: a multilevel analysis of SLDHS 2020 data.
articles.authors: Muse YH, Abdullahi MA, Muse AH et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mass media is a critical tool for disseminating health information. This study identifies factors associated with women's media exposure and its link to healthcare utilization in Somaliland.
METHODS: Using SLDHS 2020 data ([Formula: see text]), we applied multilevel binary logistic regression to account for individual and community-level variations., with results reported as adjusted odds ratios (AOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) (p < 0.05).
RESULTS: Significant disparities in media access exist based on wealth quintile and residential status. Multilevel modeling revealed that community-level factors account for approximately 16% of the variance in media exposure. Women in the highest wealth quintile and those in urban areas had significantly higher odds of exposure compared to nomadic and rural counterparts.
CONCLUSION: Media exposure in Somaliland is shaped by structural, socioeconomic, and community-level barriers rather than individual choice alone. Policymakers should move beyond reliance on traditional broadcasting and prioritize community-based interpersonal communication, mobile/SMS health messaging, and outreach through trusted local health workers to reach uneducated, low-literate, rural, and nomadic women.

articles.title: A novel Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet (HALP)-based prognostic model to predict the progression of premenopausal breast cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Zhang S, Xu L, Peng W
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of breast cancer is increasing annually in premenopausal patients, necessitating an improved prognostic prediction model. The hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) serves as a comprehensive index that assesses systemic inflammatory response, nutritional status, and immune function.
METHODS: A total of 310 patients with invasive breast cancer (IBC) were enrolled, binary logistic regression and Cox multivariate analysis were applied to determine the risk factors for recurrence or metastasis, and the optimal cut-off value was determined using the Youden index. The prediction performance was compared using the Kaplan-Meier method and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: In the premenopausal cohort, Cox multivariate analysis demonstrated that TNM stage (HR = 2.33, 95% CI: 1.264-4.28, P = 0.007), and HALP (HR = 0.25, 95%CI: 0.095-0.64, P = 0.004) were independent prognostic factors for progression-free survival (PFS). Positive epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) (P < 0.0001) and Cytokeratin 5/6 (CK5/6) expression (P = 0.0048), higher TNM stage (P < 0.0001), and lower HALP (P < 0.0001) were significantly associated with worse PFS. A prediction model for IBC was established based on HALP, EGFR, and CK5/6. The AUC of the combined HALP-EGFR model was 0.764, which was better than single predictive model, as well as the traditional TNM stage model. Moreover, a comprehensive model integrating TNM stage, EGFR, CK5/6, and HALP achieved an even higher AUC of 0.844.
CONCLUSION: Our results indicate that the HALP-based prognostic model, particularly when combined with EGFR and further integrated with TNM stage and CK5/6, demonstrates high predictive value in premenopausal IBC patients, providing valuable guidance for individualized treatment.
ETHICS APPROVAL AND REGISTRATION: The study was reviewed and approved by the Ethics Committee of The Affiliated Changzhou No. 2 People's Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (2018KY039_01). Date: January 1st, 2018.

articles.title: Practice and evaluation of digital therapy technologies for nutritional management in high-risk groups of gestational diabetes: a real-world study.
articles.authors: Feng T, Sun B, Dong J et al.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overweight and obesity among women of childbearing age have become a major public health challenge affecting reproductive health worldwide. Excessive gestational weight gain and obesity during pregnancy substantially elevate the risk of gestational complications, particularly gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), which poses threats to maternal and infant safety. Consequently scientific and effective intervention strategies for gestational weight management are urgently required.
METHODS: Pregnant women at high risk for GDM who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria were enrolled in the study. Participants were allocated into an intervention group and a control group based on their preference. The intervention group received digital therapy management, whereas the control group received routine gestational care. Intervention effectiveness was assessed based on appropriate gestational weight gain (GWG), GDM incidence, and adherence.
RESULTS: A total of 700 pregnant women at high risk for GDM were included, comprising 504 in the intervention group and 196 in the control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between the groups, although significant differences were noted in gravidity, parity, and educational level. A higher proportion of participants in the intervention group achieved appropriate GWG during the second and third trimesters compared with in the control group, with a statistically significant between-group difference in the third trimester (P = 0.047). No statistically significant difference in the incidence of GDM was observed between the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Digital therapeutics during pregnancy effectively improved gestational weight management, with greater benefits observed over time. However, this improvement did not reduce GDM incidence.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2300071496, registered 16 May 2023.

articles.title: Association between Toxoplasma gondii infection and diabetes in pregnant women: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Mirmomeni SAM, Moslemi A, Ghasemikhah R
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally prevalent zoonotic parasite that can cause significant maternal and neonatal complications during pregnancy. Diabetes mellitus, a condition associated with impaired immune function, may increase susceptibility to such infection. Despite the severe consequences of toxoplasmosis in immunocompromised individuals, no systematic review has previously evaluated its association with diabetes in pregnant women.
METHODS: Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar (updated in August 2025). Eligible human observational studies reporting Toxoplasma gondii infection among pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), type 1 diabetes, or type 2 diabetes were included. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using Hoy et al.'s tool and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata version 17.
RESULTS: Out of 198 retrieved articles, 9 studies (7 case-control and 2 cross-sectional) met the inclusion criteria. In cross-sectional studies, pooled IgG seroprevalence among diabetic pregnant women was 29% (95% CI: 0.22-0.35), with low heterogeneity (I² = 23.63%). IgM seroprevalence was 7% (95% CI: 0.02-0.12). Case-control meta-analysis revealed a significant association between IgG seropositivity and diabetic pregnancy (OR = 2.07, 95% CI: 1.66-2.58; p < 0.001) without evidence of publication bias or heterogeneity. IgM seropositivity was not significantly different between diabetic and healthy pregnant women (OR = 1.81, 95% CI: 0.97-3.35; p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Diabetic pregnant women exhibit a significantly higher prevalence of chronic T. gondii infection (IgG) compared to non-diabetic controls, highlighting a potential association that warrants further investigation. However, the association with acute infection remains unclear. More prospective, geographically diverse studies are needed to clarify causality, underlying mechanisms, and clinical outcomes.
